Title
Phase-locked low-intensity focused ultrasound (LIFU) to cervical nodose ganglion to prevent stress-induced gastric mucosal injury by reweighting vagal afferent gain and restoring vagovagal defense

Hypothesis/goal-as-question
Can phase-locked LIFU of the cervical nodose ganglion, timed to intrinsic autonomic/visceral rhythms, durably lower the central gain of gastric vagal afferent transmission in the nucleus tractus solitarius (NTS) and thereby stabilize vagovagal reflexes that preserve mucosal blood flow and barrier under acute stress, preventing stress-induced gastritis without pharmacologic blockade? This tests whether timing-aware peripheral neuromodulation can create a low-gain, protective set-point in the brain–gut axis. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3062484/?utm_source=openai))

Atomic strategy
Exploit natural respiratory and gastric rhythm windows to bias synaptic plasticity at the first vagal relay: deliver brief LIFU bursts to nodose afferent somata during late expiration and specific gastric slow-wave phases when NTS gating is maximally permissive, with the objective of inducing durable downscaling of hyperexcitable glutamatergic afferent→NTS synapses and normalizing dorsal motor nucleus outputs that control mucosal perfusion and secretion. The acoustic drive leverages mechanosensitive ion channels (Piezo, TRP, K2P) for transient excitability shifts without lesioning. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7274478/?utm_source=openai))

Rationale
- Pathophysiology: Acute psychological/physiological stress provokes gastric mucosal ischemia–reperfusion, oxidative injury, and neurogenic inflammation; WIRS models reproduce mucosal lesions with neutrophil influx and TRP-dependent neuropeptidergic signaling. Vagal circuits strongly regulate gastric accommodation, perfusion, and secretions via nodose→NTS→DMV pathways. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/9324161/?utm_source=openai))
- Anti-inflammatory reflex: Efferent vagal output engaging α7 nicotinic receptors on macrophages suppresses mucosal cytokine release; augmenting this axis is protective in gut inflammation but is not targeted in stress gastritis. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4540232/?utm_source=openai))
- Modulation modality: LIFU modulates neural excitability through mechanotransduction in ion channels and synapses with millimeter-scale focus; peripheral vagus/nodose is accessible for ultrasound and has been acoustically modulated in rodents. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6996285/?utm_source=openai))
- Timing control surface: Respiratory pacing at ≈0.1 Hz enhances cardiovagal baroreflex gain via NTS mechanisms; the gastric slow wave is 2–4 cpm (mode ≈3 cpm). Phase-locking stimulation to these rhythms should maximize efficacy and promote consolidation of a low-gain state. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5709795/?utm_source=openai))

Specific aims
1) Demonstrate acute protection: In rats, test whether nodose LIFU time-locked to late expiration reduces mucosal injury and preserves perfusion during WIRS compared with sham and non-phase-locked LIFU. Primary outcomes: lesion index, laser-Doppler mucosal blood flow, adherent mucus, oxidative stress markers. Secondary: gastric pH/acid output, EGG stability (2–4 cpm), HRV/BRS, cytokines (TNF, IL-1β). ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/9324161/?utm_source=openai))
2) Establish plasticity and durability: After a 2‑week course of daily phase-locked LIFU, assess whether protection persists 72 h after the last session. Readouts: NTS c-Fos and synaptic marker changes after gastric distension, DMV firing probability to standardized vagal input ex vivo, sustained baroreflex sensitivity, and reduced injury on repeat WIRS. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3062484/?utm_source=openai))
3) Define mechanistic and parameter space: Map LIFU parameters (frequency 0.5–1.5 MHz, pulse repetition, duty cycle, intensity within safety limits) versus effects on nodose excitability in vivo and afferent field potentials recorded in NTS. Use mechanosensitive channel blockers (e.g., GsMTx4) to test ultrasound–mechanotransduction dependence. Compare expiration-locked versus inspiration-locked timing relative to outcomes. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6996285/?utm_source=openai))

Study design and methods
- Model: Adult rats subjected to standardized WIRS (3–6 h) to induce reproducible acute gastric mucosal lesions. Randomized, blinded, parallel groups: Sham; LIFU non-phase-locked; LIFU expiration-locked; LIFU inspiration-locked; Positive-control vagal electrical stimulation. Sample size powered on lesion index reduction (≥30%) with α=0.05, 1–β=0.8. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/9324161/?utm_source=openai))
- Targeting: High-frequency ultrasound imaging localizes the cervical nodose (inferior) ganglion; focus verified by microbubble-free acoustic mapping and by modulation of evoked vagal compound action potentials at subthreshold levels in a subset. Safety: IEC 62359 limits observed; temperature rise monitored by thermocouples. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6996285/?utm_source=openai))
- Stimulation timing: Respiratory phase from plethysmography; gastric phase from cutaneous EGG. Deliver 100–300 ms LIFU bursts at late expiration and fixed EGG phase offset; closed-loop controller keeps phase error <30°. Respiratory pacing at 0.1 Hz used in a subset to amplify baroreflex gating. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5709795/?utm_source=openai))
- Primary mucosal outcomes: Stereological lesion scoring, laser-Doppler flowmetry, Alcian blue–periodic acid–Schiff for adherent mucus, myeloperoxidase and malondialdehyde assays. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/9324161/?utm_source=openai))
- Autonomic/central outcomes: HRV and baroreflex sequence method; NTS c-Fos after standardized gastric distension; DMV neuron excitability in slices. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5043049/?utm_source=openai))
- Inflammation: Gastric mucosal TNF, IL‑1β, IL‑6; macrophage α7nAChR expression; mast cell counts/degranulation. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4540232/?utm_source=openai))
- Mechanistic probe: Systemic GsMTx4 to attenuate mechanosensitive channel activation during LIFU; expect reduced efficacy if mechanotransduction is necessary. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7274478/?utm_source=openai))

Predicted results and interpretation
- Expiration-locked nodose LIFU reduces lesion burden, preserves mucosal perfusion/mucus, stabilizes EGG normogastria, and increases BRS versus sham and non-phase-locked LIFU. Sustained benefits after a 2‑week course indicate plastic reweighting of afferent→NTS synapses and restored DMV outputs controlling mucosal defense. Loss of benefit with GsMTx4 implicates mechanosensitive channels. Together, these would support the atomic claim that timing-aware nodose neuromodulation can downshift interoceptive gain and protect the gastric mucosa under stress. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/9324161/?utm_source=openai))

Novelty and feasibility
- Prior work shows: (i) nodose/NTS control of gastric function; (ii) LIFU can modulate neural excitability via mechanosensitive ion channels; (iii) 0.1 Hz breathing augments baroreflex/NTS gating; (iv) stress models produce reproducible mucosal injury. To our knowledge, no studies have targeted nodose with phase-locked LIFU to prevent stress-induced gastritis or to induce durable plasticity in NTS-related vagovagal circuits, making this a mechanistically grounded yet unconventional therapy concept. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3062484/?utm_source=openai))

Milestones and endpoints
- Go/no-go at 6 months: ≥30% reduction in lesion index and ≥20% increase in mucosal blood flow with expiration-locked LIFU vs sham; no bradyarrhythmias or off-target effects. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/9324161/?utm_source=openai))
- Year 1: Durable protection after 2‑week course; increased BRS; reduced NTS c-Fos to gastric distension; parameter map defining safe/effective acoustic windows. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5043049/?utm_source=openai))
- Year 2: Large-animal feasibility (porcine) of cervical targeting and closed-loop timing; design of a human pilot (noninvasive nodose LIFU with respiration/EGG phase-locking) with endoscopic mucosal perfusion imaging as surrogate endpoint. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8188893/?utm_source=openai))

Risks and mitigations
- Mis-targeting/off-target autonomic effects: Real-time imaging and dose titration; exclude animals with >15% heart rate depression during test pulses. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6996285/?utm_source=openai))
- Insufficient plasticity: Extend sessions and optimize phase relationship; add respiratory pacing at 0.1 Hz to amplify NTS gating. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5709795/?utm_source=openai))
- Null results despite acute effects: Conclude that acute gating without consolidation is insufficient; pivot to combined central (NTS) targeting or adjunctive behavioral entrainment.

Impact
If validated, this establishes a repeatable, device-only therapy that reprograms interoceptive gain at the gut–brain interface—preventing stress-induced gastritis by stabilizing vagovagal defense, not by suppressing acid or broadly blocking nociception. It generalizes a phase-aware neuromodulation paradigm for autonomic disorders where maladaptive central gain and rhythm desynchrony dominate. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3062484/?utm_source=openai))

Title
Junctional-variance–clamped gastric patches trained ex vivo to resist neurogenic stress

Integrated research question-hypothesis
Can human gastric epithelial patches that are preconditioned ex vivo and engineered to clamp the amplitude and slew rate of cAMP/Ca2+ microdomain transients at the perijunctional actomyosin ring prevent stress-induced barrier failure in vivo and create local “firebreaks” that protect adjacent host mucosa without altering central stress circuitry or the resident microbiota? The premise is that neurogenic stress signals (e.g., CRF-family peptides, catecholamines, substance P) converge on MLCK-driven tight‑junction opening; clamping second‑messenger variance at junctional microdomains should raise the threshold for barrier failure under repeated stress surges. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4288093/?utm_source=openai))

Atomic strategy
Redefine second messengers as buffers, not wires: install a genetically encoded “Junctional Variance Clamp (JVC)” in gastric mini‑tissues that absorbs fast cAMP/Ca2+/IP3 excursions at tight‑junction microdomains so that stress pulses cannot exceed MLCK activation thresholds, while preserving baseline signaling needed for secretion and restitution. Microdomain targeting is enforced by AKAP/PDE4 and junctional adaptor motifs known to restrict cAMP spread at the apical membrane. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15611099/?utm_source=openai))

Rationale
- Stress peptides and autonomic outputs increase gastric permeability via peripheral pathways that include mucosal nerves and mast cells; peripheral CRF can reproduce stress‑induced barrier dysfunction in gut mucosa. Therefore, neutralizing downstream variance at the epithelial interface should be effective across heterogeneous upstream drivers. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4288093/?utm_source=openai))
- MLCK activation by Ca2+/calmodulin and related pathways is the proximate effector opening tight junctions; preventing transient peaks in local Ca2+ and cAMP should stabilize ZO‑1/occludin/claudin complexes during stress. ([frontiersin.org](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/drug-delivery/articles/10.3389/fddev.2026.1692219/full?utm_source=openai))
- Ex vivo conditioning on a human stomach‑on‑chip with luminal flow and peristaltic‑like deformation more faithfully recapitulates gastric microenvironment to select for resilient phenotypes before implantation. ([pubs.rsc.org](https://pubs.rsc.org/en/content/articlelanding/2018/lc/c8lc00910d?utm_source=openai))
- AhR agonist indole‑3‑aldehyde (IAld), a postbiotic from stress‑resilient donors, enhances epithelial barrier programs and reduces inflammatory signaling; adding IAld during training biases organoids toward durable mucin/TJ expression without needing to alter the host microbiome. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10710743/?utm_source=openai))
- Orthotopic transplantation of human gastric organoids into injured mouse stomach demonstrates feasibility of mucosal repair and engraftment, enabling repeated endoscopic deployment. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5591948/?utm_source=openai))

Specific aims
Aim 1. Build the Junctional Variance Clamp (JVC) module and validate microdomain clamping in human gastric organoids.
- Construct set:
  - JVC-cAMP: AKAP-anchored PDE4D variants fused to junctional targeting motifs (e.g., ZO‑1 PDZ‑binding peptides) with a PKA‑responsive promoter to auto‑scale PDE during spikes.
  - JVC-Ca2+: calbindin/parvalbumin chimeras fused to ZO‑1/occludin‑binding peptides to buffer subapical Ca2+ microdomains that drive MLCK.
  - JVC-IP3: apically targeted inositol‑5‑phosphatase to dampen IP3 bursts near ER–PM junctions.
- Readouts in hGOs/hGEMs on a stomach‑on‑chip under rhythmic deformation and flow:
  - FRET biosensors for cAMP and Ca2+ at junctions; quantify peak height, dV/dt, and recovery.
  - TEER and fluorescein/4 kDa dextran flux during pulsed exposure to CRF, NE/Epi, and substance P at physiological ranges.
  - MLCK activity (MLC‑pS19), junctional continuity (ZO‑1/occludin/claudin), and vesicular trafficking.
- Success criterion: ≥50% reduction in cAMP/Ca2+ peak amplitude and slew with preserved basal signaling; ≥40% attenuation in stress‑induced permeability and MLC‑pS19 versus controls across ligands.

Aim 2. Train and select organoid lineages for durable resilience with donor‑derived postbiotics and ENS‑like stress patterns.
- Conditioning regimen: chronic IAld perfusion (10–50 µM) during daily neuromechanical stress cycles (peristaltic stretch + ligand pulses) to induce AhR‑dependent barrier programs in epithelia.
- Selection metrics: maintenance of TEER during stress, low second‑messenger variance, high mucin/TJ transcripts, low NF‑κB target induction; rank lineages by composite “Resilience Index.”
- Success criterion: conditioned JVC lineages outperform unconditioned JVC and vector controls by ≥25% on the Resilience Index after 14‑day cycles. ([pubs.rsc.org](https://pubs.rsc.org/en/content/articlelanding/2018/lc/c8lc00910d?utm_source=openai))

Aim 3. Test efficacy and durability of engineered patches in vivo and assess neighborhood protection.
- Model: orthotopic endoscopic placement of JVC‑engineered, IAld‑conditioned gastric epithelial patches into superficial mucosal injuries in immunodeficient mice; after engraftment, subject animals to standardized neurogenic stress challenges.
- Endpoints:
  - Gastric permeability (oral FITC‑dextran), acid back‑diffusion injury, histologic scoring, MLC‑pS19, and junctional continuity at and adjacent to the patch edge.
  - Neighborhood effect: compare barrier metrics in host mucosa 0–3 mm from the patch versus >10 mm remote.
  - Durability: patch function over 8 weeks with repeated stress cycles; evaluate need and feasibility of re‑implantation.
- Success criterion: ≥40% reduction in permeability and histologic injury at and within 3 mm of patch borders versus control patches; maintained effect after repeated stress. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5591948/?utm_source=openai))

Key methods
- Organoid sourcing: human gastric organoids from surgical discards; derivation to monolayers for chip seeding; QA by lineage markers and acid/mucin secretion.
- Stomach‑on‑chip: dual‑channel microfluidic device enabling luminal flow, rhythmic wall strain (0.1–0.2 Hz), and pulsed exposure to stress ligands; integrate FRET imaging and TEER. ([pubs.rsc.org](https://pubs.rsc.org/en/content/articlelanding/2018/lc/c8lc00910d?utm_source=openai))
- Genetic engineering: lentiviral/AAV delivery of JVC constructs; clonal isolation; off‑target assessment by RNA‑seq and electrophysiology of parietal cell acid secretion baselines.
- Conditioning: IAld and matched vehicle; optional addition of SCFAs for exploratory synergy. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10710743/?utm_source=openai))
- In vivo delivery: mucosa‑adherent hydrogel slurry with organoids applied via endoscope; fixation with fibrin/PEG hydrogel; engraftment monitoring by endoscopy and reporter imaging. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5591948/?utm_source=openai))

Mechanistic endpoints and analytics
- Variance clamping: quantify local cAMP/Ca2+ microdomain statistics; calculate threshold‑exceedance probability versus MLCK activation using joint distributions.
- Barrier mechanics: TEER/flux dynamics under stress pulsing; FRAP of ZO‑1 to assess junctional turnover.
- Systems readouts: single‑cell RNA‑seq/ATAC‑seq to confirm AhR target induction and absence of prosecretory hyperactivation; targeted phospho‑proteomics at junction complexes.

Risk assessment and mitigations
- Risk: cAMP suppression could impair restitution or secretion. Mitigation: microdomain‑restricted PDE4 with PKA‑feedback promoter to prevent basal over‑suppression; verify normal restitution in scratch assays. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15611099/?utm_source=openai))
- Risk: IAld effects context‑dependent. Mitigation: use dose‑response, AhR antagonist controls, and stop‑condition rules; proceed only if barrier enhancement occurs without pro‑inflammatory transcription. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10710743/?utm_source=openai))
- Risk: engraftment variability. Mitigation: use hydrogel carriers and niche‑preserving delivery protocols; pre‑screen for adhesion/expansion capacity. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5591948/?utm_source=openai))

Milestones
- M1 (6 months): JVC modules localized to junctions; ≥50% reduction in stress‑evoked cAMP/Ca2+ peaks on‑chip with preserved basal signaling.
- M2 (12 months): IAld‑conditioned JVC lineages with ≥25% higher Resilience Index; stable phenotype after 14‑day washout. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10710743/?utm_source=openai))
- M3 (18 months): In vivo efficacy with ≥40% reduction in permeability and injury at/near patches; demonstration of re‑application feasibility. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5591948/?utm_source=openai))

Innovation
- Converts epithelial second‑messenger microdomains into adaptive buffers to defeat neurogenic stress convergence on MLCK—an interface‑level fix independent of CNS modulation. ([frontiersin.org](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/drug-delivery/articles/10.3389/fddev.2026.1692219/full?utm_source=openai))
- Couples human stomach‑on‑chip training under peristaltic deformation with donor‑derived postbiotic IAld to pre‑install barrier programs before implantation. ([pubs.rsc.org](https://pubs.rsc.org/en/content/articlelanding/2018/lc/c8lc00910d?utm_source=openai))

Expected outcome and significance
A reproducible, replaceable epithelial patch therapy that raises the local threshold for stress‑induced gastric barrier failure, creating protective zones that contain injury spread during chronic stress without systemic immunosuppression or neuroaxis modulation. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4288093/?utm_source=openai))

Title
State-gated, mark-sensing chromatin editing to erase stress memory in gastric stem cells

Central hypothesis–question
Do repeated psychological-stress episodes inscribe repressive chromatin “scars” in gastric stem/progenitor cells that amplify vulnerability to future injury, and can a mark-sensing, state-gated erasure of these scars restore mucosal resilience without altering acid secretion? This posits that: (i) restraint-like stressors elicit mucosal ischemia/ROS, neurohumoral outputs, and aberrant mechanics that injure the corpus/antral epithelium; (ii) stem/progenitor pools in the isthmus/base sustain the lining and can harbor durable chromatin changes; (iii) epithelial stem cells in barrier tissues exhibit epigenetic “inflammatory memory,” making a similar phenomenon plausible in stomach; and (iv) repressive marks such as DNA methylation, H3K27me3 and H3K9me3 stabilize maladaptive programs. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7210023/?utm_source=openai))

Atomic strategy
Exploit the mark itself as the trigger for its removal: transiently express reader–eraser fusions (e.g., MBD–TET1cd for 5mC, CBX/HP1 chromodomain–KDM6A/KDM4cd for H3K27me3/H3K9me3) under a mechanotransduction-responsive minimal promoter (8xGTIIC TEAD) so that editing occurs only when gastric epithelia enter a high-strain, injury-prone state and only at loci carrying the pathological marks; loss of reader affinity as marks are erased provides automatic shutoff. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5055179/?utm_source=openai))

Specific aims
1) Define stress-evoked epigenetic scars in gastric stem/progenitor cells.
2) Build and validate TEAD-gated, mark-sensing erasers in gastric organoids under controlled mechanical stress.
3) Pilot in vivo feasibility and mucosal protection in a chronic restraint-stress model.

Aim 1. Identify chromatin scars after repeated stress
- Model and sampling
  - Mice: chronic restraint stress (CRS) or water-immersion restraint stress (WIRS) for 10–14 days; sham controls. Harvest corpus/antrum. Isolate isthmus/base stem/progenitor fractions (Bmi1+/Mist1-lineage) and matched epithelium. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7210023/?utm_source=openai))
- Multi-omic profiling
  - WGBS/oxWGBS for 5mC/5hmC; CUT&Tag for H3K27me3, H3K9me3; ATAC-seq for accessibility; RNA-seq. Target analysis of barrier/restoration genes (Tff1/2/3, Muc5AC, tight-junction/adhesion, restitution programs). Benchmark against known repressive-mark biology. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13148-022-01305-8?utm_source=openai))
- Functional correlation
  - Ex vivo scratch/wound assays in organoids derived from stressed vs control mice; barrier function (TEER, FITC–dextran flux), restitution speed, and response to catecholamine/ROS challenge. Human gastric organoids from biopsies to assess translational conservation. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10393332/?utm_source=openai))
- Decision gate
  - Proceed if stress increases repressive marks and/or hypermethylation at defense/restitution enhancers in stem/progenitors with associated functional deficits.

Aim 2. Engineer and test TEAD-gated, mark-sensing erasers in gastric organoids
- Construct design
  - Reader–eraser fusions: MBD–TET1cd; CBX7chromodomain–KDM6Acd; HP1α/βchromodomain–KDM4Acd. Catalytic-dead and reader-dead controls. Expression driven by 8xGTIIC minimal promoter (TEAD-responsive). Optional destabilization domains (PEST) to limit dwell time. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5055179/?utm_source=openai))
- Rationale and safeguards
  - State gating: YAP/TAZ–TEAD activity reports epithelial strain/actomyosin tension; 8xGTIIC promoters are standard reporters of this input. Reader affinity ensures locus- and state-dependent engagement; erasure weakens binding, creating negative feedback. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6192510/?utm_source=openai))
- Gastric organoid systems and stress emulation
  - Human corpus/antral organoids (patient-derived) and mouse organoids; apply cyclic stretch/pressure pulses or substrate stiffening to raise TEAD activity; confirm nuclear YAP/TAZ and 8xGTIIC reporter induction. Overlay catecholamine/GC and ROS to mimic stress milieu. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10393332/?utm_source=openai))
- Readouts
  - On-target editing: locus-specific bisulfite/oxBS, CUT&Tag for H3K27me3/H3K9me3 before/after editor induction; kinetics of mark loss and re-gain after stress. 
  - Transcriptome/accessibility rescue: RNA-seq/ATAC-seq at identified scarred enhancers and genes.
  - Function: restitution speed after micro-wounding, mucus production, tight junction integrity, survival under ROS/ischemia-like hypoxia. Use live juxtamucosal pH-compatible conditions reflective of near-neutral gland microenvironment. ([ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK53093/?utm_source=openai))
- Specificity/off-target controls
  - Compare TEAD-gated vs constitutive promoter; reader-dead and catalysis-dead variants; measure global 5mC/ChIP changes and proliferation. SunTag or dCas9–TET1 at fixed loci used as positive controls for demethylation efficacy. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9665145/?utm_source=openai))

Aim 3. Pilot in vivo feasibility in CRS mice
- Delivery and gating
  - Epithelial-tropic AAV or transient mRNA–LNP delivering TEAD-gated reader–erasers to gastric mucosa; include HIF-1α ODD degron to stabilize payloads selectively in hypoxic injured pits, adding microenvironmental gating. Dosing during CRS bouts to capture high-strain windows. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC20916/?utm_source=openai))
- Outcomes
  - Primary: reduction in ulcer burden/erosions, improved histologic restitution, restored mucus/TFF expression.
  - Mechanism: locus-level mark reversal in sorted isthmus cells, normalization of stress-response transcription.
  - Safety: off-target epigenetic changes (WGBS snapshot), proliferation indices, dysplasia surveillance.

Key methods and measurement details
- Mechanical gating verification: 8xGTIIC-luc/fluorescent reporters quantify TEAD drive; nuclear YAP/TAZ localization by IF as orthogonal readout. Piezo1–NFAT target genes and Ca2+ imaging can provide complementary mechanical-state markers if needed. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0012160625001666?utm_source=openai))
- Reader–eraser activity: locus ChIP/CUT&Tag distance mapping from reader footprints; time-course to establish self-limiting kinetics as binding weakens with mark removal.
- Organoid stressors: cyclic stretch (Flexcell), brief hypoxia, NE/cortisol pulses, ROS microbursts; assays aligned with documented stress-induced mucosal injury in rodents. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7210023/?utm_source=openai))

Feasibility and novelty cross-check
- Gastric stem/progenitor biology and organoid models are established, allowing scar mapping and intervention at niche-relevant states. Mechanotransduction via YAP/TAZ and the 8xGTIIC promoter is widely validated as a strain reporter. Reader-linked TET1 and demethylases have been functionally deployed for targeted demethylation; coupling reader affinity to the inverse enzyme to make “mark-present-only” erasers is a logical extension and provides auto-termination on successful editing. Barrier epithelial stem cells demonstrate durable chromatin memory after inflammatory injury in skin and intestine, supporting the core hypothesis that gastric stem cells can encode stress memory. Hypoxia-ODD gating is an accepted strategy to confine protein stability to injured microenvironments. Together, this stack is mechanistically grounded and repeatable, yet not part of any current gastritis therapy. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10393332/?utm_source=openai))

Success criteria and milestones (18–24 months)
- M6–9: Identify ≥500 differentially hypermethylated or H3K27me3/H3K9me3-gained regions in stressed isthmus cells with associated transcriptional repression of restitution/barrier genes; demonstrate organoid functional deficits. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7210023/?utm_source=openai))
- M12–15: TEAD-gated reader–erasers induce locus-specific mark removal with ≥2-fold gene reactivation and restore wound closure/barrier metrics under stress, with <1% genome-wide off-target shift. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/nbt.3658?utm_source=openai))
- M18–24: Pilot in vivo dosing reduces lesion burden by ≥30% vs vehicle and shows locus-specific scar erasure in isthmus cells without dysplasia.

Risks and mitigations
- Weak or absent repressive scars: pivot to DNA methylation-dominant erasure first (MBD–TET1cd), guided by WGBS; if marks are mixed, test combinatorial but still reader-gated editors. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10215725/?utm_source=openai))
- Insufficient TEAD drive in corpus isthmus: confirm strain paradigms; if necessary, add Piezo→NFAT minimal promoter variants while retaining mark-sensing core logic. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42059278/?fc=None&ff=20260501191901&v=2.19.0.post6+133c1fe&utm_source=openai))
- Off-target chromatin effects: use reader-dead and catalysis-dead controls, limit expression with short-lived constructs and ODD gating during hypoxic injury. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC20916/?utm_source=openai))

Impact
If successful, this establishes a modality that converts the stomach’s own injury signals and the presence of aberrant chromatin marks into a self-limiting, repeatable erasure of stress memory in gastric stem cells—interrupting relapse biology without touching acid secretion. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7210023/?utm_source=openai))

Title
Perivagal redox-impedance sensing to trigger closed-loop vagus nerve stimulation that preempts stress-induced (neurogenic) gastritis

Background and rationale
- Psychological stress shifts central autonomic set-points via PVN→brainstem pathways, reducing vagal tone and favoring proinflammatory gastric mucosal responses. Vagal circuits in NTS/DMV integrate these signals and control efferent vagal output to the stomach. Oxytocinergic PVN neurons project to DVC (NTS/DMV) and modulate cardiorespiratory-vagal dynamics, linking stress neuroendocrine state to vagal control. This defines a tractable central–autonomic axis but does not yet provide an early peripheral control signal. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2967641/?utm_source=openai))
- Gastric mucosal inflammation under stress involves mast-cell activation, cytokines, and early oxidative bursts; TRPA1/TRPV1-expressing vagal afferents are redox-sensitive, rendering local ROS both a driver and a biomarker of imminent neurogenic gastric injury. Surgical or functional vagal impairment worsens mucosal defense, underscoring the protective potential of efferent vagal signaling. ([ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK499926/?utm_source=openai))
- The “inflammatory reflex” (cholinergic anti-inflammatory pathway; CAP) provides a mechanistic route whereby efferent vagus suppresses cytokine production via α7nAChR-expressing immune effectors; VNS reduces inflammatory activity in preclinical sepsis, colitis, and in early clinical Crohn’s/RA studies. These effects can occur with brief, well-tolerated stimulation and can be deployed repeatedly. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/nature01321?utm_source=openai))
- Redox-responsive thiol–disulfide hydrogels reversibly change crosslink density upon H2O2/thiol exchange, shifting swelling, stiffness, and ionic conductivity; dynamic conductive hydrogels and interdigitated electrodes enable impedance transduction. In vivo H2O2 sensing on implant electrodes has been demonstrated in the cochlea, supporting feasibility of implantable ROS electrochemical readouts. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9222492/?utm_source=openai))

Gap and atomic strategy
- Gap: There is no chronic, organ-proximal biomarker that rises before symptom onset and directly gates VNS to re-engage CAP for gastric protection.
- Atomic strategy: Recast perivagal oxidative microbursts—proximal readouts of neuroimmune activation—as the control signal. A reversible thiol–disulfide hydrogel cuff transduces local ROS into impedance changes that trigger short, patterned VNS bursts to preempt gastric inflammation.

Hypothesis (research question is equivalent)
- Do transient increases in perivagal ROS during acute psychological stress precede and predict gastric mucosal injury, and does triggering brief, pattern-optimized VNS at a hydrogel-defined redox threshold suppress downstream cytokine release and epithelial injury without cardiovascular side effects? ([ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK499926/?utm_source=openai))

Specific aims
1) Establish temporality and specificity of perivagal ROS in stress-induced gastritis.
2) Engineer and calibrate a perivagal thiol–disulfide redox-impedance cuff for chronic ROS sensing.
3) Test closed-loop ROS-triggered VNS versus open-loop and sham in preventing stress-gastritis.
4) Demonstrate repeatability and individualization across recurrent stress episodes.

Aim 1: Temporality and specificity of perivagal ROS
- Model: Water-immersion restraint stress (WIRS) or CRH-stress in adult rats.
- Sensing: Implant a cervical perivagal microelectrode (Pt) channel for cyclic voltammetry/pulsed amperometry of H2O2 (cochlear-validated waveform), alongside a separate EIS channel for the hydrogel device (installed in Aim 2). Simultaneous gastric readouts: lesion scoring, histology, tissue ROS (dichlorofluorescein), mucosal cytokines, mast-cell degranulation; autonomic surrogates: HRV and baroreflex sensitivity. Determine whether perivagal ROS rises minutes before mucosal injury/cytokine surge. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0925400525005647?utm_source=openai))
- Controls: Catalase microinfusion near cuff to quench H2O2; neck motion/temperature references to deconfound artifacts.

Milestone: Perivagal ROS leading mucosal injury by ≥5–15 min with AUC-ROC ≥0.8 for predicting injury onset.

Aim 2: Redox-impedance cuff engineering and calibration
- Materials: PEG- or HA-based hydrogel crosslinked by reversible disulfides (pyridyl disulfide chemistry or thiol–disulfide exchange). Embed interdigitated microelectrodes; tune baseline ion content to yield a stable impedance spectrum. Bench-calibrate Δ|Z| and phase versus [H2O2] (1–100 µM) and redox cycling; verify reversibility over ≥10^4 cycles. Characterize modulus matching to perineurium to avoid mechanosensitization. ([onlinelibrary.wiley.com](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1002/pola.29539?utm_source=openai))
- In vivo: Implant bilaterally; compare redox-active cuff versus redox-inert control gel. Track long-term stability (EIS drift), tissue response, and signal-to-artifact ratio during spontaneous movement.

Milestone: In vivo Δ|Z| proportional to perivagal H2O2 with r ≥ 0.7; stable over 8 weeks.

Aim 3: Closed-loop prevention trial
- Controller: Threshold/accumulation detector on Δ|Z| slope (perivagal redox index). On threshold crossing, deliver 0.1–0.5 s VNS burst, amplitude titrated sub-bradycardic, leveraging parameters known to engage CAP while minimizing cardiac effects; optional cardiac-synchronized bursting if needed. Primary endpoints: gastric lesion index, mucosal cytokines (TNF, IL-1β, IL-6), myeloperoxidase, and barrier markers; secondary: HRV-HF power, baroreflex sensitivity, and behavioral pain proxies. Arms: closed-loop ROS-triggered VNS; open-loop matched dose; sham. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0022480404003737?utm_source=openai))
- Mechanistic verification: α7nAChR antagonist or splenic nerve block in subgroups to confirm CAP dependence; DMV-targeted stimulation cohort (literature-based anti-inflammatory without bradycardia) as positive control. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38670240/?utm_source=openai))

Milestone: ≥40% reduction in lesion index and cytokines versus sham; non-inferior or superior to open-loop at lower total stimulation time.

Aim 4: Repeatability and personalization
- Over 6–8 weeks, induce multiple stress episodes. Use individual baseline redox dynamics to adapt thresholds. Evaluate durability (signal, tissue response), prevention efficacy across episodes, and stimulation economy. Quantify safety: ECG, blood pressure, laryngeal/respiratory effects, nerve histology.

Milestone: Stable prevention across ≥5 stress episodes with ≤20% false-trigger rate and no persistent bradycardia.

Methods summary
- Animal preparation and endpoints: Standard WIRS/CRH protocols; blinded histology; multiplex cytokines; electrogastrography optional.
- Electronics/algorithms: Low-amplitude EIS (kHz band) with 4-wire referencing, motion/temperature compensation; on-board thresholding with lockout windows to avoid burst clustering.
- Statistics: Time-to-injury analyses, mixed-effects models across repeated episodes, pre-registered primary/secondary outcomes.

Innovation and novelty
- Introduces perivagal ROS as a peripheral, organ-proximal, pre-symptomatic control signal for autonomic neuromodulation. There is prior VNS anti-inflammatory efficacy and chronic vagal cuff technology, but no prior perivagal ROS-sensing hydrogel interfaced to a nerve for closed-loop inflammation control. In vivo implant H2O2 sensing is feasible (cochlea), dynamic disulfide hydrogels provide reversible redox-to-impedance transduction, and CAP engagement by brief VNS is established—this proposal integrates them to prevent, not palliate, neurogenic gastritis. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6517481/?utm_source=openai))

Feasibility and risk management
- Signal ambiguity: Address with catalase controls, redox-inert gel, dual-sensor confirmation (electrochemistry + impedance).
- Cardiovascular safety: Use cardiac-sparing VNS parameters and monitor HR/ECG continuously; DMV-targeted control cohort. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38670240/?utm_source=openai))
- Chronic interface: Employ softness- and adhesion-optimized hydrogels; track EIS drift; leverage best practices from vagal cuff electrodes. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10823593/?utm_source=openai))

Success criteria and deliverables (24 months)
- Year 1: Demonstrate predictive perivagal ROS dynamics; bench/in vivo calibration of the redox-impedance cuff; regulatory-grade biocompatibility package. ([onlinelibrary.wiley.com](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1002/pola.29539?utm_source=openai))
- Year 2: Show closed-loop superiority or dose-sparing non-inferiority versus open-loop for preventing stress-gastritis across repeated episodes; mechanistic CAP verification. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2118357/?utm_source=openai))

Translational outlook
- Human translation paths: Perivagal minimally invasive cuff with EIS readout and on-device control; initial endpoints in functional dyspepsia with stress-exacerbated symptoms and mucosal biomarkers. CAP clinical precedents in Crohn’s/RA de-risk the effector; the novelty lies in the preventive, redox-driven trigger. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10798868/?utm_source=openai))

Key references
- PVN→DVC oxytocinergic modulation and autonomic control: ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2967641/?utm_source=openai))
- Stress gastritis pathophysiology and ROS: ([ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK499926/?utm_source=openai))
- TRPA1/TRPV1 redox-sensitive vagal afferents: ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3160477/?utm_source=openai))
- Inflammatory reflex and anti-inflammatory VNS: ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/nature01321?utm_source=openai))
- Redox-responsive thiol–disulfide hydrogels and conductive hydrogel impedance: ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9222492/?utm_source=openai))
- In vivo implant H2O2 sensing: ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0925400525005647?utm_source=openai))

Title
Activity-coupled somatostatin from gut-innervating nociceptors to interrupt the stress–ulcer brain–gut loop

Rationale
Psychological stress activates the HPA axis and autonomic circuits, shifting gastric control toward sympathetic dominance and altering vagal tone; downstream effects include impaired mucosal defense, ischemia, and acid-mediated injury. Gastric barrier compromise and acid back-diffusion activate capsaicin-sensitive afferents (e.g., TRPV1+), which relay distress to brainstem/limbic sites and help close a pathological brain–gut feedback loop that perpetuates injury. Sensory neuropeptides bidirectionally shape mucosal outcomes: CGRP supports hyperemia and protection, whereas tachykinins can drive neurogenic inflammation. Interrupting ascending nociceptor traffic while simultaneously restoring local cytoprotection is a direct way to break the loop at the gut interface. ([journals.physiology.org](https://journals.physiology.org/doi/10.1152/physrev.00042.2017?utm_source=openai))

Atomic strategy
Convert gut-innervating nociceptors into a local, on-demand source of somatostatin (SST) so that the same afferent activity that signals gastric distress triggers SST release at peripheral terminals. SST will (i) activate Gi-coupled somatostatin receptors on nociceptors to reduce excitability and transmitter release, and (ii) inhibit parietal/ECL-driven acid secretion, restoring mucosal defenses. This single mechanism is designed to reduce gut-to-brain “distress” signaling and acid injury in one step. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11207395/?utm_source=openai))

Central hypothesis
Periodic, peripherally targeted LNP delivery of mRNA encoding preprosomatostatin to dorsal root and vagal sensory neurons will produce activity-dependent SST release from gastric afferent terminals, thereby reducing ascending nociceptor drive and suppressing gastric acid output; this will prevent or attenuate stress-induced gastric mucosal injury and disrupt the reinforcing brain–gut stress circuit. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5424629/?utm_source=openai))

Specific aims
Aim 1. Build and validate a peptide-decorated LNP that delivers mRNA to gut-innervating sensory neurons in vivo.
- Formulation: Ionizable LNPs decorated with a neuron-binding peptide (e.g., Tet1) for DRG/nodose uptake; mRNA encodes preprosomatostatin with native signal peptide to ensure dense-core vesicle sorting and amidation. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11141738/?utm_source=openai))
- Target mapping: Retrograde trace from stomach wall (FluoroGold) to identify gut-projecting DRG/nodose neurons; quantify LNP-driven reporter expression in traced neurons versus off-target tissues. ([ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK532291/?utm_source=openai))
- Peripheral restriction: Confirm negligible CNS transfection and brain exposure after IV or intrathecal dosing using reporter assays and biodistribution.

Aim 2. Demonstrate activity-coupled SST release from sensory terminals and local physiological actions in the stomach.
- Ex vivo and in vivo readouts: In anesthetized rats, evoke gastric nociceptor activity (acid pulses) and measure evoked SST levels in gastric venous effluent and lamina propria microdialysate; assess changes in mucosal blood flow and permeability. Record single-unit or calcium signals from traced afferents to show reduced excitability after LNP-SST. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/7502920/?utm_source=openai))
- Receptor engagement: Use peripherally restricted SSTR2 antagonist to reverse effects and verify mechanism; assess reductions in tachykinin release. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11207395/?utm_source=openai))
- Acid secretory physiology: Quantify histamine-stimulated and vagal-stimulated acid output before/after LNP-SST; expect suppression consistent with SST action on ECL/parietal pathways. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12109247/?utm_source=openai))

Aim 3. Test efficacy in stress-induced gastric injury and disruption of the brain–gut loop.
- Model: Restraint water-immersion stress (RWIS) in rats to induce mucosal lesions. Dose LNP-SST prophylactically (e.g., 2 weeks prior) and therapeutically (24 h prior). Primary endpoint: macroscopic/microscopic lesion index; secondary endpoints: mucosal blood flow, barrier integrity, and luminal bleeding. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7265141/?utm_source=openai))
- Circuit readouts: Quantify c-Fos in NTS/PBN and HPA markers (plasma corticosterone) as surrogates for ascending distress signaling reduction. ([journals.physiology.org](https://journals.physiology.org/doi/10.1152/physrev.00042.2017?utm_source=openai))
- Durability/repeatability: Track transgene expression and efficacy decay to define redosing interval; repeat LNP dosing to demonstrate sustainable protection without integration.

Experimental plan and methods
1) Nanoparticle engineering and targeting
- LNP composition: Standard ionizable lipid/PEG-lipid/cholesterol/phospholipid blend; surface Tet1 peptide via maleimide-PEG-lipid. Optimize size (~80–100 nm) and pKa for neuronal uptake. Validate uptake/transfection in primary DRG cultures. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11141738/?utm_source=openai))
- mRNA design: Cap1, GC-optimized coding sequence for preproSST; 5’/3’ UTRs tuned for neuronal translation; poly(A) ~120 nt. The preprohormone’s intrinsic trafficking ensures DCV packaging and amidation, enabling Ca2+-dependent release with nociceptor activity. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5424629/?utm_source=openai))
- In vivo delivery: IV or intrathecal administration; compare DRG/nodose transfection efficiencies; corroborate with prior DRG-directed LNP and mRNA reports. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39896578/?utm_source=openai))

2) Physiology and mechanism
- Nociceptor excitability: Extracellular recordings or GCaMP imaging of traced gastric afferents during acid back-diffusion; evaluate shifts in firing thresholds and discharge after LNP-SST vs LNP-control. ([ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK53093/?utm_source=openai))
- Secretory outputs: Measure basal and stimulated gastric acid secretion in pylorus-ligated or perfused stomach preparations; expect SST-mediated reductions. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12109247/?utm_source=openai))
- Mucosal defense: Laser-Doppler flowmetry for hyperemia and Evan’s blue/fluorescein for permeability; expect improved perfusion indirectly via reduced injury, despite modest afferent silencing. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5333589/?utm_source=openai))

3) Disease efficacy
- RWIS protocol with blinded scoring of lesions and histology; evaluate dose–response and timing. Brainstem c-Fos mapping indexes reduced afferent drive; plasma corticosterone indexes HPA engagement. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7265141/?utm_source=openai))

Outcomes and interpretation
- Support for hypothesis: LNP-SST reduces gastric afferent activity during injury, suppresses acid output, decreases lesion scores, and dampens c-Fos in visceral sensory nuclei under RWIS.
- Mechanistic specificity: Antagonism of SSTR2 restores afferent activity and acid secretion; LNP without SST has no effect. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11207395/?utm_source=openai))
- System-level effect: By reducing gut-to-brain distress signals and acid injury simultaneously, the vicious cycle weakens at its origin.

Risk, limitations, and mitigation
- Targeting breadth: DRG-wide transfection could induce unwanted peripheral analgesia. Use minimal effective doses, gut-nerve retrograde selection metrics, and refine peptide ligands to favor gut-projecting neurons. Monitor somatosensory thresholds. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11141738/?utm_source=openai))
- Over-suppression of beneficial CGRP hyperemia: Titrate expression to dampen excessive firing without abolishing protective reflexes; verify maintained mucosal perfusion. ([journals.physiology.org](https://journals.physiology.org/doi/10.1152/physrev.00059.2021?utm_source=openai))
- Delivery route: If IV targeting is suboptimal, pivot to intrathecal LNPs, which have demonstrated DRG delivery for nucleic acids. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39896578/?utm_source=openai))

Milestones
- Year 1: LNP-SST construct, DRG/nodose transfection and peripheral restriction established.
- Year 2: Activity-coupled SST release and gastric physiology modulation demonstrated.
- Year 3: RWIS efficacy and brain–gut loop biomarkers improved; redosing interval defined.

Innovation
- Reframes nociceptors as a renewable, local endocrine source that is self-timed by their own activity; delivers dual benefits—afferent silencing and acid suppression—without central manipulation or permanent integration. Uses clinically advancing LNP-mRNA methods redirected to peripheral sensory neurons for stress-ulcer prevention. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39896578/?utm_source=openai))

Title
Donor-stratified human gastric slices and spatial metabolomics to discover and locally reapply endogenous pro‑resolving mediators for stress‑induced (neurogenic) gastritis

Hypothesis–Question
Do stress‑resilient human gastric mucosa encode a reproducible, microdomain‑resolved metabolite program at nerve–epithelium–immune interfaces that limits neurogenic injury and accelerates repair; and can re‑applying these endogenous mediators locally, in repeated doses, reset susceptible mucosa toward a durable, pro‑resolution state without systemic neuroendocrine suppression? ([ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK53093/?utm_source=openai))

Atomic Strategy
Treat the gastric mucosa as a spatially organized, excitable chemical field in which neuropeptide inputs (e.g., SP/CGRP) and paracrine outputs (e.g., histamine from ECL cells) drive injury–defense dynamics; mine stress‑resilient tissue for the small molecules it deploys during resolution, then re‑apply these molecules, repeatedly and locally, to impose a resilience bias. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/8048007/?utm_source=openai))

Specific Aims
1) Build a donor‑stratified, precision‑cut human gastric mucosal slice platform that preserves native neuro‑immune‑epithelial and ECM architecture to expose stress “memory” ex vivo and enable repeated sampling. Feasibility is supported by organotypic slice culture in GI tissues and stomach tumors. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4754739/?utm_source=openai))
2) Use microdomain‑resolved metabolomics (nanoDESI/DESI MSI and CE‑MS) to identify endogenous, locally acting mediators that (i) rise in resilient donors during neurogenic challenge/resolution and (ii) causally restore barrier function, perfusion, and secretory balance when applied to susceptible tissue. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2587601/?utm_source=openai))
3) Translate the minimal effective mediator set into a repeat‑dose, stomach‑local intervention and test durability and mechanism in gastric organoids maintained in defined synthetic hydrogels tuned for mechanotransductive stabilization. ([frontiersin.org](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/pharmacology/articles/10.3389/fphar.2021.707891/full?utm_source=openai))

Rationale and Mechanistic Anchors
- Neurogenic inputs: Capsaicin‑sensitive afferents release CGRP and tachykinins that regulate mucosal blood flow and protection; SP activates mucosal mast cells via NK1/MRGPRX2 to amplify inflammation. ([journals.physiology.org](https://journals.physiology.org/doi/10.1152/physiologyonline.1999.14.5.201?utm_source=openai))
- Acid/secretory axis: ECL‑derived histamine is the dominant paracrine driver of parietal cell acid secretion; prostaglandins and somatostatin counterbalance. ([ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK547758/?utm_source=openai))
- Endogenous cytoprotection candidates: PGE2/EP signaling, adenosine A2A agonism, endocannabinoid CB1 signaling, and H2S donors support mucus/bicarbonate, blood flow, anti‑inflammation, and reduced injury. ([journals.physiology.org](https://journals.physiology.org/doi/10.1152/physrev.00004.2008?utm_source=openai))
- Durable state control: Mechanical and inflammatory cues feed into YAP/TAZ‑centered mechanotransduction and chromatin remodeling that can encode epithelial “memory”; defined hydrogel mechanics/ligands can stabilize or shift this state in organoids. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6192510/?utm_source=openai))

Experimental Plan

Aim 1: Human gastric precision‑cut mucosal slices
- Source and preparation: Acquire corpus/antrum tissue from bariatric/oncologic margins; prepare 200–300 μm slices with vibrating microtome; culture at controlled O2 on porous supports. Preserve nerves, ECL, parietal, mucous, endothelial, fibroblast, and mast cell compartments. Validate viability (calcein/PI), structure (H&E, immunostains), and basal secretory tone. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4754739/?utm_source=openai))
- Standardized neurogenic challenge: Apply pulses of SP, CGRP, and norepinephrine ± acid microbursts; block smooth‑muscle contraction (e.g., nicardipine) to reduce motion artefacts. Readouts: transepithelial resistance, tight junction relocalization, mucus thickness, histamine in superfusate (ECL output), mast cell degranulation, and perfusion surrogates (NADH/FAD autofluorescence). ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4754739/?utm_source=openai))
- Donor stratification: Define “resilient” vs “susceptible” tissue by composite score (faster barrier restitution, greater reactive hyperemia, lower degranulation) under identical provocation.

Aim 2: Spatial and single‑cell‑scale metabolomics to discover resilience mediators
- Mapping: Perform DESI/nanoDESI‑MSI on cryosectioned slices to resolve small‑molecule gradients along gland axis, nerve–epithelium contacts, and mast cell/ECL niches during baseline, peak challenge, and resolution windows. Complement with CE‑ESI‑MS on microdissected regions or single cells. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2587601/?utm_source=openai))
- Candidate classes a priori: prostaglandins (e.g., PGE2/EP4 bias), adenosine/inosine, endocannabinoids (AEA/2‑AG), sulfide‑related species, specialized pro‑resolving lipid mediators; discovery remains unbiased. Link abundance trajectories to functional readouts from Aim 1. ([journals.physiology.org](https://journals.physiology.org/doi/10.1152/physrev.00004.2008?utm_source=openai))
- Causality tests: Microinject/topically pulse purified candidates into susceptible‑donor slices during provocation; quantify (i) reduced mast cell degranulation, (ii) moderated ECL histamine release, (iii) recovery of TEER and junctions, (iv) hyperemic response. Receptor‑level antagonism (EP4, A2A, CB1) to confirm on‑target action; repeat twice‑daily for 7–10 days to assess sustained efficacy without tachyphylaxis. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2014644/?utm_source=openai))

Aim 3: Translation to repeat‑dose, stomach‑local intervention using defined matrices
- Gastric organoid culture in synthetic matrices: Derive donor organoids and maintain in xeno‑free hydrogels (e.g., PEG‑based or polysaccharide VitroGel) with gastric‑relevant adhesion peptides and degradability; tune stiffness/viscoelasticity to resilient‑tissue set‑points measured from Aim 1. ([frontiersin.org](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/pharmacology/articles/10.3389/fphar.2021.707891/full?utm_source=openai))
- Mechanism/durability: Apply the minimal mediator set identified in Aim 2 under repeated neurogenic provocation; measure sustained improvements in barrier genes, reduced inflammatory transcription, and YAP/TAZ localization with accompanying ATAC‑seq changes consistent with a pro‑resolution chromatin state. Withdraw mediators and test persistence. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6192510/?utm_source=openai))
- On‑demand local release concept (ex vivo validation): Covalently tether mediators in the hydrogel with acid‑ or protease‑labile linkers enriched during flares (e.g., low pH, tryptase); verify triggerable release and retained efficacy on slices. Iterate kinetics to avoid desensitization.

Endpoints and Success Criteria
- Discovery: A short list (≤5) of endogenous small molecules whose spatial dynamics uniquely mark resilience and that, when locally reapplied, restore barrier/perfusion and normalize secretory balance during neurogenic challenge. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9533735/?utm_source=openai))
- Repeatability: Equal or improved efficacy with twice‑daily dosing over ≥7 days without loss of effect on slices and organoids.
- Mechanistic sufficiency: Antagonist blockade abrogates benefit; imposing resilient hydrogel mechanics enhances mediator efficacy and stabilizes a pro‑resolution epigenetic program. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/nprot.2017.095?utm_source=openai))
- Safety/Specificity proxy: Minimal effects in unchallenged tissue; no enhancement of acid secretion at baseline; no requirement for systemic HPA manipulation.

Risk Assessment and Mitigations
- Human gastric slice viability/throughput: If limited, leverage adjacent‑normal stomach margins from tumor resections and adapt validated intestinal slice workflows; maintain high O2 and motion control. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4944870/?utm_source=openai))
- Analyte identification: Combine MSI with targeted LC/CE‑MS/MS and authentic standards to resolve isomers/isobars; use receptor pharmacology to confirm function. ([pubs.acs.org](https://pubs.acs.org/doi/10.1021/acs.analchem.5c00157?utm_source=openai))
- Inter‑donor variability: Use within‑donor crossover designs and mixed‑effects modeling; prioritize mediators with convergent effects across donors.

Deliverables
- A validated, human, donor‑stratified gastric slice assay capturing neurogenic injury–resolution dynamics.
- Spatial metabolomic atlas of resilience vs susceptibility microdomains and a causal mediator short list.
- Prototype repeat‑dose, stomach‑local mediator formulation with ex vivo on‑demand release and a mechanistic biomarker panel (barrier recovery, perfusion response, YAP/TAZ‑linked chromatin accessibility) indicating durable reprogramming toward resilience. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4447318/?utm_source=openai))

Title
Paired chemoreflex challenge plus respiratory-gated auricular VNS to inoculate dorsal vagal complex reflexes against stress-induced gastritis

Integrated hypothesis–question
Can repeated pairing of a mild, controlled chemoreflex challenge (low-dose CO2 rebreathing) with expiratory-gated transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS) drive use-dependent plasticity in the dorsal vagal complex (DVC) that retunes vagovagal reflexes toward faster, stronger gastric protection during psychological stress, thereby preventing stress-induced gastritis? The bet is that pairing a safe “practice stress” with vagal afferent activation will consolidate a protective default in NTS→DMV circuits that generalizes to later heterotypic stressors. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7416561/?utm_source=openai))

Atomic strategy
Exploit associative plasticity in DVC by timing taVNS bursts to the expiratory phase while subjects experience brief, sub-anxiogenic hypercapnia. This consistently co-activates chemoreceptor→NTS inputs and vagal afferents during a defined arousal microstate, strengthening NTS→DMV synapses and inhibitory gating so protective vagal efferent patterns deploy preemptively when real stress arrives. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29060561/?utm_source=openai))

Rationale (minimal evidentiary spine)
- Vagal efferents via the cholinergic anti-inflammatory pathway restrain cytokine output from macrophages and related cells (α7nAChR), a mechanism relevant to gastric mucosal defense. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/nrd1797?utm_source=openai))
- taVNS modulates human gastric motility and stabilizes gastric slow waves; it reverses cold-stress–induced gastric dysrhythmia in healthy subjects. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1935861X2100125X?utm_source=openai))
- Intermittent hypoxia/hypercapnia recruit carotid body and pulmonary afferents that project to NTS, where BDNF/TrkB-linked plasticity mechanisms are engaged by repeated bouts. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7416561/?utm_source=openai))
- Respiratory-gated auricular VNS (RAVANS), especially expiratory-locked bursts, modifies autonomic output and brainstem activity, providing a proven timing framework for state-dependent afferent drive. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29060561/?utm_source=openai))
- Low-dose CO2 inhalation (≤3.5%) is physiologically safe across repeated sessions in healthy adults, enabling chronic, repeatable “practice stress” without sympathetic overdrive. ([journals.physiology.org](https://journals.physiology.org/doi/10.1152/japplphysiol.01053.2025?utm_source=openai))
- Stress-induced gastric injury depends on brainstem autonomic circuits (DVC) and dysregulated vagovagal control; aVNS mitigates stress-evoked gastric lesions in rats. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7265141/?utm_source=openai))

Specific Aims
Aim 1 (preclinical mechanistic test): Determine whether paired chemoreflex–taVNS conditioning reweights DVC circuitry and protects the gastric mucosa under stress.
- Model: Adult rats.
- Conditioning (14 days, 5 sessions/week): four 2-min bouts of 3% CO2 (nose cone) separated by 3-min room air; during each CO2 bout deliver left-ear taVNS bursts (trágus) gated to expiration (e-RAVANS; 1 s trains at 20 Hz, 200 μs, 1–2 mA, duty-cycled to exhalation). Sham, unpaired (random taVNS), and single-modality controls included. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29060561/?utm_source=openai))
- Endpoints before and after conditioning: 
  - Circuit plasticity: NTS/DMV BDNF and TrkB expression; miniature IPSC/EPSC ratios; glycinergic/GABAergic receptor trafficking (slice electrophysiology/immunohistochemistry). ([journals.physiology.org](https://journals.physiology.org/doi/abs/10.1152/jn.00241.2022?utm_source=openai))
  - Autonomic setpoint: resting HRV (RMSSD, HF power), baroreflex sensitivity.
  - Gastric control: in vivo motility and mucosal blood flow (laser Doppler).
- Stress challenge and protection readouts:
  - Heterotypic acute stressors (restraint water-immersion; cold immobilization). Quantify mucosal lesion area, permeability, mast cell degranulation, and cytokines (TNF-α, IL-6). ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7265141/?utm_source=openai))
  - Anti-inflammatory reflex engagement: gastric tissue cytokine suppression relative to controls. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/nrd1797?utm_source=openai))
- Primary success criterion: Paired conditioning reduces lesion area ≥40% versus sham and outperforms single-modality arms, with concurrent increases in NTS/DMV BDNF/TrkB and strengthened inhibitory tone.

Aim 2 (human proof-of-mechanism): Test whether paired conditioning stabilizes gastric electrophysiology and autonomic responses during psychological stress.
- Design: Randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled, 2-arm trial in healthy adults (n≈60).
- Conditioning (4 weeks, 3 sessions/week): Each session includes four 2-min bouts of 2.5–3.0% CO2 (tight-fitting mask) paired with e-RAVANS (left cymba conchae; 20 Hz, 200 μs pulses; intensity titrated to strong but comfortable paresthesia) time-locked to expiration using a respiratory belt; sham = room air + earlobe stimulation, same schedule. Safety monitoring includes SpO2, end-tidal CO2, blood pressure. ([journals.physiology.org](https://journals.physiology.org/doi/10.1152/japplphysiol.01053.2025?utm_source=openai))
- Pre/post stress challenge: Trier Social Stress Test and cold-pressor. Outcomes:
  - Gastric electrophysiology: body-surface gastric mapping (BSGM) stability, slow-wave frequency variance. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36997454/?utm_source=openai))
  - Autonomic and endocrine: HRV (HF power), salivary cortisol AUC.
  - Symptoms: validated upper-GI symptom scales during/after stress.
- Primary success criterion: Greater preservation of BSGM stability and HF-HRV during stress in paired-conditioning arm versus sham; reduced stress-evoked dyspeptic symptoms.
- Secondary/exploratory: Serum cytokines; near-term persistence (2–4 weeks post).

Aim 3 (pilot patient signal): In stress-sensitive functional dyspepsia or recurrent “stress gastritis” phenotype, assess symptom and physiological benefits after an 8-week at-home paired-conditioning program.
- Outcomes: Dyspepsia severity index, gastric accommodation (nutrient drink test), BSGM, HRV. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8887908/?utm_source=openai))
- Feasibility: adherence, adverse events.

Intervention details and dosing logic
- CO2 dose: Target 2.5–3.0% (humans) and 3% (rats) to engage chemoreflex without provoking anxiety/sympathetic surge; session caps and continuous oximetry ensure safety. ([journals.physiology.org](https://journals.physiology.org/doi/10.1152/japplphysiol.01053.2025?utm_source=openai))
- Timing: Expiratory gating preferentially boosts cardiac-vagal influence and has demonstrated autonomic effects; aligning taVNS to expiration during CO2 bouts enforces consistent associative pairing in DVC. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29060561/?utm_source=openai))
- taVNS parameters: 15–25 Hz, 200–300 μs pulse width, intensity at sensory threshold +10–20%. Session structure creates repeated, state-locked co-activation windows to promote Hebbian plasticity. 
- Generalization test: Use heterotypic stressors to probe whether protection extends beyond the trained stimulus class.

Mechanistic readouts mapped to endpoints
- Central plasticity: Increased NTS/DMV BDNF/TrkB and strengthened inhibitory (glycinergic/GABAergic) tone after intermittent chemoreflex activation indicates metaplastic shift toward protective gating. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3702218/?utm_source=openai))
- Reflex expression: Enhanced vagal efferent output during stress (HRV, baroreflex) and stabilized gastric slow waves/motility reflect a faster-onset protective reflex. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1935861X2100125X?utm_source=openai))
- Mucosal defense: Reduced cytokines and lesion area in animal stress models index engagement of the vagal anti-inflammatory pathway and improved perfusion/barrier integrity. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/nrd1797?utm_source=openai))

Statistical plan
- Aim 1: Power for ANOVA (four arms) to detect 40% lesion reduction (α=0.05, 1–β=0.8) based on historical RWIS variance; post hoc Tukey for paired vs single-modality contrasts.
- Aim 2: Mixed-effects models on BSGM stability and HF-HRV with fixed effects for arm, time, and stress; pre-registered primary endpoints and multiplicity control (Hochberg).

Risks and mitigations
- Sympathetic sensitization from gas challenge: held below 3.5% CO2, short bouts, continuous monitoring. ([journals.physiology.org](https://journals.physiology.org/doi/10.1152/japplphysiol.01053.2025?utm_source=openai))
- taVNS nonresponders: titration to percept threshold, electrode placement verification; adherence sensors.
- Ulcerogenic off-targets from vagal drive: use afferent-focused auricular stimulation rather than cervical efferent drive; monitor gastric acidity and symptoms. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1935861X2100125X?utm_source=openai))

Innovation
- Reframes “stress management” as operant conditioning of a defined brainstem reflex using a precisely timed, paired afferent protocol.
- Integrates a safe, tunable chemoreflex micro-challenge with respiratory-gated taVNS to write durable protective defaults into the DVC—distinct from prior open-loop VNS or generic hypoxic preconditioning that lacked associative timing and gastric targeting. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29060561/?utm_source=openai))

Go/no-go milestones
- Aim 1: ≥40% lesion reduction with circuit plasticity signature (NTS/DMV BDNF/TrkB up, inhibitory tone up).
- Aim 2: Preservation of BSGM stability and HF-HRV during stress with effect size d≥0.6; acceptable safety/adherence.
- Proceed to Aim 3 only if both milestones are met.

Anticipated impact
If successful, this yields a repeatable, mechanism-grounded “stress vaccine” protocol—state-locked, paired conditioning that generalizes across stressors, reduces stress-evoked gastric injury, and is feasible for chronic outpatient use. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35597733/?utm_source=openai))

Title
Stress-gated purinergic rebalancing at the gastric mucosal surface to prevent and reverse stress-induced gastritis

Background and rationale
- The healthy gastric surface maintains a near-neutral pH microclimate within the adherent mucus–bicarbonate gel, protecting epithelium from luminal acid and pepsin; hyperemia and prostaglandins/peptides (e.g., CGRP, NO) support this barrier. Under stress, microcirculatory compromise and barrier failure allow acid back-diffusion and injury. ([journals.physiology.org](https://journals.physiology.org/doi/full/10.1152/ajpcell.00102.2004?utm_source=openai))
- Gastrointestinal epithelial and immune cells release ATP during mechanical/chemical stress; extracellular ATP activates P2X/P2Y receptors, with P2X7 signaling promoting inflammasome activation and cytokine release that disrupt barrier function. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8721002/?utm_source=openai))
- Adenosine, generated by ectonucleotidases (CD39→CD73), signals via A2A/A2B receptors to support epithelial tight junctions, mucus hydration, and vasodilation, countering inflammatory injury. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10930693/?utm_source=openai))
- Degrading extracellular ATP with apyrase reduces inflammation in colitis models, and enzyme-tethered hydrogels that generate adenosine (CD73 or CD39/CD73) have been validated for local tissue protection in ischemic limbs and heart, suggesting a modular platform for focal purinergic control. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4703960/?utm_source=openai))

Atomic insight (single strategy)
Convert stress-elevated extracellular ATP at the gastric surface into adenosine in situ to flip signaling from injurious P2X7-dominant to pro-resolving A2A/A2B-dominant states—using the stress signal (ATP surge) as the substrate-gated trigger for protection.

Hypothesis–question
If we bias purinergic tone toward adenosine at the gastric mucosal interface only when ATP spikes occur, can we re-establish microclimate pH, tighten junctions, and sustain restitution without CNS/systemic modulation—and do so repeatedly during chronic stress exposures? ([journals.physiology.org](https://journals.physiology.org/doi/full/10.1152/ajpcell.00102.2004?utm_source=openai))

Specific aims
1) Map stress-triggered ATP/adenosine dynamics and receptor activation at the gastric surface.
2) Engineer a mucoadhesive, gastric-retentive ectonucleotidase platform that converts ATP→AMP→adenosine at the mucosal interface and functions across repeated stress cycles.
3) Test local efficacy and autonomy (with minimal systemic exposure) in chronic stress–induced gastritis models.

Approach

Aim 1: Define purinergic failure modes under stress
- Model systems: human gastric epithelial monolayers and organoids; rat gastric mucosa ex vivo; in vivo rodent restraint/cold-stress gastritis.
- Readouts:
  - ATP microdomain kinetics by surface-tethered luciferase; adenosine by enzyme-coupled electrochemical probes.
  - Receptor-state biomarkers: P2X7 pore formation/caspase-1 activation; A2A/A2B downstream cAMP/PKA-VASP phosphorylation; tight junction integrity (TEER; ZO-1/occludin localization).
  - Barrier function: juxtamucosal pH microelectrodes; fluorescein permeability; laser-Doppler mucosal blood flow.
- Mechanistic tests: acute ATP scavenging (soluble apyrase) and A2A/A2B agonism to confirm that ATP depletion and adenosine signaling rescue barrier parameters under stress challenges. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8721002/?utm_source=openai))

Aim 2: Build a substrate-gated, repeatable mucosal adenosine generator
- Construct: gastric-mucoadhesive hydrogel/nanosheet (e.g., catechol-modified chitosan or PEG-4MAL) with immobilized CD39 and CD73 at controlled densities; optional protease-shields for luminal stability; designed to operate at surface pH ~6–7 within the mucus layer. ([journals.physiology.org](https://journals.physiology.org/doi/full/10.1152/ajpcell.00102.2004?utm_source=openai))
- Performance criteria:
  - Kinetics: Michaelis–Menten parameters in mucus simulant; ability to depress ATP transients (μM–mM) and raise adenosine locally.
  - Function under gastric conditions: activity at surface pH; shear and acid exposure in bioreactor simulating antral peristalsis; adhesion strength to gastric mucus.
  - On-demand behavior and repeatability: cycling experiments with intermittent ATP pulses and acid exposure to demonstrate reversible, substrate-limited activation without drift in baseline purine levels.
  - Containment: negligible systemic adenosine rise; stability over 6–12 h gastric residence.
- Benchmarks: compare to soluble enzymes and to CD73-only gels (to test rate-limiting steps). ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8159890/?utm_source=openai))

Aim 3: Demonstrate local protection and autonomy in vivo
- Design: gastric-localized dosing (oral gel that adheres to corpus/antrum); repeat dosing across days of stress exposure.
- Endpoints:
  - Primary: lesion area/severity; juxtamucosal pH recovery; microvascular flow; epithelial restitution rate at micro-wounds.
  - Mechanistic: mucosal ATP/adenosine ratios; suppressed P2X7 activation; enhanced A2A/A2B signaling; cytokine profile shift; maintained tight junctions.
  - Autonomy and safety: no change in CNS behavior; minimal plasma adenosine; no hypotension/bradycardia; normal gastric emptying.
- Controls: vehicle gel; inactive enzyme gel; systemic A2A agonist positive control to benchmark efficacy but contrast systemic exposure. ([journals.physiology.org](https://journals.physiology.org/doi/full/10.1152/ajpcell.00102.2004?utm_source=openai))

Key predictions and falsification
- Prediction: stress challenges create reproducible ATP spikes at the mucosal surface that temporally precede barrier failure; local ATP→adenosine conversion prevents P2X7 engagement, preserves near-neutral juxtamucosal pH, boosts mucosal perfusion, and accelerates restitution. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8721002/?utm_source=openai))
- Falsification: if ATP spikes are absent or conversion fails to shift receptor signaling (P2X7 unchanged; A2A/A2B not engaged), barrier metrics will not improve despite enzyme presence.

Innovation relative to current care
- Converts the stress signal itself (extracellular ATP) into the protective effector (adenosine), creating a closed-loop, local shield rather than upstream CNS modulation or global antisecretory therapy. No existing gastric therapy uses on-demand ectonucleotidase catalysis at the mucosal interface; enzyme-tethered purinergic hydrogels are validated in other tissues and are repurposed here for gastric mucosa. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8159890/?utm_source=openai))

Feasibility and risk management
- Enzyme activity at the gastric surface is supported by the established neutral microclimate within the mucus layer; immobilization improves localization and stability. If enzyme stability limits performance, replace with modRNA delivery to transiently express CD39/CD73 in surface cells using a mucoadhesive depot. Monitor for undesirable effects on acid secretion; tune dosing window and enzyme ratio to favor barrier protection without hypersecretion. ([journals.physiology.org](https://journals.physiology.org/doi/full/10.1152/ajpcell.00102.2004?utm_source=openai))

Milestones
- Year 1: establish ATP/adenosine maps and receptor-state biomarkers; demonstrate in vitro rescue with soluble enzymes.
- Year 2: finalize mucoadhesive ectonucleotidase construct; show repeatable, on-demand ATP suppression and adenosine generation under simulated gastric conditions.
- Year 3: show in vivo efficacy and autonomy with repeated dosing; confirm safety and negligible systemic exposure; down-select for translational formulation.

Impact
A substrate-gated, mucosa-local purinergic switch could prevent and treat stress-induced gastritis by restoring the stomach’s own surface defenses with repeatable, brain-independent control—generalizable to other mucosal injuries where extracellular ATP drives inflammation. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4405224/?utm_source=openai))
