text:
Title
Thermostat Transfer via Push–Pull Referencing and NEAT Overflow: A closed-loop melanocortin–orexin circuit to normalize adiposity in humans.

Background and rationale
Body-fat signals (leptin, insulin) modulate antagonistic arcuate nucleus populations (AgRP/NPY vs POMC/CART). Falling leptin evokes strong, multi-axis defense of weight loss; sustained high leptin weakly defends against gain, consistent with an asymmetric, low-leptin–sensitive control and acquired leptin resistance. Melanocortin (MC4R) outputs suppress appetite and increase sympathetic outflow/thermogenesis, while circuit plasticity in ARC contributes to “defended” adiposity. These features are conserved in rodents and humans. ([journals.physiology.org](https://journals.physiology.org/doi/full/10.1152/physrev.00028.2020?utm_source=openai))

Obesity-resistant phenotypes often display higher spontaneous activity (NEAT) when overfed; in humans, overfeeding-induced variation in NEAT predicts fat gain, while orexin signaling scales arousal/locomotion and links surplus to activity. Thus, a “behavioral overflow” path can dissipate surplus without relying solely on autonomic thermogenesis. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/9880251/?utm_source=openai))

Central melanocortin signaling regulates peripheral lipid handling and sympathetic tone; in humans, intranasal MC4R agonism acutely increases subcutaneous WAT lipolysis and muscle sympathetic nerve activity. Leptin–hypothalamus–SNS pathways increase skeletal-muscle fatty-acid oxidation via AMPK, and microvascular recruitment enhances nutrient uptake in high-turnover tissues. These mechanisms together support active routing of substrates away from storage. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21629206/?utm_source=openai))

Clinical tools now exist that engage these nodes: MC4R agonist setmelanotide (approved in MC4R-pathway genetic obesity) reduces hunger and can increase energy expenditure; selective orexin-2 receptor (OX2R) agonists (e.g., danavorexton/TAK-925; oveporexton/TAK-861) promote wakefulness with emerging human safety data—thus feasible levers for a translational, closed-loop “thermostat” that copies motifs from naturally lean individuals. ([fda.gov](https://www.fda.gov/drugs/news-events-human-drugs/fda-approves-first-treatment-weight-management-people-certain-rare-genetic-conditions?utm_source=openai))

Hypothesis–question (inseparable)
Can a personalized push–pull adiposity reference, coupled to an “overflow-to-NEAT” switch and melanocortin tone, automatically normalize body fat by simultaneously reducing appetite, increasing energy expenditure, and shunting nutrients toward oxidation whenever current adiposity signals exceed an individualized healthy reference?

Atomic strategy
Implement a minimal two-timescale, push–pull integrator of leptin/insulin (short-term vs long-term averages) that, when the short-term composite exceeds the long-term baseline, triggers paired, low-intensity central outputs: (a) MC4R agonism to impose satiety and bias lipid mobilization/oxidation; (b) OX2R agonism to raise arousal and NEAT, converting surplus into movement. This single-threshold, dual-output actuation mimics the obesity-resistant “permission to lose fat” circuit and leverages established melanocortin and orexin biology. ([journals.physiology.org](https://journals.physiology.org/doi/full/10.1152/physrev.00028.2020?utm_source=openai))

Specific aims
- Aim 1: Derive and validate an individualized adiposity reference. Over 6 weeks, obtain daily dried-blood-spot leptin and fasting insulin to compute an exponentially weighted moving average (EWMA, τlong≈30 days) and a short-term average (τshort≈24–72 h). Define surplus when (leptin × normalized insulin)short − (leptin × normalized insulin)long > θ (personalized). Test that this surplus metric correlates with transient fat balance (respiratory quotient shifts, postprandial TG area under curve). ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2990627/?utm_source=openai))
- Aim 2: Test the NEAT overflow switch. In a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, crossover study, deliver short-acting OX2R agonist microdoses only on surplus days and quantify changes in NEAT (triaxial accelerometry, posture allocation), total 24-h EE (indirect calorimetry and doubly labeled water), and sleep metrics. Primary endpoint: surplus-triggered increase in NEAT energy >10% vs yoked, time-matched placebo days. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36934366/?utm_source=openai))
- Aim 3: Test melanocortin gating of appetite and partitioning. Concurrent with Aim 2 triggers, deliver low-dose MC4R agonism (setmelanotide SC microdose or intranasal MSH/ACTH(4–10)) and measure ad libitum intake, subcutaneous WAT glycerol release (microdialysis), and muscle microvascular recruitment (contrast-enhanced ultrasound) during mixed-meal tests. Primary endpoints: reduction in ad libitum energy intake (≥15%) and increased WAT lipolysis and muscle perfusion vs yoked placebo. ([dailymed.nlm.nih.gov](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/search.cfm?labeltype=all&query=SETMELANOTIDE&utm_source=openai))
- Aim 4: Integrate into a 12-week closed-loop trial. Compare three conditions in randomized blocks: (i) closed-loop paired triggers (MC4R+OX2R on surplus), (ii) single-channel triggers (MC4R-only or OX2R-only), (iii) yoked open-loop placebo. Primary outcome: change in DXA fat mass; secondary outcomes: hunger ratings, 24-h EE, RER, TG clearance, and safety.

Design and methods
- Participants: 60 adults, BMI 30–40 kg/m2, without narcolepsy or major cardiovascular disease. Power is set to detect 3% fat-mass difference at 12 weeks with 80% power.
- Sensing: Daily home finger-stick dried-blood spots for leptin/insulin; CGM for glycemic context; wearable accelerometry; weekly indirect calorimetry; doubly labeled water at baseline and week 12.
- Actuation:
  - MC4R module: setmelanotide SC microdose (label-informed safety monitoring) or intranasal MSH/ACTH(4–10) on surplus days; titrated to minimize side effects while achieving satiety/lipolytic signals. ([accessdata.fda.gov](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2024/213793s007lbl.pdf?utm_source=openai))
  - NEAT module: OX2R agonist (e.g., danavorexton/oveporexton) administered mid-morning on surplus days to avoid sleep disruption; evaluate BP/HR continuously for 6 h post-dose. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36934366/?utm_source=openai))
- Mechanistic readouts: subcutaneous WAT microdialysis (glycerol), muscle CEUS perfusion index, mixed-meal RER, oral fat-tolerance TG AUC, and optional microneurography in a substudy to index MSNA. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3335901/?utm_source=openai))
- Safety: Continuous ambulatory BP/HR on trigger days; pigment/skin monitoring and mood screens for MC4R agonist; sleep diaries and actigraphy for OX2R agonist. ([accessdata.fda.gov](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2024/213793s007lbl.pdf?utm_source=openai))

Predicted causal chain (testable)
- Surplus detection above the long-term baseline engages MC4R and OX2R. MC4R output imposes satiety and increases sympathetic drive to BAT/WAT, shifting partitioning and promoting lipolysis; OX2R output elevates arousal/locomotor drive, scaling NEAT. Together they lower effective energy intake and increase expenditure; concurrent SNS and microvascular actions bias substrate delivery/oxidation in muscle/BAT, limiting re-esterification. Net result: automatic fat-mass normalization back toward the personalized baseline. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5244821/?utm_source=openai))

Endpoints and success criteria
- Primary mechanistic success (Aims 2–3): on surplus-trigger days vs yoked placebo, observe (i) ≥10% increase in NEAT EE and ≥15% reduction in ad libitum intake; (ii) increased WAT glycerol and muscle perfusion; (iii) left-shifted RER. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/9880251/?utm_source=openai))
- Primary clinical success (Aim 4): closed-loop paired triggers reduce DXA fat mass by ≥5% vs open-loop placebo over 12 weeks, with preserved resting EE.
- Secondary: improved TG clearance; reduced hunger ratings; acceptable safety.

Novelty and impact
- Novel “thermostat transfer”: a two-timescale push–pull reference that copies obesity-resistant set-point computation and actuates orthogonal outputs only when adiposity is above one’s own baseline. Prior work documents the biology (asymmetry, melanocortin, orexin, NEAT variability) but not a personalized, closed-loop pairing of MC4R and OX2R to enforce satiety plus behavioral overflow as a single decision. ([journals.physiology.org](https://journals.physiology.org/doi/full/10.1152/physrev.00028.2020?utm_source=openai))
- Translational tractability: uses existing or near-clinical agents (setmelanotide; OX2R agonists) and standard sensors/biomarkers, enabling rapid movement to Phase 2 if signal is confirmed. ([fda.gov](https://www.fda.gov/drugs/news-events-human-drugs/fda-approves-first-treatment-weight-management-people-certain-rare-genetic-conditions?utm_source=openai))

Risk management
- OX2R agonists can elevate arousal and affect BP/HR; mitigate via morning dosing, dose titration, ambulatory monitoring, exclusion of hypertension. ([cdn.clinicaltrials.gov](https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/12/NCT05022212/Prot_SAP_000.pdf?utm_source=openai))
- MC4R agonists carry pigmentation and mood warnings; use microdoses, dermatologic/mood monitoring, predefined stop rules. ([accessdata.fda.gov](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2024/213793s007lbl.pdf?utm_source=openai))

Milestones
- Year 1: Biomarker calibration and algorithm finalization (Aim 1).
- Year 2: Acute crossover studies (Aims 2–3), go/no-go on predefined mechanistic thresholds.
- Year 3: 12-week closed-loop randomized trial (Aim 4); if successful, proceed to multi-center Phase 2.

Clinical translation vision
Integration into a compact home system: automated leptin/insulin sampling (capillary micro-sampler), cloud EWMA computation, and on-demand paired micro-dosing of MC4R/OX2R agents. The single-threshold, dual-output actuation satisfies the requirement for automatic sensing, parallel modulation of appetite, energy expenditure (NEAT), and nutrient partitioning, reproducing the “permission to lose fat” logic found in naturally lean individuals. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21629206/?utm_source=openai))

text:
Title
An implantable “mechanical adipostat” that enforces an upper adiposity limit via Piezo1-gated secretion of anorectic and repartitioning hormones

Background and gap
- Adipose expansion is a mechanical as well as endocrine event; mature adipocytes and adipose stroma experience sustained tensile/compressive loads as depots enlarge. Piezo1 is expressed in mature adipocytes and transduces stretch into Ca2+ signals that influence adipocyte programs, including FGF1 signaling and diet-induced adaptations. Yet this native mechanosensing has not been harnessed as a closed-loop therapeutic actuator. ([annualreviews.org](https://www.annualreviews.org/docserver/fulltext/physiol/84/1/annurev-physiol-060721-100935.pdf?accname=guest&checksum=3DEABDE76FE36AA91E5F38EA4E4EDA26&expires=1780188650&id=id&utm_source=openai))
- Energy intake can be reduced pharmacologically (GLP-1 receptor agonists; amylin analogs) and energy expenditure and lipid handling can be modulated hormonally (FGF21; ANGPTL4 controls LPL to divert triglyceride clearance away from adipose during fasting). No existing therapy uses depot strain itself to trigger a proportional, self-extinguishing tri-axis response. ([diabetesjournals.org](https://diabetesjournals.org/care/article/48/2/292/157724/Efficacy-of-GLP-1-Receptor-Agonists-on-Weight-Loss?utm_source=openai))

Unified hypothesis (question indistinguishable)
If sustained mechanical strain in subcutaneous white adipose tissue (sWAT) marks pathologic overshoot of body-fat mass relative to a healthy set point, then a Piezo1-gated, strain-thresholded implant that secretes (i) an anorectic peptide, (ii) an EE-promoting hepatokine, and (iii) a local LPL brake will automatically and reversibly normalize appetite, energy expenditure, and nutrient partitioning. How much strain-time integral above threshold is required, and what output gains per axis, to implement a clinically safe, individualized “upper adiposity limit” in humans?

Atomic strategy
Reinterpret sWAT mechanical strain as the primary adiposity error signal and couple it, via Piezo1-Ca2+ duty cycle with a built-in low-pass time filter, to proportional secretion of a minimal, clinically validated polyhormone program that extinguishes as strain remits.

Design overview
- Sensor: Autologous or universal donor human adipose stromal cells (hASCs) engineered to express a Piezo1 variant with tuned activation/inactivation (quantified half-activation tension) and a Ca2+→calcineurin/NFAT transcriptional relay. Cells are immobilized in an immunoprotective, ECM-anchoring hydrogel sheet sutured onto sWAT. The construct experiences the same depot-level strains as the host tissue; sustained strain elevates Ca2+ pulse duty cycle and NFAT target expression. ([annualreviews.org](https://www.annualreviews.org/docserver/fulltext/physiol/84/1/annurev-physiol-060721-100935.pdf?accname=guest&checksum=3DEABDE76FE36AA91E5F38EA4E4EDA26&expires=1780188650&id=id&utm_source=openai))
- Actuators (single polycistron with stoichiometric tuning):
  1) Appetite suppression: secreted GLP-1 analog or amylin analog cassette (clinically validated reduction in energy intake/weight). ([diabetesjournals.org](https://diabetesjournals.org/care/article/48/2/292/157724/Efficacy-of-GLP-1-Receptor-Agonists-on-Weight-Loss?utm_source=openai))
  2) Energy expenditure: secreted FGF21 (human data support links to cold-induced thermogenesis and adipose browning; clinical analogs improve metabolic profiles). ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3537100/?utm_source=openai))
  3) Nutrient partitioning: low-level ANGPTL4 secretion targeted to the juxtaposed depot endothelium to transiently reduce local LPL when strain is high, diverting postprandial triglyceride clearance away from overfilled sWAT. Output ceiling and spatial confinement limit systemic TG excursions. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8666355/?utm_source=openai))
- Dynamics: A transcriptional integrator (NFAT-driven promoter with slow deactivation and protein-level degradation tags) implements a strain-time requirement; as depot strain and intracellular acyl-lipid load fall, Ca2+ duty cycle drops, transcription wanes, and hormone levels decay—automatically scaling feedback to residual error (no external control).

Specific aims

Aim 1. Quantify mechano-thresholding and time-integration needed for safe activation.
- Build Piezo1-NFAT reporter hASCs; plate in tunable-stiffness 3D matrices and apply calibrated biaxial stretch/wrinkling to emulate sWAT strain. Measure Ca2+ duty cycle, NFAT activity, and output kinetics versus tension and duration. Define strain set points that ignore meal-scale transients but respond to sustained overfill. ([annualreviews.org](https://www.annualreviews.org/docserver/fulltext/physiol/84/1/annurev-physiol-060721-100935.pdf?accname=guest&checksum=3DEABDE76FE36AA91E5F38EA4E4EDA26&expires=1780188650&id=id&utm_source=openai))
- Success criterion: τactivation ≥ 6–12 h at ≥ physiologic strain for 10–20% depot overfill; τdeactivation ≤ 24–48 h as strain normalizes.

Aim 2. Build and tune the tri-axis actuator cassette for proportional, reversible control.
- Construct a single NFAT-responsive polycistron encoding: (GLP-1 analog or amylin analog), FGF21, and ANGPTL4 with orthogonal secretion signals and adjustable Kozak/promoter strengths. Map strain→dose curves in vitro and in sWAT-on-a-chip microphysiologic systems with human endothelium to quantify local LPL inhibition and TG flux redirection. ([diabetesjournals.org](https://diabetesjournals.org/care/article/48/2/292/157724/Efficacy-of-GLP-1-Receptor-Agonists-on-Weight-Loss?utm_source=openai))
- Success criterion: Each axis achieves preset half-maximal effect at a common NFAT activity level; ANGPTL4 produces ≥30% reduction in local LPL with ≤20% rise in bulk media TG.

Aim 3. Demonstrate closed-loop adiposity control and automatic shutoff in vivo.
- Implant encapsulated mechano-hormone sheets onto sWAT in diet-induced obese humanized mice or minipigs. Challenge with overfeeding to elevate depot strain. Endpoints:
  - Intake: continuous monitoring; expected reduction under activation. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5573908/?utm_source=openai))
  - EE/thermogenesis: indirect calorimetry; thermal imaging or 18F-FDG PET of BAT; circulating FGF21. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3537100/?utm_source=openai))
  - Partitioning: tracer-labeled TG clearance to sWAT vs oxidative tissues; endothelial LPL activity near implant; plasma TG safety. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6779329/?utm_source=openai))
  - Dynamics: activation hysteresis, on/off half-times, stability across weight cycles.
- Success criterion: When fat mass exceeds set point by pre-specified percentage, the system lowers food intake ≥15%, raises 24-h EE ≥5%, and reduces sWAT TG uptake ≥25%; outputs subside to baseline as weights return to set point, with no sustained hypertriglyceridemia or hypophagia.

Aim 4. Translation engineering and safety.
- Manufacturability: GMP hASC lines, hydrogel sheets compatible with laparoscopic placement/removal; potency lot-release via stretch bioassay.
- Safety gates: encode kill-switch (iCasp9); cap maximal ANGPTL4 using PEST tags and miRNA target sites to prevent hepatic spillover; monitor TGs, pancreatic enzymes, gallbladder and heart rate.
- Comparator: pharmacologic GLP-1RA ± amylin ± FGF21 analogs alone to test whether mechanical gating improves efficacy, durability, and safety at lower average exposures. ([diabetesjournals.org](https://diabetesjournals.org/care/article/48/2/292/157724/Efficacy-of-GLP-1-Receptor-Agonists-on-Weight-Loss?utm_source=openai))

Key measurements and analyses
- Mechanics: depot strain mapping by MRI-based elastography and ultrasound elastography against implant Ca2+ telemetry.
- Intake and EE: CLAMS; doubly labeled water in large animals.
- Lipid flux: compartmental modeling of tracer kinetics to quantify LPL-controlled partitioning changes. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6779329/?utm_source=openai))
- Statistics: predefined superiority margins for closed-loop condition vs pharmacologic open-loop controls; mixed-effects models for repeated measures; Bayesian posterior for individual set-point estimates.

Risk assessment and mitigations
- Hypertriglyceridemia from ANGPTL4: mitigate with local delivery geometry, low expression ceiling, and automatic decay; stop-rule on TG thresholds. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8666355/?utm_source=openai))
- Over-suppression of intake: choose amylin or GLP-1 analog with short systemic half-life from the implant; removal-ready device; monitor lean mass. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17505051/?utm_source=openai))
- Insufficient EE gain: if FGF21 effect size is inadequate, adjust weighting toward intake and partitioning; preserve atomic strategy (mechanical gating), not pathway proliferation. ([annualreviews.org](https://www.annualreviews.org/docserver/fulltext/pharmtox/63/1/annurev-pharmtox-032322-093904.pdf?accname=guest&checksum=A2C143968B11F9210F928784AB17740F&expires=1778229704&id=id&utm_source=openai))

Milestones
- Year 1: Define strain thresholds and integrator kinetics; finalize actuator stoichiometry.
- Year 2: Show closed-loop control and automatic shutoff in small animal; establish safety windows.
- Year 3: Scale to minipig with human-scale sheets; submit IDE-enabling package (device removability, manufacturing, toxicology).

Innovation
- Converts depot strain—a slow, adiposity-specific variable—into a master control signal for tri-axis metabolic correction, using only validated hormonal actuators and intrinsic shutoff as the error shrinks. To our knowledge, no prior implant senses adipose strain via Piezo1 to enforce an individualized upper adiposity limit. ([annualreviews.org](https://www.annualreviews.org/docserver/fulltext/physiol/84/1/annurev-physiol-060721-100935.pdf?accname=guest&checksum=3DEABDE76FE36AA91E5F38EA4E4EDA26&expires=1780188650&id=id&utm_source=openai))

Expected impact
A removable, programmable, closed-loop adipostat that complements or reduces doses of current incretin/amylin/FGF21 drugs, restores symmetry in weight defense, and individualizes the upper limit of healthy adiposity based on a physical property of fat depots.

Title
Adipocyte fullness-to-therapy: a stoichiometric lipid-droplet sink switch that turns on appetite suppression, thermogenesis, and nutrient repartitioning only when fat cells are overfilled

Central hypothesis and question
Hypothesis-question (indivisible): Can mature human adipocytes be endowed with a single, intrinsic “fullness brake” by exploiting lipid-droplet surface area as a stoichiometric sink that, once a geometric setpoint is exceeded, abruptly derepresses a compact polycistronic program to 1) suppress appetite, 2) increase white-fat thermogenesis, and 3) repartition nutrients away from storage—and does this autonomous adipocyte circuit reset as adipocytes shrink? The underlying premise is that adipocyte hypertrophy produces a massive increase in a unilocular lipid-droplet (LD) surface juxtaposed to a thin cytoplasmic rim with enhanced organelle contacts; LDs selectively recruit amphipathic-helix proteins to their phospholipid monolayer, and these biophysical features can be harnessed to create a ligand-free, geometry-tuned setpoint for gene control. ([rupress.org](https://rupress.org/jcb/article/208/5/501/54544/The-cell-biology-of-fat-expansionThe-cell-biology?utm_source=openai))

Atomic strategy
Convert LD surface growth into depletion of a limiting, engineered corepressor that is required to assemble a nuclear repressor. As LD area expands, an LD-anchored sink titrates the corepressor below the repressor’s dissociation threshold, causing an ultrasensitive collapse of repression and coordinated activation of a therapeutic polycistron. Amphipathic helices provide selective LD partitioning, and stoichiometric sequestration confers an intrinsic threshold and steep input–output slope. No exogenous drugs or brain-derived signals are required; the pathology (adipocyte hypertrophy) is the input. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5764114/?utm_source=openai))

Background and novelty check (concise)
- LD geometry and organelle proximity scale with adipocyte hypertrophy; LDs can exceed 100 µm with cytoplasm compressed to a rim and frequent ER/mitochondria contacts. ([rupress.org](https://rupress.org/jcb/article/208/5/501/54544/The-cell-biology-of-fat-expansionThe-cell-biology?utm_source=openai))
- Amphipathic-helix proteins selectively insert into LD monolayers via packing defects; LD targeting does not require dedicated import machinery. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5764114/?utm_source=openai))
- Protein sequestration is a proven route to ultrasensitive thresholds in gene circuits. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2694680/?utm_source=openai))
- Prior obesity “closed-loop” gene circuits sensed circulating fatty acids with engineered nuclear receptors in implanted non-adipocyte cells; adipocyte-autonomous LD-surface–titration to drive multi-axis outputs was not found. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/ncomms3825))
- Adipose-targeted AAV capsids (e.g., Rec2, V7) and adipocyte promoters enable in vivo translation. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11467673/?utm_source=openai))
- Secretion-enabled GLP-1 gene therapies via signal peptide and furin-cleavable designs show systemic efficacy from non-enteroendocrine tissues, supporting feasibility of adipocyte secretion. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2940489/?utm_source=openai))
- Inducing UCP1 in white adipose increases energy expenditure in vivo. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4967236/?utm_source=openai))
- Adiponectin gene therapy improves insulin sensitivity and systemic metabolism, aligning with nutrient repartitioning. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3461354/?utm_source=openai))

Design overview
- Sensor (single variable: LD surface area): a soluble corepressor Cofactor-C fused to an LD-targeting amphipathic helix (e.g., humanized ALPS/PLIN-derived AH) that partitions onto the LD monolayer in proportion to available LD surface. As LD area increases, the nuclear/cytosolic pool of free Cofactor-C is depleted.
- Actuator: a bipartite repressor R that requires Cofactor-C to form a high-affinity DNA-bound complex (R:C). R carries a human DNA-binding domain and a human KRAB-like repression module; without C, R has low DNA affinity/stability and fails to repress.
- Output: a single promoter controlling a humanized, P2A-linked polycistron encoding:
  1) a secretion-enabled, DPP4-resistant GLP-1 receptor agonist (signal peptide + furin site + GLP-1(7–37/A8G) or exendin-4 variant), to suppress appetite centrally,
  2) UCP1 to increase white-fat thermogenesis,
  3) adiponectin to improve systemic insulin sensitivity and promote fatty-acid oxidation in liver/muscle.
- Tissue restriction: adipocyte-specific mini-Adipoq or mini-aP2 promoter for R and C.
- Delivery: adipose-tropic AAV capsid (e.g., Rec2 or V7) with miR-122/miR-1 target sites to de-target liver/heart. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11467673/?utm_source=openai))

Predicted behavior
- Lean state (small LD area): free Cofactor-C exceeds R:C Kd → strong repression → outputs OFF.
- Hypertrophy (LD area crosses setpoint): LD sink lowers free Cofactor-C below threshold → repression collapses → outputs ON; GLP-1 reduces intake; UCP1 raises expenditure; adiponectin biases nutrient flux away from storage.
- As adipocytes shrink, LD area and sink capacity fall → free Cofactor-C rises → repression re-forms → outputs return to baseline (closed-loop homeostasis).

Specific aims

Aim 1. Build and calibrate the LD-surface stoichiometric sink switch in mature human adipocytes.
- System: Primary human preadipocytes differentiated to mature adipocytes; OA/PA loading to expand LDs across physiological sizes; live-cell LD imaging and morphometrics.
- Constructs:
  - R: human DBD (e.g., ZF array) + KRAB; low intrinsic DNA affinity unless dimerized with C.
  - Cofactor-C: humanized heterodimer partner of R (engineered coiled-coil) ± nuclear export tag; N-terminus fused to validated LD-targeting AH.
  - Reporter: R-responsive minimal promoter driving Nluc-PEST.
- Quantification:
  - Map LD surface area vs. reporter activation; estimate effective setpoint and Hill slope; test reversibility by β-adrenergic lipolysis and FA withdrawal.
  - Controls: AH-deficient Cofactor-C; nucleus-restricted Cofactor-C; off-target organelle anchors.
- Success criteria: >15-fold dynamic range; steepness (Hill n≥3); reversible OFF→ON→OFF over repeated lipid loading/unloading. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5764114/?utm_source=openai))

Aim 2. Replace the reporter with a compact three-axis therapeutic polycistron and validate function in vitro.
- Output cassette (single ORF, P2A-linked): SP–furin–GLP‑1RA variant; UCP1; adiponectin.
- Tests:
  - Appetite axis: quantify GLP‑1RA secretion (ELISA); DPP4 stability; activity in GLP‑1R reporter cells.
  - Thermogenesis: mitochondrial respiration and proton leak (Seahorse) after UCP1 induction; UCP1 protein.
  - Repartitioning: adiponectin secretion; conditioned-media effects on hepatocyte and myotube FAO gene programs.
  - Circuit integrity: LD-size dependence of the full cassette ON state; leak in lean-size cells.
- Success criteria: GLP-1RA secretion sufficient to activate GLP‑1R reporter; ≥2× increase in proton leak/OCR with UCP1; ≥1.5× increase in adiponectin; preserved thresholding. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2940489/?utm_source=openai))

Aim 3. In vivo proof-of-concept: autonomous body-fat–linked control of intake, expenditure, and partitioning.
- Vectors: Adipocyte-specific R/C cassettes and therapeutic cassette packaged in adipose-tropic capsids (Rec2 or V7); include liver/heart de-targeting miR sites.
- Models: Diet-induced obese (DIO) C57BL/6J mice; lean controls.
- Protocol:
  - Dose-ranging tail-vein AAV; confirm depot transduction by reporter pre-runs.
  - Endpoints over 12 weeks: food intake; indirect calorimetry (EE, RER); core temperature; body composition (MRI); depot histology; plasma GLP‑1 and adiponectin; WAT UCP1.
  - Mechanistic link: within-depot single-cell analyses correlating LD area with reporter/effector induction; reversibility during weight loss phase.
  - Safety: glucose homeostasis; GI adverse signs; liver enzymes; off-target transgene by ddPCR; anti-capsid immunity.
- Go/no-go: ≥10% reduction in ad libitum intake; ≥10% increase in EE; ≥15% fat-mass reduction without lean-mass loss; reversal of phenotypes after weight normalization. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11467673/?utm_source=openai))

Key design choices and justifications
- Why LD-surface titration: LD monolayers recruit amphipathic helices in proportion to available surface; using Cofactor-C as a finite pool implements an area-coupled setpoint. This is orthogonal to ligand-PPAR sensing and to our knowledge has not been applied to adipocyte-autonomous therapy control. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5764114/?utm_source=openai))
- Why stoichiometric ultrasensitivity: sequestration yields sharp thresholds with minimal parts; setpoint tunable via Cofactor-C expression/affinity. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2694680/?utm_source=openai))
- Outputs chosen for clinical plausibility:
  - GLP‑1RA: secretion-enabled GLP‑1/Ex4 constructs are validated for durable systemic delivery via gene therapy. Appetite suppression is potent and clinically proven. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2940489/?utm_source=openai))
  - UCP1: white-fat UCP1 induction increases EE and combats obesity in vivo. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4967236/?utm_source=openai))
  - Adiponectin: endocrine signal that improves insulin sensitivity and lipid handling; gene therapy evidence in mice. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3461354/?utm_source=openai))
- Humanization and delivery: human protein domains and adipocyte promoters minimize immunogenicity; adipose-tropic AAV capsids enable multi-depot targeting with reduced liver transduction. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11467673/?utm_source=openai))

Milestones, risks, and mitigations
- Potential leak at lean sizes: increase operator number; strengthen R:C affinity window; add weak condensate-forming IDRs to the LD sink to sharpen thresholds (optional).
- Excess GLP‑1RA exposure: dose vector; cap cassette with a 3′ UTR ribozyme for auto-titration; alternatively swap GLP‑1RA for low-dose GDF15 variant with known anorexigenic efficacy if needed. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28846097/?utm_source=openai))
- UCP1 overactivation risk: cap UCP1 with a degron responsive to reduced lipid load to accelerate OFF kinetics upon weight loss.

Readouts and success criteria
- Biophysical: LD area vs. transcriptional state curve with reversible hysteresis band appropriate to physiological weight cycling.
- Functional: closed-loop normalization—when fat mass exceeds a preset threshold, intake drops, EE rises, and systemic insulin sensitivity improves; when fat normalizes, circuit silences and metrics revert toward baseline without oscillation.

Translational path
- Vector engineering: finalize humanized sequences; manufacture adipose-tropic capsids (e.g., V7/Rec2) under GMP; biodistribution in NHPs.
- Safety pharmacology: GLP‑1RA exposure margins; immunogenicity; off-target profiling.
- Patient selection and endpoint strategy: adults with BMI ≥30 kg/m² and elevated visceral fat fraction; primary endpoint—percent body-weight reduction with preservation of lean mass; key secondary endpoints—HbA1c, HOMA-IR, hepatic fat by MRI-PDFF.

If successful, this work establishes a first-in-class, drug-free, adipocyte-autonomous homeostat that translates a physical hallmark of obesity—LD surface expansion—into coordinated, reversible control of appetite, thermogenesis, and nutrient partitioning.

Title
Lipid bilayer–stress-gated endocrine sentinel to preempt adipose overflow and restore homeostasis

Central hypothesis and integrated research question
Hypothesis/question: Can membrane lipid bilayer stress—an early, systems-level signature of adipose “overflow” and lipotoxicity—be converted into a single, ultrasensitive trigger that, once a personalized set point is exceeded, automatically coordinates appetite suppression, increased energy expenditure, and nutrient partitioning away from fat storage to normalize whole-body energy balance? Bilayer stress in ER membranes is directly induced by saturated lipid load and membrane packing defects and is sensed by UPR transducers (IRE1/PERK) independent of unfolded proteins; this occurs in obesity and high-fat feeding and precedes overt end-organ injury. If we harness this state change as the universal “overflow” cue and route it into a tri-axial endocrine response, we can correct the asymmetry wherein lipid spillover and insulin resistance do not naturally suppress appetite or raise expenditure. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3606975/?utm_source=openai))

Atomic strategy
Reframe “excess fat” as “pathologic membrane lipid saturation.” Build a single-input, multi-output gate in a retrievable, peripherally implanted cell therapy that: (1) detects sustained ER bilayer stress; (2) splits that signal with graded thresholds to drive three endocrine outputs—early partitioning/oxidation, then thermogenesis, then anorexia; (3) shuts off automatically when stress resolves.

Design overview
Platform: Encapsulated, retrievable human cells (clinical-grade hydrogel macroencapsulation) implanted subcutaneously. Encapsulation ensures immune isolation, dosing by cell number, and removal if adverse events arise; closed-loop, FA-responsive designer-cell implants for obesity provide direct precedent. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3868331/?utm_source=openai))

Sensor/gate: Human IRE1α-based lipid bilayer stress switch. Use a luminal-domain–truncated IRE1α (ΔLD-IRE1α) that is selectively activated by membrane lipid saturation to drive XBP1s-dependent transcription. This captures the physical-chemistry transition (increased saturation, PA/cholesterol shifts) that marks lipotoxicity, not normal fasting NEFA excursions. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3606975/?utm_source=openai))

Signal splitter: Three synthetic UPRE promoters with tuned affinity/architecture to impose ordered activation (high-affinity first, low-affinity last), implementing a competitive hub without crosstalk. Output hierarchy:
- P1 (highest affinity, lowest threshold): hepatokine FGF21 secretion—drives lipid oxidation and thermogenic programming, shifting nutrient use away from adipose storage and increasing EE. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26441838/?utm_source=openai))
- P2 (intermediate threshold): continued FGF21 plus booster of thermogenic/beiging program (e.g., co-expression of a UCP1 enhancer module via secreted agonism of β-Klotho/FGFR synapse), sustaining increased EE and fat oxidation. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26441838/?utm_source=openai))
- P3 (highest threshold): GDF15 secretion—potent, hindbrain-acting anorexigen that reduces food intake via GFRAL/RET, additive with GLP-1 mechanisms. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41574-021-00529-7?utm_source=openai))

Partitioning axis rationale: FGF21 promotes fatty-acid oxidation and thermogenic substrate use in BAT/beige adipose and muscle, diverting nutrients from storage toward oxidation; this satisfies the “nutrient partitioning away from fat storage” requirement while also increasing energy expenditure. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26441838/?utm_source=openai))

Failsafes: Small-molecule off-switch using IRE1 RNase inhibitors (4μ8C; KIRA6) to silence XBP1s signaling if adverse effects occur; device retrieval as definitive reversal. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3326519/?utm_source=openai))

Specific aims and workplan

Aim 1. Validate bilayer-stress sensing as an early, robust marker of adipose overflow and calibrate the set point.
- 1A. In vitro calibration: Expose ΔLD-IRE1α/UPRE-reporter cells to lipid mixes modeling physiologic NEFA flux vs lipotoxic states (e.g., palmitate-rich, cholesterol/PC:PE shifts). Quantify XBP1s activation kinetics, hysteresis, and discrimination versus unfolded-protein ER stressors. Expect selective activation by lipid saturation, consistent with IRE1’s TMD-based sensing. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3606975/?utm_source=openai))
- 1B. In vivo correlation: Implant neutral reporter devices into DIO mice; longitudinally correlate UPRE activity with adipose hypertrophy, plasma NEFA/DAG/ceramide, hepatic DAG/PKCε translocation, and insulin resistance indices to confirm that the sensor reports “overflow” antecedents of metabolic dysfunction. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3921899/?utm_source=openai))
Milestone: Define subject-specific set-point parameters (promoter strength, sensor expression) yielding on/off around the lipotoxic transition.

Aim 2. Build the graded tri-axial response and tune activation order.
- 2A. Construct three UPRE promoters with differing motif multiplicity/spacing to establish P1 < P2 < P3 activation thresholds under ΔLD-IRE1α control; validate ordering in vitro by lipid-titration series and single-cell reporters.
- 2B. Implement the effectors: P1/P2 drive secreted human FGF21 (± signal peptide optimization); P3 drives human GDF15. Verify secretion, bioactivity on target cells (β-Klotho/FGFR, GFRAL/RET assays), and additivity of EE and anorexia mechanisms. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26441838/?utm_source=openai))
- 2C. Closed-loop behavior: In adiposity-clamp mouse models, demonstrate autonomous entry into P1 then P2 with rising lipid stress, and addition of P3 only when stress persists—followed by de-escalation as stress normalizes.

Milestones: Ordered activation with <10% false positives during fasting/refeeding; return-to-baseline within 24–48 h after stress resolution.

Aim 3. Efficacy and safety in obese rodents and NHPs; translation parameters.
- 3A. Rodent efficacy: In DIO mice, quantify reductions in ad libitum intake (GDF15), increases in EE and BAT thermogenesis (indirect calorimetry, thermal imaging, UCP1), and re-partitioning metrics (respiratory exchange ratio, tracer lipid fate) under free-living feeding. Secondary endpoints: hepatic steatosis, insulin sensitivity. Expect multi-axis correction: lower intake via GFRAL, higher EE and oxidation via FGF21. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41574-021-00529-7?utm_source=openai))
- 3B. Lipid safety: Monitor plasma TG and lipoprotein profiles. If hypertriglyceridemia emerges during early P1, retune UPRE thresholds and FGF21 dose to increase oxidative clearance. (ANGPTL4 is reserved for future adipose-restricted versions due to systemic TG elevation risk.) ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8666355/?utm_source=openai))
- 3C. NHP feasibility: Scale device dose to lean mass; assess pharmacodynamic windows for FGF21 and GDF15; evaluate tolerability and reversibility using 4μ8C/KIRA6 if needed. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3326519/?utm_source=openai))

Novelty and feasibility
- Novelty: Prior obesity circuits used fatty-acid sensors to drive a single anorectic hormone (e.g., pramlintide); none, to our knowledge, convert lipid bilayer stress into a graded, multi-output endocrine program that simultaneously controls intake, EE, and partitioning. The sensor exploits a physical state transition (membrane saturation) known to mark obesity-linked lipotoxicity, not just FA concentration. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3868331/?utm_source=openai))
- Biological plausibility: IRE1 integrates lipid bilayer stress; XBP1s-responsive promoters are well-characterized; GDF15 and FGF21 are validated human-targetable axes for appetite and energy/fuel handling. Encapsulated designer cells with lipid-responsive control have reversed DIO in mice, supporting translational cell-therapy delivery. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1097276517304392?utm_source=openai))

Experimental methods (concise)
- Molecular: ΔLD-IRE1α constructs; UPRE promoter library; insulated expression cassettes; secreted human FGF21 and GDF15 cDNAs; multiplexed barcoded reporters for threshold mapping. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1097276517304392?utm_source=openai))
- Cell engineering: GMP-compatible human cell line; site-specific integration; secretion testing; bioassays for β-Klotho/FGFR and GFRAL/RET signaling. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26441838/?utm_source=openai))
- Devices: Hydrogel macroencapsulation; diffusion modeling; in vivo telemetry for device-local lipid profiles. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3868331/?utm_source=openai))
- In vivo: DIO mouse and NHP studies; indirect calorimetry; isotope tracers for lipid flux; histology; plasma metabolomics; off-switch trials (4μ8C, KIRA6). ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3326519/?utm_source=openai))

Success criteria
- Autonomous, reversible control with minimal oscillation: ≥15% sustained weight reduction vs sham in DIO mice; ≥10% increase in EE and ≥20% shift of lipid flux to oxidation at matched intake; normalized hepatic DAG/PKCε and improved insulin sensitivity; absence of chronic hypertriglyceridemia. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3921899/?utm_source=openai))

Risk assessment and mitigation
- Nausea with GDF15: tune P3 threshold; permit GLP-1 co-therapy if needed given additive mechanisms. ([dom-pubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com](https://dom-pubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/dom.14663?utm_source=openai))
- Hypertriglyceridemia: favor FGF21-dominant early response; restrict any future ANGPTL4 modules to adipose-restricted formats; real-time TG monitoring with off-switch. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8666355/?utm_source=openai))
- Off-target UPR engagement: ΔLD-IRE1α favors lipid stress; benchmark activation against tunicamycin/thapsigargin to ensure selectivity; include RNase-off controls. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3606975/?utm_source=openai))

Path to human translation
- Delivery: First-in-human as a removable macroencapsulated cell therapy secreting human FGF21 and GDF15 under ΔLD-IRE1α/UPRE control; device dose escalated to a personalized lipid-stress set point determined from baseline lipidomics and indirect calorimetry.
- Clinical endpoints: Safety, tolerability, appetite/EE biomarkers, body weight/adiposity, hepatic fat fraction, insulin sensitivity.
- Expansion: After safety, explore AAV hepatocyte–directed versions with the same lipid-stress gate for durable expression, leveraging human experience with liver-tropic AAVs and with endocrine gene therapies (e.g., GLP‑1RA). ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10687323/?utm_source=openai))

Impact
Using a single, early, physics-based signal of metabolic risk to trigger a tri-axial endocrine response directly addresses the biological asymmetry that permits lipid overflow without homeostatic correction. The proposed gate-and-split architecture is mechanistically minimal, tunable, and designed for clinical reversibility. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3606975/?utm_source=openai))

text:
Title: A lipid droplet phase-transition sentinel that enforces adipocyte size limits and coordinates whole-body appetite, expenditure, and nutrient partitioning

Rationale and prior art check
- Adipocyte hypertrophy disrupts insulin signaling and provokes chronic, proinflammatory adipose remodeling; ER stress and adipocyte death with crown-like macrophage structures rise with obesity, linking hypertrophy to systemic insulin resistance. ([ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK555602/?utm_source=openai))
- Lipid droplets (LDs) originate by neutral-lipid phase separation at the ER; seipin/LDAF complexes pattern LD biogenesis and geometry, and LD surfaces can nucleate protein condensates, indicating that LD-associated phase transitions are intrinsic and engineerable. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41594-021-00718-y?utm_source=openai))
- Liquid–liquid phase separation (LLPS) underlies threshold-like cellular decisions and can be repurposed to assemble activators in situ, supporting a condensate-based sensor/actuator. ([frontiersin.org](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/cell-and-developmental-biology/articles/10.3389/fcell.2026.1759561/full?utm_source=openai))
- Multicistronic IRES-based vectors have enabled coordinated co-expression of multiple effectors in preclinical and clinical contexts, supporting a single-trigger, multi-hormone output. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6920891/?utm_source=openai))
- Endocrine effectors with human evidence for the three axes exist: GLP-1 pathway for appetite suppression, FGF21-class signals for thermogenic programming/energy expenditure, and adiponectin pathway for insulin sensitization and anti-lipogenesis. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0002934325000592?utm_source=openai))

Hypothesis and goal
- Hypothesis: Hypertrophic adipocytes exhibit LD-surface crowding and composition shifts that can be harnessed to nucleate an engineered, LD-tethered protein condensate only beyond a geometry/composition threshold; this condensate can act as a single sentinel that (i) triggers a coordinated secretory triad reducing appetite, increasing energy expenditure, and shifting nutrient partitioning away from fat storage, and (ii) at a higher burden threshold, commits the most oversized adipocytes to immunologically quiet apoptosis to prevent inflammatory spillover.
- Goal: Build and test an adipocyte-autonomous “LD-Phase Sentinel” that enforces a depot fat-mass set point and normalizes systemic energy balance without continuous external dosing.

Atomic strategy
- Convert the physical driver of dysfunction—LD expansion and surface crowding—into the trigger itself: an LD-tethered, multivalent scaffold that undergoes a phase transition only when LD radius/surface chemistry cross a critical threshold, thereby assembling a single actuator that controls both secretory homeostasis and, at a higher threshold, cell-autonomous deletion.

Specific aims

Aim 1. Engineer and validate the LD-Phase Sentinel as an adipocyte size-threshold sensor
- Concept: An LD-monolayer–anchored multivalent scaffold forms a condensate only when local binding site density and lipid composition (neutral lipid load, phospholipid packing) exceed a calibrated threshold characteristic of hypertrophic adipocytes. Condensation spatially coalesces split actuator domains to switch “ON.”
- Readouts:
  - Single-cell threshold curves: condensate nucleation probability versus LD diameter and adipocyte volume.
  - Hysteresis and reversibility when lipid load decreases (loss of condensate and actuator OFF).
  - Off-target assessment in lean adipocytes and non-adipocytes.
- Justification: LD formation and growth reflect neutral-lipid phase separation at ER–LD sites; LD surfaces can nucleate protein condensates, supporting a geometry/composition-coupled commitment point. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41594-021-00718-y?utm_source=openai))

Aim 2. Couple the sentinel to a single-transcript tri-axis secretome to normalize system-level energy balance
- Design: A multicistronic, IRES-based secretory cassette expressed only when the sentinel is ON, delivering:
  - An anorectic effector (GLP‑1 pathway analog class) for appetite suppression.
  - A thermogenic/adipose–muscle effector (FGF21-class) to raise energy expenditure and promote beige/brown activation.
  - An insulin-sensitizing, anti‑lipogenic effector (adiponectin-pathway class) to divert nutrients away from re-esterification and improve partitioning to oxidation.
- Control features: Relative expression tuned by IRES choice/position and transcriptional strength; fast OFF via degron-based turnover when the sentinel dissolves upon burden reduction; depot-restricted expression to reduce systemic peaks.
- Justification: GLP‑1 agonism reduces food intake; FGF21 elevates thermogenic capacity and energy expenditure in models; adiponectin signaling enhances insulin sensitivity and fatty-acid oxidation. IRES-based multicistronic vectors enable coordinated co-expression from one trigger. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0002934325000592?utm_source=openai))

Aim 3. Add a staged, immunologically quiet ablation mode for the most hypertrophic adipocytes
- Design: The same condensate serves as a stage gate: when condensate size/lifetime exceed a higher critical threshold (reflecting extreme hypertrophy), a second actuator commits the cell to intrinsic apoptosis with minimized proinflammatory signaling, leveraging tissue efferocytosis for silent clearance.
- Endpoints:
  - Evidence of apoptosis (intrinsic pathway markers) without necrotic/pyroptotic signatures.
  - Efficient efferocytosis by adipose-resident macrophages; absence or reduction of crown-like structures compared to uncontrolled hypertrophic death.
- Justification: Apoptosis normally proceeds with anti-inflammatory efferocytosis; in obesity, disordered adipocyte death drives inflammatory CLS—motivating a tightly gated, quiet elimination of only the worst offenders. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/8093429/?utm_source=openai))

Experimental approach and evaluations

- In vitro adipocyte systems
  - Generate human primary or iPSC-derived adipocytes exhibiting a range of LD sizes by controlled lipid loading. Quantify LD geometry, sentinel condensation (live-cell imaging), and ON/OFF behavior vs. size.
  - Secretome profiling upon sentinel ON: quantify tri-axis effectors and downstream signaling in co-cultured hypothalamic neurons (appetite-relevant transcriptional responses), beige adipocytes/myotubes (thermogenic markers, oxygen consumption), and hepatocytes/myotubes (insulin signaling, fatty-acid oxidation).
  - Stage-gated apoptosis testing: trigger high-burden states; confirm apoptosis markers and macrophage efferocytosis in adipocyte–macrophage co-culture with minimal inflammatory cytokines. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/8093429/?utm_source=openai))

- Ex vivo human adipose explants
  - Assess depot-restricted activation, local cytokine milieu, and macrophage phenotypes (efferocytosis vs. CLS formation) during burdened vs. relieved states. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7311368/?utm_source=openai))

- In vivo proof-of-concept
  - Rodent obesity models: dose–response of sentinel activation vs. depot fat fraction; effects on food intake, energy expenditure, RER, insulin sensitivity, and ectopic lipid deposition. Histology for CLS and inflammatory markers to benchmark safety.
  - Reversibility: post-weight loss or caloric normalization, confirm sentinel OFF, secretome decline, and halt of ablation.

Key measurements and success criteria
- Single-cell thresholds: a sharp increase in ON-state frequency above defined LD diameter; rapid OFF upon lipid reduction.
- Systemic endpoints: reduced caloric intake, elevated energy expenditure, improved insulin sensitivity, and reduced hepatic/muscle lipid without hypertriglyceridemia.
- Tissue safety: minimal CLS density and inflammatory cytokines compared with untreated hypertrophic controls; preserved stromal/vascular integrity. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41418-022-01062-4?utm_source=openai))

Risk analysis and mitigation
- Risk: Over-secretion causing adverse effects.
  - Mitigation: Depot-restricted expression; tunable IRES stoichiometry; degradable transcripts/proteins; threshold calibration to activate only in hypertrophy. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6920891/?utm_source=openai))
- Risk: Incomplete efferocytosis leading to inflammation.
  - Mitigation: Tight staging of the ablation gate; confirm apoptotic, not lytic, death; optimize sentinel thresholds to minimize event frequency while preserving efficacy. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/8093429/?utm_source=openai))
- Risk: Insufficient human thermogenic response to FGF21-class agents.
  - Mitigation: Combine with alternative thermogenic adipokine classes in the cassette during optimization; prioritize human-relevant endpoints. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12938967/?utm_source=openai))

Innovation
- A single, geometry/composition-coupled LD-surface condensate acts as the master sensor and actuator, turning the biophysical cause of adipocyte dysfunction into the control knob for endocrine normalization and, only when necessary, quiet cell culling. This unifies set-point detection and tri-axis correction in an adipocyte-autonomous, clinically modular format. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11163294/?utm_source=openai))

Translational path
- Modularity supports stepwise translation: depot-targeted delivery, biomarker monitoring of sentinel activation, and reversible control via tuning thresholds. The approach builds on validated physiologies (GLP‑1 appetite control, FGF21 thermogenesis, adiponectin insulin sensitization) and clinically used multicistronic expression strategies, aligning with human translation. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0002934325000592?utm_source=openai))

text:
Title
AdipoSink: A lipid-droplet partitioning homeostat that derepresses endogenous anti‑obesity programs only when adiposity exceeds a set point

Background and rationale
- In white adipocytes, lipid droplet (LD) surface area expands with hypertrophy. Proteins are targeted to and reversibly sequestered on LD monolayers by amphipathic helices and LD‑targeting motifs from perilipins and ER‑to‑LD cargo such as GPAT4/LiveDrop; LDs act as generic sequestration sites that modulate protein availability. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4807253/?utm_source=openai))
- Central appetite control can be reduced by endocrine signals such as FGF21 (acting via FGFR1c/β‑Klotho in specific hypothalamic nuclei to suppress sugar intake and modulate sympathetic outflow) and GDF15 (acting via GFRAL neurons in the area postrema/NTS), whereas human energy expenditure can be increased by β3‑adrenergic activation of BAT. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4756759/?utm_source=openai))
- Nutrient partitioning between adipose and oxidative tissues is controlled by LPL and angiopoietin‑like proteins; increasing ANGPTL4 or directly repressing adipose LPL reduces triglyceride uptake into white fat and shuttles lipid fuel to muscle/BAT, particularly under conditions that increase thermogenic demand. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6779329/?utm_source=openai))
- Anti‑CRISPR proteins (e.g., AcrIIA4) potently block dCas9 DNA binding and thus CRISPRa/i, enabling protein‑level “brakes” on transcriptional effectors. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6331597/?utm_source=openai))
- Novelty: Although LD sequestration and Acr‑based dCas9 control are established independently, using endogenous LD growth as a tunable “mass‑to‑concentration inverter” to passively titrate an anti‑CRISPR brake and thereby implement an adiposity‑proportional, set‑point homeostat for multi‑axis weight control has not, to our knowledge, been applied to obesity therapeutics. Prior work shows LDs can broadly sequester proteins and regulate their availability, but not as an in vivo adiposity comparator driving endocrine/thermogenic outputs. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0962892407001602?utm_source=openai))

Hypothesis and goal
A constitutively expressed anti‑CRISPR “brake,” fused to a lipid‑droplet–targeting peptide, will partition into expanding LDs as adiposity increases, reducing its free cytosolic concentration and thereby derepressing a dCas9‑based program that: (i) suppresses appetite (via FGF21 pulses), (ii) increases energy expenditure (via adipocyte beiging/thermogenesis), and (iii) redirects nutrient partitioning away from white fat (via adipose LPL repression and hepatoprotective NRG4). This single physicochemical titration implements an automatic, depot‑weighted set point without digital comparators.

Atomic strategy
Exploit passive partitioning into lipid droplets as the sole comparator: the LD surface is the growing sink whose capacity scales with fat mass; sink‑driven sequestration of the brake inverts mass (fat) into signal (free activator), producing graded, adiposity‑proportional derepression.

Specific aims
1) Engineer and calibrate an LD‑titrated anti‑CRISPR brake in human adipocytes.
2) Couple derepression to three clinical axes with endogenous effectors.
3) Validate set‑point control and cardiometabolic outcomes in vivo; define translational parameters for human dosing.

Aim 1: LD‑titrated brake design, calibration, and set‑point tuning
- Construct: Express AcrIIA4 fused to a validated LD‑targeting motif (e.g., perilipin 11‑mer amphipathic helix or GPAT4/LiveDrop segment) under an adipocyte promoter (AdipoQ or FABP4). Co‑express dCas9‑VPR (for activation) and dCas9‑KRAB (for repression) targeted to endogenous loci (below). At low adiposity, high free AcrIIA4 blocks dCas9 DNA binding; as LD surface increases, AcrIIA4 partitions to LDs, decreasing free brake and allowing graded target engagement. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6331597/?utm_source=openai))
- In vitro calibration (human primary subcutaneous adipocytes, 3D adipose organoids): Induce a controlled LD size series (lipid loading) and quantify Acr–LD partition coefficients and cytosolic free Acr by fluorescence ratiometry; fit derepression curves of a CRISPRa reporter to LD surface area to extract the threshold and slope (Hill coefficient).
- Set‑point tuning: Adjust LD affinity (mutate AH hydrophobic residues), brake expression (promoter strength), and stoichiometry relative to dCas9 to position the activation threshold at a clinically defined body‑fat percent. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29316443/?utm_source=openai))
- Safety containment: Include an orthogonal small‑molecule off‑switch (e.g., miRNA‑gated Acr expression in hepatocytes to prevent liver exposure; a drug‑inducible degron on dCas9) for preclinical risk mitigation. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6648350/?utm_source=openai))

Aim 2: Three‑axis endogenous effectors under LD‑derepressed control
- Appetite suppression: CRISPRa of FGF21 from adipocytes to deliver peripheral FGF21 pulses; this engages KLB/FGFR1c CNS targets to reduce sugar preference and adjust sympathetic tone without relying on continuous exogenous drugs. Escalation option if needed: low‑duty‑cycle GDF15 pulses by CRISPRa with strict upper bounds to avoid malaise. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7053867/?utm_source=openai))
- Energy expenditure: CRISPRa of PRDM16 and UCP1 in subcutaneous white adipocytes to drive beige conversion and thermogenesis; complement with sensitization to sympathetic input (e.g., ADRB3 upregulation), leveraging evidence that β3 agonism increases BAT activity and REE in humans. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7190915/?utm_source=openai))
- Nutrient partitioning away from fat: CRISPRi of LPL and/or CRISPRa of ANGPTL4 selectively in white adipose depots to reduce local TG uptake; combine with beiging so liberated lipid is oxidized in beige/BAT and muscle (physiologic routing). Add CRISPRa of NRG4 in adipocytes to suppress hepatic lipogenesis and improve fatty‑liver risk. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7334813/?utm_source=openai))
- Single‑vector logic: All targets are controlled by the same LD‑titrated derepression, ensuring that the three axes rise and fall together with the weighted sum of depot adiposity.

Aim 3: Distributed sensing architecture, in vivo efficacy, and translational metrics
- Depot weighting: Deliver the cassette systemically via adipose‑tropic AAV/LNP with promoter/enhancer choices that bias expression to visceral vs subcutaneous depots, converting body‑fat distribution into a weighted global output (higher weight on visceral fat). Blood integrates these local derepression outputs into systemic endocrine/thermogenic responses.
- Mouse DIO studies: 
  - Primary endpoints: food intake and macronutrient preference; REE and RER by indirect calorimetry; PET‑CT BAT activity; body composition; hepatic steatosis (MRI‑PDFF); fasting/postprandial TG and FFA flux with stable isotopes. 
  - Mechanism endpoints: depot‑specific UCP1/PRDM16 induction; serum FGF21 excursions vs LD size; LPL activity and ANGPTL4 expression in WAT; muscle/BAT lipid uptake. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7190915/?utm_source=openai))
- NHP feasibility: Biodistribution, appetite/macronutrient preference assays, safety labs, and triglyceride handling under standardized mixed meals.
- Human translation plan: 
  - Indications: adults with visceral obesity and NAFLD risk. 
  - Dose‑finding: vector dose and LD‑affinity variant define the set‑point; target a BMI‑ and waist‑adjusted fat‑percent threshold. 
  - Biomarkers: circulating FGF21 pulses scaling with DXA‑measured fat mass; plasma TG handling; supraclavicular thermography; continuous energy expenditure via room calorimetry. 
  - Safety: monitor nausea (if GDF15 option pursued), BP/HR (β3 sensitization context), and hypertriglyceridemia risk from WAT LPL repression; adjust depot weighting and brake affinity accordingly. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7923658/?utm_source=openai))

Experimental plan (concise)
- Module engineering: 
  - Brake: AcrIIA4‑LDtag fusions (PLIN2‑AH or GPAT4‑LiveDrop) validated for LD localization using live‑cell microscopy; evaluate variants spanning LD affinities to bracket desired thresholds. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4807253/?utm_source=openai))
  - Effectors: dCas9‑VPR sgRNAs to FGF21, PRDM16, UCP1, NRG4; dCas9‑KRAB sgRNAs to LPL (WAT‑restricted expression to avoid BAT interference). 
- Systems characterization: Quantify the transfer function mapping LD surface area → free brake → target gene expression → phenotypes (intake, EE, partitioning). Fit a compact control model to guide clinical set‑point selection.
- Comparative controls: (i) constitutive effector expression without LD control, (ii) Acr‑free dCas9, (iii) BAT‑only or WAT‑only targeting to test axis necessity/sufficiency.

Milestones and success criteria
- M1: In vitro monotonic, tunable derepression of a reporter with LD size (R² > 0.8; coefficient of variation < 20% across donors). 
- M2: In DIO mice, ≥15% reduction in energy intake (with reduced sugar preference), ≥10% increase in REE, and ≥30% reduction in WAT LPL activity with increased muscle/BAT lipid uptake, all engaged only above the preset adiposity threshold. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7053867/?utm_source=openai))
- M3: NHP proof‑of‑principle endocrine readouts (FGF21 pulses scaling with fat mass) and safety profile enabling Phase 1 initiation.

Risk assessment and contingency
- Appetite axis potency: If FGF21 alone yields insufficient intake suppression, layer a low‑duty‑cycle GDF15 CRISPRa arm gated by a higher adiposity threshold to limit aversive signaling; predefine stop rules based on validated AP/NTS pathway biomarkers. ([academic.oup.com](https://academic.oup.com/edrv/article/41/4/bnaa007/5822811?utm_source=openai))
- Triglyceride handling: If WAT LPL repression elevates plasma TGs, increase BAT/beige load (PRDM16/UCP1) and/or reduce WAT ANGPTL4 dose; reserve a liver‑directed ANGPTL3‑siRNA add‑on in nonresponders. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10342861/?utm_source=openai))
- Off‑target editing is minimized by using dCas9‑based transcriptional modulation and tissue‑restricted promoters; Acr‑based global brake provides an additional containment layer. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6331597/?utm_source=openai))

Why this is mechanistically tight and clinically oriented
- The LD sink is a stable, physics‑level comparator that directly scales with adipocyte fat, eliminating fragile multi‑node comparators while restoring native endocrine and thermogenic programs. LD targeting and protein sequestration are established; Acr‑based dCas9 control is robust; FGF21, PRDM16/UCP1, LPL/ANGPTL4, and NRG4 are endogenous nodes with human‑relevant evidence. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4807253/?utm_source=openai))

Expected outcome
A single‑cassette, depot‑weighted, LD‑titrated derepression circuit that activates only when body fat exceeds a tunable set point, coordinately suppressing appetite, increasing energy expenditure, and shifting nutrient partitioning away from storage—thereby repairing the missing “over‑fat” feedback with an elegant, translation‑ready homeostat.

text:
Title
A programmable acyl‑CoA threshold switch in subcutaneous “adipometer” cells to impose a weight‑gain ceiling via coordinated appetite, energy‑expenditure, and nutrient‑partitioning control

Hypothesis and goal
A cell‑autonomous comparator that measures intracellular long‑chain acyl‑CoA (LC‑acyl‑CoA) burden in engineered subcutaneous adipocyte‑like cells can serve as a faithful proxy for whole‑body adiposity. When LC‑acyl‑CoA persistently exceeds a tunable threshold, the circuit should automatically trigger three outputs—GLP‑1 secretion (appetite suppression), FGF21 secretion (energy expenditure), and localized ANGPTL4‑based nutrient partitioning away from adipose deposition—thereby establishing a clinically adjustable “ceiling” on weight gain while remaining quiescent below the set point.

Atomic strategy
Exploit substrate‑proximal sensing: use a mammalianized FadR transcription factor as an LC‑acyl‑CoA‑responsive switch, buffered by an intracellular acyl‑CoA sink to implement a hard threshold. Crossing the threshold synchronously induces a minimal, pre‑validated polyhormonal program (GLP‑1, FGF21, and a locally acting ANGPTL4 module). The acyl‑CoA sink passively absorbs transient post‑meal spikes, ensuring the system only responds to chronic adiposity.

Rationale and supporting evidence
- LC‑acyl‑CoA levels report lipid influx/storage pressure and can be monitored or sensed in mammalian cells; multiple genetically encoded acyl‑CoA biosensors validate dynamic LC‑acyl‑CoA readouts in live mammalian cells. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10014278/?utm_source=openai))
- Bacterial lipid TFs are redeployable in eukaryotes: FadR functions as an LC‑acyl‑CoA‑regulated transcription factor (dissociates from DNA upon ligand binding), and has been implemented as a fatty‑acyl‑CoA sensor in yeast; closely related bacterial TF sensors (FapR) have been adapted to mammalian cells. These establish feasibility and motivate a FadR‑based mammalian switch. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8180525/?utm_source=openai))
- Acyl‑CoA binding proteins (ACBP family) buffer intracellular LC‑acyl‑CoA pools, supporting a sink‑based thresholding design; we will use non‑secreted intracellular variants to avoid endocrine ACBP effects. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0141813017301216?utm_source=openai))
- Outputs are translationally validated:
  - GLP‑1 from engineered skin/encapsulated cells reduces weight gain and improves glucose control in mice and is compatible with subcutaneous cell‑therapy devices. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5555372/?utm_source=openai))
  - FGF21 increases energy expenditure and reduces adiposity across modalities (protein, gene therapy, mRNA), supporting its role as an EE actuator. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/18840786/?dopt=Abstract&utm_source=openai))
  - ANGPTL4 regulates tissue‑specific LPL activity and lipid partitioning; domain engineering (fibrinogen‑like domain, FLD) can separate thermogenic/lipolytic actions from LPL inhibition, enabling local adipose nutrient diversion with reduced systemic triglyceride impact. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8666355/?utm_source=openai))

System design overview
- Sensor: Human‑codon‑optimized E. coli FadR fused to a mammalian transcriptional effector (e.g., Gal4‑VP64) controlling a synthetic promoter with multimerized FadR operators. In high free LC‑acyl‑CoA, FadR leaves DNA, switching promoter state. Threshold and gain are tuned by operator multiplicity and FadR affinity. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8180525/?utm_source=openai))
- Thresholding sink/comparator: Co‑express a cytosolic, non‑secreted ACBP variant (and/or engineered acyl‑CoA‑binding domain) at defined stoichiometry to sequester LC‑acyl‑CoA up to a preset capacity; only persistent overload raises free LC‑acyl‑CoA to flip the FadR switch. DNA decoy operators provide a secondary TF sink for sharper transitions and hysteresis. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0141813017301216?utm_source=openai))
- Effectors (multi‑axis, single cassette):
  1) Appetite: secreted GLP‑1 analog (DPP4‑resistant) under FadR control. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5555372/?utm_source=openai))
  2) Energy expenditure: secreted FGF21 (or long‑acting variant). ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/18840786/?dopt=Abstract&utm_source=openai))
  3) Nutrient partitioning: ANGPTL4‑FLD tethered locally (e.g., ECM‑binding tag) to bias lipolysis/thermogenesis in adjacent WAT with minimal systemic LPL inhibition. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5625043/?utm_source=openai))
- Therapeutic chassis and delivery: Subcutaneous, encapsulated human preadipocyte‑like or dermal progenitor cells engineered ex vivo and implanted as a patch; this leverages established subcutaneous cell‑therapy platforms feasible for clinical translation. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34861146/?dopt=Abstract&utm_source=openai))

Specific aims

Aim 1. Build and calibrate a mammalian FadR acyl‑CoA threshold switch.
- Construct FadR‑Gal4VP64 and a UAS‑reporter; integrate into human preadipocyte‑like cells. Quantify dynamic range using LC‑acyl‑CoA perturbations (fatty‑acid loading, CPT1 inhibition/activation) while independently measuring LC‑acyl‑CoA with an orthogonal biosensor for ground truth. Tune operator number and FadR variants to set activation EC50 and Hill slope. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10014278/?utm_source=openai))
- Implement sink/comparator by graded expression of cytosolic ACBP variants; map sink capacity versus reporter activation and introduce operator decoys to sharpen threshold and create on/off hysteresis. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0141813017301216?utm_source=openai))
Milestones: >20‑fold dynamic range; <10% activation to meal‑like acute spikes; sustained activation only under chronic lipid loading.

Aim 2. Wire therapeutic effectors and quantify closed‑loop multi‑axis control in vitro and in vivo.
- Clone a tri‑cistronic effector cassette (GLP‑1, FGF21, ANGPTL4‑FLD‑ECM‑tether) under the FadR promoter. Validate secretion, bioactivity, and lack of off‑target endocrine effects in vitro.
- Encapsulate engineered cells and implant subcutaneously in diet‑induced obese mice. Endpoints:
  - Appetite axis: food intake and hypothalamic pSTAT3/ARC neuropeptide markers under ad libitum and refeeding. GLP‑1 pharmacodynamics. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5555372/?utm_source=openai))
  - Energy‑expenditure axis: indirect calorimetry, RER, BAT/WAT thermogenic gene expression; FGF21 pharmacokinetics/pharmacodynamics. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/18840786/?dopt=Abstract&utm_source=openai))
  - Nutrient‑partitioning axis: in vivo radiolabeled TRL‑TG tracking to WAT vs oxidative tissues; local vs plasma ANGPTL4 levels; plasma TG safety margins. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8666355/?utm_source=openai))
Milestones: Significant reductions in energy intake, ≥10–15% increase in energy expenditure, and demonstrable diversion of TRL‑TG away from WAT without hypertriglyceridemia.

Aim 3. Demonstrate programmable adiposity set‑point and ceiling behavior with safety.
- Threshold tuning: Vary sink expression and operator decoys to set distinct “on” thresholds (e.g., 30%, 35%, 40% body fat in mice) and quantify hysteresis (higher on‑threshold than off‑threshold) to avoid oscillations.
- Closed‑loop challenge: After weight normalization below set point, re‑challenge with high‑fat diet to test automatic re‑engagement; after return below set point, confirm autonomous shutoff.
- Safety: Monitor biomarkers (lipids, liver, pancreas), behavior, and cardiovascular parameters; verify no chronic GLP‑1 nausea‑like phenotypes at set point. Explant analysis for fibrosis and device integrity. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34861146/?dopt=Abstract&utm_source=openai))
Milestones: Reproducible on/off control around preset adiposity with durable efficacy and acceptable safety over 12–16 weeks.

Key design and measurement details
- Orthogonal sensing validation: Parallel use of an LC‑acyl‑CoA fluorescent biosensor to independently confirm intracellular trigger levels during activation. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10014278/?utm_source=openai))
- Minimizing systemic ANGPTL4 effects: Use FLD‑only constructs with ECM‑tether motifs to localize action near the implant; target plasma TG change <20% from baseline. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5625043/?utm_source=openai))
- Encapsulation/device: Use clinically familiar subcutaneous macro/micro‑encapsulation to enable retrieval and immune isolation; leverage experience from subcutaneous endocrine cell implants. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34861146/?dopt=Abstract&utm_source=openai))

Anticipated outcomes
- A minimal, tunable, substrate‑proximal adiposity sensor‑actuator that counters weight gain with synchronized appetite, expenditure, and partitioning responses, yet remains inert during normal fluctuations.
- A clinician‑settable adiposity ceiling by adjusting sink capacity/operator decoys, enabling personalized therapy.

Risk mitigation
- If FadR dynamic range in mammalian nuclei is suboptimal, explore alternative TF fusions or operator architectures; feasibility is supported by bacterial TF sensors adapted to eukaryotes and mammalian malonyl‑CoA TF sensors. ([pubs.acs.org](https://pubs.acs.org/doi/10.1021/acssynbio.9b00118?utm_source=openai))
- If systemic ANGPTL4 effects elevate TG, down‑titrate FLD expression, strengthen local tethering, or swap to alternative local partitioning levers (e.g., adipose‑restricted LPL modulation).
- If GLP‑1 tolerance emerges, the ceiling still holds via EE/partitioning; GLP‑1 can be cycled or replaced by dual agonist variants in the same cassette.

Path to translation
- Human primary cell chassis with GMP‑compatible encapsulation, dose‑finding on threshold and effector output, and clear biomarkers (circulating GLP‑1, FGF21; local ANGPTL4) support a pre‑IND package.
- The approach repurposes validated endocrine effectors while introducing a novel, mammalianized LC‑acyl‑CoA comparator to restore symmetric weight regulation. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10014278/?utm_source=openai))

Success criteria
- Preclinical: robust, reversible set‑point enforcement with ≥15% reduction in body weight relative to control, sustained for ≥12 weeks, with normal activity and acceptable safety labs.
- Translational: scalable manufacturing of encapsulated, retrieval‑capable implants with predictable thresholds and dose‑response in large animals.
