Title: Crossing the resealing–damage threshold in DMD by boosting synaptotagmin‑7–driven lysosomal exocytosis in myofibers

Hypothesis/research question:
- Can targeted upregulation of synaptotagmin‑7 (Syt7) in dystrophin‑deficient skeletal muscle shorten the lifetime of sarcolemmal microtears enough to keep intracellular Ca2+ excursions below cytotoxic thresholds, thereby reducing necrosis, inflammation, and fibrosis without restoring dystrophin? Syt7 is the high‑affinity Ca2+ sensor for lysosomal exocytosis; its loss impairs membrane resealing and causes myositis, whereas Ca2+‑triggered lysosomal fusion is a core, conserved repair response in mechanically stressed tissues. To our knowledge, AAV‑mediated Syt7 augmentation has not been tested in DMD, despite gene‑therapy precedents for other repair components (e.g., MG53; SNARE tuning). ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0092867401004214?utm_source=openai))

Atomic strategy:
- Single intervention: increase Syt7 availability at the subsarcolemma so that lysosomes dock/fuse faster upon injury-triggered Ca2+ spikes, converting unavoidable micro‑failures into brief, self‑limiting events.

Specific aims:
1) Define the quantitative resealing gain from Syt7 upregulation in human DMD myotubes and mdx fibers.
- Construct: AAV-MyoAAV2A capsid carrying MCK‑driven human Syt7 with C‑terminal lysosome retention signal intact; include miR-124/miR‑9 target sites (neurons) and miR‑208a (cardiomyocytes) to de-target off‑muscle transduction; incorporate a FKBP12F36V‑degron for titratable stabilization with dTAG ligand during dosing studies.
- In vitro: laser- or saponin‑wound DMD iPSC‑myotubes expressing GCaMP7; endpoints: resealing half-time (FM1‑43 dye loss), LAMP1 externalization kinetics, Ca2+ AUC above toxicity threshold, and mitochondrial depolarization probability.
- Ex vivo: single‑fiber wounding in mdx EDL with two‑photon injury; pharmacologic Ca2+ clamps to map Syt7 dose–response.
- Success metric: ≥40% reduction in resealing half-time and ≥50% reduction in Ca2+ AUC per lesion versus AAV‑GFP controls. Mechanistic grounding: Syt7 mediates Ca2+‑regulated lysosomal fusion and its deficiency impairs cell resealing; repair in muscle relies on SNARE/Syt7‑dependent exocytosis. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0092867401004214?utm_source=openai))

2) Test therapeutic efficacy of muscle‑targeted Syt7 delivery in mdx mice.
- Dosing: single IV dose of AAV‑MyoAAV2A‑MCK‑Syt7 at 3×10^13 vg/kg in 4‑week mdx; compare to empty vector. Include cohort with inducible dTAG control to tune expression if off‑target effects arise.
- Primary endpoints (8 and 16 weeks post‑dose): in situ TA eccentric‑contraction force drop; Evans blue dye uptake; serum CK; fibrotic area (Picrosirius Red) and hydroxyproline; macrophage and T‑cell infiltration (F4/80, CD3); NF‑κB/TGF‑β pathway activation; survival/ambulatory behavior.
- Secondary endpoints: lysosomal exocytosis markers (cell‑surface LAMP1), repair proteins recruitment; proteomics of trafficking/repair modules to benchmark against prior repair gene therapies (e.g., MG53; STX4). Rationale: enhancing membrane repair by exocytosis improves dystrophic phenotypes in other models; Syt7 is the canonical Ca2+ sensor for this arm. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22314291/?utm_source=openai))

3) Safety, biodistribution, and control.
- Off‑target control: neuron and cardiomyocyte de‑targeting via embedded miR target cassettes; biodistribution by ddPCR; transcript profiling for Syt7 in brain/heart.
- Arrhythmia and neurobehavior screens; serum chemistry; complement activation/anti‑capsid titers.
- Over‑repair risk: histology for lysosomal burden, autophagy flux, and myofiber vacuolization; degron‑based reversal if adverse findings emerge.
- Vector choice: use muscle‑tropic engineered capsid (MyoAAV2A) to reduce hepatic/neuronal exposure while maintaining skeletal muscle transduction efficiency. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42332716/?utm_source=openai))

Experimental design and methods:
- Vector engineering: codon‑optimized human SYT7 cDNA; MCK promoter; WPRE; bGH polyA; 4× tandem miR‑124/miR‑9 and 4× miR‑208a target sites in 3′ UTR; FKBP12F36V degron fused via flexible linker.
- In vitro human models: DMD iPSC‑myotubes and CRISPR DMD primary myoblasts; transduction at MOI 3–5×10^4; wound‑assay automation with high‑speed imaging.
- In vivo physiology: blinded randomization; power analysis for 30% effect size; pre‑registered endpoints; sex‑balanced mdx cohorts.
- Analytics: quantitative image analysis of repair kinetics; Ca2+ AUC integration; force–injury curves; RNA‑seq for inflammatory/fibrotic signatures; targeted proteomics of SNARE/Syt7 pathways. Foundational mechanisms: Ca2+‑regulated lysosomal exocytosis is a primary PM repair route; Syt7 binds anionic lipids/SNAREs to trigger fusion at low micromolar Ca2+. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0092867401004214?utm_source=openai))

Translational plan:
- Manufacturability: Syt7 cassette (<2.5 kb payload with regulatory elements) fits single AAV; platform is scalable to GMP.
- Patient stratification: ambulant boys with confirmed DMD mutations; baseline muscle injury markers to enrich for frequent microtear phenotype.
- Biomarkers: microtear burden by circulating CK and muscle‑derived cfDNA; microdialysis assays for extracellular vesicle LAMP1; MRI‑T2 mapping for edema/fibrosis.
- Combination logic: compatible with exon‑skipping or micro‑dystrophin; orthogonal mechanism reduces Ca2+ injury regardless of dystrophin status, aligning with the compensatory networks seen in mdx mice. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3589167/?utm_source=openai))

Milestones and go/no‑go:
- Milestone 1: ≥40% resealing acceleration and ≥50% Ca2+ AUC reduction in vitro (go).
- Milestone 2: ≥30% reduction in eccentric force drop and ≥30% reduction in Evans blue uptake at 8 weeks (go); dose‑response established.
- Milestone 3: no cardiotoxicity/neurological adverse events; acceptable biodistribution with <5% vector genomes in brain (go).

Risk assessment and mitigations:
- Off‑target expression: minimized by muscle‑tropic capsid and miR de‑targeting; monitor by tissue qPCR and immunostaining. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42332716/?utm_source=openai))
- Overactivation of lysosomal pathways: titratable degron; histopathology surveillance.
- Translational uncertainty: if rescue is partial, combine with costamere/ECM reinforcement in follow‑up studies; as an orthogonal option, explore basement‑membrane toughening via peroxidasin‑guided collagen IV sulfilimine cross‑link density tuning in localized muscle beds, given BM mechanics dependence on NC1 cross‑links. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4128002/?utm_source=openai))

Novelty check summary:
- Core mechanism is established: Syt7 is the Ca2+ sensor for lysosomal exocytosis that mediates plasma‑membrane repair; its deficiency impairs resealing and causes muscle inflammation. We found no reports of AAV‑mediated Syt7 overexpression as a DMD therapy; available gene‑therapy efforts in the repair space have targeted other nodes (e.g., MG53, syntaxin‑4), leaving Syt7 augmentation untested. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0092867401004214?utm_source=openai))

Expected outcome and impact:
- If successful, Syt7 augmentation will lower the incidence–amplitude–lifetime product of injury‑induced Ca2+ loads below degeneration thresholds, reducing necrosis and fibrosis without touching dystrophin. The approach is agnostic to mutation class, modular with existing therapies, and directly operationalizes a compensatory pathway that likely contributes to the mdx mouse’s relative resilience. ([journals.physiology.org](https://journals.physiology.org/doi/full/10.1152/physrev.00037.2014?doi=10.1152%2Fphysrev.00037.2014&utm_source=openai))

Title
Protease-activated, satellite cell–targeted integration of a self-maintaining utrophin activator to durably restore membrane stability in Duchenne muscular dystrophy

Hypothesis/Goal (unified)
If we program Pax7+ satellite cells only during their natural activation windows to install a minimal, self-maintaining epigenetic “on-switch” at the endogenous utrophin (UTRN) regulatory landscape, the daughter myofibers will inherit high utrophin, stabilizing sarcolemma and secondarily normalizing calcium handling, inflammation, and fibrosis across regeneration cycles in DMD, without touching the DMD gene. The key is to couple (1) delivery specificity to turnover-associated protease cues in dystrophic muscle and (2) persistence to an integrated chromatin module that sustains UTRN activation via native reader–writer feedback. Prior work shows CRISPRa upregulation of endogenous utrophin can ameliorate dystrophy and is now achievable in a single AAV; our pivot is to shift the programming event upstream into the stem-cell compartment and make it self-maintaining. ([rnajc.ucsf.edu](https://rnajc.ucsf.edu/sites/rnajc.ucsf.edu/files/PIIS0092867417312473.pdf?utm_source=openai))

Atomic strategy
Turnover-gated programming of stem cells: use a protease-activatable, muscle-tropic AAV to transiently deliver an integrating, compact trans‑epigenetic activator that seeds a BRD4–p300–H3K27ac positive-feedback “island” at UTRN enhancers/promoter in satellite cells only when injury elevates extracellular MMPs and SCs initiate activation. This single, well-timed installation event yields durable, heritable utrophin upregulation in regenerated fibers. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6404099/?utm_source=openai))

Proposed design
- Vector logic
  - Capsid: a myotrophic AAV variant with demonstrated satellite-cell transduction (e.g., MyoAAV family) outfitted as a “provector” by embedding MMP-cleavable peptide locks that mask receptor engagement; high MMP activity in dystrophic/injured muscle unmasks transduction, focusing delivery during SC activation. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13174644/?utm_source=openai))
  - Cargo: a bipartite, single-dose system
    - Transient component: mRNA for a hyperactive DNA transposase (e.g., SB100X or PiggyBac) to achieve genomic insertion only during the brief S/G2 windows that accompany SC activation. The enzyme degrades rapidly, minimizing remobilization risk. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4191042/?utm_source=openai))
    - Integrating component: a compact transposon encoding a muscle-lineage–restricted, CRISPRa-class trans‑epigenetic activator targeted to UTRN regulatory elements (sgRNA array + microdCas effector), but engineered for epigenetic maintenance rather than continuous transgene burden. The effector fuses a p300 HAT core to a BRD4 bromodomain reader, converting local acetylation into sustained recruitment and further acetylation—a known positive feedback that stabilizes active chromatin. Expression is driven by a Pax7/MCK hybrid control to confine activity to SCs and early myogenic progeny, avoiding non-muscle cells. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-022-35375-2?utm_source=openai))

- Built-in “self-reinforcing memory” at UTRN
  - The activator is recruited via sgRNAs to UTRN promoter/enhancer sites; initial H3K27ac deposition recruits BRD proteins (including BRD4), which in turn enhance P-TEFb–mediated transcriptional competency. The fused BRD4-reading module re-binds acetylated nucleosomes and keeps p300 locally active, sustaining an acetylation island and high UTRN transcription without continuous high-level effector expression. BRD4’s mitotic bookmarking supports inheritance through SC divisions. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-022-35375-2?utm_source=openai))

- Turnover coupling and specificity
  - Injury/dystrophy-elevated MMPs activate the capsid; simultaneous SC exit from quiescence provides the only window for efficient genomic integration and locus accessibility, aligning permanent changes with natural repair pulses while keeping quiescent SCs and non-muscle tissues largely unmodified. Early activation factors (FOS, MYOD) mark this window and rationalize a narrow dosing time course. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6404099/?utm_source=openai))

Experimental plan and milestones
- Aim 1: Establish turnover-gated SC transduction and integration
  - In mdx and cardiotoxin-injured wild-type muscles, compare provector-MyoAAV versus unlocked capsid for Pax7+ cell transduction and transposon integration (sgRNA-targeted amplicon capture; vector DNA smFISH). Endpoints: %Pax7+ nuclei carrying integrated cassette; absence in off-target tissues. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6404099/?utm_source=openai))
- Aim 2: Demonstrate durable UTRN activation and inheritance
  - In sorted SCs and derived myofibers across multiple regeneration cycles, quantify UTRN mRNA/protein, H3K27ac and BRD4 occupancy at UTRN regulatory regions, and dependence on BRD4 acetyl-reading (acute JQ1 challenge to test maintenance sensitivity). Endpoints: sustained ≥3–5× UTRN upregulation with stable acetylation island after effector downshift. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6376993/?utm_source=openai))
- Aim 3: Test functional rescue and disease modification
  - Outcomes: sarcolemmal integrity (Evans blue uptake), specific force, resistance to eccentric injury, serum CK, Ca2+ homeostasis markers, fibrosis and inflammatory signatures. Compare to (a) empty provector and (b) non-integrating AAV-CRISPRa “MyoAAV-UA” in myofibers. Expect superior durability from SC programming. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11894210/?utm_source=openai))
- Aim 4: Safety and off-target profiling
  - Genomic insertion mapping (LAM-PCR/ATAC–LAM), integration site enrichment relative to oncogenic loci, transposase transcript clearance, biodistribution with and without prior muscle injury, anti-capsid immunity. Decision gates: integration hotspot avoidance; no clonal expansion signals.

Key feasibility supports
- Endogenous UTRN activation by CRISPRa improves dystrophic muscle and now fits within a single AAV payload; our design keeps that endogenous-locus logic but relocates it to SCs and adds maintenance. ([rnajc.ucsf.edu](https://rnajc.ucsf.edu/sites/rnajc.ucsf.edu/files/PIIS0092867417312473.pdf?utm_source=openai))
- MyoAAV-class capsids transduce myofibers and satellite cells at higher rates than legacy serotypes, providing a delivery foothold across relevant cell types. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13174644/?utm_source=openai))
- Protease-activatable AAVs are validated in other tissues; adapting the MMP-cleavable lock to dystrophic muscle provides a principled spatial–temporal gate. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6404099/?utm_source=openai))
- Positive-feedback stabilization of active chromatin via p300–BRD4 interactions is a well-described mechanism that can be harnessed for epigenetic memory at UTRN. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-022-35375-2?utm_source=openai))

Risk assessment and mitigations
- Insertional mutagenesis: use integration-mapping to select lower-risk transposon systems/configurations; deliver only transposase mRNA; include self-inactivation of transposase ORF and no internal promoter driving it in the transposon. Stop criteria for hotspot clustering.
- Off-target activation: Pax7/MCK hybrid control, injury-gated capsid, and SC-restricted dosing window reduce exposure; sgRNA design and ChIP–qPCR confirm on-target chromatin remodeling at UTRN.
- Immunogenicity: SC programming minimizes chronic transgene burden in myofibers; reduced effector expression after chromatin “set” lowers ongoing antigen load relative to classic AAV. Compare to historical AAV microdystrophin experiences and dose accordingly. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41434-025-00561-6?utm_source=openai))

Translational path
- Indication: ambulant boys with DMD lacking severe cardiomyopathy at enrollment; systemic, weight-adjusted dosing coincident with a mild, controlled injury surrogate (e.g., brief tourniquet/ischemia–reperfusion of a limb) to amplify MMP cues in a defined territory for first-in-human safety readouts.
- Biomarkers: fiber-type–matched utrophin immunostaining in biopsies; plasma CK; MRI T2/fat fraction; functional endpoints (6MWT/motor scales); vector shedding and NAb titers.
- Manufacturability: single-vector provector design with split cargo (transposase mRNA + transposon) remains within scalable AAV production constraints; no need for repeated dosing once SC programming succeeds.

What makes it new
- Prior utrophin CRISPRa focuses on myofibers and episomal expression; here, we reframe therapy as a one-time, turnover-gated programming of stem cells that installs an endogenous-locus, self-maintaining epigenetic “on” state, using a capsid that is only unlocked by disease-associated protease activity. To our knowledge, this convergence—protease-activated, SC-targeted delivery plus integrated, BRD4–p300 maintenance of UTRN—has not been attempted in DMD models. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11894210/?utm_source=openai))

text:
Title
Disease-chromatin-gated activator for DMD: a myonuclear switch that senses dystrophic epigenetic signatures and drives a compensatory repair program

Hypothesis/Goal
Dystrophic myonuclei accumulate reproducible epigenetic signatures that reflect chronic calcium overload, oxidative stress, and inflammatory signaling. A chromatin-reader-gated transcriptional activator, delivered to muscle, can recognize these dystrophy-specific histone/DNA mark patterns and, only in such nuclei, amplify endogenous pro-repair, calcium-handling, and anti-fibrotic gene programs sufficiently to stabilize sarcolemma, normalize ion homeostasis, and reduce pathology in Duchenne muscular dystrophy without restoring dystrophin. This asks whether the epigenome of disease itself can be the on-switch for treatment selectivity and efficacy. ([jmg.bmj.com](https://jmg.bmj.com/content/61/11/1003?utm_source=openai))

Atomic strategy
Exploit disease-encoded chromatin marks as the gating signal: engineer a compact “reader–actuator” that becomes a potent activator only when multivalently bound to histone modifications enriched at dystrophic stress enhancers, thereby boosting nearby endogenous compensatory networks in the same nucleus while remaining inert in healthy muscle. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41394756/?fc=None&ff=20251215130744&v=2.18.0.post22+67771e2&utm_source=openai))

Rationale
- DMD pathophysiology is system-wide: membrane fragility causes persistent Ca2+ influx, activating calpains and downstream damage; inflammation and TGF-β signaling promote fibrosis; regeneration becomes ineffective. These processes correlate with durable shifts in myonuclear histone acetylation/methylation and DNA methylation that distinguish dystrophic from healthy muscle. Thus, chromatin state is a stable, nucleus-intrinsic classifier and a therapeutically targetable input. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8063049/?utm_source=openai))
- Clinical benefit from HDAC inhibition in DMD supports epigenetic involvement but lacks spatial specificity to diseased nuclei. A reader-gated switch would localize action where marks are abnormal, minimizing off-target activity. Synthetic chromatin reader–actuators have been shown to engage defined histone marks and reprogram transcription in mammalian cells, establishing feasibility of mark-sensing activators. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38508835/?utm_source=openai))
- AAV is the most established platform for body-wide skeletal and cardiac muscle delivery, enabling practical translation of a compact genetic switch. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11866442/?utm_source=openai))

Specific Aims
Aim 1. Define dystrophy-enriched chromatin mark constellations that can gate activation without engaging healthy muscle.
- Question: Which histone mark combinations and local features (e.g., H3K27ac/H3K4me3 clusters at stress/inflammation enhancers; loss of repressive marks at repair loci) are consistently enriched in DMD myonuclei and absent or weak in age-matched controls?
- Approach summary: Integrate existing epigenetic literature in DMD with new multi-omic mapping in human DMD myotubes and mdx muscle to nominate mark pairs or triplets that maximize disease/healthy separability and co-localize with genes in membrane repair, Ca2+ handling, and fibrosis control. Predefine a short list of reader domains (e.g., PHD, BRD) whose binding specificities match these constellations. Success criterion: at least two mark combinations with ≥3-fold enrichment in dystrophic vs. healthy myonuclei at candidate enhancers. ([jmg.bmj.com](https://jmg.bmj.com/content/61/11/1003?utm_source=openai))

Aim 2. Build and validate a chromatin-reader–gated activator that is inert in healthy muscle and active in dystrophic nuclei.
- Design principle: Multivalency-dependent activation. Fuse two compatible histone mark reader modules to a minimal transcriptional activation module via a geometry that requires simultaneous binding to the nominated marks to assemble a functional activator. When bound, the actuator biases transcription at engaged enhancers toward endogenous compensatory genes (e.g., annexin network and membrane reseal machinery; Ca2+ clearance/buffering; anti-fibrotic/inflammation-dampening factors). In the absence of clustered disease marks, the parts remain unassembled and inactive.
- Readout: In human DMD vs. healthy myotube nuclei and in mdx muscle, quantify 1) activator chromatin occupancy; 2) selective transcriptional gain of the targeted compensatory gene sets; and 3) absence of activation in healthy muscle. Success criterion: disease/healthy activation ratio ≥10 with upregulation of predefined gene modules and no proinflammatory/fibrogenic drift. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41394756/?fc=None&ff=20251215130744&v=2.18.0.post22+67771e2&utm_source=openai))

Aim 3. Test functional efficacy and safety in dystrophic muscle.
- Endpoints: membrane stability under contraction, Ca2+ homeostasis, inflammatory/fibrotic remodeling, and muscle performance. Expect reduced calpain pathway engagement, improved Ca2+ handling, and lowered fibrosis compared with control AAVs. Safety focuses on off-target activation and immune responses to the transgene and vector. Go/no-go: functional improvement with acceptable safety margins and durable expression. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8063049/?utm_source=openai))

Design features that enforce disease selectivity and safety
- Epigenetic mark logic: Use tandemed reader domains with cooperative binding to two marks enriched only in dystrophic nuclei. This creates a high-avidity requirement that normal chromatin cannot meet, reducing leak. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8928417/?utm_source=openai))
- Optional injury-history lock-in: Add a removable autoinhibitory segment linked by a calpain-cleavable sequence so that sustained Ca2+/calpain activity—common in dystrophic fibers—unmasks the activator. This converts pathological protease activity into a necessary activation step and further biases action to the most damaged fibers. Feasibility is supported by well-characterized calpain activity in DMD muscle and validated intracellular calpain-cleavable linkers in live-cell reporters. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2075236/?utm_source=openai))
- Output confinement: The activator acts at endogenous stress-primed enhancers within the same nucleus, leveraging local chromatin context to co-amplify a coordinated set of protective genes instead of overexpressing a single supraphysiologic factor.

Planned outputs and system-level effects
- Membrane integrity: enhance endogenous membrane resealing networks and costamere support to reduce microlesions and secondary Ca2+ influx.
- Ca2+ homeostasis: bolster clearance and buffering programs to curb calpain activation and mitochondrial overload.
- Inflammation/fibrosis: bias expression toward anti-inflammatory and anti-fibrotic regulators to limit fibro-adipogenic replacement and preserve regenerative capacity. Together, these effects address multiple DMD pathologies without touching dystrophin. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8063049/?utm_source=openai))

Translational path
- Delivery: Systemic AAV with muscle-tropic capsids is clinically advanced and scalable; the reader–actuator payload is compact and AAV-compatible. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11866442/?utm_source=openai))
- Pharmacology: Activation is restricted to dystrophic nuclei via chromatin logic (± calpain gate), minimizing exposure of healthy tissues. Tunability derives from reader affinity/valency and activator strength.
- Clinical positioning: Adjunct or standalone disease-modifying therapy, potentially combinable with steroids or anti-fibrotics. Distinct from dystrophin-restorative approaches; mechanism leverages the disease epigenome as the therapeutic input. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38508835/?utm_source=openai))

Risk assessment and mitigations
- Risk: Reader promiscuity or activation at unintended sites. Mitigation: engineer dual-mark cooperativity and benchmark off-target transcriptional drift in healthy muscle.
- Risk: Insufficient potency. Mitigation: optimize reader geometry and activation domain strength; select mark constellations with highest enrichment at functionally validated enhancers.
- Risk: Immunogenicity. Mitigation: use human-derived modular domains and conservative expression levels; standard AAV de-risking strategies.

Milestones
- Year 1: Map candidate mark constellations; nominate reader pairs and validate disease-selective chromatin binding in nuclei.
- Year 2: Demonstrate selective activation of compensatory gene modules and favorable pathway shifts in human DMD myotubes and mdx muscle.
- Year 3: Show functional benefit with safety margins in dystrophic muscle and define a manufacturing-ready AAV construct for IND-enabling studies.

Impact
If successful, this establishes a new therapeutic class: disease-chromatin-gated gene regulators that read the pathology to drive its own compensation—generalizable beyond DMD wherever stable epigenetic signatures mark diseased cells. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41394756/?fc=None&ff=20251215130744&v=2.18.0.post22+67771e2&utm_source=openai))

text:
Title
Context-gated, DSB-free epigenetic “myogenic lock” in muscle satellite cells for dystrophin-agnostic therapy of Duchenne muscular dystrophy

Background and Rationale
Dystrophin loss renders myofibers damage-prone, producing chronic cycles of necrosis and a cytokine field (TGF-β/SMAD, NF-κB) that impairs satellite cell differentiation and sustains fibrosis. TGF-β/SMAD3 directly antagonizes myogenic transcription factors, providing a mechanistic basis for regeneration failure. Fibro-adipogenic progenitors (FAPs) are the principal collagen source, while satellite cells remain present but functionally skewed, indicating that restoring satellite-cell myogenesis without dystrophin replacement could improve muscle quality. Fibrotic stiffening elevates YAP/TAZ-TEAD activity, integrating with TGF-β to reinforce a non-regenerative niche. Therefore, the disease state provides orthogonal, cell-extrinsic inputs—sustained inflammation and stiffness—that can be converted into control signals for selective, durable reprogramming of satellite cells toward productive myogenesis. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC312830/?utm_source=openai))

Atomic Strategy
Write an intrinsic, heritable bias in satellite-cell chromatin—an epigenetic “myogenic lock”—but only in niches exhibiting sustained mechano-inflammatory signatures of dystrophic pathology, using DSB-free CRISPR epigenome editors that simultaneously lift myogenic enhancers and silence pro-fibrotic/anti-myogenic nodes.

Central Hypothesis
If disease-context signals (stiffness-driven YAP/TAZ and chronic NF-κB/TGF-β activity) gate a one-time, DSB-free epigenetic edit in satellite cells that activates endogenous myogenic circuitry and represses fibrosis-amplifying loci, then these cells will resist anti-myogenic cues and continuously contribute to muscle repair despite persistent dystrophin deficiency. ([journals.physiology.org](https://journals.physiology.org/doi/10.1152/ajpcell.00541.2024?utm_source=openai))

Specific Aim 1: Build and validate a YAP/TAZ- and inflammation/TGF-β-gated, split-dCas9 “myogenic lock” circuit in human myogenic cells
- Design: AAV-delivered, split dCas9 effector system under two inputs: (i) a TEAD-responsive synthetic enhancer (e.g., multimerized TEAD sites) that integrates YAP/TAZ nuclear activity from stiff niches; and (ii) an NF-κB/SMAD-responsive promoter. Coincidence and duration are required to reconstitute dCas9 effectors and trigger a recombinase “memory” flip, enforcing permanency while minimizing basal activity. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/6992423/?utm_source=openai))
- Epigenetic write: Guide sets target (a) endogenous myogenic super-enhancers (CRISPRa via dCas9-p300/activator) and (b) cis-regulatory elements driving anti-myogenic/pro-fibrotic programs (CRISPRi/epigenetic repression via dCas9-KRAB or H3K9 writer), establishing mutual inhibition between competing fates without DNA breaks. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6981169/?utm_source=openai))
- Readouts: Durable activation of MyoD/MyoG programs despite TGF-β exposure; repression of TEAD/YAP targets associated with fibrosis; maintenance of myogenic differentiation on stiff substrates. Mechanistic validation includes chromatin marks and transcriptional state stability after withdrawal of signals. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC312830/?utm_source=openai))

Specific Aim 2: Test efficacy of the “myogenic lock” in dystrophic muscle contexts
- In vitro dystrophic niche modeling: Apply sustained TGF-β/NF-κB cues and stiff matrices to primary human myogenic cultures to emulate DMD-like mechano-inflammatory context; assess whether the lock sustains myogenic differentiation and fusion while attenuating ECM/fibrotic gene induction. ([journals.physiology.org](https://journals.physiology.org/doi/10.1152/ajpcell.00541.2024?utm_source=openai))
- In vivo proof-of-principle in mouse models: Deliver the gated editors using myotropic AAV capsids with documented mononuclear-cell transduction (e.g., AAVMYO-class variants) and benchmark against serotypes with limited MuSC transduction to quantify delivery gaps. Endpoints: myofiber regeneration indices, fibrosis burden, satellite-cell lineage output, and persistence of epigenetic edits. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9344975/?utm_source=openai))

Specific Aim 3: Establish a translational delivery path
- In vivo route: Optimize engineered, myotropic capsids for mononuclear cell access in dystrophic muscle, guided by recent reports of improved delivery to muscle-resident cells in disease settings. Evaluate dose–response and biodistribution to minimize off-target organ exposure. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11987650/?utm_source=openai))
- Ex vivo autologous route: As a parallel path, install the lock in patient-derived satellite cells ex vivo followed by focal intramuscular implantation to high-need muscle groups, leveraging feasibility data for human satellite-cell isolation and engraftment in focal indications. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5918346/?utm_source=openai))

Innovation
- Disease-context computation: Converts stiffness and inflammation—robust, orthogonal hallmarks of DMD—into signals that confine editing to pathological niches, reducing on-target burden in healthy tissue. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39925133/?utm_source=openai))
- Break-free, multiplexed epigenome writing: Uses dCas9-based activation and repression to create an asymmetric, durable bias toward myogenesis without introducing DSBs, addressing genotoxicity and large-payload limitations. ([tandfonline.com](https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/pdf/10.2217/epi-2023-0281?utm_source=openai))
- Memory of cure: A recombinase “flip” captures the edited state, ensuring persistence after transient editor expression and limiting chronic immunogenic exposure.

Feasibility and Prior Art Check
- Biology: TGF-β/SMAD antagonizes myogenic factors; NF-κB sustains inflammatory inhibition; YAP/TAZ integrates stiffness to drive fibrogenic programs in FAPs and modulates fate in muscle progenitors—supporting the choice of inputs. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC312830/?utm_source=openai))
- Tools: TEAD-responsive synthetic enhancers (e.g., 8xGTIIC) are established activity reporters adaptable as disease sensors; CRISPR epigenome editors (dCas9-p300/KRAB) are validated for enhancer tuning; split-protein and recombinase memory systems enable conditional assembly and durability. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/6992423/?utm_source=openai))
- Delivery: AAV transduction of satellite cells in vivo is challenging but not zero; engineered capsids (MyoAAV, AAVMYO2) increase delivery to muscle-resident mononuclear cells, and focal ex vivo implantation of autologous satellite cells is a plausible bridge for initial clinical testing. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4288464/?utm_source=openai))
- Novelty: No prior DMD study was found that uses a stiffness- and inflammation-gated, DSB-free epigenome-editing plus recombinase-memory approach to permanently bias satellite-cell fate toward myogenesis. Related uses of CRISPRa/i and YAP/TAZ reporters exist, but not this integrated, pathology-sensing lock focused on satellite-cell fate control in dystrophic muscle. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6981169/?utm_source=openai))

Outcomes and Readouts
- Primary: Increased myonuclear accretion from satellite cells, improved fiber caliber distributions, reduced collagen deposition, and sustained myogenic transcriptional programs under chronic TGF-β/NF-κB exposure. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC312830/?utm_source=openai))
- Mechanistic: Targeted chromatin changes at myogenic enhancers and TEAD/NF-κB/SMAD-associated cis-regulatory elements; durable recombinase-flipped state in edited satellite cells.

Risk Mitigation
- Off-target epigenetic effects: Use compact, high-specificity guide sets; confine effector expression by dual-input gating and temporal integration to require sustained disease signals. Bench off-target chromatin profiling against primary myogenic cells. ([tandfonline.com](https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/pdf/10.2217/epi-2023-0281?utm_source=openai))
- Delivery uncertainty: Dual-path delivery (engineered AAV and ex vivo focal implantation) de-risks translation; early clinical testing can prioritize focal muscles where ex vivo implantation is clinically practical. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5918346/?utm_source=openai))

Milestones
- Year 1: Build and validate gated epigenetic lock and memory in human myogenic cells under mechano-inflammatory contexts; define guide sets and minimal enhancer/promoter motifs. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/6992423/?utm_source=openai))
- Year 2: In vivo efficacy and safety in dystrophic mice; compare delivery routes/capsids; establish durability and reversibility boundaries.
- Year 3: Preclinical package for IND-enabling studies focusing on focal-muscle ex vivo implantation; biodistribution, immunogenicity, and tumorigenicity assessments.

Impact
This project reframes DMD therapy as control of regenerative state rather than replacement of the missing structural protein. By writing a context-gated, durable myogenic bias into satellite cells without correcting dystrophin, it addresses regeneration failure and fibrosis as coupled systems problems—potentially synergizing with future dystrophin-restoration strategies while providing independent functional benefit. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37324396/?utm_source=openai))

text:
Title: Stress-gated CRISPRa upregulation of junctophilin‑1 to recompact triads and suppress pathological Ca2+ entry in Duchenne muscular dystrophy

Integrated hypothesis-question
Can converting dystrophic Ca2+ stress into a control signal to upregulate endogenous junctophilin‑1 (JPH1) in adult myofibers restore fetal-like triad geometry, confine excitation–contraction Ca2+ microdomains, and thereby reduce store‑operated Ca2+ entry (SOCE), necrosis, and fibrosis without touching the dystrophin locus? In DMD, triad components (including JPH1) are degraded or mislocalized, leading to E–C uncoupling and enhanced SOCE; targeted JPH1 restoration could attack Ca2+ dysregulation at its structural source. Evidence: JPH1 is a required triad tether in skeletal muscle E–C coupling; dystrophin-deficient muscles show calpain-1–mediated proteolysis/dissociation of JPH1; and SOCE via STIM1–Orai1 is upregulated and disease-modifying in DMD models. To date, gene therapy aimed at increasing JPH1 in dystrophin‑deficient skeletal muscle has not been reported; CRISPRa delivery to muscle is feasible with compact activators. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40097154/?utm_source=openai))

Atomic strategy
Let dystrophic Ca2+ signals gate a muscle-targeted CRISPRa that lifts endogenous JPH1 modestly (≈1.5–2×). This single lever re-compacts T‑tubule–SR junctions, improving CaV1.1–RyR1 coupling fidelity and shrinking ectopic Ca2+ microdomains that drive SOCE activation, calpain activity, and degeneration. A Ca2+‑responsive promoter aligns JPH1 induction to periods of mechanical stress, limiting chronic remodeling. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40097154/?utm_source=openai))

Specific aims
Aim 1. Build a stress-gated, muscle-directed CRISPRa‑JPH1 system and validate on-target upregulation and triad re‑compaction.
- Construct: Single‑AAV “MyoAAV‑CRISPRa‑JPH1” carrying dCasMINI‑VPR under a synthetic promoter with multimerized NFAT elements fused to a myofiber‑biased minimal promoter; express a gRNA array tiling the proximal JPH1 promoter/enhancers. Use muscle‑tropic MyoAAV capsid for skeletal and limited cardiac transduction; include microRNA response elements (e.g., miR‑122) to suppress hepatic expression. Rationale: Single‑AAV CRISPRa in muscle is validated; NFAT cis‑elements confer Ca2+‑responsive transcriptional gating. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-025-57831-5?utm_source=openai))
- In vitro: Differentiate human DMD iPSC‑myotubes and mdx myotubes. Readouts: JPH1 mRNA/protein, super‑resolution imaging of JPH1/RyR1/CaV1.1 colocalization; EM quantification of triad density/spacing; Ca2+ spark frequency; SOCE (Mn2+ quench; Fura‑2 store‑depletion protocol); calpain activity.
- Stress-gating test: Elicit Ca2+ stress (electrical pacing, hypo‑osmotic stretch) and quantify promoter on/off kinetics and reversibility.

Aim 2. Test efficacy in mdx and D2.mdx mice with activity‑aligned dosing.
- Dosing: Systemic MyoAAV‑CRISPRa‑JPH1 at low, mid, high vg/kg; intramuscular contralateral controls. Eccentric contraction treadmill bouts at prespecified weeks to engage NFAT gating.
- Primary endpoints (12–16 weeks post‑dose): Triad ultrastructure (TEM), JPH1 levels, SOCE amplitude and activation threshold in single fibers; in situ EDL force drop after eccentric contractions; serum CK; histology (necrosis, central nuclei), hydroxyproline (fibrosis), macrophage/Neutrophil infiltration.
- Secondary endpoints: RNA‑seq for off‑target transcriptional changes; whole‑body function (treadmill endurance, grip); diaphragm contractility ex vivo.
- Mechanism checks: STIM1/Orai1 protein and colocalization; resting [Ca2+]i and calpain-1 activity; test whether benefits track with reduced SOCE burden. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20427714/?utm_source=openai))

Aim 3. Safety, durability, and translational controls.
- Safety pharmacology: Twitch/tetanus kinetics to exclude contraction‑slowing; ECG to monitor inadvertent cardiac effects; biodistribution and immunogenicity (anti‑capsid, anti‑Cas). Stop‑criteria: >15% slowing of twitch rise/relaxation or off‑target activation by RNA‑seq in non‑muscle tissues.
- Durability and re‑dosing: Follow cohorts to 9–12 months; quantify JPH1 expression decay and function. Explore LNP‑mRNA boosts for dCasMINI‑VPR to avoid AAV redosing barriers.
- Comparator arms: (i) constitutive CRISPRa‑JPH1 (no NFAT gating) to test safety/efficacy trade‑offs; (ii) exploratory JPH1+HSPG2 dual‑target CRISPRa to evaluate orthogonal reinforcement of the basement membrane and growth‑factor presentation. Perlecan’s BM roles justify combination but will be advanced only if JPH1 alone is sub‑therapeutic. ([frontiersin.org](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/physiology/articles/10.3389/fphys.2023.1189731/full?utm_source=openai))

Key design choices and justifications
- Target choice (JPH1): JPH1 is the skeletal‑muscle triad tether; its loss or proteolysis in dystrophin deficiency correlates with E–C uncoupling. Modest upregulation aims to restore native architecture without ectopic structures. ([journals.physiology.org](https://journals.physiology.org/doi/10.1152/physrev.00024.2021?utm_source=openai))
- Disease‑aligned control: NFAT‑based promoter gates CRISPRa activity to high‑Ca2+ states typical of injury/strain, minimizing constitutive remodeling. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6019284/?utm_source=openai))
- Vector platform: Single‑AAV delivery of compact CRISPRa to muscle has been demonstrated; MyoAAV achieves skeletal and cardiac tropism with superior muscle specificity, supporting clinical scalability. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-025-57831-5?utm_source=openai))
- Systems‑level effect: Re‑compacted triads should reduce aberrant microdomain Ca2+ that recruits SOCE, addressing a validated pathogenic axis in DMD. Combination with perlecan activation is reserved as an orthogonal reinforcement of sarcolemma–ECM load distribution if needed. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20427714/?utm_source=openai))

Experimental methods summary
- CRISPRa components: dCasMINI‑VPR; U6‑driven multi‑gRNA cassette (3–4 guides) to JPH1 proximal promoter/enhancers; SPc5‑12 or CK8m basal myofiber element downstream of 6×‑NFAT repeats; WPRE‑less design to reduce cargo size; microRNA response elements for liver restriction.
- Ca2+ physiology: Spark imaging (confocal line‑scan), SOCE by thapsigargin store depletion and Mn2+ quench; resting [Ca2+]i with ratiometric dyes; calpain activity by casein substrate.
- Structure: TEM stereology for triad counts and spacing; STED microscopy for CaV1.1–RyR1–JPH1 nanodomain alignment.
- Function: In situ EDL and diaphragm force/fatigue protocols; eccentric injury assay; ambulatory behavior and endurance.

Milestones and decision gates
- Stage 1 (months 0–9): In vitro proof (≥1.5× JPH1; ≥30% SOCE reduction; no slowing of twitch Ca2+ transients). Go if achieved in ≥2 DMD lines.
- Stage 2 (months 6–18): mdx efficacy (≥25% reduction in force drop after eccentric contractions; ≥30% reduction in CK; histologic improvement). Advance to D2.mdx if met.
- Stage 3 (months 12–30): Durability/safety, NHP biodistribution with MyoAAV‑CRISPRa‑JPH1 regulatory‑grade lot; finalize clinical candidate.

Clinical translation plan
- Indication: Ambulatory and non‑ambulatory DMD with preserved skeletal muscle mass. Exclude severe cardiomyopathy in phase 1 due to skeletal‑specific target (JPH1).
- Dose and route: Single IV MyoAAV‑CRISPRa‑JPH1; staggered dose‑escalation with steroid cover.
- Endpoints (Phase 1/2): Safety; biomarker panel (plasma CK, myomiRs), muscle biopsy for JPH1/triad metrics and SOCE markers; function (NSAA/6MWT for ambulatory; PUL/respiratory measures for non‑ambulatory).
- Combination potential: If partial responders, evaluate add‑on HSPG2 CRISPRa or SERCA‑centric Ca2+ handling modulators in separate cohorts, maintaining dystrophin‑independent mechanism. ([frontiersin.org](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/physiology/articles/10.3389/fphys.2023.1189731/full?utm_source=openai))

Risk assessment and mitigations
- Over‑compaction/arrhythmogenic risk: Focus on skeletal muscle; avoid cardiac JPH2 targeting. Monitor twitch/tetanus kinetics; set upper JPH1 expression bounds.
- Immunogenicity (Cas/capsid): Use minimal dCas; humanized activator; transient immunosuppression; screen pre‑existing AAV NAbs.
- Off‑target transcription: gRNA tiling restricted to JPH1 regulatory DNA; RNA‑seq and ATAC‑seq safety screens.

Why this is the right question now
DMD therapies that correct dystrophin only partially normalize Ca2+ handling. Asking whether a stress‑gated, precision increase of an endogenous triad tether can collapse pathological Ca2+ microdomains tests an underexploited structural primitive of muscle function. It aligns with fetal logic, uses proven delivery (single‑AAV CRISPRa) and validated disease axes (JPH1 loss; SOCE upregulation), and stays dystrophin‑independent. ([journals.physiology.org](https://journals.physiology.org/doi/10.1152/physrev.00024.2021?utm_source=openai))

text:
Title
Damage-gated enhancer editing to convert fibrotic fibroblasts into basement membrane–producing, perivascular-like support cells in Duchenne muscular dystrophy

Hypothesis–Question
If we open chromatin at endogenous basement membrane (BM) and mural-cell loci specifically in injury-activated fibro/adipogenic progenitors (FAPs), will these cells reposition to vascular/myofiber BM interfaces, switch from fibrillar-scar output to thin BM assembly, stabilize microvasculature, and thereby reduce muscle injury in DMD—without restoring dystrophin?

Rationale
- In DMD, membrane fragility triggers cycles of necrosis and inflammation that expand PDGFRα+ FAPs; TGF-β/mechanotransduction (YAP/TAZ) biases them into collagen I/III–secreting myofibroblasts, stiffening endomysium and sustaining pathology. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6519730/?utm_source=openai))
- Dystrophic muscle exhibits vascular dysfunction with reduced perfusion, leak, and altered microvascular architecture; improving capillary density or pericyte coverage ameliorates disease features. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9979239/?utm_source=openai))
- Perivascular identity and BM assembly associate with PDGFRβ/CSPG4 (NG2) and N‑cadherin–mediated endothelial contact; BM integrity relies on collagen IV, laminins, nidogens, and perlecan (HSPG2). Redirecting fibroblasts toward BM adhesion (α6β1 laminin, α1β1 collagen IV) and BM secretion could replace bulky scar with a compliant, protective sheath. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9199463/?utm_source=openai))
- CRISPR epigenetic activators (dCas9–p300) can open enhancers in vivo; injury/hypoxia/inflammation-responsive synthetic promoters enable spatially and temporally restricted expression. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25849900/?utm_source=openai))
- AAV delivery to FAPs is feasible with appropriate serotype/promoter selection. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42437777/?utm_source=openai))

Atomic strategy
Flip the fibroblast’s ECM “default” by enhancer-level activation of perivascular/BM programs in lesion-activated FAPs, so they preferentially align to existing BM tracks (vessels and myofibers) and deposit collagen IV/laminin nets rather than interstitial collagen I/III scars.

Specific aims
1) Build a damage-gated AAV epigenetic editor that activates perivascular/BM loci in FAPs.
2) Test whether edited FAPs reposition to BM interfaces, suppress interstitial fibrosis, and stabilize microvasculature in mdx muscle.
3) Evaluate safety, durability, and reversibility of the edited state.

Design and methods
- Editing payload
  - Editor: split-intein dual AAV5 encoding Sa-dCas9–p300core (to fit AAV) under a compact synthetic “injury gate” promoter (SMAD/HRE/TEAD composite) plus miRNA detargeting sites for myomiRs (miR-1/133/206) and endothelial-enriched miRNAs to prevent expression in myofibers and ECs. The gate leverages TGF-β/SMAD, hypoxia (HIF), and stiffness/YAP-TEAD activity that spike in dystrophic lesions. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6519730/?utm_source=openai))
  - Guides: multiplexed U6 gRNAs targeting validated enhancers near PDGFRB, CSPG4, COL4A1/2, LAMB1/2, NID1, HSPG2 to induce a BM/mural program. Include optional CRISPRi (dCas9–KRAB) mini-cassette with one or two gRNAs to dampen COL1A1/3A1 super-enhancers if BM activation alone is insufficient; KRAB is placed under a weaker copy of the injury gate to avoid over-suppression. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25849900/?utm_source=openai))
- Targeting to FAPs
  - Capsid/promoter: AAV5 with a 826-bp Pdgfra promoter to bias transduction/expression to FAPs after intramuscular delivery; confirm with AAV9 as secondary option shown to infect FAPs in PDGFRα-Cas9 mice. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42437777/?utm_source=openai))
- Model and dosing
  - mdx mice (8–12 weeks). TA and diaphragm injections with 1–2×10^11 vg/TA per vector (both editor halves + gRNA vector). Repeat once at 3–4 weeks if needed to cover lesion waves.
- Readouts (4–8 weeks)
  - Cell-intrinsic conversion: single-cell RNA-seq/ATAC of PDGFRα+ cells to assess upregulation of PDGFRB/CSPG4/NOTCH3 and BM genes (COL4A1/2, LAMB1/2, NID1, HSPG2); ChIP–H3K27ac at targeted enhancers. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9199463/?utm_source=openai))
  - Repositioning/adhesion shift: immunostaining for CDH2 (N‑cadherin), integrin α6 and α1 on edited FAPs; quantification of cell alignment along CD31+ capillaries and dystrophin-independent myofiber BM (laminin/collagen IV). ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6314553/?utm_source=openai))
  - Matrix switch and mechanics: SHG and IHC to quantify COL1/3 vs COL4/laminin ratios; AFM nanoindentation for endomysial stiffness. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9364315/?utm_source=openai))
  - Microvascular function: pericyte coverage (NG2/PDGFRβ), Evans blue/dextran leakage, capillary density and perfusion (laser Doppler/contrast ultrasound). Expect increased coverage/linearization and reduced leak. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6949491/?utm_source=openai))
  - Muscle outcomes: serum CK, in situ TA force, contraction-induced damage assays; activity wheel performance. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9979239/?utm_source=openai))
- Controls
  - AAV-null; injury-gate–driven dCas9 without p300; KRAB-only anti-COL1/3; non-targeting gRNAs; positive control for angiogenesis (e.g., Flt1 loss-of-function model reference). ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6932757/?utm_source=openai))

Milestones and decision points
- M1: ≥3× induction of BM genes and ≥2× increase in H3K27ac at targeted enhancers in FAPs ex vivo; proceed to in vivo.
- M2: In mdx TA, ≥30% of edited PDGFRα+ cells adopt PDGFRβ/CSPG4^high state with BM adhesion markers and align to CD31+ vessels/myofiber BM.
- M3: Tissue-level shift: ≥40% reduction in COL1/3 area fraction with ≥30% increase in COL4/laminin at endomysium; ≥25% reduction in vascular leak; ≥15% improvement in specific force.
- No-go: evidence of arteriolar lumen narrowing (>10%), ischemic necrosis, or off-target activation in ECs/myofibers triggers pivot to transient LNP-mRNA CRISPRa delivery or removal of COL1/3 KRAB arm.

Risk management
- Mural over-coverage/stenosis: limit editor expression with the injury gate and titratable degron-fused dCas9–p300; incorporate NOT gates with cell-specific miRNA target sites to detarget ECs/myofibers. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7846768/?utm_source=openai))
- Off-target chromatin activation: use multiple short gRNAs per enhancer with activity/binding orthogonalization; whole-transcriptome and off-target ATAC monitoring; sunset expression as lesion resolves (hypoxia/TGF-β down). ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25849900/?utm_source=openai))
- Immunogenicity: use Sa-dCas9 variants with humanized sequences; local (intramuscular) dosing; consider transient steroid cover per clinical gene therapy practice.

Feasibility and path to translation
- Payload and delivery have precedents for in vivo enhancer activation and for FAP-selective AAV expression. A first-in-human path would prioritize localized limb muscles with image-guided intramuscular AAV5-PDGFRα-gated dosing, biomarker monitoring of collagen IV/laminin turnover, and perfusion/leak endpoints, while entirely avoiding dystrophin manipulation to maintain orthogonality to current exon-skipping/micro-dystrophin standards. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5732045/?utm_source=openai))

Expected outcome
By converting lesion-activated fibroblasts into BM-producing, perivascular-like support cells at the sites and times they are pathogenic, the proposal aims to replace stiff scar with a compliant, vessel-stabilizing sheath that distributes mechanical load and reduces inflammatory traffic—attenuating core DMD pathophysiology without targeting dystrophin. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6519730/?utm_source=openai))

text:
Title
Event-gated gene therapy for Duchenne muscular dystrophy using membrane-anchor displacement to activate intrinsic repair and calcium-control programs

Background and significance
- In DMD, loss of dystrophin destabilizes the sarcolemma, causing contraction-induced microtears, pathological Ca2+ influx, calpain activation, mitochondrial dysfunction, and repeated necrosis–regeneration with inflammation and fibrosis. Ca2+ overload is a convergent driver of myofiber death. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10330733/?utm_source=openai))
- Damaged myofibers rapidly expose phosphatidylserine (PS), recruit annexins, dysferlin, and ESCRT machinery to patch lesions; Annexin A6 is a key repair effector and recombinant ANXA6 reduces injury in vivo. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4915191/?utm_source=openai))
- Inner-leaflet lipid remodeling accompanies injury. The MARCKS effector domain electrostatically sequesters PIP2 at the membrane; Ca2+/calmodulin binding or PKC phosphorylation rapidly displaces MARCKS from the membrane, releasing PIP2 and changing local signaling—an intrinsic, reversible switch that reports sustained Ca2+ microdomains. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC1304070/?utm_source=openai))
- AAV vectors enable efficient, myofiber-directed gene delivery across species with muscle-tropic capsids. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4641337/?utm_source=openai))

Hypothesis–goal (inseparable)
If we convert loss of membrane compartmentalization during dystrophic stress into an intrinsic “go” signal, then myofibers can autonomously and transiently express protective payloads (membrane repair and Ca2+ control) only during pathological episodes, thereby reducing necrosis without constitutive overexpression or targeting the dystrophin gene.

Atomic strategy
Exploit Ca2+-driven displacement of a membrane-tethered anchor to liberate a latent transcriptional effector. Specifically, use a MARCKS-effector–based membrane tether that sequesters a destabilized transcription factor (TF) at the inner leaflet in resting muscle; sustained lesion-associated Ca2+/calmodulin causes anchor release and nuclear entry. This couples circuit activation to the temporal pattern of pathological Ca2+ microdomains characteristic of membrane failure in DMD. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8063049/?utm_source=openai))

Specific aims
1) Engineer and calibrate a MARCKS-anchor displacement transcriptional switch in myofibers.
2) Demonstrate event-gated protection in human DMD iPSC–derived myotubes and in vivo in mdx mice.
3) Establish translational parameters: delivery, dose–response, durability, and safety.

Research plan

Aim 1. Engineering and calibration
- Construct: AAV cassette expressing a myofiber-specific, membrane-tethered TF (e.g., compact TF with PEST degron) fused to a MARCKS effector domain (ED) and N-terminal myristoylation signal. In the basal state, positive charges in MARCKS-ED bind acidic lipids and sequester PIP2, holding the TF at the membrane and exposing the degron. During sustained Ca2+ microdomains, Ca2+/calmodulin binds MARCKS-ED, neutralizes electrostatics, and releases the fusion into the cytosol; unmasking an NLS enables nuclear import to drive a compact synthetic promoter controlling a therapeutic payload. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC1304070/?utm_source=openai))
- Temporal filter: The TF carries a short half-life degron so single, brief Ca2+ spikes fail to accumulate nuclear TF; only repeated or prolonged microdomains surpass expression threshold (chronic-damage discriminator). ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8063049/?utm_source=openai))
- Bench calibration: In C2C12 myotubes and human DMD iPSC myotubes, quantify TF nuclear translocation and reporter output under: (i) electrical pacing (physiological transients), (ii) laser wounding, and (iii) ionomycin-evoked sustained Ca2+ plateaus. Define activation criteria (duration–amplitude phase space) and leak rate. Validate dependence on Ca2+/calmodulin with pharmacologic modulators. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8063049/?utm_source=openai))
- Alternative anchors (risk hedge): Replace MARCKS-ED with PH(PLCδ1) to respond to PIP2 loss near injury; select variant based on best physiological discrimination. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0304415798000112?utm_source=openai))

Aim 2. Event-gated protection in cellular and animal models
- Therapeutic outputs (compact, non-dystrophin):
  - Membrane repair: Annexin A6 (ANXA6) to stabilize repair caps and promote lesion constriction. ([journals.physiology.org](https://journals.physiology.org/doi/full/10.1152/physrev.00037.2014?doi=10.1152%2Fphysrev.00037.2014&utm_source=openai))
  - Ca2+ control: Calpastatin to restrain calpain activity during Ca2+ overload. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8063049/?utm_source=openai))
- In vitro efficacy: In DMD iPSC myotubes subjected to repetitive laser wounding, quantify: time to reseal (FM dyes), Ca2+ transient area-under-curve, calpain activity, mitochondrial membrane potential, and survival with MARCKS-switch+payload versus constitutive payloads and vector controls. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4915191/?utm_source=openai))
- In vivo efficacy: Systemic AAV9 or next-generation muscle-tropic capsid delivery in mdx mice. Endpoints at 4–12 weeks: Evans Blue uptake (sarcolemmal leak), serum CK, in situ force after eccentric contractions, histopathology (central nuclei, fibrosis), mitochondrial pathology, and inflammation markers, comparing MARCKS-switch+payload vs constitutive payloads and null. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9344975/?utm_source=openai))
- Mechanism verification: Intravital imaging of reporter and endogenous ANXA6 recruitment at lesions to confirm event-coupled induction; calcium imaging to correlate switch activation with sustained microdomains. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4915191/?utm_source=openai))

Aim 3. Translation parameters and safety
- Dose finding and biodistribution: Titrate vector genomes/kg to map transduction and on-target activation under voluntary wheel running (physiologic load) vs forced eccentric exercise (pathologic load). Use myofiber-restricted promoters to minimize off-tissue expression. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4641337/?utm_source=openai))
- Off-target activation analysis: Assess liver and heart for circuit activation under systemic inflammation or ischemia; include miRNA target sites to de-target non-myofiber lineages if needed.
- Durability and reversibility: Longitudinal tracking of reporter “on-time” fractions and payload expression to demonstrate event-limited bursts rather than chronic expression.
- Immunogenicity: Monitor anti-capsid and anti-transgene responses; use human proteins (ANXA6, calpastatin) to minimize neoantigens. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4098646/?utm_source=openai))
- Manufacturability: Single- or dual-vector AAV depending on payload size. Use compact regulatory elements and 2A linkers to remain within packaging limits. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27459604/?utm_source=openai))

Innovation and novelty
- Converts an intrinsic, lesion-proximal biophysical signature—sustained Ca2+ microdomains that displace a membrane anchor—into a therapeutic command. To our knowledge, no myofiber-targeted AAV therapy has used MARCKS-based anchor displacement as an event-gated switch for DMD. The approach avoids dystrophin targeting and constitutive transgene burden while addressing membrane instability and Ca2+-driven necrosis central to DMD pathology. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10330733/?utm_source=openai))

Anticipated outcomes and decision points
- Success criteria: Reduced Evans Blue uptake, CK, and force deficit after eccentric contractions with equivalent or lower total transgene exposure than constitutive strategies; demonstration that protective expression scales with damage frequency. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10330733/?utm_source=openai))
- No-go criteria: High basal leak in resting muscle, failure to discriminate physiological twitches, or toxicity from repeated brief activations. If observed, pivot to PH(PLCδ1)-based anchoring or add a second temporal gate (e.g., promoter requiring cumulative TF). ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0304415798000112?utm_source=openai))

Optional extension (exploratory)
- Lesion-PS co-gating: Combine MARCKS switch with a PS-sensing input (using high-affinity lactadherin C2–based biosensor driving a co-required cofactor) to further restrict activation to true membrane lesions where PS is exposed. SynNotch-like architectures are powerful but classically require trans-ligand pulling; thus, we limit PS use here to biochemical co-gating rather than force-gated Notch cleavage. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10373266/?utm_source=openai))

Impact
A membrane-anchor–displacement switch directly ties therapeutic dose to the frequency and duration of sarcolemmal failure events. By boosting annexin-mediated repair and restraining calpain only when and where needed, this approach addresses upstream triggers of DMD degeneration, offering a path to a durable, scalable adjunct or alternative to dystrophin-centric therapies. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6819108/?utm_source=openai))

Title
Tension-gated proteolytic release to preempt contraction-induced injury in Duchenne muscle

Hypothesis/Goal (merged)
If early, subcatastrophic contractile tension in dystrophin-deficient myofibers is converted into brief nuclear transcriptional pulses, then endogenous membrane-repair and Ca2+-handling programs can be deployed before sarcolemmal tearing and Ca2+ overload, reducing necrosis, inflammation, and fibrosis without re-expressing dystrophin. DMD pathogenesis is driven by contraction-induced membrane rupture, aberrant Ca2+ influx with calpain/mitochondrial injury, and secondary inflammation/fibrosis; membrane-repair machineries (annexins, dysferlin/ESCRT) are inducible but too slow or insufficiently primed. Therefore, a gene therapy that uses internal tension as an early-warning input and activates these protective systems anticipatorily should change the damage–repair race in favor of the cell. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10811648/?utm_source=openai))

Atomic strategy
Exploit talin–vinculin mechanosensing at costameric adhesions as a force-thresholded trigger to liberate a membrane-tethered transcriptional activator via proteolytic cleavage; repeated low-amplitude activations are integrated by a leaky “load-history” module to gate expression of a minimal, rapid-acting membrane-repair program. Talin rod domains unfold in the 5–10 pN regime to expose vinculin-binding sites that recruit active vinculin; we will couple this conformational event to protease proximity and cargo release without perturbing native adhesion mechanics. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3980218/?utm_source=openai))

Innovation and prior art check
- Mechanogenetic circuits exist (e.g., TRPV4- or Piezo1-driven promoters and ultrasound-Piezo1 control) but have not used talin–vinculin unfolding to trigger protease-gated release or been applied as an autonomous, activity-coupled DMD therapy. Our proposal differs by using cytoskeletal force as the input and a proteolytic release as the actuator, rather than Ca2+-channel activation per se. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7840132/?utm_source=openai))
- Talin-based constructs have been used as tension reporters, not as therapeutic actuators that drive gene expression via protease release in muscle. We find no reports of AAV-delivered talin/vinculin–protease transcriptional circuits for DMD. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4862330/?utm_source=openai))

Specific aims
1) Build and calibrate a talin–vinculin tension-gated protease-release sensor that produces nuclear pulses under physiologic myofibrillar loading but remains quiescent at rest.
2) Implement a genetic leaky integrator that converts repeated pulses into thresholded activation to avoid chronic signaling yet anticipate high-use periods.
3) Demonstrate preemptive protection in vivo in mdx muscle by upregulating a compact membrane-repair program, quantifying membrane stability, Ca2+ handling, inflammation, and fibrosis.

Approach

A. Sensor–actuator design (Aim 1)
- Architecture: A membrane-proximal scaffold bearing (i) a high-affinity vinculin-binding site (VBS) peptide derived from talin, fused to one half of a split TEV protease (sTEV-N), and (ii) a costamere-localized adaptor (e.g., α7β1-integrin tail–binding peptide) fused to the complementary protease half (sTEV-C). Active vinculin recruited to unfolded talin during contraction will bind the VBS, bringing sTEV halves into proximity for reconstitution. The reconstituted protease cleaves a cognate site in a nearby tether to release Gal4–VP64 (or a compact TALE/VPR) from the inner leaflet, triggering transcription from a compact UAS minimal promoter. Precedent: vinculin binding requires force-exposed talin VBS; split-protease–mediated membrane release can drive transcription in mammalian cells. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3980218/?utm_source=openai))
- Force thresholding: Choose VBS variants with defined vinculin affinities and spacer mechanics so recruitment occurs at forces typical of early contraction, not passive tone. Calibrate thresholds by traction assays and FRET-talin controls. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0006349525035325?utm_source=openai))
- Localization: Confine the circuit to costameres via β1D-integrin cytotail or ILK-binding motifs to sample relevant loads without competing with endogenous talin function (use low-expression, short-lived components to minimize stoichiometric interference). ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3589167/?utm_source=openai))
- Readouts: Nuclear TF pulse amplitude/duration; activation precedence relative to dye-uptake and CK release under eccentric contractions.

B. Load-history leaky integrator (Aim 2)
- Implement a time-integration layer by giving the released activator a tunable protein half-life (degron/PEST) so each pulse contributes a small increment; only when cumulative activity surpasses a setpoint does it cross-activate an effector promoter (AND gate via co-activator requirement). This frequency-to-amplitude conversion is a standard synthetic control motif and reduces false positives from sporadic events. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.17158?utm_source=openai))

C. Minimal effector cassette (Aim 3)
- Rationale: The fastest salvage pathway for sarcolemmal injury is annexin lattice “patching” and ESCRT-mediated scission; these are endogenous, Ca2+-sensitive, and effective when pre-positioned. We will encode a compact, two- to three-gene polycistron to bias this axis. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8155887/?utm_source=openai))
- Initial effector set (AAV-sized): AnxA6–P2A–AnxA1 ± CHMP4B. Annexin A1/A6 promote lattice formation and curvature at wounds; CHMP4B is a core ESCRT-III subunit for lesion shedding. Selection reflects cDNA size compatibility and mechanistic immediacy. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8155887/?utm_source=openai))
- Secondary readouts: Reduced Ca2+ spikes and calpain activation; preserved mitochondrial potential; reduced NF-κB activation; lowered macrophage infiltration and collagen deposition in vivo. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10330733/?utm_source=openai))

Vectors and delivery
- Dual-AAV system: Vector 1 (sensor + reporter) and Vector 2 (effector polycistron). Use myotropic, liver-detargeted capsids to lower dose and improve safety; compare AAV9 to recent muscle-tropic variants showing improved skeletal and cardiac transduction with reduced hepatic uptake. Employ muscle-specific promoters (e.g., CK8/C5-12) and intronic miRNA target sites to avoid off-muscle expression. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40989879/?utm_source=openai))
- Route and dose: Systemic tail-vein in mdx; begin at sub-therapeutic vg/kg and escalate with biodistribution and transduction quantification given dose-related AAV risks in muscle. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-024-52002-4?utm_source=openai))

Milestones and decision criteria
- In vitro (C2C12 myotubes): Sensor dynamic range ≥10-fold; activation precedes membrane dye uptake under controlled strain; integrator ON only after defined pulse frequency; no activation at rest.
- Ex vivo (intact muscle): Acute eccentric contraction shows reduced Evans Blue Dye uptake and blunted Ca2+ transients with circuit ON versus OFF. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3589167/?utm_source=openai))
- In vivo (mdx): At 8–12 weeks post-dosing, decreased serum CK, improved specific force, reduced macrophage infiltration and fibrosis versus controls; durability across exercise regimens.

Risk analysis and mitigations
- Off-target adhesion perturbation: Use VBS bait rather than engineering native talin; cap expression with weak promoters and degrons; confirm focal adhesion morphology is unaltered.
- Constitutive activation in stiff/fibrotic ECM: Integrator decay constant enforces OFF during rest; require dual-input (vinculin recruitment AND cofactor) to trigger cleavage.
- Immunogenicity of orthogonal parts: Humanize linkers and minimize steady-state abundance; AAV dose reduction via myotropic capsids to decrease vector-related toxicity. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-024-52002-4?utm_source=openai))
- Ineffective effector choice: Head-to-head screens comparing annexin-only, ESCRT-only, and combined cassettes; if insufficient, pivot to CRISPRa upregulation of endogenous repair genes using split activators (dual AAV) with the same sensor input.

Validation of mechanistic premises and novelty
- DMD damage cascade and availability of repair pathways are well-characterized. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10811648/?utm_source=openai))
- Talin unfolding exposes VBS that recruit vinculin at physiologic forces, providing a specific, thresholded mechanical readout. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3980218/?utm_source=openai))
- Mechanogenetic gene circuits have been demonstrated in non-muscle contexts, supporting feasibility of force-to-gene conversion, but not via talin–vinculin–protease release nor for DMD. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7840132/?utm_source=openai))
- Protease-triggered transcriptional release at membranes is established with viral protease sensors, validating the actuator concept. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4487218/?utm_source=openai))

Expected outcomes and interpretation
- If successful, tension pulses during normal activity will elicit short, anticipatory transcriptional bursts that pre-position annexins/ESCRT components, shortening tear “open time,” limiting Ca2+ overload and downstream injury. Improvements in membrane integrity and reduced inflammatory/fibrotic remodeling would confirm that shifting response timing, not merely expression level, is sufficient to alter DMD trajectory. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8155887/?utm_source=openai))

Translational path
- Optimization in canine DMD models after mdx validation; nonhuman primate biodistribution with selected myotropic capsid; CMC for dual-AAV; biomarkers: serum CK, MRI T2 mapping, microdystrophin-independent endpoints; initial FIH in non-ambulant adolescents with activity-linked dosing schedule to probe anticipatory protection while monitoring AAV safety. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-024-52002-4?utm_source=openai))

Go/no-go gates
- GO: ≥30% reduction in EBD uptake and ≥20% increase in specific force in mdx TA with acceptable histology at clinically plausible AAV doses.
- NO-GO: Constitutive activation at rest, adhesion defects, or lack of protection despite adequate transduction.
