Title
Dual-channel safe-harbor barcoding for one-amplicon quantification of HSCT engraftment and polyclonal reconstitution across all hematopoietic lineages

Central question-hypothesis
Can a single, safe-harbor–inserted barcode cassette that encodes two orthogonal information channels—a constant region for absolute donor marking and an adjacent high-entropy region for clonal identity—enable a one-amplicon assay that (i) confirms engraftment quantitatively and (ii) resolves polyclonal reconstitution dynamics across myeloid, lymphoid, erythroid, and megakaryocytic compartments for one year post-HSCT, including anucleate outputs via an RNA “mirror” of the barcode? We posit yes, if the cassette is integrated non-virally into human HSCs at a genomically validated safe harbor with stable expression and minimal positional effects, and is read out from DNA (nucleated cells) and from a compact, ubiquitously transcribed barcode RNA captured from reticulocytes and platelets. Prior work has barcoded HSPCs using integrating viruses or targeted AAV6 donors at AAVS1 for clonal tracking, but has not delivered a single-locus, non-viral, dual-channel design that couples engraftment quantification with lineage-wide clonal readout, nor extended that readout to anucleate compartments. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8065704/?utm_source=openai))

Atomic strategy
Place two independent information streams in one safe-harbor cassette: a conserved constant region (CRC) shared by all edited donor cells to quantify engraftment by digital PCR, immediately adjacent to a high-entropy variable region (HVR) encoding clone IDs for diversity and dynamics by targeted sequencing. Mirror the HVR sequence in a minimal Pol II transcript so the same primer pair retrieves the barcode from genomic DNA (nucleated lineages) and cDNA (reticulocytes/platelets), unifying the assay across all compartments. Platelet and reticulocyte RNA cargo are well documented and recoverable by RNA-seq/RT-PCR; thus, an expressed barcode can be captured from these anucleate outputs without accessing nucleated precursors. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3670814/?utm_source=openai))

Specific aims
- Aim 1: Engineer and validate a dual-channel barcode cassette at a human HSPC-safe harbor.
- Aim 2: Establish a one-amplicon clinical-style assay that simultaneously measures donor engraftment (CRC, dPCR) and clonal composition (HVR, amplicon-NGS) from DNA and RNA sources.
- Aim 3: Conduct a longitudinal HSCT pilot with barcoded “tracer” HSCs to quantify polyclonal reconstitution across all hematopoietic lineages, including platelets and reticulocytes, for 12 months.

Innovation
- One-locus, one-amplicon, two-channel readout merges donor engraftment and clonal diversity within a single analytical pipeline—distinct from STR/SNP chimerism (engraftment only), TCR/BCR repertoire (lymphoid-limited), or viral insertion-site/barcode methods (integration-site dependence, viral donors). ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8065704/?utm_source=openai))
- Non-viral safe-harbor integration of a compact, expressed barcode aligns with emerging clinical ex vivo HSPC editing practice while avoiding AAV donor use and random integration. We select CLYBL (or newer validated GSH such as Rogi loci) over AAVS1 given reports of variable silencing at AAVS1. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4294658/?utm_source=openai))
- RNA “mirror” extends clonal readout to platelets and reticulocytes, leveraging established platelet/reticulocyte transcript recovery in clinical workflows. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3670814/?utm_source=openai))

Approach

Aim 1: Cassette design, non-viral safe-harbor integration, and functional validation
- Safe harbor and guide selection
  - Primary target: CLYBL intron locus (reduced perturbation and robust expression versus AAVS1). Backup: newly validated Rogi1/2 sites. Include insulators only if required by expression stability tests to minimize cassette size. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4294658/?utm_source=openai))
- Cassette architecture (≤900 bp payload)
  - CRC: 80–120 bp synthetic sequence absent from the human genome, flanked by primer/probe sites for absolute quantification by dPCR/qPCR.
  - HVR: 20–28 bp degenerate barcode with sequence-level error-correcting constraints and Hamming distance ≥3 to mitigate dropouts and sequencing/PCR errors.
  - Minimal Pol II transcript: compact ubiquitous promoter (short EF1α/EFS or miniCMV, ~200–300 bp) driving a 120–180 bp intronless transcript containing the HVR in its 3′ UTR and a short synthetic poly(A) signal (~50–80 bp). The genomic HVR and the transcribed HVR are identical, enabling the same amplicon for DNA and cDNA.
- Non-viral integration in human CD34+ HSPCs
  - Deliver Cas9 RNP targeting the safe harbor plus a long ssDNA or circular ssDNA donor (cssDNA) containing the cassette with 60–120 bp homology arms. Recent data support non-viral long-ssDNA/cssDNA donors enabling kilobase-scale knock-ins in primary human cells, including HSPCs, at practical efficiencies for tracer marking while maintaining viability. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12630883/?utm_source=openai))
  - Optimize electroporation and culture (SCF, TPO, Flt3L) with HDR enhancers where appropriate, balancing viability and insertion rate. Benchmarks: ≥10% on-target knock-in in total CD34+ cells; confirmed in phenotypic HSC subsets. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5603407/?utm_source=openai))
- Release criteria and functional validation
  - Genomic: on-target junction PCR, ddPCR copy number, and targeted capture to exclude off-target integrations; Southern or inverse PCR as needed.
  - Cellular: colony-forming unit assays; xenotransplantation into NSG mice to confirm multilineage output and durability of the edited clones relative to unedited controls. Prior HSPC barcoding studies demonstrate feasibility of clonal readout post-engraftment; our design replaces viral/AAV6 donors with non-viral, safe-harbor–targeted donors. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/7610558/?utm_source=openai))

Aim 2: One-amplicon assay for engraftment and clonal diversity across DNA and RNA
- Primer/probe design
  - One primer pair flanking CRC+HVR yields a 220–260 bp amplicon. A hydrolysis probe specific to CRC supports absolute donor-marked fraction by dPCR from genomic DNA of peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs). The same primers amplify the transcript-embedded HVR from platelet and reticulocyte cDNA.
- DNA workflow (nucleated lineages)
  - Sample PBMCs and lineage-sorted subsets (neutrophils/monocytes/B/T/NK) at days ~+14, +28, +60, +90, +180, +365. dPCR on CRC estimates percent donor-marked cells (engraftment surrogate); amplicon-NGS enumerates HVRs to compute clonal richness and evenness. Compare engraftment calls with institutional STR/SNP chimerism and NGS chimerism controls. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8065704/?utm_source=openai))
- RNA workflow (anucleate lineages)
  - Platelet-rich plasma and reticulocyte-enriched fractions processed for RNA with DNase treatment. RT using gene-specific primer to the cassette 3′ region to minimize background. Amplicon-NGS of the same HVR reports megakaryocytic and erythroid clonal outputs, leveraging established platelet/reticulocyte transcriptomics. Include exogenous RNA spike-in for per-sample recovery normalization. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3670814/?utm_source=openai))
- Quantitation and integration
  - Engraftment: absolute donor-marked fraction from PBMC DNA (CRC dPCR).
  - Diversity: HVR count-based frequencies per compartment; compute Shannon/Simpson diversity and Gini indices; longitudinal state-space modeling of clone trajectories.
  - Cross-compartment mapping: align HVRs across DNA (myeloid/lymphoid) and RNA (platelet/reticulocyte) to infer lineage allocation and stability.

Aim 3: First-in-human tracer HSCT pilot for longitudinal, lineage-wide clonal dynamics
- Design
  - Allogeneic HSCT recipients (n=15). From donor apheresis, split CD34+ cells: 5–10% edited with the cassette (“tracer” dose) and 90–95% unedited. Co-infuse to decouple therapeutic intent from research marking, enhancing safety and regulatory feasibility.
- Sampling schedule and endpoints
  - Blood at days +14, +28, +60, +90, +180, +365. Primary endpoints: agreement of CRC dPCR engraftment with standard chimerism; time to full donor marking; sensitivity for microchimerism (≤0.1%). Secondary endpoints: compartment-specific clonal diversity; stability/shift of dominant clones; concordance of megakaryocytic/erythroid HVRs with contemporaneous myeloid HVRs.
- Analytics and success criteria
  - Power to detect ≥10% shifts in top-10 clone ranks across timepoints with FDR<0.1 at 200,000 reads/sample. Technical CV<10% for CRC dPCR across replicates. Recovery of barcode transcripts from platelets and reticulocytes in ≥80% of scheduled draws, consistent with known biology of platelet/reticulocyte RNA. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3670814/?utm_source=openai))

Risk assessment and mitigations
- Editing efficiency and payload size
  - If ≤5% KI, increase cssDNA donor length for improved HDR and optimize RNP delivery; cssDNA has recently enabled kilobase insertions in HSPCs with higher efficiency than linear ssDNA. If expression from CLYBL is insufficient, evaluate Rogi loci; avoid AAVS1 if silencing encountered. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-025-66318-2?utm_source=openai))
- Platelet/reticulocyte RNA variability
  - Normalize to external spike-in and to stable platelet RNAs; schedule draws away from acute inflammatory events when feasible. Extensive literature supports recoverable and analyzable platelet mRNA despite low copy numbers. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3670814/?utm_source=openai))
- Clinical and regulatory feasibility
  - Ex vivo, non-viral RNP + long-ssDNA/cssDNA donor aligns with evolving HSPC editing practice and avoids integrating viral vectors; the tracer co-infusion strategy limits exposure while yielding robust longitudinal data. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5603407/?utm_source=openai))

Milestones and timeline (year 1–2)
- Months 0–6: Cassette finalization; non-viral KI optimization in CD34+ cells; on-target specificity; in vitro multilineage differentiation; amplicon assay lock.
- Months 6–12: Small-animal validation of durability and neutrality; clinical protocol activation; first 5 HSCT patients enrolled.
- Months 12–24: Complete enrollment (n=15); longitudinal sampling to day +365; analysis and comparison with institutional chimerism assays; go/no-go for scale-up.

Expected outcomes and impact
- A clinically amenable, single-amplicon platform that quantitatively confirms donor engraftment and resolves polyclonal dynamics across all hematopoietic compartments, including anucleate outputs, without viral vectors or multi-assay complexity.
- Immediate utility as a research-grade tracer approach to benchmark graft composition, conditioning intensity, and post-transplant interventions; pathway to regulated clinical assays due to minimal, well-characterized genomic intervention in a safe harbor.

Key prior observations underpinning feasibility
- Platelets and reticulocytes carry recoverable RNA suitable for RT-PCR/NGS, enabling clonal readouts from anucleate lineages. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3670814/?utm_source=openai))
- Barcoding HSPCs enables clonal tracking post-engraftment; previous work used AAV6 at AAVS1 or viral vectors, motivating a non-viral, safe-harbor alternative. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/7610558/?utm_source=openai))
- CLYBL and newly validated GSH loci provide more stable, less disruptive transgene expression than AAVS1, which can undergo lineage-dependent silencing. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4294658/?utm_source=openai))
- Long ssDNA/circular ssDNA donors can mediate kilobase-scale, non-viral targeted insertions in primary human cells, including HSPCs, at practical efficiencies. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-025-66318-2?utm_source=openai))

Regulatory and clinical translation considerations
- The cassette is non-therapeutic and compact, inserted at a vetted safe harbor; risk is mitigated by tracer dosing and comprehensive genomic QC. Assay uses standard dPCR and short-amplicon NGS compatible with CLIA workflows and chimerism assay paradigms. Comparative validation against STR/SNP/NGS chimerism will be included in the pilot. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8065704/?utm_source=openai))

Title
BAR-PE: A single-locus, endogenous, prime-edited identifier enabling simultaneous engraftment confirmation and multilineage clonal diversity tracking after HSCT

Atomic strategy
Write a static, clone-unique, PAM-disrupting micro–barcode into a pre-validated, transcriptionally buffered 3′UTR window of a ubiquitously expressed gene in donor HSCs using prime-editing RNPs, so that the same 120–180 bp locus can be read from DNA in nucleated blood cells and from mRNA in platelets and reticulocytes, enabling one assay to quantify engraftment and clonal reconstitution across all hematopoietic compartments for 1 year. Evidence base: platelets and reticulocytes carry translatable mRNAs derived from megakaryocytes and late erythroid precursors, enabling RNA-based readouts in anucleate compartments; prime editing is feasible in human HSPCs ex vivo with optimizations; prime editing has been adapted for molecular recording and lineage tracing in mammalian systems. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7253186/?utm_source=openai))

Hypothesis/goal
A single, PAM-disrupting, prime-edited endogenous identifier (“endoID”) placed in a transcriptionally buffered 3′UTR window will: (i) provide an unambiguous digital signal of donor engraftment in blood, and (ii) yield unbiased, quantitative estimates of clonal diversity and lineage contributions across myeloid, lymphoid, erythroid, and megakaryocytic outputs, using one targeted amplicon assay on DNA (nucleated cells) and RNA (platelets/reticulocytes).

Differentiation from prior art
- Not STR chimerism or TCR/BCR repertoires; no reliance on antigen receptor rearrangements or donor/recipient polymorphisms.
- Not retroviral/AAV integration barcoding; no exogenous cassettes or vector integration maps. Prior HSPC barcoding work used viral knock-ins with barcode cassettes; here, we introduce compact edits at a native locus via DSB-free RNP prime editing. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/7610558/?utm_source=openai))

Specific aims
1) Define a clinically suitable “buffered transcribed barcode window” (BTW).
- Identify 5–10 candidate 3′UTR windows (80–150 bp each) within housekeeping transcripts with robust expression in leukocytes, platelets, and reticulocytes. Screen windows by MPRA and CRISPRi-perturbation in human megakaryocyte and erythroid cultures to select a BTW exhibiting no significant effects on host transcript abundance, stability, or cell fitness upon 8–12 nucleotide substitutions/insertions.

2) Engineer static endoIDs in human CD34+ HSCs with prime-editing RNPs.
- Use PE4/PE5max RNP plus epegRNA cocktails encoding mutually exclusive barcode edits and PAM-disrupting bases to enforce one-and-done writing per cell and prevent re-editing collisions. Optimize with deoxynucleoside supplementation and Vpx-mediated SAMHD1 degradation for HSPC prime-editing efficiency and edit–to–indel ratios. Validate preservation of LT-HSC phenotype and multilineage output in vitro and in NSG/NBSGW xenografts. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/10195679/?utm_source=openai))

3) Build the single-assay clinical readout.
- Develop a UMI-tagged, high-fidelity amplicon sequencing workflow using the same primer pair for: (a) gDNA from sorted nucleated lineages (neutrophils/monocytes, B, T, NK) and total leukocytes, and (b) cDNA from purified platelets and reticulocytes for the BTW transcript. Establish bioinformatic pipelines to call endoID haplotypes, deconvolve clonal abundances, and compute engraftment and diversity metrics longitudinally (up to 12 months).

Experimental design and methods
- Donor cells and editing: Mobilized peripheral-blood CD34+ cells (allogeneic or autologous contexts). Electroporate PEmax mRNA and synthetic epegRNA pool (10–50 designs) with calibrated stoichiometry to achieve ≤1 endoID per cell; include nicking sgRNA where needed. Employ PAM-disrupting edits (per-pegRNA) to terminate editing after single write. Benchmark on-target efficiency, edit purity, and off-targets by amplicon-seq and CHANGE-seq on top candidates. Validate maintenance of LT-HSC properties by CD34+CD90+CD49f+ subset tracking, CFU assays, LTC-IC, and xenograft repopulation.
- BTW discovery: In vitro–derived human megakaryocytes and erythroblasts built from cord blood CD34+ cells. MPRA libraries with the candidate 3′UTRs ± barcode edit palettes; select windows with <5% expression deviation and no predicted RBP/miRNA motif creation/loss. Confirm expression of the host transcript in platelets/reticulocytes by RNA-seq and targeted RT-qPCR. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7253186/?utm_source=openai))
- Sample schedule post-transplant: days ~14, 28, 56, 90, 180, 270, 365. From each draw: PBMCs, granulocytes, platelets (leukocyte-depleted platelet-rich plasma), and enriched reticulocytes (thiazole orange+ fraction). Extract DNA (nucleated subsets) and RNA (platelets/reticulocytes). Generate UMI-labeled libraries from the same BTW locus. Platelet and reticulocyte RNA-based endoIDs validate readout in anucleate compartments. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7253186/?utm_source=openai))
- Controls: Pre-infusion aliquot to establish endoID library composition; in vitro mixing standards to calibrate detection limits; spike-in of known-frequency synthetic controls to quantify absolute sensitivity across matrices.

Primary endpoints
- Engraftment confirmation: Presence of any endoID in blood at ≥10 UMI-supported molecules per 20,000 cell equivalents (LoD established by spike-ins).
- Clonal diversity: Number of unique endoIDs and diversity indices (Shannon, Simpson, Gini) in total leukocytes and lineage-sorted fractions at each time point; stability of multi-lineage clones over 12 months.
- Lineage balance: For each endoID, proportions across myeloid, lymphoid, platelet, and reticulocyte compartments; detection of lineage-restricted or dominant clones.
- Safety and function: Editing distribution across HSPC hierarchy, colony output, and xenograft repopulation; transcriptome integrity near BTW; off-target profile; assessment of editing-related stress. Note: PE genotoxicity has been reported in HSPCs and will be explicitly evaluated and mitigated. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11147503/?utm_source=openai))

Analytical framework
- One-locus, two-matrix quantification: Joint model integrates DNA-based endoID counts (nucleated compartments) with RNA-based counts (platelets/reticulocytes) to estimate per-clone production rates corrected for compartment-specific RNA/DNA yields and cell lifespans.
- Collision avoidance and double labeling: PAM-disrupting edits plus mutually exclusive epegRNAs minimize multi-endoID cells; any rare collisions are detectable as multi-haplotype reads and excluded from clonal counts. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/10195679/?utm_source=openai))
- Comparative novelty benchmark: Run head-to-head with AAV6 barcode cassette–based HSPC tracking in preclinical xenograft arms to verify equal or lower bias and higher clinical amenability (non-viral, DSB-free, single amplicon, cross-compartment readout). ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/7610558/?utm_source=openai))

Milestones and timeline (18–24 months)
- Months 0–6: BTW discovery and validation; finalize pegRNA palette; establish PE RNP conditions in CD34+ cells.
- Months 6–12: Preclinical qualification: xenografts, longitudinal sampling, pipeline lock; finalize SOPs for blood processing and dual DNA/RNA endoID assay.
- Months 12–24: First-in-human feasibility (n≤6; autologous gene-editing or allogeneic pilot with ethics approval): demonstrate assay turnaround <5 days and stability of clonal metrics through 6–12 months.

Regulatory and clinical translation considerations
- Non-viral, DSB-free RNP delivery reduces integration risks; small neutral edits at a vetted BTW minimize perturbation. Prime editing in human HSPCs is advancing with ex vivo feasibility, but safety must be demonstrated given reports of genotoxicity in HSPCs; this protocol includes orthogonal genomic and functional safeguards before clinical deployment. Platelet/reticulocyte RNA readouts use minimally invasive sampling and established RNA-seq/RT-PCR practices. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/10195679/?utm_source=openai))

Success criteria
- ≥20% of infused LT-HSCs carry a single, high-fidelity endoID; no measurable impact on LT-HSC frequency, lineage output, or repopulation versus unedited controls.
- Engraftment detected by day ~14 via leukocyte DNA and corroborated by platelet/reticulocyte RNA by day ~28; ≥90% concordance between DNA and RNA–derived clonal rankings thereafter.
- Stable or diversifying polyclonal repertoire (Shannon index within predefined bounds) without emergence of editing-linked dominant clones over 12 months.

Expected impact
An endogenous, prime-edited, RNA/DNA-readable identifier consolidates engraftment verification and whole-lineage clonal assessment into one assay compatible with clinical timelines and sampling. It eliminates vector integration mapping, extends readouts to anucleate lineages via RNA, and creates a path to regulated, low-risk clonal tracking in HSCT. ([doi.org](https://doi.org/10.1126%2Fscience.adx3800?utm_source=openai))

text:
Title
MEI-HaploTrack: A single targeted sequencing assay that uses donor-specific mobile element insertion barcodes and haplotype-imbalance tracts to quantify engraftment and polyclonal reconstitution after HSCT

Hypothesis and integrated research question
Can a targeted, UMI-enabled sequencing assay that (i) reads donor- versus recipient-unique polymorphic mobile element insertions (MEIs; Alu/L1/SVA) as stable, binary barcodes and (ii) simultaneously monitors haplotype-imbalance tracts linked to these MEIs detect both donor engraftment levels and the number and dynamics of long-term HSC-derived clones across all hematopoietic lineages over the first post-transplant year? STR and SNP/InDel-based chimerism methods quantify engraftment but are not designed to resolve neutral clonal scars; conversely, clonal assays often rely on disease- or integration-derived tags. MEIs offer multi-locus, neutral germline barcodes for chimerism, and haplotype-resolved allele-imbalance tracts arising from copy-neutral LOH (CN-LOH) or related mosaic chromosomal alterations (mCAs) during rapid post-transplant expansion can serve as natural, lineage-spanning clonal marks. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10380370/?utm_source=openai)) ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7200591/?utm_source=openai)) ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6054542/?utm_source=openai))

Atomic strategy
Exploit the genome’s native, binary presence/absence MEI polymorphisms as donor/recipient barcodes while tiling MEI-anchored haploblocks genome-wide so that any emergent neutral CN-LOH/mCA in an LT-HSC converts a set of heterozygous markers to homozygosity along a tract. The same targeted reads that quantify chimerism also expose coherent, longitudinally persistent haplotype-imbalance tracts that define and track LT-HSC clones across divergent lineages.

Specific aims
- Aim 1: Build a clinically amenable targeted panel of 3,000–5,000 MEI-anchored haploblocks.
  - Locus selection: curate Alu/L1/SVA presence/absence polymorphisms distributed genome-wide, prioritize intergenic/intronic, low-constraint regions; design amplicons/capture baits spanning the MEI junction and 1–5 kb of flanking sequence harboring dense SNPs/indels to enable haplotype phasing and tract inference. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3158055/?utm_source=openai))
  - Assay architecture: multiplex PCR or hybrid-capture with UMIs, 2×150 bp sequencing; validated locus-specific MEI genotyping approaches (e.g., ME-Scan concept) guide primer/bait design and junction readout. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2996938/?utm_source=openai))

- Aim 2: Validate engraftment quantification against STR and SNP/InDel NGS standards.
  - Pretransplant genotyping (donor, recipient) identifies informative MEIs; post-transplant samples (whole blood and lineage sorts) yield donor fraction by maximum-likelihood aggregation of MEI presence/absence counts with UMI deduplication and binomial uncertainty. Compare accuracy and LoD to STR PCR and SNP/InDel NGS in split samples. ([ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK608246/?utm_source=openai))

- Aim 3: Detect and longitudinally track neutral clonal haplotype-imbalance tracts.
  - Computational detection: phased MEI-linked SNPs create haploblocks; coherent shifts in allele balance across adjacent blocks define CN-LOH/mCA tracts at low VAF using change-point/CUSUM-style statistics adapted for UMI counts; persistent tracts across time and across divergent lineages (myeloid and lymphoid; plus erythroid/megakaryocytic precursors in marrow) define LT-HSC clones. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/1701.04387?utm_source=openai))
  - Biological grounding: CN-LOH/mCAs are established features of hematopoiesis that can mark clones; rapid proliferative stress post-HSCT provides opportunity for emergence or expansion to detectable levels. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6054542/?utm_source=openai))

Study design

Cohort and sampling
- Prospective, n=60 adults undergoing allo-HSCT (varied donor types; myeloablative and reduced-intensity).
- Time points through 1 year: days +30, +60, +100, +180, +270, +365.
- Cell sources per time point:
  - Peripheral blood: neutrophils, monocytes, B cells, T cells, NK cells (immunomagnetic or flow sorts).
  - Bone marrow aspirate at +30, +180, +365: erythroid precursors (CD71+GlyA+), megakaryocytic precursors (CD41/42+). Platelets/RBCs are anucleate; nucleated precursors are the appropriate genomic substrates. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9446524/?utm_source=openai))

Laboratory workflow
- Panel and library preparation: multiplex UMI-tagged amplicons/capture; dual-indexing; batch TAT ≤5 days.
- Sequencing depth: ~2–3M read pairs/sample (supports chimerism ≤0.3–1% and detection of tract VAF ≥1%).
- Controls: donor- and recipient-only DNA; in silico and wet spike-ins at 10%, 1%, 0.3%.

Primary outcomes
- Engraftment accuracy and limit of detection relative to STR and SNP/InDel NGS benchmarks; acceptance if absolute error ≤2% at 5–100% donor and LoD ≤1%. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10380370/?utm_source=openai))
- Clonal diversity metrics:
  - Number of independent haplotype-imbalance tracts meeting persistence criteria (present in ≥2 divergent lineages and ≥2 consecutive time points).
  - Clone size trajectories (tract VAF over time) and cross-lineage distribution per clone.

Secondary outcomes
- Relationship of early mixed chimerism and specific clonal trajectories with relapse or graft dysfunction.
- Feasibility metrics: assay failure rate, hands-on time, per-sample cost model.

Analysis plan
- Chimerism: Bayesian hierarchical model across informative MEIs per sample and lineage; propagate UMI-based molecular counts to credible intervals.
- Tract calling: phased haploblocks constructed from MEI-linked SNPs/indels; scan for segments with coordinated allelic shift from 0.5 toward 0/1 consistent with CN-LOH or segmental CNA; require cross-lineage and longitudinal concordance; control FDR by sample-swapping nulls and synthetic mixtures. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6054542/?utm_source=openai))
- Lineage provenance filter: only clones detected in both myeloid and lymphoid (and, when available, erythroid/megakaryocytic precursors) are declared LT-HSC–derived; lineage-restricted tracts flagged as transient progenitor clones.

Differentiation from existing methods
- Not STR, SNP-only, or TCR/BCR repertoire. It uses donor-specific, binary MEI presence/absence as the primary chimerism barcode and haplotype-aware detection of neutral CN-LOH/mCAs as clonal marks in a single targeted assay. Existing clinical chimerism platforms do not exploit MEIs or haplotype-imbalance tractography for clonal dynamics. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8065704/?utm_source=openai))

Clinical translation features
- Sample types are standard HSCT draws; no genetic engineering; UMI-targeted sequencing is CLIA/CAP-amenable.
- Turnaround and cost comparable to current NGS chimerism panels, with added clonal resolution. ([frontiersin.org](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/genetics/articles/10.3389/fgene.2023.1282947/full?utm_source=openai))

Risk analysis and mitigations
- Risk: Low tract incidence in some patients within 1 year could limit clonal resolution.
  - Mitigations: (i) high locus count and genome-wide tiling to maximize tract intercept probability; (ii) sensitivity to pre-existing low-VAF donor mCAs that expand post-transplant; (iii) optional inclusion of a compact, intergenic SNP-UMI subpanel to boost haploblock density without altering the workflow. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41588-023-01553-1?utm_source=openai))
- Risk: Rare functional MEIs could be under selection.
  - Mitigation: prefilter panel to intergenic/intronic, low-conservation sites; remove loci showing longitudinal deviation inconsistent with donor fraction. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3158055/?utm_source=openai))

Milestones
- Year 1 Q1–Q2: Panel finalization, analytical validation (precision, LoD, specificity) on contrived mixes.
- Q2–Q4: Enroll first 30 patients; interim analysis of engraftment concordance vs STR/SNP methods; initial tract detection performance.
- Year 2 Q1–Q2: Complete enrollment and 1-year follow-up; finalize clinical performance and clonal dynamics models.

Success criteria
- Engraftment: noninferior to STR and SNP/InDel NGS with LoD ≤1% and strong linearity across 1–100%. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10380370/?utm_source=openai))
- Clonal dynamics: ≥60% of evaluable patients with ≥1 persistent cross-lineage tract detected; reproducible clone size trajectories across time points.

Expected impact
A single, panel-based assay that simultaneously delivers (i) engraftment confirmation/quantitation and (ii) lineage-spanning, label-free clonal tracking—without reliance on STRs, immune receptor repertoires, or vector integrations—bridges current clinical monitoring with population-genetics–grounded, mechanistically interpretable clonal readouts. It leverages stable MEI barcodes for chimerism and haplotype tractography for neutral clonal marks, aligning with real-world clinical workflows. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8065704/?utm_source=openai))

text:
Title
DIME-Track: A single-assay, native long-read framework to quantify engraftment and lineage-resolved clonal reconstitution after HSCT using endogenous sequence barcodes and methylation

Premise and rationale
- Platelets retain mitochondria and mtDNA; erythropoiesis and megakaryopoiesis leave lineage-specific methylation footprints in plasma cfDNA and platelets, enabling readouts for anucleate end products. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10529105/?utm_source=openai))
- Oxford Nanopore sequencing (ONT) detects DNA methylation directly on native molecules and supports adaptive sampling for on-device enrichment; Cas9-guided adaptor ligation (nCATS) enables amplification-free enrichment of the entire mtGenome and selected nuclear loci. Duplex basecalling further reduces error and preserves per-strand modified base calls. ([genome.cshlp.org](https://genome.cshlp.org/content/early/2025/03/07/gr279159124?utm_source=openai))
- Somatic mtDNA variants function as natural, heritable clonal barcodes in human hematopoiesis and have been used to reconstruct clonal dynamics, including in transplant contexts. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6408267/?utm_source=openai))

Hypothesis–question
Can a single native-molecule assay that jointly reads endogenous sequence barcodes (mtDNA and selected neutral nuclear variants) and per-molecule methylation classify donor/recipient contributions (engraftment) and quantify lineage-resolved polyclonal reconstitution over one year after HSCT, including erythroid and megakaryocytic compartments which lack nuclear DNA in circulation? If so, what clone–lineage–time features most predict subsequent graft stability or relapse?

Atomic strategy
Exploit same-molecule linkage of sequence and methylation on ONT reads, with targeted mtDNA and sentinel nuclear regions enriched by Cas9 and optionally prioritized by adaptive sampling, to build a barcode-by-lineage frequency matrix over time. Lineage labels come from: (a) cell sorting for nucleated subsets; (b) platelet mtDNA for megakaryocytes; and (c) cfDNA methylation deconvolution for erythroid lineage. Shared barcode presence across divergent lineages constrains clone ancestry and filters artifacts.

Specific aims
1) Establish pre-transplant donor/recipient endogenous barcode panels (mtDNA haplotypes/heteroplasmies and neutral nuclear SNVs/indels) and validate ONT duplex nCATS performance for ultra-low-frequency detection in blood-derived DNA. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7145730/?utm_source=openai))
2) Build and analytically validate the DIME-Track assay: simultaneous readout of chimerism and lineage-resolved clonal diversity from whole blood, platelets, and plasma cfDNA.
3) Prospectively test DIME-Track longitudinally (day +14 to +365) in allo-HSCT, relating clone–lineage trajectories to clinical outcomes (stable engraftment, mixed chimerism, relapse).

Study design and cohorts
- Discovery set (n=20 donor–recipient pairs): peripheral blood pre-HSCT for barcode discovery.
- Prospective validation (n=60 allo-HSCT recipients): blood at days ~+14, +28, +56, +90, +180, +270, +365.
- Comparator assays: standard STR or NGS SNP chimerism; targeted myeloid panel (CHIP/relapse risk); clinical CBC/flow. ONT-based chimerism assays exist but do not provide unified methylation-based lineage resolution with endogenous barcodes; DIME-Track explicitly targets this gap. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39181323/?utm_source=openai))

Biospecimens and lineage coverage per time point
- Buffy coat for nucleated leukocytes; magnetic selection or standardized short FACS for granulocytes, monocytes, NK, CD4 T, CD8 T, B cells.
- Platelet-rich plasma for platelet mtDNA (megakaryocytic output). ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10529105/?utm_source=openai))
- Plasma for cfDNA; methylation deconvolution to quantify erythroid progenitor and megakaryocyte contributions, complementing sorted leukocyte fractions. ([doi.org](https://doi.org/10.1038%2Fs41467-018-07466-6?utm_source=openai))

Wet-lab workflow (single unified library strategy; 6–8 h hands-on, 24 h run)
1) DNA extraction:
   - Nucleated cells: HMW genomic DNA.
   - Platelets: total DNA (mtDNA-dominant).
   - Plasma: cfDNA.
2) nCATS panel design:
   - Full mitochondrial genome (single/tiled gRNA cut sites) to capture haplotypes/heteroplasmies.
   - 50–100 neutral nuclear loci (intronic/intergenic deserts, polymorphism-sparse) for private somatic SNVs discovered pre-HSCT; optional inclusion of PCDH methylation-barcode loci for orthogonal epigenetic barcoding. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7145730/?utm_source=openai))
3) Library prep:
   - Dephosphorylation and Cas9 RNP cutting; ONT adaptor ligation.
   - Pool barcoded libraries from all compartments; load on MinION/PromethION.
4) Sequencing:
   - Duplex-capable basecalling; modified base calling for 5mC/5hmC.
   - Optional adaptive sampling to upweight nuclear targets if background is high. ([software-docs.nanoporetech.com](https://software-docs.nanoporetech.com/dorado/0.8.2/basecaller/duplex/?utm_source=openai))

Computational workflow
- Basecalling: Dorado duplex with modified base models (per-read methylation; per-strand calls). ([software-docs.nanoporetech.com](https://software-docs.nanoporetech.com/dorado/0.8.2/basecaller/duplex/?utm_source=openai))
- Variant calling:
  - mtDNA: haplotype phasing; heteroplasmy estimation per compartment; strand-consensus filters.
  - Nuclear panel: SNV/indel calling with duplex constraints; per-target error models.
- Methylation and lineage assignment:
  - For sorted subsets: methylation used as QC and state annotation.
  - For cfDNA: deconvolution against reference hematopoietic methylomes to quantify erythroid and megakaryocyte-derived fragments. ([doi.org](https://doi.org/10.1038%2Fs41467-018-07466-6?utm_source=openai))
- Barcode-by-lineage matrix:
  - For each endogenous barcode b and lineage l at time t, estimate frequency f(b,l,t) with Bayes–beta-binomial credible intervals incorporating per-target error rates and duplex status.
  - Cross-compartment constraint: barcodes observed in both myeloid and lymphoid arms are flagged as early HSC-derived; lineage-restricted signals are modeled as later progenitor contributions or restricted sampling.
- Dynamical modeling:
  - Fit neutral-drift/birth–death models to f(b,l,t) to separate true clonal shifts from sampling noise; compute diversity (Shannon/Simpson), evenness, and Gini for each lineage over time.
  - Engraftment metrics: donor fraction per lineage from donor-private barcodes; recipient MRH sensitivity from recipient-private barcodes at <1% VAF enabled by duplex + targeted enrichment. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7145730/?utm_source=openai))

Primary endpoints and success criteria
- Analytical:
  - LoD for donor/recipient-private barcodes ≤0.5% VAF (mtDNA) and ≤1% VAF (nuclear), verified with contrived mixes and longitudinal duplicates; duplex requirement reduces false positives. ([software-docs.nanoporetech.com](https://software-docs.nanoporetech.com/dorado/0.8.2/basecaller/duplex/?utm_source=openai))
  - Concordance with STR/NGS chimerism across total leukocytes (R≥0.95).
  - Correct lineage assignment for erythroid and megakaryocytic contributions from cfDNA/platelets (agreement with clinical indices, e.g., reticulocyte count and platelet recovery). ([doi.org](https://doi.org/10.1038%2Fs41467-018-07466-6?utm_source=openai))
- Clinical:
  - Time-to-engraftment detection (first donor fraction >95%) non-inferior to standard of care; earlier detection of mixed chimerism in any compartment by ≥7 days in ≥30% of cases.
  - Association of early diversity metrics (day +56) with 1-year outcomes (relapse/mixed chimerism), adjusted for disease risk.

Assay novelty and clinical translation
- Existing chimerism methods (STR, SNP panels, or ONT-based chimerism) do not provide a unified, lineage-resolved clonal map from native molecules across nucleated and anucleate compartments; DIME-Track integrates endogenous barcodes with methylation-based lineage readouts in one assay. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39181323/?utm_source=openai))
- Feasibility: single phlebotomy; fractionation with standard clinical workflows; sequencing on MinION/PromethION with per-sample reagent cost scalable via pooling and adaptive/CRISPR enrichment; turnaround 48–72 h. ONT supports direct methylation calling without bisulfite, reducing complexity and preserving long-range phasing. ([nanoporetech.com](https://nanoporetech.com/platform/accuracy?utm_source=openai))
- Regulatory path: lab-developed test with contrived-mix calibration, external controls, and cross-platform concordance; no genetic modification.

Risk management
- Low-frequency calling errors: enforce duplex requirement, replicate libraries, strand-aware filters, and per-site error models; prioritize mtDNA (high copy) for early time points. ([software-docs.nanoporetech.com](https://software-docs.nanoporetech.com/dorado/0.8.2/basecaller/duplex/?utm_source=openai))
- Variable cfDNA yield: use fixed plasma volumes; integrate leukocyte/platelet signals when cfDNA is marginal; adaptive sampling to boost target coverage. ([nanoporetech.com](https://nanoporetech.com/document/adaptive-sampling?utm_source=openai))
- mtDNA dynamics confounding lineage inference: treat mtDNA primarily as clonal barcode, not lineage marker; rely on methylation deconvolution and sorted subsets for lineage classification. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11938731/?utm_source=openai))

Milestones
- Months 0–6: Panel design; contrived-mix benchmarking; duplex calling SOPs; establish LoD.
- Months 6–18: Enroll discovery and validation cohorts; iterate deconvolution models; lock analysis pipeline.
- Months 18–24: Finalize performance characteristics; correlate early clone–lineage metrics with 1-year outcomes; readiness assessment for CLIA deployment.

Expected outcomes
- A validated, longitudinal assay that simultaneously confirms engraftment and quantifies polyclonal, lineage-resolved reconstitution—including erythroid and megakaryocytic—using endogenous markers, with clinical turnaround and cost compatible with routine HSCT follow-up. ([doi.org](https://doi.org/10.1038%2Fs41467-018-07466-6?utm_source=openai))

text:
Title
Orthogonal endogenous barcoding for quantitative assessment of engraftment and polyclonal reconstitution after HSCT

Central question/hypothesis
Can a single, clinically amenable assay that combines prospectively written nuclear epigenetic identifiers with prospectively written mitochondrial haplotypes unambiguously confirm donor engraftment and quantify long-term, cross-lineage clonal diversity—including anucleate compartments—over the first year after HSCT? The hypothesis is that (i) transient, ex vivo installation of locus-targeted CpG methylation patterns in donor CD34+ cells is mitotically heritable through hematopoietic differentiation, and (ii) concurrent installation of neutral, designed mtDNA SNV haplotypes provides a high-sensitivity, anucleate-compatible readout; the joint signal resolves true LT-HSC polyclonality from early progenitor bursts and oligoclonal dominance. dCas9–DNMT3A/3L editing in HSPCs yields inheritable methylation transmitted to progeny, and DdCBE/TALED base editors create precise mtDNA edits; mtDNA is retained in platelets whereas mitochondria are cleared during reticulocyte maturation, motivating a dual-axis design. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10450654/?utm_source=openai))

Atomic strategy
Write two orthogonal, heritable, non-integrating identifiers into donor HSCs ex vivo—(1) combinatorial CpG methylation states at pre-selected, noncoding “barcode modules” in the nuclear genome and (2) a low-load set of neutral mtDNA SNVs forming a designed haplotype. After HSCT, decode both identifiers by targeted amplicon sequencing from the same routine clinical specimens. Presence of any engineered identifier confirms engraftment; the frequency distributions of unique identifier combinations across myeloid, lymphoid, erythroid precursors, and megakaryocytic/platelet samples quantify clonal diversity and cross-lineage sharing.

Specific aims
Aim 1. Define safe, stable nuclear barcode modules and editing conditions for durable methylation memory in human HSPCs.
Aim 2. Engineer high-fidelity, neutral mtDNA haplotypes in HSPCs and establish sensitive detection in platelets and nucleated subsets.
Aim 3. Build and clinically simulate a single-sample, dual-readout assay and analysis pipeline to estimate engraftment fraction and clonal diversity metrics longitudinally to 12 months.

Rationale and novelty
- Endogenous mtDNA variants already serve as robust retrospective clonal barcodes in hematopoiesis and other tissues, but are not prospectively designed nor optimized for clinical monitoring; DdCBE/TALEDs now enable precise, programmable mtDNA edits. This creates a forward-designed organellar barcode recoverable from platelets, an anucleate lineage that retains mitochondria. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6408267/?utm_source=openai))
- Targeted epigenetic editing with dCas9–DNMT3A/3L establishes mitotically heritable methylation and persistent repression at selected loci; here, methylation is used not to regulate genes but as a binary identity code at noncoding safe-harbors—distinct from STR chimerism, TCR/BCR repertoires, and integration-site mapping. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5532369/?utm_source=openai))
- Platelets harbor functional mitochondria whereas mature RBCs lack them due to BNIP3L/NIX-dependent mitophagy; therefore organellar barcodes extend coverage to megakaryocytic outputs (platelets) and motivate marrow timepoints for erythroid precursors. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7073649/?utm_source=openai))

Study design and methods

Donor material and editing
- Source: Mobilized peripheral blood CD34+ cells from allogeneic donors (research-use aliquot of the clinical graft).
- Editing window: 18–24 h post-collection under clinically standard HSPC culture (low-cytokine, UM171 optional for maintenance), then washout and cryopreserve the small “barcode aliquot” to be spiked into the clinical product immediately before infusion at a predefined fraction (e.g., 1–5%). This avoids modifying the therapeutic bulk while enabling rigorous in vivo readouts of clonal dynamics.

Nuclear methylation barcode writing (Aim 1)
- Targets: 12–16 intergenic modules (200–400 bp each) in constitutively inactive, enhancer-poor regions with low 5hmC/turnover, distributed across chromosomes to minimize local interference.
- Editors: Chemically modified mRNA encoding dCas9–DNMT3A–DNMT3L (and a KRAB-containing variant for select modules) plus multiplexed sgRNAs (2–3 per module). Nucleofection into freshly isolated CD34+ cells.
- Rationale for durability: De novo methylation deposited by DNMT3A/3L is copied by DNMT1, and combinatorial KRAB/D3A+L can confer longer-lived chromatin states in human cells and in HSPCs. We will benchmark persistence during in vitro multilineage differentiation and in xenograft repopulation. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5532369/?utm_source=openai))
- Barcode complexity: Each module is binary (methylated/on vs baseline/off); 12 modules yield up to 4096 states. Practically, editing multiplicity and cell numbers define the realized dictionary.

Mitochondrial haplotype writing (Aim 2)
- Targets: 8–10 mtDNA loci curated for neutrality (synonymous or deep intergenic noncoding sites avoiding tRNA/rRNA). Each donor HSC receives a sparse subset (2–4 edits) to form unique, low-load haplotypes.
- Editors: High-fidelity DdCBE or TALED pairs delivered as modRNA by nucleofection; use HiFi-DdCBE or DddA variants and NES-optimized designs to minimize off-targets. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41587-022-01486-w?utm_source=openai))
- Tuning heteroplasmy: Titrate editor dose and exposure to achieve initial per-locus heteroplasmy 5–30%, sufficient for detection yet minimizing organellar fitness effects. Validate respiration and mt content in edited HSPCs before infusion.

Preclinical validation
- In vitro differentiation: Track barcode persistence across CFU assays and liquid cultures to granulocytic/monocytic, B, NK, and erythroid/megakaryocytic fates; decode by targeted bisulfite/enzymatic-conversion sequencing (nuclear) and multiplex mtDNA amplicons (organellar).
- In vivo xenografts: NSG recipients receive spiked “barcode aliquot.” At weeks 4, 8, 12, 24, 52, sample PB (whole blood, platelet-rich plasma) and BM aspirates. Sort neutrophils, monocytes, B, T, NK, CD34+, erythroblasts, and megakaryocytes when available. Mature RBCs are excluded from nuclear decoding; platelets enable organellar decoding of megakaryocytic output. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7073649/?utm_source=openai))

Clinical-simulation assay workflow (Aim 3)
- Single-specimen framework: From one EDTA tube at each visit, split DNA for two targeted libraries built on a unified amplicon platform:
  - Panel A (nuclear): 12–16 barcode modules profiled by enzymatic-conversion or bisulfite amplicons with molecular identifiers.
  - Panel B (mtDNA): 20–40 short amplicons covering edited loci and a background panel for heteroplasmy baselining.
- Lineage coverage plan:
  - Myeloid/lymphoid: Whole blood and sorted PBMC subsets for both panels.
  - Megakaryocytic: Platelet-rich plasma for mtDNA panel; marrow megakaryocytes for both panels when clinically obtained.
  - Erythroid: Marrow erythroblasts at days ~+30, +100, +365; optional reticulocyte-enriched PB early post-engraftment for mtDNA panel.
- Turnaround and cost: Two small targeted libraries per timepoint (≤60 amplicons total). Same sequencer run for both panels; analysis pipeline merges counts.

Primary endpoints and analyses
- Engraftment confirmation: Detection of any engineered nuclear barcode state and/or engineered mtDNA haplotype above a predetermined LOD in PB at ≥day +14 confirms donor-derived output.
- Clonal diversity and sharing:
  - Define clone IDs by unique nuclear barcode patterns; mtDNA haplotypes serve as orthogonal tags to detect collisions and to read anucleate outputs.
  - Compute per-lineage and cross-lineage clonal frequency distributions; quantify Shannon diversity, Pielou evenness, Gini dominance, and cross-lineage Jaccard sharing. Compare early (MPP-dominated) vs late (LT-HSC) phases.
  - Model mtDNA drift using Wright–Fisher heteroplasmy dynamics to avoid clone misassignment; probabilistic linkage of organellar to nuclear IDs in nucleated subsets calibrates platelet-only deconvolution. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41726901/?utm_source=openai))
- Decision readouts:
  - True LT-HSC polyclonality: Many clones shared across myeloid and lymphoid at late timepoints with stable evenness.
  - Oligoclonal dominance: Increasing Gini and loss of cross-lineage sharing; early myeloid bursts not sustained across time.

Comparator and controls
- Orthogonal chimerism (STR) run once per subject to benchmark engraftment sensitivity (not used for diversity).
- No-editor controls to define background methylation and mtDNA heteroplasmy.
- Spike-in standards: synthetic methylated controls and plasmid mtDNA controls to calibrate LOD/LOQ.

Safety and feasibility considerations
- Nuclear epigenetic editing is confined to intergenic modules; off-target methylation monitored by targeted capture around modules and by RNA-seq sentinel genes. Persistence and heritability of dCas9–DNMT3A/3L marks in HSPCs and progeny are established; KRAB/D3A+L combinations can extend durability when needed. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10450654/?utm_source=openai))
- Mitochondrial editing uses HiFi editors and neutral sites to minimize organellar dysfunction; whole-mtDNA deep sequencing quantifies off-targets, which are substantially reduced in HiFi designs. Platelets’ mitochondrial content supports sensitive detection from peripheral blood. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41587-022-01486-w?utm_source=openai))
- Clinical pathway: Editing is applied only to a research “barcode aliquot” spiked into the graft (no therapeutic gene modification), limiting regulatory risk while preserving biological interpretability of in vivo hematopoiesis.

Milestones
- Year 1: Finalize barcode modules and mtDNA loci; demonstrate persistence and neutrality in vitro; establish sequencing panels and analysis.
- Year 2: Complete xenograft validation; demonstrate 12-month longitudinal readout with concordant nuclear/organellar calls; finalize SOPs.
- Year 3: Prospective observational pilot in HSCT patients (barcoded aliquot spiking protocol), reporting engraftment sensitivity, lineage coverage, and diversity metrics vs clinical outcomes.

Go/no-go criteria
- Go: ≥90% recovery of intended nuclear barcodes in ≥3 lineages at ≥day +100; platelet mtDNA haplotype detection at all timepoints with LOD ≤0.1% VAF; absence of growth disadvantage vs mock-edited controls.
- No-go: Evidence of editor-induced HSPC fitness loss; persistent off-target mtDNA edits >1% VAF at unintended loci.

Expected impact
The dual, orthogonal, prospectively written identifiers transform HSCT monitoring from donor fraction measurements to quantitative, lineage-spanning clonal ecology. The approach distinguishes durable LT-HSC engraftment from transient progenitor bursts, measures true polyclonality vs oligoclonal takeover, and extends coverage to platelets—an established gap for nuclear barcodes—while remaining compatible with routine clinical specimens and turnaround. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6408267/?utm_source=openai))

text:
Title: Disappearing-ink episomal barcodes to quantify engraftment and polyclonal reconstitution after HSCT from whole-blood sampling

Unified question-hypothesis
Can non-integrating, episomal DNA barcodes delivered to donor CD34+ cells serve as a single, clinically amenable assay that both (i) confirms donor engraftment and (ii) quantifies clonal diversity and lineage-specific proliferative history over 12 months post-HSCT, by exploiting the division-dependent dilution of episomes (“disappearing ink”) and recovering barcodes from nucleated blood cells as DNA and from anucleate outputs as RNA? The core bet is that episomal vectors persist in quiescent/slow-cycling HSCs and early progenitors but are geometrically diluted with mitoses in progeny, generating informative decay kinetics per lineage measurable from peripheral blood alone. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2835240/?utm_source=openai))

Atomic strategy
Switch the clonal mark from a heritable, integrating barcode to a non-integrating episomal barcode whose copy number decays predictably with cell division. The decay itself encodes proliferative history; the barcode spectrum encodes clonal richness/evenness. This single design change converts every routine blood draw into a joint readout of engraftment status and polyclonal dynamics without bone-marrow sampling. Integrating lentiviral barcodes dominate current hematopoietic lineage tracing; leveraging integration-deficient lentiviral (IDLV) episomes as the barcode constitutes the conceptual pivot. ([ashpublications.org](https://ashpublications.org/blood/article/115/13/2610/26844/Cellular-barcoding-tool-for-clonal-analysis-in-the?utm_source=openai))

Platform overview (clinical constraints addressed)
- Vector and tag: IDLV-delivered DNA barcodes (non-integrating 1-/2-LTR circles) that persist in nondividing cells, express transiently, and dilute proportionally with cell division. Barcode recovery uses targeted PCR from nucleated lineages. For erythroid/megakaryocytic coverage, include a minimal RNA barcode unit so platelets and reticulocytes, which inherit megakaryocyte/erythroid RNAs despite lacking nuclei, can be assayed by RT-PCR from plasma fractions enriched for platelets or reticulocytes. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2835240/?utm_source=openai))
- Sample source and logistics: Peripheral blood only; sorted leukocyte subsets, platelet-rich plasma, and reticulocyte-enriched red cell fractions at scheduled timepoints up to 1 year. Existing clinical analyzers and immunomagnetic enrichments already quantify reticulocytes and isolate their RNA. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9804789/?utm_source=openai))
- Regulatory feasibility: Ex vivo manipulation with non-integrating vectors reduces genotoxicity relative to integrating marks; residual integration is measurable and monitorable. Assay is targeted PCR/NGS with turnaround on the order of days and cost comparable to small targeted sequencing panels. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3751548/?utm_source=openai))

Specific aims
Aim 1. Engineer and qualify an IDLV “disappearing-ink” barcode library optimized for clinical tracking.
- Design: High-complexity, noncoding barcode cassette flanked by PCR handles; include an independent minimal Pol II promoter-polyA unit that transcribes a barcode RNA (no protein ORF) to enable detection in anucleate outputs (platelets) and in reticulocytes. IDLV ensures episomal delivery; episomes are known to be transcription-competent yet progressively lost with proliferation. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2835240/?utm_source=openai))
- Mechanistic rationale: In quiescent/slow-cycling LT-HSCs, episomes persist longer; in rapidly amplifying myeloid/erythroid progenitors, barcode DNA decays faster, encoding lineage-specific division histories. The same clones’ barcodes appear as RNA in platelets and reticulocytes, which inherit megakaryocyte/erythroid RNAs. ([journals.asm.org](https://journals.asm.org/doi/10.1128/jvi.78.6.2906-2920.2004?utm_source=openai))
- Distinguishing novelty: Prior hematopoietic barcoding relies on genomic integration for permanence; the deliberate use of non-integrating IDLV episomes as mitotically dilutable clonal tags for HSCT has not been the standard paradigm. Related “barcode-decay” lineage tracing with episomal libraries supports feasibility of decay-based inference, but has not been developed for clinical HSCT monitoring. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7894992/?utm_source=openai))

Aim 2. Establish a whole-blood assay to jointly measure engraftment and polyclonal diversity across all hematopoietic compartments.
- Lineage coverage:
  - Myeloid and lymphoid: Extract DNA from sorted granulocytes, monocytes, B, T, NK cells; amplify barcode DNA. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7894992/?utm_source=openai))
  - Erythroid: Enrich circulating reticulocytes and amplify barcode RNA by RT-PCR; reticulocytes retain RNA and are accessible from blood. ([journals.physiology.org](https://journals.physiology.org/doi/full/10.1152/physiolgenomics.00247.2006?utm_source=openai))
  - Megakaryocytic: Isolate platelets from platelet-rich plasma and amplify barcode RNA; platelets carry megakaryocyte-derived RNAs and support RNA-seq–like measurements. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7253186/?utm_source=openai))
- Engraftment confirmation metric: Presence of any donor barcode above limit-of-detection in peripheral blood leukocytes within early post-transplant windows constitutes molecular engraftment; longitudinal increase and multilineage detection confirm hematopoietic output. Integrating methodologies (STR chimerism; TCR/BCR repertoires; integration-site analysis) serve as orthogonal comparators but are not required for the primary assay. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7894992/?utm_source=openai))
- Clonal diversity metric: Within each lineage and timepoint, compute richness and evenness (Shannon/Hill numbers) from the barcode spectrum; across time, model clone-level abundance trajectories. These metrics are directly comparable to integrating-barcode studies yet derive from episomal tags. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39523608/?utm_source=openai))

Aim 3. Calibrate and model lineage-specific episome decay to infer proliferative histories and 1-year dynamics.
- Model: Fit a geometric dilution model per lineage and clone in a state-space framework that links observed barcode counts to underlying cell numbers via division-dependent loss and sampling/assay noise. The key parameter is an effective per-division retention probability that differs by lineage due to proliferation kinetics. IDLV episomal literature supports direct proportionality of loss to mitotic activity. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2835240/?utm_source=openai))
- Longitudinal identifiability: Early timepoints (weeks 2–12) contain highest DNA signal in rapidly cycling outputs; later timepoints (months 3–12) retain signal predominantly in slow-cycling compartments and as RNA in platelets/reticulocytes, sustaining 1-year readouts. Platelet and reticulocyte transcriptomics are routine and stable enough to support serial quantification. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7253186/?utm_source=openai))
- Cross-validation: Compare inferred proliferation parameters against known lineage turnover (e.g., granulocyte rapid turnover vs. slower lymphoid kinetics) and against any available clinical metrics (ANC recovery, reticulocyte counts). Literature on lineage tracing with integrating barcodes provides expected qualitative hierarchies for validation. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7894992/?utm_source=openai))

Study design and analysis plan
- Cohort: Prospective HSCT recipients with donor consent for ex vivo barcoding of a defined fraction of CD34+ cells. Non-integrating marking lowers theoretical insertional risk; perform limited integration-site surveillance to quantify any rare IDLV integration events reported in genome-editing template studies. ([iris.unisr.it](https://iris.unisr.it/retrieve/3e59c5b8-0ffd-41c8-aee8-f8750d59a0c5/PIIS1934590922003782.pdf?utm_source=openai))
- Sampling cadence: Peripheral blood at dense intervals early (e.g., weekly in the first 2 months) then monthly through 12 months; isolate leukocyte subsets, platelets, and reticulocyte-enriched fractions for barcode detection as DNA (nucleated) and RNA (anucleate outputs).
- Assay: Targeted PCR/RT-PCR with unique molecular identifiers and spike-in standards to control for PCR jackpotting and extraction efficiency; small-panel NGS.
- Outcomes:
  - Primary: Concordant engraftment confirmation and polyclonal diversity indices across lineages from the same assay.
  - Secondary: Lineage-specific decay constants; between-patient heterogeneity in clonal evenness; detection of clonal skew or dominance emergence.
- Statistics: Mixed-effects models for clone trajectories; diversity rarefaction curves to standardize depth; pre-specified thresholds for engraftment positivity based on assay LOD/LOQ established in Aim 1.

Risk assessment and mitigation
- Signal decay vs. 1-year horizon: Episomes dilute with proliferation; signal could fall below detection late. Mitigation: leverage RNA barcodes in platelets and reticulocytes for sustained detection of lineage output; employ sensitive targeted amplification and UMIs; focus inference on early-to-mid windows for rapidly cycling lineages and on slow-cycling/renewing compartments later. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7253186/?utm_source=openai))
- Residual integration: Although IDLVs are designed to avoid integration, rare integrations can occur. Include low-depth integration-site profiling on a subset of samples to document frequency and ensure the readout is not dominated by integrated events. ([iris.unisr.it](https://iris.unisr.it/retrieve/3e59c5b8-0ffd-41c8-aee8-f8750d59a0c5/PIIS1934590922003782.pdf?utm_source=openai))
- Clinical feasibility: IDLVs have been broadly studied as safer, non-integrating delivery vehicles; ex vivo manipulation of donor HSPCs is standard in gene/cell therapy workflows. Assay relies on blood draws and targeted sequencing, aligning with clinical timelines and costs. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3751548/?utm_source=openai))

Exploratory extension (optional, for improved identifiability)
In a parallel arm, evaluate whether adding a minimal, subthreshold S/MAR motif to a minicircle barcode (delivered by electroporation) extends episome nuclear residence without enabling robust replication, thereby creating a slower-decay tracer to complement IDLV’s faster decay for ratiometric inference. Classical S/MAR episomes replicate once per cell cycle and are mitotically stable at low copy numbers via SAF-A tethering; this arm explicitly tests whether shortened/attenuated S/MAR fragments can provide limited tethering without full replicon behavior, a property not established and thus treated as exploratory. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6789156/?utm_source=openai))

Milestones and readouts for success
- Demonstrate in vitro that barcode copy number in dividing hematopoietic progenitors follows predicted geometric dilution, while remaining more stable in quiescent HSPC-enriched cultures. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2835240/?utm_source=openai))
- In patients, show that:
  - Engraftment is called from the first weeks post-HSCT using the same assay that later quantifies clonal diversity.
  - Myeloid lineages exhibit faster barcode DNA decay than lymphoid, while platelets/reticulocytes provide persistent RNA-barcode detection across months. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7253186/?utm_source=openai))
  - Diversity indices and decay parameters correlate with clinical course and known hematopoietic kinetics, providing actionable, lineage-resolved reconstitution maps.

Expected impact and novelty
This work reframes HSCT clonal tracking around a non-integrating, decay-informative mark, eliminating the need for bone marrow sampling and distinguishing itself from STR chimerism, TCR/BCR repertoire tracking, and retroviral integration–site or integrating-barcode approaches. It leverages established IDLV episomal biology and routine platelet/reticulocyte transcriptomics to deliver a single, blood-based assay that simultaneously answers “has engraftment occurred?” and “how diverse and dynamic is reconstitution across all lineages?” over the first post-transplant year. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2835240/?utm_source=openai))

text:
Title: Endogenous mtDNA Haplotypes as Single-Assay Barcodes for Engraftment Confirmation and Polyclonal Reconstitution After HSCT

Hypothesis-goal (indistinguishable): A single, clinically-deployable assay that phases full-length mitochondrial genomes per cell and co-captures surface immunophenotypes can quantify donor engraftment and lineage-resolved clonal diversity across myeloid, lymphoid, erythroid-precursor, and megakaryocytic compartments, and track their dynamics over one year post-HSCT by exploiting (i) physical co-segregation of mtDNA variants as clonal barcodes and (ii) deterministic shifts in heteroplasmy shaped by sequential differentiation bottlenecks. This leverages endogenous mtDNA variation already validated for human lineage tracing and, in HSCT, avoids exogenous labeling while improving upon fragmentary short-read approaches. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6408267/?utm_source=openai))

Atomic strategy: Treat the hematopoietic hierarchy as a signal-processing cascade that transforms stochastic mtDNA heteroplasmy in progenitors into lineage-stable, phased haplotypes. Read out those haplotypes per single cell with long-read sequencing and co-segregation analysis to define clones; assign cell types via simultaneous antibody–oligo tags to compute chimerism and diversity in one run. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6408267/?utm_source=openai))

Specific aims
- Aim 1: Build and analytically validate a droplet single-cell “mtDNA+ADT” assay that outputs, per cell, (a) a phased, error-corrected full-length mtDNA haplotype and (b) a lineage/state label from antibody-derived tags (ADTs). Demonstrate accurate donor–recipient assignment and clone calling across neutrophils/monocytes/NK/T/B, erythroid precursors/reticulocytes, and platelets. Note: mature RBCs lack mitochondria; reticulocytes and platelets retain mitochondria and are therefore assayable. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3157046/?utm_source=openai))
- Aim 2: Quantify engraftment and clonal diversity per lineage using co-segregation-defined clones and bottleneck-aware variance models; derive decision metrics (e.g., donor fraction, Shannon index, Gini) and QC thresholds.
- Aim 3: Longitudinally track clonal dynamics at prespecified timepoints through 12 months; relate shifts to clinical events and known reconstitution kinetics (early innate recovery, delayed adaptive). ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3103296/?utm_source=openai))

Assay concept and workflow
- Sample schedule and coverage
  - Peripheral blood: weeks 2–6, months 3, 6, 9, 12. Platelet-rich plasma for megakaryocytic output; buffy coat for myeloid/lymphoid; reticulocyte-enriched fraction (CD71high) for erythroid output; marrow aspirate once at month 1–3 for erythroblasts if clinically indicated. Platelets and reticulocytes are included because they retain mitochondria during their functional windows. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6828734/?utm_source=openai))
- Droplet chemistry (single-assay readout)
  - Cell indexing: Encapsulate single cells/platelets/reticulocytes with lysis and reverse-crosslinking buffers, a panel of oligo-tagged antibodies (TotalSeq-compatible), and barcoded primer sets. ADTs generate per-cell lineage/state readouts as in established DNA+protein droplet workflows. ([missionbio.com](https://www.missionbio.com/products/platform?utm_source=openai))
  - Full-length mtDNA capture: Perform tiled long-range PCR (e.g., 3×5.6 kb) using high-fidelity polymerase within droplets. Primers carry cell barcodes and molecule-level UMIs to enable per-cell and per-molecule consensus. Pool, clean up, and prepare long-read libraries (ONT). This enables per-molecule phasing and low-frequency heteroplasmy quantification after UMI consensus, as shown in single-cell full-length mtDNA methods (iMiGseq, Cas9-guided enrichment) adapted here for droplet-barcoded inputs. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10164560/?utm_source=openai))
  - Sequencing and TAT: ONT flow cells; basecalling and demultiplexing by cell barcodes; 24–48 h turnaround in a clinical lab setting.
- Bioinformatics
  - Error suppression: Build UMI consensus per long amplicon, merge tiled fragments to reconstruct full-length, phased haplotypes per cell; eliminate strand- and homopolymer-associated artifacts by consensus and read-level filters validated for long-read UMI approaches. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-020-19687-9?utm_source=openai))
  - Donor–recipient assignment: Compare per-cell haplotypes to donor/recipient references (buffy-coat snapshots at baseline) using multi-SNP haplotype distance, robust to heteroplasmy.
  - Clone definition by co-segregation: Construct a co-segregation matrix of phased variants across cells/timepoints; define clones as variant sets that co-occur above stability thresholds; allow nested subclones when additional variants arise. Prior single-cell studies show mtDNA variants can act as physical, heritable barcodes across hematopoietic lineages, including in HSCT with single-cell assays. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6408267/?utm_source=openai))
  - Bottleneck-aware analytics: Model within-lineage heteroplasmy mean/variance as a function of expected differentiation bottlenecks and proliferative bursts; deviations flag oligoclonal dominance or lineage bias during reconstitution.
  - Outputs per timepoint: For each lineage and globally—(i) donor fraction; (ii) clone count and diversity indices; (iii) largest-clone fraction; (iv) clonal turnover rate; (v) QC flags (e.g., multi-haplotype per droplet).

Validation plan
- Technical
  - Spike-in mixtures of donor/recipient leukocytes with known ratios to test assignment accuracy across heteroplasmy levels; platelet and reticulocyte controls to confirm lineage coverage.
  - Concordance with orthogonal standards in a subset: STR chimerism for donor fraction; traditional single-cell DNA+protein for immunophenotype agreement. ([ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK608246/?utm_source=openai))
- Biological
  - Compare lineage-specific recovery curves with established HSCT kinetics (myeloid early; NK early; T/B delayed). Discrepancies trigger investigation for graft dysfunction or infection. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3103296/?utm_source=openai))

Cohort and longitudinal design
- Enroll 40 allo-HSCT recipients. Collect baseline donor/recipient gDNA for haplotypes. Sample per schedule; store excess material for confirmatory tests. Follow standard-of-care; no genetic manipulation; minimal added marrow sampling.

Clinical translation considerations
- Single-assay dual readout: chimerism and clonal diversity from the same per-cell dataset with comprehensive lineage coverage, including platelets and erythroid precursors. Mature RBCs are excluded by biology. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3157046/?utm_source=openai))
- Feasibility: Builds on proven components—ADTs in droplet DNA workflows and full-length mtDNA long-read phasing—with adaptation to combine them. ([missionbio.com](https://www.missionbio.com/products/platform?utm_source=openai))
- TAT and cost: ONT-based, 24–48 h; panelized antibodies; scalable droplets; compatible with LDT development.
- Edge-case mitigation: If donor and recipient mtDNA haplotypes are unusually similar, add ≤20 short nuclear SNP amplicons into the same droplet reaction without changing workflow class; triggers only when haplotype distance is below pre-specified thresholds.

Milestones and success criteria
- Year 1: Analytical validation (≥99% accurate donor assignment in leukocyte spike-ins at ≥1% minor fraction; clone recall F1 ≥0.9 in mixes).
- Year 2: Prospective HSCT pilot (n=20): per-lineage donor fraction concordance with STR within ±5%; reportable diversity metrics with intra-assay CV ≤10%; detect emergent oligoclonal dominance ≥4 weeks before clinical relapse in at least two cases (signal-generation endpoint). ([ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK608246/?utm_source=openai))
- Year 3: Expanded validation (n=20): demonstrate clinical utility signals (association of diversity metrics with GVHD/relapse) to justify a regulated LDT.

Novelty relative to prior art
- Unlike STR chimerism or immune-receptor repertoire assays, this platform uses phased, full-length mtDNA per cell as endogenous barcodes and unites donor assignment and clonal diversity with simultaneous immunophenotyping in a single assay. Prior HSCT lineage-tracing with mtDNA has leveraged fragmentary reads from scATAC/RNA; here, per-cell long-read phasing and co-segregation enable direct clonal definitions and robust longitudinal matching, including platelets and erythroid precursors. ([ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK608246/?utm_source=openai))

Contingencies
- If long-amplicon efficiency in droplets is suboptimal, switch to Cas9-guided mtDNA enrichment on barcoded single-cell lysates prior to ligation and ONT sequencing; retain the same ADT co-capture and analysis stack. Feasibility of Cas9-guided full-length mtDNA enrichment has been demonstrated. ([doi.org](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-022-33530-3?utm_source=openai))

Ethics and risk
- Minimal-risk, observational sampling aligned with clinical draws; single optional marrow aspirate. No exogenous genetic modification; data de-identified.

Deliverable: A clinically amenable, single-assay platform for simultaneous engraftment confirmation and polyclonal reconstitution profiling across all hematopoietic lineages, with validated longitudinal clone tracking to one year post-HSCT. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6828734/?utm_source=openai))
