text:
Title
A pre-installed, epigenetically written clonal ID and lineage ledger for single-assay, longitudinal assessment of HSCT engraftment and polyclonal reconstitution

Rationale
- DNA methylation is mitotically heritable and encodes lineage history; epimutation-based lineage inference has emerged for hematopoiesis but relies on endogenous, stochastic marks not designed for transplant readouts. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11014487/?utm_source=openai))
- Programmable DNA methylation writers (ZF/TALE/dCas9–DNMT) can lay down targeted CpG methylation at defined loci, establishing durable, locally confined marks measurable by targeted sequencing. ([academic.oup.com](https://academic.oup.com/nar/article/45/4/1703/2605790?utm_source=openai))
- cfDNA in plasma contains contributions from erythroblast and megakaryocyte progenitors, enabling access to nucleated precursors of anucleate outputs; targeted methylation assays can quantify these contributions. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10662131/?utm_source=openai))
- Enzymatic methyl-seq (EM-seq) and targeted methylation sequencing provide robust, low-input clinical readouts. ([febs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com](https://febs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/1878-0261.70303?utm_source=openai))
- Error-correcting DNA barcodes derived from coding theory (e.g., Reed–Solomon-based designs) improve clone calling robustness in the face of PCR/seq errors. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6142223/?utm_source=openai))

Central question-hypothesis
Can a single, pre-installed synthetic genomic cassette—combining a robust error-corrected clonal ID with lineage-gated, heritable CpG “pads”—enable a one-assay measurement that simultaneously confirms donor engraftment and quantifies polyclonal, pan-lineage reconstitution over 1 year after HSCT?

Atomic strategy
Install in donor CD34+ HSPCs a compact safe-harbor cassette that:
- encodes a Reed–Solomon–redundant clonal identifier for high-fidelity engraftment and clone counting, and
- places adjacent synthetic CpG “pads” that are selectively written by a tethered de novo methyltransferase only when hematopoietic lineage programs open pad-specific access.
One targeted enzymatic methylation readout from whole blood (cells) plus plasma (cfDNA) decodes both the clonal IDs and the lineage-experience pad states at each timepoint.

Specific aims
Aim 1. Engineer and validate a synthetic clonal ID plus lineage ledger cassette (CLL-cassette) in human HSPCs.
- Design: (a) a 60–100 bp clonal ID block with an error-correcting codebook (RS-derived) to minimize barcode collisions and enable correction of substitution/indel errors; (b) 6–10 adjacent CpG-dense pads insulated by boundary elements. The DNMT writer is targeted to the cassette via high-affinity DNA-binding domains and restricted by short-range spreading to confine activity. ([academic.oup.com](https://academic.oup.com/nar/article/45/4/1703/2605790?utm_source=openai))
- Lineage gating concept: pad accessibility is controlled by local motif architectures tuned to be preferentially occupied within myeloid, lymphoid, erythroid, or megakaryocytic transcriptional environments; when accessible, the tethered writer deposits predefined binary methylation patterns (pad on/off), which are then mitotically maintained.
- In vitro validation: differentiate engineered HSPCs toward myeloid, lymphoid, erythroid, and megakaryocytic fates; quantify pad-specific methylation states and stability through serial replating; ensure minimal off-target methylation by WGBS sampling near the cassette and at sentinel loci. ([academic.oup.com](https://academic.oup.com/nar/article/45/4/1703/2605790?utm_source=openai))

Aim 2. Demonstrate single-assay engraftment confirmation and clonal diversity measurement across all lineages in vivo.
- Xenotransplant model: transplant engineered human HSPCs into NSG mice; collect monthly peripheral blood for 6–12 months. Perform one targeted EM-seq panel capturing the clonal ID block and CpG pads from leukocyte gDNA and plasma cfDNA per timepoint. ([febs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com](https://febs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/1878-0261.70303?utm_source=openai))
- Outputs: (a) Engraftment fraction (sum of valid clonal IDs / total reads) benchmarked against standard chimerism; (b) clonal abundance distribution (Shannon/Simpson indices) from RS-decoded IDs; (c) lineage engagement per clone from pad states. Confirm erythroid/megakaryocytic coverage using cfDNA, leveraging known lineage-of-origin methylation in plasma. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10662131/?utm_source=openai))

Aim 3. Establish analytical and clinical translation parameters.
- Analytical robustness: simulate and empirically assess error profiles; verify RS decoding accuracy, pad call reproducibility, and detection limits for low-frequency clones. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6142223/?utm_source=openai))
- Clinical feasibility: define blood volumes, sequencing depth, turnaround, and cost for a quarterly sampling schedule over 1 year post-HSCT; compare against STR chimerism, TCR/BCR repertoire methods, and integration-site analysis on the same specimens.

Study design and readout
- Cassette delivery: site-targeted integration into a hematopoietic safe harbor; single-copy preference to avoid multi-locus confounds.
- Writer restriction: DNMT3A/3L catalytic module tethered to the cassette to minimize genome-wide exposure; expression driven by a hematopoietic-restricted, low-level promoter with degron control. ([academic.oup.com](https://academic.oup.com/nar/article/45/4/1703/2605790?utm_source=openai))
- Sampling: at 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, and 12 months post-transplant, draw whole blood; isolate leukocyte DNA and plasma cfDNA.
- Assay: a single targeted enzymatic methylation sequencing panel amplifies the clonal ID and pad regions; identical panel applied to both leukocyte DNA and cfDNA. ([febs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com](https://febs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/1878-0261.70303?utm_source=openai))
- Decoding and quantitation: RS decoding yields per-clone counts; pad methylation called by CpG-majority within each pad. Outputs integrated into a joint clonal-lineage matrix per timepoint; temporal dynamics modeled with state-space approaches to quantify clonal stability, expansion, contraction, and lineage bias.

Key endpoints and success criteria
- Primary: concordant engraftment fraction versus clinical chimerism at all timepoints (non-inferiority margin pre-specified).
- Secondary: accurate clonal diversity metrics in leukocytes; sensitivity to detect ≥1% clone frequency; stability of pad calls across cell divisions.
- Tertiary: detection of erythroid and megakaryocytic lineage engagement from plasma cfDNA pad states, with correlation to reticulocyte counts and platelet dynamics. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10662131/?utm_source=openai))

Risk assessment and mitigations
- Off-target methylation risk: restrict writer localization to the cassette; include insulators; validate off-target landscape in vitro before transplantation. ([academic.oup.com](https://academic.oup.com/nar/article/45/4/1703/2605790?utm_source=openai))
- Low cfDNA representation of the cassette: combine leukocyte DNA (robust clonality and engraftment) with cfDNA (access to erythroid/megakaryocytic progenitors); increase amplicon multiplicity for cfDNA panel to boost sensitivity. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10662131/?utm_source=openai))
- Editor persistence: employ self-limiting expression (degrons) or inducible shutoff after initial months once pad states are established.

Differentiation from existing methods
- Unlike STR chimerism or immune-receptor repertoire sequencing, the CLL-cassette unifies engraftment confirmation and clone-resolved, pan-lineage readouts in a single targeted methylation assay without relying on endogenous sequence polymorphisms or retroviral integration maps. It leverages designed, heritable epigenetic writing at a synthetic locus and error-corrected clonal IDs to raise quantitative reliability. ([academic.oup.com](https://academic.oup.com/nar/article/45/4/1703/2605790?utm_source=openai))

Milestones
- Months 0–9: In vitro cassette engineering; writer confinement; lineage pad calibration; analytical pipeline finalized.
- Months 9–24: Xenotransplantation cohort; longitudinal sampling; cross-validation against standard clinical assays.
- Months 24–30: Pre-IND package for a prospective observational study embedding the single-assay readout alongside standard post-HSCT monitoring.

Expected impact
A compact, pre-installed clonal ID and lineage ledger read by one targeted enzymatic methylation assay can provide durable, quantitative confirmation of engraftment and high-fidelity, clone-resolved reconstitution maps across all hematopoietic lineages for up to 1 year after HSCT, using routine blood draws and plasma. ([febs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com](https://febs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/1878-0261.70303?utm_source=openai))

text:
Title
ECC-Barcode HSCT: A single-locus, edit-then-silenced, error-corrected recombinase barcode for simultaneous donor engraftment quantification and clonal diversity tracking from peripheral blood

Central hypothesis and goal
A single-copy barcode installed at a validated safe-harbor in donor CD34+ HSPCs, stochastically resolved once ex vivo by orthogonal recombinases and then permanently silenced, will provide an invariant, heritable identifier that (i) quantifies donor chimerism and (ii) measures polyclonal reconstitution across all hematopoietic lineages via one targeted sequencing assay on longitudinal peripheral blood samples up to 1 year. Platelet and reticulocyte compartments will be captured by brief lineage-restricted barcode RNA output, enabling comprehensive lineage coverage without cell sorting. Prior work has shown recombinase-based barcoding in mice, platelet/reticulocyte RNA detectability, and clinical-grade HSPC safe-harbor editing; here we integrate these concepts into a clinically scalable, single-assay platform for HSCT. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5905670/?utm_source=openai))

Atomic strategy
Replace phenotype-based cell sorting with a one-time, ex vivo recombinase resolution of a compact barcode cassette integrated at a fixed genomic locus, followed by edit-then-silence. Read the same short barcode region from: (a) genomic DNA of nucleated cells for myeloid/lymphoid lineages; (b) barcode RNA in platelets and reticulocytes for megakaryocytic/erythroid lineages, using a unified UMI-amplicon assay. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5905670/?utm_source=openai))

Innovation
- Single-locus, error-corrected barcode: A recombinase-resolved cassette with built-in parity bits provides high diversity and on-board error detection/correction, unlike random STRs, TCR/BCR sequencing, or viral/AAV barcode libraries. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5905670/?utm_source=openai))
- Edit-then-silence: One-time ex vivo recombination; thereafter the barcode locus is transcriptionally quiescent, minimizing biological burden and drift while retaining detectability in anucleate lineages via brief, lineage-gated barcode RNAs. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4797142/?utm_source=openai))
- Clinically compatible integration: Cas9 RNP targeting to CCR5 or AAVS1 with donor template delivery optimized for HSPCs; approach is aligned with ex vivo clinical gene-editing workflows. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6731271/?utm_source=openai))
- Single-assay readout: One multiplexed UMI-amplicon workflow quantifies total donor chimerism and deconvolves clonal diversity across all lineages from the same blood draw, enabling year-long longitudinal tracking. Prior HDR-barcoding in HSPCs (BAR-Seq/TRACE-Seq) lacked a parity-encoded, edit-then-silenced single cassette designed for direct clinical readout including anucleate lineages. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41596-021-00529-x?utm_source=openai))

Specific aims
1) Engineer and validate the ECC-barcode safe-harbor locus in human CD34+ HSPCs.
2) Build and lock a unified clinical assay to read chimerism and clonal diversity from peripheral blood DNA/RNA.
3) Demonstrate quantitative performance, lineage coverage, and longitudinal stability in humanized mouse models and translated QC samples from clinical HSCT products.

Aim 1. Engineer and validate ECC-barcode in human CD34+ HSPCs
- Design
  - Safe-harbor targeting: Cas9 RNP to CCR5 or AAVS1; donor template (0.9–1.5 kb) with: (i) recombinase-resolvable barcode core; (ii) flanking cHS4 insulators; (iii) a 70 bp synthetic “donor-engraftment tag” adjacent to the barcode for absolute chimerism measurement. Deliver donor by rAAV6 (for kilobase-sized inserts) under GMP-like conditions. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6731271/?utm_source=openai))
  - Barcode core: Interleaved loxP/lox2272 and FRT/F3 sites bracketing eight 20–24 bp “data tiles” and three 20–24 bp “parity tiles” (Hamming(11,k) scheme). A single controlled Cre/Flp pulse produces an irreversible, diverse, error-correctable genotype per HSC. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5905670/?utm_source=openai))
  - Edit-then-silence: Final cassette architecture lacks active promoters in stem/progenitor and nucleated lineages. Two ultra-minimal lineage promoters drive 80–120 nt noncoding barcode RNAs only in late megakaryocytic (PF4) and erythroid (ALAS2) stages; embedded miR-142-3p sites suppress off-lineage leakage. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4797142/?utm_source=openai))
  - Transient recombinase delivery: Cre and Flp mRNA electroporation; no persistent expression.
- Experiments
  - Editing metrics: On-target HDR, allele dosage, and off-target assessment by targeted capture and high-depth sequencing; p53 activation profiling to mitigate AAV6 dose-related DDR. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1934590922003782?utm_source=openai))
  - Barcode diversity/neutrality: Clonal outgrowth assays; colony-forming units; xenotransplant limiting dilution to test long-term repopulation and multilineage output versus mock-edited controls. 
  - Cassette quiescence: RNA-seq/qPCR to confirm minimal transcription in HSPCs and nucleated progeny.

Go/no-go criteria
- ≥20% single-allele HDR in CD34+CD90+ HSPCs with ≤5% loss of repopulating capacity versus mock; no off-target events above pre-specified thresholds; stable cassette with no ongoing recombination after day 3. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-019-11962-8?utm_source=openai))

Aim 2. Build and lock a unified clinical assay for simultaneous chimerism and clonal diversity
- Assay schema (one tube; two libraries)
  - DNA library (buffy coat): UMI-tagged amplicon spanning engraftment tag + barcode tiles; co-amplify a host reference locus for absolute chimerism by ratio-metric ddPCR/NGS. 
  - RNA library (platelet-rich plasma; reticulocyte-enriched fraction): RT-UMI amplicon using the same primers directed to the barcode RNA. Platelet and reticulocyte RNA presence provides megakaryocytic/erythroid coverage. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3937023/?utm_source=openai))
- Error model
  - Use parity tiles for single-error correction/double-error detection; UMI consensus calling; synthetic spike-ins for limit-of-detection calibration (target 0.1–0.5% clone fraction).
- Outputs
  - Engraftment: fraction of donor-engraftment tag reads relative to host reference (primary endpoint).
  - Clonal diversity: unique corrected barcode states and their frequencies; Shannon and Hill diversity indices; lineage-specific clone contributions by comparing DNA vs barcode RNA fractions.
- Turnaround/cost
  - <72 h from draw to report; short-read sequencing of a single 300–450 bp amplicon per library; <$300/sample projected at pilot scale.

Aim 3. Demonstrate quantitative performance and longitudinal stability
- Models
  - Human CD34+ HSPC NSG xenografts with ECC-barcode; peripheral blood sampling at weeks 2, 4, 8, 12, 24, 36, 52.
  - Parallel BAR-Seq/TRACE-Seq comparators to benchmark diversity quantification and temporal stability. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41596-021-00529-x?utm_source=openai))
- Endpoints
  - Accuracy vs orthogonal standards: whole-blood STR chimerism for engraftment; concordance analysis; recovery of expected clonal structures from defined cell mixes.
  - Lineage coverage: detection of barcode RNA in platelets/reticulocytes and alignment with nucleated-cell clonal spectra.
  - Longitudinal robustness: clone gain/loss dynamics; parity-corrected error rates ≤10^-4/base per timepoint; reproducibility across sites.

Study design and analysis
- Sample size: n≥10 xenografts per arm to detect ≥20% difference in recovered clone counts with 80% power (negative binomial model).
- Bioinformatics: demultiplexing; UMI consensus; parity correction; maximum-likelihood deconvolution of clone frequencies; diversity indices with bootstrap CIs; mixed-effects models for longitudinal changes.
- Risk mitigation
  - HDR burden: optimize rAAV6 dose; consider short ssDNA donors and more compact cassettes if needed. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1934590922003782?utm_source=openai))
  - Anucleate RNA instability: stabilize barcode RNA with short circRNA scaffold or GC-balanced hairpins if sensitivity is insufficient; pre-specify fallback to megakaryocyte-derived mRNA capture only, while retaining whole-blood DNA as primary readout. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4797142/?utm_source=openai))
  - Regulatory: demonstrate absence of persistent recombinase transcripts/proteins; no constitutive transgene expression; safe-harbor integration with comprehensive off-target profiling.

Milestones
- Month 6: Cassette integrated and resolved in CD34+ HSPCs; neutrality and quiescence confirmed.
- Month 12: Locked clinical assay SOP; LOD established; external proficiency panel passed.
- Month 18: Xenograft study complete; pre-IDE package drafted with safety dossier.
- Month 24: First-in-human observational feasibility in surplus apheresis QC samples from allogeneic HSCT donors (no infusion) to demonstrate analytical validity against STR chimerism.

Expected outcomes
- Single-assay quantification of donor engraftment and clonal diversity with error-corrected barcodes across all hematopoietic lineages, including platelets and reticulocytes, using routine peripheral blood sampling up to 1 year.
- Superior robustness to sequencing/PCR errors via parity tiles and UMIs.
- Clear differentiation from STR/TCR/BCR/retroviral-integration approaches and from HDR barcoded libraries by employing a single, edit-then-silenced, error-corrected barcode cassette in a fixed safe-harbor, optimized for clinical translation. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9927566/?utm_source=openai))

Comparative context and feasibility
- Recombinase barcoding is established in mouse hematopoiesis but not deployed for human HSCT tracking; safe-harbor HDR in HSPCs is clinically advancing; platelets and reticulocytes provide analyzable RNAs. The proposed convergence is novel and clinically tractable. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5905670/?utm_source=openai))

Ethics and compliance
- All human cell collections under IRB-approved consent; animal studies under IACUC protocols; biosafety per institutional guidelines for ex vivo gene editing.

Deliverable
A validated, clinic-ready barcoding and analytics package (cassette design, editing and recombination SOPs, blood-based dual library kit, and analysis software) capable of simultaneous engraftment confirmation and clonal diversity assessment in HSCT without cell sorting.

text:
Title
Physio-Temporal Demixing with Mitochondrial Anchors (PTDMA): A single-assay, clinically amenable framework to quantify engraftment and polyclonal reconstitution after HSCT from serial peripheral blood

Unified hypothesis-question
Can we noninvasively reconstruct the number, identity, and trajectories of engrafted hematopoietic clones after HSCT by treating each peripheral blood lineage as a distinct temporal filter on shared clonal production, and calibrating this demixing with endogenous mitochondrial DNA barcodes measured in serial, minimally sorted blood compartments? If so, can the same data stream also yield a robust donor–recipient engraftment readout?

Atomic strategy
Exploit known lineage-specific maturation delays and survival kinetics as orthogonal temporal filters to separate latent clonal “factory” outputs across lineages, while using naturally occurring mitochondrial variants (haplotypes and somatic heteroplasmies) detected in leukocytes and platelets as sparse genetic anchors that tie model components to real clones and provide a direct engraftment signal. Platelets and leukocytes retain mitochondria/mtDNA, reticulocytes transiently retain mitochondria before RBC maturation, and erythrocytes lack mitochondria—together enabling multilineage anchoring with predictable temporal offsets. ([ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK470328/?utm_source=openai))

Specific aims
- Aim 1. Build and validate a mechanistic, lineage-coupled state-space model that represents each lineage as a convolution of latent clonal production with lineage-specific impulse responses (maturation delay + survival kernel). Use expectation–maximization with Kalman filtering and Rauch–Tung–Striebel smoothing for joint inference of clone number, abundances, and kernel parameters from noisy longitudinal data. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10585354/?utm_source=openai))
- Aim 2. Develop a targeted, multiplex mtDNA amplicon panel and sorting-lite workflow to generate time-resolved mitochondrial haplotype/heteroplasmy profiles from granulocytes, monocytes, B, T, NK cells, platelets, and CD71+ reticulocytes (when present). Use donor–recipient mtDNA haplotype mixture as an orthogonal engraftment readout and mtDNA somatic variants as anchors linking computationally inferred components to biological clones. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6929387/?utm_source=openai))
- Aim 3. Prospective test in allogeneic HSCT recipients: determine agreement with standard chimerism (STR/SNP) for engraftment, and quantify resolution/accuracy of clonal diversity and dynamics across all major lineages over 12 months. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8065704/?utm_source=openai))

Study design and cohort
- Population: 30 consecutive adult allogeneic HSCT recipients (varied donors/sources) at a single center; exclude recent massive transfusion at enrollment; record transfusions prospectively.
- Sampling schedule: peripheral blood at weeks 1–12 (weekly), months 4–12 (monthly).
- Clinical readouts each timepoint: CBC with differential, absolute lymphocyte subsets by a 6–8 color panel, reticulocyte count, hemoglobin, platelets.
- Sorting-lite fractions: granulocytes, monocytes, CD3+ T, CD19+ B, CD56+ NK, platelets, CD71+ reticulocytes (early months only). Low-pressure immunomagnetic enrichment acceptable for throughput.
- Nucleic acid assays:
  - Targeted mtDNA panel (∼20–40 amplicons covering high-heteroplasmy and hypervariable regions) at ≥5,000× depth per fraction.
  - Optional shallow WGS of buffy coat at months 1, 6, 12 for benchmarking somatic mtDNA burden.
- Reference test: standard-of-care STR/SNP chimerism on whole blood and available subsets at matched visits. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8065704/?utm_source=openai))

Assay workflow and analytics
- Wet lab
  - Same-day processing; platelet isolation before leukocyte lysis to prevent cross-contamination.
  - DNA extraction optimized for low-input platelet mtDNA; UMIs to suppress sequencing/PCR error.
- Signals
  - Counts: lineage absolute counts (CBC/flow), hemoglobin, platelet count, reticulocyte percentage.
  - Genetics: mtDNA haplotype mixture in bulk fractions for donor–recipient engraftment; somatic heteroplasmy trajectories per fraction as sparse clonal anchors; acknowledge erythrocytes lack mtDNA while reticulocytes retain mitochondria only for ∼1 day after marrow egress. ([ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK264/?report=reader&utm_source=openai))
- Forward model
  - Latent clonal production u_k(t) for clone k.
  - Lineage response h_L(t): fixed-form kernels encoding maturation lag τ_L and survival/clearance with timescale θ_L; initialize priors from literature (e.g., platelets ∼7–10 days, monocytes ∼1–2 days, neutrophils short but debated, RBC mass strongly low-pass with ∼100–120-day lifetime, reticulocytes ∼1 day). Treat lymphocyte channels with mixture of fast and slow components. ([ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK470328/?utm_source=openai))
  - Observation: y_L(t) = Σ_k (h_L * u_k)(t) + ε_L(t). A joint observation vector over lineages is fitted.
  - Constraints: non-negativity; cross-lineage lag coupling; clone-sparsity via spike-and-slab prior; lineage-specific scaling.
  - Anchoring: force a subset of components to match measured mtDNA variant allele fraction (VAF) trajectories in platelets/leukocytes/reticulocytes for clones carrying those variants; estimate mapping from VAF to cell fraction per lineage using mtDNA copy-number heuristics and learned scaling.
  - Engraftment: donor–recipient mtDNA haplotype mixture in leukocytes/platelets yields percent-donor estimate; compare to STR/SNP chimerism. Note: this is a hypothesis test; clinical validation is part of Aim 3. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4260364/?utm_source=openai))
  - Inference: extended/unscented Kalman filter + RTS smoother; model selection by Bayesian evidence to choose clone number; uncertainty via bootstrap over timepoints. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10585354/?utm_source=openai))

Outcomes
- Primary
  - Agreement of percent-donor engraftment between PTDMA mtDNA haplotype mixture and STR/SNP chimerism (concordance correlation; Bland–Altman at each time window). ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8065704/?utm_source=openai))
  - Time-resolved clonal diversity (Hill/Shannon indices) and number of active clones contributing ≥5% to at least one lineage at any time.
- Secondary
  - Cross-lineage lag motifs recovered for anchored clones (e.g., myeloid/platelet early pulses, delayed erythroid mass changes) and their stability over time.
  - Early detection of clonal shifts preceding cytopenias, GVHD flares, or relapse, compared against clinical events.
  - Comparative information yield vs routine counts alone and vs genetic-only approaches (e.g., WGS-based somatic phylogenies where available). ([doi.org](https://doi.org/10.1038%2Fs41586-024-08128-y?utm_source=openai))

Validation and benchmarking
- Simulations: generate synthetic cohorts using published lineage half-lives and stochastic clonal production; assess identifiability and error under sampling densities matching HSCT follow-up. ([ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK470328/?utm_source=openai))
- Pilot real-world: blinded analysis of 10 historical HSCT cases with archived serial samples to de-risk workflow.
- Prospective: pre-specified success if (i) engraftment concordance correlation ≥0.9 vs STR/SNP; (ii) at least 70% of clones identified by mtDNA anchors have matching demixed components; (iii) lineage-coupled model outperforms lineage-independent models in AIC/BIC and out-of-sample prediction.

Novelty and rationale
- Distinct from STR chimerism and TCR/BCR/viral integration methods: PTDMA primarily exploits physiological temporal filters and maturation lags across all lineages for demixing, using mtDNA as minimal, endogenous anchors rather than the main measurement. This leverages established biology that platelets and leukocytes contain mitochondria/mtDNA, reticulocytes transiently retain mitochondria, and erythrocytes do not, enabling a practical multilineage anchor scheme from blood alone. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4260364/?utm_source=openai))
- Prior dynamic models have used state-space estimation on barcoded clonal data; here we repurpose the estimator to a new identifiability regime based on lineage-specific impulse responses plus sparse mtDNA constraints. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10585354/?utm_source=openai))
- Mitochondrial variants are validated endogenous lineage-tracing barcodes in hematopoiesis and are sensitive readouts of clonal hematopoiesis burden with age, supporting feasibility for anchor definition. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6469926/?utm_source=openai))

Clinical translation plan
- Sample type: peripheral blood only; ≤20 mL per visit; no marrow.
- Assay time: 48–72 h from receipt to report (counts + mtDNA panel + model).
- Cost drivers: targeted sequencing (amplicon-based), limited sorting, modest compute; amenable to CLIA workflow adaptation.
- Reporting: single, longitudinal dashboard with percent-donor engraftment, number of active clones, diversity metrics, and clone-specific lineage contributions over time.

Anticipated limitations and mitigations
- RBC compartment: absence of mitochondria prevents late genetic anchoring; mitigate by early reticulocyte anchoring and enforcing expected lagged, low-pass coupling to hemoglobin thereafter. ([ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK264/?report=reader&utm_source=openai))
- Platelet peculiarities: platelets can release mitochondria/extracellular mtDNA; apply rigorous isolation and DNase treatment to minimize cfDNA contamination; rely on consistent within-subject trends. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4260364/?utm_source=openai))
- Neutrophil lifespan uncertainty: treat as learnable parameter within reasonable priors; sensitivity analyses across reported ranges. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5225409/?utm_source=openai))
- Donor–recipient mtDNA haplotype similarity: if haplotypes are insufficiently distinct, fall back to standard STR/SNP chimerism for engraftment benchmarking at those timepoints. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8065704/?utm_source=openai))

Milestones
- Month 0–6: finalize panel and workflow; synthetic data validation; pilot n=10 archived cases.
- Month 6–24: enroll n=30; complete longitudinal sampling; interim analysis at 6 months for feasibility.
- Month 24–30: primary endpoint analysis; finalize assay specifications for prospective CLIA validation.

Ethics and data governance
- Genetic testing limited to mitochondrial loci; consent includes disclosure plan for incidental donor–recipient haplotype information; data de-identified; compliance with transplant society recommendations for genetic testing post-HSCT. ([astctjournal.org](https://www.astctjournal.org/article/S2666-6367%2823%2901708-6/fulltext?utm_source=openai))

Success criteria
A single, minimally invasive assay and model that (i) matches or exceeds STR/SNP chimerism for engraftment tracking, and (ii) provides quantitative, lineage-resolved clonal diversity and trajectory estimates over one year post-HSCT, enabling earlier and more precise clinical interventions.

text:
Title
State-gated allele-response profiling from peripheral blood to resolve incomplete penetrance

Hypothesis and integrated research goal
- Hypothesis/Goal: Penetrance of common disease-risk SNPs is governed by whether the relevant regulatory elements become functionally competent in specific immune cell states; a minimal ex vivo “gate-provocation” assay on FACS-sorted blood subsets, combined with targeted genotyping and bulk chromatin profiling, will expose state-dependent, allele-specific regulatory activity that predicts which risk-variant carriers will develop disease. Prior work shows regulatory variant effects are frequently context-dependent under immune activation and enriched in stimulated chromatin, but has not been operationalized for clinical penetrance prediction. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4064786/?utm_source=openai))

Atomic strategy
- Convert static genotype into a conditional signal by provoking lineage-appropriate state transitions ex vivo, then quantify per-locus, per-subset allele-specific chromatin responses as a low-dimensional, interpretable feature that scales individual disease odds. Mechanistic basis: stimulation reveals genetic regulatory effects via chromatin gating; allelic imbalance in accessibility/marks is a proximal readout of cis-regulatory impact. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6858557/?utm_source=openai))

Study population and design
- Indication: autoimmune disease exemplar (rheumatoid arthritis and/or systemic lupus erythematosus), where risk heritability is enriched in immune regulatory elements, particularly upon activation. Case group: clinically diagnosed adult patients. Control group: asymptomatic adults carrying matched risk variants (family-based or biobank-identified). Discovery n≈500 per disease; external validation n≈300. Outcomes: disease status and, where available, onset/severity. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-020-18180-7?utm_source=openai))

Sample collection and sorting
- Peripheral blood (30–40 mL) collected once.
- FACS panel (8–10 subsets): CD14+ and CD16+ monocytes, naïve/memory CD4 and CD8 T cells, B cells, NK cells, plasmacytoid DCs. Sorting yields baseline aliquots and matched stimulated aliquots per subset.

Gate‑provocation stimuli (single, lineage-anchored, 1–4 h)
- Monocytes: LPS (TLR4).
- T cells: anti-CD3/CD28.
- B cells: anti-IgM/IgG.
- pDCs: CpG-A.
- Rationale: minimal, canonical pathways that robustly remodel chromatin and expose response eQTL/caQTL effects without complex time courses. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4064786/?utm_source=openai))

Molecular assays (moderate complexity)
- Targeted genotyping: fixed panel of GWAS risk SNPs for the indication (amplicon or low-pass WGS).
- Bulk chromatin profiling per subset and condition: ATAC-seq or CUT&Tag for H3K27ac. Library merging across loci of interest keeps depth moderate. Quality metrics: TSS enrichment, FRiP/peak counts, nucleosomal patterning. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26656845/?utm_source=openai))

Feature engineering (allele- and state-aware, interpretable)
- Availability Aℓ,c: normalized baseline accessibility/acetylation at locus ℓ in cell subset c.
- Gating response ΔAℓ,c: change after stimulation (stim – baseline).
- Allelic imbalance AIℓ,c: reference vs alternate read imbalance at heterozygous sites within peaks/marks.
- State‑gated allele impact index Gℓ,c = AIℓ,c × ΔAℓ,c; set to 0 if locus not accessible (Aℓ,c below threshold).
- Mosaic load Mlineage: fraction of subsets within a lineage where Aℓ,c exceeds threshold.
- These features are directly supported by stimulated caQTL and allelic-imbalance literature and are observable in bulk assays. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6858557/?utm_source=openai))

Predictive modeling and outputs
- Primary model: hierarchical causal Bayesian logistic regression with partial pooling across loci and subsets to estimate genotype×state effects on disease risk; monotonic priors enforce nonnegative contribution of ΔA for risk alleles where literature supports direction. Secondary deployment model: distilled ensemble of shallow decision trees for auditability and point-of-care scoring. Outputs: calibrated penetrance probability with per-locus, per-subset contribution decomposition and uncertainty intervals.
- Baselines: PRS alone; PRS + unstimulated Aℓ,c; whole-blood transcriptome predictors where available. Improvement quantified by AUC, calibration slope, Brier score, net reclassification improvement.

Analytical controls and confounding management
- Batch/stimulation controls: internal reference donors per run; spike-in normalization for CUT&Tag; stimulus potency QC by sentinel loci response.
- Cellular composition: use FACS yields and CBC differential as covariates; within-subset normalization mitigates global shifts.
- Genetic ancestry: include principal components; evaluate transportability across ancestries.
- Technical replicates in a 10% subset to bound measurement error.

Power and sample size (guideline)
- With ~50–100 informative loci per disease and modest effect sizes (odds ratios at the 1.1–1.3 scale), n≈500 cases and matched carriers supports detection of incremental log-odds contributions from Gℓ,c after shrinkage. Simulation from pilot variance components will finalize n.

Planned pilots and milestones
- Pilot 1 (n=60): assay feasibility, stimulus QC, reproducibility of Aℓ,c, ΔAℓ,c, and AIℓ,c across runs; preliminary Gℓ,c distribution.
- Pilot 2 (n=150): train initial hierarchical model; assess delta over PRS; downselect most discriminative locus–subset pairs to a compact panel (e.g., 20–30 features) for scaling.
- Full study: train/lock model; validate in external cohort; compare to PRS and blood transcriptome classifiers; produce “penetrance report” prototype.

Clinical translation and operations
- Sample type: single blood draw; all steps compatible with clinical labs.
- Cost control: fixed subset panel; bulk assays; targeted genotyping; batch processing.
- Turnaround: 72 h from blood draw to penetrance report in a centralized lab; long‑term, tree‑based distilled model supports decentralized scoring.

Success criteria
- Primary: statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement over PRS in distinguishing affected vs unaffected carriers, with well-calibrated probabilities.
- Secondary: interpretable per-locus/subset attributions consistent with known stimulated immune biology and published stimulated heritability enrichments. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6858557/?utm_source=openai))

Novelty relative to prior art
- Prior studies mapped response eQTL/caQTL and allelic imbalance under stimulation, and some used stimulated transcriptomes for prognosis in specific settings; none established a clinically deployable, allele- and state-resolved chromatin provocation assay to predict penetrance among risk-variant carriers. This proposal operationalizes state-gated genotype effects for individualized risk prediction. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4064786/?utm_source=openai))

Risk assessment and mitigations
- Variability in stimulation responses: mitigate by per-run controls, sentinel-locus QC, and excluding failed-stimulus aliquots.
- Sparse heterozygosity at some loci: rely on ΔAℓ,c and lineage mosaic features; instrument causal attribution where AIℓ,c is present.
- Disease heterogeneity: begin with a single disease; extend to others after validation.

Ethics and data governance
- Informed consent for ex vivo stimulation and genomic assays.
- Privacy-preserving model training; share only derived features for multi-site analyses.
- Return of results protocol for penetrance probabilities and genetic counseling.

Dissemination
- Release of standardized gate‑provocation and feature extraction protocol, along with an open-source modeling package and an anonymized, feature-level dataset for benchmarking.

References (key support)
- Context-dependent eQTLs under immune activation and their relevance to autoimmunity. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4064786/?utm_source=openai))
- Stimulated chromatin accessibility reveals disease heritability and candidate regulatory variants. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6858557/?utm_source=openai))
- Allelic imbalance and caQTL methods enabling allele- and state-aware chromatin features. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6858557/?utm_source=openai))
- Prior example of ex vivo stimulation improving clinical prediction (asthma exacerbation), motivating clinical translation. ([academic.oup.com](https://academic.oup.com/jamia/article/24/6/1116/4004728?utm_source=openai))

text:
Title
A functional “environment-compressed” assay for penetrance: nanoparticle-corona challenges of SNP-engineered hepatocytes with an AND-gated inflammatory reporter

Integrated hypothesis–goal
Patient plasma contains a combinatorial milieu of ligands (lipoproteins, complement fragments, cytokines) that can push sensitized intracellular nodes past activation thresholds only in carriers of specific risk SNPs. Compressing this milieu into standardized nanoparticle protein coronas preserves its receptor-level logic while reducing assay variability. Presenting patient-specific coronas to pooled, isogenic iPSC-derived hepatocytes bearing risk SNPs and a minimal NF-κB∧STAT3 AND-gated reporter will yield a discrete Penetrance Activation Index (PAI) that separates carriers likely to convert risk into disease from non-converting carriers. This aims to resolve incomplete penetrance using a clinically tractable blood-based, genotype-aware functional test. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13269704/?utm_source=openai))

Atomic strategy
Route the patient’s high-dimensional plasma state through a reproducible, standardized corona interface that preferentially presents apolipoproteins and complement/acute-phase effectors to cognate hepatocyte receptors (LDLR/SR-BI; complement receptors/TLR4), then read a binary fate decision only when both environmental drive and a SNP-shifted intracellular threshold are simultaneously met (NF-κB ∧ STAT3 promoter with slight positive feedback). ([pubs.rsc.org](https://pubs.rsc.org/en/content/articlelanding/2017/nr/c7nr06437c?utm_source=openai))

Specific aims
1) Engineer and qualify a “compressed-environment” input using standardized nanoparticle coronas from patient plasma.
- Select 2 nanoparticle (NP) chemistries (100±20 nm carboxylated polystyrene; 100±20 nm silica) with opposite surface properties to span corona diversity. Incubate with 0.5 mL EDTA plasma at fixed protein:surface ratios; isolate hard coronas; quantify protein/lipid content; archive aliquots. Assess lot-to-lot reproducibility and per-patient personalization. Minimal targeted corona panel: ApoA-I, ApoB, ApoE, C3/C3d, C4b, CRP, clusterin, α1-antitrypsin, SAA; add one lipid class ratio (CE/TG). ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13269704/?utm_source=openai))
- Mechanistic validation: show that apo-enriched coronas increase hepatocyte association via SR-BI/LDLR and that complement-rich coronas enhance NF-κB priming; test with BLT-1 (SR-BI inhibitor), LDLR-blocking antibody, EGTA/Mg2+ and EDTA (pathway-selective complement inhibition). Outcome: receptor- and complement-dependence curves. ([pubs.rsc.org](https://pubs.rsc.org/en/content/articlelanding/2017/nr/c7nr06437c?utm_source=openai))

2) Build a pooled, isogenic iPSC-hepatocyte panel with allele barcodes and an NF-κB∧STAT3 AND-gated reporter tuned for digital flips.
- Edit 3–5 common hepatic risk loci (e.g., NAFLD/TG handling) into a reference iPSC line to generate isogenic pairs; associate each allele with a short expressed barcode in a neutral 3′ UTR for pooled deconvolution from the same lysate. Differentiate to hepatocyte-like cells (HLCs). Validate basic hepatic function in perfused culture. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34262995/?utm_source=openai))
- Reporter: synthetic promoter harboring κB and STAT-response elements, plus minimal positive feedback (auto-activation via a weak transactivator) to ensure ultrasensitive, bistable response; calibrate with IL-1β±IL-6 pulses (acute-phase synergy in hepatocytes). Readout by fluorescence and qPCR. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-017-02055-5?utm_source=openai))
- Pooling and linkage: co-culture all edited genotypes; after exposure, quantify (i) reporter-ON cell fraction by imaging/flow and (ii) genotype proportions via RT-qPCR of allele barcodes from the same lysate, assigning per-genotype ON fractions by deconvolution. Pooled barcoded-perturbation methods establish feasibility of joint phenotype/genotype readout. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9650298/?utm_source=openai))

3) Clinical pilot: compute a Penetrance Activation Index from dynamic challenges and benchmark against PRS and conventional biomarkers.
- Recruit n=60 adults: 30 carriers of prespecified risk SNP(s) with and without disease; 30 non-carriers matched. Collect 2–3 mL EDTA plasma. Prepare coronas (two NP types), plus controls: pooled-healthy corona, albumin-only corona, heat-inactivated vs native complement states. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11864229/?utm_source=openai))
- Expose pooled isogenic HLC monolayers in perfused Transwells to time-structured pulses: prime (10 min), challenge (40 min), recovery (60 min), washouts between conditions. Perfusion improves physiological response fidelity. ([journals.physiology.org](https://journals.physiology.org/doi/full/10.1152/ajpcell.00331.2012?utm_source=openai))
- Outputs per sample: (a) genotype-resolved reporter-ON fractions over time; (b) targeted secretome (albumin, urea, ANGPTL3/4, SAA, selected chemokines); (c) minimal corona panel values. Define PAI as the maximal excess of reporter-ON fraction for risk vs non-risk genotype under the patient’s corona relative to pooled-healthy corona, normalized by cell-intrinsic activation to IL-1β+IL-6. Model PAI against case/control status and clinical indices. 

Design and methods

Assay workflow
- Plasma handling: standardize anticoagulant; pre-clear; split for “native” and “heat-inactivated (56°C, 30 min)” arms to control complement effects. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11864229/?utm_source=openai))
- Corona preparation: incubate plasma with NPs (pre-validated size/charge); wash to isolate hard corona; quantify bound protein. Maintain constant NP:cell ratios across tests; confirm negligible cytotoxicity at working doses; if needed, use corona eluates (protein-only) as a fallback.
- Hepatocyte culture: iPSC-HLC monolayers in perfused Transwells; confirm albumin/urea and CYP activity stability under flow. ([journals.physiology.org](https://journals.physiology.org/doi/full/10.1152/ajpcell.00331.2012?utm_source=openai))
- Reporter calibration: determine threshold settings using cytokine titrations, establish digital flip and hysteresis; confirm NF-κB∧STAT3 dependence with pathway inhibitors. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-017-02055-5?utm_source=openai))
- Exposure regimen: present corona-coated NPs in short pulses under flow to mimic transient systemic exposures; include recovery windows to reveal adaptation vs persistent activation.
- Readouts and integration: live imaging for reporter; multiplex ELISA for secretome; RT-qPCR for allele barcodes and a 12-gene pathway panel. Single lysate per condition supports integrated genotype↔state mapping.

Controls
- Environmental: pooled-healthy plasma corona; albumin-only corona; lipoprotein-depleted plasma corona; complement-inactivated corona; NP-only vehicle.
- Mechanistic: SR-BI/LDLR blockade; complement pathway chelation (EGTA/Mg2+, EDTA); TLR4 inhibitor for coronas rich in endotoxin-independent activators but reported to signal through TLR4/MyD88. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11214757/?utm_source=openai))
- Genetic: wild-type genotype line and corrected isogenic controls.

Primary endpoints
- Penetrance Activation Index (PAI): for each patient sample, max over time of [ONfraction(risk) − ONfraction(non-risk)] under the patient’s corona minus the same under pooled-healthy corona, normalized to cytokine calibration.
- Classification: ROC/AUPRC for case-vs-control among carriers; calibration plots vs clinical severity strata.

Statistics and modeling
- Mixed-effects logistic models for ON probability with fixed effects for genotype, corona type (NP surface), complement state, and targeted corona features; random effects for donor and batch. Sparse models (L1) to maintain interpretability.
- Mediation analysis: quantify how specific corona features (e.g., ApoE/C3d) shift the genotype threshold (interaction terms).

Feasibility and translatability
- Personalized protein coronas are stable, reproducible, and diagnostic-informative; apolipoprotein/complement content governs receptor engagement and immune activation, providing a mechanistic handle. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13269704/?utm_source=openai))
- NF-κB/STAT3 synergy in hepatocytes is established for acute-phase programs, supporting an AND-gated reporter at a real node of disease-relevant decision-making. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5707366/?utm_source=openai))
- Perfused hepatocyte monolayers are standard microphysiology, enabling temporal challenges with improved function and viability. ([journals.physiology.org](https://journals.physiology.org/doi/full/10.1152/ajpcell.00331.2012?utm_source=openai))
- Genotype–phenotype linkage via expressed barcodes is supported by pooled barcoded-perturbation platforms, adaptable here without single-cell omics. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/5181115/?utm_source=openai))

Milestones
- M1 (3 months): Corona standardization; targeted corona panel performance; receptor-block validation.
- M2 (6 months): Edited HLC pool with calibrated NF-κB∧STAT3 reporter; digital flip confirmed.
- M3 (12 months): 60-sample pilot completed; PAI classifier trained; comparison to PRS and standard labs.

Risk assessment and mitigations
- NP toxicity or artifactual uptake: pre-validate inert doses; confirm receptor mediation; switch to corona-protein eluates if needed. ([documentserver.uhasselt.be](https://documentserver.uhasselt.be/bitstream/1942/30445/1/acsnano.9b03824.pdf?utm_source=openai))
- Complement-mediated cytotoxicity: use heat-inactivated arm; chelation controls; titer dose under flow. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11864229/?utm_source=openai))
- Reporter ambiguity: enforce AND logic and shallow positive feedback; benchmark with pathway inhibitors and cytokine titrations. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/18523635/?utm_source=openai))

Deliverable
A clinic-facing, moderate-complexity functional assay that integrates SNP genotype with current systemic chemistry to report a discrete penetrance risk score from blood, surpassing static PRS by testing whether the patient’s environment can actually flip a sensitized cellular switch. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13269704/?utm_source=openai))

text:
Title
Dynamic “wake-up” mapping of risk enhancers in human blood using time-resolved nascent RNA and pooled-donor immune challenges

Hypothesis and goal (inseparable)
Conditional risk variants exert penetrant effects only when stimulus-activated transcription factors open the relevant enhancer and drive nascent transcription; therefore, measuring allele-resolved nascent RNA immediately after defined immune/metabolic challenges in pooled human blood cells will predict, for each carrier, the specific trigger conditions under which their risk program becomes active. The clinical output is a per-person, per-trigger “wake-up map” rather than a static risk score. This leverages time-resolved metabolic RNA labeling and intentional pooled-donor challenges demultiplexed by natural genetic variation. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s43586-022-00157-z?utm_source=openai))

Atomic strategy
Exploit temporal separation of RNA synthesized after a trigger from RNA existing before the trigger via short 4-thiouridine (4sU) labeling and base-conversion detection (SLAM-/NASC-like). Quantify, within the same assay and well, the allele-specific new/total RNA ratio at sentinel risk genes and enhancers as the direct, causal readout of trigger-gated enhancer activity. Perform challenges in pooled PBMC/whole-blood cultures so all donors share the same paracrine milieu; recover donor identity and genotypes from the same libraries by SNP-based demultiplexing. The single scalar per locus—Δnascent (stimulated vs. baseline) normalized by total RNA—constitutes the “wake-up score.” ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6637240/?utm_source=openai))

Specific aims
1) Build a clinically compatible assay for allele-resolved nascent transcription in human blood
- Sample: fresh PBMCs or small-volume whole-blood aliquots from at-risk yet asymptomatic adults.
- Challenge panel: type I IFN (IFN-β), IFN-γ, TLR4 (LPS), glycolytic stress (low glucose + lactate), and lipid stress (palmitate/oleate). IFNs are included because they potently upregulate antigen presentation programs central to many immune diseases. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/9301532/?utm_source=openai))
- Temporal labeling: add 4sU at t=0 with stimulus; harvest at 30–60 min (“early nascent”) and 4 h (“early steady-state”). 4sU is rapidly incorporated into newly synthesized RNA; chemical conversion enables new/old RNA separation without dual libraries. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5783291/?utm_source=openai))
- Library design: a targeted capture panel (≈250–400 transcripts) covering:
  a) disease-anchored sentinel genes near common immune/metabolic risk loci and their eRNAs if transcribed;
  b) pathway sentinels (ISGs, NF-κB, STAT targets);
  c) HLA class I/II transcripts for immune-state readout and optional allele resolution;
  d) 50–200 high-MAF identity SNPs embedded as short amplicons recovered from the same lysate (TARGET-seq–style) or resolved through expressed SNPs, enabling genotype-aware demultiplexing. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7320622/?utm_source=openai))
- Output per donor per condition: gene- and allele-specific “wake-up scores” = new/(new+old) after stimulation, minus baseline at matched time.

2) Use intentional pooled-donor challenges to expose G×E and paracrine dependencies
- Pool 4–8 donors per well (balanced by carrier status for pre-specified variants). Pooled cultures experience the same primary trigger and shared secondary cytokines released by hyper-responders. Demultiplex donors using genotype-based methods (e.g., demuxlet/Vireo/Souporcell) from the same sequencing data; quantify within-well cytokine pathway activity via sentinel ISGs/NF-κB modules to model paracrine dose. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5784859/?utm_source=openai))
- Rationale: pooled IFN-β–treated lupus PBMCs have been profiled with demuxlet, demonstrating feasibility of pooled, stimulated donor designs; here, the novelty is coupling this with nascent-RNA readouts to resolve the causal moment of enhancer activation and explicitly using the shared paracrine environment as a second-layer trigger. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5784859/?utm_source=openai))
- Readouts: per locus and donor, estimate two thresholds: θprimary (dose–response to the applied stimulus) and θparacrine (inferred from sentinel cytokine modules within the same well). The combination defines a two-hit “penetrance gate” for each risk enhancer.

3) Validate clinical translatability and predictive value
- Cohort: 60–100 individuals enriched for carriers of common immune/metabolic risk haplotypes (e.g., HLA-DR/DQ alleles, IRF7/STAT1-pathway variants, lipid-handling loci). HLA allele-specific expression will be extracted to relate genotype to antigen-presentation responsiveness. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7320622/?utm_source=openai))
- Reproducibility: repeat a subset of donors across independent pools to quantify technical and pool-level variance; compute intraclass correlation of wake-up scores.
- Prospective link: for a subset, collect orthogonal ex vivo endpoints (e.g., monocyte HLA-DR induction by IFN-γ, type I IFN–induced HLA-I upregulation) and simple in vivo, low-risk readouts (e.g., ISG fold-change after seasonal influenza vaccination) to test whether high ex vivo wake-up scores predict stronger in vivo activation under analogous triggers. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5568224/?utm_source=openai))

Design and methods
- Donor pooling and demultiplexing
  a) Pool equal-cell inputs from 4–8 donors per condition/timepoint; include matched baseline wells (with 4sU but no stimulus).
  b) Demultiplex using a genotype-referenced tool (demuxlet/demuxalot) where genotypes exist, or genotype-free (Vireo/Souporcell) otherwise; both are validated for PBMC pools. Doublets are flagged and excluded. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5784859/?utm_source=openai))
- Metabolic labeling and sequencing
  a) Add 4sU (100–200 μM) at t=0; terminate at planned times; perform SLAM-like alkylation to mark new transcripts; prepare targeted RNA libraries with UMI counting. NASC-/scSLAM-like protocols achieve robust new/old separation with short labeling (15–60 min). ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6637240/?utm_source=openai))
  b) In the same workflow, capture HLA transcripts (for allele-specific counts with scHLAcount) and a compact genomic SNP panel or expressed-SNP calls for donor ID. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7320622/?utm_source=openai))
- Triggers and doses
  a) IFN-β (10–1000 IU/mL), IFN-γ (1–100 ng/mL), LPS (1–100 ng/mL), metabolic stressors at physiologically relevant ranges; pilot titrations establish EC50 for pathway sentinels.
  b) IFNs are mechanistically justified triggers because they induce HLA class I/II and reshape antigen presentation, a key axis for many immune-mediated diseases. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/9301532/?utm_source=openai))
- Analytics
  a) Compute, per donor–gene–allele–time–condition, NewFraction = new/(new+old). Define Wake-up Score = NewFractionstim − NewFractionbaseline at matched time.
  b) For loci with exonic SNPs, estimate allele-specific wake-up asymmetry (ASEwake = NewFractionallele1 − NewFractionallele2). For noncoding variants, use target-proximal transcripts/eRNAs as sentinels.
  c) Fit simple, interpretable models (logistic or piecewise-linear) that map stimulus dose and inferred paracrine activity to a binary “on/off” enhancer state per donor and locus, yielding θprimary and θparacrine. Calibrate against orthogonal protein endpoints (e.g., flow cytometry HLA-DR mean fluorescence intensity after IFN-γ). ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5568224/?utm_source=openai))
  d) Report per-person “wake-up maps”: a table listing triggers/doses where each locus crosses its activation threshold, with confidence intervals.

Controls and quality gates
- Negative controls: 4sU-minus wells; vehicle controls; heat-inactivated cytokines.
- Positive controls: canonical immediate-early genes for each pathway (e.g., ISG15, IFIT1 for type I IFN; CXCL10, GBP1 for IFN-γ).
- Technical: ERCC or cell-matched spike-ins to assess conversion efficiency; replicate pools to quantify batch.
- Biological: include noncarriers matched by ancestry; randomize donors across pools to avoid pool-genotype confounding.

Power and sample size
- With 4–8 donors per pool and 3–5 pooled replicates per condition, demultiplexing methods maintain high assignment accuracy; demuxlet and successors have been validated on pooled PBMCs, including under cytokine stimulation. Signals in nascent RNA after 15–60 min labeling are detectable for thousands of genes, enabling per-target power concentration in a targeted panel. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5784859/?utm_source=openai))

Clinical translation
- Sample type and logistics: ≤20 mL blood; same-day processing; assay completes within 2–3 days.
- Cost and complexity: targeted sequencing (≤400 genes) and pooled culture reduce cost versus full scRNA-seq; analysis yields interpretable thresholds (on/off under defined triggers) rather than opaque embeddings.
- Interpretability: outputs are simple condition–response thresholds per locus (e.g., “IFN-γ ≥2 ng/mL triggers HLA-DQ induction in donor X”), directly actionable for exposure counseling or monitoring.

Risk, limitations, and mitigations
- Paracrine variability: treat pooled paracrine signals as measured covariates using sentinel gene modules; replicate pools to stabilize estimates.
- Locus coverage: non-exonic variants lack direct ASE; use proximal sentinel transcripts or eRNAs and, where needed, modest locus-specific amplicons.
- Labeling toxicity: verify viability and pathway readouts across 4sU doses; fall back to 5-EU/LET-seq–style labeling if needed. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11640990/?utm_source=openai))

Milestones
- Months 0–6: finalize panel; establish dosing/time windows; show reproducible wake-up scores in 12 donors across two pools per condition.
- Months 6–12: scale to 60–100 donors; derive θprimary and θparacrine per locus and donor; lock analysis.
- Months 12–18: prospective validation against orthogonal endpoints and limited in vivo analogs (e.g., post-vaccination ISG response).

What is novel relative to prior art
- Metabolic labeling has been used to read nascent transcription, including at single-cell resolution, but not to generate per-person, per-trigger enhancer “wake-up maps” for incomplete penetrance in prospective human challenge designs. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s43586-022-00157-z?utm_source=openai))
- Pooled PBMC demultiplexing is established (including under IFN-β stimulation), but prior work used it mainly to reduce cost/batch or for eQTL discovery; here, pooling is intentional to model real paracrine co-triggers and to estimate per-donor paracrine thresholds coupled to nascent-RNA causality. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5784859/?utm_source=openai))
- Using HLA transcripts as dual-purpose readouts (donor-identifying, allele-resolved immune-state reporters) within a time-resolved nascent RNA assay provides a mechanistically anchored, clinically interpretable bridge from genotype to dynamic antigen-presentation responsiveness. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7320622/?utm_source=openai))

Go/no-go criteria
- Go if ≥70% of targeted loci show measurable wake-up scores with test–retest ICC ≥0.6 and demultiplexing assignment accuracy ≥95% in pools.
- No-go if labeling or pooling irreducibly increases variance such that thresholds cannot be estimated with ≤20% relative error.

Deliverable
A clinically deployable, blood-based assay and accompanying “wake-up map” per individual that specifies which exposures (and approximate doses) are predicted to activate otherwise silent risk programs—resolving incomplete penetrance as a function of conditions rather than as a static probability.

text:
Title
Genotype-conditioned control reserve and attractor occupancy from a single blood draw to resolve incomplete penetrance

Rationale
- Incomplete penetrance is common and hampers risk prediction; carriers of pathogenic variants may remain disease-free across large population cohorts. Predicting who will manifest disease requires modeling how genotype interacts with cellular regulatory state, not genotype alone. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-025-61698-x?utm_source=openai))
- Gene-regulatory networks (GRNs) exhibit multistability; epigenetic configuration sets barrier heights between quasi-stable attractors, while transcripts record fast state. A quasi-potential “landscape” is a principled way to quantify state occupancy and transition propensities. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/nrg.2016.98?utm_source=openai))
- Closed-loop feedback motifs (proportional/integral action) endow robustness and adaptation in biological regulation; negative regulatory nodes (e.g., NF-κB/IκB, JAK–STAT/SOCS) are canonical examples. Quantifying subject-specific “loop gain” provides a mechanistic resilience parameter. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC18287/?utm_source=openai))
- Genetic effects on gene expression are context dependent; stimulation unmasks dynamic eQTLs and enhancer-priming phenomena, supporting perturbation as an informative probe of penetrance risk. ([kennedy.ox.ac.uk](https://www.kennedy.ox.ac.uk/publications/452867?utm_source=openai))
- Multi-block PLS/O2PLS is a lightweight, interpretable integration framework for genomics and multi-omics. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4959355/?utm_source=openai))
- Genetically predicted expression (GReX) separates the genetic component of expression from environmental/residual components; here, the residual can be reinterpreted as a control-theoretic “error” signal. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26258848/?utm_source=openai))
- Whole-blood standardized ex vivo stimulation (e.g., TruCulture) yields reproducible, clinic-friendly functional readouts (transcript and cytokine panels) suitable for multi-center studies. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1521661617301985?utm_source=openai))

Atomic strategy
Use genotype to set each subject’s predicted regulatory set-point (via a low-dimensional genotype→omics map). Define resilience as the capacity of a subject’s closed-loop regulation to minimize the deviation (error) of observed omics from this set-point at baseline and under a mild standardized perturbation. Model disease risk as a function of two interpretable quantities jointly estimated from the same blood sample: (i) Regulatory Gain Index (RGI) from stimulus-response error dynamics and (ii) Attractor Occupancy Score (AOS) from baseline epigenome/transcriptome mixtures along learned attractor axes.

Hypothesis-question
In carriers of the same disease-risk variants, those who will manifest disease have lower pathway-specific control reserve (RGI) and higher occupancy of a disease-aligned attractor (AOS) in relevant blood-accessible lineages, whereas resilient carriers display preserved or enhanced control reserve that counteracts the genotype bias. Can two interpretable indices—RGI and AOS—measured from a single clinically feasible blood draw distinguish future penetrant versus resilient carriers and outperform PRS alone? ([elifesciences.org](https://elifesciences.org/articles/61548?utm_source=openai))

Study overview
- Cohorts
  - Discovery: N≈600 adults enriched for carriers of established risk variants for an immune-mediated or cardiometabolic condition (e.g., autoimmune or inflammatory traits with blood readouts), balanced by ancestry and sex; include unaffected carriers and matched non-carriers. Clinical endpoints: baseline disease status and 3–5 year prospective follow-up for incident disease.
  - Validation: External N≈400 with the same ascertainment and follow-up structure.

- Biospecimen and assays (single visit at enrollment)
  1) Genotyping: genome-wide array with imputation; extract LD-pruned SNP dosages for established risk loci and eQTLs.
  2) Baseline “slow” and “fast” omics:
     - Targeted DNA methylation panel (100–300 CpGs) selected from immune enhancers at disease/eQTL loci (slow variable).
     - Targeted transcript panel (300–600 genes) capturing sentinel pathways (NF-κB, JAK/STAT, interferon, metabolic stress, autophagy, ER stress) plus housekeeping controls (fast variable).
  3) Standardized ex vivo whole-blood stimulation (TruCulture): two conditions—LPS and IFN-γ; 0 h and 4 h collection for RNA (same transcript panel) and supernatant cytokines (12–20 plex). This leverages established multicenter reproducibility while keeping complexity moderate. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1521661617301985?utm_source=openai))

Modeling plan
1) Genotype→omics latent mapping (set-point estimator)
   - Train sPLS/O2PLS models linking SNP dosage (X) to baseline omics blocks Yslow (methylation) and Yfast (transcripts). Retain K components (K≈3–6) explaining maximal shared covariance with sparsity for interpretability.
   - Predict genotype-implied baseline state: Ŷ|X. The residual e0 = Yobs − Ŷ|X defines baseline control error by pathway/component. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4959355/?utm_source=openai))

2) Attractor axes and occupancy (AOS)
   - Interpret O2PLS joint components as attractor axes: slow-loadings approximate epigenetic barrier structures; fast-loadings are readouts.
   - Fit a constrained mixture model over the K axes to obtain subject-specific mixture weights w ∈ ΔK; define AOS as the probability mass on disease-aligned axes derived from case-control labeling in discovery. This leverages the quasi-potential view without heavy mechanistic fitting. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/nrg.2016.98?utm_source=openai))

3) Regulatory Gain Index (RGI)
   - Compute ΔYstim for each stimulus as Y4h − Y0h, and its genotype-predicted counterpart ΔŶ|X by passing X through the same latent map learned on baseline and refit on stimulated data via transfer learning. The dynamic control error edyn = ΔYstim − ΔŶ|X.
   - For each latent pathway/component c, estimate RGIc = 1 − ||edyn,c||/||ΔŶ|X,c|| with sign to capture anti-phase correction; optionally include damping proxy using paired cytokine output. Higher RGI implies stronger effective feedback/robustness along that pathway. This control-theoretic framing builds on integral/negative feedback principles and the empirical value of dynamic eQTL mapping. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC18287/?utm_source=openai))

4) Composite penetrance predictor
   - Fit a survival/ordinal regression for incident disease with predictors: PRS (baseline), AOS, RGI (per-pathway), and covariates (age, sex, ancestry PCs, batch).
   - Primary contrast: PRS-only vs PRS+AOS+RGI. Hypothesis: AOS+RGI add significant discrimination/calibration beyond PRS. ([elifesciences.org](https://elifesciences.org/articles/61548?utm_source=openai))

Endpoints and evaluation
- Primary endpoint: Time to incident disease among asymptomatic carriers at baseline.
- Secondary endpoints: Cross-sectional disease status; pathway-level interpretability (which axes/gains drive risk); portability across ancestries.
- Metrics: C-index for time-to-event; AUC/PR-AUC at fixed horizons; calibration curves; NRI/IDI vs PRS; decision-curve analysis.

Mechanistic validation (ex vivo)
- In a subset (n≈100), modulate predicted weak-gain pathways pharmacologically in whole blood (e.g., low-dose NF-κB or JAK–STAT inhibitors/agonists) and test whether RGI increases and AOS shifts away from disease-aligned occupancy, providing causal support without high complexity.

Clinical workflow and translatability
- One blood draw; closed-tube stimulation; targeted multiplex transcript and cytokine panels; targeted methylation. All assays have established clinical or near-clinical platforms (e.g., Nanostring, targeted bisulfite). Outputs: two interpretable indices (AOS, RGI) and a report of pathway-level deficits. ([onlinelibrary.wiley.com](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1002/eji.202350519?utm_source=openai))

Power and sample size (sketch)
- Assuming 20–30% event rate over 5 years and modest correlation among AOS/RGI and PRS (r<0.3 due to orthogonal design), N≈600 discovery provides >80% power to detect ΔC-index ≥0.05 at α=0.05 for PRS vs PRS+AOS+RGI using time-dependent ROC. External N≈400 targets replication of effect sizes within ±25%.

Data analysis controls
- Cross-validated tuning of sparsity and K; nested CV for performance; permutation tests for stability of loadings; ancestry-stratified models; ComBat or RUV variants for unwanted variation; pre-registered decision rules for component labeling; robust regression on edyn to mitigate leverage points. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/1211.4259?utm_source=openai))

Key risks and mitigations
- Risk: Linear latent models may underfit non-linear biology. Mitigation: limit goals to interpretable axes and gains; if residual structure remains, add kernelized PLS in sensitivity analyses. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40147788/?utm_source=openai))
- Risk: Stimulus choice may not probe disease-relevant axes. Mitigation: two orthogonal stimuli (LPS, IFN-γ) cover TLR and interferon programs tied to many immune traits; iterate stimulus panels in validation if needed. ([kennedy.ox.ac.uk](https://www.kennedy.ox.ac.uk/publications/452867?utm_source=openai))
- Risk: GReX mapping errors. Mitigation: restrict to genes/SNPs with high prediction accuracy in blood; use within-cohort training to minimize cross-population drift. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26258848/?utm_source=openai))

Novelty and feasibility
- Prior work decomposes expression into genetic and residual components (GReX) and maps context-specific regulatory effects; however, reframing residuals as control error and combining genotype-implied set-points with standardized whole-blood perturbation to estimate subject-specific regulatory gain and attractor occupancy for penetrance prediction is, to our knowledge, untested in a clinically translatable pipeline. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26258848/?utm_source=openai))

Milestones
- Year 1: Panel design; assay optimization; discovery enrollment initiated; pre-registered analysis plan.
- Year 2: Complete discovery; finalize latent models; derive AOS/RGI; internal validation.
- Year 3: External validation; ex vivo mechanistic modulation subset; finalize clinical reporting specification.

Deliverables
- Two validated, interpretable indices (AOS, RGI) with software and SOPs.
- Evidence that AOS+RGI improve discrimination and calibration over PRS for predicting penetrance among risk-variant carriers.
- A mechanistically grounded, clinic-ready assay/report compatible with existing blood workflows and moderate cost.

References supporting mechanistic premises and feasibility
- Control-theoretic robustness/adaptation in biology. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC18287/?utm_source=openai))
- Multistability/landscapes for cell states and epigenetic barriers. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/nrg.2016.98?utm_source=openai))
- Context-dependent regulatory genetics via stimulation (dynamic eQTLs/enhancer priming). ([kennedy.ox.ac.uk](https://www.kennedy.ox.ac.uk/publications/452867?utm_source=openai))
- Lightweight, interpretable multi-omics integration (sPLS/O2PLS). ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4959355/?utm_source=openai))
- Genetically predicted expression (GReX) decomposition. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26258848/?utm_source=openai))
- Standardized whole-blood stimulation feasible in clinics. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1521661617301985?utm_source=openai))
- PRS transferability/limitations motivating beyond-PRS approaches. ([elifesciences.org](https://elifesciences.org/articles/61548?utm_source=openai))
