text:
Title: Gate-metric mediation of incomplete penetrance: quantifying signaling thresholds and stress compensation in blood immune cells to identify protective mechanisms in resilient carriers

Integrated hypothesis-question
- Do germline risk variants determine disease only when cell-intrinsic signaling gates cross activation thresholds, and do resilient carriers avoid disease because their gates remain buffered and/or re-tuned under stress? Can we quantify this “gating reserve” and stress-evoked compensation in peripheral blood to resolve penetrance and expose protective mechanisms that are therapeutically transferable? Digital/bistable switching and ultrasensitive thresholds are established features of TCR, Ras/ERK, NF-κB, and STAT signaling, suggesting small upstream differences can yield discrete state transitions; genetic influences on cell state are often context dependent. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2662698/?utm_source=openai))

Atomic strategy
- Replace static, baseline -omics with a minimal, ex vivo, dose-titration readout of pathway gate parameters (EC50, Hill slope, Emax) in defined blood cell types, with and without a mild metabolic co-stress. Model germline variants as causes of gate shifts and stress-evoked reallocation, and test whether these mediate disease vs resilience among carriers. This reframes penetrance as “distance-to-threshold” rather than cumulative linear genetic burden. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3896501/?utm_source=openai))

Cohort and clinical setting
- Target disease area: autoimmunity with known incomplete penetrance and IL-2/IL-2R/STAT signaling involvement (e.g., T1D, IBD). Enroll three groups: affected carriers of established risk alleles (e.g., IL2RA, PTPN2), resilient carriers (≥40 years, no diagnosis), and noncarriers matched on age/sex. Peripheral blood only; cryopreservation allowed. Prior work shows IL2RA and PTPN2 variants modulate IL-2 responsiveness, supporting pathway choice. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8684452/?utm_source=openai))

Assay design (moderate complexity; clinically compatible)
- Stimuli and gates:
  1) IL-2→JAK/STAT5 gate in CD25hi Tregs and CD8+ T cells (ten-point IL-2 titration; 5-min to 30-min readouts). Phospho-flow quantifies pSTAT5 per subset; EC50/Hill/Emax estimated per individual. ([aacrjournals.org](https://aacrjournals.org/clincancerres/article/12/19/5850/192981/Multiparametric-Flow-Cytometric-Analysis-of-Signal?utm_source=openai))
  2) TLR4→NF-κB gate in monocytes (LPS titration; p-p65 or nuclear RelA). Switch-like NF-κB behaviors justify gate metrics. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5516862/?utm_source=openai))
- Stress-reallocation probe (2×2 matrix applied during titrations):
  - Normal vs low glucose (or mild oligomycin) × ± primary stimulus to reveal immune–metabolic coupling without cytotoxicity. Prior work shows monocytes under glucose limitation shift to fatty-acid oxidation and adjust respiratory capacity, indicating measurable compensations. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5447039/?utm_source=openai))
- Secondary cell-state panel:
  - Parallel small CITE-seq (targeted 200-gene panel + 40 antibodies) in a subset of donors to validate transcriptional/protein modules engaged at near-threshold doses; pool donors and assign cells by genetic demultiplexing to reduce cost. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5784859/?utm_source=openai))

Genetic data and pooling logistics
- Germline genotyping by SNP array or low-pass WGS for all participants. For pooled single-cell validation runs, assign donors by genetic demultiplexing from scRNA reads (demuxlet/freemuxlet/Vireo) to scale experiments while retaining donor resolution. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5784859/?utm_source=openai))

Primary measurements and derived mediators
- Gate parameters per person and cell type: EC50, Hill slope, Emax for pSTAT5 (Tregs, CD8+), and for NF-κB in monocytes. These are robust, interpretable pharmacodynamic parameters measurable in whole blood/PBMC and used clinically as biomarkers. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2933839/?utm_source=openai))
- Gating reserve index (GRI): minimal fold margin between estimated in vivo ligand exposure band (clinical ranges or ex vivo surrogate) and each individual’s activation EC50; lower GRI implies proximity to pathological activation.
- Stress compensation vector (SCV): stimulus-induced changes in mitochondrial spare capacity proxy (flow-based TMRE or Seahorse subset), glycolytic markers, and surface activation under low glucose or mild oligomycin; summarizes reallocation under compound constraint. Prior work demonstrates compensatory shifts preserving function under glucose deprivation during LPS activation. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5447039/?utm_source=openai))

Analysis plan
- Hierarchical Bayesian mediation:
  - Exposure: genotype at disease-associated loci (including IL2RA, PTPN2).
  - Mediators: gate parameters (EC50, Hill, Emax) and SCV features with genotype×stress interactions.
  - Outcome: affected vs resilient carrier status (and age-at-onset where available).
  - Goals: estimate indirect effects genotype→(gates/SCV)→phenotype; quantify individual posterior distance-to-threshold; compare against PRS. High-dimensional Bayesian mediation and multi-mediator causal modeling frameworks are established and allow shrinkage and correlated mediator selection. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10423053/?utm_source=openai))
- Validation of context dependence:
  - Replicate associations under stimulated vs baseline conditions; leverage dynamic-eQTL evidence that genetic effects are often treatment- and cell-type-specific. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10519413/?utm_source=openai))
- Positive controls:
  - Expect lower IL-2 EC50 in Tregs vs effectors and wide inter-individual EC50 range; replicate known genotype–IL-2 signaling links (IL2RA, PTPN2). ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6581624/?utm_source=openai))

Key outcomes
- Mechanistic penetrance decomposition:
  - Identify which risk loci act primarily by shifting gate setpoints or steepening slopes, and whether resilient carriers counter-shift these parameters and/or show adaptive SCV signatures under combined stress.
- Predictive, interpretable metrics:
  - Combine GRI and SCV into a penetrance-modifier score that outperforms PRS and remains transparent to clinicians (potency, slope, reserve). ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3896501/?utm_source=openai))
- Therapeutic hypotheses for prevention:
  - Gate retuning: low-dose IL-2 variants or receptor-biased agonists to selectively adjust Treg EC50 without overactivating effectors; partial TLR antagonism to raise monocyte activation thresholds. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7291599/?utm_source=openai))
  - Capacity bolstering: metabolic supports that preserve spare respiratory capacity during inflammation (e.g., FAO support in low glucose contexts) to prevent threshold crossing. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5447039/?utm_source=openai))

Feasibility and translational fit
- Sample type and cost: single blood draw; phospho-flow dose–response is routine and scalable with barcoding; limited 2×2 stress keeps complexity moderate; optional small CITE-seq subset for validation and mechanism anchoring. ([aacrjournals.org](https://aacrjournals.org/clincancerres/article/12/19/5850/192981/Multiparametric-Flow-Cytometric-Analysis-of-Signal?utm_source=openai))
- Biological realism: switch-like NF-κB and digital Ras/ERK behaviors validate the gate concept; IL-2→pSTAT5 EC50/Hill/Emax are measurable and vary across individuals and subsets; genetic effects often manifest under stimulation, aligning with our perturbation-first readouts. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5516862/?utm_source=openai))
- Novelty check: prior work maps dynamic eQTLs and shows genotype effects under perturbation, and clinical phospho-flow studies quantify EC50/Hill in immune cells; however, integrating germline variation with ex vivo gate parameters and stress-evoked compensation as explicit mediators of incomplete penetrance—and using “distance-to-threshold” as the individual-level output—has not been systematically developed. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10519413/?utm_source=openai))

Milestones
- Year 1: establish assay precision; derive GRI/SCV; confirm known genotype–signaling links (IL2RA/PTPN2); preregister Bayesian mediation model. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8684452/?utm_source=openai))
- Year 2: enroll full carrier cohorts; fit mediation; benchmark penetrance-modifier score vs PRS; nominate protective patterns.
- Year 3: small interventional pilot ex vivo/in vitro: test whether candidate drugs (e.g., receptor-biased IL-2 muteins or mild TLR antagonists) restore resilient gate/SCV profiles in affected carriers’ cells. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7291599/?utm_source=openai))

Deliverables
- Public protocol for blood-based gate-metric profiling with standardized titration panels.
- Open-source Bayesian mediation pipeline producing per-individual “distance-to-threshold” reports.
- Shortlist of protective gate/SCV patterns and matched therapeutic levers for prevention trials.

Ethical and data considerations
- Focus on minimal-risk blood assays; consent for recontact; return-of-results limited to validated gate/SCV measures with clear actionability; data de-identified with genotype–phenotype linkage for mediation only.

Success criterion
- A parsimonious, clinically compatible system that explains why two carriers diverge in outcome by quantifying how close their immune signaling gates are to failure—at rest and under realistic stress—and that reveals protective mechanisms present in resilient carriers for preventive translation. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2869519/?utm_source=openai))

Title
Calibrated Extreme-Value Bursting Signatures (CEBaS) for genotype-informed penetrance prediction from blood single cells

Summary
Question-hypothesis: Among carriers of disease-risk variants, do genotype-linked increases in the extreme right tail of allele-resolved single-cell expression—measured in precisely gated blood cell states—identify those who will convert to disease, even when mean expression and polygenic risk are similar? We posit that penetrance emerges when rare “super-bursts” in key pathways cross cellular decision thresholds. Thus, a calibrated tail-centric readout from accessible tissues should outperform averages for predicting who manifests disease. This focuses measurement on mechanistic bursting features known to vary with promoter switching and enhancer action, while staying clinically practical. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10323239/?utm_source=openai))

Atomic strategy
Replace mean-based biomarkers with a single calibrated tail statistic that captures burst-size–driven extreme expression events per allele within disease-relevant blood cell states. The statistic is anchored to an absolute scale using a small ladder of loci with known allelic states, enabling site-to-site comparability and interpretable clinical thresholds. This avoids non-identifiable full telegraph parameter fitting from sparse scRNA-seq while retaining direct mechanistic linkage to bursting. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41131798/?utm_source=openai))

Specific aims
1) Build a targeted multimodal single-cell assay for joint per-cell genotyping, transcriptomics, and surface-protein state gating in blood.
2) Develop and calibrate an extreme-value “Burst Tail Index” that reports allele- and cell-state–specific burst instability on an absolute scale.
3) Test whether genotype-linked tail elevation predicts near-term disease conversion or current subclinical pathology better than PRS and mean/variance metrics.

Rationale and prior knowledge
- Transcription occurs in bursts governed by promoter ON/OFF switching and polymerase loading; enhancers and cis variants modulate burst frequency and size with modest effects on means but pronounced effects on distributional shape. Allele-resolved studies show frequency shifts drive monoallelic incidence, while size changes thicken the high-expression tail. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8498946/?utm_source=openai))
- Parameter identifiability from snapshot scRNA-seq is limited for full telegraph models, motivating robust summary statistics that preserve mechanistic sensitivity. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41131798/?utm_source=openai))
- EVT offers principled estimation of right-tail behavior and has improved biomarker discovery when distributional shape is considered; however, tail-focused EVT has not been standardized as a clinical single-cell biomarker in blood. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7768656/?utm_source=openai))
- Joint per-cell mutational status, RNA, and surface proteins in single cells from human blood is feasible with TARGET-seq–like genotyping and CITE-seq immunophenotyping, enabling allele-resolved counts within tightly defined immune states. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12149610/?utm_source=openai))

Study design

Cohorts and samples
- Discovery cohort: 200 adults (United States), enriched for carriers of known risk SNPs in an immune or metabolic pathway (e.g., type 1 interferon or lipid handling); 1–2 blood draws (10–20 mL) per participant at baseline and 6–12 months for outcome adjudication (conversion to clinical disease, flare, or imaging/biomarker-defined subclinical progression).
- Validation cohort: independent 200-participant set with identical processing.
- Inclusion focuses on conditions with accessible immune readouts; final phenotype chosen to ensure at least 15–20% event rate over follow-up for power.

Assay and data generation
- Targeted multimodal single-cell workflow:
  - Per-cell targeted DNA amplicons for 150–250 SNPs (index and proxies), including disease-risk and calibrator loci; joint whole-transcriptome or 300-gene targeted RNA; 40–80 CITE-seq antibodies for precise blood lineage/activation states. Implement using TARGET-seq+/CITE-seq–style chemistry to barcode DNA, RNA, and ADTs from the same cell. Aim for 50,000–100,000 cells per donor after QC to ensure stable tail estimation within key subsets. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12149610/?utm_source=openai))
- Cell-state gating: derive standardized immune subsets (e.g., classical/intermediate/nonclassical monocytes; naive/effector T; neutrophil-like immature cells if available) using ADTs; restrict analyses to predefined states to reduce confounding by compositional shifts.

Calibrators and absolute scaling
- Include a 10–15 locus “calibration ladder” spanning:
  - Imprinted/monoallelic reference loci (tail ~0 by design in inactive allele contexts).
  - Strong cis-eQTLs with established allelic activity differences.
  - Housekeeping controls with narrow tails.
- Use these to map observed tail statistics to an absolute “cells-above-threshold per 10,000 cells” and to approximate burst-size–dominated vs frequency-dominated regimes, enabling cross-run comparability and fixed clinical cutoffs. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28190458/?utm_source=openai))

Primary measurement: Burst Tail Index (BTI)
- For each gene×allele×cell-state×donor, compute allele-resolved UMI counts; define a high threshold u as the 95th percentile of controls or ladder-matched quantiles within the same state; model exceedances (counts − u)+ with a generalized Pareto distribution; estimate tail shape ξ and scale σ via bias-reduced POT estimators with stability checks. Report BTI as a calibrated function of ξ, σ, and tail exceedance rate τ, mapped to “cells above clinically relevant expression level per 10,000.” Parallelly record a Silent-Fraction Index (SFI) as the zero/near-zero mass proxy for burst frequency. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0378375809000068?utm_source=openai))

Modeling and prediction
- Hierarchical genotype→tail model: Bayesian partial pooling across cells and donors links genotype dose (0/1/2 risk alleles) and local haplotype context to BTI and SFI for risk genes within relevant cell states, adjusting for age/sex/ancestry, batch, library capture, and state proportions.
- Penetrance score: for each donor, compute posterior probability that BTI (or BTI,SFI vector) for a prespecified gene set exceeds calibrated clinical thresholds in ≥1 critical cell state. Compare discrimination vs PRS, mean expression, dispersion, and ASE imbalance. Use nested cross-validation and external validation.

Endpoints and analyses
- Primary endpoint: AUC for predicting conversion/subclinical progression within 12 months.
- Secondary: Net reclassification improvement vs PRS; interpretability (which allele×state drives risk); robustness across sites.
- Mechanistic validation: test whether BTI preferentially increases in genes/pathways where bursting size (not frequency) is known to respond to enhancer or TF perturbation; optionally benchmark on perturbable ex vivo stimuli (e.g., TLR agonists) to verify state-dependence. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1097276516001854?utm_source=openai))

Power considerations
- EVT tail parameters require sufficient exceedances; with 50k–100k cells per donor and subset frequencies of 5–15%, simulations indicate >200–500 exceedances per gene×state are attainable for targeted panels. Design thresholds (u) adapt to maintain ≥150 exceedances per unit, trading precision and bias per Pickands–Balkema–de Haan theory. Interim checks will adjust panel size or pooling rules. ([en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extreme_value_theory?utm_source=openai))

Quality control and mitigations
- Identifiability: avoid full telegraph parameter inversion from scRNA-seq; use tail summaries with calibration to maintain mechanistic interpretability while respecting known identifiability limits. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41131798/?utm_source=openai))
- Allelic assignment: phase informative SNPs per gene using targeted DNA reads; require minimal allele-UMI counts per cell; borrow strength via hierarchical pooling.
- Cell activation artifacts: implement standardized blood handling and cryopreservation, with matched controls and ADT-based activation covariates. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42446933/?utm_source=openai))
- Threshold stability: perform Hill/mean-excess plots and threshold stability checks; predefine ladder-anchored quantiles to reduce operator degrees of freedom. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0378375809000068?utm_source=openai))

Clinical translation
- Sample: peripheral blood; logistics compatible with routine phlebotomy and centralized processing.
- Complexity: targeted panels and low-dimensional tail metrics; portable Bayesian pipeline; per-patient report lists the specific allele×cell-state pairs with elevated BTI and corresponding posterior penetrance probability.
- Interpretability: BTI units are “cells above threshold per 10,000” in a defined state, aligned to known calibrators; clinicians can see which pathway and cell state drives risk.

Milestones
- Year 1: finalize panels; establish calibration ladder; technical validation with replicates and spike-ins.
- Year 2: discovery cohort enrollment; lock analysis; interim futility/feasibility.
- Year 3: external validation; head-to-head with PRS; pre-IDE discussion for clinical study.

Novelty assessment
- While bursting and allele-specific kinetics are established, and heavy-tailed expression has informed bulk biomarker discovery, a calibrated extreme-value, allele- and cell-state–resolved tail index as a clinical single-cell blood biomarker—and its explicit use for penetrance prediction—does not appear standardized or reported, supporting methodological novelty with translational plausibility. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7978379/?utm_source=openai))

text:
Title
Genotype-linked metabolic recovery movies in blood cells to resolve incomplete penetrance

Rationale and prior art check
- Label-free NAD(P)H fluorescence lifetime imaging (FLIM) quantifies redox metabolism and distinguishes immune cell states in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs). Dynamic lifetime components reflect free/bound NAD(P)H and NADPH contributions, and track perturbation responses over minutes. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41867750/?utm_source=openai))
- Early-warning theory predicts that weakening of restoring forces near a tipping point yields slower recovery, higher variance, and elevated lag-1 autocorrelation; these statistical indicators are established across biological systems. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/nature08227?utm_source=openai))
- Isothermal microfluidic genotyping (LAMP or electrochemical melt curves) is rapid, low-cost, and compatible with optical readout; single-cell isothermal assays (e.g., droplet RT-LAMP) demonstrate feasibility of per-cell nucleic acid calls on-chip. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7126597/?utm_source=openai))
- Gap/novelty: I did not find prior demonstrations that couple same-cell NAD(P)H FLIM recovery trajectories in primary human blood cells with on-chip targeted SNP genotyping; existing works either image FLIM without genotype or perform on-chip genotyping without dynamic FLIM. This integration is the methodological novelty to test penetrance. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41867750/?utm_source=openai))
- Clinical motivation: Incomplete penetrance is common and undermines static, genotype-only risk estimates. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9380816/?utm_source=openai))

Hypothesis (integrated with question)
Among carriers of the same disease-risk SNP(s), those who will manifest disease have measurably weaker redox homeostatic control in blood immune cells, revealed as slower and noisier return of NAD(P)H lifetimes to baseline after a standardized sublethal oxidative/energetic pulse. A scalar “metabolic resilience index” derived from recovery time and fluctuation decay improves discrimination of future disease among carriers beyond polygenic risk scores.

Atomic strategy
Treat resilience as a control parameter measured from the shape of a cell’s return-to-equilibrium path. Extract per-cell restoring rate k and noise persistence from NAD(P)H FLIM movies after a calibrated pulse; link these parameters to targeted risk SNP genotype measured on the same cell.

Specific aims
1) Build and validate a microfluidic FLIM–genotype chip for PBMCs that delivers per-cell NAD(P)H lifetime recovery trajectories and matched on-chip SNP calls within 90 minutes. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4046109/?utm_source=openai))
2) Quantify resilience metrics—recovery time-to-ε (T*), exponential rate k = 1/τrec, overshoot, variance, and lag-1 autocorrelation—after a standardized pulse; test critical slowing/noise predictions. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/nature08227?utm_source=openai))
3) In carriers of known risk variants (case-control and prospective cohorts), determine whether genotype-conditioned resilience metrics predict disease status and outperform PRS alone.

Methods

Cohorts and samples
- Discovery case-control: adults with known pathogenic/risk variants that show incomplete penetrance (n≈60 affected carriers; n≈60 unaffected carriers; n≈60 non-carrier controls), peripheral blood collected in EDTA. (Variant sets chosen for expected effects on mitochondrial/redox control or stress responses; examples include common GWAS risk SNPs and selected moderate-effect variants. Genotyping panel finalized a priori.)
- Prospective replication: n≈300 carriers without clinical disease at enrollment, 2-year follow-up for incident events relevant to the variant class.

Chip and assay workflow (Aim 1)
- PBMC capture: Density gradient or RBC lysis; load 1–2×10^6 cells/mL into a PDMS/glass device with hydrodynamic traps (50–200 cells/field).
- Perturbation: 30–60 s pulse of 25–75 μM H2O2 or 2-deoxyglucose (±pyruvate) followed by rapid washout at constant temperature and oxygenation. Pulse choice alternates across fields to map stress-response space; doses validated for sublethality.
- Imaging: Two-photon FLIM of NAD(P)H at 1–2 Hz for 2 min baseline, 1 min pulse, and 8–10 min recovery. Use fast-FLIM hardware/phasor analysis to sustain frame rate and limit dose. Extract per-cell free/bound fractions and bound lifetimes over time. ([biophotonics.illinois.edu](https://biophotonics.illinois.edu/research/nonlinear-imaging/fast-FLIM?utm_source=openai))
- Same-cell genotyping: Following imaging, valve-route each trapped cell to an addressable nanoliter chamber containing alkaline lysis and LAMP primers for a targeted SNP panel (10–50 loci; allele-specific LAMP or mismatch-tolerant LAMP with melt analysis). Optical readout via the same microscope path or integrated photodiodes; optional confirmatory electrochemical melt curves for loci with homopolymers. Turnaround per cell: ≤30–40 min post-lysis. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7126597/?utm_source=openai))
- Quality control: Include synthetic controls and heterozygote references; replicate a subset with off-chip qPCR/genotyping.

Signal processing and metrics (Aim 2)
- Per cell, compute:
  - T*: time to return within 5% of pre-pulse bound-fraction baseline.
  - k = 1/τrec from exponential fit to post-pulse trajectory.
  - Overshoot amplitude (% above/below baseline).
  - Noise statistics on detrended residuals during recovery window: variance and lag-1 autocorrelation ρ1; estimate confidence by block bootstrap. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/nature08227?utm_source=openai))
- Recovery surface: For each genotype g and stress magnitude s, define Sg(s) = E[T*|g,s]. Fit a generalized additive or piecewise-linear model; characterize curvature and threshold-crossing behavior. Provide a per-individual Resilience Index R = w1·k(s0) − w2·ρ1(s0) − w3·T*(s0), weights learned with nested cross-validation.

Study design and analyses (Aim 3)
- Primary endpoint (case-control): AUC of R vs. PRS to classify affected vs. unaffected carriers; test improvement with DeLong and net reclassification improvement.
- Secondary endpoints:
  - Genotype–resilience mapping: hierarchical model k ~ β0 + βg·Genotype + βb·baseline + (1|donor); report effect sizes per SNP and credible intervals.
  - Stress dependence: identify s at which genotype effects on k are maximal (threshold-crossing).
  - Additivity: test whether combining two orthogonal pulses (oxidative vs. energetic) improves prediction.
- Prospective endpoint: hazard ratio for incident disease per SD decrease in R among carriers, adjusted for PRS and covariates (age, sex, baseline inflammation markers).
- Benchmarks and controls:
  - Static FLIM baselines alone vs. dynamic metrics.
  - Replicate-pulse concordance (intraclass correlation).
  - Photodamage controls (sham imaging) and oxygen/temperature stabilization. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8935353/?utm_source=openai))

Power considerations
- For case-control AUC improvement from 0.65 (PRS) to 0.80 (R+PRS), α=0.05, β=0.2, n≈55 per group suffices; we target n=60/group. Prospective power depends on event rate; with 20% 2-year incidence in high-risk carriers, n=300 yields >80% power to detect HR≥1.8 per SD in R.

Feasibility and risk mitigation
- Biological plausibility: NAD(P)H FLIM captures mitochondrial/redox control and has been applied to immune cells and to time-resolved drug responses; recovery is reversible and quantifiable. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11406703/?utm_source=openai))
- Instrumentation: Fast FLIM mitigates temporal undersampling of rapid metabolic shifts. ([biophotonics.illinois.edu](https://biophotonics.illinois.edu/research/nonlinear-imaging/fast-FLIM?utm_source=openai))
- Genotyping on-chip: Direct-LAMP and microfluidic LAMP platforms are robust; electrochemical melt analyses discriminate heterozygotes. Single-cell isothermal assays (RT-LAMP in droplets) support per-cell nucleic acid detection feasibility. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7126597/?utm_source=openai))
- Confounders: Control for cell subset composition (simultaneous widefield immunofluorescence of CD3/CD14/CD19 with low-intensity excitation or post hoc deconvolution using lifetime clusters); standardize caffeine/medication abstinence; record circadian timing.

Clinical translation
- Sample: 4–6 mL peripheral blood; processing-to-answer <2 hours.
- Output: Interpretable report including R at s0, genotype panel result, and categorical risk strata with 95% CIs; designed as an adjunct to PRS, not a replacement.
- Cost: Capital FLIM microscope can be centralized; per-test consumables dominated by microfluidic and LAMP reagents; electrochemical option reduces optics requirements for point-of-care prototypes.

Milestones
- M1 (6 months): Chip v1 with validated FLIM movies and optical LAMP calls in PBMCs; analytical CVs and genotyping concordance >98% on controls. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7126597/?utm_source=openai))
- M2 (12 months): Case-control dataset with recovery surfaces; pre-specified primary analysis complete; external QC blinded repeats.
- M3 (24 months): Prospective cohort 1-year interim readout; locked model and clinical reporting format.

Decision criteria for success
- k and T* differ between affected and unaffected carriers within at least one stress condition with |Δk|/SD ≥ 0.5 and FDR<0.05.
- R+PRS significantly outperforms PRS alone (AUC Δ≥0.1) in case-control and predicts incident disease in prospective cohort (HR per SD ≥1.5).
- Analytical robustness: test–retest ICC ≥0.75 for k and ρ1; per-locus genotyping call rate ≥95% with heterozygote accuracy validated by orthogonal assays.

Deliverables
- Open protocol for “genotyped recovery FLIM” on PBMCs.
- Software to compute resilience metrics and recovery surfaces with uncertainty.
- A validated, generalizable dynamic biomarker of penetrance that complements static PRS with mechanistically grounded, interpretable resilience parameters. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/nature08227?utm_source=openai))

text:
Title
Titrate-to-Reveal: a single-cell, stimulus–response assay to resolve incomplete penetrance among equal-risk carriers

Premise
Risk SNPs often perturb cis-regulatory affinity, but their phenotypic impact is gated by cellular state and pathway input level. Context-specific and time-varying eQTLs under immune stimulation demonstrate that genetic effects emerge or invert only in particular dose–time windows, consistent with nonlinear TF–enhancer dose–response behavior. Therefore, protective carriers likely occupy operating points where identical risk variants remain subthreshold under physiological inputs. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/ng.2945?utm_source=openai))

Atomic question-hypothesis
Among individuals carrying the same disease-risk haplotype, do those who remain healthy exhibit reproducible shifts in dose–time response surfaces of key signaling–regulatory modules that buffer enhancer output, and can these shifts be quantified in accessible blood cells to predict who will develop disease?

Atomic strategy
Force cells to traverse the regulatory nonlinearity by graded, time-resolved stimulation of a pathway mechanistically coupled to the risk locus (e.g., TNF→NF-κB, IFN-γ→STAT1, IL-6→STAT3). Simultaneously read per-cell targeted genotype and proximal protein-state markers, then learn per-individual “protective shift” parameters (ΔEC50, Δslope, Δadaptation) that separate unaffected from affected carriers.

Specific aims
1) Map genotype-conditioned dose–time response surfaces in PBMC subsets from matched affected vs unaffected carriers.
2) Train a Bayesian hierarchical model of genotype-by-state-by-input interactions to estimate individual protective shift parameters and predict clinical status among carriers.
3) Functionally test whether small, clinically plausible perturbations that mimic protective shifts move affected carriers’ cells into a protected operating regime.

Study population and sampling
- Disease contexts: immune-mediated diseases with known stimulus-coupled risk loci (e.g., IBD/TNF–NF-κB; RA/IFN–JAK–STAT). Carriers of matched risk haplotypes are recruited as two cohorts: affected (diagnosed) and unaffected (age- and sex-matched, family-based when feasible).
- Sample: fresh PBMCs (50–80 mL EDTA blood) processed within 4 hours.

Assay platform (integrated genotype + state)
- Discovery (months 0–18): single-cell targeted DNA + protein sequencing (Mission Bio Tapestri) to jointly measure per-cell SNP panel (GWAS risk locus ± LD proxies; 50–200 amplicons) and phospho/surface proteins indexing pathway state and lineage (oligo-tag antibodies). This provides a practical, validated single-cell genotype–phenotype readout at scale. ([missionbio.com](https://www.missionbio.com/products/platform?utm_source=openai))
- Translation (months 12–36, down-selection): cost-reduced microfluidic single-cell ddPCR split-lysate workflow for a minimal SNP panel (≤10) plus multiplexed fluorescence phenotyping (e.g., pSTAT1/pSTAT3/p65; lineage) and droplet indexing of dose/time; supported by established single-cell ddPCR and droplet splitting/phenotyping methods. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10886679/?utm_source=openai))

Stimulation and readouts
- For each donor, major PBMC subsets (CD14+ monocytes, CD4+ T cells, B cells, NK cells) are assayed.
- Inputs: 6-point dose titrations (log-spaced) for pathway-matched ligands (e.g., TNF, IFN-γ, IL-6) and 4 timepoints capturing rise/adaptation (e.g., 15, 60, 180, 360 min).
- Readouts per cell: targeted genotype, phospho-TF and signaling nodes (e.g., pSTAT1, pSTAT3, p-p65), chromatin proxy (H3K27ac IF, optional), and lineage/surface markers. Dynamic eQTL literature supports dose/time dependence of genetic effects under these stimuli. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/ng.2945?utm_source=openai))

Computational model and outputs
- Model: Bayesian hierarchical latent-variable model linking per-cell genotype (with uncertainty), cell subset, stimulus dose, and time to protein-state readouts. The core term estimates allele-by-state-by-input interactions; individual-level random effects summarize protective shifts on interpretable axes (ΔEC50, Δslope, Δmax, Δadaptation).
- Training and validation: nested cross-validation across individuals; calibration with posterior predictive checks. Primary endpoint is discrimination of affected vs unaffected carriers; secondary endpoints include prospective prediction in an independent carrier set.
- Deliverable: a compact “Protective Operating Index” per individual that quantifies how far and along which axis a patient is from the protected regime; format suitable for the translational ddPCR panel.

Aim-by-aim plan
Aim 1. Dose–time penetrance surface mapping
- Design: 60 carriers per cohort (n=120), balanced sex/age; two repeat blood draws for within-person stability (subset n=40).
- Analysis: For each locus–pathway pair and cell type, fit response surfaces stratified by genotype dosage; test for cohort differences in surface parameters. Expectation: reQTL-like effects that peak at intermediate doses or early timepoints, with protective carriers shifted away from the threshold. Prior studies of response/dynamic eQTLs ground feasibility. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/ng.2945?utm_source=openai))

Aim 2. Predictive modeling and minimal marker set
- Train hierarchical model on discovery data; compute variable importance to down-select to ≤8 proteins and ≤10 SNPs for the translational assay.
- Compare against PRS derived from the same loci; primary metric AUROC; hypothesis: Protective Operating Index outperforms PRS among equal-risk carriers because it captures G×state×input interactions. Context-dependent genetic effects justify the superiority of state-conditioned models over static PRS. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9174272/?utm_source=openai))

Aim 3. Causal validation
- Short ex vivo perturbations that mechanistically adjust the inferred protective axis: low-dose JAK inhibition (shifts STAT EC50), IκB kinase modulation (alters NF-κB slope/adaptation), or chromatin softening (low-dose HDACi) in a limited window to test reversibility of the surface. Success criterion: movement of affected-carrier cells into the protected operating region without genotype change.
- Optional locus-proximal CRISPRi/a at sentinel enhancers in donor-derived cells to verify that surface shifts buffer SNP effects as predicted by the model. Dose–response nonlinearity in TF–enhancer systems supports this test design. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12324873/?utm_source=openai))

Statistical considerations
- Power: With 120 donors and ~3,000–10,000 cells/donor, we expect >80% power to detect cohort differences of ≥0.2 in normalized EC50 (SD ~0.3) for common risk haplotypes (MAF ≥0.2) at FDR 5% after multi-level modeling and shrinkage.
- Confounding control: batch-randomized stimulations; technical covariates in the hierarchy; replicate draws; cell-type stratification.

Clinical translation pathway
- Discovery: Tapestri-based assay standardizes single-cell DNA+protein in CLIA-like workflows, enabling immediate feasibility in hospital labs. ([missionbio.com](https://www.missionbio.com/products/platform?utm_source=openai))
- Translation: ddPCR split-lysate + fluorescence microfluidics offers a low-cost (<$80/sample consumables at scale) targeted test with interpretable readouts, compatible with portable thermal cyclers and benchtop droplet imaging; prior single-cell ddPCR and droplet FACS recovery de-risk engineering. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10886679/?utm_source=openai))
- Report: Protective Operating Index and recommended minimal perturbation to achieve protection-equivalent shift, enabling therapy selection or prevention trials among carriers.

Milestones and timeline
- Months 0–6: panel design; assay optimization; pilot (n=10 donors).
- Months 6–18: discovery cohort accrual; Tapestri runs; preliminary modeling.
- Months 18–30: down-selection to minimal marker set; ddPCR microfluidic translation; independent validation cohort.
- Months 30–36: clinical assay specification and prospective test in carriers at risk.

Risk assessment and mitigations
- Weak or absent surface separation: expand cell types or pathway; increase time resolution near early responses; leverage tensor factorization to isolate shared modules across stimuli. Prior reQTL/dynamic eQTL evidence reduces this risk. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/ng.2945?utm_source=openai))
- Genotype calling uncertainty per cell: use probabilistic genotype in the hierarchy and impose cell-to-individual priors; Tapestri platform maturity mitigates discovery-phase risk. ([missionbio.com](https://www.missionbio.com/products/platform?utm_source=openai))
- Cost/throughput: two-tier design—discovery by sequencing, translation by ddPCR—keeps complexity moderate and outputs interpretable.

Innovation
- Moves beyond PRS by explicitly measuring and modeling genotype-by-state-by-input interactions under controlled titration to expose penetrance thresholds.
- Integrates per-cell genotype with proximal protein-state readouts in clinically accessible blood using validated and translatable technologies. ([missionbio.com](https://www.missionbio.com/products/platform?utm_source=openai))

Expected impact
A clinically actionable, interpretable predictor of disease development among equal-risk carriers that identifies the minimal state perturbation needed to confer protection, enabling targeted prevention and mechanism-guided intervention trials.

Title
Protective Mediator Kinetics: An allele-conditioned, single-cell assay to identify and install resilient immune states in risk-variant carriers

Background and Rationale
- Many common-disease risk variants act through context-specific regulatory effects on gene expression that manifest only in particular cell states or upon stimulation; stimulus- and time-dependent eQTLs in human monocytes, dendritic cells, and CD4+ T cells are enriched at GWAS loci and shaped by baseline chromatin “priming.” Thus, incomplete penetrance likely reflects how pre-existing cellular states bias early response trajectories and threshold crossing. ([kennedy.ox.ac.uk](https://www.kennedy.ox.ac.uk/publications/452867?utm_source=openai))
- Installing protective initial conditions is plausible: innate immune “trained immunity” demonstrates that short exposures can durably reprogram myeloid cells via metabolic/epigenetic mechanisms, altering early response amplitudes and resolution kinetics—sometimes beneficial, sometimes detrimental—suggesting a tunable lever for resilience. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41577-020-0285-6?utm_source=openai))
- Spatially resolved, padlock probe–based in situ genotyping with rolling-circle amplification (RCA) and in situ sequencing enables allele-specific detection of DNA/RNA variants within single cells, while multiplexed smFISH methods such as MERFISH quantify tens to hundreds of transcripts in the same cells; padlock/RCA chemistry and error-robust barcoding schemes support highly multiplexed, clinically compatible targeted panels. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26240388/?utm_source=openai))

Atomic Strategy
Measure, model, and modulate a small set of “mediator node” programs—early-response modules whose kinetics gate threshold transitions—directly within allele-stratified single immune cells from blood. Use a brief standardized stimulus to expose kinetic differences between affected and resilient carriers; then emulate resilient mediator kinetics pharmacologically and verify shift in the same targeted, allele-resolved assay.

Hypothesis/Question
Do risk-variant carriers who remain disease-free exhibit distinct, druggable early mediator kinetics (within specific blood cell subsets) that mediate genotype-to-phenotype effects, and can installing those kinetics reduce downstream pathogenic responses in risk carriers?

Specific Aims
Aim 1. Build an allele-conditioned, mediator-kinetics assay in PBMCs.
- Integrate allele-specific padlock/RCA genotyping of selected risk/LD-proxy SNPs with a 60–80-gene MERFISH-style transcript panel capturing mediator modules (e.g., NF-κB immediate early, type I IFN, oxidative stress/Nrf2, autophagy, resolution markers) plus cell-type markers. Perform T0 baseline and T1 = 60–120 min after a standardized stimulus (e.g., low-dose TLR agonist) on cytospun PBMCs. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26240388/?utm_source=openai))
Deliverables: per-cell, per-allele mediator activity and kinetic features (early amplitude, slope, partial return).

Aim 2. Identify protective mediator nodes and quantify causal mediation.
- Construct a compact mediator graph per cell type: SNP → mediator node(s) → ex vivo functional readout (e.g., secreted cytokine burst by cell-type ELISA from matched wells). Estimate natural indirect effects to test whether differences in mediator kinetics account for resilience while keeping models low-dimensional and interpretable. Benchmark against static predictors and TWAS-style associations to ensure added value beyond conventional polygenic models. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10846672/?utm_source=openai))
Deliverables: Protective Mediator Index (PMI) and Trajectory Bias Score (TBS) that classify resilient vs affected carriers and quantify intervention targets.

Aim 3. Emulate protective mediator kinetics and verify installation.
- Short, crossover pilot in risk carriers: assign each participant to a 2-week, low-risk pre-conditioning regimen chosen from a small panel of approved modulators (e.g., metabolic or epigenetic modulators with human safety data) selected ex vivo to shift PMI/TBS toward resilient profiles. Re-measure with the same allele-conditioned assay to confirm kinetic shifts and reduced ex vivo inflammatory output. Ground choice of agents in trained-immunity and enhancer-priming biology while avoiding pro-inflammatory overtraining. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41577-020-0285-6?utm_source=openai))
Deliverables: Protective State Emulation Score (PSES) documenting achieved shift toward resilient kinetics.

Study Design and Methods
Cohorts
- N≈150 adult carriers of pre-specified common risk variants (multi-disease panel enriched for immune and stress-response loci), stratified into: affected (diagnosis or elevated clinical endophenotype) vs resilient (age- and ancestry-matched carriers without disease). Leverage ancestry-aware SNP panels; balance sex and age.

Sample and Stimulus
- Peripheral blood draw; PBMC isolation; aliquots for: (i) mediator-kinetics imaging assay (cytospins), (ii) cell-type–resolved functional readouts (supernatants for multiplex cytokines from matched cultures), and (iii) minimal bulk RNA/protein QC.
- Standardized stimulus: low-dose LPS or R848 to elicit innate modules with minimal cytotoxicity; timepoints T0 and T1=90 min (pilot-optimized). Stimulus/timepoint selection is justified by known dynamics and enriched response-eQTLs in early windows. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5559603/?utm_source=openai))

Integrated Measurement
- Allele-specific padlock/RCA: design gap-fill ligation probes for target SNPs in cDNA or genomic DNA with high-fidelity ligases; in situ RCA to generate rolonies; sequencing-by-ligation or barcoded readout to call alleles in single cells. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26240388/?utm_source=openai))
- Multiplexed RNA imaging: MERFISH-style error-robust barcodes for mediator and marker transcripts; optional RCA-amplified FISH variants for sensitivity on blood smears. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/4662681/?utm_source=openai))
- Registration: co-localize allele rolonies with RNA barcodes in the same cells; assign cell types via marker genes; quantify mediator features.

Readouts and Indices
- Per-cell mediator features: early amplitude (ΔT1–T0), slope estimate (finite-difference), partial recovery (for 2-step stimuli, optional).
- PMI: cell-type–weighted, allele-conditioned mediator node activities (e.g., NF-κB early-response, IFN-I, Nrf2, autophagy).
- TBS: probability that early kinetics will enter a high-output attractor vs resilient basin, estimated via logistic regression with monotone constraints for interpretability.
- Clinical tie-in: correlate PMI/TBS with ex vivo cytokine burst and clinical endophenotypes (e.g., hsCRP or disease activity scores) to establish translatability.

Analysis Plan
- Mediation: test SNP→Mediator→Function pathways per cell type with bootstrapped confidence intervals; report indirect/direct effects and proportion mediated.
- Generalization: nested cross-validation; calibration plots; decision-curve analysis versus PRS or TWAS-informed baselines. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10846672/?utm_source=openai))
- Feature stability: subsample cells and participants to estimate robustness; limit model to ≤10 mediator features to maintain clinical interpretability.

Intervention Pilot (Aim 3)
- Ex vivo screen: in each participant, pre-screen 6–8 approved modulators on short PBMC cultures to rank agents that shift PMI/TBS toward resilient profiles without enlarging cytokine burst.
- In vivo crossover: two 2-week periods separated by washout; primary endpoint is within-person change in PMI/TBS and reduction in ex vivo cytokine burst post-regimen; safety labs tracked. Choice of candidate modulators and dosing windows informed by trained-immunity and immunometabolic literature. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41577-020-0285-6?utm_source=openai))

Feasibility and Novelty
- Mechanistic grounding: enhancer priming links baseline chromatin to later stimulus-specific TF binding; dynamic eQTLs peak in early windows that our assay targets. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6548559/?utm_source=openai))
- Measurement innovation: allele-resolved padlock/RCA co-registered with multiplex RNA imaging provides single-cell coupling of genotype and mediator state in blood—targeted, lower cost than full single-cell multi-omics, and compatible with cytology workflows. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26240388/?utm_source=openai))
- Conceptual novelty: focuses on modifiable mediator kinetics and trajectory bias rather than static risk. Outputs (PMI, TBS, PSES) are interpretable and clinically actionable, enabling preventive emulation of healthy states.

Milestones and Success Criteria
- Year 1: Validate allele calling (>95% concordance with genotyping) and mediator panel reproducibility (CV<15% across replicates). Demonstrate dynamic range at T1 and cell-type assignment accuracy (>90%). ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26240388/?utm_source=openai))
- Year 2: Show that PMI/TBS discriminate resilient vs affected carriers (AUROC≥0.75) and that ≥30% of SNP→function effects are mediated via identified nodes in at least one cell type.
- Year 3: In crossover pilot (N≈30), achieve within-person PSES improvement ≥0.5 SD and ≥20% reduction in ex vivo cytokine burst without adverse inflammatory escalation.

Risks and Mitigations
- Allele miscalling or low sensitivity: employ dual-padlock designs and optimized ligases; confirm with orthogonal genotyping. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5829746/?utm_source=openai))
- Overtraining toward pro-inflammation: prioritize modulators that flatten overshoot and accelerate resolution; gate on decreased ex vivo cytokine burst despite PMI/TBS shifts. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41577-020-0285-6?utm_source=openai))
- Batch effects and complexity: limit to two timepoints and ≤80 transcripts; include fiducials and pooled reference controls per slide; pre-register analysis to maintain interpretability.

Expected Impact
This project delivers a clinically translatable assay and intervention logic that identifies and installs protective mediator kinetics in risk-variant carriers—resolving incomplete penetrance by acting on state-level, druggable nodes rather than static genotype, and enabling prevention-oriented precision medicine. ([kennedy.ox.ac.uk](https://www.kennedy.ox.ac.uk/publications/452867?utm_source=openai))

Title
τ-Guard: A genotype-conditioned, single-cell dynamical assay and reversible “signal sink” intervention to preempt disease commitment in incomplete penetrance

Background and rationale
- In many incompletely penetrant diseases, risk SNPs perturb parameters of gene-regulatory/signaling networks that undergo bifurcations; cells commit when inputs and internal gain push them across a threshold. Near such transitions, recovery from perturbations slows (critical slowing), offering early-warning readouts of proximity to commitment. This has been demonstrated for cell-fate transitions and epithelial–mesenchymal decisions, and has spawned analysis frameworks that explicitly exploit bifurcation signatures. ([journals.plos.org](https://journals.plos.org/plosbiology/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pbio.2000640&utm_source=openai))
- High-throughput single-cell methods now link genotype to state (RNA/protein) in the same cell, including targeted droplet DNA–RNA co-assays (e.g., SDR-seq), plate-based targeted DNA+RNA (TARGET-seq), and RNA/protein co-readouts (CITE-seq), enabling clinically compatible measurements in PBMCs. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12510883/?utm_source=openai))
- Extracellular “sinks” (e.g., engineered decoy receptors and catalytic depleters) can transiently reduce the free concentration or lifetime of commitment-driving ligands/metabolites, keeping hypersensitive networks below threshold without permanent pathway blockade; decoy sinks are standard-of-care in other contexts (e.g., aflibercept, etanercept), and systemic metabolite depletion (e.g., asparaginase) illustrates catalytic sink principles. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3338918/?utm_source=openai))

Hypothesis–goal as a single question
Can a standardized ex vivo pulse–chase applied to clinically accessible cells from risk-variant carriers yield a genotype-conditioned “τ-score” (a relaxation-time proxy of critical slowing) that both (i) identifies the subset of carriers likely to progress and (ii) guides short, reversible sink interventions that reduce τ and prevent commitment?

Atomic strategy
Measure and control a single dynamical scalar per genotype–state: distance-to-commitment encoded in the post-pulse recovery time τ. If τ is high (slow recovery), transiently bleed the relevant upstream driver with an extracellular sink until τ shifts below a predefined safety band.

Study design overview
- Population: Adults carrying validated GWAS risk SNPs for a bifurcation-prone immune pathology (pilot: TLR/IFN-axis autoimmunity in first-degree relatives and cases in remission) and matched controls.
- Sample: Fresh PBMCs (and plasma for ligand baselining).
- Standardized pulse–chase: Short exposure to a pathway-relevant ligand (e.g., LPS, IFN-α, TNF-α) followed by washout; three to five fixed timepoints (e.g., 0, 15, 60, 240 min).
- Readout (same cells): Targeted droplet DNA–RNA co-assay to genotype 50–200 risk/LD SNPs and quantify a 100–300 gene state panel; add 30–60 antibody-derived tags for key surface/state proteins (CITE-seq). Timepoints multiplexed by sample barcodes for a pooled run; parallel phospho-signaling dynamics profiled by barcoded mass cytometry (CyTOF) on sister aliquots to capture rapid post-translational decay. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12510883/?utm_source=openai))

Specific aims and methods
Aim 1. Build the τ-Guard assay and derive τ-scores
- Construct disease-axis gene/protein signatures capturing immediate-early and feedback nodes. Use barcoded timepoints to fit a first-order relaxation model per genotype–cell-type subset: S(t) = S∞ + (S0 − S∞)e^(−t/τ) (hierarchical Bayesian fits across single cells within each subset). The subset-level τ-score is the posterior mean of τ; uncertainty is propagated to all downstream analyses.
- Validate dynamical sensitivity: show larger τ under conditions known to destabilize the pre-commitment state (dose ramp, co-stimulation) and recover shorter τ with negative-feedback strengthening (e.g., phosphatase activators) in vitro. Document standard early-warning features (variance, lag-1 autocorrelation) as secondary checks. ([journals.plos.org](https://journals.plos.org/plosbiology/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pbio.2000640&utm_source=openai))

Aim 2. Link τ to genotype and penetrance
- Jointly model τ as a function of genotype (per-SNP and poly-locus), cell identity, and baseline plasma ligand levels. Test whether carriers with historical disease or subclinical activity exhibit elevated τ in specific immune subsets relative to non-penetrant carriers and controls.
- Novelty check: to our knowledge, τ as a clinical single-cell dynamical risk metric integrated with SNP genotype has not been established; existing works demonstrate critical slowing in cell fate and time-stamped single-cell dynamics but not genotype-conditioned τ-based risk for incomplete penetrance. ([journals.plos.org](https://journals.plos.org/plosbiology/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pbio.2000640&utm_source=openai))

Aim 3. Closed-loop prevention via reversible sinks
- Select sink class matched to the driver ligand/metabolite inferred from Aim 1 (e.g., soluble decoy receptor/aptamer for cytokines or catalytic depletion for metabolites). Titrate ex vivo to define the minimal sink dose that shifts τ below the safety threshold without altering identity markers. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3338918/?utm_source=openai))
- Test preemption: under a subthreshold chronic input that otherwise yields commitment markers at late timepoints, apply brief sink pulses during the window of elevated τ; quantify prevention of commitment (failure to upregulate late differentiation/inflammatory modules and phospho-endpoints) at single-cell resolution.

Aim 4. Translational feasibility
- Reproducibility and cost: targeted panels, droplet chemistry, and sample barcoding keep per-sample costs moderate while preserving interpretability; throughput >10^4 cells/run supports clinical stratification. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10494938/?utm_source=openai))
- Clinical workflow: a same-visit blood draw supports τ-Guard profiling; if τ is high in a genotype-defined subset, schedule short prophylactic sink pulses in high-risk windows (e.g., infection, postpartum) with ex vivo re-testing of τ to confirm on-target damping before any in vivo trial.

Key measurements and analysis
- Primary endpoint: τ-score difference between penetrant vs non-penetrant carriers within matched cell types, adjusted for age/sex/medications.
- Secondary endpoints: early-warning metrics (variance, autocorrelation), stability of identity markers, and dose–response of τ to sink.
- Modeling: partial pooling across donors; genotype-by-state interaction terms; out-of-sample evaluation to test whether baseline τ predicts future flare/surrogates over 6–12 months (banked baseline samples where possible).

Controls and orthogonal validation
- Dynamics verification: on a subset, record rapid signaling kinetics (e.g., NF-κB/ERK) by time-resolved cytometry or live imaging and confirm that longer relaxation correlates with elevated τ-score from snapshot assay. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3627543/?utm_source=openai))
- Genotype capture: cross-validate SNP calls against independent bulk genotyping; for transcribed variants, compare targeted RNA and DNA concordance. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10494938/?utm_source=openai))

Success criteria and decision gates
- Technical: CV of τ <20% across replicate runs; stable τ estimates with 3–5 timepoints; accurate per-cell genotype assignment rate >90%. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12510883/?utm_source=openai))
- Biological: prespecified τ elevation (≥25%) in penetrant vs non-penetrant carriers in at least one immune subset; sink reduces τ into the predefined safe band with concurrent reduction of late commitment markers without identity drift.
- Translational: assay turnaround <72 h from phlebotomy; projected per-test reagent cost within a clinically viable range using targeted panels.

Risk assessment and mitigations
- Per-cell vs subset τ: exact per-cell trajectories are not required; subset-level τ inferred from time-stamped single-cell snapshots is sufficient, and kinetics can be cross-checked by barcoded mass cytometry or limited live-cell validation. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3627543/?utm_source=openai))
- Stimulus choice: select axis-relevant ligands; if unknown, run a small panel and choose the one that maximizes τ separation with minimal off-target effects.
- Sink specificity and safety: prioritize short-acting decoys/enzymes with established safety; titrate ex vivo on donor cells before any human exposure. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3338918/?utm_source=openai))

Deliverables
- A validated, clinically compatible τ-Guard assay reporting a genotype-conditioned τ-score per immune subset from blood.
- An ex vivo dosing guide for reversible sinks that demonstrably shorten τ and preempt commitment markers.
- A decision framework to nominate at-risk carriers for targeted, time-bound prophylaxis, shifting the paradigm from passive prediction to active, reversible prevention.

Title
Resonance-breathing–driven CSF–autonomic entrainment as an awake surrogate for sleep’s restorative dynamics under time-restricted sleep

Background and Rationale
- Sleep expands interstitial space by ~60% and accelerates convective CSF–interstitial exchange, facilitating metabolite clearance; this effect is strongly modulated by noradrenergic tone. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24136970/?dopt=AbstractPlus&utm_source=openai))
- Human sleep features coupled low-frequency neural, hemodynamic, and CSF oscillations; these macroscopic rhythms coordinate clearance and autonomic downshift. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31672896/?utm_source=openai))
- In awake humans, respiration is a dominant driver of CSF flow; slow/deep breathing and paced-breathing paradigms augment CSF pulsatility measured by real-time MRI. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6705733/?utm_source=openai))
- Breathing at the individual cardiorespiratory resonance frequency (~0.1 Hz) maximizes baroreflex gain, HRV, and vagal afferent signaling—the same axis sleep leverages to impose parasympathetic predominance. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4179748/?utm_source=openai))
- Vagal efferent activity mediates the cholinergic anti-inflammatory reflex; augmenting vagal tone acutely restrains pro-inflammatory cytokine production. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17273548/?utm_source=openai))
- Lateral decubitus positioning enhances glymphatic transport relative to supine/prone in rodents, suggesting posture can modulate human perivascular patency. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26245965/?utm_source=openai))

Atomic Strategy
Exploit 0.1 Hz cardiorespiratory resonance breathing—augmented by lateral decubitus micro-bouts—to mechanotransduce sleep-like CSF and venous pulsations and to impose a synchronized parasympathetic state during wakefulness, thereby partially substituting for sleep’s clearance and homeostatic control across neurocognitive, metabolic, immune, and autonomic axes. The causal kernel is mechanical and timing-based: entrain low-frequency pressure oscillations that drive CSF movement while simultaneously maximizing baroreflex-mediated vagal output.

Hypothesis (also the research question)
Can brief, scheduled bouts of resonance-frequency breathing during wakefulness, optionally performed in lateral decubitus, induce a multiaxial recovery state—indexed by enhanced CSF pulsatility, improved autonomic balance, dampened inflammatory signaling, and stabilized cognition/metabolism—that approximates the restorative effects seen after sufficient sleep? ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31672896/?utm_source=openai))

Specific Aims
- Aim 1 (Mechanistic): Quantify the effect of resonance breathing on CSF flow dynamics and autonomic tone during wakefulness.
- Aim 2 (Efficacy under sleep restriction): Test whether scheduled resonance-breathing micro-bouts improve neurocognitive performance, metabolic control, and inflammatory markers after acute sleep restriction.
- Aim 3 (Optimization): Determine whether lateral decubitus positioning during resonance breathing enhances mechanistic and clinical effects.

Design and Methods
- Population: Healthy adults (ages 18–40) with normal sleep; within-subject, randomized, counterbalanced crossover.
- Sleep manipulation: Two conditions separated by ≥7 days: (a) normal sleep (≥7 h, night −1), (b) restricted sleep (4 h, night −1).
- Interventions (day 0, 09:00–17:00):
  - Resonance breathing (RB): 12-minute guided breathing at individual resonance frequency (4.5–6.5 breaths/min) with HRV biofeedback to sustain high-amplitude LF oscillations; four sessions spaced every 2 hours. ([frontiersin.org](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/neuroscience/articles/10.3389/fnins.2020.570400/full?utm_source=openai))
  - Control breathing (CB): Iso-attention audio guidance at 0.25 Hz or spontaneous breathing without HRV feedback (matched duration; counterbalanced).
  - Posture sub-condition (optimization): In 50% of RB sessions, subjects lie lateral decubitus with 10° head elevation; remaining RB sessions are seated. Posture order randomized. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26245965/?utm_source=openai))

Primary Endpoints
- CSF/vascular mechanics (Aim 1):
  - Real-time phase-contrast MRI in aqueduct and foramen magnum (visit-level lab substudy, n=24): mean and peak CSF velocity, stroke volume, and respiratory vs cardiac spectral contributions during RB vs CB. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6705733/?utm_source=openai))
  - Resting-state fMRI (global BOLD power in 0.01–0.1 Hz band) during RB vs CB; coherence with respiratory belt signal. ([alz-journals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com](https://alz-journals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/alz.079182?utm_source=openai))
  - Autonomic: HRV (RMSSD, HF power, LF power, LF/HF), baroreflex sensitivity (sequence/transfer-function methods) during sessions. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10412682/?utm_source=openai))
- Multiaxial recovery (Aim 2):
  - Neurocognitive: Psychomotor vigilance task lapses and median RT; 2-back accuracy; task-switch cost; subjective sleepiness (KSS).
  - Metabolic: Oral glucose tolerance test AUC (08:30 baseline, 14:30 repeat); resting energy expenditure via indirect calorimetry pre/post day; capillary lactate every 2 hours.
  - Immune: Plasma IL-6, TNF-α, CRP at 08:00, 13:00, 17:00. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17273548/?utm_source=openai))
  - Autonomic carryover: Post-intervention HRV and baroreflex sensitivity (17:00 seated rest).
- Optimization (Aim 3):
  - Compare RB-lateral vs RB-seated for MRI CSF metrics (lab substudy) and PVT performance.

Key Procedures
- Resonance frequency determination: Standardized stepped-breathing protocol with HRV biofeedback to identify the rate yielding maximal LF power and baroreflex gain. ([frontiersin.org](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/neuroscience/articles/10.3389/fnins.2020.570400/full?utm_source=openai))
- MRI protocol: 3T scanner; PC-MRI velocity encoding aligned to respiratory belt; pseudorandomized RB/CB blocks; head immobilization; lateral decubitus feasibility assessed in subset with appropriate coils. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6705733/?utm_source=openai))
- Safety: Continuous SpO2 and end-tidal CO2 during breathing tasks; abort criteria for dizziness or hypocapnia.

Predicted Outcomes
- Aim 1: RB will increase respiratory-band CSF pulsatility and stroke volume versus CB and augment HRV and baroreflex indices; magnitude of CSF change will correlate with HRV amplitude across individuals. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6705733/?utm_source=openai))
- Aim 2: Under sleep restriction, RB days will show fewer PVT lapses, improved working memory, reduced IL-6/TNF-α, more favorable OGTT AUC, and higher post-day HRV compared with CB.
- Aim 3: Lateral decubitus during RB will further increase CSF pulsatility and modestly enhance cognitive outcomes relative to seated RB. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26245965/?utm_source=openai))

Mechanistic Interpretation
- If RB increases CSF respiratory pulsatility and improves multiaxial endpoints under sleep restriction, this supports the claim that low-frequency cardiorespiratory entrainment can substitute key sleep-linked clearance and autonomic functions during wake, via a single mechanotransductive and reflexive pathway rather than stimulant masking. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31672896/?utm_source=openai))

Statistical Plan
- Mixed-effects models with fixed factors Condition (Sleep: normal vs restricted), Breathing (RB vs CB), and Posture (lateral vs seated in RB), random intercepts for subjects.
- Primary mechanistic effect: RB>CB on CSF stroke volume and HRV (α=0.05, Bonferroni-corrected).
- Power: n=40 main cohort detects d=0.45 on PVT lapses (within-subject) at 0.8 power; n=24 MRI substudy detects d=0.65 on CSF stroke volume.

Novelty and Feasibility
- Novelty: Directly tests whether a single, scalable, wake-time, timing/mechanical intervention can induce sleep-like CSF–autonomic dynamics and cross-axis recovery. Prior work has not linked resonance breathing to glymphatic-relevant CSF mechanics and multiaxial outcomes under sleep restriction in humans. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6705733/?utm_source=openai))
- Feasibility: RB and HRV biofeedback are safe and field-deployable; MRI protocols for respiratory-modulated CSF flow are established.

Go/No-Go Criteria
- Go if RB significantly increases respiratory-band CSF stroke volume and HRV versus CB and improves at least two domains (neurocognitive performance and one of metabolic/immune/autonomic) under sleep restriction.
- No-Go if mechanistic effects on CSF pulsatility are absent or if multiaxial outcomes do not trend in the predicted direction despite confirmed autonomic resonance.

Potential Extensions
- Closed-loop RB using real-time HRV and respiratory–BOLD coupling to phase-lock low-frequency neural–vascular oscillations.
- Application in operational settings requiring sustained performance with constrained sleep; integration with lateral micro-rest postures. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31672896/?utm_source=openai))
