Title
Mechanical-memory–gated, ECM-anchoring topical hydrogel to prevent adipocyte-to-myofibroblast transition in keloid microenvironments

Hypothesis/Question
Can a single, topical application of an extracellular-matrix–anchoring hydrogel that records cumulative mechanical load and softens only after surpassing a keloid-typical stress-history threshold normalize the pericellular mechanics around dermal adipocytes, thereby preventing adipocyte-to-myofibroblast transition (AMT) and preserving adipocyte metabolic/regenerative functions, while remaining inert on normal skin? ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5505833/?utm_source=openai))

Rationale
- Keloids exhibit chronically elevated matrix stiffness, dense collagen/periostin-rich ECM, and sustained mechanotransduction with nuclear YAP/TAZ; these cues promote fibrotic programs independent of transient wound mechanics. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5505833/?utm_source=openai))
- Keloid tissue displays hypoxia and glycolytic reprogramming with lactate accumulation and acidosis, marking a persistent metabolic state distinct from healthy skin. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7718484/?utm_source=openai))
- Adipocyte differentiation and function are suppressed by stiff matrices via FAK–RhoA/ROCK and YAP/TAZ activation; preventing sustained nuclear YAP/TAZ maintains adipogenic/PPARγ tone. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9367348/?utm_source=openai))
- AMT contributes to fibrosis across organs and has been reported under profibrotic stimuli (e.g., TGF-β), though some studies contest the extent of adipocyte contribution in wounds; this proposal targets adipocytes within keloid/perilesional dermis where chronic mechanics are maximal. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7518402/?utm_source=openai))
- Mechanophore-crosslinked hydrogels can be engineered to undergo covalent scission under mechanical load and can be tuned toward fatigue/cumulative activation (“mechanical memory”). No keloid therapy currently leverages such time-integrated mechanochemical gating. ([pubs.rsc.org](https://pubs.rsc.org/en/content/articlelanding/2025/qo/d4qo02060j?utm_source=openai))

Atomic strategy
Convert chronic, directional mechanical load unique to keloids into a local, durable soft-niche response: a mechanophore-crosslinked hydrogel remains inert on normal skin but, after accumulating the keloid’s stress history, undergoes network scission and modulus drop at the tissue interface, reducing effective pericellular stiffness sensed by adipocytes and preventing YAP/TAZ nuclear localization that drives AMT. ([pubs.rsc.org](https://pubs.rsc.org/en/content/articlelanding/2025/qo/d4qo02060j?utm_source=openai))

Intervention concept (“MEMO-SHIELD”)
- Formulation: A thin, skin-adhesive patch with short dissolvable microprojections deposits an ECM-anchoring hydrogel precursor within upper-to-mid dermis of the scar. The hydrogel network incorporates mechanophores (e.g., gem‑dihalocyclopropane or spiropyran crosslinkers) calibrated to undergo scission under cyclic loading amplitudes measured in keloid tissue over days, not under acute loads typical of normal skin. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5485571/?utm_source=openai))
- Targeting/retention: The backbone bears collagen/periostin-binding motifs to concentrate within dense keloid ECM and minimize spread into compliant, low-density normal dermis. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4262479/?utm_source=openai))
- Mechanism of action: Once the cumulative stress threshold is reached, crosslink scission transitions the hydrogel to an ultra-soft, pericellular coating that mechanically decouples adipocytes from the stiff ECM, lowering focal adhesion maturation, actomyosin tension, and YAP/TAZ nuclear import. A purely mechanical mode avoids systemic metabolic interference. ([doi.org](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41563-026-02590-x?utm_source=openai))
- Optional secondary gate (exploratory): modest pH/lactate stabilization of the softened state via boronic acid–lactate interactions to extend residence in acidic, glycolytic keloid regions without initiating activation alone. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7718484/?utm_source=openai))

Specific aims

Aim 1. Engineer and calibrate a mechanical-memory hydrogel for keloid-relevant stress histories.
- 1.1 Synthesize ECM-binding, mechanophore-crosslinked hydrogel (vary mechanophore type/loading; tune leverage arms and network architecture).
- 1.2 Quantify activation thresholds under cyclic compression/shear that mimic measured keloid stress spectra; fit a damage-accumulation model to define a time-integrated activation criterion. ([pubs.rsc.org](https://pubs.rsc.org/en/content/articlelanding/2025/qo/d4qo02060j?utm_source=openai))
- 1.3 Demonstrate post-activation modulus drop (G′), viscoelasticity, and stability at skin temperatures and ionic strength; assess persistence with/without lactate at pH 6.4–6.8. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-020-2612-2?utm_source=openai))
Success metrics: Distinct fatigue-dependent activation; ≥10× drop in local modulus after threshold loading; minimal activation under single or brief high-amplitude loads.

Aim 2. Test whether activation suppresses AMT and preserves adipocyte function in 3D human co-cultures.
- 2.1 Build 3D cultures of primary human dermal adipocytes (or adipocyte-differentiated ASCs) embedded in decellularized keloid ECM or stiff synthetic gels; overlay with inert vs. pre-activated vs. memory-gated hydrogels; apply cyclic mechanical stimulation. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31255664/?utm_source=openai))
- 2.2 Readouts: YAP/TAZ nuclear/cytoplasmic ratio; FAK/MLC phosphorylation; α‑SMA and COL1A1; adipocyte markers (PPARγ, PLIN1, FABP4); lipid droplet morphology; glucose uptake and lipolysis rates. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9367348/?utm_source=openai))
- 2.3 Challenge with TGF‑β1; determine whether mechanical decoupling alone blunts AMT signaling compared to controls. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7518402/?utm_source=openai))
Success metrics: With activation, reduced nuclear YAP/TAZ and α‑SMA; maintained adipocyte markers and metabolic flux; effect absent with inert hydrogels on compliant matrices.

Aim 3. Evaluate selectivity, durability, and safety in human keloid explants and in vivo.
- 3.1 Human keloid and matched normal-skin explants: apply patches once; track in-tissue hydrogel activation (mechanophore fluorescence), modulus mapping (AFM), and pericellular YAP/TAZ in adipocyte-rich layers over 4–6 weeks. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9124765/?utm_source=openai))
- 3.2 In vivo (human keloid xenograft or hypertrophic scar model): single application; end points at 2, 4, 8 weeks—scar stiffness, adipocyte lineage markers, collagen content, recurrence indicators; biodistribution of polymer fragments. 
- 3.3 Off-target evaluation: contralateral normal skin for inadvertent activation; systemic chemistry, local inflammation, and epidermal barrier integrity.

Experimental design and key methods
- Mechanophore selection and tuning: Compare spiropyran vs. gDCC crosslinkers for cyclic-fatigue sensitivity; use single-molecule force spectroscopy and bulk rheology to map scission probability vs. cycle count and amplitude; embed ratiometric mechanochromic reporters to visualize activation in tissue. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5485571/?utm_source=openai))
- ECM targeting: Conjugate collagen- or periostin-binding peptides; quantify binding in human keloid vs. normal dermis sections. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4262479/?utm_source=openai))
- Mechanotransduction assays: Live-cell YAP/TAZ reporters; traction force microscopy; FAK/RhoA activity biosensors; confirm that softening precedes YAP/TAZ nuclear exit on dynamic-softening substrates. ([doi.org](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41563-026-02590-x?utm_source=openai))
- Metabolic preservation: Seahorse extracellular flux for adipocytes; insulin-stimulated glucose uptake; glycerol/NEFA release; ensure no impairment by inert (pre-activation) hydrogel. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9367348/?utm_source=openai))

Selectivity and single-dose durability logic
- Spatial: ECM-binding concentrates hydrogel in dense keloid matrices enriched for periostin/collagen. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4262479/?utm_source=openai))
- Temporal: Activation requires accumulation of mechanical dose (cycles × amplitude), absent in transiently stressed normal skin. ([pubs.rsc.org](https://pubs.rsc.org/en/content/articlelanding/2025/qo/d4qo02060j?utm_source=openai))
- Durability: Post-scission network remains ultra-soft and retained by ECM binding; optional lactate-stabilization slows reswelling/dissolution within glycolytic, mildly acidic niches. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7718484/?utm_source=openai))

Outcomes and interpretation
- Support for hypothesis: Activated hydrogel reduces pericellular stiffness and YAP/TAZ, prevents α‑SMA induction, and maintains adipocyte metabolic function in keloid-like settings, with no activation or metabolic impact on normal skin.
- Ambiguous outcome: If partial suppression occurs, titrate mechanophore density and ECM-binding valency to increase local softening.
- Refutation: If AMT proceeds despite mechanical decoupling, adipocyte reprogramming may be dominated by nonmechanical cues; pivot to add a minimal, ECM-tethered ROCK inhibitor that is released only upon the same mechanical-memory trigger, keeping the gating atomic and local. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41192091/?utm_source=openai))

Novelty and feasibility
This work introduces a time-integrated mechanochemical gate as the therapeutic selector in keloid tissue—distinct from stiffness-only or pathway-only strategies—and applies mechanophore hydrogels as a pericellular softening therapy to block AMT. Prior reports establish mechanophore activation under force and dynamic substrate softening controlling YAP/TAZ, but no topical, single-dose, mechanical-memory therapy has been reported for keloids. ([pubs.rsc.org](https://pubs.rsc.org/en/content/articlelanding/2025/qo/d4qo02060j?utm_source=openai))

Milestones and go/no-go criteria
- M1 (Month 6): Hydrogel with ≥10× post-activation softening; activation only after ≥10^4 cycles at keloid-relevant amplitudes; negligible activation under acute loads. Go if met. ([pubs.rsc.org](https://pubs.rsc.org/en/content/articlelanding/2025/qo/d4qo02060j?utm_source=openai))
- M2 (Month 12): In 3D cultures, activated condition shows ≥50% reduction in nuclear YAP/TAZ ratio and α‑SMA with preserved adipocyte metabolic readouts vs. controls. Go if met. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9367348/?utm_source=openai))
- M3 (Month 18): Human explants show selective in-tissue activation, reduced stiffness, maintained adipocyte markers for ≥4 weeks after single application, no activation in normal-skin explants. Advance to in vivo.

Risk management
- Conflicting AMT evidence: Focus on adipocytes within keloid/perilesional dermis; include lineage and single-cell analyses to verify target cell engagement. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7518402/?utm_source=openai))
- Insufficient mechanical dose in vivo: Empirically calibrate mechanophore sensitivity and microprojection placement depth using explant mapping.
- Off-target activation by external strain: Validate high fatigue-dependence; patch geometry to dampen incidental external loads.

Impact
A single-application, self-targeting material that reads the keloid’s mechanical history and then locally normalizes pericellular mechanics offers a pathway-specific yet drug-sparing route to preserve adipocyte function and halt AMT without perturbing normal skin. If successful, this establishes mechanical-memory gating as a generalizable design principle for fibrosis-selective topical therapeutics. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9124765/?utm_source=openai))

text:
Title
Ratiometric microenvironment–gated PPARγ prodrug to stabilize adipocyte identity and prevent adipocyte-to-myofibroblast transition in keloids by single-dose topical delivery

Premise and rationale (evidence check)
- In fibrotic skin, intradermal adipocytes can convert into myofibroblast-like cells under profibrotic conditions; this adipocyte–myofibroblast transition (AMT) coincides with suppression of PPARγ programs and gain of ACTA2/COL1A1 expression. Evidence from lineage-tracing and reviews in dermal fibrosis supports AMT as a contributor to the myofibroblast pool. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/nrrheum.2014.223?utm_source=openai))
- Keloids exhibit aberrant mechanotransduction (integrin–FAK/ROCK; YAP/TAZ nuclear localization) and stiffness/tension-dependent signaling that sustain fibrosis. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5505833/?utm_source=openai))
- Keloid fibroblasts are glycolytically reprogrammed with elevated lactate production and features of the Warburg effect; lactate and extracellular acidosis can activate latent TGF-β and drive myofibroblast differentiation and collagen synthesis. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29337061/?utm_source=openai))
- PPARγ agonists counter myofibroblast differentiation and dermal fibrosis; recent data show that topical rosiglitazone enhances adipogenesis and reduces fibrosis in irradiated skin, supporting a local, adipocyte-stabilizing mechanism. ([journals.physiology.org](https://journals.physiology.org/doi/10.1152/ajplung.00383.2004?utm_source=openai))
- Relative/ratio coding of signals, rather than absolute levels, can gate fate decisions in TGF-β/SMAD networks, suggesting that decoding the combination of acidity and lactate (both elevated in keloids) can increase selectivity. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5389321/?utm_source=openai))
- Novelty check: we find reports of PPARγ agonists inhibiting keloid fibroblast collagen in vitro and of topical PPARγ in skin injury, and lactate-responsive/bioresponsive materials exist; however, we find no report of a lactate- and pH-gated PPARγ prodrug designed for keloid-selective, single-dose topical therapy to stabilize adipocyte identity. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4937738/?utm_source=openai))

Unified hypothesis-question
Can a single-dose topical depot that unmask a PPARγ agonist only when both extracellular lactate and acidity exceed keloid-specific thresholds maintain adipocyte identity in the lesion and block adipocyte-to-myofibroblast transition, while sparing normal skin adipocytes?

Atomic strategy
Exploit the keloid-exclusive combination of high lactate and low pH as a ratiometric gate to locally unmask an otherwise inert PPARγ agonist, thereby restoring PPARγ activity precisely where AMT pressure is highest and leaving normal skin unaffected.

Specific aims
- Aim 1. Define the keloid-exclusive ratiometric window (lactate:pH) that precedes adipocyte dedifferentiation.
- Aim 2. Engineer and validate a dual-gated, lactate- and pH-activated PPARγ prodrug with strict off-state at normal skin conditions.
- Aim 3. Build a single-application, occlusive topical depot that provides sustained, self-limiting activation only within keloid tissue and evaluate efficacy and adipocyte preservation ex vivo and in vivo.

Approach

Aim 1. Define the actionable microenvironment thresholds
- Samples: freshly excised keloids and adjacent normal skin; if available, spontaneously regressing keloids.
- Measurements:
  - Microdialysis of interstitial lactate and pH mapping across keloid core–rim–perilesional skin; stiffness by shear-wave elastography on tissue blocks; oxygenation by phosphorescence lifetime imaging.
  - Early AMT gate readouts in adipocyte-lineage cells (adiponectin+ or PLIN1+): YAP/TAZ nuclear translocation, PPARγ target down-shift (FABP4, ADIPOQ), cytoskeletal remodeling prior to α-SMA induction.
- Analysis: determine the lactate and pH ranges (and their ratio) associated with early, reversible PPARγ suppression/YAP-TAZ activation in keloid vs. normal skin; set design targets for dual-gating chemistry. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5505833/?utm_source=openai))

Aim 2. Dual-gated PPARγ prodrug (chemistry and cell-level validation)
- Prodrug design:
  - Parent drug: rosiglitazone or pioglitazone analog with a phenolic or amine handle.
  - Trigger 1 (pH gate): acid-labile ketal/acylal linker tuned to cleave at pH ≤ 6.6; negligible cleavage at pH ≥ 7.2.
  - Trigger 2 (lactate gate): dynamic covalent phenylboronic ester tether that undergoes transesterification with α‑hydroxyacids; high-mM lactate in keloids displaces the drug or breaks a polymer–drug bridge, completing unmasking. Alternative path if needed: incorporate lactate oxidase microreactors in the depot to convert lactate to H2O2 and trigger a boronate carbamate cleavage; absent high lactate, H2O2 remains below threshold. ([patents.google.com](https://patents.google.com/patent/US20220211822A1/en?utm_source=openai))
- In vitro activation:
  - Prodrug stability and activation kinetics across a matrix of pH (7.4 to 6.2) and lactate (1 to 20 mM) to map an AND gate consistent with Aim 1 thresholds.
  - Off-target tests in neutral pH/low-lactate conditions using human abdominal skin explants.
- Functional assays:
  - Human adipocytes and adipose-derived stromal cells exposed to profibrotic cues (TGF-β1, cyclic stretch); measure maintenance of PPARγ targets, lipid droplet integrity, and suppression of α‑SMA/COL1A1 upon gated activation vs. free drug vs. vehicle.
  - Keloid fibroblast co-cultures to test paracrine normalization (reduced TGF-β activation, collagen I production). ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5009398/?utm_source=openai))

Aim 3. Single-application topical depot with sustained, self-limiting action
- Formulation:
  - Mucoadhesive/skin-adhesive hydrogel matrix (e.g., polyacrylate–chitosan interpenetrating network) loaded with the dual-gated prodrug microdomains; occlusive silicone backing for residence ≥4 weeks.
  - Release is diffusion-limited; activation is lesion-limited (requires lactate and acidity). As the niche normalizes (lactate/pH return toward physiologic), activation wanes, creating built-in negative feedback.
- Ex vivo efficacy:
  - Human keloid organotypic cultures and skin-on-chip with perfused gradients to recreate lesion lactate/pH; endpoints: adipocyte identity retention (PPARγ targets), reduced AMT, matrix softening (AFM), reduced YAP/TAZ nuclear localization in adipocyte-lineage cells, and collagen biochemistry.
- In vivo model:
  - Human keloid xenografts in immunodeficient mice; single application of the depot vs. vehicle vs. free drug gel. Outcomes at 1–8 weeks: depot integrity, localized drug activation (MALDI imaging), adipocyte preservation, fibrosis indices, and mechanical properties. Safety: systemic exposure low; normal skin adjacent to xenograft shows no activation.
- Comparator and context:
  - Topical free PPARγ agonist arm benchmarks feasibility but lacks selectivity; the dual-gated prodrug should match or exceed anti-fibrotic efficacy with minimal off-target effects. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13213667/?utm_source=openai))

Readouts, endpoints, and success criteria
- Biochemical: sustained PPARγ target expression in adipocyte-lineage cells within keloid tissue; reduction in α‑SMA/COL1A1 and TGF-β activation markers compared to controls. ([journals.physiology.org](https://journals.physiology.org/doi/10.1152/ajplung.00383.2004?utm_source=openai))
- Biophysical: reduction in pericellular stiffness and reversal of YAP/TAZ nuclear localization in adipocyte-lineage cells. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5505833/?utm_source=openai))
- Metabolic: reduced extracellular lactate and normalization of pH within the treated niche over time; concomitant decline in prodrug activation consistent with self-limiting behavior.
- Selectivity: no activation or adipocyte perturbation in adjacent normal skin; minimal systemic exposure.
- Single-dose durability: therapeutic effects persisting ≥4 weeks from one application.

Risk mitigation and alternatives
- If the lactate gate is insufficiently selective, strengthen the AND logic by tuning pKa of the boronate and cleavage pH of the acylal; as needed, integrate low-loading lactate oxidase confined within the depot to avoid tissue exposure. ([patents.google.com](https://patents.google.com/patent/US20220211822A1/en?utm_source=openai))
- If PPARγ agonism alone is suboptimal, screen second-generation ligands with stronger adipocyte-stabilizing, anti-fibrotic profiles but retain the same dual-trigger architecture to preserve selectivity. ([journals.physiology.org](https://journals.physiology.org/doi/10.1152/ajplung.00383.2004?utm_source=openai))

Impact
By translating a ratiometric, lesion-only activation logic into a dual-gated topical PPARγ prodrug, this work directly targets the earliest reversible stage of adipocyte fate loss in keloids. It aims to block AMT where and when it starts, while preserving normal adipocyte metabolic and regenerative functions and meeting the single-application constraint. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/nrrheum.2014.223?utm_source=openai))

text:
Title
Mechanics-AND-ROS–gated topical depot to lock dermal adipocyte identity and prevent keloid initiation

Unified hypothesis–goal
Keloid-prone wound edges simultaneously exhibit abnormal matrix stiffness/tension and oxidative metabolism that converge on YAP/TAZ–MRTF programs to suppress PPARγ-driven adipocyte identity and enable adipocyte-to-myofibroblast transition (AMT). A single topical depot that remains inert on normal skin but releases an adipocyte “identity-lock” only when both pathological mechanics and reactive oxygen species (ROS) are present will prevent AMT at the wound margin and reduce keloid initiation and growth while preserving normal adipocyte metabolic and regenerative functions. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9124765/?utm_source=openai))

Atomic strategy
Digitize the analog keloid niche using a dual-gated linker architecture embedded in a skin-adhesive hydrogel: mechanophore scission under pathological strain primes the depot (Gate A), and subsequent ROS cleavage completes cargo release (Gate B). No single cue can trigger release; normal skin never meets both thresholds, so adipocyte function is preserved.

Rationale
- Dermal adipocytes (dWAT) are plastic, participate in wound repair, and can dedifferentiate toward fibroblast/myofibroblast phenotypes under profibrotic cues. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11665542/?utm_source=openai))
- Keloids show elevated matrix stiffness/tension and LOX-mediated crosslinking; offloading tension mitigates progression. YAP/TAZ is activated in keloid fibroblasts and links mechanics to pro-fibrotic programs. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9124765/?utm_source=openai))
- Keloid fibroblasts undergo a Warburg-like shift with increased glucose uptake and lactate; oxidative stress markers and NOX4-driven ROS are elevated, supporting a redox-activated gate. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8229441/?utm_source=openai))
- Mechanophores (for example, spiropyrans) embedded in polymer networks undergo force-activated bond scission or switching; ROS-cleavable thioketals enable on-site, wound-compatible release. Combining them implements an AND logic in a topical format. ([pubs.rsc.org](https://pubs.rsc.org/en/content/articlehtml/2023/me/d3me00002h?utm_source=openai))
- We did not find prior reports of a mechanophore-AND-ROS–gated topical depot to stabilize adipocyte identity for keloid prophylaxis, indicating novelty. ([pubs.acs.org](https://pubs.acs.org/doi/10.1021/acsapm.0c00019?utm_source=openai))

Innovation
- Converts pathological stiffness from a risk to a trigger by mechanochemical scission within a hydrogel adhered over wound edges.
- Adds a biochemical confirmation (ROS) to prevent false positives from transient mechanical loads.
- Targets adipocyte fate directly (PPARγ-biased “identity lock”) rather than treating established keloids.

Device–material concept
- Patch: hyaluronic-acid–based adhesive hydrogel (skin-friendly) crosslinked with a low-threshold mechanophore crosslinker array (e.g., spiropyran diacrylate variants) distributed in a semi-interpenetrating network.
- Dual-gated linker: mechanophore scission unmasks pendant thioketal–caged carbonate linkers tethering a membrane-permeant, short-residence PPARγ agonist prodrug; ROS in the keloid niche cleaves the thioketal, releasing active cargo. ([pubs.rsc.org](https://pubs.rsc.org/en/content/articlehtml/2023/me/d3me00002h?utm_source=openai))
- Self-tapering kinetics: as matrix mechanics and ROS normalize during healthy resolution, further activation halts, enabling single-application durability without chronic exposure.

Proposed cargo (identity-lock)
- A locally acting PPARγ agonist prodrug (partial agonist bias) designed with a cleavable carbonate to minimize systemic exposure and avoid sustained receptor overactivation; the aim is to stabilize adipocyte chromatin and transcription at PPARG super-enhancer communities during the vulnerable window. Secondary backup arm: microdose ROCK-pathway modulator to dampen MRTF-A bursts during peak tension. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13121437/?utm_source=openai))

Specific aims

Aim 1. Map the “unlocking” window and thresholds in human keloid-prone tissue.
- Ex vivo elastography on patient keloids and adjacent normal skin to quantify local Young’s modulus and spatial heterogeneity; pair with redox reporters for ROS. Define mechanical and ROS percentiles distinguishing keloid from normal skin. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9124765/?utm_source=openai))
- In primary human dermal adipocytes cultured on tunable-stiffness matrices, quantify PPARγ activity, YAP/TAZ nuclearization, MRTF-A translocation, and AMT markers under stipulated ROS levels to establish a 2D trigger map (strain/ROS) that correlates with identity loss. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5505833/?utm_source=openai))
Milestone: Identify a stiffness–ROS region that robustly predicts PPARγ suppression and α-SMA induction.

Aim 2. Engineer and validate the Mechanics-AND-ROS gate.
- Synthesis: prepare HA hydrogels with mechanophore crosslinkers whose activation ranges overlap keloid-modulus–induced strain energy densities observed in Aim 1; install thioketal-caged carbonate linkers on the drug. ([pubs.rsc.org](https://pubs.rsc.org/en/content/articlehtml/2023/me/d3me00002h?utm_source=openai))
- Bench tests: rheometry-coupled fluorogenic mechanophore reporters to calibrate scission vs. macroscopic strain; ROS-titration to define thioketal cleavage kinetics; 2-signal assays to confirm no release with single triggers over physiological ranges of normal skin. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5285479/?utm_source=openai))
- Biological function: on stiff vs. soft substrates ± ROS, measure depot release, intracellular drug levels, PPARγ target activation, and blockade of AMT in human dermal adipocytes co-cultured with keloid fibroblast conditioned media. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7518402/?utm_source=openai))
Milestone: ≥10× selectivity index for release on “keloid” vs. “normal” conditions and ≥70% suppression of AMT markers without impairing lipid handling.

Aim 3. Single-application prophylaxis in vivo.
- Human keloid xenograft and rabbit ear hypertrophic scar models with standardized partial-thickness wounds at keloid-prone margins; apply one patch at wounding. Endpoints: dWAT adipocyte identity retention (PPARγ, Perilipin), reduced YAP/TAZ nuclear localization, decreased α-SMA+ area, collagen organization, stiffness reduction by shear-wave elastography, and blinded scar severity scoring at 4–8 weeks. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0301562920300120?utm_source=openai))
- Pharmacokinetics/toxicity: depot residual drug, local vs. systemic exposure, glucose–insulin homeostasis, and skin barrier integrity. Stop rule if systemic levels exceed microdose margins.

Trigger parameterization
- Mechanics gate: target activation at local effective moduli matching keloids (order 100 kPa) and below mechanophore scission competing with backbone failure; tune by mechanophore density and network architecture. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9124765/?utm_source=openai))
- ROS gate: tune thioketal half-life to cleavage at ROS levels documented in keloid fibroblasts while remaining inert at normal skin baselines. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36608994/?utm_source=openai))

Key controls
- Single-trigger controls (mechanics-only; ROS-only) to confirm AND logic.
- Non-mechanophore hydrogel and non-thioketal linker controls.
- Cargo-null depot to isolate material effects.

Risk mitigation and alternatives
- If lactate rather than ROS proves a better discriminator in a given cohort, replace Gate B with a lactate-oxidase microdomain that converts excess lactate to H2O2 to drive the same thioketal cleavage; stability and pH coupling are engineered per boronic/LOx precedents. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10911815/?utm_source=openai))
- If mechanophore thresholds are too high for cutaneous loads, integrate a thin, pre-strained elastic overlayer to amplify skin motions into higher local chain tension without increasing tissue stress; retain ROS gate for specificity. ([pubs.acs.org](https://pubs.acs.org/doi/10.1021/acsapm.0c00019?utm_source=openai))

Outcomes and interpretation
- Success: selective, motion- and redox-dependent microdosing that maintains adipocyte identity and reduces keloid indices after a single application, with no impairment of lipid handling or regenerative functions in normal skin.
- Failure modes: release on normal skin (over-sensitive gates) or insufficient activation in keloids (under-sensitive gates); iterate by adjusting mechanophore substitution and thioketal chemistry.

Why this will preserve normal adipocyte function
- Normal skin rarely exhibits the co-occurrence of keloid-range stiffness and elevated ROS; the depot remains dormant and does not perturb PPARγ programs or adipocyte metabolism. As mechanics and ROS normalize in healing tissue, further release self-terminates. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9124765/?utm_source=openai))

Evidence anchors
- dWAT plasticity and AMT in wound healing/fibrosis. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11665542/?utm_source=openai))
- YAP/TAZ mechanotransduction in keloids and fibrosis. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5505833/?utm_source=openai))
- Keloid glycolytic shift and elevated lactate/ROS. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29337061/?utm_source=openai))
- Keloid stiffness quantification. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9124765/?utm_source=openai))
- Mechanophore activation in polymer networks and ROS–thioketal release in wounds. ([pubs.rsc.org](https://pubs.rsc.org/en/content/articlehtml/2023/me/d3me00002h?utm_source=openai))

Timeline and milestones (18 months)
- Months 0–6: Threshold mapping (Aim 1), mechanophore–thioketal chemistry finalized (Aim 2 synthesis).
- Months 7–12: In vitro dual-gate validation, AMT blockade assays (Aim 2 biology).
- Months 13–18: Single-dose prophylaxis in vivo, stiffness/structure/function endpoints (Aim 3).

Deliverable
A first-in-class, logic-gated, single-application topical platform that turns the keloid microenvironment into the actuator for on-demand release of an adipocyte identity-lock, preventing AMT and keloid initiation while sparing normal skin.

Title
One-shot, tri-gated epigenetic locking of dermal adipocytes against myofibroblast transition in keloid microenvironments

Premise
- Keloid lesions exhibit a coincidence of three cues: high matrix stiffness/mechanical tension that drives YAP/TAZ activity; hypoxia that stabilizes HIF-1α; and chronic inflammation with NF-κB activation. Together these sustain profibrotic gene expression and ECM accumulation. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9124765/?utm_source=openai))
- Dermal white adipose tissue (dWAT) contributes to skin regeneration but, under these cues, adipocytes/adipocyte progenitors can dedifferentiate and yield myofibroblast-like cells, reducing dWAT’s regenerative/metabolic functions. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11665542/?utm_source=openai))

Hypothesis-question (inseparable)
Can a single, topical administration of a tri-conditionally activatable, locus-targeted DNA methyltransferase install durable, adipocyte-sparing repression at profibrotic response elements only within hypoxic, inflamed, high-tension niches of keloid tissue, thereby preventing adipocyte dedifferentiation without perturbing normal skin?

Atomic strategy
Translate the pathological coincidence (hypoxia + MMP-rich inflammation + high cytoskeletal tension) into a one-time burst of targeted CpG methylation at SMAD/TEAD-driven profibrotic enhancers in adipocytes, by gating nuclear entry, stability, and catalytic unmasking of a programmable DNA methyltransferase so that activity occurs only where all three cues co-occur. After the burst, heritable methylation maintains repression without continued drug exposure. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5389507/?utm_source=openai))

Specific aims
1) Map “dedifferentiation-competence” enhancers in keloid adipocytes.
- Isolate adipocyte-lineage cells from fresh human keloid vs. adjacent normal skin. Perform ATAC-seq/ChIP-seq (H3K27ac, SMAD2/3, TEAD1/4) to identify profibrotic response elements that open under triad cues; cross-validate with single-cell RNA-seq for ACTA2, CTGF induction signatures. Prioritize elements uniquely accessible in adipocytes within keloid tissue. Bench-validate cue-dependence using tunable stiffness substrates (0.5–50 kPa), hypoxia (1% O2), and TNFα/IL-1β. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9124765/?utm_source=openai))
2) Build a tri-gated ZF–DNMT3A(3L) epigenetic writer that activates only under the keloid triad.
- Construct a human zinc-finger array targeting the Aim 1 elements; fuse to a DNMT3A–DNMT3L single-chain effector to enhance on-target methylation density/spread. Add: a HIF‑1α oxygen-dependent degradation (ODD) domain for hypoxia-only stabilization; an MMP‑2/9/14–cleavable autoinhibitory peptide occluding the catalytic site for inflammation gating; and a mechanosensitive NLS mask based on a talin-rod–derived helical bundle that unfolds under cytoskeletal tension to expose a classical NLS, enabling import only on stiff substrates. Validate each gate separately and in combination using engineered cell systems. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC20916/?utm_source=openai))
3) Deliver once, topically, and test durability/selectivity.
- Formulate the protein in proteolipid nanoparticles embedded within dissolving hyaluronate microneedles to deposit cargo into upper dermis/dWAT. Evaluate in ex vivo human keloid slices and human keloid xenografts. Assess targeted methylation, repression of ACTA2/CTGF from adipocytes, preserved adipogenic programs (PPARG, CEBPA), and absence of effects in adjacent normoxic, low-tension skin. Track persistence ≥12 weeks post single dose. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2293299/?utm_source=openai))

Innovation
- A protein-level, triple-coincidence AND-gate integrates hypoxia (ODD), inflammatory remodeling (MMP-cleavable autoinhibition), and mechanical context (force-unmasked NLS) to confine editing to keloid microdomains—distinct from promoter-based logic or single-cue targeting. Nuclear import sensitivity to local mechanostructural context and force-unmasking of cryptic motifs are grounded in talin mechanotransduction and recent evidence that cargo mechanics near an NLS modulate import kinetics. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9339221/?utm_source=openai))
- Uses targeted DNMT3A–DNMT3L to write methylation at specific enhancers for durable repression after a transient pulse, avoiding chronic signaling inhibition. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5389507/?utm_source=openai))

Experimental design and methods
Aim 1 methods
- Tissue processing: collagenase digestion, buoyancy and flow sorting for PLIN1+/FABP4+ adipocytes and PDGFRα+ adipocyte progenitors.
- Multi-omic mapping under triad cues: ATAC-seq, H3K27ac, SMAD2/3 and TEAD1/4 ChIP-seq; differential motif analysis; enhancer–gene linking by co-accessibility.
- Selection of 3–5 conserved 18–20 bp ZF targets per enhancer; in silico genome-wide off-target scan.

Aim 2 methods
- Construct ZF–DNMT3A(3L) with: (i) HIF‑1α ODD (aa 401–603) for normoxia degradation; (ii) MMP‑cleavable autoinhibitory peptide masking DNMT3A active site; (iii) talin R3/R4–based helical bundle masking a monopartite NLS; linker design to set unfolding in the 5–10 pN regime typical of cells on stiff matrices. Gate validation:
  - Hypoxia gate: pulse-chase stability at 21% vs. 1% O2; pVHL dependence. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC1190339/?utm_source=openai))
  - MMP gate: cleavage kinetics with recombinant MMP-2/9/14; inhibition by GM6001; specificity panel. Keloid-conditioned media challenge. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/16086739/?utm_source=openai))
  - Mechanical gate: nuclear import assays on tunable gels ± actomyosin inhibitors; import abolished on soft (≤1 kPa) substrates; restored on stiff (≥20 kPa). Incorporate optogenetic NLS controls to benchmark import dynamics. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7614780/?utm_source=openai))
- Function: targeted methylation by bisulfite amplicon-seq; repression by qPCR/PRO-seq; enhancer accessibility by ATAC-seq; chromatin states by CUT&Tag.
- Specificity: off-target methylation by WGBS low-pass; RNA-seq; rescue with catalytically dead DNMT3A control. Note: prior reports show context-dependent stability of induced methylation; we therefore target enhancers with high methylation-retention propensity and DNMT3A–DNMT3L to improve durability. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9316731/?utm_source=openai))

Aim 3 methods
- Formulation: proteolipid nanoparticles optimized for protein cargo; embed in dissolving microneedles (300–700 μm) for intradermal/dWAT deposition. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2293299/?utm_source=openai))
- Models: (i) ex vivo human keloid slices with O2 gradients; (ii) human keloid xenografts on immunodeficient mice.
- Readouts (weeks 1–12): locus-specific methylation; adipocyte lineage tracing; adipocyte marker retention (PLIN1, PPARG), suppressed αSMA induction under TGF‑β challenge; preserved lipolysis/lipogenesis; lesion biomechanics and collagen content.

Selectivity and safety
- Tri-gating minimizes normoxic, low-MMP, low-tension skin exposure: ODD enforces rapid degradation in normoxia; absence of MMP cleavage blocks catalysis; soft matrices or relaxed cytoskeleton prevent nuclear import. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC20916/?utm_source=openai))
- Off-cell-type activity: ZF sites chosen within adipocyte-accessible enhancers reduce activity in fibroblasts where those elements are closed.
- Off-target editing: minimized by ZF design, DNMT3A variants with reduced nonspecific DNA affinity, and transient exposure; monitor with WGBS and RNA-seq. ([mdpi.com](https://www.mdpi.com/1422-0067/21/2/502?utm_source=openai))
- Immunogenicity: use humanized domains; topical/local exposure; assess anti-drug antibodies and local reactogenicity.

Topical single-dose product concept
- Device: single-use dissolving microneedle patch preloaded with proteolipid nanoparticles containing the tri-gated ZF–DNMT3A(3L) protein.
- Dosing: one 30–60 min application over the tension ridge of the keloid.

Milestones and go/no-go criteria
- Aim 1: Identify ≥3 adipocyte-accessible profibrotic enhancers opening under triad cues.
- Aim 2: Demonstrate >80% protein degradation at 21% O2 and >5-fold stabilization at 1% O2; >90% loss of activity without MMP cleavage; ≥5-fold increase in nuclear import on ≥20 kPa vs. ≤1 kPa substrates; ≥40% CpG methylation gain across targets; ≥70% repression of ACTA2/CTGF induction under triad.
- Aim 3: After single dose, maintain target methylation and adipocyte identity for ≥12 weeks; no significant transcriptomic perturbation in adjacent normal skin.

Anticipated outcomes and impact
- A lesion-autonomous, one-time epigenetic lock that prevents adipocyte-to-myofibroblast transition only where hypoxia, inflammation/MMPs, and high tension coincide—preserving dWAT metabolic/regenerative functions and avoiding chronic therapy. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11665542/?utm_source=openai))

Novelty and feasibility cross-check
- Tri-gated, protein-level AND logic combining ODD stabilization, MMP-cleavable autoinhibition, and a mechanically unmasked NLS for targeted DNA methylation has not been reported. Each gate is individually grounded in prior biology: ODD-based hypoxia targeting; MMP-cleavable control in protease-rich lesions; and mechanical control of nuclear import via proximity mechanics/cryptic site exposure. The combined, topical, single-dose application to lock adipocyte fate in keloids is, to our knowledge, unprecedented. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC20916/?utm_source=openai))

Success criteria
- Durable, locus-specific methylation at selected enhancers; blocked adipocyte dedifferentiation under triad cues; preserved adipocyte metabolic functions; no effect in normal skin; single-dose efficacy sustained for ≥3 months.

Title
Perilesional efferocytosis-gated topical nanovesicle adhesive to preserve dermal adipocyte identity and block keloid edge expansion

Hypothesis–question
Can a single-application, microenvironment-gated apoptotic-mimic nanovesicle adhesive applied to perilesional skin force a switch in local adipocyte-lineage cells toward a sustained, nonprofessional efferocytic program that captures and catabolizes keloid-derived extracellular vesicles and DAMPs, thereby maintaining adipocyte identity and halting adipocyte-to-myofibroblast transition and lateral keloid expansion? This asks if the pathological flux (ROS, acidity, lactate, EVs) leaking from keloids can be converted into the trigger and fuel for a protective adipocyte barrier zone. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8229441/?utm_source=openai))

Atomic strategy
Exploit perilesional pathology-gated exposure of phosphatidylserine (PS) ligands on apoptotic-membrane nanovesicles to engage TAM/PS/scavenger receptors on adipocyte-lineage cells and resident myeloid cells, initiating continual efferocytosis that depletes pro-fibrotic vesicles and debris and, through lipid catabolism, reinforces PPAR/LXR programs that preserve adipocyte identity. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4987730/?utm_source=openai))

Rationale and novelty
- Keloids exhibit a stiff, inflammatory, metabolically skewed microenvironment with elevated ROS and lactate; they release pro-fibrotic extracellular vesicles that amplify TGF-β signaling and matrix production. These gradients are strongest at the advancing edge. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9124765/?utm_source=openai))
- Dermal adipocytes/preadipocytes at the interface can undergo adipocyte-to-myofibroblast transition (AMT), contributing to fibrosis and loss of dWAT. Preventing this transition while preserving metabolic function is the correct control point. ([faseb.onlinelibrary.wiley.com](https://faseb.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1096/fj.202400653R?utm_source=openai))
- Preadipocytes and mesenchymal stromal cells possess nonprofessional phagocytic/efferocytic capability; PS-bearing liposomes or apoptotic-mimic membranes drive efferocytosis, whose lipid digestion activates LXR/PPAR programs that support continual uptake and pro-resolving metabolism. This suggests adipocyte-lineage cells can be biased into “cleanup sinks.” ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/9973318/?utm_source=openai))
- No reports were found of a topical, ROS/pH-unmasked apoptotic-membrane–coated nanovesicle adhesive to reprogram perilesional adipocyte-lineage cells against keloid propagation; current keloid nanomedicine focuses on siRNA/phototherapy or exosome therapies rather than perilesional efferocytosis gating. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S016836592500001X?utm_source=openai))

Therapeutic concept
Perilesional Efferocytosis-Gated Adhesive (PEGA): a peelable, bioadhesive hydrogel patch embedding PEG-masked apoptotic-membrane nanovesicles (AM-NVs). In acidic/ROS-rich perilesional skin, acetal/boronate linkers shed the PEG cloak to expose PS-rich apoptotic membranes, engaging TAM/PS/scavenger receptors on adipocyte-lineage cells and local macrophages. Captured keloid EVs/DAMPs are routed to lysosomes; liberated lipids/amino acids fuel OXPHOS and activate LXR/PPAR, reinforcing adipocyte identity and sustained efferocytosis. A one-time application maintains a local depletion zone while sparing normal skin where unmasking does not occur. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10180867/?utm_source=openai))

Specific aims
- Aim 1. Establish that perilesional human dermal adipocyte-lineage cells can be driven into a sustained efferocytic, adipocyte-preserving state by PS-exposed nanovesicles under keloid-like conditions.
  - Inputs: Primary human perilesional dWAT progenitors and mature adipocytes from keloid surgeries; keloid-conditioned media and purified keloid EVs; AM-NVs vs PEG-masked AM-NVs.
  - Readouts: Uptake of labeled EVs; lysosomal routing (TFEB nuclear translocation, LysoTracker, LIPA dependency); adipocyte identity markers (PPARγ, C/EBPα), myofibroblast markers (αSMA, COL1A1), YAP/TAZ activity, mitochondrial respiration; blockade with anti-PS, anti-CD36, and TAM inhibitors to map receptor usage. Success criterion: PS-exposed AM-NVs increase EV capture and maintain adipocyte identity while suppressing αSMA in keloid-like media. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34146092/?utm_source=openai))

- Aim 2. Engineer and validate PEGA’s pathological gating and one-application kinetics.
  - Formulation: HPMC/PVP bioadhesive hydrogel with embedded AM-NVs bearing pH/ROS-cleavable PEG (acetal and aryl-boronate linkers). Tuning of linker half-life to unmask at pH 6.2–6.6 and 50–500 µM H2O2 ranges measured in keloid edge; retain masking at pH 7.2–7.4. Sustained nanovesicle release over ≥4 weeks. Optional AND-gating: low-density anti–FN-EDA or periostin aptamers to enhance capture specificity in keloid ECM. Bench tests: unmasking kinetics, mechanical adhesion on ex vivo skin, depth-of-penetration, and drug reservoir stability. Success criterion: ≤10% unmasking at physiologic pH/ROS; ≥70% unmasking at perilesional conditions; continuous release matching 3–4 week wear-time. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7284449/?utm_source=openai))

- Aim 3. Demonstrate perilesional protection and keloid edge arrest ex vivo and in vivo.
  - Models: Human keloid skin explants retaining dWAT; xenografted human keloid with adjacent human dWAT in immunodeficient mice. One PEGA application circumferentially to perilesional skin; controls: blank hydrogel, masked AM-NVs, and standard-of-care steroid ointment.
  - Outcomes: (i) Edge expansion rate by optical planimetry; (ii) dWAT thickness and adipocyte lineage fate mapping (Adipoq-lineage if available); (iii) perilesional αSMA+ fraction, collagen deposition, and stiffness by elastography/AFM; (iv) interstitial EV burden and soluble mediators (TGF-β1, CCL2/CCL3) at the edge; (v) systemic exposure. Success criterion: significant reduction of keloid edge growth and preservation of dWAT with minimal impact on distant skin. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6987198/?utm_source=openai))

Experimental design and methods (concise)
- AM-NV fabrication: Generate apoptotic membranes from donor cells (irradiated RBCs or cultured cells), enrich for PS/PE, and coat ~120 nm biodegradable cores. Cloak with PEG via dual-cleavable acetal/boronate linkers; quantify PS exposure pre/post unmasking by Annexin V binding. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11304272/?utm_source=openai))
- Pathology gating: Calibrate unmasking against pH and H2O2 simulating keloid edges; validate on human keloid explants. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4622884/?utm_source=openai))
- Efferocytosis readouts: Track EV capture by adipocyte-lineage cells; dependence on TIM/BAI1/CD36/TAM mapped by blocking; test that lipid catabolism of cargo drives OXPHOS and LXR/PPAR activation that correlates with αSMA suppression. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13070255/?utm_source=openai))
- Perilesional selectivity: Apply PEGA to normal human skin explants; require no increase in adipogenic or myofibroblast markers and no cytokine skewing. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7284449/?utm_source=openai))

Key endpoints
- Primary: Maintenance of adipocyte identity (PPARγ/C/EBPα, perilipin) and repression of αSMA in perilesional cells exposed to keloid EVs. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7853423/?utm_source=openai))
- Secondary: Reduced interstitial EV/DAMP levels and TGF-β activity at the edge; preserved dWAT thickness; decreased local stiffness; arrested lateral keloid expansion after one application. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34146092/?utm_source=openai))
- Mechanism confirmation: Efferocytosis dependence (loss of effect with TAM blockade or PS masking) and metabolic coupling (loss with LIPA inhibition or LXR/PPAR antagonism). ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8137840/?utm_source=openai))

Selectivity and safety logic
- Spatial gate: Unmasking requires acidic/ROS-rich perilesional milieu; normal skin lacks these cues. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4622884/?utm_source=openai))
- Biological gate: High EV/DAMP burden at edges preferentially engages sinks; normal skin has low ligand flux. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10536244/?utm_source=openai))
- Functional gate: Effector program sustained only if cargo fuels OXPHOS/LXR/PPAR; without cargo, the program extinguishes. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12703062/?utm_source=openai))
- Safety assays: No amplification of TGF-β signaling; no impairment of keratinocyte/fibroblast homeostasis; low systemic absorption; sterility and pyrogen testing of AM-NVs. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7284449/?utm_source=openai))

Milestones and go/no-go
- M1 (Month 6): Demonstrate pathology-gated unmasking and sustained AM-NV release for ≥28 days in vitro and on ex vivo skin. Go if on/off ratio ≥7 at edge-like vs. normal conditions. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7284449/?utm_source=openai))
- M2 (Month 12): Show adipocyte identity preservation with ≥40% reduction in αSMA and ≥2× EV uptake in perilesional adipocyte-lineage cells vs controls under keloid EV exposure. Go if effects are abrogated by PS/TAM blockade. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8137840/?utm_source=openai))
- M3 (Month 18): In explant/xenograft, one PEGA application reduces edge expansion ≥30% and preserves dWAT with no adverse epidermal changes. Advance to IND-enabling formulation work. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6987198/?utm_source=openai))

Contingencies
- If adipocyte-lineage cells show insufficient TAM/PS-receptor–mediated uptake, bias toward scavenger receptor CD36 targeting on preadipocytes and enrich PS density to improve engagement; alternatively, allow resident macrophages to serve as primary efferocytes while monitoring adipocyte outcomes. Kill if even maximal PS exposure fails to alter perilesional EV burden or αSMA. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12150950/?utm_source=openai))

Why this proposal satisfies constraints
- Selectivity: Dual microenvironment gating (pH/ROS and high EV burden) confines activation to keloid edges. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4622884/?utm_source=openai))
- Preservation of adipocyte function: Efferocytosis-coupled LXR/PPAR signaling and OXPHOS support adipocyte identity and metabolism. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8137840/?utm_source=openai))
- Topical, single administration: Bioadhesive hydrogel depot with controlled release and removable patch architecture enables one-application durability. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7284449/?utm_source=openai))
- Novelty: No prior topical, apoptotic-mimic, pathology-unmasking nanovesicle adhesive has been reported for keloids or for reprogramming perilesional adipocyte-lineage cells into efferocytic sinks. Current keloid nanoplatforms target fibroblasts directly with photodynamic/siRNA approaches rather than building a perilesional capture barrier. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S016836592500001X?utm_source=openai))

System-level impact to test
If successful, the perilesional “sink-and-shield” converts the expanding keloid from a source-dominated system to a depleted-edge system: (i) less EV/DAMP/TGF-β signaling reaches adipocyte-lineage cells, (ii) adipocyte identity is maintained, (iii) stiffness accretion and edge mechanics stabilize, and (iv) pathological gradients collapse without perturbing normal skin. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34146092/?utm_source=openai))

Title
Density-gated αv-integrin blockade as a keloid-only “stop-healing” cue to prevent adipocyte-to–myofibroblast transition (AMT) using a single-application topical depot

Central hypothesis and question
Hypothesis: Pathologic receptor clustering on stiff, hypoxic, TGF-β–rich keloid ECM creates a unique integrin/TGF-β receptor topography that can be read as “abnormal density” by a low-affinity, multivalent ligand. When and only when such clustering is encountered, the ligand stabilizes on the cell surface, sterically blocks αv-integrin–mediated activation of latent TGF‑β and dampens focal-adhesion mechanotransduction, thereby relieving repression of adipogenic programs and selectively halting adipocyte dedifferentiation and myofibroblast-like transition in keloid tissue. Can a receptor-density reader be engineered into a topical, single-application depot that flips a durable “stop-healing” state in keloids without perturbing normal skin adipocytes? Evidence base: AMT occurs at wound edges and in fibrotic skin as adipocytes downregulate PPARγ, gain α‑SMA, and contribute ECM; this is sustained in fibrotic contexts with persistent TGF‑β/SMAD and mechanotransduction (FAK–YAP/TAZ) signaling. Keloids show increased focal adhesions, integrin activity, TGF‑β elevation, and stiffness-linked progression. αv‑integrins mechanically activate latent TGF‑β and cross-talk with TGF‑β receptors to reinforce fibrosis. Blocking TGF‑β outputs or mechanotransduction reduces myofibroblast features and collagen; restoration of adipogenic programs accompanies fibrosis resolution. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11665542/?utm_source=openai))

Atomic strategy
Exploit a keloid-only physical signature—abnormally high local density (clustering) of αv‑integrins at mature focal adhesions—to gate engagement of a multivalent, low‑affinity ligand (“Density Reader”). The ligand binds weakly to single receptors and therefore ignores normal skin; but avidity becomes high on abnormally clustered αv‑integrins in keloid ECM, yielding selective surface occupancy that blocks integrin‑mediated latent TGF‑β activation and attenuates FAK→YAP/TAZ signaling upstream of AMT. This is a single insight: convert receptor‑cluster density into the stop signal for healing. Inspiration: engineered circuits and multivalency can discriminate targets by antigen density; fibrosis presents receptor clustering rather than mere overexpression. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/8025675/?utm_source=openai))

Specific aims
Aim 1. Map the actionable density window of αv‑integrins in keloid vs. normal skin.
- Quantify αvβ3/β5/β6/β8 and β1‑family integrin cluster spacing/size and focal adhesion area in primary human keloid fibroblasts (KFs), keloid-adjacent fibroblasts, and normal dermal fibroblasts (NDFs) on native keloid vs. normal ECM using STED/TIRF super‑resolution microscopy; co‑stain FAKpY397, vinculin, and LTBP1–LAP complexes.
- Define the density threshold (receptors/µm2 and inter‑epitope spacing) that differentiates keloid from normal surfaces under static and cyclic strain. Expectation: KFs display larger, denser focal adhesions and heightened strain‑responsive clustering. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/16155910/?utm_source=openai))

Aim 2. Engineer and optimize a collagen-retaining, TG2‑anchorable αv‑integrin Density Reader.
- Scaffold: a flexible PEG-peptidic hub bearing 6–12 low‑affinity αv‑binding motifs (RGD/isoDGR and αvβ6/β8‑biased sequences), spaced to require ≥keloid‑like cluster densities for avid binding; include non‑RGD β1‑collagen‑receptor–sparing motifs to reduce off‑target β1 blockade.
- Function: on clustered αv‑integrins, the scaffold sterically occludes integrin traction on LAP/LTBP (impairing latent TGF‑β activation) and dampens FAK recruitment; on sparse integrins it dissociates.
- Depotization: append TG2 substrate tags (Q/K motifs) and decorin‑interactive elements to favor local crosslinking/retention in keloid ECM where TG2 and decorin‑DS complexes are enriched; include a weak collagen‑binding handle for initial residency. Target weeks‑long half‑life. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19729474/?utm_source=openai))

Aim 3. Formulate a single‑application topical patch that delivers the Density Reader into keloid dermis and verifies selective AMT blockade.
- Device: an occlusive, adhesive hydrogel patch with a dissolvable microneedle perimeter (≤600 µm) to bypass stratum corneum and deposit the scaffold into the upper/mid‑dermis of keloid; central hydrogel acts as a moisture‑retentive reservoir for 24–48 h, then removed. Single application per treatment cycle. Topical transdermal platforms and microneedles are established for dermal drug delivery and scar therapy. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10326306/?utm_source=openai))
- Selectivity testing ex vivo: Side‑by‑side punch biopsies (keloid core/periphery vs. matched normal skin) mounted in Franz cells; apply the patch. After 72 h: quantify scaffold retention (biotin‑handle), TG2‑mediated crosslinking, and diffusion profiles.

Aim 4. Demonstrate mechanistic shutdown of pro‑fibrotic signaling and rescue of adipocyte identity only in keloid conditions.
- Acute signaling: in KFs vs. NDFs on keloid vs. normal ECM ± cyclical strain, measure: (i) active TGF‑β (bioassay), (ii) SMAD2/3 nuclear localization and pSmad2/3, (iii) FAKpY397 and YAP/TAZ nuclear indices, (iv) CTGF and collagen I/III transcripts. Expect selective suppression in keloid‑context cultures. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10031116/?utm_source=openai))
- AMT endpoints: adipocyte lineage–traced human dWAT organoids or adipocyte‑enriched skin explants exposed to keloid‑conditioned microenvironment (stiff ECM + TGF‑β). Readouts: PPARG, CEBPA, PLIN1, adiponectin restoration; reduced ACTA2 (α‑SMA), COL1A1/3A1; EdU incorporation in dedifferentiated adipocytes; lipid droplet re‑accumulation. Expect rescue only with Density Reader under keloid conditions. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11665542/?utm_source=openai))
- Controls: (a) equimolar monovalent RGD peptide (tests necessity of density gating), (b) non‑binding scrambled multimer (tests specificity), (c) pan‑TGF‑β neutralizing antibody (mechanistic ceiling).

Design, constructs, and key parameters
- Ligand head groups: blend of αv‑favoring RGD/isoDGR and αvβ6/β8‑biased sequences; individual Kd 0.5–5 µM to prevent stable binding on sparse receptors. Multivalency 8–12 to set avidity threshold near measured keloid cluster densities. ([pubs.acs.org](https://pubs.acs.org/doi/abs/10.1021/acs.jmedchem.8b01123?utm_source=openai))
- Spacing: 5–20 nm inter‑ligand spacing arrays, tuned to the cluster inter‑receptor distances mapped in Aim 1.
- TG2‑anchoring module: Q‑donor/K‑acceptor repeats flanking collagen/decorin‑interactors to enhance in situ crosslinking and residence within decorin‑rich keloid ECM. ([journals.plos.org](https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pone.0172263&utm_source=openai))
- Formulation: hydrogel PSA patch (medical‑grade) with microneedles composed of GelMA/PEGDA or comparable materials dissolving within minutes to deposit 100–300 µg scaffold per cm2 of lesion. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37688542/?utm_source=openai))

Primary outcomes and decision criteria
- Density discrimination: ≥10‑fold higher surface dwell time and binding on keloid ECM/KFs vs. normal ECM/NDFs under identical ligand concentrations. (Pass if ratio ≥10.)
- Mechanistic effect: ≥50% reduction in active TGF‑β, SMAD target gene expression, FAKpY397, and YAP/TAZ nuclear index in keloid‑context cultures; ≤15% change in normal‑context cultures. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10031116/?utm_source=openai))
- AMT blockade/resolution: in keloid‑context adipocyte cultures, ≥2‑fold increase of PPARG/CEBPA/PLIN1 with ≥50% reduction in ACTA2/COL1A1; lipid re‑accumulation; no significant effect in normal adipocyte cultures. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11665542/?utm_source=openai))
- Single‑application durability: in ex vivo tissue and a pilot xenograft model, scaffold persistence ≥3–4 weeks within keloid ECM; sustained signaling suppression throughout residence window (monthly dosing cadence).

Selectivity and safety logic
- Pathology-only engagement: requires abnormal αv‑integrin clustering and high focal-adhesion density, common in keloids but not in healthy dermis. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/16155910/?utm_source=openai))
- Upstream, extracellular action: blocks αv‑integrin traction on latent TGF‑β without global immunosuppression; minimizes perturbation of normal adipocyte metabolism.
- Local retention: TG2/decorin‑facilitated anchoring and hydrogel occlusion constrain diffusion and systemic exposure. ([journals.plos.org](https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pone.0172263&utm_source=openai))

Validation and comparators
- Compare to: (i) topical FAK‑i hydrogel (positive control for mechanotransduction inhibition), (ii) PPARγ agonist (positive control for antifibrotic/adipogenic bias) delivered at equal molar surface concentrations. Expect Density Reader to match signaling suppression but with superior lesion selectivity due to density gating. ([doctrc.org](https://doctrc.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/03/Gurtner.pdf?utm_source=openai))

Potential risks and mitigations
- Risk: αv‑integrin redundancy and compensation via β1‑collagen receptors. Mitigation: titrate αv‑bias while sparing β1; combine with mild ERK/ROCK attenuation if needed in follow‑on work. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3857356/?utm_source=openai))
- Risk: inadequate dermal deposition via topical route. Mitigation: dissolvable microneedle perimeter proven for scar dermis; optional laser‑assist in resistant plaques. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37688542/?utm_source=openai))
- Risk: off‑target binding in normal high‑integrin tissues. Mitigation: low‑affinity monomers, multivalency thresholding; confirm no adhesion blockade in normal skin ex vivo.

Milestones and timeline (24 months)
- Months 0–6: Density mapping, scaffold library synthesis, in vitro density discrimination.
- Months 6–12: Mechanistic assays (TGF‑β activation, SMAD/FAK/YAP), AMT rescue in organoids/explants.
- Months 12–18: Patch engineering, ex vivo human tissue deposition/retention, durability.
- Months 18–24: Small‑animal xenograft with human keloid tissue; pharmacodynamics; safety.

Innovation
- First therapeutic to use receptor‑cluster density—not ligand abundance—to gate antifibrotic action in scars, adapting antigen‑density sensing concepts from engineered T cells to a topical extracellular ligand system. This reframes “stop‑healing” as a physical‑topology readout of the scar microenvironment. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/8025675/?utm_source=openai))

Expected impact
A single‑application, lesion‑selective topical that shuts down the abnormal healing loop by preventing αv‑integrin–dependent TGF‑β activation and mechanotransduction only where integrin clustering is pathologic. This preserves adipocyte metabolic and regenerative functions in normal skin while enabling redifferentiation within keloids. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19729474/?utm_source=openai))
