text:
Title: Embedded spectral beacons and wedge-aware reconstruction to democratize robust in situ cryo-ET from imperfect samples

Question–Hypothesis–Goal:
Can co-imaging deterministic periodic nanostructures with cells provide the missing ground truth needed to (i) estimate per-tilt, spatially varying transfer and anisotropy in messy lamellae and (ii) drive a compact, wedge-aware reconstruction that yields reproducible in situ structures on modest compute, even when preparations are imperfect? If so, then cryo-ET can be standardized without demanding expert-only sample perfection. This directly targets the missing wedge, low SNR, and spatial heterogeneity that currently limit in situ cryo-ET and its validation. ([cryoem101.org](https://cryoem101.org/chapter-4-et/?utm_source=openai))

Atomic strategy:
Embed a wafer-fabricated periodic “spectral beacon” next to the biological region so that each tilt series carries known Fourier components through the same thickness, charging, and curtaining fields as the specimen. Use these beacons to identify and factor out a smooth, per-tilt spatial sensitivity field, while reconstructing the biological volume in a Slepian (PSWF) basis matched to limited-angle support. This single perturbation—adding a deterministic periodic reference—converts unknown acquisition variability into estimable parameters and conditions the inversion to respect the information ceiling. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0304399113001587?utm_source=openai))

Specific aims:
1) Fabricate and validate cryo-ET calibration grids with integrated periodic nanogratings.
- Engineer lithographically patterned Si3N4 supports bearing arrays of Au nanodots/lines (1–50 lp/µm), positioned at the periphery of cell-adhesion micropatterns so that FIB-milled lamellae include both cell and beacon. Demonstrate survival of patterns through plunge-freezing, cryo-FIB, and tilt imaging. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2840046/?utm_source=openai))
- Show that beacon Bragg peaks remain sharp across tilts and thicknesses typical of lamellae, enabling per-tilt estimates of magnification anisotropy and modulation/contrast transfer along known spatial frequencies. Compare against existing lattice/pixel standards (graphene oxide, gold lattice) and streptavidin monolayer crystals used in SPA, which calibrate imaging but have not standardized cryo-ET transfer anisotropy under lamella conditions. ([journals.iucr.org](https://journals.iucr.org/paper?buy=yes&cnor=ft5128&utm_source=openai))

2) Estimation of per-tilt spatial sensitivity maps using a SENSE-style multiplicative field anchored by beacons.
- Model each projection Iθ(u) = Aθ{ sθ(x) · f(x) } + n, where f(x) is the unknown biological density, Aθ encodes geometry and CTF for tilted, thick specimens, and sθ(x) is a smooth field capturing thickness/charging/contamination. Estimate sθ(x) as a low-DoF B‑spline field whose amplitudes are fit by minimizing beacon residuals plus a smoothness prior; alternate with updates of f(x). This repurposes the MRI parallel-imaging notion of coil-sensitivity maps to cryo-ET’s spatially varying contrast. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0304399111000878?utm_source=openai))
- Integrate modern CTF tools that account for tilt, thickness, and astigmatism to improve identifiability and reduce variance, using the beacon to set an absolute scale per tilt. ([elifesciences.org](https://elifesciences.org/articles/97227?utm_source=openai))

3) Wedge-aware reconstruction in a compact Slepian basis with beacon-anchored calibration.
- Expand f(x) in a truncated 3D PSWF basis tailored to the specimen support and measured angular coverage; solve for coefficients by conjugate-gradient with beacon-informed preconditioning. PSWFs minimize spectral leakage outside the observed wedge, improving conditioning without inventing unsupported frequencies; 2D PSWFs already underpin steerable methods in SPA, but have not been exploited for cryo-ET limited-angle inversion. ([epubs.siam.org](https://epubs.siam.org/doi/abs/10.1137/16M1085334?utm_source=openai))
- Provide a compute-lean path: basis truncation aligns DoF with measurable information, lowering GPU and storage demands relative to voxel grids, and enabling small-lab adoption. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S104784771300316X?utm_source=openai))

Methods and work plan:
- Beacon design and grid production:
  - Wafer-scale photolithography on Si3N4 windows to pattern Au nanodot/line arrays spanning logarithmically spaced spatial frequencies; optional passivation islands to position cells over adjacent clear areas for lamella targeting. Validate mechanical and thermal robustness and compatibility with standard glow discharge and plunge-freeze. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8689146/?utm_source=openai))
- Biological preparation:
  - Seed mammalian cells on micropatterned grids; vitrify; prepare lamellae that intentionally vary in thickness and show induced curtaining to test robustness; acquire dose-symmetric tilt series with energy filtering. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6949126/?utm_source=openai))
- Algorithmic pipeline:
  - Beacon spectral extraction: detect Bragg peaks across tilts; fit per-tilt magnification anisotropy, astigmatism proxies, and vignetting to the known beacon spectrum.
  - Joint estimation: alternate between sθ(x) update (B‑spline field fit driven by beacon residuals and low-frequency content in projections) and PSWF coefficient updates for f(x), with Aθ including spatially varying defocus for tilted thick specimens. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0304399111000878?utm_source=openai))
  - Implementation: open-source CPU/GPU code with PSWF operators and NUFFT backends; provide precompiled grids and synthetic data for training/evaluation. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S104784771300316X?utm_source=openai))

Validation and metrics:
- Beacon-consistency curve (BCC): ratio of reconstructed to ground-truth beacon amplitudes vs. spatial frequency and tilt; serves as an external, tomography-native metric not relying on half-set independence (which is violated in tomograms). Compare BCC with conventional FSC-like surrogates and with deep-learning wedge-inpainting outputs. ([cryoem101.org](https://cryoem101.org/cryoet-chapter-5/?utm_source=openai))
- Biological fidelity:
  - Subtomogram averages of recurring motifs (e.g., ribosomes, microtubules) from messy-prep datasets; measure isotropy of resolution and axial elongation relative to baseline WBP/SIRT + IsoNet/DeepDeWedge. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-024-51438-y?utm_source=openai))
  - Cross-dataset reproducibility: same cell line and condition on different days/operators; assess variance in recovered structures and BCC reproducibility.
- Acquisition-efficiency sensitivity:
  - Systematically reduce tilt range and increase thickness to test whether beacon/SENSE+PSWF maintains usable reconstructions under harsher conditions while respecting the information ceiling. ([pubs.rsc.org](https://pubs.rsc.org/en/content/articlehtml/2011/sm/c0sm00441c?utm_source=openai))

Anticipated outcomes:
- Standardized, shareable calibration grids whose deterministic spectra allow per-tilt transfer/anisotropy estimation under real lamella physics—extending prior uses of crystalline/graphene/gold standards beyond pixel-size checks into tomography-native calibration. ([journals.iucr.org](https://journals.iucr.org/paper?buy=yes&cnor=ft5128&utm_source=openai))
- A compact, wedge-aware reconstruction with explicit, low-parameter modeling of spatially varying context, improving robustness on imperfect specimens without large-scale compute. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0304399111000878?utm_source=openai))
- A practical validation metric (BCC) that complements or replaces gold-standard FSC assumptions that break for tomograms. ([cryoem101.org](https://cryoem101.org/cryoet-chapter-5/?utm_source=openai))

Risks and mitigations:
- Beacon–biology interference: Micropattern cells to keep beacons peripheral; FIB to include partial beacon fields in lamella margins; verify that nearby Au features do not perturb cellular ultrastructure within the region of interest. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41592-019-0630-5?utm_source=openai))
- Weak beacon visibility at high tilt/large thickness: Increase beacon duty cycle and choose frequency bands robust to CTF zeros at given defocus; use energy filtering. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2784817/?utm_source=openai))
- Overfitting of sθ(x): Regularize with beacon-only loss at beacon locations plus smoothness priors; monitor leakage by testing on control grids lacking beacons.

Milestones and deliverables (18 months):
- M6: Release v1 beacon grids (design files, fabrication protocol) and a public EMPIAR-style dataset with paired messy vs. cleaner preparations on the same grids; baseline BCC and reconstruction code. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8689146/?utm_source=openai))
- M12: Joint sθ(x)+PSWF reconstruction with live acquisition reports (per-tilt transfer/anisotropy) and BCC; validation on cellular lamellae across variable thickness. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0304399111000878?utm_source=openai))
- M18: Community kit: grids, reference datasets, dockerized pipeline, and quantitative SOP for beacon-based calibration; manuscript comparing against WBP/SIRT+IsoNet/DeepDeWedge on identical tilt series. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-024-51438-y?utm_source=openai))

Why this advances the field:
- It reframes imperfect preparation as a calibrated signal pathway rather than a nuisance by introducing a deterministic, co-imaged prior that renders spatially varying artifacts estimable and correctable.
- It ties inversion complexity to information content via a wedge-aware Slepian basis, improving conditioning and reducing compute/storage, directly supporting democratization. ([epubs.siam.org](https://epubs.siam.org/doi/abs/10.1137/16M1085334?utm_source=openai))

Prior art and novelty check:
- Nanofabricated gold fiducial arrays exist for alignment in ET and crystalline supports (e.g., streptavidin) and graphene/gold lattices are used for pixel and image-quality calibration in SPA; however, their explicit co-use in cryo-ET as spectral beacons to estimate per-tilt transfer anisotropy under lamella conditions appears absent. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0304399113001587?utm_source=openai))
- Spatially varying CTF modeling for tilted, thick specimens is known but not coupled to an external spectral reference nor framed as a SENSE-like multiplicative sensitivity field to absorb prep heterogeneity. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0304399111000878?utm_source=openai))
- PSWFs are established in SPA steerable analyses but have not been developed into a 3D wedge-aware reconstruction basis for cryo-ET. This proposal does so, aligning basis functions with observable support. ([epubs.siam.org](https://epubs.siam.org/doi/abs/10.1137/16M1085334?utm_source=openai))

Success criterion:
- On intentionally imperfect lamellae, recover less-elongated, more isotropic subtomogram averages and improved beacon-consistency curves at equal dose/tilt range and with ≤1 high-end GPU, relative to state-of-practice reconstructions and deep learning wedge completion. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-024-51438-y?utm_source=openai))

Title: Reconstruction-free, angle-subset predictive likelihood for in situ cryo-ET validation and structure determination

Background and rationale
- In situ cryo-ET measures noisy, CTF-modulated 2D projections of a stationary 3D Coulomb potential at multiple tilts under a strict dose budget, distributing electrons across 40–60 images and lowering per-tilt SNR; the missing-wedge and anisotropic CTF complicate alignment and downstream validation. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0091679X19300548?utm_source=openai))
- Tomogram-first subtomogram averaging (STA) propagates alignment/model correlations that violate SPA half-set independence and forces reliance on FSC-like criteria ill-suited to anisotropic sampling; RELION-4.0 partially mitigates this by optimizing an approximate 2D-image likelihood via “pseudo-subtomograms,” but still leverages volumetric proxies. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8133831/?utm_source=openai))
- Projection-domain cross-validation exists (e.g., even/odd-tilt FSC and NLOO leave-one-out reprojections), yet it depends on a reconstructed tomogram, limiting its diagnostic specificity for per-tilt and per-particle failures. ([immunology.ox.ac.uk](https://www.immunology.ox.ac.uk/publications/104039))
- In medical CT/PET, projection-domain statistical reconstruction with ordered subsets (OSEM/ML-EM) and Radon-transform consistency conditions provide native validation signals without requiring fully converged 3D volumes; these tools are underused in cryo-ET. ([osti.gov](https://www.osti.gov/biblio/6610165?utm_source=openai))

Hypothesis and goal (undistinguished)
- Treating each tilt image as an independent observation of the same stationary 3D particle, we can enforce measurement-physics-consistent agreement across angle-stratified subsets and require accurate prediction of withheld tilts. If this criterion is met, the particle and its pose are reliably determined without constructing a tomogram; if it fails, the discrepancy localizes misalignment, CTF errors, deformation, or contamination at the raw-tilt level. The goal is a tomography-native, reconstruction-free validation-and-estimation workflow that lowers compute and standardizes quality control for broad adoption.

Atomic strategy
- Import PET-style ordered-subset maximum-likelihood (OSEM) to fit a per-particle, physics-grounded generative model directly to raw tilts, and quantify cross-subset coherence and held-out predictive likelihood as the primary validity signal; augment with local Radon moment-consistency tests as an orthogonal check on per-angle/per-particle projection groups. ([osti.gov](https://www.osti.gov/biblio/6610165?utm_source=openai))

Specific aims
1) Build a projection-only, particle-ROI likelihood with angle-subset EM updates (OSEM-ET).
2) Establish tomography-native validation metrics: subset-agreement, predictive log-likelihood for withheld tilts, and low-order Radon consistency residuals per particle and per angle.
3) Demonstrate reproducible in situ structure determination and robust failure diagnostics at reduced compute vs. tomogram-first STA and pseudo-subtomogram approaches. ([elifesciences.org](https://elifesciences.org/articles/83724?utm_source=openai))

Methods

A. Forward model and data
- Data: cryo-FIB lamella tilt series (dose-symmetric schemes), aligned globally by standard tools; emClarity-style raw-tilt access for ground-truth comparisons. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6281437/?utm_source=openai))
- Particle ROIs: detected by existing template matching or deep segmentation; extract fixed-size per-tilt windows.
- Physics: weak-phase linear imaging with per-tilt 2D CTF, envelope and dose-dependent attenuation, anisotropic noise power, defocus gradient with tilt; local background modeled as colored Gaussian. Assumptions match established cryo-ET practice. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8133831/?utm_source=openai))

B. OSEM-ET (projection-only EM with angle-stratified subsets)
- Latent variables: per-particle 3D pose; optional conformational class; nuisance parameters for per-tilt background and small in-plane warps.
- Parameterization: compact 3D particle representation constrained by a bandlimit matched to dose/CTF support; no volume reconstruction for the full tomogram, only per-particle latent map or low-rank basis sufficient to predict tilts under known geometry.
- EM updates:
  - E-step: per-tilt posterior responsibilities over pose/class using current latent map and physics; split the tilt stack into 3–5 disjoint angle subsets (e.g., interleaved or sectorized).
  - M-step: update latent map and pose hyperparameters by maximizing the expected complete-data log-likelihood for one subset at a time (ordered subsets). Unobserved directions remain unpenalized (missing data). ([osti.gov](https://www.osti.gov/biblio/6610165?utm_source=openai))
- Outputs per iteration: subset-specific parameter estimates, per-tilt predictive images, and residual fields.

C. Tomography-native validation metrics
- Subset agreement: convergence of pose and latent-map updates across disjoint angle subsets; large Kullback–Leibler divergence or parameter spread flags inconsistency.
- Predict-the-missing: hold out individual tilts or entire angle sectors; compute predictive log-likelihood of withheld images given fitted parameters from remaining subsets, corrected for CTF/noise. This generalizes NLOO without a tomogram. ([immunology.ox.ac.uk](https://www.immunology.ox.ac.uk/publications/104039))
- Residual physics compliance: whiten residuals by the per-tilt noise power and CTF; test spectral flatness and expected dose-dependent decay of high-frequency residual power.
- Local Radon consistency: build per-particle sinograms (line integrals within the ROI) and evaluate low-order Helgason–Ludwig moment conditions over observed angles; report polynomial-moment residuals and their angle dependence. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3097419/?utm_source=openai))

D. Comparative baselines and datasets
- Baselines: tomogram-first STA with gold-standard FSC; RELION-4.0 pseudo-subtomograms approximating direct 2D-likelihood; emClarity with tomoCPR. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8133831/?utm_source=openai))
- Public datasets with established ground truth and varying thickness/dose; synthetic phantoms for controlled missing-wedge and SNR sweeps. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0091679X19300548?utm_source=openai))

E. Experiments
- E1: Per-particle validation under controlled degradations. For each particle and condition, report subset-agreement spread, predictive log-likelihood of withheld tilts, Radon-moment residuals, and final STA resolution if the validated particles are passed to a conventional averager.
- E2: Failure-mode localization. Correlate validation metrics with known misalignment, defocus error, or charging; visualize angle-resolved residual maps to recommend tilt exclusions before any 3D reconstruction.
- E3: Reproducibility and democratization. Compare compute time, memory/storage, and operator interventions against STA and pseudo-subtomogram workflows on a single-GPU workstation; quantify resolution per unit GPU-hour and proportion of particles passing validation. ([elifesciences.org](https://elifesciences.org/articles/83724?utm_source=openai))

Success criteria
- Predictive generalization: median per-particle, per-tilt log-likelihood of withheld data within 5% of in-sample tilts across angle sectors.
- Cross-subset coherence: inter-subset pose variance below a threshold consistent with tilt-angle priors; significant outliers identify mispicks or deformation.
- Orthogonal agreement: particles passing OSEM-ET criteria also show near-zero low-order Radon moment residuals over observed angles.
- Downstream gains: when validated particle/tilt subsets are used in standard averaging, resolution and map anisotropy improve relative to using all tilts without validation, at lower compute and storage cost.

Risk and mitigation
- Risk: WPOA breakdown at large thickness/tilt. Mitigation: enforce stricter bandlimits and exclude high-tilt sectors when residuals indicate modeling failure. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8133831/?utm_source=openai))
- Risk: Overfitting latent maps in ultra-low SNR. Mitigation: early stopping via predictive likelihood, angle-subset regularization, and dose-aware priors.
- Risk: Radon-ROI boundary effects. Mitigation: tapered windows and low-order moment tests robust to partial-angle coverage. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3097419/?utm_source=openai))

Deliverables
- Open-source OSEM-ET implementation with containerized CLI; per-particle validation reports (subset-agreement, predictive likelihood, Radon residuals) and recommended tilt exclusions.
- Reference datasets and protocols to reproduce benchmarks against STA, pseudo-subtomograms, and emClarity-based pipelines. ([elifesciences.org](https://elifesciences.org/articles/83724?utm_source=openai))

Why this advances the field
- It reframes limited-angle, low-SNR acquisition from a liability to a validation resource by demanding cross-angle predictive agreement at the raw-tilt level, avoiding tomogram-first correlations and providing diagnostics before costly 3D steps. It aligns with modern trends toward using raw tilt images directly but eliminates dependence on volumetric proxies and FSC-style assumptions that do not hold in tomography. ([elifesciences.org](https://elifesciences.org/articles/83724?utm_source=openai))

Title: A priori reconstructability scoring for in situ cryo-ET via directional resolution kernels and leave-one-out reprojection metrics

Hypothesis/Question (indistinguishable): Can we predict, before or very early in data collection, whether a biologically localized molecular target embedded in a cellular lamella will yield a reproducible in situ structure by estimating its spatially varying, directional resolution from the planned tilt geometry, dose allocation, and expected biological support, and by verifying this prediction with projection-level leave-one-out reprojection residuals? If so, a lightweight “success calculator” could triage targets and guide acquisition for smaller labs. The need arises because cryo-ET data are limited by a missing wedge and low per-image SNR from dose fractionation, and tomogram-level correlations undermine SPA-style gold-standard FSC assumptions; directional anisotropy and spatially varying imaging parameters further complicate validation. ([frontiersin.org](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/molecular-biosciences/articles/10.3389/fmolb.2022.934465/full?utm_source=openai))

Atomic strategy: Reframe reconstructability as a property of the measurement operator conditioned on the target’s biological embedding. Compute local directional resolution kernels from a forward model G that encodes the tilt scheme, dose-weighted noise covariance, and CTF, restricted to biologically plausible supports (e.g., membranes/filaments). Validate the prediction by leave-one-out reprojection residuals at the projection level and by ptychography-inspired overlap-consistency within spatially overlapping tomographic patches to quantify redundancy where the biology naturally creates it. ([agupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com](https://agupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1029/2001JB000412?utm_source=openai))

Specific aims
- Aim 1. Build a tomography-native directional resolution estimator for biologically localized targets.
- Aim 2. Calibrate and validate predictions with projection-level leave-one-out reprojection and overlap-consistency residuals.
- Aim 3. Deploy and test a “success calculator” that prospectively triages targets and issues stop/go decisions early in acquisition.

Background and rationale
- Biological embedding governs reconstructability. In situ targets occupy membranes, filaments, or clusters with preferred orientations and variable copy numbers; these features create anisotropic signal and local redundancy or sparsity. Consequently, whether a target is reconstructable depends on the interplay between its embedding and the anisotropic sampling of a tilt series. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33020915/?utm_source=openai))
- Limitations of current validation. The missing wedge and per-tilt SNR loss impose directional resolution anisotropy; SPA-style half-map FSC is not directly applicable to single tomograms, motivating projection-level cross-validation and directional metrics such as 3DFSC. ([frontiersin.org](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/molecular-biosciences/articles/10.3389/fmolb.2022.934465/full?utm_source=openai))
- Transferable methodology. Seismic tomography quantifies spatially varying, anisotropic resolution via resolution matrices and jackknife tests under correlated measurements. We adapt these ideas to cryo-ET. ([agupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com](https://agupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1029/2001JB000412?utm_source=openai))
- Redundancy-inspired validation. In ptychography, overlap-consistency between adjacent probe positions provides robust, local error metrics despite missing Fourier regions. We borrow this logic for overlapping tomographic patches. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5247528/?utm_source=openai))

Research plan

Aim 1. Directional resolution kernels for biologically localized targets
- 1.1 Forward operator and noise model. Construct a linearized forward operator G that maps a local target density x to the tilt images y, including the per-tilt CTF, dose-weighting, and tilt-dependent noise covariance Cd. Restrict x to biologically plausible supports (surface/curve masks) inferred from low-resolution tomograms or prior biology. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2784817/?utm_source=openai))
- 1.2 Resolution matrix and directional ellipsoids. Estimate the local resolution matrix R = (GT C_d^{-1} G + λL)^{-1} GT C_d^{-1} G, with L a weak smoothness prior on the biological manifold. The principal axes of R define a directional resolution ellipsoid; its axis lengths yield predicted resolvable feature sizes along biologically relevant directions. Voxel- or patch-wise scores Sdir summarize recoverability. Use Lanczos-based approximations for localized regions to keep compute tractable. ([agupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com](https://agupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1029/2001JB000412?utm_source=openai))
- 1.3 Directional sampling and anisotropy benchmarking. Compare Sdir to 3DFSC-style directional metrics computed from early, low-dose reconstructions to ensure consistency of predicted vs observed anisotropy. This establishes face validity before more expensive acquisition. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8294179/?utm_source=openai))
- Outputs: software that ingests planned tilt scheme, lamella thickness, dose budget, and target localization to produce spatial maps of Sdir and directional resolution ellipsoids. Decision rules: green-light (Sdir above threshold for target size), yellow (collect with modified tilt/dose), red-light (do not collect).

Aim 2. Cross-validation and overlap-consistency to calibrate predictions
- 2.1 Projection-level leave-one-out cross-validation (NLOO). For each tilt j, reconstruct from all other tilts, reproject to tilt j, and compute frequency-weighted residuals that account for differing noise statistics and dose. Aggregate per-tilt residuals to obtain an angular dependence of reconstruction stability and a global cross-validated quality metric. Use this as ground truth for calibrating Sdir thresholds. ([immunology.ox.ac.uk](https://www.immunology.ox.ac.uk/publications/104039))
- 2.2 Overlap-consistency in tomograms. Partition the tomogram into overlapping patches aligned to biological supports (e.g., sliding windows on membranes). Reconstruct coarse patch models independently from complementary tilt subsets and compute overlap-consistency residuals between neighboring patches and between reprojected patch models and raw data, weighted by local directional completeness. This yields a redundancy map that should correlate with Sdir if the target is reconstructable. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5247528/?utm_source=openai))
- 2.3 Threshold derivation with digital phantoms. Generate synthetic tomograms with controlled tilt geometry, SNR, and biologically realistic supports and copy-number distributions to learn operating points relating Sdir and the cross-validated residuals to achievable resolution of known targets. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34003255/?utm_source=openai))
- Outputs: calibrated mapping from Sdir and residual metrics to predicted achievable resolution for different target sizes and embeddings.

Aim 3. Prospective deployment and assessment in real labs
- 3.1 Integration with acquisition. Connect the estimator to on-the-fly pipelines (e.g., Tomo Live-like workflows) so that after a small starter subset of tilts, the tool issues an early stop/go recommendation, updates Sdir with measured noise/CTF, and proposes tilt/dose adjustments. ([journals.iucr.org](https://journals.iucr.org/d/issues/2024/04/00/qv5004/?utm_source=openai))
- 3.2 Benchmark datasets. Assemble a panel of cellular targets spanning membrane proteins, filament-bound complexes, and cytosolic assemblies with varied copy numbers. For each, plan acquisition via the success calculator, record predictions, and compare against downstream outcomes (subtomogram averaging resolution, directional anisotropy, and reproducibility across tilt subsets). Use directional metrics for consistency checks. ([portlandpress.com](https://portlandpress.com/biochemj/article/478/10/1827/228677/Current-data-processing-strategies-for-cryo?utm_source=openai))
- 3.3 Comparative baselines. Compare against standard gold-standard FSC-based triage in STA pipelines and against directional 3DFSC alone to demonstrate added predictive value from operator-based Sdir and NLOO residuals. Emphasize cases where half-map independence is questionable due to shared tomogram information. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7116126/?utm_source=openai))
- Outputs: a validated, resource-light triage tool and public datasets linking planned geometry, biological embedding, predicted Sdir, and achieved results.

Methods and implementation details
- Biological support estimation: from a binned tomogram, segment membranes/filaments with conventional tools; build surface/curve masks as supports for x. This constrains G and L to the biologically plausible manifold, reducing parameter count and compute.
- Operator construction: precompute per-tilt CTF, dose-weighted noise spectra, and sampling functions; use block-sparse representations to enable localized Lanczos estimates of R on GPUs with modest memory.
- Validation metrics: NLOO residual spectra per tilt; patchwise overlap-consistency residuals; directional 3DFSC of early reconstructions; final STA resolutions when applicable. ([immunology.ox.ac.uk](https://www.immunology.ox.ac.uk/publications/104039))
- Statistical calibration: regress achieved resolution and reproducibility on Sdir and residual metrics across phantoms and real datasets to set decision thresholds.

Milestones and success criteria
- M1 (Months 1–6): Implement localized R and Sdir; reproduce known anisotropy trends on public data; agreement with 3DFSC directional anisotropy on early maps. Success criterion: Sdir rank-orders regions by eventual directional resolution measured by 3DFSC. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8294179/?utm_source=openai))
- M2 (Months 7–12): NLOO reprojection module and overlap-consistency residuals calibrated on phantoms; operating thresholds established. Success criterion: receiver-operating characteristic AUC > 0.85 for predicting whether a target reaches a pre-specified resolution bin under a given tilt scheme. ([immunology.ox.ac.uk](https://www.immunology.ox.ac.uk/publications/104039))
- M3 (Months 13–24): Prospective tests in two labs; demonstrate at least 30% reduction in low-yield acquisitions without loss of successful targets. Success criterion: prospective concordance between success calculator decisions and final outcomes across target classes.

Risk assessment and mitigations
- Risk: Overconfidence from model mismatch (e.g., unknown heterogeneity). Mitigation: keep Sdir conservative via priors only on geometry/support, not detailed structure; use NLOO residuals as an empirical check.
- Risk: Computational cost. Mitigation: localized Lanczos approximations and sparse operators; restrict evaluation to user-specified ROIs; use early-tilt updates to avoid full reconstructions. ([academic.oup.com](https://academic.oup.com/gji/article/138/2/293/595935?utm_source=openai))
- Risk: Novelty overlap with prior projection cross-validation. Mitigation: differentiate by providing spatially varying, directional resolution kernels that incorporate the planned acquisition and biological support; use NLOO only as calibration and real-time check. ([immunology.ox.ac.uk](https://www.immunology.ox.ac.uk/publications/104039))

Deliverables
- Open-source “success calculator” producing spatial maps of directional resolution ellipsoids and reconstructability scores from planned acquisition parameters and target localization; optional online mode for early-tilt stop/go.
- Public benchmark phantoms and real datasets with ground-truth outcomes; standardized reporting of Sdir, NLOO residuals, overlap-consistency, and 3DFSC directional anisotropy.

Why this will democratize in situ cryo-ET
- The tool converts microscope settings and basic biological context into actionable, localized, directional estimates of what is actually resolvable and how much redundancy is present, replacing ad hoc trial-and-error. It respects the missing wedge, low per-tilt SNR, and correlated data, and avoids reliance on SPA-style independence assumptions that are not met in tomography, substituting projection-level cross-validation and directional metrics designed for the modality. ([frontiersin.org](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/molecular-biosciences/articles/10.3389/fmolb.2022.934465/full?utm_source=openai))

Proposal title
Geometry-locked, autoinhibited proximity modifiers to selectively dismantle centriole rosettes and normalize centrosome number in aneuploid-prone cells.

Hypothesis and goal
A de novo, ring-patterned protein that only stabilizes when it simultaneously matches the ninefold cartwheel geometry of two adjacent nascent centrioles around a single mother (“centriole rosette”) will unmask a proximity-modifying effector to locally deplete rosette components and abort supernumerary procentriole maturation, thereby restoring bipolar spindle formation without perturbing normal centriole duplication. This pivots the general goal—intracellular therapeutic function beyond binding—toward organelle rescue via geometry-encoded selectivity. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11113234/?utm_source=openai))

Atomic strategy
Encode symmetry-and-spacing matching as the primary recognition code: weak, distributed contacts arranged in a de novo ninefold ring that can avidly engage only when two SAS-6–templated cartwheels are present at the correct radial offset on a mother centriole. Correct geometric registration unlocks an autoinhibited “latch,” exposing an effector that recruits endogenous ubiquitin-proteasome machinery to the rosette microdomain; everywhere else, the construct remains inert. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3131366/?utm_source=openai))

Rationale
- Centriole cartwheels provide an intrinsic ninefold architectural code set by SAS-6 rings; this code is universal across centrioles and underlies procentriole initiation. In centriole amplification, overexpression or dysregulation of PLK4/STIL/SAS-6 yields “rosette” arrangements—multiple SAS-6–positive procentrioles encircling one mother—producing repeated, closely spaced cartwheel geometries not present during normal one-daughter duplication. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3089914/?utm_source=openai))
- Multivalency with rigid spatial patterning can produce superselective binding that turns on sharply only above a density/spacing threshold; this “pattern code” discriminates assemblies by geometry rather than single-site affinity. Applying this principle intracellularly provides a tunable filter that ordinary binders or small molecules lack. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3131366/?utm_source=openai))
- The centrosome is a native hub for ubiquitin-proteasome activity, so proximity recruitment at rosettes can drive local proteostasis decisions with minimal redistribution. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27294844/?utm_source=openai))
- Autoinhibited de novo switches (LOCKR family) demonstrate that compact protein cages can mask functions until a specific interaction displaces a “latch,” establishing feasibility for geometry-gated activation. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-019-1432-8?utm_source=openai))

Design concept
- Geometry filter: a compact, de novo helical repeat scaffold presenting nine weak “stickers” (e.g., generic coiled-coil or short helical motifs) on a rigid ring with SAS-6–matched angular spacing; a second, offset ring on the opposite face provides a defined ring-to-ring distance matching the average separation of two adjacent rosette cartwheels on a mother centriole. Individually, each sticker is low affinity; avidity and residence time emerge only when both rings simultaneously engage two neighboring cartwheels—an event unique to rosettes. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0959440X20301421?utm_source=openai))
- Autoinhibitory latch: an intramolecular decoy masks the effector-docking groove. Only when dual-ring engagement satisfies the geometric constraints does the multivalent energy gain outcompete the decoy and flip the latch, exposing the effector site (contextual ON switch). ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-019-1432-8?utm_source=openai))
- Effector logic: the unmasked site recruits an endogenous E3-adaptor or proteasome-proximal factor to locally ubiquitylate or destabilize SAS-6/PLK4/STIL complexes at the rosette, collapsing extra procentrioles while leaving single nascent daughters below the activation threshold untouched. Because the centrosome concentrates UPS components, modest recruitment is expected to be sufficient and spatially confined. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27294844/?utm_source=openai))

Specific aims
1) Define geometric tolerance windows
- Quantify how ring radius, inter-sticker angle, and inter-ring spacing set the superselective activation threshold for dual-cartwheel engagement, and identify parameter ranges that exclude single-daughter states but include rosettes found in amplification. Readouts: geometry-dependent binding/activation curves and sharpness (Hill-like) of the ON transition. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3131366/?utm_source=openai))
2) Demonstrate rosette-selective action in living cells
- In cell models of centriole amplification (e.g., PLK4 dysregulation), test whether constructs activate only at rosette-bearing centrosomes, reduce extra procentrioles, and normalize spindle bipolarity, while sparing cells with normal duplication. Readouts: rosette incidence, centriole counts, spindle geometry, chromosome segregation fidelity. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4113104/?utm_source=openai))
3) Establish mechanism and confinement
- Show that activation requires geometry-locked dual engagement and latch displacement; confirm that proximal UPS recruitment and local turnover occur at the rosette without global proteostasis perturbation. Readouts: dependence on latch strength, loss of function with geometry mismatch, local ubiquitylation markers at centrosomes. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27294844/?utm_source=openai))
4) Functional impact in disease-relevant contexts
- In cancer cell lines with endogenous centrosome amplification, evaluate whether selective rosette dismantling decreases mitotic errors and aneuploidy proxies, with acceptable viability and minimal off-target phenotypes. Outcome benchmarks: reduced multipolarity and micronuclei without interfering with normal centriole cycles. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/nrc3995?utm_source=openai))

Success criteria and falsification
- Success: a geometry-locked, autoinhibited construct exhibits a superselective activation curve that turns on only in rosette-bearing cells and restores bipolar spindles while maintaining normal duplication in controls.
- Falsifiers: activation in single-daughter states; diffuse cytosolic activation; requirement for high-affinity monovalent contacts (loss of geometry dependence). Superselectivity failure would refute the atomic strategy. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3131366/?utm_source=openai))

Risk management and safety
- Off-target centriole loss is mitigated by AND-gating: dual-ring coincidence plus latch displacement. Weak stickers prevent activation at isolated cartwheels; autoinhibition prevents baseline activity. If needed, tune latch strength to require sustained residence time, filtering transient encounters. Avoids global condensate disruption or immune activation. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-019-1432-8?utm_source=openai))

Novelty and differentiation
- Moves beyond target binding to an intracellular organelle-rescue modality that exploits architectural codes to gate catalytic action. Prior multivalency/superselectivity has been applied mainly to extracellular or model surfaces; here it is repurposed as an intracellular therapeutic filter keyed to centriole rosette geometry. Combining symmetry-matched avidity with an autoinhibited switch for proximity editing at a native UPS hub is, to our knowledge, unreported. ([pubs.acs.org](https://pubs.acs.org/doi/10.1021/jacs.2c08529?utm_source=openai))

Impact
- Provides a route to correct centrosome amplification—a driver of chromosomal instability—without systemic mitotic poisons or broad kinase inhibition. If successful, the “geometry-locked activation” paradigm generalizes to other lattice- or ring-based machines (e.g., inflammasome ASC filaments, clathrin lattices), establishing a class of de novo intracellular therapeutics that act by reading and editing mesoscale architecture. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2211124717310768?utm_source=openai))

Title
Composite-interface misfold sensors that convert aggregate density into localized, ubiquitin-independent aggrephagy

Hypothesis/Question
Can a de novo protein that senses high local density of exposed hydrophobic/β-edge features on misfolded clients assemble a composite effector interface only on such surfaces, thereby recruiting LC3 and triggering spatially confined aggrephagy while sparing healthy proteomes? If so, does this ubiquitin-independent, density-gated mechanism outperform native p62/NBR1 pathways and small-molecule LC3 tethers (ATTEC) in selectivity and self-limiting behavior? ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4192669/?utm_source=openai))

Atomic strategy
Exploit multivalency: make the output (LC3 recruitment) contingent on a composite binding site that exists only when multiple weak-affinity misfold sensors co-dock on the same misfolded surface. This AND-gate is inaccessible to monomeric interactions and collapses when misfold density falls, implementing auto-shutoff. Colocalization-dependent activation is established with de novo switches (Co-LOCKR) and clustering-activated degraders; here it is repurposed to read out misfold density and couple it to aggrephagy. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7976376/?utm_source=openai))

Specific Aim 1. Build a de novo misfold-density sensor with weak monovalent affinity and avidity-driven surface engagement
- Design: A helical repeat scaffold with a shallow hydrophobic groove tuned for KD 50–200 μM to generic exposed hydrophobic/β-edge motifs enriched on misfolded clients. Low affinity reduces off-target binding to natively folded proteins; avidity upon clustering drives surface engagement. Recognition of exposed hydrophobics is the core proteostasis signal inside cells. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4192669/?utm_source=openai))
- Assays: (i) Peptide microarrays and model substrates (heat-denatured luciferase, partially unfolded TDP‑43 LCD) to quantify KD and avidity. (ii) Live-cell recruitment to stress-induced foci (MG132 or heat shock). (iii) In vitro condensate assays to confirm preferential partitioning into aberrant, hydrophobic-enriched condensates. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41580-020-00326-6?utm_source=openai))
- Success criteria: Monomer KD ≥50 μM; avidity apparent KD ≤1 μM on multivalent surfaces; negligible binding to properly folded controls.

Specific Aim 2. Encode a composite LC3-recruitment interface that forms only upon sensor co-docking
- Design principle: Each sensor monomer presents one face of a cryptic effector-binding groove; when N≥3 monomers are co-docked on the same client surface, their faces tessellate into a high-affinity site for a minimal LC3-binder (either an engineered multivalent LIR arranged in cis across the assembly or a single short adaptor that binds the composite groove and carries a LIR). This converts misfold density into LC3 engagement without needing ubiquitin tagging. p62 achieves aggrephagy via oligomerization and multivalent LC3/ubiquitin contacts; here we generalize the logic to misfold features directly. ([journals.biologists.com](https://journals.biologists.com/jcs/article/136/10/jcs260888/310878/Aggrephagy-at-a-glance?utm_source=openai))
- Minimality: Prefer a single-chain sensor whose LIR is autoinhibited by intramolecular packing and becomes avid only in the assembled state (concentration-dependent relief), avoiding extra components. Colocalization-gated exposure of functional peptides is proven in de novo switches. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-019-1432-8?utm_source=openai))
- Assays: (i) LC3 pulldown vs. monomeric sensor; (ii) FRAP of aggresomes to show LC3 recruitment and autophagosome engagement; (iii) Autophagic flux dependence via ATG5/7 knockout. 
- Benchmarks: Compare to ATTEC (LC3–mHTT tethers) and to p62 overexpression. Expect higher selectivity (activity only at misfold-dense loci) and less global autophagy induction. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-019-1722-1?utm_source=openai))

Specific Aim 3. Demonstrate selective clearance and safety in disease-relevant models
- Models: mHTT (polyQ-expanded), tau P301S, and TDP‑43 stress granule models where pathological condensates/aggregates form. Aggregates represent high-density misfold landscapes suitable for AND-gating; aggregate-selective degradation by clustering has precedent. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41580-020-00326-6?utm_source=openai))
- Readouts: Target load (Western, filter trap), aggregate metrics (number, size, solidity), viability, proteome perturbation (TMT proteomics), stress responses (HSF1/ISR markers), and translation near foci (SunTag reporters).
- Safety gates: Titrate monomer affinity and the N required for composite assembly to avoid action on sparse misfold exposure; survey off-target condensates (stress granules, P‑bodies) for perturbation. 

Design/implementation details
- Sensor–client interaction: Computationally place small hydrophobic pockets along a curved helical repeat so binding requires a patch size unlikely on native surfaces but common on misfolded clients. Introduce charge patterning to disfavour native interfaces. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8243209/?utm_source=openai))
- Composite interface geometry: Use Rosetta to enforce that three sensor copies must adopt a defined relative orientation (as when co-tethered on a curved aggregate surface) to assemble a contiguous effector groove. Penalize spontaneous oligomerization in solution to enforce density gating. Colocalization-gated activation of buried peptides is a solved design problem in LOCKR-like systems, supporting feasibility. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-019-1432-8?utm_source=openai))
- Effector choice: Start with LIR-based LC3 recruitment to drive aggrephagy, as LC3 tethers can clear disease proteins without elevating basal autophagy. As a secondary modality, test a clustering-activated RING-only degrader to probe UPS routing at aggregates. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-019-1722-1?utm_source=openai))
- Controls: (i) Monomer-only LIR exposure mutant (safety failure control) to quantify background effects. (ii) Sensor lacking composite faces. (iii) p62ΔUBA (ubiquitin-blind) to benchmark ubiquitin-independent aggrephagy. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3320095/?utm_source=openai))

Milestones and go/no-go
- M1 (Months 0–6): Achieve avidity-driven binding (apparent KD ≤1 μM) and no detectable LC3 recruitment by monomeric sensor. Go if monomeric background LC3 binding <5% of composite-activated binding.
- M2 (Months 6–12): Composite-interface–dependent LC3 recruitment in cells with ≥10-fold on/off ratio; aggregate area reduced ≥40% without increased global LC3‑II. Go if reduction is LC3- and ATG5-dependent and proteome changes are limited (<2% proteins altered ≥2-fold).
- M3 (Months 12–24): Disease models show selective clearance and rescued viability with minimal ISR/HSR activation; performance surpasses ATTEC and p62 overexpression for selectivity. Kill if off-target condensate disruption or growth defects persist after affinity/threshold retuning. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-019-1722-1?utm_source=openai))

Why this fills the modality gap
- Not mere binding: Produces defined intracellular outcomes—localized aggrephagy—by constructing the effector interface only where misfold density is high.
- Distinct from receptor agonism/antagonism: Fully intracellular, proteostasis-wiring modality.
- Leverages protein-scale advantages: Multivalency, composite-surface formation, and colocalization-gated conformational exposure are not accessible to small molecules or antibodies. Current degraders and receptors lack a density-AND gate tied to misfold features; ATTEC and p62 depend on specific bivalent chemistries or ubiquitin concentration, respectively, whereas this design reads the fundamental misfold signal. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-019-1722-1?utm_source=openai))

Risk, mitigations, and alternatives
- Risk: Off-target action at legitimate condensates. Mitigation: Tune monomer KD; require N≥3 assembly; enforce geometry that matches aggregate curvature; restrict expression. 
- Alternative: If LC3 routing is insufficient, swap output to a clustering-activated RING E3 microdomain to test UPS clearance specifically at aggregates; aggregate-activated RING degraders have shown selectivity for pathological assemblies. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39208111/?utm_source=openai))

Outcome
A first-in-class, self-regulating intracellular therapeutic that turns pathological misfold density into a composite interface for LC3 recruitment, enabling autonomous on/off control of aggrephagy with minimal collateral proteostasis disruption. If validated, the platform generalizes to other effectors (e.g., local translation dampening) by swapping the composite-recruited module while retaining the same density-sensing core. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7976376/?utm_source=openai))

text:
Title
A curvature-gated, PTM-coded protein switch that locally routes damaged organelles to either selective autophagy or ER-driven membrane replenishment

Hypothesis and research goal
A single de novo intracellular protein that integrates (i) local membrane curvature at damaged organelles and (ii) global cell-state post-translational modification (PTM) patterns can deterministically toggle between two mutually exclusive functions: assembling the WIPI2–ATG16L1 LC3-lipidation machinery for selective autophagic clearance when damage is local, versus scaffolding ER–organelle contact and lipid transfer (VAP–VPS13/ATG2) to rebuild/repair when global stress indicates insufficient capacity. This controller prevents net loss of organelle mass that arises when clearance proceeds without commensurate biogenesis. The research goal is to design, build, and validate such a switchable protein and show that it restores organelle homeostasis better than constitutive autophagy activation.

Atomic strategy
Exploit a BAR-domain dimer as a curvature-gated localizer at damaged membranes and couple it to a phosphorylation/redox “PTM code” that flips a coiled-coil exposure mask. One mask exposes multivalent WIPI2/ATG16L1-recruiting SLiMs to drive LC3 lipidation and selective autophagy; the alternate mask exposes high-avidity ER-contact modules (FFAT arrays) that recruit VAP and, by extension, VPS13/ATG2 lipid-transfer tethers to expand or repair the damaged membrane. BAR provides lesion topology specificity; the PTM code sets the global bias. Autophagy initiation via WIPI2–ATG16L1 and ER–isolation-membrane lipid transfer via VAP–VPS13/ATG2 are well-established entry points for pathway execution. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3718966/?utm_source=openai))

Construct: BARCODE (BAR-Conformation-Decoding Effector)
- Localizer: Minimal N-BAR scaffold (derived from SNX18/Endophilin-B family) with endogenous interaction sites attenuated but curvature affinity retained (H0/H1 amphipathic insert preserved). Purpose: nucleate on high-curvature ruptures/tubules of damaged mitochondria, lysosomes, or ER subdomains. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3718966/?utm_source=openai))
- PTM-code switch: A phosphorylation-switchable hetero–coiled-coil (validated de novo designs) fused to a redox-sensitive disulfide clamp (roGFP-derived cysteine geometry) drives cooperative exposure/burial of two effector cassettes:
  - Code “D” (degradation-permissive): low AMPK, reduced redox → cassette A exposed.
  - Code “R” (rebuild-permissive): high AMPK-like phosphorylation pattern and mild oxidation → cassette B exposed. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-021-21622-5?utm_source=openai))
- Effector cassette A (clearance): Multivalent WIPI2- and ULK1/FIP200-binding SLiMs optimized for avidity plus ATG16L1-recruiting motifs to drive local LC3 lipidation and phagophore nucleation at the lesion. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8455133/?utm_source=openai))
- Effector cassette B (rebuild): Tandem high-affinity FFAT motifs to capture ER VAP-A/B and create ER–lesion contacts; the cell’s endogenous VPS13/ATG2 then bridges lipids across this contact to expand/repair the damaged membrane. Design includes spacing/valency tuned to favor sustained contact. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7610837/?utm_source=openai))

Specific aims

Aim 1. Build BARCODE and validate orthogonal control of localization and state.
- 1.1. Purified BAR modules: liposome tubulation and curvature binding in vitro; quantify Kd vs radius using tethered nanotube assays. Introduce charge-neutralizing mutations outside H0/H1 to reduce unintended partners while preserving curvature sensing. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5444402/?utm_source=openai))
- 1.2. PTM-code actuation: In cells, drive “D” with baseline conditions; drive “R” with AMPK activation (AICAR) or nutrient stress and modest oxidative shift (H2O2 pulse). Use FRET reporters inserted across the masking coiled-coil to confirm binary exposure states at the organelle surface. The phosphorylation-switchable coiled-coil and roGFP disulfide chemistry anchor feasibility. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-021-21622-5?utm_source=openai))
- 1.3. Lesion targeting: Validate recruitment to damaged lysosomes (LLOMe), mitochondria (photo/antimycin microlesions), and ER tubule rips. Co-localization with galectins or damage reporters confirms lesion adjacency.

Milestone: BARCODE accumulates at damaged membranes; PTM-code toggles exposure of cassette A vs B without altering BAR localization.

Aim 2. Demonstrate curvature-gated selective autophagy when code = “D”.
- 2.1. Autophagy assembly: Quantify local WIPI2 and ATG16L1 recruitment, LC3-PE puncta formation, and cargo sequestration at BARCODE-positive lesions by live-cell imaging and proximity labeling. WIPI2-driven ATG16L1 recruitment is the critical initiation node. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8455133/?utm_source=openai))
- 2.2. Functional clearance: For mitochondria, measure Parkin-independent mitophagy readouts (mt-Keima flux, TOM20 loss) restricted to damaged subdomains neighboring BARCODE lattices. For lysosomes, assess recovery of cathepsin activity after clearance of damaged fragments.
- 2.3. Off-targets: RNA-seq and proteomics confirm no global proteostasis disruption; autophagic flux remains localized.

Milestone: BARCODE-D increases lesion-proximal LC3 lipidation and removal of damaged subdomains without reducing total organelle mass.

Aim 3. Demonstrate ER-contact–driven membrane replenishment when code = “R”.
- 3.1. Contact formation: Test whether cassette B creates stable ER–lesion contacts via FFAT–VAP. Track VAP, VPS13A/C and ATG2A/B recruitment and residence time at BARCODE lattices; visualize lipid flux using PA/PC probes across contacts. FFAT–VAP is the canonical ER anchor for these lipid-transfer bridges. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7610837/?utm_source=openai))
- 3.2. Repair/expansion efficacy: For lysosomes, quantify restoration of LysoTracker/pH, cathepsin activity, and membrane integrity after LLOMe. For mitochondria, measure recovery of ΔΨm and cristae integrity after focal lesions. For ER, assess continuity and tubule regrowth after laser ablation.
- 3.3. Dependency tests: Acute VAP-A/B depletion or VPS13/ATG2 knockdown should abrogate BARCODE-R rescue but not affect BARCODE-D autophagy, separating pathways. ATG2/VPS13 lipid transfer roles at autophagosome/contacts support this dependency. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/6548141/?utm_source=openai))

Milestone: BARCODE-R increases ER–lesion contacts and restores organelle function by lipid transfer–driven membrane replenishment.

Aim 4. Systems-level test of “clear-without-shrinkage” control logic
- 4.1. Challenge cells with chronic, distributed microdamage (low-dose ROS) versus focal, transient damage. In BARCODE-expressing cells, quantify net organelle copy number/capacity (mtDNA content, lysosome number and activity, ER area) versus health (ATP, viability).
- 4.2. Compare against controls: constitutive autophagy activators and TFEB overexpression. Expect BARCODE to preserve capacity under distributed stress better than autophagy-only strategies, because it switches to rebuild mode when global stress is high. TFEB’s role in lysosome biogenesis under mTORC1 control rationalizes the comparison. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22692423/?utm_source=openai))

Design considerations and controls
- Mutual exclusivity: Effector cassettes are physically masked/unmasked by the PTM-coded coiled-coil; opposing SLiMs are never co-present at high valency on the same molecule.
- Valency thresholds: BAR lattice density sets a proximity threshold before either effector acts, limiting diffuse pathway activation.
- Minimal parts: No exogenous receptors/ligands; relies on core autophagy and contact-site machinery with proven recruitment axes (WIPI2→ATG16L1; FFAT→VAP→VPS13/ATG2). ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8455133/?utm_source=openai))

Feasibility, novelty, and why proteins are required
- Feasibility rests on: BAR curvature localization in autophagy, WIPI2–ATG16L1 structural recruitment logic for LC3 lipidation, and VAP–FFAT–VPS13/ATG2 contact-mediated lipid transfer for membrane growth/repair. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3718966/?utm_source=openai))
- Novelty: No prior system combines curvature classification with a PTM-coded, mutually exclusive routing between selective autophagy and ER-driven lipid transfer/repair. Existing engineered LIR adapters/eLIRs only drive degradation; they do not implement a rebuild mode. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-023-39404-6?utm_source=openai))
- Protein-scale advantages: Geometry sensing (BAR), multivalency, and scaffolded lipid-transfer recruitment cannot be replicated by small molecules/antibodies. Lipid channel proteins (VPS13/ATG2) move bulk glycerolipids to expand membranes—this is a protein-only capability. ([rupress.org](https://rupress.org/jcb/article/221/5/e202202030/213104/Structural-and-biochemical-insights-into-lipid?utm_source=openai))

Readouts and success criteria
- Switch fidelity: >90% correct cassette exposure under defined PTM states; FRET and protease-access assays confirm.
- Local execution: ≥2-fold enrichment of WIPI2/ATG16L1 and LC3-PE at BARCODE-D lesions; ≥2-fold enrichment of VAP/VPS13/ATG2 and ER–lesion contacts at BARCODE-R lesions.
- Functional outcome: Under focal damage, faster clearance half-time without loss of global organelle content. Under distributed stress, preserved or increased organelle capacity with restored function versus autophagy-only controls.

Risk assessment and mitigations
- Risk: Simultaneous activation of both arms. Mitigation: Hard mutual masking, and engineering cassette-incompatible spacers to prevent mixed lattices.
- Risk: Excess ER tethering. Mitigation: FFAT valency titration; deploy phospho-FFAT variants to add reversibility. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7999203/?utm_source=openai))
- Risk: BAR off-target curvature binding. Mitigation: Employ lesion-conditional recruitment (e.g., add weak galectin-binding microdomain) only if needed; start with BAR-only to minimize added parts.

Deliverables
- A sequence-defined, human-cell–expressible BARCODE protein with validated two-state control.
- Quantitative datasets showing conditional routing to clearance or repair and net improvement in organelle homeostasis across stress regimes.

Impact
A single protein that senses lesion geometry and decodes global PTM patterns to choose clearance or rebuilding addresses a gap not met by degraders or TFEB agonists: it preserves function by coupling disposal with replacement at the site of failure. It is directly testable and modular for different organelles by swapping targeting SLiMs or contact motifs. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10374877/?utm_source=openai))

text:
Title
Client-induced, logic-gated “misfold patrol” proteins for selective ubiquitination of aberrant intracellular conformations

Central hypothesis (framed as a research question)
Can a de novo protein that (i) preferentially engages misfolded conformational ensembles via entropic capture and (ii) uses the accumulated binding energy to unmask an E3-ligase–recruiting surface, (iii) nucleating only transient, client-dependent microcompartments, achieve selective proteasomal clearance of aberrant intracellular proteins without perturbing global proteostasis?

Atomic strategy
Exploit the kinetic and thermodynamic advantages of disordered/fuzzy interfaces to sense misfold exposure, and convert multivalent engagement energy into a conformational switch that exposes a short SPOP-recruiting motif only when multiple aberrant patches are engaged long enough to exceed a defined threshold. This gates local E3 assembly and ubiquitination at sites of high aberrancy, not on native proteins. The approach couples three validated biophysical principles—IDR/fuzzy capture of non-native surfaces, binding-energy–gated conformational switching, and valency-dependent PQC microcompartmentation—into a single, self-limiting actuator. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5016563/?utm_source=openai))

Specific aims and workplan

Aim 1. Engineer and validate an entropic-capture misfold sensor (Ecms)
- Design: A 12–20 kDa de novo scaffold bearing 3–4 short amphipathic/π-rich “fuzzy” capture segments (8–12 aa each) positioned by flexible linkers to maximize encounter rate and weak multivalent binding to exposed hydrophobic/β-edge features enriched on non-native states; monovalent contacts are individually weak to avoid native binding.
- Rationale: IDRs and fuzzy complexes minimize entropic penalties and can increase capture radius (fly-casting), enabling preferential engagement of conformationally labile, hydrophobic-patch–rich states over compact native folds. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5016563/?utm_source=openai))
- Assays: Compare binding kinetics/affinities of Ecms to (a) native vs destabilized mutants of model clients (e.g., firefly luciferase L33P; TDP-43 ΔLCD), (b) thermally perturbed states, using stopped-flow, smFRET, and cellular BiFC. Benchmark selectivity vs Hsp70 substrate reporters and ANS binding; verify low occupancy on native proteome by limited proteolysis–mass spectrometry. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8243209/?utm_source=openai))
- Success criteria: ≥10-fold higher residence time on misfold-enriched vs native states at 37°C with ≤5% native proteome pulldown.

Aim 2. Construct a binding-energy–gated, self-limiting E3-recruitment switch (LOCKR-E3)
- Design: Fuse Ecms to a de novo latching cage (LOCKR-like) that masks a minimal SPOP-binding motif (consensus MATH-site degron) inside the cage. Only when ≥2–3 capture segments are simultaneously engaged does the cumulative binding free energy unlock the cage and expose the SPOP motif; disengagement recloses the cage, terminating activity. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10697137/?utm_source=openai))
- Rationale: Degron masking/unmasking is a native regulatory logic; designed protein switches can allosterically expose functional peptides in an AND-gated fashion. SPOP is a Cul3 adaptor that forms active ubiquitination condensates with substrates, providing a native amplification environment upon recruitment. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9095673/?utm_source=openai))
- Assays: In cells, monitor cage opening with FRET sensors; co-IP SPOP/Cul3 only under misfold load; verify ubiquitination of client but not Ecms itself. Map chain linkages (K48 vs K63) by linkage-specific antibodies. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11805624/?utm_source=openai))
- Success criteria: ≥5-fold increase in client ubiquitination only under misfold stress; reversible loss of E3 recruitment within minutes after stress relief.

Aim 3. Enable client-induced, thresholded microcompartmentation to concentrate E3 and clients locally
- Design: Add a weak, reversible dimerization/oligomerization interface (e.g., low-affinity coiled-coil) to LOCKR-E3. When multiple Ecms bind densely misfolded targets, crosslinking lowers the effective critical concentration, nucleating small, dynamic microcompartments that enrich SPOP/Cul3 and clients; below threshold, Ecms remain diffuse.
- Rationale: PQC leverages phase-separated/condensed hubs to triage misfolded proteins; SPOP and ubiquitin adaptors operate in condensates that are sites of active ubiquitination. Engineered condensates have been shown to recruit ubiquitination machinery or even proteasomes directly for selective degradation; we restrict this behavior to misfold-high locales via our gate. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7924994/?utm_source=openai))
- Assays: Live-cell FRAP to quantify liquidity and reversibility; proteasome recruitment by immunofluorescence; perturb valency (mutate capture segments) to demonstrate thresholding. Rescue experiments with MG132/MLN4924 to confirm UPS/E3 dependence. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-026-72967-8?utm_source=openai))
- Success criteria: Induced foci only under elevated misfold burden, rapid dissolution upon recovery, and enhanced, localized K48-linked ubiquitination of clients.

Aim 4. Functional tests in disease-relevant misfold models and safety profiling
- Models: (i) Cytosolic destabilized enzyme model (mutant luciferase); (ii) TDP-43 or tau oligomer stress in neuronal cells; (iii) ER/mitochondrial stress spillover to cytosol.
- Readouts: Decrease of detergent-insoluble species; restoration of organelle function (ΔΨm, ERAD flux); cell viability under proteotoxic stress; global proteome stability (TMT-MS) to exclude broad proteostasis perturbation; transcriptomics for stress responses.
- Controls: Ecms lacking capture segments; LOCKR with scrambled SPOP motif; constitutively open vs locked switch; SPOP-depleted cells to confirm pathway reliance. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6803047/?utm_source=openai))
- Safety gates: Cage remains closed basally; low-affinity monomers minimize nonspecific sequestration; no direct immune activation modules; activity contingent on aberrancy density and dwell time.

Design details and implementation notes
- Capture segment composition: Short aromatic/hydrophobic patterns (e.g., Φ-x-Φ, W/Y enrichment) tuned to penalize native polar/charged surfaces; validated by reduced binding to well-folded reference proteins and enhanced binding to exposed hydrophobes on destabilized variants. This leverages IDR “fuzzy” binding and fly-casting to gain encounter probability without high-affinity monovalent contacts. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5016563/?utm_source=openai))
- Gate thermodynamics: Calibrate cage ΔGclose−open to require ≥2 capture arms engaged for ≥10 s (set by linker lengths and avidity). Use Rosetta-guided designs and cell-based reporter screens to select constructs with minimal baseline opening. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10697137/?utm_source=openai))
- E3 choice: Prefer SPOP because its condensates are naturally ubiquitination-competent and Cul3-associated; recruitment has been observed to concentrate ubiquitination within nuclear bodies and other condensates. If SPOP is limiting in a cell type, swap to an ELF-characterized ligase surface or alternative adaptors with condensate propensity. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6803047/?utm_source=openai))
- Alternative routing (contingency): If some clients are too large for the proteasome, append a cryptic LC3-interacting region (LIR) masked by the same gate to hand off oversized assemblies to autophagy only when the gate is open, maintaining the same AND logic. ([mdpi.com](https://www.mdpi.com/2073-4409/11/15/2415?utm_source=openai))

Milestones and quantitative decision points
- M1: Biophysical selectivity of Ecms (≥10× residence time on misfold vs native). Go/No-Go.
- M2: Conditional E3 recruitment (≤5% basal opening; ≥5× increase under misfold load). Go/No-Go.
- M3: Thresholded microcompartments (appearance only above pre-defined client valency; half-life <2 min after stress relief). Go/No-Go.
- M4: Functional rescue (≥50% reduction in insoluble client and restoration of organelle metrics with no >5% proteome-wide abundance shifts). Advance to in vivo models.

Anticipated outcomes and risk mitigation
- The system should selectively ubiquitinate aberrant conformers early, preventing aggregate maturation and downstream organelle failure. If basal activity is non-zero, increase cage stability or reduce capture arm hydrophobe density. If SPOP recruitment is insufficient, increase SPOP-motif valency modestly or pivot to direct proteasome-recruiting short cationic motifs shown to promote proteasome engagement within engineered condensates (kept under the same gate). ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-026-72967-8?utm_source=openai))

Why this is distinct and feasible
- Distinct from receptor agonism/antagonism: an entirely intracellular, logic-gated PQC augmenter that executes a defined function—selective ubiquitination and clearance—rather than mere binding.
- Feasible: Each module (fuzzy capture segments; LOCKR-like gated peptide exposure; recruitment of a native condensate-forming E3) is individually validated in related contexts. Their coupling here is novel in purpose and architecture: sensing misfold ensembles, converting binding energy into a conformational decision, and confining the UPS reaction to emergent microenvironments at aberrant sites. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5016563/?utm_source=openai))

References (key supporting precedents)
- IDR/fuzzy and fly-casting principles enabling entropic capture: Frontiers in Mol. Biosci. 2016; PNAS/Reviews on IDP binding kinetics. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5016563/?utm_source=openai))
- PQC condensates and spatial triage (JUNQ/IPOD; adaptor/E3/proteasome enrichment): Nat. Rev./review 2021; UBQLN2/SPOP condensate literature. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7924994/?utm_source=openai))
- Designed conformational gates that unmask functional peptides on binding: de novo LOCKR hinge/cage systems. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10697137/?utm_source=openai))
- Engineered condensates driving degradation (feasibility; alternative direct proteasome recruitment): recent studies demonstrating antibody-enriched condensates with proteasome targeting. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42129171/?utm_source=openai))
