Title
Geometry-first control of endogenous gene expression via locus-specific magneto-tethering

Central question/hypothesis
Can an externally applied, reversible, sequence-specific magnetic tether that acutely decreases enhancer–promoter separation drive predictable changes in transcriptional bursting and cell phenotype in the absence of recruited chromatin enzymes? If yes, this demonstrates that physical proximity alone is sufficient to modulate gene output in epithelial cells and neurons, separating geometry from chemistry in the causal chain of gene regulation. Prior looping tools relied on protein dimerizers at targeted loci; a field-driven, enzyme‑independent potential should provide a cleaner, faster perturbation of 3D genome structure. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/ncomms15993?utm_source=openai))

Atomic strategy
Convert two endogenous DNA loci into “magnetic beads on a chromatin polymer” and impose a tunable, time‑programmed attractive potential between them using an external magnetic field. This shifts the contact‑probability distribution without invoking methylation or histone modification machinery, enabling temporal ordering: structure change within seconds to minutes, nascent transcription within minutes, phenotype within hours to days. Feasibility of locus‑specific magnetic micromanipulation inside the nucleus has been established, but it has not been used to install enhancer–promoter loops to control gene expression. ([institut-curie.org](https://institut-curie.org/publications/live-cell-micromanipulation-genomic-locus-reveals-interphase-chromatin-mechanics))

Model systems and target loci
- Epithelial: Non‑transformed human mammary epithelial cells (e.g., MCF10A). Target an endogenous adhesion gene with a well‑separated distal enhancer (candidate identified by ATAC‑seq and Micro‑C in-house). Phenotype: cell–cell adhesion strength and epithelial barrier function (e.g., dissociation index, TEER).
- Neuronal: Human iPSC‑derived cortical neurons. Target BDNF promoter IV and its activity‑linked enhancer(s). Phenotype: firing rate and burst synchrony on multi‑electrode arrays.

Intervention design: locus‑specific magnetic tethers
- Locus tags: Install short, inert 20–24 bp landing pads by CRISPR prime editing immediately proximal to the chosen enhancer and promoter to enable hybridization of complementary capture oligonucleotides. Tags are noncoding and minimize endogenous machinery engagement.
- Magnetic probes: Monodisperse iron‑oxide nanoparticles coated with antifouling/zwitterionic polymers for nuclear compatibility, each functionalized with a sequence‑specific capture oligo (one probe per locus). Nuclear targeting is achieved by physicochemical coatings; no chromatin‑modifying enzymes are recruited. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s12551-025-01349-z?utm_source=openai))
- Actuation: Microfabricated poles or external magnets apply low‑picoNewton effective forces/gradients inside living-cell nuclei to bias coalescence of the two nanoparticle‑decorated loci, as shown feasible for single‑locus manipulation. Field withdrawal relaxes the constraint. ([institut-curie.org](https://institut-curie.org/publications/live-cell-micromanipulation-genomic-locus-reveals-interphase-chromatin-mechanics))

Readouts and timing logic
- Structure: Live two‑color tracking of tagged loci and magnetic probe fluorescence to quantify locus–locus distance and co‑movement during field pulses; orthogonal confirmation by targeted 4C/Micro‑C in matched samples.
- Transcription: Endogenous nascent RNA imaging via minimal MS2/MCP tagging introduced at the target gene 3′ UTR, or intron‑smFISH time courses where tagging is impractical. Quantify burst frequency and burst size changes versus field dose.
- Phenotype: Epithelial adhesion (dissociation assay; TEER trajectories) and neuronal network activity (MEA metrics). The analysis explicitly tests lag structure: Δdistance (t0–t2 min) → Δnascent RNA (t5–30 min) → Δphenotype (t4–72 h).

Key experiments and falsification
Aim 1. Calibrate reversible, dose‑dependent geometric control
- Deliver locus‑specific magnetic probes; establish field–response curves for mean and fluctuating enhancer–promoter separations. Demonstrate reversibility and lack of global nuclear deformation by imaging untargeted reference loci. Quantify the effective attractive potential added to a Rouse‑like polymer using the measured displacement statistics. Success metric: monotonic, titratable reduction in median separation with rapid on/off kinetics. ([institut-curie.org](https://institut-curie.org/publications/live-cell-micromanipulation-genomic-locus-reveals-interphase-chromatin-mechanics))

Aim 2. Establish sequential causality from geometry to expression to epithelial phenotype
- Pulse protocol: Alternate short (seconds–minutes) field pulses with imaging epochs to ensure structural perturbation precedes any transcriptional response.
- Transcriptional effect: Show that increased contact probability increases burst frequency at the target promoter and that the magnitude follows the imposed structural “dose.” Polymer theory predicts a supra‑linear increase in encounter rate as end‑to‑end distance distribution is narrowed; test this prediction by fitting burst frequency to the measured contact‑time enrichment. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/1403.1236?utm_source=openai))
- Phenotype linkage: Quantify how sustained duty cycles that elevate mean expression produce graded improvements in adhesion/barrier function. Falsification criteria: if matched controls (scrambled tags; one‑locus targeting; nanoparticles without field) show identical transcriptional changes, geometry is not causal under these conditions.

Aim 3. Portability and generality in neurons
- Repeat the protocol at BDNF promoter–enhancer pairs in iPSC‑derived neurons. Assess transcriptional bursting and network activity. A positive result argues that geometry‑first control extends to post‑mitotic cells with distinct chromatin mechanics.

Controls and side‑effect audits
- Geometry‑only controls: Deploy the magnetic field in cells lacking either nanoparticle species or with one incorrect oligo to rule out field or mass effects.
- Enzyme‑independence audit: Time‑resolved ChIP‑qPCR for selected histone marks at target regions during short pulses; expect no mark changes at perturbation onset. Transcription changes should vanish upon field withdrawal without hysteresis attributable to covalent marks.
- Off‑target mechanical audit: Track unrelated loci to confirm local rather than global nuclear deformation.

Quantitative analysis
- Contact–burst transfer function: Reconstruct P(burst|contact) by aligning distance trajectories with nascent RNA trajectories in the same cell, estimating information flow using time‑lagged mutual information and Granger causality tests. Expect peak predictive power from structure to transcription at short lags (minutes), with reversed tests failing when lags exclude the structural epoch. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10714922/?utm_source=openai))
- Dose–response and hysteresis: Map field amplitude/duty cycle to contact time fraction and to mean expression; lack of hysteresis upon withdrawal supports an enzyme‑independent mechanism.

Distinctiveness relative to prior art
CRISPR‑based looping systems (CLOuD9; LADL) demonstrate reversible enhancer–promoter bridging but do so by assembling multivalent protein complexes at DNA, potentially conflating geometry with coactivator recruitment or condensate formation. The proposed magnetic tether is enzyme‑silent and actuated externally, delivering a faster and cleaner ordering of events: geometry first, chemistry later if at all. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/ncomms15993?utm_source=openai))

Risk assessment and contingency
- If effective forces at dual loci are insufficient to appreciably raise contact probability, increase capture valency per locus (more nanoparticles per tag) or refine field gradients; feasibility is supported by prior intracellular chromatin micromanipulation with near‑pN forces. ([institut-curie.org](https://institut-curie.org/publications/live-cell-micromanipulation-genomic-locus-reveals-interphase-chromatin-mechanics))
- Orthogonal validation (contingency): Use a peptide nucleic acid (PNA) dimer with a photocleavable linker to impose a defined, reversible loop between short homopurine targets flanking the same enhancer–promoter pair. PNA duplex invasion into dsDNA is enzyme‑free and well‑characterized; photocleavage provides a second, non‑magnetic route to rapid structural switching. Concordant transcriptional effects across both modalities would strengthen the geometry‑first claim. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC47834/?utm_source=openai))

Expected outcomes and interpretation
- A rapid, reversible increase in enhancer–promoter co‑localization elevates transcriptional burst frequency and, with sustained duty cycles, modifies cell‑level phenotypes in epithelial cells and neurons. A null result under strong geometric bias would constrain models in which proximity is neither limiting nor rate‑controlling for the assayed loci.

Milestones and deliverables
- Year 1: Build and validate locus‑specific magnetic tethers; demonstrate reversible nanometer‑to‑submicron distance control at two endogenous pairs. ([institut-curie.org](https://institut-curie.org/publications/live-cell-micromanipulation-genomic-locus-reveals-interphase-chromatin-mechanics))
- Year 2: Complete epithelial causality tests and phenotype link; deliver the calibrated contact–burst transfer function.
- Year 3: Port to neurons; replicate causality and phenotype link; optional PNA contingency module.

Novelty and impact
This work repurposes nuclear magnetic micromanipulation—from a mechanics probe to a causal, enzyme‑independent control knob for gene regulation—to test whether geometry alone is sufficient to tune endogenous transcription and phenotype. No prior study has used field‑actuated, sequence‑specific nanoparticles to install enhancer–promoter contacts for functional gene control in living cells. ([institut-curie.org](https://institut-curie.org/publications/live-cell-micromanipulation-genomic-locus-reveals-interphase-chromatin-mechanics))

text:
Title
Bio-orthogonal, ligand-gated Pol II microcompartments as a sufficiency test for endogenous gene activation in epithelial cells and neurons

Central question/hypothesis
Does a local, bio-orthogonally assembled RNA polymerase II (Pol II)–rich microcompartment at a silent endogenous promoter or enhancer suffice to increase transcriptional burst frequency and drive a cell-type-relevant phenotype in epithelial cells or neurons, without rewiring chromatin looping or relying primarily on histone/DNA methylation changes? Prior locus-tethered condensate systems (optogenetic CasDrop/LAMPS) show that engineered condensation at specific loci can modulate transcription; small-molecule–induced proximity can recruit activators; however, a pre-programmed, locus-specific small-molecule proximate assembly that nucleates a Pol II hub at an endogenous gene has not been established. This gap enables a clean sufficiency test of “factory” creation at native chromatin. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0092867418314569?utm_source=openai))

Atomic strategy
Create a bio-orthogonal, chemically gated, weakly multivalent proximity network at the chosen locus that concentrates Pol II and associated general initiation/elongation factors via transient high-frequency rebinding. The 3D structural event is a mesoscale condensate-like microdomain at the locus; causality is assayed as: inducible compartment appearance → increased nascent transcriptional bursts → cell-type phenotype. The mechanism leverages selective partitioning and multivalency of transcriptional assemblies, without enforcing stable looping or recruiting chromatin-modifying enzymes as the primary driver. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/7572565/?utm_source=openai))

Specific aims

Aim 1. Build and verify a bio-orthogonal, small-molecule–gated “factory” at an endogenous silent locus.
- Rationale: Locus-targeted condensation can be induced optogenetically; chemically induced proximity (CIP) reliably assembles functional complexes; heterobifunctional molecules can recruit endogenous transcriptional machinery to DNA. We will combine these logics in a bio-orthogonal design. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10065442/?utm_source=openai))
- Design: Use a locus-tethered, sequence-programmable DNA-binding module with an orthogonal protein tag (Handle A) and a separately expressed Pol II–interacting effector bearing a complementary orthogonal tag (Handle B). A cell-permeable dimerizer (CIP) binds A and B to nucleate a local, weakly multivalent assembly that enriches endogenous Pol II and general factors through low-affinity interactions. This preserves native geometry and avoids stable tethering or loop enforcement. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1074552104003370?utm_source=openai))
- Readouts of 3D state: Rapid, reversible foci formation at the targeted locus; liquid-like dynamics by photobleaching recovery; enrichment of endogenous Pol II/Mediator/BRD4 at the foci; minimal bulk chromatin repositioning. Prior work defines these hallmarks and feasibility. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0092867418314569?utm_source=openai))
- Novelty check: While CasDrop/LAMPS use protein optogenetics to seed locus-specific condensates, and CIPs recruit activators in synthetic contexts, a small-molecule–gated, bio-orthogonal proximate assembly that concentrates endogenous Pol II at an endogenous locus to test sufficiency has not been reported; a recent AAV system shows related chemical recruitment of transcriptional machinery to a transgene, supporting feasibility and underscoring the novelty at endogenous loci. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40298110/?utm_source=openai))

Aim 2. Test transcriptional sufficiency and kinetic mechanism at target genes in epithelial cells and neurons.
- Rationale: Condensate-like promoter hubs modulate burst frequency/size; Pol II/Mediator/BRD4 coalesce at transcription foci. We will quantify whether induced “factory” formation raises nascent transcription and Pol II dwell/elongation without primary reliance on histone/DNA methylation. ([biorxiv.org](https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898/2026.05.24.727549v1?utm_source=openai))
- Endpoints of gene expression: Increased burst frequency and output at the targeted gene (nascent RNA quantification; polymerase occupancy and elongation metrics). Reversibility upon ligand removal defines kinetic control, not structural hardwiring. ([biorxiv.org](https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898/2026.05.24.727549v1?utm_source=openai))
- Independence from primary epigenetic modification: Compare expression gains with/without short-term inhibition of major chromatin writers/readers while preserving Pol II function; monitor local histone/DNA methylation to ensure changes, if any, are secondary to the engineered proximity event. Prior condensation tools reported transcriptional activation concomitant with local reconfiguration but did not isolate bio-orthogonal chemical gating; we do. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10065442/?utm_source=openai))

Aim 3. Link transcriptional changes to cell-type phenotypes with a defined causal chain.
- Epithelial case: Induce a keratinocyte differentiation or barrier gene whose upregulation yields measurable epithelial traits (e.g., junctional integrity, barrier markers). Neuronal case: Induce a silent neuronal activity gene whose expression alters excitability or morphology. Outcome metrics are triggered only when the locus-local microcompartment forms and track in magnitude with engineered proximity strength. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10065442/?utm_source=openai))
- Causal chain validation: Time-resolved alignment of (i) microcompartment onset at the locus, (ii) nascent transcript rise, (iii) phenotype emergence; disruption of condensate-like properties (e.g., reduced multivalency) abolishes both transcriptional and phenotypic effects, as observed in locus-targeted condensation literature. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0092867418314569?utm_source=openai))

Design principles and controls
- Bio-orthogonality: Use interaction pairs and linkers that have no endogenous counterparts to minimize crosstalk and ensure that observed effects derive from engineered proximity rather than native coactivator feedback. CIP systems (e.g., FRB/FKBP-family, and other orthogonal pairs) provide established scaffolds for such gating. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1074552104003370?utm_source=openai))
- Kinetic capture over stable tethering: Engineer weak, multivalent interfaces to favor rapid rebinding and high local collision frequency, consistent with how IDR-mediated hubs enrich factors without fixed stoichiometry. Predict increased burst frequency with minimal change in burst duration. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8176841/?utm_source=openai))
- Negative/mechanistic controls: (i) Handle A without Handle B (no factory); (ii) Handle B lacking multivalency (no factory); (iii) targeting a safe-harbor locus (factory without transcriptional outcome); (iv) ligand-inactive analogs; (v) optogenetic positive controls from prior literature to benchmark dynamic range. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10065442/?utm_source=openai))

Expected outcomes and decision points
- If local microcompartment formation increases nascent transcription and produces a phenotype while primary epigenetic marks remain largely unchanged during the activation window, the “factory sufficiency” hypothesis is supported. If expression requires concurrent histone acetylation or chromatin remodeling to manifest, factory formation is necessary but not sufficient; the design then becomes a probe for the threshold of cofactor dependence. Condensate literature suggests promoter hubs and Pol II-rich foci correlate with bursts; CIPs provide temporal control for causality—together offering a stringent sufficiency test at endogenous loci. ([biorxiv.org](https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898/2026.05.24.727549v1?utm_source=openai))

Impact and novelty
This work reframes control of gene expression from architectural rewiring to bio-orthogonal kinetic assembly at native chromatin, creating a stringent, chemically gated sufficiency test at endogenous genes in physiologically relevant cells. It integrates established locus-specific condensation concepts and proximity chemistry in a new configuration: endogenous-locus, small-molecule–gated assembly of a Pol II microcompartment that minimizes reliance on epigenetic modifiers as primary drivers. Prior methods achieved either locus specificity via optogenetics or chemical control without endogenous-locus condensate nucleation; bridging these solves a key mechanistic question. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0092867418314569?utm_source=openai))

Risk and alternatives
If direct enrichment of Pol II proves inefficient, substitute or co-recruit Mediator/TFIID subcomplexes known to colocalize with Pol II foci, maintaining bio-orthogonal gating and weak multivalency. If condensate-like behavior is not observed, tune valence and off-rates of the engineered interfaces within ranges known to modulate condensate formation at loci. These adjustments preserve the atomic strategy. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42244740/?utm_source=openai))

Validation of mechanistic premises and novelty
- Locus-targeted condensate formation can modulate transcription at endogenous loci (CasDrop, LAMPS). ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0092867418314569?utm_source=openai))
- Transcriptional activity correlates with Pol II/Mediator/BRD4 coalescence and promoter hubs affecting bursting kinetics. ([biorxiv.org](https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898/2026.05.24.727549v1?utm_source=openai))
- Small-molecule–induced proximity robustly recruits activators and controls transcription; a recent heterobifunctional recruiter of endogenous machinery to a DNA cassette supports feasibility for chemical recruitment, but endogenous-locus condensate nucleation by a pre-programmed small molecule remains unreported, preserving novelty. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7914288/?utm_source=openai))

text:
Title
MagTopo: Reversible gene control by magnetically gating loop extrusion and enhancer–promoter proximity in epithelial cells

Rationale and integrated question–hypothesis
Can externally imposed, locus-specific steric boundaries and mechanical proximity alone—without recruiting epigenetic enzymes—rewire 3D chromatin architecture to modulate transcriptional bursting and drive epithelial phenotype shifts? We hypothesize that superparamagnetic, locus-tethered nanoparticles can (i) act as reversible kinetic barriers to cohesin-driven loop extrusion to re-route enhancer traffic, and (ii) enforce or release enhancer–promoter proximity under applied fields, thereby tuning burst frequency and producing measurable epithelial phenotypes. This rests on: (a) cohesin extrudes DNA loops until barriers halt it; extrusion shapes TADs and promoter–enhancer contact probability, and is directly visualized in vitro, (b) sufficiently large DNA-bound obstacles impede cohesin motion, implying an engineered steric block can gate extrusion, (c) optogenetic/chemical locus repositioning and bridging can modulate expression but rely on protein–protein chemistry; a purely mechanical alternative remains underexplored, (d) magnetic nanoparticles can be actuated inside nuclei and have been used to micromanipulate genomic loci. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31780627/?utm_source=openai))

Atomic strategy
Treat enhancer–promoter distance and extrusion path as controllable mechanical variables. Install inert, dCas9-addressed superparamagnetic nanoparticles (MNPs) as “traffic gates” that (1) transiently block or divert extrusion at defined sites to bias which promoter an enhancer contacts, and (2) magnetically pull together or release enhancer- and promoter-bound MNPs to toggle proximity. Switching the external field flips 3D state → transcriptional bursting parameters → epithelial phenotype, without primary reliance on chromatin-modifying enzymes. Enhancer proximity primarily tunes burst frequency; thus proximity gating should produce fast, reversible changes in nascent transcription. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4970759/?utm_source=openai))

Specific aims
Aim 1. Build and validate locus-tethered magnetic gates in human epithelial cells.
- System: MCF10A or Caco-2 cells engineered with (i) dCas9-HaloTag-NLS for addressability, (ii) MS2-tagged intron at the target gene for live nascent RNA imaging, and (iii) fluorescent operators (e.g., minimal CRISPR tags) near target enhancer and promoter for distance readout.
- MNPs: ~15–20 nm Fe3O4 cores with biocompatible zwitterionic phosphonate copolymer coats for nuclear stability; conjugate Halo-ligand or sgRNA-adaptor oligos to bind dCas9 at chosen sites. Validate nuclear import, on-target occupancy, and low background chromatin binding. Use microfabricated magnetic pillar arrays or external gradient coils to generate sub-piconewton to few-piconewton forces.
- Benchmarks: (i) On-target enrichment by CUT&RUN for MNP-associated tags, (ii) no recruitment of p300/BRD4/KMTs by ChIP–qPCR in the first hour after actuation, (iii) cell viability and DNA damage markers negative, (iv) calibrated MNP displacement under field in living nuclei. ([pubs.acs.org](https://pubs.acs.org/doi/10.1021/acs.nanolett.3c00688?utm_source=openai))

Aim 2. Topology gating: create temporary TAD boundaries and detours to re-route enhancer traffic.
- Design: Position MNP “roadblocks” at one or both sides of a promoter-proximal CTCF site or within the corridor between enhancer and an off-target promoter. Field ON aggregates/aligns MNPs to increase effective obstacle size (>20 nm), stalling or diverting cohesin to favor the intended enhancer–promoter contact; Field OFF disperses/reduces effective obstacle size, restoring native routing.
- Readouts of 3D state: rapid Micro-C/HiChIP (cohesin/CTCF) at 30–60 min; live two-color genomic distance imaging; polymer modeling to predict loop frequency shifts under barrier density.
- Success metric: reversible increase in target enhancer–promoter contact frequency with concomitant decrease in off-target contacts upon Field ON, returning to baseline upon Field OFF. Mechanistic sufficiency is grounded in the known barrier sensitivity of cohesin to large DNA-bound obstacles. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5167347/?utm_source=openai))

Aim 3. Proximity gating: impose/remove enhancer–promoter contact to tune bursting and epithelial phenotypes.
- Design: Bind MNPs to the enhancer and promoter; apply field gradients to bring labeled loci within <150 nm and hold for defined dwell times, then release. No effector domains are recruited.
- Transcriptional outcomes: quantify burst frequency and size via MS2 live imaging and smFISH; expectation is primary modulation of burst frequency with minute-scale kinetics upon proximity enforcement. Steady-state mRNA by RNA-seq at 2–6 h and protein at 24–48 h. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4970759/?utm_source=openai))
- Phenotypes: choose barrier-forming gene(s) with mapped enhancers (e.g., CLDN4/OCLN). Measure TEER, tight-junction continuity (ZO1 immunostaining), and collective migration in wound-healing assays. Demonstrate full causal chain: 3D state switch → burst frequency shift → mRNA/protein change → TEER/migration change.

Experimental design and controls
- Target selection pipeline: use public Hi-C/HiChIP to shortlist epithelial loci with clear enhancer–promoter pairs and boundary architecture; incorporate MS2 tagging by CRISPR HDR at the promoter-proximal intron.
- Magnetic actuation: (i) TAD gate mode—MNPs at barrier positions only; (ii) Proximity mode—MNPs at enhancer and promoter. Duty cycles: 1–10 min ON pulses with equal OFF recovery windows to test reversibility.
- Controls: scrambled sgRNAs; nonmagnetic but size-matched nanoparticles; field-only; dCas9 without MNPs; optogenetic LADL positive control at same locus to benchmark effect sizes, noting chemistry-based bridging vs mechanical proximity. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6599567/?utm_source=openai))
- “No enzyme” verification: ChIP–qPCR/ChIP–seq for H3K27ac/H3K9me3/DNMT3A targets at early time points (≤2 h) to confirm topology precedes any chromatin mark changes; RNAPII pausing metrics to exclude transcriptional-blocking artifacts.

Key measurements and success criteria
- 3D architecture: ≥2-fold reversible change in target enhancer–promoter contact frequency by Micro-C/HiChIP and ≥25% reduction in median enhancer–promoter distance by live imaging upon Field ON; return to baseline OFF.
- Transcription: ≥1.5–3-fold change in burst frequency with minimal change in burst size within 30–60 min of actuation; reversibility within 1–2 h after release. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4970759/?utm_source=openai))
- Phenotype: ≥15–25% change in TEER aligned temporally downstream of transcriptional effects; reversal on release or cleavage of MNP–DNA tether.

Feasibility and novelty check (condensed)
- Mechanistic base: cohesin-mediated loop extrusion halted by barriers is established; single-molecule data indicate large obstacles (≥~20 nm) block cohesin motion, directly supporting steric gating. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31780627/?utm_source=openai))
- Prior art: CRISPR-GO and LADL reposition/bridge loci via chemical/optogenetic dimerization; our approach substitutes externally actuated steric barriers and mechanical proximity, minimizing endogenous enzymatic engagement. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6239909/?utm_source=openai))
- Actuation feasibility: magnetic manipulation inside nuclei and locus micromanipulation with coated iron oxide nanoparticles have been demonstrated, enabling our proposed nuclear-scale forces and addressability. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3192970/?utm_source=openai))
- Expression logic: enhancer proximity predominantly regulates burst frequency, matching our expected fast, reversible output without invoking histone/DNA modification programs. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4970759/?utm_source=openai))

Risk analysis and mitigations
- Off-target tethering or chromatin damage: minimize MNP load, use high-specificity sgRNAs, monitor γH2AX/53BP1; include nonmagnetic size-matched controls.
- Field-induced heating: operate in low-frequency, low-amplitude static/gradient regimes; monitor nuclear temperature with fluorescent thermometers.
- Insufficient force transmission: increase MNP valency via small clusters (still <100 nm hydrodynamic) to remain above the cohesin-blocking threshold while preserving nuclear mobility.
- Locus-specific insensitivity: screen 3–5 loci; prioritize those with well-defined enhancer corridors and measurable epithelial outputs.

Milestones
- Month 0–6: Build MNP chemistry, on-target occupancy, nuclear actuation calibration.
- Month 6–12: Demonstrate reversible topology gating at one locus (3D metrics).
- Month 12–18: Show burst frequency control and reversible TEER change; full causal chain.
- Month 18–24: Generalize to a second epithelial locus and benchmark against LADL.

Deliverable
A validated, enzyme-independent “mechanogenetic” platform that writes and erases chromatin logic by gating extrusion and proximity with magnetic nanoparticles, establishing 3D architecture as reversible, information-bearing control over gene expression and epithelial phenotype.

text:
Title
Organizer-anchored, DNA-density-gated condensates to reweight enhancer–promoter contact probabilities and control gene expression in epithelial cells

Integrated hypothesis–question
Can a self-limited condensate that is (i) anchored to endogenous CTCF/cohesin loop anchors and (ii) only assembles when enhancer and promoter targets are simultaneously occupied, shift local 3D chromatin proximity to modulate transcription and cell phenotype—independent of covalent chromatin marks—and does acute, light-triggered dissolution extinguish these effects? The premise is that loop extrusion sets baseline encounter statistics within TADs and that transcriptional output scales with enhancer–promoter proximity and dwell time; condensates at active regulatory hubs provide a physical means to concentrate the transcriptional apparatus. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7566886/?utm_source=openai))

Atomic strategy
Reweight the conformational ensemble inside an existing TAD by creating a DNA-density-gated, self-limited condensate “brace” that amplifies native enhancer–promoter co-occupancy without nucleating ectopic contacts. Anchoring to loop organizers constrains topology; an intramolecular competitor on each scaffold monomer caps free valences so that condensation is unlocked only when enhancer and promoter guides co-target and locally exceed a critical DNA-bound scaffold density. Acute light release of a monovalent displacer caps scaffold valences and dissolves the condensate to test necessity. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-022-31856-6?utm_source=openai))

System design
- Targeting/anchoring: Use dCas9 with guide sets to (a) the promoter and distal enhancer of an epithelial gene (primary: CDH1 in MCF10A) and (b) sequences immediately adjacent to convergent CTCF sites flanking the CDH1 TAD to provide positional anchoring without perturbing CTCF motifs. Guides to anchors are sub-stoichiometric relative to enhancer/promoter guides to bias position, not nucleate. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7566886/?utm_source=openai))
- Scaffold monomer: A genetically encoded SUMO–SIM multivalent repeat where a subset of SIMs is masked in cis by a tethered intramolecular decoy (“autoinhibitory SIM-cap”). At low local DNA occupancy, cis masking keeps effective valence below the percolation threshold; when enhancer and promoter are co-occupied within tens of nanometers, trans interactions outcompete the cis decoy, crossing a local critical concentration and forming a self-limited condensate. ([journals.aps.org](https://journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevLett.129.128102?utm_source=openai))
- Light-gated dissolution: A LOVTRAP-like module cages a high-affinity monovalent SIM peptide; blue light releases the peptide, globally capping SUMO valences and dissolving the condensate without altering DNA binding or sticker identity—an acute, reversible test of physical clustering. ([jstage.jst.go.jp](https://www.jstage.jst.go.jp/article/biophysico/20/2/20_e200027/_pdf/-char/en?utm_source=openai))

Specific aims and experiments
Aim 1. Build and calibrate the DNA-density-gated, organizer-anchored condensate
- Construct dCas9–Scaffold fusions and gRNAs (enhancer, promoter, anchors). Verify nuclear expression and correct targeting by live-cell CRISPR imaging.
- Calibrate autoinhibition: mutate the intramolecular SIM-cap to tune the free-valence fraction and define the assembly threshold using FRAP, number-and-brightness analysis, and opto-release titrations.
- Controls: (i) scaffold with disabled SUMO–SIM interaction; (ii) guides singly targeting enhancer or promoter only; (iii) no anchor guides. These set baselines for density gating and anchoring contributions. ([journals.aps.org](https://journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevLett.129.128102?utm_source=openai))

Aim 2. Test 3D structure → transcription causality at the endogenous CDH1 locus
- Structure readouts: Perform Micro-C or targeted HiChIP for cohesin/Pol II to quantify enhancer–promoter contact frequency and multiway hubs within the TAD, comparing assembled versus disassembled states (light-on competitor release). Live two-color CRISPR imaging reports enhancer–promoter dwell-time distributions. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32534241/?utm_source=openai))
- Transcription readouts: Introduce MS2 stem loops into CDH1 to measure burst frequency and amplitude in real time; complement with nascent RNA-seq/PRO-seq after 30–60 min assembly or dissolution.
- Epigenetic independence check: CUT&RUN for H3K27ac/H3K4me3 at enhancer/promoter before and after acute assembly/dissolution (≤1–2 h) to confirm transcriptional changes precede or occur without mark remodeling. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7145697/?utm_source=openai))
- Comparators: (i) CasDrop (dCas9-IDR optocondensates) to benchmark against de novo nucleation; (ii) CLOuD9 (dCas9 heterodimer bridging) to benchmark against direct tethering. Expect distinct structural signatures and kinetics if physical crowding versus simple bridging is operative. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6724728/?utm_source=openai))

Aim 3. Close the chain to phenotype in epithelial cells
- Phenotypes: In MCF10A, quantify adherens junction integrity (E-cadherin/β-catenin localization), monolayer morphology, and collective migration (wound-healing assays) as CDH1 output is tuned by condensate assembly/dissolution. Record time-locked reversibility upon light-triggered dissolution. 
- Off-target/ectopic contact audit: Use capture-C across neighboring TADs and RNA-seq to ensure minimal inter-TAD rewiring or global transcriptional drift, leveraging anchoring plus self-limitation to confine effects. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-022-31856-6?utm_source=openai))

Decision criteria and predictions
- Necessary and sufficient: If assembly increases enhancer–promoter contact probability and dwell time, elevates CDH1 burst frequency, tightens junctions, and reduces migration—and each effect acutely reverses with light-triggered valence capping—then 3D clustering is causal. Failure of the disabled-SUMO/SIM mutant to produce these changes refutes condensate dependence. ([journals.aps.org](https://journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevLett.129.128102?utm_source=openai))
- Topology constraint: Anchoring should enhance in-TAD rewiring while suppressing inter-TAD contacts versus de novo nucleators such as CasDrop. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6724728/?utm_source=openai))

Feasibility, novelty, and safeguards
- Feasibility rests on: (i) well-established loop-extrusion/CTCF anchoring and enhancer biology; (ii) optogenetically controlled condensates at genomic sites (CasDrop as precedent); (iii) valence control and capping principles from associative-polymer physics and condensate biology. Our advance is to merge organizer anchoring with DNA-density-gated, self-limited assembly and a dissolution test that targets valence—not DNA binding or sticker identity—to isolate a purely physical mechanism. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7566886/?utm_source=openai))
- Safety/constraints: No recruitment of epigenetic enzymes; edits are limited to dCas9 landing and MS2 tagging. Acute light pulses for dissolution avoid global chemical perturbants (e.g., aliphatic alcohols).

Milestones and timeline
- Months 0–6: Construct and calibrate scaffolds; define assembly thresholds and light-dissolution kinetics in MCF10A.
- Months 6–12: Establish CDH1 locus targeting; complete structure and transcription causality tests under assembly/dissolution.
- Months 12–18: Phenotype closure; comparator benchmarking (CasDrop, CLOuD9); generalize to a second epithelial gene.

Primary outcomes
A physically grounded, organizer-anchored, DNA-density-gated condensate that selectively amplifies native enhancer–promoter communication to control gene expression and epithelial phenotype, with on-demand dissolution that cleanly demonstrates the causal role of 3D clustering upstream of transcription—distinct from de novo nucleators and simple molecular bridges. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6724728/?utm_source=openai))

text:
Title
Geometry-first control of neuronal gene expression by exogenous magnetic separation of enhancer–promoter contacts

Premise and gap
Engineered looping systems (LADL; dCas9–CRY2/CIBN) and locus re-localization (CRISPR‑GO) demonstrate that forced proximity and nuclear compartment targeting can modulate transcription, but they conflate geometry with recruitment of protein scaffolds and endogenous enzymatic pathways. Direct, real‑time mechanical separation of specific endogenous enhancer–promoter pairs in living cells has not been used to test necessity/sufficiency of proximity for lineage‑relevant transcriptional bursting and downstream phenotype. Recent live‑cell studies established that piconewton magnetic forces can displace tagged genomic loci by micrometers within minutes in human cells, providing a minimally biochemical handle to rewrite 3D distances with sub-hour precision, but they did not pursue gene‑regulatory or phenotypic outcomes. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6599567/?utm_source=openai))

Atomic strategy
Impose an exogenous, locus‑specific, time‑programmed separation on a defined enhancer–promoter pair to drop contact dwell time below the initiation threshold, thereby acutely reducing burst frequency and mRNA output; then propagate this change to a quantifiable neuronal phenotype. The only primary lever is distance/dwell‑time control via mechanical force; no recruitment of chromatin writers/erasers.

Unified hypothesis–question
Does a reversible, exogenously imposed increase in enhancer–promoter separation—applied at defined timescales and magnitudes—suffice to downshift transcriptional bursting of an identity‑coupled neuronal gene (3D structural change → expression change → neuronal phenotype), independent of DNA methylation or histone modifications?

Model system and target
- Human iPSC-derived excitatory cortical neurons (day 35–45).
- BDNF locus: activity-dependent enhancers (e.g., +3/+6/+9 kb cluster) contacting promoter I/IV during depolarization drive neuronal morphology and synaptic function. Target a single well-characterized enhancer–promoter pair within the same TAD.

Approach overview
- Use sequence-specific, nuclease-dead CRISPR binders only as address tags to recruit superparamagnetic handles to the enhancer (primary) and optionally to the promoter (secondary), without effector domains. Apply calibrated magnetic field gradients to displace the enhancer away from the promoter or toward the nuclear periphery. This separates geometry from enzymatic signaling and provides millisecond–minute control. ([institut-curie.org](https://institut-curie.org/publications/live-cell-micromanipulation-genomic-locus-reveals-interphase-chromatin-mechanics))
- For sufficiency controls, transiently force proximity with light-activated looping (LADL) and then test whether magnetic separation abolishes the induced expression—demonstrating that geometry is the dominant driver under both native and engineered proximity. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6599567/?utm_source=openai))

Specific Aims

Aim 1. Build and validate locus-specific magnetic separation of an endogenous enhancer.
1.1 Handle recruitment
- Express dCas9 fused to a high-affinity tag (e.g., SunTag or biotin-acceptor) targeted by gRNAs to the enhancer; deliver streptavidin- or anti-tag–functionalized 20–50 nm superparamagnetic nanoparticles (MNPs). Use minimal copy number to avoid steric crowding. Confirm binding by live imaging with orthogonal fluorescent labels. Methods for intranuclear MNP targeting and force application have been demonstrated in human cells. ([institut-curie.org](https://institut-curie.org/publications/live-cell-micromanipulation-genomic-locus-reveals-interphase-chromatin-mechanics))
1.2 Distance and force calibration
- Co-label enhancer and promoter with orthogonal CRISPR imaging (e.g., dCas9–MS2/PP7 RNA scaffolds) to track 3D positions. Map displacement vs. field gradient to estimate applied forces (target 0.1–5 pN). Validate that field application alters enhancer–promoter distance and contact dwell-time distributions within seconds–minutes. ([institut-curie.org](https://institut-curie.org/publications/live-cell-micromanipulation-genomic-locus-reveals-interphase-chromatin-mechanics))
1.3 Temporal primacy
- Establish that geometric separation precedes transcriptional change: simultaneous live‑cell imaging of distance and nascent RNA using intronic smFISH burst capture (fixed-time cohorts) and, where feasible, MS2 knock‑in at BDNF promoter IV for live nascent transcription.

Milestones/success criteria
- ≥300 nm increase in median enhancer–promoter separation and ≥50% reduction in >10 s dwell events under depolarization.
- No immediate (<10 min) changes in H3K27ac/H3K4me1 at the enhancer or H3K4me3 at the promoter (CUT&RUN snapshot), establishing non-enzymatic primacy.

Aim 2. Quantify how distance/dwell-time thresholds set BDNF burst kinetics.
2.1 Controlled stimuli
- Induce activity with 25 mM KCl or optogenetic ChR2 stimulation. Apply magnetic fields in defined regimes:
  - Pulse separation: 10–60 s pulses to selectively lower dwell time while minimally altering mean distance.
  - Step separation: sustained 5–30 min displacement.
2.2 Burst modeling
- Infer burst frequency and duration from nascent RNA traces; compute distance–burst cross‑correlation with time-lag analysis to test whether reductions in proximity predict subsequent reductions in initiation probability.
2.3 Threshold mapping
- Sweep force and orientation to generate a geometry–burst response surface. Fit critical separation and minimum dwell thresholds for initiation. Report parameters as candidate “geometric operating points” for the BDNF regulatory unit.

Milestones/success criteria
- Monotonic decrease in burst frequency with increased separation; identification of a minimal separation or sub‑threshold dwell time that suppresses >70% of bursts during stimulation.

Aim 3. Demonstrate phenotype-level consequences and identity protection.
3.1 Neuronal phenotype readouts
- Over 48–72 h of scheduled separation during daily activity bouts, quantify:
  - Dendritic complexity and spine density (Sholl analysis; PSD95/Synapsin puncta).
  - Activity patterns (calcium imaging; firing synchrony).
- Expect reduced BDNF-dependent dendritic growth and synaptic maturation under sustained separation vs. sham.
3.2 Identity locking against ectopic activation
- Ectopic proximity challenge: deploy LADL to transiently bridge a non-neuronal (epithelial) enhancer, chosen for sequence compatibility and within-range genomic distance, to a neuronal promoter. Immediately apply magnetic separation targeted to the recruited enhancer to block contact. Evaluate whether separation prevents misexpression and preserves neuronal markers and electrophysiological identity. This tests whether mechanical insulation can abort lineage-foreign activation without editing genome sequence or invoking chromatin modifiers. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6599567/?utm_source=openai))

Causality and constraint compliance
- Primary intervention is mechanical geometry control; no writer/eraser domains are recruited.
- Temporal order explicitly measured: geometry change → nascent transcription change → downstream morphology/physiology.
- Any later chromatin mark changes are recorded as downstream effects, not drivers.

Controls
- Non-targeting MNPs; gRNA-scrambled loci; field‑off sham; promoter‑only or enhancer‑only tagging; proximity sufficiency via LADL without fields; CRISPR‑GO tethering to nuclear speckles/lamina as an alternative geometry perturbation without mechanical force. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6239909/?utm_source=openai))
- Phototoxicity/field controls: identical illumination/field protocols in cells lacking handles.

Readouts and analyses
- Live 3D distances and contact dwell-time distributions (CRISPR imaging).
- Nascent and mature BDNF RNA (MS2/live; intron/exon smFISH; RT‑qPCR).
- Protein output (BDNF ELISA).
- Phenotypes (morphology, synaptic markers, calcium imaging).
- Statistics: mixed‑effects models linking distance metrics to bursting and phenotype; Granger causality to verify geometry-first directionality.

Risk mitigation and alternatives
- If endogenous targeting yields insufficient force coupling, introduce a small operator array (e.g., 256x gRNA landing pads) by HDR near the enhancer to amplify handle valency while preserving local sequence function.
- If neuronal readouts prove variable, replicate in epithelial keratinocytes with an identity enhancer–promoter pair (e.g., KRT locus) and quantify cytoskeletal/adhesion phenotypes.

Expected outcomes and impact
- A calibrated, quantitative demonstration that defined increases in enhancer–promoter separation acutely and reversibly reduce transcriptional bursts and propagate to neuronal structure/function—without relying on DNA methylation or histone modifications.
- A generalizable paradigm: use exogenous mechanics to enforce correct gene‑regulatory geometry and to block lineage‑inappropriate enhancer contacts, offering a clean causal tool distinct from enzymatic epigenetics. ([institut-curie.org](https://institut-curie.org/publications/live-cell-micromanipulation-genomic-locus-reveals-interphase-chromatin-mechanics))

Future extension (optional)
- Replace field-based control with rigid, reversible DNA‑origami “struts” delivered to the nucleus to serve as passive mechanical insulators once geometric operating points are known; recent work shows nuclear delivery of functional DNA nanodevices is feasible. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11225781/?utm_source=openai))

Timeline and feasibility
- Months 0–6: handle design/validation; force–distance calibration.
- Months 6–12: Aim 2 threshold mapping under activity.
- Months 12–18: Aim 3 phenotype and identity‑locking challenge.

Title
Programmable chromatin origami with combinatorial AND-gated bridges to causally control gene expression in epithelial cells and neurons

Summary
Goal: Establish a mark-independent, programmable method to control gene expression by rewiring 3D chromatin architecture with engineered, geometry-defined protein bridges. We build a “local-rule” grammar using orthogonal protein–protein interfaces (PPIs) fused to zinc-finger DNA-binding domains (DBDs) to specify multi-point enhancer–promoter contacts, and require coincident occupancy at multiple genomic addresses (AND-gating) to ensure specificity. We test causal links: engineered 3D change → transcriptional change → cell phenotype, in human epithelial cells and iPSC-derived neurons. This sidesteps endogenous chromatin modifiers and frames regulation as mesoscale mechanics rather than epigenetic editing. Prior looping tools (CLOuD9, LADL, OptoLoop) demonstrate that forced proximity can modulate transcription, but they typically use one bridging chemistry and two-site tethers; multi-contact, rule-based folding with intrinsic combinatorial gating has not been established in living cells. We address that gap. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/ncomms15993?utm_source=openai))

Prior work and gap
- Genome topology emerges from loop extrusion by cohesin and boundary insulation by CTCF, which shapes TADs and modulates enhancer–promoter encounter probabilities. However, the field lacks a general, programmable way to impose synthetic multi-contact topologies at chosen loci with built-in specificity logic. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-020-2151-x?utm_source=openai))
- Forced looping has been achieved by tethering natural loop factors (e.g., LDB1 at β-globin) and by dCas9-based inducible bridges (CLOuD9, LADL/OptoLoop), establishing feasibility of proximity-driven expression control. Yet these systems do not provide a modular “staple” grammar to compose multiple contacts or require multi-site coincidence to stabilize loops. A recent bioorthogonal click approach (BPCL) forms multiway contacts chemically, underscoring the opportunity to realize multi-contact logic with protein interfaces and DNA-protein addressability. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5737898/?utm_source=openai))

Central question (hypothesis and goal merged)
Can a minimal set of orthogonal, geometry-defined protein “staples,” each targeted by compact ZF-DBDs, and assembled only upon coincident multi-site occupancy (AND-gating), re-route enhancer traffic to a selected promoter and produce predictable, reversible changes in burst kinetics and cell phenotype without invoking DNA methylation or histone modifications as the primary mechanism? ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11058250/?utm_source=openai))

Atomic strategy
Translate DNA-origami-style local rules into chromatin folding by:
- Address layer: ZF-DBDs specify genomic “staple landing pads.”
- Interaction layer: pairs/sets of orthogonal coiled-coil PPIs (e.g., SYNZIP families) encode which addresses bind each other.
- Specificity layer: split, low-affinity subinterfaces that only assemble into a high-avidity bridge when all programmed sites are occupied (logical AND), stabilizing the intended multi-point contact and suppressing off-target loops. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3339576/?utm_source=openai))

Specific Aims

Aim 1. Build and validate an AND-gated, two-to-three point chromatin bridge that increases enhancer–promoter contact dwell time and burst frequency.
- Design: Construct ZF–PPI fusions targeting one promoter-proximal site (P) and two enhancer sites (E1/E2) within a well-characterized reporter safe harbor (e.g., AAVS1) engineered with an MS2-tagged gene. Use orthogonal coiled-coil heterodimers (e.g., SYNZIP1:2, 5:6) split into subinterfaces such that P+E1+E2 occupancy is required to complete two concurrent PPIs and lock a P–E1–E2 “triangle.” No effector domains are included. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3339576/?utm_source=openai))
- Readouts: Targeted Micro-C/HiChIP to quantify contact enrichment and 3D geometry; live-cell MS2 imaging and smFISH to extract burst frequency/size; no primary reliance on histone marks (ChIP is used only as a control to confirm absence of systematic changes). ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6300980/?utm_source=openai))
- Controls: (i) single-site occupancy mutants (no assembly); (ii) pairwise-only bridges (P–E1 or P–E2) to test necessity of tri-point avidity; (iii) displacer peptide to transiently disrupt one PPI for reversibility. Positive control: dCas9-based inducible loop (CLOuD9) at the same locus to benchmark effect size. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/ncomms15993?utm_source=openai))
- Success criteria: Step-like increase in P–E contact dwell time; increase in burst frequency >1.5× with minimal change in burst size; negligible global mark changes.

Aim 2. Convert the staple set into a local-rule grammar for multi-contact folding and quantify design–function transfer.
- Design: Expand to four to five “staples” using additional orthogonal coiled-coils to create a corridor that channels chosen enhancers to the promoter while insulating flanks, composing nested loops/sub-TADs. Layout rules (who-binds-whom) are the only variables; protein components are reused. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10361782/?utm_source=openai))
- Readouts: Capture-C/Micro-C to map intended corridors vs. spurious contacts; MS2 bursting; polymer-model-informed targets for contact probability vs. genomic distance provide quantitative expectations. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-020-2151-x?utm_source=openai))
- Success criteria: Monotonic gain in promoter contact occupancy and burst frequency as correct staples accumulate; ablation of a minimal spanning set collapses the topology and expression.

Aim 3. Deploy to endogenous loci in human epithelial cells and neurons and demonstrate 3D→expression→phenotype causality.
- Target selection: Choose, per cell type, a gene with a validated distal enhancer and measurable phenotype (e.g., barrier integrity for epithelium; excitability metrics for neurons). Select 2–3 addresses per region based on accessibility and absence of coding sequence; install ZF–staples as in Aims 1–2. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41576-019-0128-0?utm_source=openai))
- Readouts: 3D: Capture-C at target locus; Expression: nascent RNA by intronic smFISH; Phenotype: transepithelial electrical resistance (TEER) in epithelial monolayers; multi-electrode array (MEA) firing patterns or calcium imaging in iPSC-derived neurons. Confirm that disrupting one staple acutely reverses both expression and phenotype. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41576-019-0128-0?utm_source=openai))
- Success criteria: Pre-registered thresholds linking engineered 3D gain to burst-frequency increase and to phenotype shift; replication across both cell types.

Key design choices and justifications
- Orthogonal PPIs (SYNZIP toolbox) provide a scalable, addressable interaction alphabet with known geometries and low cross-talk, enabling multi-staple compositions without recruiting endogenous epigenetic modifiers. Splitting interfaces across addresses converts contact formation into a logical AND gate that suppresses off-target loops by requiring coincident occupancy. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3339576/?utm_source=openai))
- Reporter bursting as a primary functional metric is motivated by evidence that enhancer–promoter communication predominantly modulates burst frequency; causal manipulations of proximity therefore should primarily shift frequency, not size. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11058250/?utm_source=openai))
- Optional distance/orientation tuning: in a subset of constructs, insert de novo designed helical repeat (DHR) “rods” between ZF and PPI to test whether rigid nanoscale geometry further increases contact dwell time and effect size. DHRs offer length- and rigidity-tunable, genetically encodable rods validated structurally and mechanically. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/4845728/?utm_source=openai))

Milestones and quantitative endpoints
- M1 (months 0–9): AND-gated 3-point bridge increases P–E contact dwell time ≥2× and burst frequency ≥1.5× in AAVS1 reporter; reversible by PPI displacer. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/ncomms15993?utm_source=openai))
- M2 (months 9–18): Multi-staple grammar yields additive/nested contact patterns matching design; Micro-C shows intended sub-TAD-like insulation; expression scales with number of correct staples. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-020-2151-x?utm_source=openai))
- M3 (months 18–30): Endogenous deployment meets pre-registered 3D→expression→phenotype thresholds in epithelial cells and neurons; acute disruption reverses effects within 24–48 h.

Validation of constraint compliance
- No catalytic epigenetic readers/writers are used; bridges are inert scaffolds. We will profile H3K27ac/H3K9me3 at target loci to confirm no systematic mark rewriting is required for the effect. Prior forced-loop studies (LDB1 tethering; CLOuD9; LADL) show proximity alone can modulate transcription, supporting our mark-independent premise. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5737898/?utm_source=openai))

Risk assessment and mitigation
- Risk: Some genes show weak correspondence between proximity and transcription (e.g., Sox2). Mitigation: pre-screen loci with CRISPRi/CRISPRa and Capture-C to confirm enhancer dependency; use multi-point staples to increase dwell time beyond transient “hit-and-run” contacts. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/6534382/?utm_source=openai))
- Risk: Multisite targeting could still produce off-target bridges. Mitigation: choose ZF arrays with high-specificity motifs; AND-gating requires all addresses, dramatically reducing spurious assembly. Use orthogonality maps from SYNZIP sets to avoid cross-pairing. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3339576/?utm_source=openai))
- Risk: Mechanical strain or steric clash reduces efficacy. Mitigation: optional DHR linkers to tune spacing/orientation; iterate geometry based on Micro-C contact enrichment vs. predicted polymer distances. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/4845728/?utm_source=openai))

Experimental methods (selected)
- Protein modules: ZF-DBDs (16–18 bp recognition) fused via flexible or DHR linkers to split coiled-coils (SYNZIP1/2, 5/6, 3/4). Subinterfaces are designed to be weak alone and high-avidity in trans only when both enhancer and promoter addresses are occupied. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3339576/?utm_source=openai))
- Genomic targeting: Lentiviral or CRISPR-mediated integration of ZF–PPI cassettes; gBlocks for ZF arrays; safe-harbor reporter with MS2 cassette and two validated distal enhancers.
- 3D assays: Capture-C/Micro-C; live two-color labeling of E and P for distance distributions and dwell times. ([tandfonline.com](https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/19491034.2020.1782024?utm_source=openai))
- Transcription assays: MS2 live imaging; smFISH; RNA-seq for off-target expression surveillance. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6300980/?utm_source=openai))
- Phenotypes: TEER for epithelia; MEA and GCaMP imaging for neurons.

Expected outcomes and impact
- A generalizable, modular toolkit for causal control of gene expression through programmable, multi-contact chromatin topology, independent of histone/DNA methylation.
- A design grammar—akin to DNA origami staples but implemented with protein interfaces—linking local rules to predictable mesoscale folding and function.
- A validated pipeline for moving from 3D contact engineering to quantitative changes in bursting and cellular behavior in clinically relevant cell types. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9457169/?utm_source=openai))

References (selected)
- Genome organization and enhancer–promoter communication: Nature 2020; Nat Rev Genet 2019. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-020-2151-x?utm_source=openai))
- Forced looping precedents: LDB1 tethering; CLOuD9; LADL/OptoLoop; BPCL chemical multiway contacts. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4134511/?utm_source=openai))
- Orthogonal PPIs and designed geometry: SYNZIP toolbox; de novo DHR rods. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3339576/?utm_source=openai))
- Bursting linkage to proximity: reviews and live-imaging studies. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11058250/?utm_source=openai))

text:
Title
Pinpoint-assembled transcription factories for locus-specific control of gene expression via covalently seeded, reversible mesoscale scaffolds

Hypothesis and goal
A covalently “pinned” nucleation hub at an endogenous promoter can seed a reversible, multivalent polymer shell that shortens local chromatin path length and concentrates core transcription machinery within ~100 nm, thereby increasing transcriptional burst frequency and mRNA output without relying on DNA methylation or histone modifications; dissolving the shell reverses the effect. The goal is to demonstrate a sequential causal chain—3D architectural change → target gene expression change → epithelial phenotype—at the endogenous CFTR locus in human airway epithelial cells.

Atomic strategy
Separate spatial memory from functional mass: use SpyCatcher–SpyTag covalent chemistry to fix a small geometric hub at the chosen DNA site (spatial memory), while allowing a noncovalent, signal-reversible polymer scaffold (functional mass) to assemble only around that hub. This scaffold provides multivalency and confinement to recruit Pol II/Mediator through IDR-dependent partitioning, not through chromatin mark deposition. Prior art shows: (i) locus-tethered condensates/LLPS can reconfigure contacts and modulate transcription (CasDrop, LAMPS), (ii) dCas9-mediated forced loops can regulate genes, and (iii) SpyTag/Catcher can recruit effectors to dCas9, but covalently pinned, geometry-coded, reversible “factories” at endogenous loci remain underexplored. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6724728/?utm_source=openai))

System design (PinFactory)
- Seed/hub (memory): dCas9-SpyCatcher targeted with 3–6 sgRNAs across a promoter-proximal window (−500 to +200 bp) and one nearby enhancer, to create multiple docking points. A trimeric coiled-coil “hub” bearing SpyTag ligates to each dCas9-SpyCatcher, fixing a nanoscale geometry with three orthogonal faces (valence = 3) for polymer initiation. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10783489/?utm_source=openai))
- Polymer shell (functional mass): a soluble monomer carries (i) a head-to-tail, moderate-affinity coiled-coil interface for isodesmic, reversible polymerization only upon nucleation, and (ii) a synthetic low-complexity recruitment module (LC-Module; tyrosine/acidic-rich IDR lacking chromatin-binding domains) that partitions Pol II/Mediator by weak, multivalent interactions. Choice of LC-Module is guided by evidence that Pol II CTD, Mediator IDRs, and diverse TF activation domains partition into condensates and enrich initiation factors. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41594-018-0112-y?utm_source=openai))
- Reversible control: monomers include a rapidly inducible degron (AID or dTAG) and a protease-cleavable “breakpoint” in the polymer–polymer interface; auxin/dTAG triggers scaffold dissolution without changing chromatin marks, allowing on/off cycles. 
- Safeguards: no histone/DNA modifying enzymes are tethered. Tests will verify that activation persists when HAT/BRD inhibitors are applied, arguing primary action is architectural/kinetic rather than epigenetic.

Model system and phenotype readout
- Cells: primary human bronchial epithelial cells (HBECs) or 16HBE14o− monolayers at air–liquid interface.
- Gene: endogenous CFTR.
- Phenotype: CFTR function by Ussing chamber short-circuit current (Isc) with forskolin stimulation and CFTRinh-172 inhibition as ground truth. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8836180/?utm_source=openai))

Specific aims and experiments

Aim 1. Build and validate PinFactory assembly and reversibility at an endogenous locus.
- A1.1. Genomic targeting and seeding. Deliver dCas9-SpyCatcher (lentiviral, EF1α) and sgRNA arrays tiling CFTR TSS and a validated proximal enhancer. Express SpyTag–trimeric hub (DOX-inducible). Confirm covalent hub capture by proximity ligation and ChIP for the Spy epitope.
- A1.2. Polymer growth confined to seed. Express polymer monomers (DOX). Readouts: (i) appearance of a diffraction-limited focus at CFTR (CRISPR live-FISH), (ii) fluorescence recovery (FRAP) consistent with reversible polymer dynamics, (iii) increased local concentration and residence time of Halo-tagged Pol II near CFTR by single-particle tracking. LLPS/partitioning rationale is supported by Pol II CTD and Mediator IDR behaviors. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41594-018-0112-y?utm_source=openai))
- A1.3. Reversibility. Induce auxin or dTAG to degrade monomers or express TEV to cleave the polymer interface, and confirm focus dissolution, loss of local Pol II enrichment, and return to baseline chromatin distances.

Milestones: >70% of CFTR alleles show seeded foci; Pol II dwell time near CFTR increases ≥2-fold; assembly/disassembly half-times <60 min.

Aim 2. Demonstrate causality: 3D architectural change → transcriptional bursting → mRNA/protein → CFTR function.
- A2.1. 3D architecture. Quantify enhancer–promoter distances and contact frequency by live imaging and targeted 5C/HiChIP (Pol II) with and without assembly; benchmark against forced looping systems (CLOuD9/LADL literature) but without long-range CID. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/ncomms15993?utm_source=openai))
- A2.2. Transcription kinetics. Insert 24×MS2 into the 3′ UTR of endogenous CFTR by HDR (if feasible) or use intronic smFISH to extract burst frequency and size. Expect increased burst frequency upon assembly, returning to baseline upon disassembly. Locus-tethered condensate systems (CasDrop/LAMPS) support this directionality. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6724728/?utm_source=openai))
- A2.3. mRNA and protein. RT-qPCR and targeted proteomics for CFTR. Surface biotinylation to quantify membrane CFTR.
- A2.4. Phenotype. Measure Isc in Ussing chambers under forskolin ± CFTRinh-172. Expect ≥25–50% increase in CFTR-dependent current upon assembly; reversal upon disassembly. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8836180/?utm_source=openai))

Aim 3. Exclude epigenetic primary mechanisms; test robustness across stimuli.
- A3.1. Epigenetic independence. CUT&RUN/CUT&Tag for H3K27ac/H3K4me3 and WGBS at CFTR before/after assembly. Expect no early (≤6 h) increase preceding transcriptional upregulation. Maintain activation under HAT (A-485) or BRD4 (JQ1) inhibition to the extent compatible with basal transcription, indicating the primary driver is architectural/kinetic, not histone acetylation.
- A3.2. Orthogonality. Confirm no genome-wide spread by RNA-seq; off-targets limited to sgRNA-bound sites.
- A3.3. Dissociation of loop versus factory effects. Compare to CLOuD9-like enhancer–promoter dimerization without polymer shell; expect smaller effects, isolating the contribution of the local factory. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/ncomms15993?utm_source=openai))

Controls and falsification
- Non-seeding controls: monomer ± hub without dCas9-SpyCatcher; dCas9-SpyCatcher with scrambled sgRNAs.
- Recruitment-null monomer: polymerization-competent but lacking LC-Module tests whether geometry alone suffices; reduced effect would support a recruitment component.
- Positive control: light-activated LAMPS or CasDrop at CFTR to benchmark achievable Pol II enrichment and transcriptional changes. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10065442/?utm_source=openai))
- Falsification: If 3D changes occur (contacts shorten) without transcriptional or phenotypic effects, the hypothesis fails; the system then acts as a geometrical tether only. If transcriptional changes occur without measurable 3D changes, revise the model toward kinetic partitioning as the dominant driver.

Readouts linking steps
- 3D change: live distance measurements; 5C/HiChIP (Pol II).
- Machinery concentration: Pol II/Mediator ChIP and single-molecule dwell times.
- Bursting: MS2 live imaging or smFISH burst inference.
- Output: CFTR mRNA/protein; Isc traces with CFTRinh-172 blockade. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8836180/?utm_source=openai))

Expected outcomes and interpretation
- Assembly increases local Pol II/Mediator occupancy and enhancer–promoter synapse dwell time, raising burst frequency and CFTR output; disassembly reverses all steps. This aligns with condensate-based enrichment of transcription apparatus at active loci while remaining distinct from relocating DNA to pre-existing nuclear bodies (CRISPR-GO) or using global optogenetic LLPS not covalently pinned (CasDrop/LAMPS). ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6239909/?utm_source=openai))

Feasibility and novelty
- Feasibility rests on three established pillars combined in a new way: (i) locus-tethered condensates/LLPS alter contacts and transcription, (ii) CRISPR-mediated looping changes gene expression, and (iii) SpyTag/SpyCatcher supports robust, modular dCas9-linked recruitment. The novelty is the covalently pinned, geometry-coded, yet reversible polymer “factory” at an endogenous locus to drive architectural and kinetic control without primary reliance on chromatin mark editing. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6724728/?utm_source=openai))

Milestones and timeline
- Months 0–6: Construct validation; in-cell seeding and confined polymer growth; reversibility tuning.
- Months 6–12: 3D metrics and live Pol II tracking; transcriptional bursting assays.
- Months 12–18: mRNA/protein and Ussing chamber phenotyping; epigenetic independence tests; comparative benchmarking to CLOuD9/CasDrop/LAMPS. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/ncomms15993?utm_source=openai))

Impact
If successful, PinFactory establishes that directly rewriting local chromatin mesoscale architecture via a covalently anchored, reversible scaffold is sufficient to control endogenous gene output and epithelial function, without invoking DNA methylation or histone modification as the primary driver. This provides a generalizable, orthogonal route to program gene expression in epithelial and neuronal systems.
