text:
Title
Circulation-licensed, engagement-triggered mobilization and killing of AML leukemia stem cells to restore graft-versus-leukemia under non-genotoxic conditioning

Central hypothesis and research goal
Hypothesis: If LSCs are compelled to exit marrow retention and enter normoxic circulation upon target recognition, and if engineered allogeneic effectors are licensed to execute cytotoxicity only in circulation while simultaneously neutralizing checkpoint and anti-phagocytic shields, then relapse after RIC/NMA allo-HSCT can be reduced to MAC-like or lower rates without non-selective genotoxic conditioning. Goal: Develop and test an LSC-selective, compartmentalized immunotherapy that restores early, potent GVL after busulfan/TBI-free conditioning. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1083879111000243?utm_source=openai))

Atomic strategy
Invert the niche advantage: use LSC‑antigen recognition to locally convert adhesion/chemokine retention (CXCR4–CXCL12, VLA‑4–VCAM‑1, E‑selectin) into transient dispersal, then gate effector kill by a normoxia-only license so execution occurs in blood, not in hypoxic marrow or parenchyma. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7168055/?utm_source=openai))

Platform overview
- Effector: third‑party allogeneic CAR‑NK cells to minimize GVHD risk and enable off‑the‑shelf deployment; CAR targets an LSC‑preferential antigen (primary: CLEC12A/CLL‑1; alternative: CD123 with HSC-sparing controls). ([ashpublications.org](https://ashpublications.org/blood/article/141/8/856/493324/Allogeneic-natural-killer-cell-therapy?utm_source=openai))
- Recognition‑triggered egress: CAR signal drives local, short‑lived antagonism of CXCR4/VLA‑4/E‑selectin, mobilizing LSCs from BM niche to blood. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3350358/?utm_source=openai))
- Circulation‑licensed cytotoxicity: an oxygen‑sensing OFF‑switch accumulates under hypoxia to suppress NK degranulation; the inhibitor is degraded in normoxia, restoring killing in blood. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8080111/?utm_source=openai))
- On‑engagement, local immune‑evasion countermeasures: transient, activation‑induced secretion/tethering of PD‑L1 blocking scFv and SIRPα‑Fc decoy to overcome checkpoint upregulation and CD47 “don’t‑eat‑me” signaling at the blood interface. ([jci.org](https://www.jci.org/articles/view/129204?utm_source=openai))
- Conditioning: busulfan/TBI‑free donor‑engraftment using CD117 (c‑Kit) antibody (JSP191)–based regimens ± serotherapy, avoiding non‑selective genotoxic cytoreduction; preserves normal HSC engraftment capacity. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41591-025-03817-1?utm_source=openai))

Specific aims and methods
Aim 1. Build an LSC-recognition-triggered egress module and quantify mobilization kinetics.
- Design: CAR‑NK specific for CLEC12A (or CD123 in backup cohorts) with an activation-responsive promoter (NK‑validated NF‑κB/NFAT composite) driving: (a) a membrane-tethered CXCR4 antagonist microdomain and (b) secretion of short‑half‑life VLA‑4 and E‑selectin antagonists (peptidomimetics or scFvs), restricted by signal peptides ensuring perisynaptic release. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8595471/?utm_source=openai))
- Models: human AML LSC‑enriched samples in 3D humanized BM‑on‑a‑chip (endosteal+vascular niches; 1%–3% O2 zones) and NSG xenografts. Endpoints: (i) fraction of CLEC12A+CD34+CD38low cells displaced to blood compartment; (ii) time‑to‑peak LSC mobilization (AUC, tmax) with/without each antagonist; (iii) HSC homing/engraftment impact using normal CD34+CD38− cells. Benchmarks: plerixafor and uproleselan positive controls. Safety: reversal of mobilization within 24–48 h after effector removal. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8269413/?utm_source=openai))

Aim 2. Engineer and validate circulation‑licensed killing with local checkpoint/CD47 neutralization.
- Design: hypoxia‑OFF cytotoxicity. An intracellular inhibitory binder (“intrabody” or bioPROTAC) targeting a rate‑limiting NK cytotoxic effector (e.g., perforin/ZAP70 homologous signaling node) is fused to the HIF‑1α oxygen‑dependent degradation domain (ODD). Under hypoxia, the inhibitor accumulates and suppresses degranulation; in normoxia, ODD drives proteasomal degradation of the inhibitor, restoring killing. CAR activation simultaneously induces brief secretion or membrane‑tethering of PD‑L1 scFv and SIRPα‑Fc decoy to neutralize adaptive PD‑L1 upregulation and CD47 signaling at the kill site. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8080111/?utm_source=openai))
- Assays: oxygen‑clamped co‑cultures (1% vs 21% O2) with primary AML (including IFN‑γ–induced PD‑L1high) and HLA‑loss relapse samples; measure degranulation (CD107a), cytotoxicity, and macrophage phagocytosis with/without SIRPα‑Fc. Success criteria: ≥5‑fold cytotoxicity delta (normoxia/hypoxia), ≥2‑fold increase in macrophage phagocytosis with SIRPα‑Fc, and no killing of HSCs under hypoxia. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7412746/?utm_source=openai))

Aim 3. Integrate with non‑genotoxic allo‑HSCT and test relapse control against RIC/MAC benchmarks.
- Conditioning: JSP191‑based antibody conditioning (± limited serotherapy) to enable donor engraftment while avoiding busulfan/TBI. Primary readouts: donor myeloid chimerism and CD34+ engraftment kinetics; secondary: infection/GVHD profiles. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41591-025-03817-1?utm_source=openai))
- Treatment schedule: Day −1 to 0, first CAR‑NK dose to pre‑position in marrow; post‑HSCT Day +3 to +10, repeat short‑lived CAR‑NK pulses to front‑load GVL during aplasia. Rationale: RIC/NMA relies on GVL and has higher relapse risk; early, circulation‑licensed killing compensates for reduced cytoreduction without GVHD escalation typical of broad T‑cell activation. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1083879111000243?utm_source=openai))
- In vivo endpoints (humanized xenograft with co‑infused donor HSCs): (i) MRD negativity in marrow and blood; (ii) leukemia‑free survival; (iii) GVHD scores; (iv) marrow histology for HSC niche preservation. Target: relapse incidence non‑inferior to MAC historical controls with superior non‑relapse toxicity profile. ([astctjournal.org](https://www.astctjournal.org/article/S1083-8791%2818%2930569-X/fulltext?utm_source=openai))

Key design choices grounded in evidence
- Niche retention as targetable vulnerability: AML LSCs exploit CXCR4–CXCL12, VLA‑4–VCAM‑1, and E‑selectin to persist; pharmacologic antagonists mobilize blasts and sensitize to therapy while sparing HSCs when dosed transiently. This validates a mobilize‑then‑treat paradigm to dismantle sanctuary effects. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3350358/?utm_source=openai))
- Checkpoint and anti‑phagocytic shields are rapidly induced/adaptive in AML; local, engagement‑triggered PD‑L1 blockade and SIRPα‑Fc phagocytosis checkpoint disruption have preclinical/early clinical support against AML LSCs. ([jci.org](https://www.jci.org/articles/view/129204?utm_source=openai))
- Hypoxia‑sensing modules are clinically matured but typically “hypoxia‑ON”; inverting by stabilizing an inhibitor under hypoxia exploits the same ODD/VHL axis to create “hypoxia‑OFF” cytotoxicity, confining execution to normoxic blood. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8080111/?utm_source=openai))
- Allogeneic CAR‑NKs show favorable safety with minimal GVHD/CRS in trials, supporting their use to augment early GVL after RIC/NMA. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41591-023-02785-8?utm_source=openai))
- LSC antigens: CLEC12A is absent on normal CD34+CD38− HSCs; CD123 is enriched on LSCs but present on subsets of progenitors, justifying CLEC12A as primary target and CD123 as back‑up with tighter safety controls. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5867061/?utm_source=openai))

Experimental details and controls
- Payload localization and half‑life: use signal peptide + transmembrane tethers or scFv–GPI anchors for perisynaptic display; for secreted forms, use PEST/ubiquitin‑fused destabilization to achieve t1/2 <2 h; quantify diffusion radius in microfluidic flow to ensure minimal bystander HSC exposure. Benchmarks: synNotch/TRUCK‑style inducible payload delivery kinetics in T/NK cells. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0092867416312442?utm_source=openai))
- Egress quantification: multiphoton intravital microscopy of calvarial marrow to track labeled LSCs; pharmacodynamic success defined by ≥2× increase in circulating CLEC12A+ LSCs and ≥50% reduction of endosteal LSC dwell time compared with vehicle. Positive controls: plerixafor and uproleselan. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3350358/?utm_source=openai))
- Functional evasion assays: induce PD‑L1 (IFN‑γ) and test HLA‑loss AML relapse samples; measure restored cytotoxicity with local PD‑L1 scFv and enhanced macrophage uptake with SIRPα‑Fc. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7412746/?utm_source=openai))
- Hematopoietic safety: co‑culture with normal CD34+CD38− HSCs under hypoxia; require no excess apoptosis or degranulation signal versus untransduced NK; in xenografts, require preserved donor HSC engraftment and lineage output. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8269413/?utm_source=openai))

Anticipated risks and mitigations
- Antigen heterogeneity/escape: dual‑target CAR (CLEC12A±CD123) with OR‑gate and synNotch‑triggered bispecific NK/T‑engagers to broaden coverage. Go/no‑go: <70% MRD conversion triggers addition of second target. ([frontiersin.org](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/immunology/articles/10.3389/fimmu.2022.1085978/full?utm_source=openai))
- Off‑target mobilization (HSC egress): strict activation‑dependence for antagonist release, short half‑life, and dosing windows aligned to donor HSC infusion; abort criterion if >15% reduction in donor HSC marrow lodgment. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3350358/?utm_source=openai))
- Hypoxia‑OFF leakage: calibrate ODD‑inhibitor expression to minimize normoxic residual; validate dynamic range using HypoxiCAR benchmarks; add small‑molecule iCasp9 safety switch. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8080111/?utm_source=openai))
- Systemic inflammation: NK platform reduces CRS/ICANS risk; restrict checkpoint/CD47 payload to activation windows and tethered formats to avoid systemic immune disinhibition. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41591-023-02785-8?utm_source=openai))

Milestones and success criteria
- Year 1: Demonstrate ≥2× LSC mobilization without impairing HSC homing in BM‑on‑a‑chip and NSG; confirm normoxia‑licensed killing with ≥5× normoxia/hypoxia cytotoxicity ratio and checkpoint/CD47 countermeasures restoring kill of PD‑L1high and HLA‑loss AML. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11017789/?utm_source=openai))
- Year 2: Establish busulfan/TBI‑free JSP191‑based engraftment with early post‑HSCT CAR‑NK pulses achieving MRD negativity in ≥70% of xenografts and improved LFS versus RIC‑only controls, with no GVHD signal. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41591-025-03817-1?utm_source=openai))
- Year 3: IND‑enabling package: biodistribution, shedding, off‑target panel, and GMP feasibility for an off‑the‑shelf CAR‑NK incorporating the hypoxia‑OFF module and activation‑induced, tethered PD‑L1/SIRPα‑Fc payloads.

Why this should meet the clinical bar
- Compensates for RIC/NMA’s reduced cytoreduction by delivering immediate, early GVL in a safe compartment (blood) while stripping niche protection, a combination that historically improved chemosensitivity when done pharmacologically (plerixafor/upro) but not yet coupled to compartment‑restricted cellular cytotoxicity. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3350358/?utm_source=openai))
- Addresses multi‑axis immune evasion (HLA loss, PD‑L1 upregulation, CD47) at the instant of kill, where local blockade is most efficient and least toxic. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6650729/?utm_source=openai))
- Preserves engraftment by avoiding busulfan/TBI and by suppressing cytotoxicity within hypoxic marrow, protecting normal HSCs. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41591-025-03817-1?utm_source=openai))

Deliverable
A busulfan/TBI‑free allo‑HSCT adjunct that compels LSCs into a circulation “kill zone,” where allogeneic CAR‑NKs, environmentally licensed and locally disinhibited, deliver precise GVL without GVHD.

Title
Time-Stamped Poly(A) Tagging (TiSPAT): sequential, orthogonally photoactivated barcodes covalently written onto native mRNAs in the same live cell for single end-point, transcriptome-wide trajectory readout

Integrated hypothesis–goal
A cell’s evolving transcriptome can be captured at seven or more defined times (30 min to 24 h after a perturbation) in the very same live cell by repeatedly and selectively “writing” orthogonal molecular time-stamps onto the poly(A) tails of whatever mRNAs exist at each time. If these time-stamps are covalently attached at low occupancy and remain inert thereafter, a single end-point sequencing of each cell will decode its full, multi-timepoint trajectory with statistical power across many cells.

Atomic strategy
Invert repeated destructive sampling by converting ephemeral abundance at time ti into a durable, intracellular molecular memory: at each ti, uncage only the Ti probe so it hybridizes to poly(A) and becomes covalently crosslinked to nearby RNA, thereby appending a unique time barcode to the subset of mRNAs present at that moment. Repeat ≥7 times. At the end, lyse once, sequence once, and reconstruct per-cell trajectories from the barcode composition of each gene’s reads.

Specific aims
1) Chemistry and optics: Build a 7-color, orthogonally uncageable, low-occupancy oligo(dT)-barcode probe set bearing photo-crosslinkers that react in RNA–DNA heteroduplexes in live cells.
2) Single-cell longitudinal recording: Demonstrate ≥7 log-spaced time-stamps (0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 24 h) in the same viable cell after a defined perturbation, and recover per-cell, per-gene trajectories from one end-point library.
3) Validation and scale: Benchmark TiSPAT trajectories against gold-standard destructive time courses, quantify distortion/perturbation bounds, and scale to thousands of cells for heterogeneity analysis.

Rationale and feasibility
- Live-cell, light-gated oligonucleotides have been delivered and activated inside single cells and intact tissues to bind endogenous mRNA (TIVA probes), establishing the feasibility of intracellular caged capture strands and 405-nm activation in viable cells. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4586300/?utm_source=openai))
- Orthogonal photocages enable sequential, wavelength-selective uncaging in cells (e.g., DEACM vs nitroveratryl; multi-level uncaging from 505→440→365→313 nm), supporting 7-timepoint scheduling without cross-activation. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6499933/?utm_source=openai))
- Photo-crosslinkers such as diazirines and benzophenones form covalent adducts upon UV/near-UV activation and have been used on nucleic-acid probes and in RNA–DNA heteroduplex contexts, enabling stable capture of the hybridized poly(A) segment. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8341421/?utm_source=openai))
- Sequential optical control of RNAs in single cells with distinct wavelengths has been demonstrated, supporting time-sliced activation in live cells. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32484653/?utm_source=openai))
- This approach is mechanistically distinct from ADAR-based RNA “timestamps,” which require engineered reporter transcripts and do not time-stamp the native, full transcriptome. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7956158/?utm_source=openai))

Experimental plan

Aim 1. Chemistry and optics
1.1 Probe architecture
- Seven probes Pi (i=1..7), each comprises: 12–15 nt 2′-OMe/LNA oligo(dT) capture core; unique 12–16 nt time barcode Ti; a photocage specific to λi that masks hybridization (e.g., DEACM, NV, NPP, NDBF, thio-DEACM, coumarin variants); and 2–4 diazirine/benzophenone moieties along the backbone to crosslink upon 355–365 nm pulses. Low occupancy is enforced by sub-nanomolar intracellular free concentration and short illumination windows to avoid translation/decay perturbation at poly(A). ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24111849/?utm_source=openai))
- Probes are rendered cell-permeant via reversible masking (e.g., cleavable, bioreducible masking of phosphates) or by endocytosis with gentle carriers; all probes are preloaded at t<0.

1.2 Uncaging and crosslinking schedule
- At each timepoint ti: Step A, illuminate at λi (e.g., 640, 594, 561, 514, 488, 445, 405 nm; order chosen to minimize spectral bleed) for 5–15 s to remove the photocage from Pi, allowing annealing to poly(A). Step B, deliver a brief global 355–365 nm pulse (0.5–2 s, minimal dose) to activate diazirine/benzophenone and covalently fix Pi onto the poly(A)–oligo(dT) heteroduplex. Non-uncaged probes cannot anneal and thus are not crosslinked during Step B. Repeat across ≥7 log-spaced times. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32484653/?utm_source=openai))
- Illumination is widefield to process thousands of cells in parallel; power and duty cycle are tuned to remain within viability windows established by prior live-cell, light-controlled oligo methods. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4586300/?utm_source=openai))

Controls and characterization
- In vitro RNA–DNA duplex crosslink yield vs pulse energy; sequence bias assessment using synthetic poly(A) standards with controlled A-content and spike-in RNAs. ([academic.oup.com](https://academic.oup.com/chemlett/article/doi/10.1093/chemle/upae152/7739877?utm_source=openai))
- Cross-activation matrix: quantify unintended uncaging at off-wavelengths; accept ≤1% cross-talk per step. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24111849/?utm_source=openai))
- Phototoxicity bounds: viability, ROS, and transcriptional stress markers after 7 cycles; accept ≥90% viability and ≤10% stress-response induction by bulk RNA-seq relative to dark controls. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4586300/?utm_source=openai))

Aim 2. Single-cell longitudinal recording
2.1 Biological system and perturbations
- Use adherent mammalian cells with well-characterized transcriptional responses (e.g., serum refeeding, cytokine stimulation, or a small-molecule inhibitor) at t=0. Record at 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 24 h.

2.2 End-point library design
- At 24 h, lyse once. Use a 3′-capture library where Read 1 identifies the gene and poly(A) junction; Read 2 reads the covalently attached time-barcode cassette Ti. Because crosslinkers can block RT, incorporate short reverse-transcription conditions with strand-displacing polymerase and adapter designs that traverse the barcode flank; include a chemical deprotection step if needed to bypass adducts, as in Chem-CLIP-derived workflows. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2666166724004362?utm_source=openai))
- Demultiplex per cell (cell barcode) and per time (Ti) to produce a count matrix: gene × time for each single cell.

2.3 Quantitative criteria
- Per timepoint, detect ≥1,000 genes at UMI ≥1 in ≥80% of cells; per gene, coefficient of variation across technical replicates ≤0.3; cross-time leakage of barcodes ≤2%.

2.4 Same-cell verification
- Spike-in a minority of cells preloaded with a distinct, cell-identity barcode probe that is not time-gated; verify that all Ti for a given well co-occur only with that cell-ID barcode, excluding cross-cell contamination.

Aim 3. Validation and scale
3.1 Benchmarking against destructive gold standards
- Split replicate cultures: run TiSPAT in one, and perform conventional bulk/scRNA-seq at each time in the other. Compare per-gene trajectories via dynamic time-warping and impulse-response fits; accept median Pearson r ≥0.7 per gene across time, after deconvolving the expected 3′-bias intrinsic to oligo(dT) capture.

3.2 Bias audits
- Assess 3′ UTR length, poly(A) length, and RNA half-life dependencies of tagging probability; correct with calibration curves and spike-ins to minimize systematic distortion in trajectory inference.

3.3 Throughput and heterogeneity
- Implement micro-patterned wells or microfluidic chambers for thousands of individually addressed cells per run; global illumination enables simultaneous time-stamping of all wells. Analyze inter-cell heterogeneity in response amplitude, timing, and adaptation.

Risk analysis and mitigations
- Phototoxicity from repeated illumination: minimize exposure with high-quantum-yield cages, use far-red cages for early steps, confine UVA to sub-second pulses, and verify transcriptional integrity post-recording. Prior live-tissue TIVA activation supports feasibility of repeated, short 405-nm exposures when doses are constrained. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4586300/?utm_source=openai))
- Cross-activation between cages: choose cages with well-separated action spectra and validate the cross-activation matrix empirically; adjust wavelength order and intensity per step. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24111849/?utm_source=openai))
- Crosslinking efficiency and RT blockage: distribute multiple diazirines/benzophenones to raise yield at low UVA dose; adapt RT and ligation steps to traverse adducts as in photoaffinity/chem-CLIP workflows. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2666166724004362?utm_source=openai))
- Biological perturbation by transient poly(A) occupancy: enforce low occupancy (<5% of each mRNA species per step) and brief hybridization to limit interference with PABP-mediated processes; monitor decay/translation markers to confirm negligible global impact.

Milestones
- M1 (Months 0–6): Synthesize 7 fully orthogonal Pi; validate uncaging selectivity and heteroduplex crosslinking in vitro.
- M2 (Months 6–12): Show 7-step time-stamping and viability in cells; demonstrate end-point recovery of barcodes from ≥1,000 genes/cell.
- M3 (Months 12–18): Benchmark trajectories vs destructive time courses; deploy on ≥2 perturbations; scale to >1,000 cells and quantify heterogeneity.

Outcome and impact
TiSPAT converts dynamic, native mRNA abundance into an intracellular, multi-timepoint molecular ledger, enabling true same-cell transcriptome trajectories from a single end-point readout at scale. It is mechanistically distinct from pseudotime, metabolic labeling, lineage barcoding, few-gene reporters, Live-seq/aspiration, and ADAR-based RNA timestamping, because it time-stamps the endogenous transcriptome in situ via sequential, orthogonal photochemistry and covalent fixation. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4586300/?utm_source=openai))

References (selected feasibility anchors)
- Live-cell caged oligo capture and activation (TIVA). ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4586300/?utm_source=openai))
- Orthogonal wavelength-selective uncaging in cells. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24111849/?utm_source=openai))
- Photo-crosslinkers on nucleic-acid probes and RNA–DNA heteroduplex crosslinking. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8341421/?utm_source=openai))
- Sequential optical control of RNAs with distinct wavelengths. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32484653/?utm_source=openai))
- ADAR “RNA timestamp” labels engineered transcripts, not native transcriptome. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7956158/?utm_source=openai))

Title: ChronoPhase: Same-cell, multi-interval transcriptome recording via age-programmed phase-partition capture with single end-point readout

Hypothesis and goal
- Hypothesis: The kinetics of material aging in an intracellular, phase-separated RNA-capture condensate can encode absolute time into the probability that newly transcribed mRNAs are sequestered during discrete windows. By presetting multiple, log-spaced partition thresholds that are crossed autonomously as the condensate ages, a single mild cue can later convert these time-encoded states into separable molecular records, enabling ≥7 time points from 30 min to 24 h in the same living cell.
- Goal: Build and validate an intracellular capture-and-encode system that (i) continuously samples polyadenylated RNA from the cytosol within defined windows after a perturbation at t=0, (ii) assigns each captured cohort a stable, sequence-readable time index, and (iii) provides either non-destructive staged release or single end-point decoding for transcriptome-wide profiling of individual-cell response trajectories.

Atomic strategy (single conceptual insight)
- Convert time into a sequence of phase-partition boundary crossings. Engineer one condensate whose apparent affinity for mRNA-capture modules shifts in a preprogrammed, monotonic way (by intrinsic linker aging), so that “windows” open and close without external commands. One shared, late cue (e.g., salt/osmolyte shift or light) converts these embedded states into physically or chemically separable cohorts. This relies on established control of condensate assembly/disassembly and release kinetics in cells but applies it to time-encoding rather than delivery. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11582321/?utm_source=openai))

Proposed system
- Component A: Time-programmed capture condensate (TPCC)
  - A cytosolic peptide–nucleic-acid coacervate “bead” (1–3 μm) nucleated by a membrane-anchored scaffold to keep one per cell and reduce cell-to-cell variability.
  - Capture chemistry: multivalent oligo(dT)20–24 conjugated to a weak, reversible RNA-binding scaffold (PABP RRM mutants with reduced competition for translation; low expression) to sample poly(A)+ RNA broadly with limited perturbation.
  - Time encoding: a palette of orthogonal, hydrolysis-prone charge-masking linkers (e.g., thioesters, aryl esters, acetals, carbamates, and redox-labile disulfides) interspersed in the cationic peptide network. Each linker class reduces net positive charge or crosslink density with a characteristic intracellular half-life (t1/2 ≈ 0.5 h to 24 h), shifting the TPCC’s partition coefficient for poly(A)+-bound complexes at preset times.
  - Rationale: Coacervate partitioning and release are steep functions of charge density, crowding, and hydration; programmable peptide coacervates with tunable uptake/release have been demonstrated in mammalian cells. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11582321/?utm_source=openai))
- Component B: Time-index barcodes
  - Each TPCC is preloaded with seven short, sequence-distinct DNA barcodes (B1–B7), each masked by a kinetically distinct protective group that unmasks in the same half-life series used for partition tuning.
  - When a barcode unmasks, it can be ligated to captured mRNAs via splinted ligation using an encapsulated, low-activity ligase that functions only within the condensate microenvironment; result is stable barcode-on-mRNA adducts that survive downstream processing.
- Readout options
  1) Single end-point readout (primary path): At 24 h, gently lyse cells; isolate TPCCs on density/affinity; perform RNA-seq with pull-down of barcode–RNA conjugates to recover seven time-stamped transcriptomes per cell in one library.
  2) Non-destructive staged release (secondary path): Instead of barcoding, encode seven detachment thresholds; apply one mild osmotic/salt cue at 24 h to place the system near the transition. As the aged network crosses thresholds, bound RNPs or vesicle-bound RNA carriers are expelled in seven bursts collected from supernatant; examples of reversible EV capture/release with desthiobiotin/biotin chemistry support staged, gentle harvesting, though here used at collection surfaces ex vivo. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7328786/?utm_source=openai))

Specific aims
- Aim 1: Build and calibrate TPCC materials with log-spaced aging kinetics.
  - Construct a five-chemistry library of cationic peptide scaffolds bearing distinct degradable linkers; form condensates in HEK293 and one primary-cell model.
  - Quantify charge decay and dissolution thresholds in live cells by ratiometric reporters; fit first-order kinetics to select seven linkers giving target half-lives spanning 0.5–24 h.
  - Milestone: Seven distinct inflection times (±15%) for partition shift under physiological conditions.
- Aim 2: Demonstrate time-windowed capture of endogenous poly(A)+ RNA.
  - Express low-level oligo(dT)-RRM capture modules that partition into TPCC only when the local net charge exceeds a threshold; measure capture windows by spike-in RNAs turned on at known times.
  - Validate that captured RNA mirrors whole-transcriptome proportions (allowing sampling noise) and that global translation/viability are minimally perturbed (cell growth, polysome profiling).
  - Milestone: ≥70% of captured reads map to poly(A)+ mRNA; <15% change in global translation rate vs control.
- Aim 3: Encode time indexes and perform single end-point decoding after a perturbation at t=0.
  - At t=0, administer drug/genetic perturbation; TPCC ages autonomously, opening capture windows around 0.5 h, 1 h, 2 h, 4 h, 8 h, 12 h, 24 h.
  - At 24 h, lyse and perform library prep selective for barcode–RNA adducts; demultiplex reads by barcode to recover seven transcriptomes per cell.
  - Compare reconstructed trajectories to RNA timestamping (ADAR-based) benchmarks for selected transcripts to cross-validate temporal fidelity, noting that ADAR methods infer RNA age from accumulated A→I edits rather than physical capture. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7956158/?utm_source=openai))
  - Milestone: Per-cell trajectories with ≥7 time bins, each with ≥2,000 genes at UMI ≥3, and consistent ordering vs ADAR-based age inference for shared reporters.

Experimental design and methods
- Materials engineering
  - Peptide scaffold: Lys/Arg-rich with periodic degradable linkers; include minor hydrophobes to tune mesh.
  - Linker palette: choose chemistries with well-separated intracellular half-lives and orthogonal sensitivities; characterize in vitro, then in cells by FRET charge sensors.
  - Condensate nucleation: membrane-tethered low-copy scaffold (e.g., GAP43 peptide) to confine a single TPCC per cell and maintain cytosolic access.
- Capture and indexing
  - Capture module: oligo(dT)20 fused to minimized RRM scaffold; low expression by weak promoter; quantify occupancy vs free mRNA by smFISH.
  - Barcodes: seven 18–22 nt sequences prehybridized to orthogonal, kinetically unmasking hairpins; splinted ligation by a thermostable ligase adapted for 37°C and enhanced within the dense phase.
- Library prep
  - Magnetic enrichment of barcode–RNA adducts; reverse transcription with template-switch; add cell barcode and UMI; standard scRNA-seq chemistry with added barcode read.
- Scaling and heterogeneity
  - Plate ≥10,000 cells/run; include spike-in time controls; model inter-cell variability in window boundaries; fit Bayesian deconvolution to correct modest window jitter.

Controls and validation
- No-TPCC and inert condensate controls to assess perturbation.
- No-barcode and scrambled-barcode controls for specificity.
- Transcriptional spike-ins driven by drug-inducible promoters at known times to calibrate time-bin boundaries.
- Orthogonal benchmark using ADAR-based RNA timestamping for a subset of transcripts (reporters) to verify time ordering. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7956158/?utm_source=openai))

Success criteria
- Technical: Seven demultiplexed time bins per cell with distinct, non-overlapping spike-in peaks; cell viability ≥80% to 24 h; minimal global transcriptome distortion vs control.
- Biological: Perturbation-responsive pathways (e.g., immediate-early, stress, or drug-target pathways) show expected early/late kinetics with coherent single-cell heterogeneity structure.

Risk assessment and mitigation
- RNA sequestration perturbs translation: mitigate with weak-binding RRM mutants, low expression, small TPCC volume fraction; verify polysomes.
- Kinetic drift across cells: include per-cell internal standards (brief 4sU label at known times for external benchmarking) in pilot experiments; refine linker palette.
- Barcode ligation efficiency too low: enrich adducts magnetically and increase ligase local concentration within TPCC.

Novelty and relation to prior art
- Prior work established programmable coacervates with tunable uptake/release in cells and salt/redox-driven disassembly but did not record transcriptome time courses. This proposal repurposes condensate aging as an intrinsic, multi-window temporal encoder. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11582321/?utm_source=openai))
- ADAR-based RNA timestamping infers RNA age from accumulated A→I edits on engineered motifs; here, endogenous poly(A)+ RNAs are physically captured into discrete windows and barcoded, enabling whole-transcriptome, same-cell trajectories without per-transcript engineering. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7956158/?utm_source=openai))
- Reversible EV capture/release via desthiobiotin–biotin/streptavidin has been shown on devices and cell surfaces; it supports feasibility of gentle, staged release/collection should the non-destructive path be pursued, but differs mechanistically from the proposed intracellular time-encoding condensate. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7328786/?utm_source=openai))

Deliverables
- A validated TPCC construct and linker palette providing seven log-spaced capture windows from 30 min to 24 h in living cells.
- A single end-point library workflow yielding per-cell, seven-bin transcriptomes.
- Benchmark datasets comparing ChronoPhase to ADAR timestamping for shared reporters and demonstrating inter-cell response heterogeneity at transcriptome scale.

Title
Longitudinal same-cell “exported-barcode” transcriptome proxies to expose what destructive snapshots miss

Hypothesis/Question
If intracellular transcriptional program activities are externalized as multiplexed, barcoded RNAs that are preferentially packaged into extracellular vesicles (EVs) and serially captured from the same immobilized cell, then dynamic features of single-cell trajectories (onset order, pulse width, duty cycle, refractory periods) can be recovered that are unrecoverable from destructive snapshot time series; which specific features remain unrecoverable will define performance requirements for future true same-cell, transcriptome-level methods. Engineered barcoded RNA export and single-cell EV capture make this feasible; DNA-based “diaries” provide end-point, time-integrated ground truth for benchmarking. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-026-72072-w?utm_source=openai))

Atomic strategy
Externalize a compressed, pathway-axis representation of the transcriptome as secreted, time-sampled barcoded RNAs from the same living cell, using microfluidic traps to time-segment EV capture and sequencing to quantify module activity trajectories. The compression basis is TF/pathway-responsive promoters; end-point DNA recording validates integration over the full 24 h window. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11357993/?utm_source=openai))

Specific aims
1) Engineer a multiplexed “Module→Barcode EV” (MBEV) library.
2) Build a perfused single-cell microfluidic array with replaceable EV/RNA capture modules for ≥7 logarithmic time points between 30 min and 24 h post-perturbation.
3) Benchmark against destructive snapshots and an internal DNA diary to quantify information lost by snapshot-only reconstructions.

Aim 1. MBEV genetic system
- Module reporters: 48–96 cis-regulatory elements (CREs) responsive to major axes (NF-κB, AP-1, STAT1/2, IRF, p53, HIF1α, E2F/MYC, ATF4/ISR, NRF2, SRF/TCF, Notch, Wnt/TCF) each drive a short, polyadenylated barcode RNA (80–120 nt) with 2×MS2 hairpins and EV-loading motifs.
- Preferential EV loading: Co-express MCP fused to the EV tetraspanin CD63 (MCP–CD63) to actively recruit MS2-tagged barcodes into EVs; MCP–CD63 increases sgRNA/short-RNA loading into EVs by ~10^2–10^3-fold. Include EXOmotifs (e.g., GGAG/AGG/UAG) to leverage hnRNPA2B1-mediated sorting. These mechanisms are established for loading defined RNAs into EVs. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12639036/?utm_source=openai))
- Prior art and divergence: Barcoded exosomal miRNAs (bEXOmiRs) and gRNA-barcoded EVs quantify EV biogenesis in pooled assays; here, barcodes encode pathway activity and are read longitudinally per single cell, not pooled, to reconstruct dynamics. ([elifesciences.org](https://elifesciences.org/articles/41460?utm_source=openai))
- Optional yield booster: Substitute or augment with capsid/extravesicular export systems that enrich poly(A)+ RNA cargo for non-destructive transcriptomics when EV yield is limiting. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-026-72072-w?utm_source=openai))
- Calibration: Drive barcodes with titratable dCas9-VPR CRISPRa against each CRE or with defined agonists to map barcode secretion rate to promoter activity. Use step/pulse inputs (e.g., TNF-α, IFN-β, EGF, CoCl2, thapsigargin) to extract impulse responses.

Aim 2. Microfluidic same-cell time segmentation and capture
- Device: Hydrodynamic single-cell traps under continuous perfusion; concentric ring-valve regions around each cell functionalized with anti-CD63 and with complementary DNA probes to each barcode. Replace capture rings at predefined time points (0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 24 h) to time-stamp secreted material while keeping the same cell alive. Single-cell EV capture with spatially addressable coatings and time-lapse operation has been demonstrated. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8463870/?utm_source=openai))
- Throughput: 512–1024 traps to support heterogeneity analysis.
- Sample handling: After each interval, remove the capture ring, lyse bound EVs on-chip, and perform on-ring barcoded reverse transcription so each sample encodes cell ID and time interval. Sequencing yields counts per barcode per time window.
- Controls: Traps without cells; cells lacking MCP–CD63; constitutive barcode controls; spike-in synthetic barcodes perfused intermittently to estimate capture and washout kinetics.

Aim 3. Benchmarking: snapshots versus exported trajectories versus DNA diary
- Snapshots: In parallel cultures, perform destructive scRNA-seq at the same seven times; reconstruct pseudotime and RNA velocity trajectories for population-level inference.
- DNA diary: Introduce a 24–48 axis ENGRAM array in the trapped cells to record time-integrated module activity on a shared DNA “tape”; a constitutive tick cassette provides an internal time base. Sequence at experiment end to obtain integrated ground truth per axis. ENGRAM records CRE activity by expressing pegRNAs that write signal-specific edits, enabling quantitative, multiplex recording across many TF motifs. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11357993/?utm_source=openai))
- Comparison metrics: For each cell, compare exported MBEV trajectories to (i) same-cell DNA diary integrals and (ii) snapshot-only reconstructions from different cells. Quantify features unrecoverable from snapshots: short pulses (<1 h), activation order within 2–4 h windows, multi-pulse bursting, and hysteresis.

Experimental plan and analyses
- Cell model: HEK293T or K562, stable for MBEV and ENGRAM; optional GPCR/TLR pathway plugs for orthogonal stimulation.
- Perturbation at t=0; perfusion maintains constant media and ensures rapid removal of secreted vesicles so each capture ring integrates over a defined window (impulse response characterized by dye and synthetic vesicle tracers).
- Library preparation: On-ring RT with timepoint- and trap-indexed primers; pooled PCR; short-read sequencing.
- Deconvolution: Convert barcode counts to promoter activity using a secretion-convolution model fit from step inputs; correct for EV residence time and capture efficiency.
- Statistics: Mixed-effects models per module with random intercepts/slopes per cell; Granger/transfer entropy to infer module precedence; model comparison against pseudotime/velocity reconstructions to enumerate irrecoverable features.

Milestones and success criteria
- M1: ≥20 modules show monotonic calibration between known agonist dose and exported-barcode counts; LOD ≤10–50 molecules per interval. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12639036/?utm_source=openai))
- M2: ≥80% cell viability over 24 h with seven capture exchanges; stable secretion baselines in controls. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5023418/?utm_source=openai))
- M3: For at least three perturbations, exported trajectories reveal features (e.g., <60 min NF-κB pulse; delayed ATF4 ramp) that snapshots fail to reconstruct, as judged by cross-validated prediction error versus DNA diary integrals. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11357993/?utm_source=openai))

Risk and mitigation
- Low copy export: Use MCP–CD63 and EXOmotifs; if still limiting, add capsid-based exporters to raise cargo density. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12639036/?utm_source=openai))
- Cross-talk between traps: Maintain unidirectional perfusion; include spatially alternating empty traps to monitor carryover; quantify with perfused spike-ins. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8463870/?utm_source=openai))
- Biological lag of EV biogenesis: Characterize and model lag per module; use diary to correct bias in early windows.

Differentiation
- Not pseudotime/RNA velocity or metabolic labeling; not intracellular aspiration (Live-seq/NTVE) or few-gene fluorescence. It is same-cell, minimally invasive, time-segmented, module-resolved export with per-cell longitudinal capture and an orthogonal DNA ground truth. Prior EV-barcoding studies read pooled secretion or EV biology; here, barcodes encode pathway activity and are time-resolved per cell. ([elifesciences.org](https://elifesciences.org/articles/41460?utm_source=openai))

Deliverable
A validated, scalable methodology for repeated, same-cell, module-resolved measurements across ≥7 logarithmic time points (30 min–24 h), plus a quantitative map of which trajectory features destructive snapshots systematically miss and the minimal observability requirements for future same-cell transcriptome technologies. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8463870/?utm_source=openai))

text:
Title
Cell-addressable, gated vesicular export transcriptomics (CAGE-VET) for repeated, same-cell RNA-state measurements

Central hypothesis-as-question
Can short, synchronized “snapshot-and-export” pulses—comprising a reversible transcriptional pause coupled to a time-gated burst of vesicular RNA export—enable repeated, single-cell–resolved transcriptome readouts from the same living cells across 30 minutes to 24 hours after a defined perturbation?

Atomic strategy
Replace destructive lysis with episodic, externally captured transcript sampling by: (i) briefly pausing RNAP II elongation to stabilize the intracellular RNA composition, and (ii) triggering a short, inducible burst of export of endogenous poly(A)+ transcripts into affinity-capturable virus-like particles (VLPs) collected at per-cell addresses. This yields discrete, repeated transcriptome snapshots per individual cell without removing cytosol or consuming endogenous RNAs. The pause minimizes temporal blur; the export enables non-destructive readout; the addressable capture provides single-cell assignment.

Rationale and novelty check
- Non-destructive export of RNAs via engineered VLPs has been shown to recapitulate intracellular transcriptomes and to permit multi–time-point population measurements (NTVE). However, current NTVE implementations do not assign exported transcripts to individual cells when pooled, limiting single-cell trajectory inference. CAGE-VET adds per-cell addressability and snapshot gating to achieve repeated, same-cell transcriptomes. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13121718/?utm_source=openai))
- Live-seq and nanostraw-based sampling can perform sequential measurements from the same cell but rely on aspirating cytosol, limiting throughput and risking cumulative perturbation. CAGE-VET is non-aspirative and scales by parallel capture. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-022-05046-9?utm_source=openai))
- Brief CDK9 inhibition halts RNAP II pause release within minutes and is reversible, providing a practical “pause button” to sharpen each export pulse into a snapshot. ([tandfonline.com](https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.4161/trns.2.3.16172?utm_source=openai))
- Single-cell–addressable capture of secreted materials and linkage to transcriptomes has precedent (e.g., nanovials/SEC-seq), supporting feasibility of per-cell VLP capture and downstream sequencing. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41596-024-01112-w?utm_source=openai))

Specific aims
1) Engineer time-gated export of endogenous mRNAs
- Construct an inducible NTVE module consisting of: a PABP-based RNA-packaging adaptor fused to VLP scaffolds and an orthogonal epitope (e.g., FLAG) for affinity capture. Add an optogenetic clustering switch (e.g., CRY2olig) to Gag to produce rapid, light-triggered bursts of VLP assembly and budding. Validate that exported RNA profiles correlate with matched cell lysates. Outcome: tunable export pulses with defined onset and duration. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13121718/?utm_source=openai))

2) Implement reversible snapshot gating
- Administer sub-micromolar DRB (or next-generation CDK9 inhibitor) for 3–5 minutes to transiently arrest RNAP II pause release, starting 2 minutes before the export pulse and ending at pulse completion. Quantify reversibility and minimal off-target effects by imaging and sentinel gene kinetics. Outcome: minimized in-window transcriptome drift with rapid recovery. ([tandfonline.com](https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.4161/trns.2.3.16172?utm_source=openai))

3) Build a per-cell capture array for repeated sampling
- Culture cells in a high-density micro-nanowell plate (≥5,000 wells) with removable hydrogel “capture lids” bearing spatial barcodes and anti-FLAG binders. During each export pulse, dock a fresh capture lid for 5–10 minutes to bind proximate VLPs; then undock for library prep while returning cells to standard culture with a blank lid. Outcome: seven or more addressable captures per cell over 0.5–24 h with negligible cross-well crosstalk. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41596-024-01112-w?utm_source=openai))

4) Demonstrate repeated, same-cell trajectories after defined perturbations
- At t=0, apply a drug or genetic trigger. Sample at logarithmic intervals (0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 24 h) with snapshot-gated export/capture. Sequence capture-lid RNA (NTVE-optimized Smart-seq–style protocol) and reconstruct each cell’s time series. Compare to terminal scRNA-seq of the same plate at 24 h and to matched population lysates. Outcome: single-cell trajectories with transcriptome-wide coverage and time-resolved heterogeneity. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13121718/?utm_source=openai))

Experimental plan and key measurements
- Cell systems: adherent mammalian lines (HEK293T; one primary-cell model for generality).
- Export pulse calibration: quantify VLP count and RNA yield vs. light-pulse length/intensity and NTVE expression level; compute export “impulse response” to verify minute-scale control compatible with ≥7 time points in 24 h. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-026-72072-w?utm_source=openai))
- Pause calibration: measure global run-on (e.g., PRO-seq markers or sentinel nascent RNA imaging) to confirm <5 min onset and recovery post-DRB washout. ([tandfonline.com](https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.4161/trns.2.3.16172?utm_source=openai))
- Capture performance: test capture efficiency and cross-talk using mixed epitope tags and alternating checkerboard seeding; emulate SEC-seq quality controls for per-cell linkage. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41596-024-01112-w?utm_source=openai))
- Throughput: seed 2,000–5,000 wells; require ≥70% wells with ≥5 time points passing QC; target ≥5,000–10,000 detected genes per time point (after low-input optimization). ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13121718/?utm_source=openai))
- Data analysis: per-cell normalization across time using spike-ins on capture lids; infer gene-specific response kinetics; quantify intra- vs. inter-cell variability; compare to pseudotime and RNA velocity baselines.

Controls
- No-exporter and no-epitope controls for background binding.
- Export pulses without pause gating to quantify snapshot sharpening benefit.
- Vehicle-only for DRB; alternative short-acting transcription inhibitors as orthogonal validation.
- Fixed-time Live-seq or nanostraw sampling on a subset to benchmark concordance. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-022-05046-9?utm_source=openai))

Success criteria
- Correlation of exported-RNA profiles with matched lysates ≥0.8 across expressed genes at calibration points. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13121718/?utm_source=openai))
- Viability ≥90% and proliferation comparable to controls across seven sampling cycles.
- Single-cell assignment error (cross-well contamination) ≤2%.
- Detectable and consistent transcriptional trajectories in ≥70% of cells; demonstrable heterogeneity in response amplitude/onset across the population.

Risk assessment and mitigation
- Export kinetics too slow for early time points: increase expression of export components, use stronger optogenetic clustering, or extend early windows to 10–15 minutes while maintaining pause. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-026-72072-w?utm_source=openai))
- Perturbation by repeated DRB pulses: minimize concentration and exposure; verify recovery by sentinel assays; if needed, gate only export (omit pause) for late time points when drift is slower. ([tandfonline.com](https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.4161/trns.2.3.16172?utm_source=openai))
- Low RNA input per pulse: apply NTVE-optimized full-length cDNA amplification and UMIs; optionally pool two adjacent pulses for late, low-activity windows. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13121718/?utm_source=openai))
- Cell assignment: incorporate well-specific spatial barcodes and physical gaskets; validate by mixed-species assays.

Differentiation from prior work
- Versus NTVE: adds single-cell addressability and pause-gated snapshots, enabling repeated, same-cell trajectories rather than population-level or pooled readouts. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13121718/?utm_source=openai))
- Versus Live-seq/nanostraws: avoids cytosol aspiration and scales to thousands of cells in parallel with ≥7 time points. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-022-05046-9?utm_source=openai))

Milestones and timeline
- Months 0–6: Build/export tuning; validate export/lysate concordance and pause kinetics. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13121718/?utm_source=openai))
- Months 6–12: Fabricate capture arrays; establish per-cell linkage and cross-talk metrics; complete power analysis via pilot 2,000-cell run. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41596-024-01112-w?utm_source=openai))
- Months 12–18: Full experiment with ≥7 time points over 0.5–24 h post-perturbation; deliver same-cell transcriptome trajectories and heterogeneity analyses.

Impact
CAGE-VET operationalizes a true pause–measure–resume paradigm for transcriptome-wide, repeated, same-cell measurements with scalable throughput. It leverages and extends recent advances in vesicular transcript export and single-cell secretion capture, while introducing reversible snapshot gating to improve temporal fidelity. This directly addresses the unmet need for longitudinal, per-cell molecular trajectories under defined perturbations. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13121718/?utm_source=openai))
