text:
Title
Follower-only engineered myocardial tissue: IK1-reserve clamp with geometric source–sink diode to ensure host-driven activation without automaticity

Central research question and hypothesis
- Question/Hypothesis: Can an engineered human PSC–derived ventricular tissue be made inherently incapable of initiating rhythm while remaining highly excitable and strongly contractile, by preloading diastolic stability with an inward-rectifier potassium (IK1) reserve and imposing a tissue-scale source–sink asymmetry that favors host-to-patch conduction but blocks patch-to-host initiation?
- Prediction: An IK1-reserve at adult-ventricular levels combined with an asymmetric host–patch interface (“geometric diode”) will (i) abolish patch automaticity under all tested perturbations, (ii) preserve rapid conduction and robust contraction, and (iii) guarantee a quiescent follower state at the tissue level from immediate engraftment through chronic remodeling.

Atomic strategy (single conceptual change)
- Overdetermine the diastolic potential at the cell level via a tunable IK1-reserve and propagate that stability to the tissue level by designing an asymmetric source–sink interface. One change—establishing a surplus hyperpolarizing reserve—translates globally into “excitable-but-non-initiating” behavior.

Rationale (first principles)
- Automaticity emerges when net depolarizing diastolic currents exceed the stabilizing sink. Increasing IK1 raises the stabilizing sink and deepens resting membrane potential, removing diastolic depolarization without suppressing voltage-gated Na+ availability. At the tissue boundary, conduction is governed by source–sink balance: shaping geometry and coupling to create a favorable sink at the host-facing edge permits host→patch propagation while preventing patch→host breakthrough by any residual local triggers.

Specific aims

Aim 1. Build an IK1-reserve ventricular myocyte chassis that is quiescent yet highly excitable.
- Engineering:
  - CRISPR knock-in of KCNJ2 (Kir2.1) into a safe-harbor locus under a tunable, β-adrenergic–insensitive promoter (e.g., TetOn or synthetic minimal promoter), yielding adjustable IK1-reserve without catecholamine upregulation.
  - Maintain fast conduction competence via maturation (electromechanical conditioning, thyroid/T3, fatty-acid media) to enhance SCN5A/Nav1.5 and GJA1/Cx43 without additional edits.
  - Optional fail-safe (invoked only if needed by pre-defined criteria): HCN4 knockout to remove If.
- Readouts (single-cell):
  - Resting potential, INa availability (steady-state inactivation), dV/dtmax, APD90, Ca2+ transient amplitude/kinetics; spontaneous activity probability under basal and provoked states.
- Provocations:
  - Catecholaminergic: isoproterenol/forskolin.
  - Ionic: [K+]o 3–8 mM, mild hypomagnesemia, mild hypocalcemia.
  - Ischemic: hypoxia, acidosis, lactate, ATP-sensitive K+ activation.
- Success criteria (single-cell):
  - Spontaneous rate = 0 across all provocations (n≥200 cells per condition); resting potential ≤ −82 mV; dV/dtmax ≥ 150 V/s; APD90 within 10% of control matured ventricular iPSC-CMs; Ca2+ transient amplitude ≥ 90% of control.

Aim 2. Architect a “geometric diode” interface that enforces follower-only tissue behavior.
- Design principles:
  - Anisotropic, tapered isthmus at the host–patch boundary to increase host→patch source strength and host-facing sink load.
  - Graded coupling: higher Cx43 density and myocyte density on the host-proximal band; slightly reduced coupling within a narrow reverse-bias strip on the patch side to raise patch→host threshold without slowing forward conduction.
  - Segmented microdomains within the patch (CM cords separated by thin, IK1-superdense septae) to absorb local triggers and prevent reentry circuits.
- Implementation:
  - Collagen/elastin or decellularized-ECM scaffold microfabricated with funnel-shaped conduits (photopatterning/3D printing); spatial control of cell density during seeding; soluble cues to modulate Cx43 locally.
  - Two hPSC-CM sub-states by promoter tuning only: “contractor–conductor” (IK1-reserve, high Nav/Cx43) cords; “sink-septum” (ultra-IK1, slightly reduced Nav) 30–60 µm barriers that remain non-excitable but electrotonically coupled.
- Modeling and benchtop validation:
  - Bidomain simulations to select geometries that yield safety factor SFhost→patch ≥ 1.5 and SFpatch→host < 1.0 under worst-case partial coupling.
  - Optical mapping in 3D engineered tissues interfaced with ex vivo ventricular slices: measure forward conduction velocity, activation delay, and reverse breakthrough probability under burst pacing and ectopic stimulation.
- Success criteria (tissue):
  - Forward CV ≥ 25 cm/s with activation delay across interface ≤ 10 ms; zero reverse breakthroughs in >10,000 ectopic attempts across provocation matrix; no sustained reentry within patch.

Aim 3. Ensure robustness from immediate post-graft to chronic integration in vivo under stress.
- Models and procedures:
  - Acute: immunodeficient rat infarct model, epicardial placement with sutureless bioadhesive; continuous telemetry from hour 0.
  - Chronic: porcine anterolateral infarct model, epicardial patch with pre-vascularized channels.
- Provocations/timepoints:
  - Immediate (hours 0–24): incomplete coupling, inflammatory milieu.
  - Subacute (weeks 1–4) and chronic (3–6 months): remodeling and vascular integration.
  - Stress testing at each timepoint: β-agonist infusion, programmed stimulation, exercise, transient coronary occlusion (ischemia), electrolyte shifts (controlled K+/Mg2+/Ca2+).
- Endpoints:
  - Primary: zero graft-originated ectopy or tachyarrhythmia; entrainment index ≥ 0.98 (fraction of host beats captured by patch).
  - Secondary: forward-only conduction (no patch→host initiation), contractile contribution (regional strain increase ≥ 10% over graft bed), absence of reentry circuits within patch by panoramic mapping.
- Explant analysis:
  - Connexin distribution, Kir2.1 levels, fibrosis, vascularization, autonomic/neural ingrowth.

Experimental plan and methods overview
- Cell manufacturing: hPSC ventricular specification; safe-harbor KCNJ2 integration; inducible promoter calibration; clone banking; release assays (IK1 density target window; off-target edit screening).
- Tissue engineering: scaffold microfabrication; dual-state seeding by promoter dose; electromechanical maturation; pre-vascularization with endothelial/pericyte cords (structured to avoid excitable coupling).
- Electrophysiology assays: patch clamp, dynamic clamp, high-speed voltage/Ca2+ imaging, multielectrode arrays; bidomain modeling linked to measured parameters.
- Mechanical assays: traction force microscopy; sonomicrometry or speckle-tracking echocardiography in vivo.
- Statistics and power: pre-registered analysis with event-adjudication blinded; non-inferiority margin vs sham for arrhythmia incidence; superiority for regional function.

Risk analysis and mitigations
- Excess IK1 shortens APD and reduces Ca2+ entry: titrate promoter to maintain APD within 10% of matured controls; adjust afterload/electrical conditioning to preserve ICaL; exclude clones outside APD window.
- Conduction slowing from coupling gradients: iteratively tune Cx43 patterning and isthmus width to keep forward CV within target while maintaining reverse block.
- Hyperkalemia-induced depolarization: design ≥ 10 mV RMP safety margin at 5.5–6.0 mM [K+]o; invoke HCN4 knockout if spontaneous activity emerges under worst-case tests.
- Reentry within patch: enforce septation pitch below the critical wavelength; verify zero sustained circuits under burst pacing/catecholamines.
- Chronic remodeling alters interface: incorporate durable scaffold anisotropy; periodic in vivo mapping to retune inducible IK1 level if needed.

Milestones and go/no-go criteria
- M1 (Months 0–6): Single-cell success—zero automaticity across provocations; go if ≥ 90% cells meet RMP and excitability criteria.
- M2 (Months 6–12): In vitro tissue success—forward conduction with reverse block across full provocation matrix; go if zero reverse breakthroughs in ≥ 10,000 trials and CV/delay targets met.
- M3 (Months 12–24): Rat in vivo—no graft-origin ectopy over 14-day telemetry; proceed to porcine if 0 events in n≥12 animals.
- M4 (Months 24–42): Porcine—no graft-origin ectopy across acute, subacute, chronic windows; demonstrate functional augmentation without arrhythmia; proceed to IND-enabling workup.

Acceptance criteria defining “quiescent, non-arrhythmogenic follower” (must meet all)
- Tissue-level: zero spontaneous activations or sustained arrhythmias originating within the patch under baseline and all provocations; no patch→host initiation; forward entrainment ≥ 0.98.
- Cellular: spontaneous rate = 0; RMP ≤ −82 mV; dV/dtmax ≥ 150 V/s; APD within target band; preserved Ca2+ transients.
- Robustness: criteria maintained at immediate post-graft (hours 0–24), subacute, and chronic stages and under catecholaminergic stimulation, ischemia, and electrolyte perturbations.

Expected outcome and impact
- A transplantation-ready, conduction-competent myocardial patch that is electrically obedient—capable of strong, synchronous contraction when commanded by the host yet fundamentally unable to initiate or sustain competing rhythms—addressing engraftment arrhythmia at its root by design-stage decoupling of conduction competence from automaticity.

text:
Title
IK1-clamped, conduction-optimized hPSC-CM grafts that are host-locked cables, not oscillators

Central hypothesis (goal-as-question)
Can an engineered “electrotonic clamp” that imposes a dominant inward-rectifier K+ reserve while removing pacemaker currents, together with reinforced fast-Na and gap-junction pathways, produce hPSC-CM tissues that are intrinsically quiescent yet conduct and contract robustly only when driven by host myocardium, thereby eliminating engraftment arrhythmias from day 0 through chronic integration and under stress?

Atomic strategy
Convert the graft from an oscillator to a cable by installing a strong diastolic clamp (adult-like IK1) that dominates diastolic slope under all conditions. This single-system change makes the tissue an electrotonic sink that is excitable and rapidly conductive when stimulated, but cannot self-initiate depolarization.

Specific aims
1) Build the IK1-clamped, automaticity-deleted, conduction-optimized hPSC-CM line.
2) Prove tissue-level quiescence with preserved excitability, conduction velocity, and contractility across stressors in vitro.
3) Demonstrate host-locked activation without graft-origin ectopy in vivo from the immediate post-graft period through chronic follow-up.

Design and methods

Aim 1: Construct and validate the electrical design in single cells
- Edits and expression design
  - Diastolic clamp: AAVS1 safe-harbor knock-in of a Tet-tunable KCNJ2 (Kir2.1) cassette with insulated promoter to reach adult-like IK1 density (target 3–5 pA/pF at −120 mV, 35°C). Include a degron for post-graft fine-tuning if needed.
  - Remove membrane pacemaker drive: CRISPR/Cas9 knockouts of HCN4 and T-type Ca2+ channels CACNA1G and CACNA1H.
  - Preserve/boost excitability and conduction: knock-in of SCN5A and SCN1B (ratio-tuned) and GJA1 (Connexin43) under moderate, maturation-competent promoters; include 3′ UTR elements to favor intercalated-disc localization.
- QC gates (single-cell)
  - Resting membrane potential ≤ −80 mV; If density < 0.1 pA/pF at −120 mV; no spontaneous diastolic depolarization for ≥5 minutes at 35°C.
  - dV/dtmax ≥ 200 V/s; APD90 200–270 ms at 1 Hz; normal L-type ICa,L density.
  - Sodium-channel availability preserved at 6–8 mM [K+]o (≥50% of baseline window current).
- All-optical phenotyping and patch clamp to link genotype→current→AP waveform. Select two clonal lines spanning lower and higher IK1 setpoints for downstream testing.

Aim 2: Establish tissue-level guarantees of quiescence with fast, robust conduction and contraction
- 2D monolayers and 3D aligned patches
  - Fabricate anisotropic tissues on micropatterned or aligned-fiber scaffolds (anisotropy ratio ~2.5–3.5). Use solely engineered hPSC-CMs to keep a single-cell-type product.
  - Enforce uniform GJA1 distribution by brief cAMP-independent adhesion priming during assembly.
- Conduction and excitability targets
  - Conduction velocity (35°C): longitudinal ≥ 50 cm/s; transverse ≥ 20 cm/s; anisotropy ratio ≥ 2.0.
  - Capture 1:1 from 1–4 Hz with preserved force–frequency response.
- Tissue-level quiescence criteria (no external drive)
  - Zero spontaneous activity over 72 hours in normoxia; ectopy threshold testing by focal current injection shows ≥3× higher trigger threshold than unedited hPSC-CM tissues.
  - Under β-adrenergic stimulation (isoproterenol 100 nM), hypokalemia (3.0 mM), hyperkalemia (6–8 mM), acidosis (pH 6.8), hypoxia (1% O2), and simulated ischemia, no spontaneous or triggered activity in ≥95% of fields; DAD/EAD incidence < 0.1% of beats.
- Contractile function
  - Twitch force per cross-sectional area within 80–120% of control at 1 Hz; preserved calcium transient amplitude and kinetics under pacing.
- Early post-assembly “incomplete coupling” challenge
  - Immediately after seeding (first 24–48 h), prior to full junctional maturation, verify absence of spontaneous activity and successful 1:1 capture at 1–3 Hz; map electrotonic load using optical voltage mapping.

Aim 3: In vivo demonstration of host-locked activation and non-arrhythmogenicity
- Models and delivery
  - Immunosuppressed guinea pig (n=20) for high-resolution mapping and telemetry; large-animal porcine chronic infarct model (n=12) for translational conduction and safety.
  - Epicardial or intramyocardial patch implantation with surgical alignment to host fiber direction.
- Acute (hours–days) and chronic (weeks–months) endpoints
  - Host capture from day 0: optical or high-density electrogram mapping shows instantaneous entrainment of graft by sinus rhythm and by host pacing at 90–150 bpm without ectopy.
  - Arrhythmia safety: continuous telemetry for ≥4 weeks; ectopic burden from graft origin ≤ 0.1 events/hour; zero sustained VT/VF attributable to graft.
  - Conduction: activation time across graft consistent with CV targets; stimulus–response curves show graft follows host over physiologic rate range under β-agonist and during transient ischemia-reperfusion.
  - Contractile contribution: regional strain improvement versus cell-free patches without increased arrhythmic events.

Milestones, go/no-go criteria
- M1 (cell level): RMP ≤ −80 mV; If absent; no spontaneous beats; preserved APD and dV/dtmax. Go if all pass.
- M2 (tissue level): CV targets met; zero spontaneous activity across stress panel; ≥3× higher ectopy threshold versus control. Go if all pass.
- M3 (acute in vivo): day-0 host capture without graft-origin ectopy during β-agonist challenge. Go if pass.
- M4 (chronic in vivo): ectopic burden ≤ 0.1/hour and no sustained VT/VF over 4 weeks with functional benefit. Success if pass.

Risk management and tuning knobs
- Excessive IK1 shortens APD or depresses calcium entry: titrate Tet level; select lower-IK1 clone; adjust SCN5A/SCN1B ratio to preserve safety factor.
- Heterogeneity of expression leading to local sources: clonal expansion; single-cell QC; exclude outliers via flow cytometry reporter linked to KCNJ2/HCN4 loci.
- Ischemic depolarization reducing Na+ availability: preempt with elevated SCN5A reserve and robust gap junctional coupling; confirm capture under 6–8 mM [K+]o.
- Structural maturation lag post-implant: promoter choice ensuring early GJA1 expression; align graft to host fibers to minimize discontinuities.

Readouts and analytics
- All-optical voltage/calcium mapping, microelectrode arrays, traction force microscopy.
- Telemetry and programmed electrical stimulation in vivo; activation mapping to localize any ectopy.
- Predefined adjudication to attribute arrhythmias to graft versus host.

Deliverable
A GMP-translatable, single-cell-type hPSC-CM graft line and manufacturing protocol that yields electrically silent, high-velocity “cable” myocardium: quiescent at rest, immediately and chronically host-captured, and non-arrhythmogenic under catecholaminergic stimulation, ischemia, and electrolyte perturbations.

text:
Title
Local stress-hormone training imprints a mast cell–intrinsic, site-restricted secretome memory in skin

Central question and hypothesis (intentionally fused)
Do repeated, low-dose, site-restricted exposures to endogenous stress hormones program skin-resident mast cells to acquire a durable, recallable shift in secretome composition that is retained locally and alters communication with neighboring target cells? We hypothesize that glucocorticoid, catecholamine, and CRH signaling prime mast cells via receptor-driven chromatin and metabolic remodeling, producing a trained immunity–like state detectable as a compositional secretome memory at recall. This memory is cell-intrinsic, persists after a rest period, and displays site-specific signatures reflecting local skin niches.

Atomic strategy
Use “prime–rest–recall” at discrete skin sites as a single perturbation to convert mast cells into locally trained secretome states. Quantify training as a change in the relative composition of the mast cell secretome upon recall (heterologous and homologous triggers), independent of total output. Run matched in vitro and in vivo pipelines with identical dosing logic, shared secretomics, and orthogonal histamine/tryptase assays, then test functional impact on priority target cells.

Specific aims
1) Establish hormone-induced trained secretome states in mast cells in vitro.
2) Demonstrate site-restricted, mast cell–dependent trained secretome memory in mouse skin in vivo.
3) Define functional consequences of trained secretomes on priority downstream target cells.
4) Map mechanisms and site-specific determinants of training (epigenetic, metabolic, and receptor dependence).

Experimental design

Parallel systems
- In vitro: Primary murine bone marrow–derived mast cells (BMMCs) and primary human skin–derived mast cells (hMCs). Confirm FcεRI, c-Kit, GR (Nr3c1), β2-adrenergic receptor (Adrb2), and CRHR1/2 expression.
- In vivo: C57BL/6J mice; mast cell–deficient (Cpa3Cre;Mcl1fl/fl or KitW-sh/W-sh) with local adoptive reconstitution of BMMCs; Mcpt5-Cre mast cell–specific GR/Adrb2/Crhr1/2 conditional deletions for mechanistic controls.

Prime–rest–recall framework (shared logic)
- Prime (training): Repeated low-dose hormone exposures to mimic stress neuroendocrine tone.
  • In vitro: cortisol (human) or corticosterone (murine) 100 nM; norepinephrine 100 nM; CRH 10 nM; single or combined cocktail. Pulse 1 h/day for 3 days.
  • In vivo: intradermal microdosing at discrete sites (ear pinna, dorsal back, glabrous footpad). Corticosterone 100–300 nM eq., norepinephrine 100 nM, CRH 10 nM; 5 μL/site; 3 daily doses. Contralateral sites receive vehicle.
- Rest: 5–7 days without exposure (in vitro media change; in vivo no manipulation).
- Recall: Heterologous and homologous triggers to reveal memory.
  • In vitro recall: anti-IgE crosslinking, C48/80, substance P, TLR2/4 ligands, and the priming hormone(s) again.
  • In vivo recall: intradermal anti-IgE, C48/80, or substance P at trained vs control sites.

Primary readout system: quantitative secretome composition
- Sample collection
  • In vitro: supernatants at 5, 30, 120 min post-recall.
  • In vivo: dermal microdialysis or low-pressure suction blister fluid from each site; plasma for systemic spillover controls.
- Secretome multimodal profiling (compositional and absolute)
  • Proteomics: LC–MS/MS (DIA), with indexed retention-time and protein spike-ins for cross-batch normalization; targeted Olink or Luminex cytokine/chemokine panels.
  • Lipidomics: targeted LC–MS/MS for eicosanoids (PGE2, LTB4, LTC4), sphingolipids, and lysophospholipids.
  • Small molecules: amines and metabolites (histamine excluded here; see below) by LC–MS.
- Compositional analysis
  • Define a compositional secretome vector per sample (centered-log ratio, Aitchison geometry).
  • “Training Index” = cosine similarity of recall-secretome to trained baseline minus naive baseline; Earth Mover’s Distance to quantify shifts; hierarchical compositional biplots for feature loadings.
- Independent quantification of histamine and tryptase (mandated)
  • Histamine: UPLC–MS/MS with stable-isotope internal standard; confirm by fluorometric o-phthalaldehyde derivatization; report as absolute concentration and as proportion of total bioactive amines.
  • Tryptase: β-tryptase ELISA plus activity assay (e.g., Boc-Gln-Ala-Arg-AMC); normalize to cell number (in vitro) or albumin-adjusted site fluid (in vivo). Analyze separately from global secretome to avoid masking by high-abundance proteins.

Aim 1. In vitro training
- Protocol: Train BMMCs and hMCs as above; include receptor antagonists during training (RU486 for GR, ICI118,551 for β2AR, antalarmin for CRHR1) and remove before recall to test imprinting vs acute blockade.
- Readouts:
  • Degranulation kinetics (CD63/CD107a flow, β-hexosaminidase release).
  • Secretome compositional profiling; separate histamine/tryptase quantification.
  • Single-cell multiome (ATAC + RNA) at end of rest and 2 h post-recall to map trained enhancers and transcriptional programs (e.g., AP-1/GR/CREB/NR3C1 cistromes).
  • Metabolic state by Seahorse (glycolysis vs OXPHOS) and targeted metabolomics.
- Criteria for trained immunity–like memory: stimulus-nonspecific augmentation or reprogramming of recall secretome after rest, persisting without continued antagonist/agonist, and not explained by differential survival.

Aim 2. In vivo, site-specific training
- Sites: ear pinna (high vascular/nerve density), dorsal back (hair-bearing), hind paw glabrous skin (distinct innervation/ECM).
- Controls: contralateral vehicle sites; systemic hormone levels (plasma) to confirm locality; mast cell–deficient mice ± local BMMC reconstitution; receptor cKOs.
- Readouts:
  • Local secretome via microdialysis/blister fluid; separate histamine/tryptase quantification.
  • Physiology: Evans blue extravasation (vascular leakage), laser speckle imaging (perfusion), edema thickness, thermal/mechanical sensitivity (nociception/itch scoring).
  • Mast cell activation in situ: immunostaining for CD63, tryptase granule dispersion; granule ultrastructure (TEM) to distinguish full vs piecemeal degranulation.
- Localization test: prime one ear and not the other; perform recall at both. A trained response restricted to the primed ear indicates site-specific memory. In parabiosis pairs (optional), confirm lack of transfer.

Aim 3. Downstream target-cell impact (prioritized)
- Priority targets and rationale:
  1) TRPV1+/Nav1.8+ cutaneous sensory neurons (pruritus/hyperalgesia linkage).
  2) Dermal microvascular endothelium (edema and leukocyte recruitment).
  3) Keratinocytes (barrier modulation and cytokine amplification).
- Approaches:
  • Conditioned-media assays: apply in vitro trained vs naive mast cell secretomes, fractionated by size (exosomes vs soluble) and by mediator-specific immunodepletion (histamine, tryptase) to each target.
  • Readouts:
    - Neurons: calcium imaging, rheobase/current threshold, action potential frequency; SP/CGRP release.
    - Endothelium: trans-endothelial electrical resistance (TEER), FITC–dextran flux, ICAM-1/VCAM-1 expression, leukocyte adhesion under flow.
    - Keratinocytes: TEER of organotypic skin equivalents, tight junction proteins (claudin-1/occludin), cytokines (IL-33/TSLP/IL-6).
  • In vivo pharmacology: local H1R blockade, tryptase inhibitor (APC366), and COX inhibitor at recall to apportion functional contribution.

Aim 4. Mechanism and site determinants
- Receptor dependence: repeat in Mcpt5-Cre;Nr3c1fl/fl, Mcpt5-Cre;Adrb2fl/fl, and Mcpt5-Cre;Crhr1fl/fl mice; compare Training Index and physiology.
- Epigenetic imprinting: CUT&Tag for H3K4me1/H3K27ac at enhancers of secreted mediators; GR and CREB occupancy (CUT&RUN) at rest and recall.
- Memory disruption: transient BET inhibition (JQ1) or p300/CBP blockade (A-485) during training only; washout before recall.
- Site context: compare baseline transcriptomes of mast cells isolated from ear vs back vs paw after rest (scRNA-seq) and local niche factors (neuronal density, ECM stiffness). Associate niche variables with secretome principal components.

Key controls and confounders
- Hormone stability and penetration: verify local tissue levels by LC–MS; include inactive steroid analog controls.
- Cell number/viability: normalize by cell counts and viability dyes; equalize FcεRI-bound IgE before recall.
- Systemic contamination: measure plasma mediators to ensure locality; randomize site order; blinded analysis.
- Non–mast cell sources: test in mast cell–deficient mice; use cromolyn/latrunculin to block degranulation as orthogonal confirmation.

Data analysis and statistics
- Primary endpoint: difference in Training Index between trained and control conditions within site, with replication across donors/mice.
- Secondary endpoints: changes in histamine and tryptase absolute levels and proportions; target-cell functional readouts.
- Compositional statistics with permutation testing and false discovery rate control; mixed-effects models for multi-site repeated measures.

Milestones and decision points
- Go/no-go 1: In vitro Training Index > 0.2 with heterologous recall and preserved after 7-day rest.
- Go/no-go 2: In vivo site-restricted increase in Training Index and edema/perfusion response at primed vs contralateral sites; abrogation in mast cell–deficient and receptor cKO mice.
- If training is weak, adjust dose, interval, and rest length; test combined hormone primes to mirror stress physiology.

Outcomes and interpretation
- Supportive outcome: Durable, site-restricted changes in secretome composition upon recall, with independent increases/decreases in histamine and/or tryptase and predictable functional effects on neurons, endothelium, and keratinocytes. Receptor and epigenetic dependencies indicate trained immunity–like programming.
- Alternative: Tolerance-like suppression rather than augmentation; still constitutes memory if compositional shift is durable and site-restricted. Map to distinct enhancer programs and altered target-cell effects.

Deliverables (aligned to constraints)
- Parallel in vitro and in vivo datasets demonstrating trained secretome memory.
- A validated, quantitative secretome composition platform with compositional analytics.
- Separate, validated assays for histamine and tryptase with absolute and proportional reporting.
- A prioritized map of downstream target-cell effects (neurons, endothelium, keratinocytes) linked to specific mast cell mediators.
- A site-specific atlas of trained responses across ear, back, and paw, with mechanistic determinants.

Title: Collapsing adipocyte antigen presentation to extinguish adipose inflammation in obesity

Atomic strategy
- Silence CIITA-driven MHCII antigen presentation specifically in adipocytes to break the adipocyte→Th1 IFN-γ→adipocyte feed-forward inflammatory loop.

Unified hypothesis-question
- Do adipocytes act as context-dependent antigen-presenting cells whose CIITA-dependent MHCII expression is necessary and sufficient to sustain chronic adipose inflammation in obesity, and will adipocyte-specific CIITA repression reduce local immune activation and improve systemic metabolic homeostasis?

Specific aims

Aim 1. Define the adipocyte MHCII-high state and its inflammatory interactome in obesity.
- Platform: scRNA/snRNA-seq.
- Design:
  - Collect epididymal/inguinal adipose from lean vs diet-induced obese mice (12–16 weeks HFD) and perform paired stromal vascular fraction scRNA-seq and adipocyte/snRNA-seq.
  - Map CIITA/MHCII+ adipocyte states; quantify co-expression of costimulatory ligands (e.g., CD80/86, ICAM1) and chemokines (e.g., CCL2/5, CXCL9/10).
  - Infer ligand–receptor networks (adipocyte→T cell/macrophage) and trajectory from MHCII-low to MHCII-high states.
  - Validate at protein level by flow cytometry of buoyant adipocytes and immunostaining of whole-mount adipose.
- Primary readouts: fraction of MHCII+ adipocytes; strength of predicted adipocyte–T cell/macrophage interactions; association with Th1/Treg ratios and macrophage M1/M2 polarization.
- Success criterion: robust enrichment of CIITA/MHCII+ adipocyte states in obesity with predicted proinflammatory crosstalk.

Aim 2. Test necessity and sufficiency of adipocyte antigen presentation in a controlled adipose-immune organ-on-a-chip.
- Platform: organ-on-a-chip.
- Design:
  - Engineer a perfusable adipose-immune chip with primary murine (or human) mature adipocytes in 3D ECM co-cultured with autologous CD4+ T cells and monocyte-derived macrophages under obesogenic conditions (palmitate + hypoxia ± IFN-γ).
  - Perturbations (adipocyte-restricted):
    1) CIITA knockdown (siRNA or CRISPRi).
    2) MHCII functional blockade (anti-I-A/I-E or HLA-DP/DQ/DR Fab fragments) limited to adipocyte compartment.
    3) CIITA overexpression or IFN-γ priming to induce MHCII.
  - Measurements over 72–120 h: T cell activation (CD69, CD25, T-bet), cytokines (IFN-γ, TNF, IL-1β, IL-10), macrophage polarization markers (CD11c, CD206), chemokines (CCL2/5, CXCL9/10), adipocyte stress (JNK/NF-κB activity), lipolysis and insulin signaling.
- Primary readouts: effect size of adipocyte CIITA suppression on Th1 activation and macrophage M1 skewing; rescue by adipocyte-specific re-expression of CIITA.
- Success criterion: adipocyte-targeted CIITA/MHCII suppression reduces Th1/macrophage activation and adipocyte stress without impairing adipocyte viability.

Aim 3. Establish causal in vivo evidence using inducible adipocyte-specific CIITA loss-of-function.
- Platform: transgenic mouse model + scRNA-seq.
- Design:
  - Generate Adipoq-CreERT2;Ciita flox/flox mice for adult-onset adipocyte CIITA deletion.
  - Protocols:
    a) Prevention: induce deletion before HFD.
    b) Reversal: induce after 12 weeks HFD to test therapeutic window.
  - Endpoints (weeks 4–12 post-induction): adipose immune composition by flow cytometry; single-cell (sn/scRNA-seq) profiling of adipose to quantify MHCII+ adipocytes, Th1/Treg balance, macrophage states; histology for crown-like structures; metabolic tests (GTT, ITT); liver steatosis score.
- Controls: littermate flox/flox without Cre; adipocyte-specific H2-Aa deletion to separate CIITA-dependent vs -independent effects.
- Success criterion: adipocyte CIITA loss reduces local inflammation and improves insulin sensitivity, with concordant single-cell shifts away from Th1/M1 programs.

Aim 4. Therapeutic prototype and dose–response in vivo using adipocyte-targeted, reversible CIITA repression.
- Platform: transgenic mouse model (genetic proxy for a drug) + organ-on-a-chip.
- Design:
  - Use the Adipoq-CreERT2;Ciita flox/flox model as a pharmacodynamic surrogate to define efficacy thresholds (fraction of adipocytes needing CIITA suppression for benefit; time-to-effect).
  - On-chip, test ligand-directed siRNA formulations against CIITA restricted to the adipocyte channel to establish potency, durability, and off-target immune effects prior to in vivo translation.
- Primary readouts: minimal effective “target coverage” vs inflammatory endpoints; reversibility after withdrawal (Cre off-induction windows on chip).
- Success criterion: a defined target-coverage/benefit curve enabling translational design of adipocyte-directed CIITA inhibitors.

Validation, controls, and falsification
- Off-target immune suppression: assess MHCII on canonical APCs; include adipocyte-restricted interventions only; perform antigen-specific T cell assays to ensure systemic immunity is intact.
- Alternative mechanisms: if benefits persist despite adipocyte MHCII ablation, profile adipocyte senescence, ER stress, or lipotoxic signaling to rule in/out parallel drivers.
- Go/no-go: proceed if ≥30% reduction in Th1 signature and ≥20% improvement in insulin sensitivity are observed with adipocyte CIITA suppression in both chip and mouse models.

Outcomes and impact
- Mechanistic: establishes adipocyte antigen presentation as a master lever of adipose inflammation.
- Therapeutic: de-risks adipocyte-targeted CIITA/MHCII repression as a modality to reduce inflammation and restore metabolic homeostasis without broad immunosuppression.

text:
Title
Adipocyte NF-κB-to-Resolution Switch: Engineered fat cells that secrete Annexin A1 peptide to locally resolve obesity-associated inflammation

Integrated hypothesis and goal
Hypothesis-goal: Converting NF-κB activation in adipocytes from a pro-inflammatory driver into a trigger for secretion of a pro-resolving signal will reduce adipocyte-driven inflammation in obesity and restore healthy adipose-immune crosstalk.

Atomic strategy (single perturbation)
Install a genetic switch in adipocytes in which NF-κB activation induces secretion of the N‑terminal Annexin A1 peptide (Ac2‑26), a natural resolution-phase mediator that engages FPR2/ALX on immune cells to dampen cytokine production and promote efferocytosis.

Rationale
- In obesity, adipocyte NF-κB activation drives CCL2/IL‑6 secretion, lipolysis, and DAMP release that recruit and activate macrophages.
- Annexin A1/Ac2‑26 is a canonical pro-resolving cue that limits leukocyte recruitment and promotes clearance of debris without broad immunosuppression.
- Rewiring the same adipocyte trigger (NF-κB) to output a resolution mediator directly targets the causal adipocyte mechanism while flipping its tissue-level effect.

Specific aims

Aim 1. Build and validate the adipocyte NF-κB→Ac2‑26 switch in vitro.
- Construct: 5×κB minimal promoter driving a secreted Ac2‑26 peptide (signal peptide–fused), with GFP reporter via 2A. Control: empty vector or constitutive GFP.
- Cells: 3T3‑L1 and primary human preadipocytes differentiated to mature adipocytes.
- Induction/validation:
  - Stimuli: TNF‑α, palmitate, LPS (to activate adipocyte NF-κB).
  - Readouts: Ac2‑26 in medium (LC‑MS/MS or targeted immunoassay), κB reporter activity, adipocyte viability, differentiation markers (PPARγ, adiponectin), lipolysis (glycerol/NEFA).
- Mechanism checks:
  - FPR2/ALX dependence in co-cultured human monocyte-derived macrophages (MDMs) using the FPR2 antagonist WRW4.
  - Effect on adipocyte inflammatory outputs: CCL2, IL‑6, SAA3 mRNA/protein with and without TNF‑α.

Aim 2. Test paracrine resolution on an adipose tissue–on–a–chip platform.
- Platform: Microfluidic adipose chip with engineered adipocytes in a 3D matrix, human microvascular endothelium, and MDMs in the stromal compartment under low shear.
- Conditions: Obese-mimetic milieu (high palmitate, hypoxia 3%, TNF‑α).
- Endpoints:
  - Immune cell behaviors: monocyte adhesion/transmigration, MDM efferocytosis of apoptotic adipocytes, phagocytic index.
  - Inflammation: endothelial VCAM‑1/ICAM‑1, MDM cytokines (TNF‑α, IL‑1β), chemokines (CCL2), NF-κB nuclear translocation (live reporters).
  - Resolution markers: increased MerTK, Arg1, IL‑10 in MDMs.
  - Spatial gradients of Ac2‑26 across the chip (sampling ports).
- Causality tests: Add WRW4 or FPR2 siRNA in MDMs to abrogate effects; add exogenous Ac2‑26 as positive control.

Aim 3. Evaluate efficacy and mechanisms in vivo using a transgenic mouse and cell transplantation.
- Transgenic model:
  - Rosa26‑LSL‑sec‑Ac2‑26‑2A‑GFP crossed with Adipoq‑Cre to restrict the switch to mature adipocytes.
  - Diet-induced obesity (DIO; 60% HFD for 12–16 weeks).
  - Endpoints: adipose tissue macrophage content (F4/80), crown‑like structures, M1/M2 balance (CD11c/CD206), tissue cytokines/chemokines, adipocyte lipolysis rate ex vivo, systemic insulin sensitivity (secondary).
- scRNA‑seq:
  - SVF and adipocyte-enriched fractions from epididymal and subcutaneous fat.
  - Outcomes: macrophage states (inflammatory vs resolving), neutrophil presence, adipocyte NF‑κB target expression, ligand–receptor interactome (FPR2 axis), Ac2‑26 target gene signatures.
- Transplantation arm:
  - Human engineered adipocyte spheroids (from primary preadipocytes) embedded in a biocompatible hydrogel and transplanted into the perigonadal fat of immunodeficient DIO mice.
  - Readouts: local inflammation around grafts, human Ac2‑26 levels, effect on neighboring mouse macrophages; FPR2 blockade to confirm mechanism.

Validation criteria and decision points
- Aim 1 success: ≥10× inducible (vs basal) secretion of Ac2‑26 upon NF‑κB activation; reduction ≥50% in adipocyte CCL2/IL‑6 output to TNF‑α challenge in MDM co-culture, reversed by WRW4.
- Aim 2 success: ≥40% reduction in monocyte transmigration and endothelial activation; ≥2× increase in MDM efferocytosis; shift toward resolving macrophage transcriptome; all FPR2‑dependent.
- Aim 3 success: In DIO mice, ≥30% reduction in crown‑like structures, decreased pro-inflammatory macrophage fraction, improved adipose cytokine profile; scRNA‑seq shows enhanced resolution programs; transplantation yields localized anti-inflammatory zones.

Risks and contingencies
- Insufficient secretion: switch to full-length Annexin A1 with engineered secretion leader or secrete Ac2‑26 fused to an albumin‑binding domain to extend local half-life.
- Species receptor differences: prioritize human adipose chip and human cell transplantation readouts; in mice, include Fpr2-deficient cohort to verify specificity.
- Off-target systemic effects: confirm low circulating Ac2‑26, use depot-restricted expression, and test wound-healing assays for safety.

Impact
A single, mechanism-coupled reprogramming of adipocytes converts their NF‑κB–driven pro-inflammatory output into a pro-resolving signal, directly addressing how adipocytes propagate inflammation while creating distributed, tissue-local “medicine-making” cells that can be tested on-chip, in transgenic mice, and via adipocyte transplantation.

text:
Title: Decoupling adipocyte–immune mechanocontact to blunt obesity-associated inflammation

Central hypothesis (inseparable from the research goal): A sustained “force–time” signal generated at adipocyte–immune cell contacts—set primarily by adipocyte cortical tension and adhesion clustering—is necessary and sufficient to drive macrophage inflammatory activation in obese adipose tissue, independent of adipocyte death. Lowering adipocyte cortical tension below a threshold will prevent mechanocontact-driven inflammation without requiring changes in adipocyte viability.

Atomic strategy (single system-wide lever): Tune adipocyte cortical tension (actomyosin/RhoA–ROCK–talin clutch) to reduce the load-bearing capacity and dwell time of adipocyte–immune contacts, thereby keeping immune-cell mechanosensors below activation threshold.

Rationale and measurable predictions:
- Enlarged adipocytes with high cortical tension increase persistent contact and compressive load on resident macrophages and other immune cells, amplifying NF-κB/NLRP3 programs.
- Decreasing adipocyte cortical tension should: (i) shorten effective contact dwell time, (ii) reduce integrin nanocluster maturation at the interface, (iii) lower macrophage Ca2+ bursts and NF-κB nuclear translocation, and (iv) decrease tissue cytokines, all without increasing adipocyte death.
- A sharp threshold behavior is expected: once the adipocyte force–time integral falls below a critical value, inflammatory readouts drop steeply even under adipocyte metabolic stress.

Specific Aim 1 (organ-on-a-chip): Quantify and control adipocyte–immune mechanocontact and test tension-lowering as a causal anti-inflammatory switch.
- Platform: A two-compartment adipocyte–macrophage contact-on-a-chip with: (a) micromachined deformable membranes to impose defined compressive loads and gaps; (b) integrated traction sensors to read force at the interface; (c) optical control of adipocyte cortical tension.
- Adipocyte perturbations (adipocyte-restricted): 
  - Optogenetic RhoA/ROCK control (photoactivatable RhoA or photo-MLCK constructs under adiponectin promoter in primary adipocytes or iPSC-derived adipocytes).
  - Genetic clutch modulation: adipocyte-specific talin head mutant (reduced integrin–actin coupling) and non-muscle myosin II regulatory light chain phospho-mutants.
- Readouts:
  - Real-time macrophage Ca2+ imaging; NF-κB and IRF reporter translocation; cytokines (TNFα, IL-1β, IL-6) in effluent; inflammasome activation (ASC specks).
  - Contact metrics: dwell time, interface area, traction amplitude; integrin/talin/vinculin cluster size by TIRF.
  - Adipocyte viability and stress: TUNEL/cleaved caspase-3, ER-stress markers, lipolysis (glycerol/FFA), adipokines (adiponectin, leptin).
- Experiments:
  - Force–time mapping: sweep compressive load and contact duration with ± optogenetic tension changes; derive the 50% NF-κB-activation isocline.
  - Sufficiency/necessity: restore immune activation during adipocyte softening by prolonging contact dwell time mechanically; conversely, shorten dwell time at baseline stiffness to suppress activation.
- Success criteria:
  - ≥30% decrease in adipocyte cortical tension shifts the NF-κB activation threshold beyond physiologic contact dwell times; inflammatory cytokines drop ≥50% with unchanged adipocyte death.

Specific Aim 2 (transgenic mouse): Test whether adipocyte softening suppresses adipose inflammation in vivo under metabolic stress.
- Models (adiponectin-CreERT2):
  - Loss-of-function: adipocyte-specific partial Rock1/2 reduction or Myh9/Myh10 hypomorph; or expression of dominant-negative talin head to reduce integrin–actin coupling.
  - Gain-of-function (counterproof): adipocyte-specific constitutively active RhoA or phosphomimetic myosin regulatory light chain to increase cortical tension.
- Protocols:
  - Induce recombination before/during high-fat diet (12–16 weeks). Include cohorts with matched body weight and ER-stress induction to dissociate death from contact mechanics.
  - Ex vivo adipocyte stiffness by AFM; tissue mechanics by microindentation.
- Endpoints:
  - Inflammation: SVF flow cytometry (macrophage abundance, CD11c+ proportion), tissue cytokines, crown-like structure density, NF-κB p65 nuclear staining.
  - Metabolism: glucose/insulin tolerance; insulin signaling (p-AKT) in adipose; serum lipids/adipokines.
  - Cell death control: TUNEL, cleaved caspase-3, perilipin loss; ensure comparable death across groups where indicated.
- Success criteria:
  - Softened-adipocyte mice show ≥40% reduction in adipose TNFα/IL-1β and CLS density with no increase in adipocyte apoptosis; metabolic readouts improve. Stiffened-adipocyte mice show reciprocal changes.

Specific Aim 3 (scRNA-seq): Define the mechanocontact transcriptomic program and its collapse upon adipocyte softening.
- Samples:
  - SVF from epididymal and subcutaneous depots across genotypes in Aim 2 (soft, baseline, stiff) and diet states.
  - Chip co-cultures from Aim 1 harvested at defined force–time regimes.
- Analyses:
  - Cell-type annotation; macrophage state mapping (pro-inflammatory vs resolving) and pseudotime along mechanotransduction axes.
  - Module scores: NF-κB, NLRP3, Ca2+/calcineurin–NFAT, YAP/TAZ, integrin signaling in both adipocytes (droplet-containing nuclei capture or enriched adipocyte nuclei) and immune cells.
  - Ligand–receptor/contact inference (integrins–ICAM/VCAM, CD44–hyaluronan) and their load-dependence by integrating Aim 1 force metrics.
  - Construct a “mechanocontact score” predictive of inflammation from adipocyte stiffness and adhesion gene expression; validate against cytokine outputs.
- Success criteria:
  - Distinct mechanocontact gene module in macrophages collapses in softened-adipocyte conditions despite matched death/stress markers; adipocyte modules show coordinated downshift in RhoA–ROCK/talin signatures correlating with reduced inflammation.

Translational proof-of-concept within platforms:
- Screen adipocyte-restricted “mechano-decouplers” in Aim 1:
  - Peptides/small molecules that weaken integrin–talin binding in adipocytes.
  - Adipocyte-targeted delivery (FABP4/adiponectin-aptamer LNPs) of low-dose ROCK/myosin modulators.
- Advancement criteria: Candidates that reduce chip cytokines ≥60% without impairing adipocyte viability or dramatically altering basal lipolysis advance to short-term in vivo dosing in Aim 2 mice for biomarker knockdown (cytokines, CLS) over 2–4 weeks.

Controls and confound mitigation:
- Separate effects of contact vs soluble cues using transwells and microfluidic isolation.
- Ensure macrophage-intrinsic mechanosensing is unchanged by restricting perturbations to adipocytes (genetics/promoters, targeted delivery).
- Monitor adipocyte function (lipolysis, adipokines) to avoid trading inflammation for metabolic dysfunction.
- Power calculations based on pilot variance in AFM stiffness and cytokine outputs; pre-register success thresholds.

Milestones and outcomes:
- Year 1: Chip platform validated; force–time activation curve mapped; optogenetic adipocyte softening established.
- Year 2: Mouse lines characterized for adipocyte stiffness; initial inflammatory and metabolic phenotyping completed.
- Year 3: scRNA-seq mechanocontact module defined; candidate mechano-decouplers narrowed; short-term in vivo validation completed.

Impact: By identifying adipocyte cortical tension as the single controllable driver of contact-mediated inflammation, this work reframes therapeutic strategy from killing/scavenging dying adipocytes to mechanically decoupling living, stressed adipocytes from immune activation. It enables mechanism-grounded interventions that are testable across chip, mouse, and single-cell platforms and directly target how adipocytes increase inflammation.

text:
Title
Stress-to-Resolution (S2R) adipocytes: hijacking adipocyte NF-κB danger signaling to drive pro-resolving lipid biosynthesis

Hypothesis–Question
In obesity, adipocyte NF-κB activation induces CCL2 and recruits inflammatory monocytes. If we rewire this same stress-inducible output so that NF-κB drives specialized pro‑resolving mediator (SPM) biosynthesis instead, will adipocyte stress convert from a monocyte-recruiting danger signal into a self-amplifying resolution program that reduces adipose inflammation and improves metabolic control?

Atomic strategy
Single genetic switch: replace the endogenous Ccl2 coding sequence with Alox15 (12/15‑lipoxygenase) so that adipocyte NF-κB/AP‑1 inflammatory activation produces SPM precursors (17‑HDHA, 18‑HEPE) rather than CCL2. These intermediates are completed to resolvins/maresins by tissue 5‑LOX cells (macrophages), turning the same stress trigger into a pro‑resolving cue.

Specific aims
1) Build and validate S2R-adipocytes ex vivo.
2) Test stress‑to‑resolution conversion and macrophage responses on an adipose–immune organ‑on‑a‑chip.
3) Evaluate efficacy in obese mice by adipocyte transplantation and a transgenic knock‑in model; benchmark against classical “blocking” (Ccl2−/−) controls.

Design and methods
Genome engineering
- CRISPR-HDR in murine preadipocytes: replace Ccl2 CDS with Alox15‑T2A‑mNeonGreen, preserving native promoter/super‑enhancer (“Ccl2→Alox15”). Isogenic WT and Ccl2 knockout lines as controls. Confirm single-allele edit by long-read sequencing; off-targets by GUIDE‑seq subset.
- Differentiation to adipocytes; adipocyte identity by lipid accumulation, Adipoq/Pparg expression.

Mechanistic validation (ex vivo)
- Stress gating: TNFα, palmitate, hypoxia, ER stressors (tunicamycin) ± NF‑κB inhibitors. Readouts:
  - Transcription/protein: Ccl2 loss, Alox15 induction; p65 nuclear translocation.
  - Lipidomics (LC‑MS/MS): 17‑HDHA, 18‑HEPE, RvD1/D2, MaR1; AA‑eicosanoids (PGE2, LTB4, 12‑/15‑HETE).
  - Monocyte chemotaxis (transwells) to conditioned media; neutralization with anti‑CCL2 or SPM receptor antagonists; 5‑LOX inhibition (zileuton) to test paracrine completion.
  - Adipocyte lipolysis and FFA release; mitochondrial stress (Seahorse) to ensure metabolic competence.

Organ‑on‑a‑chip (Aim 2)
- Tri‑culture microphysiological system: engineered adipocytes + human microvascular endothelium + bone‑marrow–derived macrophages under lipotoxic/hypoxic flow.
- Perturbations: palmitate, oscillatory hypoxia, LPS. Readouts:
  - Macrophage polarization/resolution: scRNA‑seq (M1/M2/resolving gene programs; SPM receptor expression Fpr2/ALX, Gpr32 orthologs), flow cytometry (CD11c/CD206), phagocytosis of apoptotic adipocytes, efferocytosis index.
  - Endothelial activation: VCAM1/ICAM1, barrier integrity (TEER).
  - Secretome multiplex: CCL2, IL‑6, TNFα, IL‑10; SPM panel by LC‑MS/MS.
  - Causality: add-back of CCL2 to S2R media; SPM receptor blockade; 5‑LOX inhibition.

In vivo efficacy (Aim 3)
A) Transplantation
- Obese DIO C57BL/6J (16 weeks HFD). Bilateral subcutaneous fat‑pad “plugs” of WT vs S2R vs Ccl2−/− adipocytes (randomized contralateral design) ± dietary EPA/DHA enrichment (substrate bias toward SPMs).
- 4–6 weeks post‑engraftment:
  - Adipose scRNA‑seq (stromal vascular fraction): macrophage states, dendritic/Treg populations, chemokine modules; Alox15 expression in adipocytes.
  - Tissue lipidomics (adipose, plasma): SPMs and AA‑eicosanoids; SPM:AA ratio.
  - Histology: crown‑like structures, F4/80 infiltration, fibrosis (Picrosirius).
  - Metabolism: GTT, ITT, fasting insulin/glucose; clamp subset.
  - Mechanism: systemic zileuton or Alox5−/− host to test requirement for macrophage 5‑LOX completion.

B) Adipocyte‑specific knock‑in
- Rosa26‑LSL‑Alox15 donor targeted to Ccl2 locus with floxed STOP; Adipoq‑Cre for adipocyte specificity. HFD challenge.
- Endpoints as above; whole‑depot impacts without transplantation artifacts.

Validation criteria and statistics
- Primary endpoint: reduction in monocyte chemotaxis ≥50% ex vivo and ≥30% reduction in adipose Ly6Chi monocytes in vivo versus WT; superiority over Ccl2−/−.
- Biochemical switch: ≥3‑fold induction of 17‑HDHA/18‑HEPE with stress, SPM:AA‑eicosanoid ratio shift ≥2‑fold.
- Functional: improved GTT AUC ≥20% and reduced crown‑like structures ≥30% vs WT; maintained adiponectin/leptin balance.
- Power: n≥10 per group for in vivo endpoints (α=0.05, 1−β=0.8). Mixed‑effects models for repeated measures; FDR control for scRNA‑seq.

Falsification and decision points
- If benefits disappear with 5‑LOX blockade or in Alox5−/− hosts, resolution depends on paracrine completion (desired mechanism). If benefits persist, investigate adipocyte‑intrinsic SPM action.
- If Alox15 yields excess 12‑/15‑HETE (pro‑inflammatory), pivot to Ccl2→Cyp2j2 (E/E‑resolvins) or to Ccl2→15‑PGDH (PGE2 catabolism) while preserving the same stress‑gated switch architecture.
- If Ccl2 locus editing impairs adipocyte fitness, retarget to Saa3 or Lcn2 loci (alternative NF‑κB–responsive danger genes).

Risk management
- Off‑target inflammation: monitor 12‑/15‑HETE; bias substrates with EPA/DHA diet; consider Alox15 variant with reduced AA turnover.
- Systemic spillover: quantify plasma SPMs and cytokines; depot‑restricted delivery and adipocyte‑specific Cre.

Milestones
- M1 (Month 3): Edited adipocytes validated; stress‑induced Alox15 and SPM precursor surge confirmed.
- M2 (Month 6): Chip data show flipped macrophage/endothelial responses; scRNA‑seq resolution signatures.
- M3 (Month 12): Transplant study meets primary endpoints and outperforms Ccl2−/−.
- M4 (Month 18): Transgenic confirmation; dossier for translational vector strategy.

Impact
This single stress‑gated promoter swap directly targets a dominant adipocyte inflammatory mechanism (CCL2‑driven monocyte recruitment) and converts it into an SPM‑generating circuit. The same triggers that normally amplify adipose inflammation now initiate its resolution, turning a pathogenic feedback loop into a therapeutic one.

Title
Preempting the adipocyte inflammatory switch by restoring the α-ketoglutarate:succinate ratio to maintain PHD activity and suppress HIF-1α-driven chemokine induction

Question–Hypothesis (merged)
Do short, time-locked elevations of intracellular α-ketoglutarate (αKG) in stressed adipocytes prevent the decisive transition to an inflammatory state by sustaining prolyl-hydroxylase (PHD)–mediated HIF-1α degradation, thereby reducing adipocyte-derived chemokines and downstream adipose inflammation in obesity?

Atomic strategy
Control a single metabolic ratio—the adipocyte αKG:succinate balance—at the moment of hypoxia/lipotoxic stress to keep HIF-1α off and block the initiation of adipocyte-driven inflammation.

Rationale
- In obesity, adipocyte hypoxia and lipid overload increase succinate and lower αKG, inhibiting PHDs and stabilizing HIF-1α, which induces Ccl2/Cxcl chemokines and amplifies NF-κB signaling.
- A transient, precisely timed increase in αKG (with ascorbate as a PHD cofactor) should restore PHD activity, avert HIF-1α stabilization, and preempt the inflammatory switch.
- This intervention directly targets an adipocyte-intrinsic mechanism and is testable on available platforms.

Specific aims
1) Map the adipocyte decision boundary for the inflammatory switch.
2) Test whether αKG pulses, delivered at the boundary, prevent adipocyte inflammatory programming ex vivo.
3) Validate, in vivo, that time-locked αKG treatment or adipocyte PHD2 activation suppresses early adipose inflammation in diet-induced obesity.

Aim 1: Define the decision boundary (organ-on-a-chip + snRNA-seq)
- Platform: Adipose organ-on-a-chip with primary murine or human adipocytes under controlled O2 (21%→1–5%) and NEFA (palmitate/oleate) ramps; optional macrophage/endothelial channels for paracrine readouts.
- Reporters/assays:
  - Adipocyte HIF activity: HRE-luciferase or ODD-luc reporter adipocytes.
  - Real-time metabolites: microdialysis LC–MS to quantify intracellular/extracellular αKG and succinate; NADH/NAD+ biosensor if feasible.
  - Secretome: multiplex chemokines (CCL2, CXCL1/2), IL-6, SAA3.
- Single-nucleus RNA-seq:
  - Collect nuclei along a time course spanning pre-hypoxia, boundary crossing, and post-boundary states.
  - Pseudotime to identify the earliest transcriptional inflection preceding chemokine upregulation.
- Output: A quantitative threshold (αKG:succinate ratio and O2 level) and time window predicting chemokine induction and macrophage recruitment on-chip.

Aim 2: Preempt the switch ex vivo with αKG pulses (organ-on-a-chip)
- Intervention: Short pulses (e.g., 30–120 min) of cell-permeable dimethyl-αKG ± ascorbate, delivered when HIF reporter rises or when αKG:succinate approaches the Aim 1 threshold.
- Controls: Vehicle; dimethyl-succinate (negative control); ascorbate alone; timing-mismatch αKG pulses (after HIF is already high).
- Readouts:
  - Primary: HIF-1α stabilization (reporter, immunoblot), Ccl2/Cxcl transcription, chemokine secretion.
  - Secondary: Macrophage adhesion/migration across the endothelial channel; NF-κB target induction; mitochondrial ROS and membrane potential.
  - Minimum effective dose and pulse schedule to suppress chemokines without impairing adipocyte lipid handling.
- Success criterion: ≥50% reduction in chemokine output and macrophage recruitment with preserved adipocyte metabolic function when αKG is pulsed at, but not after, the boundary.

Aim 3: Validate prevention in vivo (transgenic mouse + snRNA-seq)
- Models:
  - Diet-induced obesity (HFD).
  - Adipocyte HIF reporter mice (HRE-luc or ODD-luc) to time-lock dosing.
  - Adipoq-CreERT2;Rosa26-TetOn-PHD2 (adipocyte-inducible PHD2 overexpression) for a genetic test of mechanism.
- Interventions:
  - Pharmacologic: Oral or i.p. dimethyl-αKG ± ascorbate given as brief pulses initiated during early HFD (weeks 1–3) and/or when in vivo adipose HIF signal rises above baseline.
  - Genetic: Induce adipocyte PHD2 overexpression at the same early window.
- Assessments:
  - Early (2–4 weeks HFD) and mid (8–10 weeks) endpoints.
  - snRNA-seq of adipose depots to quantify adipocyte state transitions and inflammatory gene programs; cell-type–resolved effects.
  - Metabolites: adipose αKG and succinate (LC–MS); tissue pimonidazole staining for hypoxia.
  - Inflammation: CCL2/CXCLs in adipose interstitial fluid; F4/80+ crown-like structures; stromal vascular fraction flow cytometry (Ly6Chi monocytes, M1/M2 macrophages).
  - Metabolic outcomes: insulin and glucose tolerance; lipolysis response.
- Success criterion: With time-locked αKG or PHD2 activation, reduced adipose chemokines and macrophage infiltration vs. controls, preserved adipocyte function, and improved insulin sensitivity.

Key controls and rigor
- Cell-type specificity: Parallel treatment of macrophages alone to rule out dominant macrophage-intrinsic effects; deconvolution by snRNA-seq.
- Temporal specificity: Same total αKG dose given off-window must not replicate benefit.
- Dose–response and safety: Monitor lactate, ketones, and acid–base status; adjust pulse intensity.
- Mechanism confirmation: Rescue experiment with dimethyl-succinate co-administration to re-lower αKG:succinate and test reversibility.

Milestones and go/no-go
- M1: Decision boundary defined with a predictive αKG:succinate threshold (Aim 1).
- M2: On-chip αKG pulses reduce chemokines ≥50% when timed to boundary (Aim 2).
- M3: In vivo, early pulsed αKG or adipocyte PHD2 activation reduces crown-like structures ≥30% and improves insulin tolerance (Aim 3).
- If M1 fails to reveal a clear threshold, pivot to enforcing PDH flux (acute PDK inhibition) to reduce lactate/HIF activation using the same timing logic on-chip, then in vivo.

Expected impact
A single-lever, time-locked metabolic intervention that keeps adipocytes below the HIF-driven inflammatory threshold, directly targeting the mechanism by which adipocytes initiate inflammation and preventing adipose tissue inflammation at its origin.

Title
Turning adipocytes into pro-resolving “healer cells” by installing an intrinsic lipid-mediator class switch

Central hypothesis-question
Can a single adipocyte-intrinsic switch that redirects eicosanoid flux toward specialized pro-resolving mediators (SPMs) convert inflammatory adipocytes into cells that actively resolve inflammation and thereby reduce adipose-tissue inflammation without weight loss?

Atomic strategy (single conceptual insight)
Install an adipocyte lipid-mediator class switch by activating ALOX15-driven SPM biosynthesis, thereby suppressing NF-κB–dependent chemokines (for example CCL2) and T cell–activating signals while increasing paracrine pro-resolving outputs that reprogram local immunity.

Rationale
- In obesity, adipocytes drive inflammation by secreting CCL2/IL-6 and proinflammatory lipid mediators and by releasing FFAs that activate TLR pathways in immune cells.
- A rare adipocyte state is predicted to exist in metabolically healthy obesity that exhibits high expression of SPM-synthesis enzymes and checkpoint ligands and low chemokine output; mimicking this state should convert diseased adipocytes into “healer cells.”
- ALOX15 is a gatekeeping enzyme for SPM production from omega-3 substrates; enforcing its expression provides a minimal, testable switch with system-wide impact.

Specific aims

Aim 1. Discover the human “healer adipocyte” program and its control nodes.
- Cohorts: Subcutaneous and visceral adipose biopsies from individuals with obesity who are metabolically healthy vs unhealthy (matched for BMI, sex, age).
- Approach: Nuclei-optimized scRNA-seq of adipocyte-enriched fractions; integrate with bulk lipidomics on matched tissue.
- Analyses:
  - Identify rare adipocyte clusters with high SPM-pathway gene expression (for example ALOX15, ALOX12, ELOVL2/5), high ADIPOQ/CD274 (PD-L1), and low CCL2/IL6/MHCII.
  - Infer regulons (for example KLF2/4, NR4A1) from scRNA-seq; prioritize ALOX15 as the minimal actionable node.
- Validation: qPCR and targeted LC-MS/MS of SPMs (RvD1, RvE1, MaR1, LXA4) from sorted mature adipocytes; confirm low CCL2 protein.

Milestone success criteria (Aim 1)
- Identification of a reproducible ALOX15hi adipocyte state in ≥2 depots with a coherent anti-inflammatory/immune-checkpoint signature and elevated SPMs ex vivo.

Aim 2. Reprogram human inflamed adipocytes into “healer cells” by ALOX15 activation and test causal mechanisms on-chip.
- Cells: Primary human adipose stromal cells (ASCs) from metabolically unhealthy donors differentiated into adipocytes; inflammatory priming with palmitate or TNF.
- Perturbation:
  - CRISPRa (dCas9-VP64) with gRNAs tiled to ALOX15 promoter/enhancers.
  - Substrate support with physiological DHA/EPA in culture media (no pharmacologic SPMs added).
- Readouts:
  - Lipid mediator profiling (LC-MS/MS): increase in SPMs; decrease in proinflammatory eicosanoids.
  - Secretome/transcriptome: reduced CCL2/IL6/SAA, reduced HLA-DRA, increased ADIPOQ and CD274 surface protein; NF-κB reporter suppression.
- Mechanistic tests (organ-on-a-chip):
  - Human adipocyte–macrophage–CD8 T cell microphysiological system under metabolic stress.
  - Outcomes: macrophage TNFα/IL-1β down, enhanced efferocytosis; reduced CD8 T cell IFN-γ and proliferation.
  - Blockade experiments: 15-LOX inhibitor and SPM receptor antagonists to reverse benefits; PD-L1 blocking antibody to dissect T cell effects.

Milestone success criteria (Aim 2)
- ≥3-fold increase in total SPMs with ≥50% reduction in CCL2 release from reprogrammed adipocytes; ≥40% reduction in macrophage NF-κB activity and T cell IFN-γ on-chip, all reversed by 15-LOX/SPM-pathway inhibition.

Aim 3. Test therapeutic conversion in vivo without weight loss using an adipocyte-specific transgenic model.
- Model: Diet-induced obese mice (16 weeks high-fat diet).
- Genetic reprogramming:
  - Adipoq-rtTA; TRE-Alox15 double-transgenic to induce Alox15 specifically in mature adipocytes in adulthood; parallel Adipoq-Cre; Rosa26-LSL-dCas9-VP64 + Alox15 gRNA line if available.
  - Induction after obesity is established; duration 3–6 weeks; pair-fed controls to match caloric intake and maintain body weight.
- Outcomes:
  - Adipose tissue inflammation: flow cytometry of SVF (CD11c+ M1-like macrophages, eosinophils, Tregs), cytokines, and chemokines; histology of crown-like structures.
  - Lipid mediators: adipose SPMs and eicosanoids by LC-MS/MS.
  - Immune-crosstalk: adipocyte PD-L1 expression; ex vivo T cell activation assays with adipocyte co-culture.
  - Metabolic: insulin tolerance and glucose tolerance tests adjusted for body weight and fat mass; serum FFAs.
- Causality tests:
  - Pharmacologic 15-LOX inhibition during induction to abrogate effects.
  - Anti–PD-L1 to test T cell–mediated contribution.
- Safety: oxidative stress markers and lipid peroxidation in adipose; liver enzymes.

Milestone success criteria (Aim 3)
- Significant reduction in adipose CD11c+ macrophages and crown-like structures and ≥2-fold increase in tissue SPMs without changes in body weight; improved insulin sensitivity independent of weight; reversal by 15-LOX inhibition.

Experimental details and controls
- Donor selection and power: n≥12 donors per human group (MHO vs MUO); mouse cohorts n≥12/arm for adequate power on inflammatory endpoints.
- Statistics: pre-registered primary endpoints (CCL2, total SPMs, CD11c+ macrophages).
- Controls: CRISPRa non-targeting gRNA; DHA/EPA substrate controls; vehicle vs inhibitor arms; depot-specific analyses (subcutaneous vs visceral).

Validation that the intervention directly targets adipocyte inflammatory mechanisms
- Demonstrate that ALOX15 activation in adipocytes decreases their intrinsic NF-κB target expression and chemokine output (CCL2/IL6), reduces antigen-presentation transcripts, and, via SPMs, reprograms macrophages and T cells toward resolution, satisfying the constraint of directly modulating adipocyte mechanisms that increase inflammation.

Risk assessment and alternatives
- If ALOX15 alone is insufficient: multiplex CRISPRa of ALOX15 with ELOVL2 to ensure DHA-derived substrate availability.
- If lipid peroxidation emerges: tune induction (Tet-on dose), add antioxidant buffering, or pivot to transcriptional regulators identified in Aim 1 (for example KLF4/NR4A1) that elevate the same SPM module.
- If PD-L1 is not engaged: rely on SPM-mediated macrophage reprogramming; alternatively test IL1RN upregulation discovered in Aim 1.

Readouts to confirm “healer adipocyte” identity
- High SPM output (RvD1/RvE1/MaR1/LXA4), high ADIPOQ and PD-L1, low CCL2/IL6/MHCII, reduced NF-κB reporter activity, and functional suppression of macrophage/T cell inflammatory outputs.

Deliverables and milestones by year
- Year 1: Human scRNA-seq maps; candidate module with ALOX15 prioritized; lipidomics confirmation.
- Year 2: CRISPRa reprogramming in primary human adipocytes; organ-on-a-chip functional validation; mechanism-of-action with inhibitors/blockade finalized.
- Year 3: Transgenic mouse induction study with causal reversals; dossier of biomarker panel and translational gRNA/chemogenomic leads.

Expected impact
A minimal, adipocyte-intrinsic switch based on ALOX15-mediated SPM biosynthesis offers a direct, testable route to convert inflamed fat into therapeutic tissue that resolves inflammation locally, improves metabolic function independent of weight loss, and establishes a blueprint for reprogramming diseased adipocytes into “healer cells.”

text:
Title
Adipocyte antigen-presentation silencing to convert fat into an anti-inflammatory tissue

Central hypothesis-question
Can enforcing a naturally occurring “CIITA-off” adipocyte state—found in lean adipose—silence MHC-II–dependent antigen presentation to CD4+ T cells and thereby reduce adipocyte-driven inflammation in obesity?

Atomic strategy (single perturbation)
Adipocyte-specific repression of CIITA, the master regulator of MHC-II, to abolish adipocyte antigen presentation and downstream Th1/M1 inflammatory amplification.

Rationale
Adipocytes increase inflammation by presenting antigen via MHC-II to CD4+ T cells, driving IFN-γ production and macrophage M1 polarization. scRNA-seq from lean adipose suggests a rare adipocyte state with minimal CIITA/HLA-D/II expression. Copying this “protective” state across all adipocytes should reduce immune activation at its source.

Specific aims

Aim 1. Discover and molecularly define protective CIITA-off adipocytes in healthy adipose using scRNA-seq.
- Samples: Epididymal (mouse) and subcutaneous (human donor) adipose; lean vs obese.
- Methods: Nuclei isolation + adipocyte-enriched snRNA-seq; integrate public lean datasets. Cluster adipocytes, quantify CIITA/MHC-II module scores, infer gene regulatory networks.
- Outputs:
  - Protective-state signature: low CIITA/MHC-II, reduced chemokines (CCL2/CCL5), low NF-κB target expression.
  - Upstream repressors/absence of inducers (e.g., reduced STAT1/IRF1 activity) and co-features to track (adiponectin high, mitochondrial stress low).
- Success criteria: Reproducible adipocyte cluster(s) with CIITA/MHC-II-low signature across species and depots; association with low local T-cell activation signatures.

Aim 2. Engineer adipocyte-wide CIITA repression and test in an obesity model.
- Model: Adipoq-Cre;Rosa26-LSL-dCas9-KRAB transgenic mice.
- Intervention: AAV8-adipocyte–tropic gRNAs targeting Ciita (vs scrambled) delivered at 6 weeks; high-fat diet (16 weeks).
- Primary readouts:
  - On-target: Ciita mRNA and MHC-II surface loss on Perilipin+ adipocytes (flow, RT-qPCR).
  - Antigen-presentation function: OT-II CD4+ T-cell proliferation/IFN-γ after OVA323–339 pulsing of isolated adipocytes.
- In vivo inflammation outcomes:
  - Adipose immune profiling (flow/scRNA-seq of SVF): CD4+ Th1/Th2 ratio, T-bet, IFN-γ; macrophage M1/M2 markers; TCR activation markers.
  - Cytokines/chemokines in adipose interstitial fluid and serum: IFN-γ, TNF, IL-6, CCL2.
  - Metabolic secondary readouts: insulin and glucose tolerance (exploratory).
- Controls: Dendritic cell and macrophage MHC-II unaffected (cell-type specificity control); IFN-γ challenge to test resistance of Ciita repression.
- Success criteria: ≥80% reduction in adipocyte MHC-II; ≥50% reduction in adipocyte-driven CD4+ T-cell activation ex vivo; significant decrease in adipose Th1/M1 markers in vivo.

Aim 3. Validate immune-calming function of engineered adipocytes in an adipose–immune organ-on-a-chip.
- Platform: Tri-culture chip with primary adipocytes (Ciita-repressed vs control), autologous CD4+ T cells, and monocyte-derived macrophages; optional microvascular endothelium channel.
- Conditions: Lipotoxic stress (palmitate), hypoxia-reoxygenation cycles to mimic obese adipose microenvironment.
- Readouts:
  - T cells: activation (CD69/CD25), cytokines (IFN-γ), proliferation (CFSE), cytotoxic mediators.
  - Macrophages: iNOS/Arg1, TNF/IL-10 secretion, phagocytic index.
  - Paracrine milieu: multiplex cytokines/chemokines; EV cargo profiling (inflammatory miRNAs).
  - Barrier function (if endothelium present): TEER/permeability.
- Causality tests: Add-back of CIITA via mRNA electroporation or IFN-γ priming in control vs Ciita-repressed adipocytes; antigen-dependence by OVA peptide pulsing.
- Success criteria: ≥50% reduction in IFN-γ and TNF; shift to M2-like macrophage markers; improved endothelial barrier vs control chips.

Key measurements and analytics
- scRNA-seq: adipocyte state maps, Th1/Th2 gene signatures, macrophage polarization states, ligand–receptor inference (e.g., MHC-II–TCR, chemokine–receptor pairs).
- Flow cytometry: adipocyte MHC-II on Perilipin+ cells; T-cell activation; macrophage polarization.
- Functional assays: OT-II proliferation; cytokine multiplex; insulin signaling in adipocytes (pAKT).
- Statistics: pre-registered endpoints; power for primary outcomes; batch-corrected mixed models for scRNA-seq.

Milestones and go/no-go gates
- M1: Identification of CIITA-off adipocyte cluster and signature conserved across datasets (go).
- M2: Efficient, adipocyte-specific Ciita repression and loss of function in antigen presentation (go).
- M3: Demonstrated reduction of T-cell activation and M1 polarization in vivo and on-chip (go to translational exploration: adipocyte-targeted AAV gRNA or siRNA therapeutics).

Risk assessment and single-path alternatives within the same mechanism
- If CIITA repression is incomplete or compensated, target another obligate MHC-II component (Rfx5 or Cd74) with CRISPRi while retaining the same antigen-presentation–silencing mechanism.
- If systemic IFN-γ overrides repression, multiplex dCas9-KRAB to Ciita promoter and IFN-γ–responsive enhancers identified in Aim 1.

Validation of therapeutic relevance
- Test delayed intervention: deliver Ciita gRNAs after 8 weeks of high-fat diet to assess reversal of established inflammation.
- Human relevance: organ-on-chip with human primary adipocytes and allogeneic CD4+ T cells; CRISPRi delivery via lipid nanoparticles to confirm translatability.

Expected impact
A single, cell-intrinsic switch—CIITA repression—reprograms adipocytes into a protective, antigen-presentation–silent state that reduces upstream immune activation. This converts fat from an inflammation amplifier into a tissue that maintains immune quiescence, meeting the goal of making adipocytes allies rather than targets.
