text:
Title
Electroaffinity Coacervate Stencil (ECS): a cell-free, implant-free, self-terminating tertiary niche that shapes endogenous bioelectric fields to stage and organize regeneration in volumetric muscle loss and critical-size bone defects

Central hypothesis
A transient, ionically conductive, fully resorbable coacervate that (i) amplifies and shapes endogenous wound DC fields and (ii) condenses/presents endogenous morphogens will impose spatial architecture and stage transitions in repair. As tissue function returns (bridging, revascularization, contractility/load-bearing), local impedance and strain profiles normalize, passively extinguishing the field and mechanically fracturing the coacervate, thereby autogenerating niche dissolution and termination.

Atomic strategy
Exploit the injury’s own bioelectricity as the master organizing variable by deploying a field-shaping, ion-conductive coacervate that captures and re-presents endogenous cues. Healing short-circuits the field and increases cyclic strain, which together disassemble the stencil—closing the loop without timers, cells, or permanent implants.

Innovation
- Uses endogenous DC fields as a global coordinator for recruitment, alignment, and vascular patterning.
- Harvests and reprograms endogenous cytokine/growth-factor traffic via heparin-mimetic “affinity condensers,” avoiding exogenous biologics.
- Couples niche persistence to functional readouts (conductivity/contractility or mineral load-bearing), yielding self-termination tied to success.

Specific aims
1) Engineer an injectable, resorbable Electroaffinity Coacervate Stencil that self-assembles in situ, aligns to local DC field lines, and spatially patterns endogenous cell ingress and morphogen presentation.
2) Program a staged repair sequence—controlled inflammation → progenitor expansion → differentiation → matrix remodeling—encoded by environment-sensing coacervate transitions without exogenous cells.
3) Demonstrate closed-loop, function-coupled self-dissolution and regenerative efficacy in murine volumetric muscle loss (VML) and calvarial critical-size defect models.

Design overview
- Form factor: Two liquid precursors co-injected to form a percolating, thixotropic, ion-conductive coacervate within the defect. No solid implants or hardware; the material is fully enzymatically/bioresorbably cleared.
- Chemistry (all GRAS-amenable, degradable):
  - Polyanion: sulfated hyaluronan or polyphosphate-enriched hyaluronan (bone) or sulfated alginate (muscle).
  - Polycation: arginine-rich chitosan or poly-L-lysine-graft-oligolysine (protease-cleavable backbones).
  - Affinity domains: heparin-mimetic sulfation patterns + short aptamer/peptoid motifs for reversible binding of SDF-1, VEGF, IGF-1, PDGF, BMPs, HGF from interstitial fluid.
  - Mechanolabile crosslinks: catch-bond peptide crosslinks engineered to rupture under cyclic strain ≥ physiologic (muscle) or to unbind under high local stiffness/mineral shear (bone).
  - Enzymolabile safety fuses: ALP-cleavable (bone) and MMP-2/9-cleavable (remodeling) linkers to guarantee clearance if function remains sub-threshold.
- Field-shaping: The ECS’s ionic conductivity (fixed anions, mobile counterions) and anisotropic microphase separation under mild DC fields create “electrical rails” that:
  - Impose myofiber-longitudinal alignment (VML).
  - Bias endothelial sprouting and arteriolar ingress along rails.
  - Direct periosteal/endosteal progenitor centripetal migration (calvaria).

Staged repair program (encoded in ECS physicochemistry)
- Phase I: Controlled inflammation (hours–days)
  - Action: High ROS/low pH strengthens electrostatic condensation and increases affinity for proinflammatory chemokines (IL-8/CXCL1), dampening their free diffusion while permissively presenting CCL2/CCL5 to recruit reparative monocytes.
  - Spatial effect: Field-shaped rails channel leukocyte ingress into laminar “repair corridors,” preventing diffuse damage.
- Phase II: Progenitor recruitment and expansion (days)
  - Action: ECS concentrates endogenous SDF-1, HGF/IGF-1, and VEGF via heparin-mimetic domains and releases them in response to protease activity from recruited cells (positive feedback). DC field galvanotaxis aligns satellite cells/MSCs/periosteal progenitors and endothelial tip cells along rails.
  - Mechanics: Coacervate soft (0.5–2 kPa muscle; 2–5 kPa bone) supports proliferation.
- Phase III: Differentiation and matrix deposition (days–weeks)
  - Action: Lactate fall and pH normalization reduce charge density; ionic crosslink annealing increases storage modulus (muscle 8–12 kPa; bone microdomains nucleate CaP via polyphosphate), biasing myogenic fusion or osteogenic differentiation.
  - Spatial effect: Rails template myotube bundles or intramembranous ossification fronts bridging the gap.
- Phase IV: Remodeling and autonomous termination (weeks)
  - Termination triggers (closed-loop):
    - Electrical: Bridging + revascularization reduce local transexcitable potential and DC field magnitude; diminished electrophoretic ion enrichment collapses coacervate percolation (sol–gel reversal).
    - Mechanical: Restored cyclic strain (muscle) or high stiffness/load transfer (bone) breaks mechanolabile crosslinks, disintegrating rails.
    - Enzymatic failsafes: ALP (bone) and balanced MMP activity (muscle/bone) complete dissolution.
  - Outcome: ECS liquefies to soluble oligomers cleared via lymphatics, ending niche activity without residual implant.

Experimental plan

Aim 1: ECS engineering and field-shaping
- In vitro
  - Build coacervates with tunable conductivity (1–10 mS/cm) and anisotropy under 50–200 mV/mm DC fields.
  - Microfluidic wound-field phantom: show rail formation, electric field line capture, and stability thresholds.
  - Endogenous factor capture assays using rodent serum/interstitial fluid to quantify binding/release kinetics for SDF-1, VEGF, IGF-1, PDGF, BMP-2/7.
- Ex vivo
  - Rat muscle and mouse calvarial explants: map ECS alignment vs native fiber/bone axes; quantify galvanotaxis of primary satellite cells, ECs, and periosteal progenitors without exogenous chemokines.

Success criteria: Rails align within 10° of native axes; ≥2× directional persistence of cell migration; selective enrichment of target morphogens (Kd,app 10–100 nM) with reversible release.

Aim 2: Programmed staging without exogenous biologics
- In vitro co-culture triads (immune–progenitor–endothelial) within ECS under dynamic pH/ROS/protease profiles mimicking phases I–III.
  - Readouts: neutrophil chemokinesis suppression with preserved monocyte recruitment; progenitor proliferation index; oriented tubulogenesis; myogenic fusion index or osteogenic marker expression.
- Mechano-tuning: cyclic strain application (0–10%, 1–2 Hz) to determine mechanofracture thresholds and differentiation outcomes.
- Bone-specific nucleation: demonstrate CaP deposition along rails via polyphosphate domains without exogenous BMP.

Success criteria: Sequential shift in secretome (pro- to pro-resolve), 3–5× increase in aligned myotube length or mineralized bridge continuity vs controls; strain-dependent rail fragmentation thresholds aligned with physiologic function.

Aim 3: In vivo efficacy and autonomous termination
- Models
  - VML: Mouse tibialis anterior 20% ablation; ECS injected to fill void; no cells/implants.
  - Bone: Mouse 4-mm calvarial critical-size defect; ECS fills defect; no grafts.
- Measurements
  - Bioelectric mapping: serial noninvasive surface electrodes + microelectrode arrays to quantify field magnitude/gradient over time.
  - Function-coupled dissolution: in vivo fluorescent mechanophore reporters embedded in ECS to track bond scission with treadmill-induced contraction (VML) or bite-force/forelimb loading surrogates (bone).
  - Outcomes: force restoration (ex vivo twitch/tetanic), gait symmetry; micro-CT bone bridging, elastic modulus; vascular perfusion (laser speckle), aligned collagen/myofiber orientation (SHG), immune phenotypes (flow cytometry), endogenous progenitor lineage tracing.
  - Persistence/termination: quantify ECS mass vs local impedance/contractility; time to complete clearance; absence of chronic inflammation or ectopic mineralization.
- Controls: saline, inert degradable gel (no field-shaping/affinity), ECS with disabled mechanolabile links.

Success criteria: ≥50% recovery of contractile force by week 6 (VML) and ≥60% defect bridging with lamellar alignment by week 8 (bone), with ECS clearance temporally coincident with restored impedance/strain within 10% of contralateral tissue.

Risk mitigation and alternatives
- If endogenous field magnitude is insufficient: add bio-safe ionic asymmetry enhancers (e.g., transient polyphosphate microdomains) to increase local field capture without external stimulation.
- If morphogen capture is off-target: tune sulfation patterns/aptamer ratios; include competitive decoys for pro-scarring cytokines (e.g., TGF-β1-biased binding while sparing TGF-β3).
- If termination lags in low-mobility contexts: lower crosslink density; increase ALP/MMP-cleavable linkers; incorporate pH-normalization–sensitive charge-shielding groups.

Milestones and endpoints
- Year 1: ECS library; validated field-shaping and endogenous morphogen condensation; staged program in vitro.
- Year 2: Ex vivo organotypic alignment and differentiation; mechano-threshold tuning.
- Year 3: In vivo VML and calvarial efficacy with documented closed-loop termination and absence of residues or chronic inflammation.

Impact
This work reframes regenerative engineering around a single global control variable—the wound’s own bioelectricity—converted by a transient ionic stencil into spatial architecture and timed morphodynamics. By tying material persistence to functional closure of the circuit (conductivity and contractility/load), the niche ends itself when its job is done, meeting the constraints of cell-free, implant-free, spatially organized, staged, and self-terminating regeneration.

text:
Title
Brake-Clearing, Mechano-Resolving Tertiary Niche for Skeletal Muscle and Bone Repair

Central hypothesis
A fully resorbable, anisotropic affinity-hydrogel that selectively scavenges endogenous inhibitory ligands (“brakes”) while templating tissue architecture will convert non-healing volumetric muscle loss (VML) and critical-size bone defects into self-organizing, self-terminating regenerative niches. Persistence of the niche is coupled to local functional recovery via mechanosensitive linkers that dissolve as contractile/load-bearing activity returns.

Atomic strategy
Instead of adding pro-healing factors, create a temporary “inhibitory sink” that locally subtracts anti-regenerative cues (fibrosis-, senescence-, and anti-angiogenesis–associated ligands and matrices). This subtraction unmasks the body’s latent pro-regenerative program, while anistropic microarchitecture imposes spatial order. The material self-erases when endogenous function resumes, closing the niche automatically.

Specific aims
1) Build a selective inhibitory-sink material that captures pro-fibrotic, anti-angiogenic, senescence-associated, and anti-proliferative signals without depleting essential morphogens.
2) Impose spatial organization of recruited immune, vascular, and progenitor populations via anisotropic mechanics and microchannels matched to muscle fascicles and osteonal units.
3) Implement a closed-loop, function-coupled termination mechanism that dissolves the niche when local cyclic strain/load surpasses preset thresholds and inhibitory ligand levels fall.

Platform design: Brake-Clearing Affinity Hydrogel (BCAH)
- Base matrix
  - Injectable, in situ–forming microporous annealed particle (MAP) hydrogel composed of hyaluronan- and gelatin-methacrylate microgels (food-grade photoinitiator or Michael-type click; body-temperature curing).
  - Fully resorbable linkers (ester, hydrazone, boronate ester) with tunable half-lives (days to weeks).
- Architecture and mechanics
  - Uniaxially aligned, interconnected microchannels (50–120 μm for VML; 150–300 μm for bone) produced by aligned microgel rods and directional annealing; provides guidance for myofiber alignment or osteon-like conduits.
  - Regional stiffness bands: 8–15 kPa for myogenic corridors; 20–40 kPa periosteal-facing zones for osteoprogenitor expansion; stiffer (60–100 kPa) load corridors to bias vessel/pericyte co-alignment.
- Inhibitory-sink modules (no exogenous cells or growth factors)
  - High-affinity, degradable capture motifs:
    - Pro-fibrotic/anti-proliferative: TGF-β1/3, myostatin (GDF8), activin A aptamers; latent TGF-β binding protein–mimetic peptides; decorin-mimetic sulfated domains.
    - Anti-angiogenic: thrombospondin-1 (CD36/β1-mimetic capture), endostatin/angiostatin heparin-mimetic microdomains.
    - Senescence/SASP resolution (time-gated): HMGB1, S100A8/9, CCL2, IL-6 aptamers protected by protease-cleavable masks (see temporal staging).
    - Axon/vessel repulsion (VML): semaphorin 3A, Netrin-1 molecularly imprinted nanoparticles (MIPs).
  - Non-depleting by-design: exclude capture for VEGF, PDGF, CXCL12 to preserve endogenous pro-regenerative gradients.
- Permissive adhesion without added growth factors
  - Minimalistic ECM ligand set (RGD, GFOGER, IKVAV) tethered at low density to permit migration and alignment without instructive morphogens.
- Delivery
  - Syringeable paste that interlocks with defect margins and cures within 3–5 minutes; no permanent hardware.

Mechanism: staged, subtraction-driven repair program
- Stage I: Controlled inflammation (0–72 h)
  - Immediate capture of TGF-β/myostatin/activin and anti-angiogenic ligands reduces early fibroblast overactivation and preserves pro-resolution macrophage polarization bandwidth.
  - SASP/DAMP capture sites remain masked by elastase/MMP-cleavable shields to avoid blunting necessary early recruitment.
  - Aligned channels permit rapid neutrophil/monocyte ingress; pore throats sized to reduce neutrophil extracellular trap retention.
- Stage II: Progenitor and vascular recruitment/expansion (days 3–14)
  - With brakes removed, endogenous CXCL12/VEGF fields drive satellite cell, periosteal/MSC, and endothelial ingrowth along channels and stiffness bands.
  - Time-gated unmasking (neutrophil elastase/MMP-9 threshold) exposes SASP/DAMP scavengers to resolve lingering chronic inflammation and reduce senescence spread.
  - Anti-angiogenic sink maintains high local angiogenic tone; pericyte engagement is favored by corridor stiffness.
- Stage III: Differentiation and matrix remodeling (weeks 2–8)
  - Gradual decline in inhibitory ligand concentration decreases sink occupancy; crosslink density drops as masked sites are exhausted and hydrolysis proceeds.
  - MMP-cleavable crosslinks permit cell-mediated tunnel widening; anisotropic stress fields align nascent myofibrils or collagen lamellae.
- Stage IV: Self-termination coupled to function
  - Mechanosensitive dissolution: supramolecular host–guest crosslinks (cyclodextrin–adamantane) and strain-labile dynamic covalent bonds (boronate ester/hydrazone) undergo accelerated dissociation under cyclic strain thresholds characteristic of recovered function:
    - VML: >3–5% local shear strain at 1–2 Hz during twitch/tetany.
    - Bone: >800–1500 microstrain during ambulatory loading.
  - Biochemical feedback: as anti-regenerative ligand levels fall below preset Kd windows, multivalent occupancy that previously stabilized the network diminishes, increasing mesh permeability and accelerating erosion.
  - If healing stalls (high inhibitor load, low strain), the niche persists and continues brake-clearing; if healing succeeds, increased strain plus low inhibitor load triggers rapid dissolution.

Closed-loop termination logic
- AND-gated degradation: fast when (cyclic strain ≥ threshold) AND (inhibitory-ligand occupancy ≤ setpoint); slow otherwise.
- Outputs: loss of material mass, pore coalescence, and microgel disassembly until complete resorption to sugars/amino acids.

Experimental plan

Aim 1: Build and validate inhibitory-sink selectivity and capacity
- Materials
  - Library of DNA/RNA aptamers and MIPs for target inhibitors; heparin-mimetic sulfated elastomers confined to microdomains to avoid VEGF depletion.
- Assays
  - Multiplex microdialysis in fibrin wound-mimic gels spiked with physiologic inhibitor panels; quantify on/off-target capture and release kinetics.
  - Protease-gated masking validation with controlled neutrophil elastase/MMP exposure profiles.
- Criteria
  - ≥80% reduction of target inhibitors within 6 h; ≤20% depletion of VEGF/CXCL12/PDGF.

Aim 2: Demonstrate architectural control and staged immune/progenitor dynamics in vivo
- Models
  - VML: rat tibialis anterior full-thickness defect; Bone: mouse critical-size femoral defect with stable external fixation (removed at union).
- Groups
  - BCAH; BCAH without affinity modules; blank MAP hydrogel; empty defect.
- Readouts
  - Early (48–72 h): scRNA-seq and spatial transcriptomics for macrophage states (M1/M2 spectrum), Tregs, neutrophils; cytokine microdialysis; inhibitor concentrations.
  - Days 7–14: satellite cell (Pax7+), FAPs, periosteal progenitors (Sca1+/CD105+), endothelial/pericyte co-alignment; vessel perfusion (lectin); axon penetration (NF200/ChAT).
  - Architecture: myofiber alignment index; osteon-like lamellae orientation by SHG; collagen III→I transition.
  - Function: in situ muscle tetanic force; bone torsional stiffness and microCT bridging.

Aim 3: Validate closed-loop, function-coupled self-termination
- Mechanosensitive dissolution
  - Implant BCAH with embedded, non-diffusive mechano-reporters (strain-activatable fluorophores) to map strain fields.
  - Correlate cyclic strain with hydrogel mass loss, mesh size (FRAP), and in vivo fluorescence of labeled microgels.
- Perturbations
  - Nerve block (VML) and limb unloading (bone) to suppress strain; treadmill and FES to enhance strain.
- Criteria
  - In high-strain cohorts: ≥80% material resorption by Week 6 (VML) or Week 8 (bone); in low-strain cohorts with persistent inhibitor load: ≤40% resorption with continued inhibitor capture.
  - Automatic dissolution onset when force recovery ≥60% baseline (VML) or torsional stiffness ≥50% contralateral (bone), without external cues.

Success metrics
- VML: ≥60% restoration of peak tetanic force by Week 8; myofiber cross-sectional area distribution overlapping contralateral; minimal interstitial collagen I/III scar fraction.
- Bone: bridging on microCT, torsional stiffness ≥60% at Week 10, organized osteons and marrow cavity reconstitution.
- Immune kinetics: timely resolution of neutrophils, M1→M2 transition, Treg rise; reduced chronic SASP markers.
- Safety: no heterotopic ossification (VML), no ectopic mineral (muscle corridors), normal serum cytokines.

Mechanistic falsification tests
- Swap inhibitory-sink panel to nonbinding controls: loss of regenerative benefit would confirm brake-clearing causality.
- Lock crosslinks to strain-insensitive chemistries: loss of function-coupled termination would prolong residence and increase fibrosis.
- Deplete VEGF/CXCL12 intentionally: predicts vascular and progenitor ingress failure despite brake-clearing.

Risk and mitigation
- Off-target sequestration of beneficial cues: confine heparin-mimetics to nanodomains; tune aptamer Kd above physiological levels for desired cues; validate in microdialysis.
- Insufficient mechanical cue for self-termination in immobilized patients: add time-lagged enzyme-cleavable backup (collagenase-sensitive linkers) that engage only after inhibitor levels remain low for >2 weeks.
- Aptamer immunogenicity/stability: use 2′-O-methyl and phosphorothioate ends; design DNase-susceptible backbones for late-phase clearance.

Milestones
- Year 1: Panel selection and on/off-target maps; first in vivo VML proof-of-concept with improved force and reduced fibrosis.
- Year 2: Bone defect efficacy with osteon organization; validated strain–dissolution curves and AND-gated termination.
- Year 3: Large-animal VML feasibility; GMP-compatible synthesis roadmap; pre-IDE safety package.

Impact
A single, cell-free, fully resorbable material that subtracts endogenous brakes and ties its own persistence to recovered function establishes a transient tertiary niche that recruits, organizes, and matures host cells, then disappears when no longer needed—closing the loop without added growth factors or implants.

text:
Title
FORCEgate: A cell-free, self-strengthening, function-gated dissolving scaffold that induces a transient tertiary regenerative niche for volumetric muscle loss and critical-size bone defects

Central hypothesis
A mechano-chemical “sentinel” embedded in a strain-stiffening, architecture-imposing, fully resorbable scaffold can convert correct, tissue-specific functional mechanics generated by recruited host cells into exposure of cryptic protease sites. This couples scaffold persistence to inadequate function and scaffold self-dissolution to restored function, enabling a staged, closed-loop regenerative program without exogenous cells or permanent hardware.

Atomic strategy
Force-gated proteolysis: cryptic, protease-degradable sequences are sterically masked inside peptide hairpins whose opening probability is a band-pass function of loading rate, amplitude, and direction. Only when local mechanics match those of healthy tissue (e.g., myofiber 1–2 Hz cyclic tension; osteogenic microstrain/compressive cycles) do hairpins open, unmasking degradable sites for cell-secreted proteases (e.g., MT1-MMP/MMP-13 in muscle; collagenases/MMP-2/-9 in bone). Sub-threshold or incoherent forces keep sites masked and simultaneously drive additional crosslinking/strain-stiffening, thereby strengthening the scaffold until competence emerges.

Specific aims
1) Engineer frequency- and amplitude-gated mechano-sentinels that expose protease-cleavable motifs only under tissue-appropriate mechanics.
2) Build a fully resorbable, anisotropic, strain-stiffening fibrous hydrogel that recruits and spatially organizes endogenous immune, vascular, and progenitor cells into a tertiary niche.
3) Demonstrate closed-loop, function-gated self-dissolution and staged repair in rodent VML and critical-size femoral defect models.
4) Map failure modes and safety boundaries; tune gating thresholds to avoid premature dissolution or chronic persistence.

Design overview
- Material platform (injectable or conformal patch):
  - Base network: peptide- and polysaccharide-based fibrous hydrogel (e.g., elastin-like polypeptide + hyaluronan/gelatin derivatives) forming aligned, micron-scale channels (20–80 μm) via directional freezing/electro-alignment; no permanent polymers or metals.
  - Dynamic crosslinks: reversible covalent and supramolecular bonds (e.g., oxime/boronate + hydrogen-bonding motifs) that self-heal and strain-stiffen under cyclic load; fatigue-resistant yet protease-degradable backbones.
  - Mechano-sentinels: peptide hairpins/cage domains embedded at network junctions that (i) mask MMP-cleavage sites and (ii) present catch/slip-bond kinetics with tunable opening under defined loading rates and directions.
  - Heparin-mimetic sulfated peptides grafted at low density to sequester endogenous chemokines/growth factors (SDF-1/CXCL12, VEGF-A, PDGF-BB, TGF-β1) from wound fluid, creating auto-refilling microgradients without exogenous factor dosing.
  - Optional mineral phase for bone: amorphous calcium phosphate nanoclusters tethered via alkaline phosphatase-cleavable linkers to bias osteogenic deposition once osteoblast activity rises; fully resorbable.

- Two tuned variants (same architecture, different gating and stiffness windows):
  - myo-FORCEgate: initial E’ 1–3 kPa, strain-stiffening to 10–15 kPa with alignment; band-pass opening near 1–2 Hz, ~5–10% fiber strain; exposes MT1-MMP/MMP-13 cleavage sites; fibers present laminin- and titin-mimetic motifs for satellite cell alignment and myotube fusion.
  - osteo-FORCEgate: initial E’ 20–40 kPa, strain-stiffening with compression to 100–300 kPa; band-pass opening under 0.5–5 Hz cyclic compression/shear, 1000–3000 με; exposes MMP-2/-9/-13 sites; fibers present collagen-mimetic and osteopontin-mimetic motifs; channels guide angiogenic invasion and osteon templating.

Spatiotemporal program (closed-loop, cell-instructed)
- Stage I: Controlled inflammation and recruitment (days 0–5)
  - Soft, high-porosity scaffold wicks serum; heparin-mimetics capture endogenous CXCL12/VEGF to attract neutrophils/monocytes/endothelial tip cells and mobilize satellite cells/MSCs/periosteal progenitors.
  - Ligand spacing and initial stiffness bias macrophages toward pro-resolving phenotypes; sentinel remains closed under disorganized forces; dynamic bonds dissipate erratic loads and prevent collapse.

- Stage II: Progenitor expansion and architectural patterning (days 3–21)
  - Cell traction aligns fibers; network strain-stiffens and increases ligand avidity (mechanical presentation of integrin ligands), creating anisotropic tracks.
  - Vascular cords use channels as conduits; pericyte recruitment via captured PDGF-BB; myoblasts fuse along fibers (VML) or osteoprogenitors align osteoid deposition (bone).
  - Sentinels still closed; sub-threshold cyclic loading drives additional crosslinking (mechanical annealing), further stabilizing architecture.

- Stage III: Differentiation and function readout (weeks 2–8+)
  - As myofibers achieve synchronous contraction or nascent bone experiences physiologic microstrain, local loading rates match sentinel band-pass; hairpins open intermittently, exposing MMP sites.
  - Cell-secreted proteases initiate localized cleavage; degradation is spatially restricted to competent microdomains, maintaining scaffold support elsewhere.

- Stage IV: Matrix remodeling and scaffold self-clearance (weeks 4–16+)
  - Progressive exposure of cleavage sites in functionally competent zones accelerates dissolution; endogenous ECM replaces scaffold; mineral phase resorbs as osteoid mineralizes (bone) or endomysial ECM matures (muscle).
  - If function declines (off-target fibrosis, inadequate loading), hairpins reclosing kinetics halt further exposure, pausing dissolution until competence returns.

Experimental plan

Aim 1: Engineer and tune mechano-sentinels
- Construct peptide hairpins masking MMP-cleavable cores with tunable opening kinetics (alter helix/loop composition).
- Single-fiber tethered force spectroscopy to quantify opening probability versus loading rate; calibrate band-pass to target tissues.
- In protease-containing media, demonstrate negligible cleavage under static/low-coherence loads and rapid cleavage under programmed cyclic loads; quantify with fluorescently quenched peptides.

Aim 2: Build anisotropic, strain-stiffening scaffolds that recruit and organize cells
- Fabricate aligned fibrous hydrogels with channel architectures; measure porosity, tortuosity, and strain-stiffening via rheology under cyclic loading.
- Perfuse with plasma to validate endogenous factor capture and retention; ELISA spatial mapping.
- In vitro co-cultures with primary macrophages, endothelial cells, and progenitors under no-cell-addition serum conditions to test recruitment from whole blood and spatial organization; quantify M1/M2 markers, angiogenic sprouting, myotube alignment or osteoid banding.

Aim 3: Demonstrate function-gated self-dissolution and staged repair in vivo
- VML (mouse tibialis anterior) and femoral critical-size defect (rat) models.
- Readouts:
  - Mechanics: ultrasound shear-wave elastography and nanoindentation for local E’; strain mapping by digital volume correlation under controlled limb motion.
  - Function: in vivo muscle twitch/ tetanic force at 1–2 Hz; bone microstrain under treadmill/controlled loading.
  - Dissolution mapping: quenched-fluorogenic sentinel reporters; histology for scaffold remnants vs new ECM; μCT for bone volume.
  - Cell dynamics: flow cytometry/spatial transcriptomics for immune and progenitor trajectories; vascular perfusion casting.
- Controls: no-sentinel degradable scaffold (timer-based), always-open MMP scaffold (premature loss), non-strain-stiffening isotropic scaffold.

Aim 4: Safety, failure modes, and tunability
- Overload/underload regimens to map the dissolution-operating window.
- Off-target protease environments (infection, hyperinflammation) to test resistance to premature exposure.
- Long-term resorption kinetics and metabolite profiling; absence of persistent fragments.

Success criteria (go/no-go)
- Sentinel selectivity: ≥10× difference in cleavage rate between target versus off-target loading regimens in protease-rich media.
- Architecture and recruitment: ≥2× increase in aligned myotube length density (VML) or osteon-like organization (bone) versus controls; ≥50% increase in perfused microvessel density within channels by week 3.
- Function before dissolution: ≥70% native-specific force (VML) or bridging with ≥60% native torsional strength (bone) prior to ≥50% scaffold mass loss in competent regions.
- Closed-loop dissolution: spatial correlation (r ≥ 0.7) between high-function microdomains and scaffold clearance; persistence where function is sub-threshold.

Innovation
- Dissolution keyed to functional mechanics via force-gated proteolysis, not time or concentration.
- A single governing principle—mechanics-controlled exposure of cryptic sites—drives recruitment staging, architectural maturation, and self-termination.
- One platform, two tunings (myo/osteo) using identical mechano-logic but different thresholds.

Risk mitigation
- If frequency selectivity is insufficient, introduce dual-gating (mechanics + local biochemical cofactor such as alkaline phosphatase for bone or Ca2+-responsive masking for muscle) while keeping the core mechanogating principle.
- If tissue forces are too weak early, integrate transient exogenous cyclic loading regimens (physical therapy) to promote alignment and strengthening without chemical additions.

Expected outcomes and impact
- A fully resorbable, cell-free, closed-loop regenerative niche that strengthens while needed and exits only when endogenous tissue proves competence.
- Reduced risk of premature scaffold loss or chronic foreign body persistence.
- A generalizable design logic for other mechanically active tissues (tendon, myocardium, cartilage).

Timeline and milestones
- Year 1: Sentinel library design and calibration; scaffold fabrication and mechanics; in vitro recruitment/organization.
- Year 2: In vivo VML proof-of-concept; demonstrate function-before-dissolution correlation.
- Year 3: Critical-size bone defect study; parameter tuning; safety and failure mapping; pre-IND enabling data package.

Title
Mechano-enzymatic Writeable Scaffolds (MEWS) that Convert Themselves into Permanent Tissue While Self-Terminating Upon Functional Recovery

Central Hypothesis (question = goal)
Can a fully resorbable scaffold be programmed so that endogenous cell activity (traction, lineage-specific enzymes, perfusion) is the only “write head” that: (i) recruits and patterns host cells into a de novo tertiary niche, (ii) locally converts transient scaffold domains into permanent, tissue-appropriate matrix (muscle collagen or bone mineralized matrix), and (iii) erases all remaining temporary material once physiologic function (contractility or load-bearing) returns?

Atomic Strategy
Dual-gated conversion: Scaffold domains remain soluble and pro-regenerative until they experience the coincidence of two endogenous signals from invading host cells—integrin-mediated traction above a tuned threshold AND lineage-relevant enzyme activity (MMPs/LOX for muscle, ALP/collagenases for bone). This dual input unmasks irreversible chemistries that polymerize or mineralize the local scaffold into mature ECM analogs. As contractility or load resumes and oxygenation normalizes, built-in mechanophore and O2-sensitive linkers trigger depolymerization of all nonconverted scaffold, coupling self-termination to a functional readout.

Innovation
- Writeable material logic: Cells both sense and actuate. No electronics, no exogenous cells, no permanent implants.
- Conversion, not disappearance: Transient domains become the repair tissue rather than resorbing as waste.
- Closed-loop termination: Dissolution engages only when mechanical function and perfusion recover, not by a preset timer.
- Spatial self-organization: Architecture emerges from stress-directed fiber alignment and enzyme/force-gated conversion, imposing pattern on recruited host populations.

Specific Aims
Aim 1. Synthesize and calibrate dual-gated, tissue-bifurcating MEWS fibers and gels.
Aim 2. Demonstrate cell-instructed recruitment, patterning, and local conversion ex vivo with host-derived factors only.
Aim 3. Validate de novo tertiary niche formation, staged repair, and conversion to permanent tissue in vivo in VML and critical-size bone defect models.
Aim 4. Prove closed-loop self-termination linked to recovered function and perfusion; quantify erasure kinetics and residuals.

Design Overview
Scaffold format: A hybrid of aligned nanofibers interpenetrated with a soft hydrogel. Both components are fully resorbable polyesters/peptides.

Three coupled modules:
1) Recruit-and-Pattern Module (host-factor concentrators + architecture)
- Heparin-mimetic sulfated polymers (e.g., sulfated alginate or PEG-sulfonate) to capture endogenous SDF-1, VEGF, PDGF, TGF-β from serum/exudate; no recombinant proteins required.
- Anisotropic fiber alignment (electrospun, 10–500 nm) to guide myotube orientation; concentric microchannels (150–300 µm) to template osteonal/vascular geometry. Channels formed by sacrificial sugar-glass fibers that dissolve post-implantation.
- Stress-directing mechanics: strain-stiffening fiber network (storage modulus G’low ~0.5–2 kPa, G’high ~5–20 kPa) that aligns under cell traction, reinforcing contact guidance and compartmentalizing myogenic vs osteogenic regions.

2) Conversion Module (dual-gated “cell writes tissue” chemistry)
- Force gate: Mechanophore-capped initiators embedded in fiber backbones and gel crosslinks (e.g., spiropyran-to-merocyanine or cyclobutene mechanocleavage motifs) that unmask reactive handles only under integrin-scale tractions (pN–nN per adhesion; macroscopic strain 2–6% for muscle, 0.5–2% for bone).
- Enzyme gate: Peptide linkers cleavable by MMP-2/9/13 and LOX exposure (muscle) or ALP-activated phosphate release and collagenase activity (bone). AND logic: both mechanophore activation and enzyme cleavage required to proceed.
- Tissue-specific conversion payloads:
  • Muscle: Collagen-mimetic peptides (CMPs; (GPO)n) and lysine/hydroxylysine-rich propeptides tethered behind gates. Upon activation, local triple-helix assembly and LOX-mediated crosslinking densify aligned collagen bundles that become permanent ECM.
  • Bone: Amorphous calcium phosphate (ACP) nanoseeds cloaked with ALP-labile phospho-serine brushes; upon ALP exposure plus traction, ACP crystallizes onto CMP-templated fibrils, forming oriented mineralized collagen. Optional inclusion of citrate-rich biodegradable polyesters to chelate Ca2+ and bias apatite orientation.
- Immune choreography: ROS-labile tethers present early M1-recruiting DAMP scavengers and CCR2/CCR5-binding decoys to confine inflammation; these tethers fragment as oxidative burst subsides, exposing αvβ3/α5β1-binding RGD and GFOGER motifs to accelerate progenitor adhesion.

3) Self-Termination Module (function-coupled erasure)
- Mechanophore-initiated depolymerization: Temporary network built from chain-shattering poly(orthocarbonate)/poly(oxalate)/poly(ketal) segments linked via force-activated retro-[4+2] or spiropyran scission points. When cyclic strain or muscle twitching/bone loading rises above calibrated thresholds for a set cycle count, cumulative scission drops molecular weight below solubility, accelerating hydrolysis and clearance.
- Perfusion switch: Nitroimidazole or boronic-ester crosslinks that are stabilized in hypoxia/high-ROS and spontaneously cleave upon normoxia/low-ROS, ensuring dissolution only after revascularization.
- Consumption coupling: All chemokine-concentrating motifs and integrin ligands are tethered to the same transient backbone; as conversion consumes the backbone into collagen/mineral, remaining recruitment cues vanish, preventing chronic niche persistence.

Approach and Methods
Aim 1. Materials synthesis and threshold tuning
- Fabricate aligned nanofibers from biodegradable polyester-urethanes or poly(1,8-octanediol citrate) with covalently integrated mechanophores (1–3 mol%).
- Form interpenetrating PEG-norbornene hydrogels with peptide crosslinks (MMP-sensitive sequences) bearing CMP pro-assemblies and ACP nanoseeds gated by ALP-labile groups.
- Calibrate force thresholds using traction force microscopy with primary murine satellite cells and periosteal MSCs on single-fiber force sensors; define the mechanophore activation strain at 1–10 nN/adhesion.
- Enzyme thresholds: Dose-response of conversion using physiological activities of MMP-2/9/13, LOX, and ALP; quantify switch fidelity (AND vs single-signal leak).
- Readouts: Spectral mechanophore state, gel-sol fraction, collagen triple-helix CD signal, mineral phase by XRD/FTIR, nanoscale stiffness by AFM.

Milestones: AND-gated conversion with leak <5% under single-signal exposure; collagen fibril D-spacing 64–67 nm (muscle construct); bone module apatite (002)/(211) ratio matching native within 20%.

Aim 2. Ex vivo recruitment, patterning, and local conversion
- Host-factor-only perfusion: Incubate scaffolds in platelet-poor plasma/exudate to preload endogenous cytokines via heparin-mimetics.
- Co-culture no-additive assays: Whole-blood → macrophage infiltration (Day 1–3), then endogenous progenitors from explanted fascia/periosteum inserts (Day 3–10); zero recombinant GFs.
- Pattern formation tests: Apply cyclic strain (muscle: 1 Hz, 4% for 1 hr/day; bone: 2% compression at 0.5 Hz) to emulate early rehab loading; map traction-driven fiber alignment and local conversion events.
- Readouts: Macrophage phenotype (CD68, iNOS→CD206 switch), progenitor expansion (Pax7+ satellite cells; Sca1+/PDGFRα+ MSCs), endothelial network formation (CD31+ lumenized channels), spatial correlation between traction hotspots and converted ECM. Quantify architectural order parameter (nematic S for myofiber alignment; osteon-like channel circularity).

Milestones: Directed myotube alignment S≥0.6 without exogenous cells; perfusable capillary-like networks spanning channels; spatial overlap coefficient ≥0.7 between traction peaks and converted ECM regions.

Aim 3. In vivo tertiary niche and tissue conversion
- Models: Mouse VML (tibialis anterior; 15–20% mass loss) and femoral critical-size defect (2–3 mm stabilized externally only during healing period with fully resorbable fixation or periosteal sleeve; no permanent hardware within defect).
- Implantation: Cell-free MEWS preloaded only with host-factor concentrators; bifurcated constructs for musculo-tendinous junctions and bone–muscle interfaces as needed.
- Staged repair tracking: Days 1–3 inflammation localization and resolution; Days 3–14 progenitor expansion and vasculature; Weeks 2–8 differentiation and matrix maturation; >8 weeks remodeling.
- Endpoints:
  • Muscle: Tetanic force recovery (in vivo peroneal nerve stimulation), cross-sectional myofiber area distribution, central→peripheral nucleation shift, collagen alignment (SHG imaging), innervation (NF-H, AChR clustering).
  • Bone: Micro-CT bone volume fraction, trabecular thickness, elastic modulus (3-point bending/nanoindentation), osteon organization around channels, bridging rate.
  • Niche metrics: Residual scaffold mass (<5% by mass at function plateau), cytokine sequestration profiles, immune phenotypes.

Milestones: ≥70% force recovery by Week 8 in VML; full cortical bridging by Week 10–12 in bone with modulus ≥70% of contralateral; residual scaffold below quantitation at functional plateau.

Aim 4. Closed-loop self-termination validation
- Mechanical trigger: Compare MEWS in animals with normal rehabilitation loading vs limb unloading. Hypothesis: Dissolution and scaffold disappearance occur only in loaded cohorts as function returns; unloaded limbs retain scaffold until loading resumes.
- Perfusion trigger: Use Doppler/oxygen-sensitive phosphorescence to time normoxia onset; correlate with cleavage of O2-sensitive linkers and disappearance of recruitment cues.
- Causality tests: Pharmacologically inhibit ALP or LOX transiently to break the AND gate; expect stalled conversion and persistent scaffold despite loading, confirming gate logic.
- Safety: Quantify soluble byproducts (oxalate, ketal-derived diols), local pH, and inflammatory markers; histopathology for ectopic mineralization or fibrosis.

Milestones: Time-to-90% scaffold disappearance correlates (R≥0.7) with function/oxygenation thresholds, not days-post-op; gate inhibition abolishes termination until rescue.

Mechanistic Staging (embedded in MEWS)
- Phase I: Controlled inflammation (Days 1–3)
  • Heparin-mimetics concentrate host chemokines; ROS-labile decoys confine M1 response.
  • MMP-rich milieu begins loosening peptide gates but cannot convert without traction.
- Phase II: Progenitor expansion and patterning (Days 3–14)
  • Stress-directed fiber alignment increases; dual-gated activation begins where cells adhere and pull.
  • Conversion to aligned collagen bundles (muscle) or mineralizing fibrils (bone) initiates in high-traction regions.
- Phase III: Differentiation and maturation (Weeks 2–8)
  • LOX crosslinking densifies muscle ECM; ALP drives mineral deposition; vasculature stabilizes within channels.
  • Recruitment cues taper as the same transient backbone is consumed into ECM.
- Phase IV: Closed-loop termination (from Week 4 onward)
  • Cyclic strain/loading increases; mechanophore scission plus normoxia cleaves remaining transient networks.
  • Residuals solubilize and clear; only converted ECM remains.

Risk Mitigation and Alternatives
- If mechanophore activation requires higher forces than cells provide, lower thresholds by increasing mechanophore density, introducing prestrain in fibers, or using softer backbones to magnify local force.
- If enzyme specificity is too broad, use tandem peptide gates (e.g., MMP-13 then LOX proximity ligation) or substrate/enzyme colocalization via collagen-binding domains.
- If mineralization overshoots, cap ACP loading and use citrate-rich polymers to moderate crystal growth kinetics.
- If immune skew is suboptimal, adjust ROS-labile decoy density; add short-lived IL-4-mimetic peptides on fast-cleaving linkers (24–48 h half-life) without sustained exogenous cytokine delivery.

Success Criteria
- Precise spatial coincidence between regions of high cell traction/enzyme activity and permanent ECM conversion.
- Architectural fidelity to target tissue (aligned myofibers; osteon-like channels with concentric lamellae).
- Functional restoration with minimal residual scaffold and no chronic inflammation or fibrosis.
- Demonstrated dependency of scaffold termination on mechanical function and perfusion rather than elapsed time.

Deliverables
- A validated, modular MEWS platform for VML and critical-size bone defects that is cell-free, implant-free, architecturally instructive, temporally staged, and self-terminating via endogenous function.
- Open-source synthesis protocols, gating designs, and in vivo datasets enabling translation to other tissues where “cells write their own niche and convert the template into themselves.”

Title
Endogenous Clot Programming for Scarless Endochondral Repair: A Cell‑Free, Self‑Terminating Tertiary Regenerative Niche for Critical‑Size Bone Defects

Atomic hypothesis
A single controllable change—decorating the patient’s own provisional fibrin clot with fetal‑healing–inspired, triggerable morphogen cassettes—converts that clot into a transient reaction–diffusion organizer that (i) recruits and spatially patterns endogenous progenitors, vasculature, and immune cells, (ii) stages endochondral repair, and (iii) shuts itself off when osteogenesis restores function, via alkaline phosphatase–driven inactivation.

Rationale (fetal constraint)
Fetal bone heals through a morphogen field that is matrix‑bound, cell‑activated, and self‑resolving. Adult defects lack this field and default to fibrosis. We will reconstruct an adult‑compatible, clot‑anchored analog without exogenous cells or permanent implants.

Specific aims
1) Build clot‑anchored morphogen cassettes that read early injury signals to initiate recruitment and fetal‑like patterning.
2) Impose architectural organization via a Turing‑type activator–inhibitor pair localized to the clot.
3) Stage endochondral repair through endogenous‑cue–gated releases.
4) Achieve closed‑loop shutdown using osteoblast alkaline phosphatase (ALP)–triggered inactivation and sequestration, coupled to matrix maturation.

System design (one‑shot, cell‑free, resorbable)
- Carrier: No exogenous scaffold. A single in situ liquid dose applied intraoperatively binds to the forming host fibrin clot via FXIIIa‑substrate tags, heparin‑binding domains, and fibrin‑affinity peptides. All components are biodegradable peptides/proteins or small molecules.
- Cassettes: Growth‑factor mimetics or full proteins fused to (i) a clot‑anchoring domain, (ii) an injury‑cue–cleavable linker, and (iii) an ALP‑responsive self‑immolative “off‑switch.”

Programmed stages and control logic
Stage 0: Arming at hemostasis (minutes–hours)
- Incorporation: FXIIIa‑reactive tags covalently crosslink cassettes into fibrin as the clot forms.
- Spatial seeding: Peripheral periosteal edges painted with a brief ring injection of inhibitor (Noggin‑prodrug) to bias inward gradients.

Stage 1: Controlled inflammation and recruitment (0–72 h)
- Inputs: Thrombin, ROS, MMP‑2/9, hypoxia.
- Actions:
  - PDGF‑BBfast: thrombin‑cleavable release for pericyte/MSC proliferation and macrophage chemokinesis.
  - CXCL12/SDF‑1gradient: heparan‑affinity tuning yields long‑range recruitment from periosteum, marrow, and endothelium.
  - Annexin A1 mimetic (Ac2‑26) ROS‑cleavable pulse to limit fibrosis and promote efferocytosis without blocking necessary M1 functions.

Stage 2: Fetalization and condensation (2–10 days)
- Latent TGF‑β3clot‑tethered: presented in LAP form; activation only under integrin traction from recruited progenitors, promoting SOX9+ condensations.
- PTHrP‑mimetic gradient: slows hypertrophy to allow organized column formation.
- Reaction–diffusion patterning:
  - Short‑range activator: fibrin‑tethered BMP‑2 microdomains (slow diffusion).
  - Long‑range inhibitor: diffusible pro‑Noggin activated by MMP‑9—produces trabecula‑scale periodicity (tens to hundreds of microns) that aligns condensations along principal stress lines as loading resumes.

Stage 3: Vascular invasion and osteogenesis (7–21 days)
- Inputs: Emergent MMP‑13 (hypertrophic chondrocytes), partial re‑oxygenation.
- Actions:
  - VEGF‑A MMP‑13–cleavable release drives vessel ingress; co‑released Ang‑1 stabilizes nascent vessels.
  - BMP‑7 MMP‑13–cleavable delayed pulse transitions condensations to RUNX2+ osteogenesis.
  - Local RGD‑lite motifs on clot enhance cell traction to further activate latent TGF‑β3 where needed, maintaining cartilage–bone interfaces during transition.

Stage 4: Remodeling and autonomous termination (≥14 days)
- Functional readout: Rising osteoblast ALP and mineral deposition indicate successful osteogenesis.
- Two‑pathway shutdown:
  1) ALP‑triggered inactivation: All morphogen cassettes carry phosphate‑caged self‑immolative linkers that, once dephosphorylated by ALP, expose an internal degron leading to rapid proteolysis and loss of activity.
  2) Mineral‑coupled sequestration: The same ALP event unmasks a poly‑Asp/bisphosphonate‑lite tag that binds hydroxyapatite, immobilizing residual factors; in parallel, an ALP‑activated Noggin burst neutralizes any remaining BMP activity.
- Outcome: Niche activity decays as stiffness, oxygenation, and ALP normalize; clot fully resorbs; no indwelling material remains.

Spatial organization without implants
- Pattern source: Tethered activator + diffusible inhibitor on a degradable clot template yields self‑organized morphogen microdomains.
- Boundary conditions: Periosteal ring pre‑paint and cortical bone margins set initial inhibitor boundary, guiding trabecular orientation.
- Mechanotransduction: Because latent TGF‑β activation requires cell traction, organization tightens preferentially along load paths, coupling architecture to function.

Safety and constraints compliance
- Cell‑free: Only proteins/peptides/small molecules; no cells or gene therapy.
- No permanent implants: All elements are clot‑decorators that degrade; no hardware.
- Tertiary niche: Induced de novo at the defect; not dependent on pre‑existing niches.
- Termination is closed‑loop: ALP/mineralization‑coupled; not a timer.

Experimental plan
Aim 1: Chemistry and biophysics
- Synthesize fusion cassettes (anchor–cue–payload–ALP switch).
- Validate: FXIIIa incorporation kinetics; ROS/MMP cleavage rates; ALP‑triggered self‑immolation; hydroxyapatite sequestration; binding to heparin/fibrin.

Aim 2: Ex vivo patterning and activation logic
- 3D clot phantoms seeded with purified enzymes to emulate Stage 1–4 inputs; image gradient formation and Turing‑like domains (fluorescently labeled activator/inhibitor).
- Traction‑dependent TGF‑β activation assay using contractile MSCs on fibrin gels with tunable stiffness.

Aim 3: In vivo efficacy in murine/rabbit critical‑size defects
- One‑shot intraoperative dosing; no scaffold.
- Readouts by stage: immune phenotype (M1→M2), progenitor recruitment (PDGFRβ+, Sca1+), condensations (SOX9), vascular ingress (CD31/EMCN), osteogenesis (RUNX2/OSX), ALP and mineral mapping, residual factor quantification.
- Function: torsional/three‑point bending, gait analysis; microCT‑based trabecular architecture vs native contralateral.

Aim 4: Robustness and shutdown validation
- Force ALP blockade (pharmacologic) to test fail‑safe mineral sequestration.
- Overexpression of MMP‑13 blockade to test timing dependencies.
- Biodistribution and systemic safety; cytokine panels.

Go/no‑go criteria
- Go: In vivo bridging of critical‑size defects with native‑like trabecular architecture, ≥80% contralateral strength by week 8 in rabbit ulnar/segmental femoral models; complete decay of exogenous signals by week 4; absence of ectopic ossification.
- No‑go: Persistent factor activity beyond ALP rise; disorganized callus; fibrotic non‑union.

Risk mitigation
- Ectopic ossification: Tighter inhibitor ring dose; stronger ALP‑activated Noggin.
- Insufficient recruitment: Increase early PDGF/SDF‑1 pulse via thrombin‑sensitive linkers.
- Premature shutdown in low‑ALP states: Redundant mineral‑binding sequestration and time‑limited ROS/MMP decay.

Translatability and manufacturing
- Recombinant proteins/peptides with clinically precedented domains (FXIIIa‑substrates, fibrin‑binding, heparin‑binding).
- Single‑use syringe kit with two chambers (anchors + payloads) that mix on application to the bleeding defect.

Extension to volumetric muscle loss (optional follow‑on)
- Swap endochondral payloads for myogenic cues while keeping the same clot‑programming and ALP‑independent termination (CK‑ or titin‑domain protease–activated off‑switches); spatial organization via activator–inhibitor pairs (HGF‑tethered activator, diffusible myostatin‑trap inhibitor) aligned by fascial boundaries.

Expected outcome
A one‑shot, cell‑free, implant‑free therapy that transiently “fetalizes” the adult bone‑injury microenvironment using the endogenous clot as a programmable organizer, recruits and patterns host cells, executes a staged endochondral program, and then self‑terminates as the tissue regains function.

text:
Title: Self-Tuning Injury-Signal Rectifier (STIR-gel) for autonomous, self-terminating tertiary regenerative niches in volumetric muscle loss and critical-size bone defects

Central hypothesis-question
Can a single, fully resorbable, mechanochemically adaptive “signal-rectifier” hydrogel that reads, concentrates, and time-gates the tissue’s own injury cues—rather than supplying exogenous cues—drive staged recruitment, patterning, vascularization, and matrix remodeling in VML and critical-size bone defects, and then switch itself off and dissolve when functional restoration normalizes the local mechanics and protease milieu?

Atomic strategy
One perturbation to the system: inject a cell-free, implant-free STIR-gel that passively harvests and rectifies endogenous biochemical and mechanical signals into steep, aligned, and time-staged gradients. The tissue’s evolving mechanics and enzyme activity both power and govern the program and provide the closed-loop stop signal for self-dissolution.

Mechanistic design
- Inputs read from the wound:
  - Chemical: endogenous heparin-binding growth factors (VEGF, PDGF, FGF2, HGF), chemokines (CXCL12, CCL2), alarmins/DAMPs (HMGB1, extracellular ATP/nucleic acids), and extracellular vesicles.
  - Enzymatic: high early neutrophil elastase/thrombin, sustained MMP-2/9 activity, gradually increasing tissue transglutaminase (FXIIIa).
  - Mechanical: high interstitial flow/edema, low modulus early; rising cyclic strain (muscle) or increasing mineral-linked stiffness (bone) over time.
  - Ionic: rising Ca2+/phosphate during osteogenesis; normalization of ROS/pH with resolution of inflammation.

- Material platform (cell-free; fully resorbable):
  - A shear-thinning, in situ–setting hydrogel network formed by reversible host–guest bonds (cyclodextrin–adamantane) interlaced with covalent crosslinks that are both MMP-cleavable and ROS-labile. Base polymers: oxidized polysaccharide (alginate/dextran) + multi-arm PEG; all bonds hydrolytically or enzymatically degradable to renally clearable oligomers.
  - Heparin-mimetic and decorin-mimetic sulfated motifs for reversible capture of endogenous heparin-binding growth factors and TGF-β family members; guanidinium-rich domains to bind nucleic-acid DAMPs/ATP.
  - Strain-alignable peptide-amphiphile nanofibers embedded at low volume fraction; these align under physiological shear/contraction to impose contact guidance for myofibers or osteoblast lamellae.
  - Yield-stress microchanneling: under early edema-driven flow, the gel forms anisotropic, percolating microchannels that rectify flow and steepen gradients; as flow subsides, channels collapse, extinguishing amplification.

- Gradient amplification and temporal staging (no exogenous proteins required):
  - Stage I: Controlled inflammation (hours–2 days). Neutrophil elastase/thrombin cleavage opens nanovalves, rapidly releasing a fraction of captured alarmins/chemokines at the defect margin to recruit innate immune cells while excess DAMPs are buffered by finite-capacity binding to prevent cytokine storm. Flow-rectified microchannels steepen chemokine gradients into the defect core.
  - Stage II: Progenitor recruitment/expansion (2–7 days). Ongoing MMP-2/9 activity progressively liberates captured CXCL12, HGF, and VEGF from heparin-mimetic domains, establishing sustained, oriented gradients that draw satellite cells/MSCs/periosteal progenitors and endothelial tip cells along the channel axes. Strain-aligned nanofibers provide anisotropic haptotaxis for myotube fusion or osteoblast sheet rotation.
  - Stage III: Differentiation and matrix deposition (1–4 weeks). Cell-secreted FXIIIa locally crosslinks glutamine–lysine motifs within the gel, sealing channels and attenuating further release while stabilizing nascent matrices. For bone, phosphoserine/phosphate-bearing motifs nucleate hydroxyapatite from incoming Ca2+/Pi, focusing mineral along stress-aligned domains; for muscle, laminin-mimetic epitopes (e.g., IKVAV/YIGSR) embedded at low density enhance myofiber maturation and neuromuscular alignment.
  - Stage IV: Remodeling/maturation and vascular integration (3–8 weeks). As vascular ingress normalizes oxygen/ROS and macrophages transition to pro-resolving states, the gel’s amplification dampens, leaving host ECM to take over guidance.

- Closed-loop self-termination (intrinsically coupled to functional recovery):
  - Dual-sensor AND gate:
    1) Protease low: when MMP/elastase activity drops below a defined threshold, protease-gated nanovalves stop opening; no further release of captured factors.
    2) Mechanics restored: when surrounding modulus and/or cyclic strain exceed setpoints (e.g., ≥20–40 kPa for muscle, higher for bone), force-accelerated retro-Diels–Alder mechanophores and catch-bond crosslinks convert to slip-bonds, triggering network depolymerization. Concurrently, diminished interstitial flow collapses microchannels, extinguishing gradient rectification.
  - Orthogonal ionic fail-safe: rising Ca2+/Pi competitively disrupts heparin-mimetic binding in bone, hastening disassembly after bridging; in muscle, resumed cyclic strain preferentially fatigues host–guest bonds, accelerating clearance.
  - Outcome: the gel fragments into short, water-soluble oligomers cleared by lymphatics/kidney; no permanent material remains.

- Tissue-specific plug-ins (same platform, no cells, no hardware):
  - Muscle mode: higher density of strain-alignable nanofibers, laminin-mimetic epitopes, and lower gel modulus to transmit contraction; channel aspect ratio tuned for long-axis guidance.
  - Bone mode: inclusion of phospho-serine/phosphate motifs and slightly stiffer baseline modulus; channel geometry tuned for osteon-like concentric lamellae and vessel–osteon co-alignment.

Specific aims
1) Build and calibrate STIR-gel as an endogenous-signal rectifier.
- Quantify binding affinities/kinetics to key endogenous factors (VEGF, PDGF, FGF2, HGF, CXCL12, CCL2, TGF-β) and DAMPs using SPR/ITC.
- In a microfluidic wound-exudate-on-a-chip with controlled interstitial flows and protease/ROS profiles, measure: gradient steepness and persistence; channel formation/collapse; staged release governed by enzyme activity.
- Define mechanical and enzymatic setpoints for the AND-gate off-switch.

2) Validate closed-loop staging and self-termination in ex vivo human wound fluids.
- Use fresh VML/bone-defect exudates to drive the gel; monitor temporally resolved capture/re-release (ELISA/proteomics), enzymatic thresholds, and mechanophore scission under modulus ramps.
- Assess sequestration vs release tradeoffs that minimize hyperinflammation while preserving early recruitment.

3) Demonstrate autonomous niche induction and architectural patterning in VML.
- Rat tibialis anterior 20% VML model; single perilesional injection of STIR-gel (muscle mode); no cells, no exogenous proteins.
- Endpoints: cell recruitment kinetics (flow cytometry, scRNA-seq), macrophage state trajectories, capillary density/sprout orientation, satellite-cell expansion (Pax7), myofiber alignment (angle dispersion), NMJ reconstitution, in situ stiffness mapping, ex vivo force production.
- Self-termination: longitudinal in vivo imaging of fluorescently labeled gel fragments and local protease/mechanics; time to full resorption; absence of chronic foreign body response.

4) Demonstrate autonomous bridging and osteon-like organization in a hardware-free bone defect.
- Mouse 4-mm calvarial critical-size defect; single injection of STIR-gel (bone mode).
- Endpoints: micro-CT volumetrics and anisotropy; concentric lamellae/osteon-like patterning; co-aligned microvasculature (µCT angiography); Raman mapping of mineral/matrix maturation; push-out/indentation mechanics.
- Self-termination and safety as in Aim 3.

Experimental design and controls
- Controls: saline; inert non-affinity gel; affinity gel with protease-insensitive crosslinks; gel that captures but cannot form flow-rectified channels; exogenous-GF–loaded gel (positive control).
- Readouts: spatial proteomics of gel-bound vs released factors; intravital imaging of gradient formation (chemokine biosensors); traction force/strain field mapping; histomorphometry; functional biomechanics.

Success criteria
- ≥2× increase in gradient steepness and ≥3× longer gradient persistence vs inert gel in vitro.
- In vivo: ≥50% increase in recruited progenitors at 72 h; aligned vasculature within channels; for VML, ≥60% restoration of tetanic force by 8 weeks with myofiber angle dispersion ≤20°; for bone, ≥75% defect bridging with osteon-like organization and ≥60% native stiffness by 8 weeks.
- Complete material resorption without chronic inflammation; termination coincident with protease low + modulus high thresholds.

Risk mitigation
- Insufficient endogenous cues: pre-wet STIR-gel with autologous wound fluid/platelet-poor plasma at the bedside to seed initial capture without adding exogenous growth factors.
- Excess fibrosis: tune decorin-mimetic density to transiently sequester TGF-β during Stage II only (release upon FXIIIa crosslinking).
- Premature dissolution: raise mechanophore threshold and add secondary hydrolysable crosslinks to extend persistence; conversely, if persistence is excessive, lower host–guest affinity or increase ROS-labile content.

Milestones and timeline (24 months)
- Months 0–6: Material synthesis; microfluidic rectification assays; define AND-gate thresholds.
- Months 6–12: Ex vivo human fluid validation; finalize muscle/bone mode formulations.
- Months 12–20: VML and calvarial defect studies; longitudinal termination mapping.
- Months 20–24: Functional endpoints, safety, and Go/No-Go criteria for large-animal translation.

Impact
STIR-gel implements a single, system-level intervention: it converts the injury’s noisy biochemical/mechanical effluent into ordered, self-limiting guidance fields that the tissue reads to regenerate itself. By coupling activation and termination to the wound’s own enzyme activity and mechanical restoration, the niche appears only when and where needed, organizes itself by the host’s stress lines, and disappears upon recovery—no cells, no hardware, no exogenous morphogens.

text:
Title: A force-gated, self-resolving synthetic niche for volumetric muscle loss and critical-size bone defects

Central hypothesis (inseparable from the research goal)
Restoration of a continuous load path across a defect is the body’s native stop signal for musculoskeletal repair. Therefore, a fully synthetic, cell-free scaffold whose stability, bioactivity, and persistence are all contingent on bearing physiologic tensile/compressive strain will (i) initiate and stage repair when it is in the load path, and (ii) autonomously terminate, dissolve, and silence morphogen signaling once native tissue assumes the load, creating a transient, tertiary regenerative niche that recruits, organizes, and programs endogenous cells without implants or exogenous cells.

Atomic strategy
Make “being in the load path” the single control variable. All instructive functions (immune orchestration, progenitor recruitment/expansion, angiogenesis, differentiation cues, and matrix remodeling) are strain-permissive; all termination functions are strain-suppressed. When tissue function returns and scaffold strain falls below a defined threshold for a defined dwell time, the niche flips state and self-immolates.

Design overview: Mechano-gated, staged, and self-terminating scaffold (cell-free; fully resorbable)
1) Material platform (injectable; no hardware retained)
- Base: shear-thinning, self-healing, fully resorbable hydrogel network reinforced with aligned, degradable nanofibers to impose tissue-scale architecture.
- Architecture: elongational-flow alignment during injection creates (a) parallel microchannels for myofiber guidance in VML and (b) osteon-mimetic concentric lamellae plus longitudinal channels for CSD. Pore topology (30–150 μm) supports vasculature and myotube/osteon formation.
- All chemistries use biodegradable polyesters/phosphoesters and peptide linkers; no persistent metals or permanent implants.

2) Force-gated niche governance (“mechano-governor”)
- Tension-shielded proteolysis: crosslinks incorporate peptide hairpins with cryptic MMP/cathepsin sites that are sterically hidden when fibers are under tensile load. High local strain maintains instruction; low strain exposes sites for rapid enzymatic cleavage.
- Catch-bond-inspired adhesion: supramolecular host–guest pairs that are force-stabilized maintain cell adhesion ligands (RGD, GFOGER, laminin-mimetic) under load. When strain falls, the complexes dissociate, decreasing further cell influx and permitting scaffold disassembly.
- Strain-threshold and dwell-time logic: a mechanochromic moiety (reporter only; no electronics) and a parallel, low-strain–exposed self-immolative linker form an AND gate: only when strain remains below σcrit for Tcrit hours does network-wide depolymerization cascade.

3) Temporal staging via endogenous-enzyme logic (no timed release)
- Stage 1 (controlled inflammation): neutrophil elastase unmasks low-dose CCL2/CSF1 mimetics to recruit monocytes; surfaces bias macrophage polarization using zwitterionic charge and phosphatidylserine-mimetic headgroups.
- Stage 2 (progenitor recruitment/expansion): early macrophage MMP9 releases CXCL12/FGF2 mimetics; aligned topography biases satellite cell and periosteal progenitor alignment and expansion.
- Stage 3 (angiogenesis and bridging): hypoxia-reducible tethers (nitroimidazole/azo-peptide analogs) release VEGF-mimetic peptide (QK) only under low pO2; as perfusion normalizes, release ceases automatically.
- Stage 4a (myogenesis): myotube maturation cues (IGF-1/agrin mimetics) are tethered behind MT1-MMP–cleavable linkers produced by invading myogenic cells.
- Stage 4b (osteogenesis): surface-bound calcium phosphate nucleators carry BMP2-mimetic peptides; progressive mineral occlusion both traps remaining cues and stiffens the construct, shifting strain off the scaffold.
- Stage 5 (remodeling and quieting): exposure of TGF-β–sequestering and heparin-mimetic domains increases as load drops, scavenging residual cytokines to prevent fibrosis/ectopic ossification.

4) Closed-loop termination coupled to function
- Mechanical readout: when native muscle or bone restores a continuous load path, scaffold strain decreases below σcrit. Low strain unmasks protease sites and activates a self-immolative backbone (benzyl-carbamate or phosphate-based) that depolymerizes the network into renally clearable oligomers.
- Vascular/oxygen readout: revascularization shuts down hypoxia-activated proangiogenic release; normoxia increases crosslink hydration, accelerating dissolution once the mechanical criterion is also met.
- Autolimitation of morphogens: mineral occlusion (bone) and basement membrane deposition (muscle) progressively bury remaining ligand tethers, flipping the niche from source to sink before final clearance.

Spatial organization without implants
- Muscle (VML): uniaxially aligned channels (50–80 μm) guide myotube fusion; alternating stiff/soft lamellae enforce fascicle spacing; tethered agrin-mimetic stripes template nascent NMJ zones.
- Bone (CSD): concentric lamellae and longitudinal channels template osteon/Haversian systems; spatially patterned BMP-mimetic density forms a centripetal osteogenic gradient from periosteal edges inward.

Research plan and milestones
Aim 1: Build and calibrate the mechano-governor
- Synthesize crosslinks with tension-shielded MMP sites and self-immolative backbones.
- Calibrate σcrit and Tcrit in bioreactors mimicking limb loading (0.5–3% strain, 0.1–2 Hz).
- Readouts: mechanochromic signal vs enzymatic half-life; rheology under cyclic load; protease accessibility assays.

Milestone: Strain-above-threshold preserves scaffold >21 days with active signaling; strain-below-threshold triggers >80% mass loss within 72 hours and 90% reduction in ligand presentation.

Aim 2: Demonstrate staged, cell-free regeneration in small animals
- VML (mouse tibialis anterior): inject scaffold; assess immune staging (flow cytometry/spatial transcriptomics), satellite cell recruitment (Pax7+/MyoD+), aligned myofiber formation, NMJ patterning, and torque recovery.
- CSD (rat femoral 8 mm): scaffold-only bridging; track periosteal progenitor influx (Sca1+/PDGFRα+), angiogenesis (CD31+/EMCN+), mineral deposition (μCT), osteon architecture (histomorphometry), and 4-point bending.
- Closed-loop termination: correlate scaffold clearance with function restoration (≥70% contralateral torque or bending stiffness) and in situ strain readout drop.

Milestone: Scaffold-free controls fail to bridge; scaffold groups achieve functional restoration with scaffold mass <5% at endpoint and no ectopic mineralization/fibrosis.

Aim 3: Stress-test autonomy and safety
- Under-loading and over-loading paradigms to test premature dissolution or persistence.
- Large-animal pilot (ovine radius defect; porcine VML) to validate load-governed termination under physiologic mechanics.
- Off-target ossification/fibrosis screens; biodistribution and clearance of degradation products.

Milestone: Termination only when mechanical competence ≥60% baseline and perfusion normalized; no persistence beyond 6 months; benign metabolites.

Risk mitigation
- If σcrit is mis-specified, incorporate a dual-sensing gate requiring both low strain and normoxia to initiate dissolution.
- If early inflammation is excessive, reduce CSF1 density and increase phosphatidylserine-mimetic content.
- If angiogenesis stalls, increase hypoxia-activatable density or channel diameter by 20–30 μm.

Success criteria (go/no-go)
- Autonomously staged recruitment and organization without exogenous cells.
- Function-linked, self-terminating dissolution with zero hardware left behind.
- For VML: aligned myofiber domains with restored specific force ≥75% by week 12 and mature NMJs.
- For CSD: bridged cortical shell, organized osteons, and bending stiffness ≥75% by week 16, with scaffold clearance.

Innovation
- Single control variable—load-path participation—governs both on-boarding of repair and its shutdown.
- Tension-shielded proteolysis and self-immolative backbones create a closed-loop, self-resolving tertiary niche.
- Spatial organization encoded mechanically at injection, not by permanent implants or external fields.

Impact
A fully synthetic, mechano-governed, self-resolving scaffold that turns itself off when healing is mechanically complete eliminates donor grafts and hardware, generalizing across muscle and bone by reading the same native stop signal: restored force transmission.

Title
Force-Gated Self-Immolative Niches (FoSiN) for Closed-Loop Regeneration of Volumetric Muscle Loss and Critical-Size Bone Defects

Central Hypothesis-Question
Can a fully resorbable, cell-free scaffold that transduces restored physiological mechanical function into a chemical self-destruction signal create a de novo (tertiary) regenerative niche that (i) recruits endogenous progenitors, immune cells, and vasculature, (ii) imposes architectural organization, (iii) executes a staged repair program, and (iv) then autonomously exits when load-bearing/contractile function is re-established?

Atomic Strategy
Embed a single mechanochemical transducer—mechanophore-capped, self-immolative polymer (SIP) crosslinks—throughout an anisotropic, bioactive scaffold. Below a calibrated force-frequency threshold, SIPs remain intact and gate staged cue release; above threshold (i.e., once healthy tissue mechanically “closes the loop”), mechanophore opening triggers SIP unzipping and rapid scaffold disassembly, terminating the niche.

Design Overview
- Material platform (all components resorbable):
  - Base matrix: gelatin–hyaluronan interpenetrating hydrogel reinforced with aligned biodegradable microfibers (electrospun collagen/gelatin for muscle; collagen–amorphous calcium phosphate composite for bone).
  - Crosslinking logic: SIP crosslinks (poly(benzyl carbamate)-type, aqueous-stable) capped with force-labile cyclobutane/retro–Diels–Alder mechanophores uniformly distributed along load paths; secondary dynamic sacrificial bonds (catechol–boronate ester) dissipate subthreshold loads.
  - Bioactive cargo (peptide mimetics/aptamers to minimize dose and off-targets) tethered via protease-specific linkers:
    - Recruitment: CXCL12-mimetic for progenitors; CCL2-mimetic for monocytes; QK (VEGF-mimetic) for angiogenesis.
    - Expansion: HGF- and IGF-1–mimetics; PDGF-BB–mimetic for stromal support.
    - Differentiation: BMP-2/7–mimetic (bone); agrin-fragment and laminin-mimetic IKVAV (muscle).
    - Remodeling and anti-fibrosis: decorin-mimetic to sequester TGF-β; Ang1-mimetic for vessel stabilization; MMP-activatable LOX-modulator kept low to avoid scar crosslinking.
  - Heparinized sinks and aptamer “sponges” embedded to quench remaining cues upon scaffold exit.
- Spatial architecture:
  - Myo-FoSiN: 3D aligned microgrooves (10–20 μm) and parallel perfusable channels (100–200 μm) for myofiber/NMJ alignment with interleaved vascular tracks; anisotropic stiffness gradient (E‖ > E⊥) guides satellite cell fusion and sarcomere registry.
  - Osteo-FoSiN: Osteon-mimetic concentric lamellae with longitudinal Haversian channels (~200 μm) and radial canaliculi-like pores; mineral stiffness gradient (outer higher, inner lower) to bias endochondral-to-intramembranous transition; resorbable calcium phosphate nanograins for osteoconduction.

Closed-Loop Mechanochemical Controller
- Threshold sensing:
  - Mechano-gating is set by SIP mechanophore scission kinetics vs loading rate.
  - Muscle preset: higher frequency (5–20 Hz), moderate strain; Bone preset: lower frequency (0.5–5 Hz), higher microstrain (1000–3000 με). Network topology routes specific frequency bands to mechanophores via viscoelastic “clutch” elements, filtering out rehab micro-movements early.
- Action:
  - Subthreshold regime: SIPs intact; cell traction and early inflammatory proteases (neutrophil elastase→MMP-9) locally cleave stage-1 tethers (chemokines) without global disassembly.
  - Suprathreshold regime (functional loading restored): mechanophore caps open, exposing triggers that initiate SIP 1,6-elimination; crosslink unzipping cascades through the network (minutes–hours), collapsing the scaffold into soluble oligomers. Simultaneously, cue-sponges are exposed to quench residual morphogens, actively terminating the niche.

Temporally Staged Repair Program (no exogenous cells)
- Stage 0: Hemostasis and antifibrotic bias
  - Rapid gelation; decorin-mimetic present; TGF-β sequestration begins immediately.
- Stage 1: Controlled inflammation and recruitment (days 0–3)
  - Elastase- and MMP-9–labile tethers release CCL2-mimetic to recruit monocytes; low-dose pro-resolving lipid mimetic is co-tethered to cap neutrophil lifespan; QK microgradients initiate endothelial tip sprouting.
- Stage 2: Progenitor influx and expansion (days 2–10)
  - MMP-2/13–labile tethers release CXCL12-mimetic and HGF/IGF-1–mimetics; anisotropic topography aligns migrating satellite cells (muscle) or periosteal/MSC progenitors (bone).
- Stage 3: Differentiation and matrix deposition (days 7–28)
  - Mechanical pre-load (subthreshold) enhances focal adhesion maturation; BMP-mimetic pulses (bone) drive osteoprogenitor differentiation; agrin-fragment plus IKVAV (muscle) promote myotube fusion and NMJ maturation; Ang1-mimetic stabilizes nascent vessels.
- Stage 4: Maturation/remodeling and autonomous exit (variable; triggered)
  - As force transmission and load paths reconstitute, mechanophore scission triggers SIP self-immolation; scaffold disassembles; sponges quench residual cues; normal mechanobiology takes over.

Specific Aims
- Aim 1: Engineer and calibrate FoSiN mechanochemical gates.
  - Synthesize SIP–mechanophore crosslinkers with tunable scission thresholds; integrate into anisotropic hydrogels.
  - Calibrate dissolution onset vs cyclic strain amplitude/frequency in benchtop rigs mirroring muscle and bone signatures.
  - Verify biocompatibility of byproducts; measure depolymerization kinetics and cue-quenching efficiency.
- Aim 2: Program spatiotemporal recruitment and organization.
  - Pattern microarchitecture (grooves/osteons) and vascular channels; load cargo on protease-specific tethers with spatially encoded densities.
  - In vitro co-culture without exogenous cell addition beyond native tissue explants to confirm endogenous cell recruitment from serum/blood surrogates; quantify alignment, migration anisotropy, and stage-specific gene expression.
- Aim 3: Demonstrate closed-loop regeneration and autonomous exit in vivo.
  - Myo-FoSiN: rodent tibialis anterior VML with graded rehab loading. Endpoints: force production, myofiber alignment index, NMJ density, vascular perfusion, scaffold disappearance timing vs force recovery.
  - Osteo-FoSiN: rat femoral critical-size segmental defect with controlled weight-bearing progression. Endpoints: microCT bridging, torsional strength, osteon organization, vessel density, scaffold disappearance timing vs load-bearing.

Methods and Metrics
- Mechanics: dynamic mechanical analysis under physiological saline; fatigue-to-failure to map mechanophore scission surfaces; strain-field mapping in scaffolds using particle tracking.
- Biology: single-cell RNA-seq and fate mapping of endogenous progenitors; immunophenotyping (M1/M2 balance); angiography; collagen alignment (SHG); mineral apposition rates; NMJ imaging.
- Closed-loop validation: correlate in vivo force/load readouts with on-animal scaffold depolymerization (fluorogenic SIP tracer); test cause–effect by modulating rehab intensity (underload/overload arms).

Risk, Failure Modes, and Mitigations
- Premature dissolution under incidental motion: incorporate sacrificial dissipative bonds and notch-insensitive fiber architectures; raise scission threshold during Stage 1 via transient ionic crosslinking that weakens as inflammation resolves.
- Insufficient physiological loading (patient immobility): design a secondary, biology-coupled failsafe (late-phase MMP-12–activated slow depolymerization) to prevent chronic persistence while preserving primary mechano-trigger dominance.
- Excess inflammation/fibrosis: enforce decorin-mimetic and pro-resolving cue ratios; restrict TGF-β activity with timed sponges; cap CCL2-mimetic dose via high-affinity, low-copy tethers.
- Overgrowth/ectopic ossification: use low-dose BMP-mimetics confined to osteon cores; TGF-β sequestration in muscle variant to avoid myofibrosis.

Milestones and Go/No-Go
- Year 1: Mechanophore–SIP library with distinct muscle vs bone thresholds; >10× difference in time-to-dissolution between subthreshold and suprathreshold regimens; cytocompatibility confirmed.
- Year 2: In vitro staged release fidelity (≥80% on-target timing by protease profile); anisotropic alignment metrics (muscle: coherency >0.6; bone: concentricity index >0.7); vascular channel patency with flow.
- Year 3: In vivo proof of closed-loop exit: ≥70% scaffold mass loss within 72 h of reaching 80% functional strength (muscle) or 70% native torsional stiffness (bone); superior function vs control scaffolds without mechanogates.

Expected Outcome and Impact
FoSiN converts the mechanical “signature” of successful healing into a biochemical off-switch, creating a tertiary niche that is self-organizing, self-staging, and self-terminating. The same forces that define restored function retire the therapy, eliminating guesswork about dwell time, avoiding permanent hardware, and generalizing across muscle and bone through tunable mechanochemical thresholds.
