text:
Title
Convex Unmixing of Exosome Fingerprints by Rapid MALDI-TOF Lipidomics with Single-Anchor Normalization

Hypothesis/Goal
A mixed exosome sample’s bulk physico-chemical fingerprint contains an approximately linear superposition of stable, cell-of-origin features. If we measure in a domain where additivity holds to first order and anchor intensities to a single exogenous standard, then constrained convex unmixing against a reference library from pure sources will rapidly and accurately quantify the mixing ratio between two cell types across a broad dynamic range.

Atomic Strategy
Choose a measurement modality with near-linear signal additivity (MALDI-TOF MS fingerprinting of intact/extracted exosomal lipids), then estimate mixture proportions with non-negative, sum-to-one convex unmixing using a fixed internal standard to linearize and stabilize intensity scaling.

Specific Aims
1) Build a locked reference library of exosome fingerprints
- Generate MALDI-TOF lipid fingerprints from pure exosomes of Cell Type A and Cell Type B across manufacturing-relevant variation (media lots, passages, bioreactor runs).
- Select a compact panel of discriminatory m/z features that are (i) stable within type, (ii) distinct across types, and (iii) minimally correlated with load or matrix fluctuations.
- Spike a single, synthetic isotopically labeled lipid cocktail as an internal anchor to correct for shot-to-shot ionization and matrix effects; fix acquisition parameters to “lock” the library.

2) Calibrate and validate a convex unmixing model with uncertainty
- Model: y = α·S_A + (1−α)·S_B + ε, with α∈[0,1], S_A,S_B reference vectors at the selected feature set.
- Correct modest non-linearities via a learned per-feature monotone mapping using anchor-normalized intensities (calibration curves from controlled mixtures).
- Solve for α by non-negative least squares with Tikhonov regularization; compute credible intervals via bootstrap over features and replicates.
- Validate against engineered mixtures spanning 5:95 to 95:5 in 5–10% steps; prespecify accuracy targets: absolute error ≤5% across 20–80% range, ≤8% at extremes; CV ≤5%.

3) Deliver a high-throughput, scalable workflow with in-line QC
- Implement 96/384-spot MALDI plates with automated spotting and batch acquisition; integrate on-plate QC triads: blank, anchor-only, pooled control.
- Build a lightweight analysis pipeline (feature extraction, anchor normalization, convex unmixing, uncertainty) delivering results in <5 minutes per sample at lab scale; scale to >120 samples/hour with automation.
- Define transfer procedures for manufacturing: at-line sampling, plate pre-templating, periodic re-locking of the library using the anchor and pooled controls; statistical process control charts to detect drift.

Methods Overview (high-level, non-procedural)
- Input: exosome preparations from two cell types (purified by a single standardized method across all conditions).
- Readout: MALDI-TOF mass fingerprints enriched for lipids (ceramides, sphingomyelins, phosphatidylserines, etc.). Lipids provide abundant, robust signals and improved additivity relative to complex proteomes.
- Normalization: a fixed, multi-component isotopically labeled lipid anchor spiked at a constant amount per spot enables within-plate and cross-plate scaling.
- Feature engineering: stability selection to identify 20–80 m/z features with high type-separation and low intra-type variance; remove features sensitive to total load via anchor-partialing.
- Modeling: anchor-normalized intensities; convex combination fit; per-feature weights inversely proportional to within-type variance; bootstrap to estimate α and 95% CI.
- Throughput: automated spotting and rapid spectra acquisition; cloud or local batch processing for real-time release-like decisions.
- Orthogonal check (for method qualification, not routine use): targeted ddPCR or small-RNA panel with two markers (one per type) to cross-verify α on a subset of samples.

Success Criteria and Metrics
- Accuracy: mean absolute error ≤5% for 20:80–80:20; ≤8% at 5:95–95:5 across n≥3 independent production runs.
- Precision: inter-plate CV ≤5%; day-to-day drift detected and corrected by anchor normalization and SPC rules.
- Speed: sample-to-result ≤5 minutes; ≥120 samples/hour with automated plate handling.
- Robustness: unchanged performance across reasonable variation in total exosome load (±2×) and matrix salt content after anchor normalization.
- Transferability: concordant α estimates (bias ≤3%) after instrument/site transfer using the same anchor and pooled control.

Risk Assessment and Mitigations
- Ion suppression/non-linearity: mitigated by isotopic anchor and feature-wise calibration; exclude features with high curvature; validate linearity on controlled mixtures.
- Batch/library drift: periodic re-locking with pooled controls; SPC charts to trigger re-calibration; versioned libraries.
- Biological heterogeneity: use multiple biological replicates per type to define S_A,S_B as mean±covariance; weight features by stability; report uncertainty.
- Low signal at extremes: concentrate input or increase shots at acquisition; algorithm inflates CI near 0/1 to avoid false certainty.

Scalability and Manufacturing Fit
- Hardware: widely available MALDI-TOF platforms, auto-spotters, barcoded plates; minimal consumables beyond matrix and anchor mix.
- Process integration: at-line aliquots from bioreactors, plate-based batching, automated QC, and electronic batch records; method supports rapid in-process ratio checks without physical sorting.

Validation Plan
- Phase 1 (lab-scale): construct library; select features; fit and cross-validate model on controlled mixtures; finalize accuracy/precision.
- Phase 2 (qualification): blind test across days/instruments; site-transfer study; orthogonal verification on 10–20% of samples.
- Phase 3 (manufacturing pilot): at-line deployment with SPC; demonstrate decision-making utility (e.g., blend adjustments) based on α estimates.

Deliverables
- Locked reference library (S_A,S_B), feature list, and anchor composition.
- Convex unmixing software with QC and uncertainty reporting.
- Validation dossier with accuracy, precision, robustness, and transfer studies.
- SOPs for measurement, analysis, and library maintenance.

Extensions
- >2 sources: expand to multi-endmember unmixing with non-negativity and simplex constraints; retain single-anchor normalization.
- Alternative readout (if instrument constraints): SERS fingerprinting with the same convex unmixing framework and anchor-based normalization.

Outcome
A rapid, accurate, and scalable method that infers the mixing ratio of exosomes from two cell types by exploiting linear additivity in MALDI-TOF lipid fingerprints, stabilized by a single internal anchor and solved by convex unmixing with quantified uncertainty.

Title
Iso-mobility microfluidic sorting for rapid, label-free quantification of exosome mixing ratios

Unified hypothesis–goal–question
If a steady, cross-stream electrolyte gradient is imposed in a pressure-driven microchannel, each exosome attains a size-independent diffusiophoretic mobility (μDP) set chiefly by its effective surface potential. Thresholding on μDP will passively separate mixed exosomes from two cell types into distinct outlets fast enough to count directly and recover their mixing ratio over 20:80–80:20 with high accuracy.

Atomic strategy
Collapse heterogeneous size and stiffness effects by operating in a regime where lateral drift depends predominantly on μDP (∼ zeta potential) and not on particle size: a constant transverse ln-salt gradient induces vDP = μDP∇lnCs, while axial advection U transports the flow. The net lateral displacement Δy ≈ (μDP∇lnCs L)/U serves as a one-parameter classifier. Geometry sets a single μ* that divides trajectories into two basins collected in separate chambers.

Proposed device and method
- Chip architecture (single-field, passive)
  - Upstream co-flow dialysis section to lower sample conductivity without dilution (thin nanoporous membrane between sample and low-ionic-strength dialysate).
  - Main separation channel (length L, height h ≈ 20–40 μm, width W ≈ 500 μm).
  - Two side reservoirs filled with hydrogel (ion-permeable, fluid-impermeable) maintain a stable transverse salt concentration difference ΔCs across the main channel.
  - Downstream Y-bifurcation defines two outlets (Left, Right) positioned so that μ < μ* exits Left and μ > μ* exits Right; an optional center waste slit can remove the overlap tail.
- Operating conditions
  - Continuous pressure-driven sample flow with average axial velocity U chosen to target Δy separation > 3σ of lateral diffusion for both populations within L.
  - Salt system: monovalent electrolyte (e.g., KCl) with tunable bulk Cs (0.1–5 mM) and pH 6.5–7.4 to maximize ΔμDP between the two exosome types while maintaining vesicle integrity.
  - Gradient control via reservoir molarity (Cleft, Cright) and hydrogel thickness; calibration once per cartridge.
- On-chip counting (label-free)
  - Interferometric scattering (iSCAT) windows integrated in each outlet channel segment provide single-particle counts at >10^5 events/min/lane with video processing.
  - Flowmeters on each outlet (thermal or Coriolis micro-sensors) quantify volumetric rates; counts normalize to concentration for QC but ratio uses event counts.
  - Optional electrical cross-check: a short-section RF impedance cytometer downstream of each window provides concordant counts on a subsampled stream.

Measurement principle and quantification
- The outlets directly yield event counts NA and NB over acquisition time τ. The estimated mixing ratio r̂ = NA/(NA + NB); 95% CI from binomial variance r̂(1 − r̂)/(NA + NB).
- Target precision: to achieve ±2% absolute error at 95% CI around r̂ ≈ 0.5 requires ≈ 2,400 total events; at 10^5 events/min this is <2 s acquisition per lane.
- Daily QC: run a two-standard mix of carboxylate- and amine-functionalized 100 nm beads (known μDP gap) to verify μ* location and counting linearity.

Specific aims and milestones
- Aim 1: Engineer stable cross-stream salt gradients and characterize μDP window.
  - Build hydrogel-side-reservoir modules; quantify ∇lnCs uniformity by fluorescence salinity probes.
  - Map Δy vs. U, L, ΔCs using bead standards to confirm size-independence over 50–200 nm.
  - Milestone: Δy separation exceeding 20 μm between standards at throughput ≥ 1 mL/h per lane.
- Aim 2: Determine μDP distributions for exosomes from the two cell types.
  - Run pure preparations to obtain outlet occupancy curves vs. μ* sweep (by adjusting ΔCs or U).
  - Choose fixed μ* maximizing Matthews correlation coefficient for binary classification.
  - Milestone: >90% correct assignment for each pure population at target flow.
- Aim 3: Quantitative validation on mixtures and complex matrices.
  - Test blinded series: 0:100 to 100:0 in 10% steps; primary endpoints: absolute error ≤5% across 20:80–80:20; analysis time ≤10 min for 100 μL samples.
  - Spike into 10% human plasma and conditioned media; assess matrix effects and correct via brief dialysis adjustments.
  - Milestone: Maintain accuracy and speed within spec; demonstrate robustness to total concentration spanning 10^7–10^10 mL−1.
- Aim 4: Scale-out and manufacturability.
  - Parallelize 64 lanes per 100×30 mm COP cartridge (hot-embossed), common manifolds for pressure and reservoirs.
  - Demonstrate ≥50 mL/h device throughput with linear scaling of counts and no cross-lane crosstalk.
  - Milestone: Coefficient of variation of r̂ across lanes ≤2%; cartridge cost <$20 at pilot scale.

Key design parameters (initial targets)
- L = 20–40 mm; W = 500 μm; h = 30 μm; U = 5–10 mm/s.
- ΔCs: 0.1→5 mM across W, yielding ∇lnCs ≈ 0.05–0.1 μm−1 near centerline.
- Hydrogel reservoir thickness 100–200 μm; water content ≥90% to minimize convection.
- Dialysis membrane MWCO ≈ 10–50 kDa; residence time ≤10 s to prevent aggregation.

Data analysis and calibration
- Real-time event detection via iSCAT difference imaging; adaptive thresholding tied to local background.
- Dead-time correction using inter-arrival distribution; coincidence probability kept <1% by automated subsampling splitter if rates exceed camera capacity.
- Daily μ* verification using bead QC mix; weekly verification with archived exosome controls.

Performance metrics and success criteria
- Distinguishability: >90% purity in each outlet for pure-type runs at chosen μ*.
- Quantitation: absolute error ≤5% for 20:80, 50:50, 80:20 mixtures; ≤8% for edge cases 10:90 and 90:10.
- Speed: sample-to-result ≤10 min for 100 μL; analysis window ≤2 min of counting.
- Throughput and scalability: ≥50 mL/h per cartridge; lane addition is linear with no sensitivity loss.
- Robustness: stable operation ≥2 h continuous run without fouling; <5% drift in μ*.

Risk assessment and mitigations
- Overlapping μDP distributions: tune salt species (LiCl vs KCl) and pH within physiological bounds to widen ΔμDP; adjust U and ΔCs to steepen classifier. If unresolved, introduce a third, central “ambiguous” outlet for exclusion without biasing ratios.
- Gradient instability or Joule heating: fully passive hydrogel reservoirs eliminate electrodes; temperature sensors near windows monitor stability; adjust pressure to maintain Peclet number.
- Matrix interference: upstream co-flow dialysis reduces protein/salt variability; brief 0.1% PVP added to suppress adhesion without altering μDP.

Path to manufacturing scale
- Materials: cyclic olefin polymer for low autofluorescence and solvent bonding; photopatterned polyacrylamide hydrogels for reservoirs; thin-film parylene membrane for dialysis.
- Processes: roll-to-roll embossing for channels; screen-printed salt reservoirs; laser bonding for assembly; automated QC of gradient with colorimetric strip at edge ports.
- Cleaning/CIP: single-use cartridge with external reusable manifold; no electrodes in wetted sample path.

Deliverables
- Open-source CAD and operating curves (Δy vs. U, ΔCs).
- Validated cartridge and manifold with 64-lane array.
- Software providing r̂ with CI in real time and audit trail.
- Cross-matrix validation report and SOP for routine use.

Impact
A single-field, size-decoupled physical classifier enables rapid, accurate, and scalable ratiometric quantification of exosomes from two cell types without labels or affinity steps, with a clear path from benchtop validation to parallelized manufacturing.

Title
Avidity-threshold glycoediting of extracellular vesicles for state-selective delivery to damaged/inflamed cells

Central hypothesis
Dense, multivalent display of E-selectin– and galectin-binding glycans on EV surfaces creates an avidity threshold that is only surpassed on damaged/inflamed cells, which upregulate E-selectin (activated endothelium) and assemble high-density galectin lattices (inflamed parenchyma). This yields state-selective capture and cargo delivery without targeting a cell lineage.

Atomic strategy
Exploit pathological lectin density, not cell identity: engineer EV surfaces exogenously to present clustered sialyl Lewis x (sLe^x) and poly-N-acetyllactosamine (poly-LacNAc) motifs at controlled valency/spatial spacing, so binding occurs only where E-selectin/galectin density is high enough to enable multivalent stabilization.

Specific aims
1) Build a modular, cell-free glycoediting toolkit to install high-valency sLe^x and poly-LacNAc on purified EVs.
2) Quantify avidity thresholds and state selectivity under physiologic shear and in inflamed parenchymal models; optimize valency/spacing for selective capture and uptake.
3) Validate selective delivery and therapeutic benefit in vivo in acute and chronic inflammation models.

Rationale
- Activated endothelium expresses E-selectin transiently and at high density during inflammation; resting endothelium does not.
- Many damaged/inflamed parenchymal cells externalize and/or accumulate galectin-3/-9 on the surface/extracellular matrix, forming lattices that preferentially bind multivalent β-galactoside/poly-LacNAc ligands.
- Multivalency and nanoscale spacing govern lectin–glycan binding avidity more than monovalent affinity; tuning these parameters enables “density-gated” binding to pathological states.

Approach

EV source and preparation
- Produce EVs from a well-characterized, scalable line (e.g., HEK293 or hMSC) using tangential flow filtration and size-exclusion chromatography; deplete protein aggregates and lipoproteins.
- Establish baseline glycome by lectin microarray and LC–MS glycomics to identify accessible acceptors.

Exogenous glycoediting chemistry (post-isolation)
- Step A: Mild surface desialylation with neuraminidase (controls: sham-treated).
- Step B: Chemoenzymatic chain extension to build poly-LacNAc:
  - B4GalT1 + UDP-Gal and B3GNT2 + UDP-GlcNAc in sequential or one-pot cycles.
- Step C: Terminal E-selectin ligands:
  - α1,3-fucosyltransferase FUT7 + GDP-Fuc to install Le^x; ST3Gal-IV + CMP–Neu5Ac to generate sLe^x.
  - Optional sulfation (GlcNAc-6-O-sulfotransferase + PAPS) to modulate selectin affinity; titrate to avoid L-selectin bias.
- Orthogonal route (for rapid screening): insert lipid-anchored glycopolymers (cholesterol/DSPE-PEG) bearing defined sLe^x/poly-LacNAc valency and 5–10 nm spacing; remove unincorporated polymers by SEC.
- Maintain EV integrity (NTA size, TEM morphology, CD9/CD63/CD81 Westerns); quantify installed glycan copy number per EV by fluorophore-labeled lectins/antibodies and absolute calibration beads.

Spatial valency engineering
- Control glycan density via enzyme stoichiometry, reaction time, and polymer mole-percent.
- Map nanoscale clustering by super-resolution (dSTORM) using labeled anti-sLe^x/galectin-binding probes; compute Ripley’s K to quantify clustering radius.

In vitro state-selectivity assays
- Activated endothelium model: Human microvascular endothelial cells stimulated with TNF-α (4–6 h) to induce E-selectin; resting cells as controls; E-selectin knockout/blocked controls.
  - Parallel-plate flow chamber at physiologic shear (1–4 dyn/cm^2): measure tethering, rolling velocity, firm adhesion of fluorescent EVs; fit to Bell model to derive effective off-rates vs E-selectin density.
- Inflamed parenchyma model: Epithelial/fibroblast lines treated with IL-1β or TGF-β to elevate cell-surface galectin-3; quantify surface galectin by flow; use galectin inhibitors (e.g., lactose or TD139) as competition controls.
  - Assess EV binding/uptake (confocal, flow cytometry) vs resting cells; determine avidity threshold by titrating EV glycan valency and plotting binding vs receptor density.
- Cargo delivery function: Load EVs with siRNA or mRNA (e.g., NF-κB pathway reporter) by electroporation or membrane permeation; quantify knockdown/reporting in activated vs resting cells; include off-target cell types.

In vivo validation
- Acute inflammation: LPS-induced lung inflammation or localized TNF-α–induced vascular activation. Administer labeled EVs IV; optical/whole-body imaging and tissue biodistribution by capillary depletion to separate endothelial vs parenchymal signals.
- Chronic inflammation: DSS colitis or arthritis models to test persistence and parenchymal targeting.
- Blockade experiments: anti–E-selectin antibody and galectin inhibitor pretreatment to parse pathway contributions.
- Therapeutic test: EVs carrying anti-inflammatory siRNA (e.g., RelA) or STING inhibitor; endpoints: cytokines, histology, edema, clinical scores.

Controls
- Untreated EVs; desialylated-only EVs; EVs with nonbinding glycans (e.g., αGal).
- Size- and charge-matched liposomes with identical glycans to compare vesicle class.
- Heat-inactivated enzymes and sugar-nucleotide–free reactions.

Success criteria and readouts
- Chemistry: >5,000 installed sLe^x/poly-LacNAc epitopes per EV; preserved size (mode shift <15 nm).
- Selectivity in vitro: ≥10-fold higher adhesion under flow to activated vs resting endothelium; ≥5-fold higher uptake in galectin-high vs galectin-low cells; blockade reduces binding by ≥70%.
- In vivo: ≥3–5× enrichment of engineered EVs in inflamed tissue vs contralateral/healthy; reduced signal with receptor blockade; minimal liver/spleen increase beyond baseline EV clearance.
- Function: ≥50% target gene knockdown in inflamed cells in vivo; significant reduction of inflammatory readouts vs controls.

Manufacturability and QC
- Enzymatic steps in continuous-flow microreactor with on-column SEC purification; sugar nucleotide recycling enzymes to cut cost.
- Batch release: NTA/TEM, protein markers, glycan epitope quantitation, endotoxin, residual enzyme/sugar nucleotides, hemolysis/complement activation assays.

Risk mitigation
- Off-target capture by leukocyte selectins: tune sulfation down; favor E-selectin–biased sLe^x; test in leukocyte-rich matrices.
- Complement activation: maintain terminal sialylation level; assess CH50 and C3 deposition; include PEGylation if needed.
- EV heterogeneity: use density gradients to enrich for CD81^high subpopulations with higher glycoprotein acceptor density; normalize by epitope per particle rather than mass.

Milestones and timeline (18–24 months)
- M1 (Month 3): Robust, scalable glycoediting with reproducible epitope density; integrity confirmed.
- M2 (Month 8): In vitro state-selective adhesion/uptake with defined avidity thresholds and blockade validation.
- M3 (Month 14): In vivo biodistribution showing selective accumulation at inflamed sites; mechanism parsed by blockade.
- M4 (Month 20–24): Therapeutic efficacy with safety profile and manufacturability package.

Deliverables
- A standardized, cell-free EV glycoediting protocol (SOP) with QC metrics.
- A glycan valency/spacing design map that defines state-selective binding windows for E-selectin/galectin pathways.
- Preclinical dataset demonstrating selective delivery and efficacy in at least two inflammation models.

Title: LECTOR—A Glycan–Lectin Complementarity Platform to Predict Organotropic Metastasis Across Cancers

Unified hypothesis–goal:
Organ-specific metastasis can be predicted from a tumor’s surface and vesicular glycan “barcode” and its complementarity to the organ-resolved lectin landscape of vascular, immune, and stromal cells. We will compute this complementarity to output a per-organ metastasis risk vector for any cancer.

Atomic strategy:
Model organotropism as a lock–key problem between tumor/exosomal glycans (lock) and organ lectins (key), quantified as a Glyco–Lectin Complementarity Index (GLCI) for each organ.

Innovation and fit:
- Purely glycobiology-based: relies on glycans and glycan-binding proteins and their measured or inferred interactions.
- Pan-cancer: uses universal glycosylation principles and exosome readouts, independent of tissue of origin.
- Predicts destination: returns a calibrated organ risk distribution, not just metastasis likelihood.
- Novelty: no existing method computes organotropic risk by explicit lectin–glycan complementarity across an organ-resolved atlas.

Proposed deliverable:
A clinical-grade computational predictor (LECTOR) fed by a minimally invasive exosomal glycan assay and/or tumor glyco-transcriptome, returning patient-specific probabilities for metastasis to lung, liver, bone, brain, lymph node, adrenal, peritoneum, and other organs.

Specific aims:

Aim 1. Build the Organ Lectin Atlas (OLA).
- Assemble organ- and cell-type–resolved expression maps for glycan-binding proteins (selectins, galectins, Siglecs, C-type lectins, asialoglycoprotein receptor, stabilins, LYVE1, etc.) from single-cell RNA-seq, spatial proteomics, and curated protein databases.
- Weight lectins by vascular accessibility, luminal display, and cell abundance to yield an organ-specific “accessible lectin vector.”
- Curate a lectin specificity matrix linking each lectin to recognized glyco-epitopes (e.g., α2,3-/α2,6-sialylation, Lewis antigens, LacNAc repeats, high-mannose, Tn/STn, fucosylation variants, sulfated GAG motifs).

Aim 2. Derive the Tumor GlycoBarcode (TGB).
- Noninvasive stream: capture patient plasma small extracellular vesicles; quantify glycan features by multiplexed lectin-binding microarray and confirmatory LC–MS glycomics on pooled samples.
- Tissue stream: infer glycan features from tumor RNA-seq of glycosyltransferases/sulfotransferases and transporter enzymes using a constraint-based glycosylation network to produce probabilistic presence of glyco-epitopes.
- Harmonize both streams into a standardized glycan feature vector with uncertainty estimates.

Aim 3. Compute organ-specific GLCI and train LECTOR.
- Define GLCI(org) = f[TGB · (lectin–glycan specificity) · OLA(org)], producing an affinity potential per organ.
- Train a calibrated multinomial Bayesian model that maps GLCI to observed first-site metastasis using retrospective cohorts with known metastatic destinations.
- Output a patient-level organ risk vector with calibrated probabilities and credible intervals.

Aim 4. Mechanistic and functional validation.
- Microfluidic “GlycoFlow” assays: perfuse patient-derived CTCs/exosomes over organ-specific endothelial monolayers engineered to modulate dominant atlas lectins; measure adhesion, rolling, and transmigration under physiologic shear; test reversibility with targeted glycosidases or lectin blockers.
- In vivo stratification: in PDX/CRISPR-engineered models differing only in specific glycosylation nodes, test whether LECTOR-predicted high-risk organs are enriched targets of metastasis.
- Prospective clinical pilot: longitudinal plasma sampling in stage II–III patients; assess whether pre-metastatic LECTOR scores forecast subsequent organ sites.

Data, features, and model details:
- Glycan feature set: α2,3 vs α2,6 sialylation balance; total sialic acid density; core/core2 O-GalNAc; Tn/STn; LacNAc repeat length; terminal galactose exposure; high-mannose prevalence; fucosylation (Le^x/a/y/b); bisecting GlcNAc; polylactosamine; GAG class and sulfation patterns (HS 2-O/6-O/N-sulfation codes).
- Lectin panel: E-/P-selectin; Gal-1/3/8/9; Siglec family (notably -7, -9); DC-SIGN/L-SIGN; MRC1; ASGPR; MBL; stabilin-1/2; LYVE1; CLEC family members.
- Knowledge-based binding kernel from glycan array data encodes lectin–epitope affinities and multivalency effects; uncertainty propagated via Bayesian priors.

Study design and milestones:
- Year 1: Build OLA and specificity kernel; optimize exosomal assay; N=300 retrospective plasma/tissue pairs across breast, lung, colorectal, melanoma, prostate, kidney.
- Year 2: Train and cross-validate LECTOR on multi-institutional cohorts (target N=1,000); pre-register performance metrics per organ.
- Year 3: Mechanistic validation in GlycoFlow and PDX; finalize analytical validation of the exosome assay.
- Year 4: Prospective pilot (N=300) across pan-cancer; decision-curve analysis for surveillance routing.

Primary outcomes:
- Discrimination: organ-specific AUC/PR-AUC for first metastatic site; top-1 and top-2 accuracy vs standard-of-care staging.
- Calibration: Brier score and calibration slope per organ.
- Mechanistic concordance: correlation between predicted organ GLCI drivers and loss-of-function/competition experiments.

Risk management and falsification:
- Heterogeneity of glycosylation: mitigate via exosome sampling (temporal smoothing) and uncertainty-aware modeling.
- Dominance of hemodynamic first-pass (liver/lung): include a neutral exposure prior; if GLCI fails to improve prediction over exposure alone, hypothesis is falsified.
- Confounding immune selection: incorporate organ-resident immune lectins (Siglecs, galectins) explicitly in OLA.

Deliverables:
- LECTOR software with documented GLCI computation.
- Organ Lectin Atlas public resource.
- CLIA-ready exosomal lectin-array kit with calibration controls.
- Reference cohorts and protocols for GlycoFlow validation.

Success criteria:
- Pre-specified improvement of ≥0.10 in organ-specific AUC over clinical baseline in at least four major metastatic organs.
- Mechanistic validation showing ≥30% reduction in adhesion/extravasation upon disrupting predicted dominant lectin–glycan pairs.
- Prospective pilot demonstrating net clinical benefit for imaging triage based on predicted top-2 organ risks.

Impact:
This work reframes organotropism as a quantifiable glycan–lectin complementarity problem, enabling a tumor-agnostic, mechanism-grounded predictor of metastatic destination that is actionable for surveillance and intervention.

text:
Title
Organ-First Glycoaddressing to Predict Organotropism Across Cancers: A Compatibility Score From Endothelial Glycocalyx–Tumor Lectin Interactions

Premise (integrated question–hypothesis)
Do human organs present stable, organ-specific “glycoaddresses” on their vascular and interstitial surfaces that act as selective welcome signs, and can a physics-informed compatibility score between these organ glycoaddresses and a patient’s tumor lectin/glycan-binding repertoire predict the first metastatic destination across cancers?

Atomic strategy
Model organotropism as a multivalent binding-energy problem between:
- Locks: accessible organ-specific glyco-epitopes within endothelial glycocalyx and adjacent matrix.
- Keys: tumor cell and extracellular vesicle (EV) surface lectins and selectin-ligand motifs.
The sum of effective binding energies under physiologic shear yields an organ-specific compatibility score that predicts where metastasis seeds first.

Specific aims
1) Build a Human Organ Accessible Glyco-Epitope Atlas
- Scope: lung, liver, bone marrow, brain microvasculature, lymph node, and peritoneum.
- Materials: primary human organ-specific microvascular endothelial cells matured under organ-mimetic cues; donor organ perfusates preserving luminal glycocalyx; decellularized tissue slices for spatial mapping.
- Measurements:
  - Multiplex cyclic lectin imaging (iterative lectin panels with enzymatic specificity controls) for spatially resolved epitope density and clustering.
  - LC–MS glycomics/glycoproteomics for N-/O-glycans; targeted disaccharide profiling for GAGs (HS/CS/DS) including sulfation codes.
  - Single-molecule force spectroscopy using canonical lectins for motif-level avidity quantification.
- Output: organ-specific motif dictionaries with quantitative parameters (abundance, valency, nanocluster spacing) and variance across donors; definition of “public core motifs” conserved per organ.

2) Define Patient Tumor Lectin Repertoires (TLR) Across Cancers
- Cohorts: pan-cancer plasma (EVs) and tumor resections (≥12 tumor types; discovery n=300; validation n=400).
- Measurements:
  - Surface proteomics (cell and EV) for galectins, Siglecs, C-type lectins, selectin ligands (sLeX/sLeA-bearing scaffolds), HS-binding domains, and glycosidases; targeted LC–MRM for clinical scalability.
  - Activity-based probes for functional lectins and sialidase/fucosidase activities.
  - Binding constants of TLRs to organ motifs via organ-mimetic glycan microarrays and acoustic/SPR under controlled shear.
- Output: per-patient TLR vector with affinities and effective valencies.

3) Construct and Validate the GlycoMatch Score
- Mechanistic model: multivalent lattice/adhesion model estimating effective on-rate and dissociation under shear; features include motif density, spacing, TLR valency, and catch/slip-bond behavior.
- Empirical layer: machine learning calibration on microfluidic adhesion readouts and clinical outcomes.
- Assays for training/validation:
  - Multi-organ GlycoHoming Chip: parallel microchannels coated with native extracts and synthetic mimetics (defined HS/CS sulfation patterns; sialylated/fucosylated N-/O-glycans on mucin-like scaffolds). Readouts: rolling velocity, arrest frequency, firm adhesion, transmigration.
  - Enzymatic perturbations (neuraminidase, heparinase I/III, fucosidase) and CRISPR perturbation of key tumor lectins for causal validation.
- Clinical endpoints: prediction of first metastatic site within 18–24 months from baseline in:
  1) high-risk localized cohorts (surveillance),
  2) de novo metastatic patients (triage of likely occult sites).
- Performance targets: AUROC ≥0.80 pan-cancer; ≥0.75 within major tumor types; decision utility demonstrated by net benefit analyses for imaging prioritization.

Experimental design and analysis
- Organ atlas reproducibility: ≥10 donors per organ; bootstrap to define core motifs; model inflammation-state covariates.
- Shear profiles: organ-appropriate wall shear stress (e.g., liver sinusoid low shear; lung microvasculature higher shear) encoded into the compatibility model.
- Confounding controls: incorporate simple vascular filtration metrics and known non-glycan cues (e.g., integrins) as nuisance covariates without diluting glyco-driven predictions.
- In vivo mechanism checks: patient-derived xenograft models with engineered lectin gain/loss and glycomimetic decoy administration to test redirection or attenuation of organotropism.

Translational outputs
- Organ Accessible Glyco-Epitope Atlas (public resource) and motif dictionary with quantitative parameters.
- GlycoMatch computational predictor (physics-informed + ML) generating per-organ compatibility scores from Atlas × TLR.
- Two deployable assays:
  1) Blood-based EV GlycoHoming Test: EV adhesion indices across organ channels outputting GlycoMatch probabilities.
  2) Targeted TLR Proteomic Panel: LC–MRM of tumor/EV lectins paired with Atlas for in silico predictions.

Milestones and timeline
- Months 0–12: Atlas v1 for six organs; glycochip prototype; cross-donor CV <20% for core motifs.
- Months 12–24: TLR profiling in 300 patients; initial GlycoMatch fit; preregistered prospective protocol.
- Months 24–36: Prospective pilot (n=200) with interim AUROC ≥0.78; finalize causal organ–lectin pairs.
- Months 36–48: External validation (n=400); lock clinical assay; tech transfer kit and software.

Risk mitigation
- Donor variability: consensus core motifs via robust statistics; sensitivity analyses across inflammatory states.
- Chip stability: migrate to synthetic glycopolymers with controlled spacing once equivalence to native extracts is shown.
- Overfitting: preregistration, nested cross-validation, and external validation; proscribed feature sets grounded in biophysics.

Success criteria
- Demonstrated causal organ–lectin pairs where perturbation switches or reduces organ-specific seeding in vivo.
- Prospective, multi-center validation meeting performance targets and improving diagnostic yield of targeted imaging.
- Regulatory-ready documentation for the EV GlycoHoming Test and TLR Panel as research-use diagnostics.

Innovation
This organ-first, compatibility-based framework reframes metastasis as selective glycoaddress recognition rather than a tumor-intrinsic propensity. By quantifying accessible organ glyco-epitopes and patient-specific lectin repertoires, the GlycoMatch Score delivers a pan-cancer, mechanistically grounded predictor of metastatic destination and exposes actionable glycan–lectin pairs for organ-specific interception.

text:
Title: Back-Propagation of Organ Settlement Glycocodes to Predict Pan-Cancer Organotropism

Central hypothesis-question (indistinguishable): Do successful metastases in a given organ converge on a minimal, organ-specific “settlement glycocode” of terminal glycan motifs and glycopeptide contexts, and can a primary tumor’s capacity to acquire each organ’s glycocode under short-term organ-derived selection pressures predict its future metastatic destination?

Atomic strategy: Treat organotropism as a glycan-mediated docking-and-survival constraint. Infer organ-invariant settlement glycocodes directly from already-settled metastatic cells in each organ, then score any primary tumor by (i) its baseline distance to each organ’s glycocode and (ii) its short-term inducibility toward that code under organ-mimetic conditions. The highest inducibility-adjusted fit predicts destination.

Innovation and why it is new:
- Reverse-inference from settled metastases to define organ glycocodes (not from primaries forward).
- Uses an “inducibility slope” (speed and extent of glycome reprogramming toward an organ code within 48 hours) as the predictive variable, rather than static glycan features alone.
- Functionally grounds predictions in adhesion/avidity to organ-specific lectin landscapes under physiological shear, creating a mechanistic linkage between glycan state and organ entry/persistence.
- Pan-cancer by design: organ settlement constraints are hypothesized to be lineage-agnostic once colonization occurs.

Deliverables:
- OrganoGlyco-Fit: a computational predictor that outputs per-organ metastasis probabilities.
- GlycoDock Chip: a microfluidic device presenting physiologic densities of organ lectin cocktails and ECM glycosaminoglycan patterns to quantify adhesion/retention of patient cells.
- A minimal 12-plex lectin/anti-glycan panel per organ for FFPE and cytometry, and a companion plasma exosome glycan signature for noninvasive testing.
- Public Organ-Settled GlycoAtlas: per-organ glycocodes and reference datasets.

Specific aims:

Aim 1. Build the Organ-Settled GlycoAtlas.
- Samples: Viable tumor cells from clinical metastases in liver, lung, brain, bone, and adrenal across ≥10 primary cancers; matched normal organ tissue; n≥50 metastases per organ.
- Single-cell surface glycomics: Lectin-barcoded CITE-seq to capture glycan motifs with transcriptomes; integrate with cell-surface capture proteomics.
- Glycan structural resolution: PGC-LC-MS/MS of released N- and O-glycans, sialic acid linkage (α2,3 vs α2,6), fucosylation (core vs outer-arm; Lewis antigens), O-glycan truncation (Tn/sTn), LacNAc extension, bisecting GlcNAc, sulfation patterns.
- Intact glycopeptide MS: Glycosite- and protein-context mapping on key adhesion/immune-evasion receptors (integrins, CD44, MUC1/16, L1CAM, PD-L1).
- Host organ lectin landscape: Endothelial/parenchymal/immune lectin proteomes (selectins, galectins, C-type lectins, Siglecs) and heparan sulfate fine structure (NS/NA sulfation, 6-O/2-O distribution).
- Outcome: For each organ, derive a compact “settlement glycocode”: minimal terminal motifs, linkage/isomer constraints, and prioritized glycopeptide contexts that are necessary and recurrently sufficient for settlement.

Aim 2. Engineer the GlycoDock functional assay.
- Device: Parallel microchannels coated with organ-specific lectin cocktails and immobilized heparan sulfate/ECM patterns at physiological densities; tunable shear (0.5–10 dyn/cm2).
- Readouts: Rolling, firm adhesion, detachment under ramped shear, and post-adhesion signaling (phospho-ERK/FAK) by live imaging; quantified as an organ-specific Avidity Index.
- Calibration: Use settled metastatic cells from each organ as positive controls; non-matching organ metastases and normal epithelial cells as controls to set organ-specific thresholds.

Aim 3. Compute inducibility toward organ glycocodes.
- Short-term organ-mimetic challenge: Culture primary tumor cells (fresh biopsy or PDX-derived) for 48 hours in organ-conditioned media (organotypic endothelial+parenchymal co-culture secretome), physiologic oxygen, and cytokine profiles; include decellularized organ ECM fragments.
- Metabolic flux probing: Pulse with stable-isotope-labeled monosaccharide precursors (e.g., 13C-ManNAc, 13C-GlcNAc, 13C-Fucose) to quantify nucleotide-sugar pool dynamics and pathway reserve capacity.
- Readouts pre/post-challenge: Lectin-barcoded single-cell profiling; intact glycopeptide MS for sentinel receptors; targeted quantification of key terminal motifs and linkages.
- Inducibility slope: For each organ, compute ΔGlycoFit = f(structural shift toward organ glycocode per unit time) × g(lectin-function gain on GlycoDock). This captures both biochemical convergence and functional docking.

Aim 4. Train, validate, and translate the OrganoGlyco-Fit predictor.
- Model: Multi-task learner integrating (i) baseline glycan distance to each organ code, (ii) ΔGlycoFit, (iii) glycoenzyme regulatory capacity (expression/epigenetic accessibility of key transferases/transporters), and (iv) nucleotide-sugar flux metrics.
- Validation:
  - Retrospective: Primary tumors with known first-site metastasis; blinded prediction of destination.
  - Prospective: Patients with high-risk primaries; serial plasma exosome glycan profiling to externalize the assay; adjudicate first-site events.
  - Causality tests: CRISPRa/i or small-molecule glycoediting to force or disrupt organ glycocodes in PDX/orthotopic models; test redirection of organotropism.
- Translation artifacts:
  - Minimal lectin/antibody IHC panel per organ for FFPE primaries.
  - Plasma exosome “settlement motif” ratios for triage when tissue is scarce.

Methods overview (key steps):
- Sample processing: Rapid cell-surface capture; gentle deglycosylation workflows to preserve sialic/fucose linkages; parallel nuclei extraction for epigenetics (ATAC-seq on glycoenzyme loci).
- Structural analytics: PGC-LC for isomers; exoglycosidase arrays for linkage confirmation; low-pH stabilization for sialic acids; targeted PRM for sentinel glycopeptides.
- Host mapping: Mass-spec disaccharide profiling of heparan sulfate; organ lectin quantification by targeted proteomics; surface density calibration on GlycoDock using quantitative fluorescence standards.
- Computational assembly: Graph-based glycan representation; Earth Mover’s Distance from primary to organ glycocode; biophysical avidity modeling vs lectin densities; inducibility modeled as time-derivative under constraint of enzyme capacity and sugar pools.

Milestones and go/no-go criteria:
- Year 1: Draft glycocodes for liver/lung/brain (n≥25 each) and functional thresholds on GlycoDock; AUC≥0.75 intra-cohort classification of settled cells to their organ by glycan features alone.
- Year 2: Inducibility slopes from 60 primaries; ΔGlycoFit adds ≥0.10 AUC over baseline distance for destination prediction in retrospective data.
- Year 3: Prospective pilot (n≥100); time-to-first-site C-index≥0.70; finalize 12-plex organ panels and exosome signatures.

Risk mitigation:
- Intra-tumor heterogeneity: Single-cell profiling; report mixture-of-codes and predict multi-organ risk envelopes.
- Organ mimic fidelity: Use multiple donors and adjustable cytokine/ECM contexts; verify by comparing induced states to clinical metastasis glycocodes.
- Non-glycan determinants: Integrate simple covariates (e.g., integrin expression) only as modulators; maintain glycobiology as the primary driver.

Expected outcomes:
- A validated, organ-specific, pan-cancer predictor of first metastatic destination based on inducibility toward organ settlement glycocodes.
- Mechanistic levers to modulate organotropism by targeting specific glycosylation steps or lectin interactions.
- A deployable clinical workflow using either tissue (lectin IHC + inducibility micro-assay) or plasma (exosome glycocode panel).

text:
Title: Endothelial “Zip Codes” for Metastasis: An Organ Lectin–Glycan Complementarity Atlas and Predictor (ELZA/ELGC)

Core hypothesis-question (inseparable):
Do organ-specific luminal endothelial lectins and glycosaminoglycan (GAG) sulfation motifs constitute stable “zip codes” that circulating tumor cells (CTCs) decode through their surface glycans, thereby determining organ-specific metastasis destinations across cancers?

Atomic strategy:
Predict organotropism by a single variable—the lectin–glycan complementarity (LGC) between a tumor’s glycan motif vector and each organ’s endothelial luminal lectin/GAG “zip code.” Higher LGC increases first-contact adhesion under flow, extravasation likelihood, and colonization probability.

Overall objective:
Deliver a pan-cancer, glycobiology-first predictor that ranks organ-specific metastatic risk from a patient’s tumor glycome, using a standardized atlas of organ endothelial lectins and GAG sulfation motifs and a biophysical LGC scoring model.

Specific aims:
1) Build the Organ Endothelial Zip Code Atlas (ELZA).
2) Parameterize the Lectin–Glycan Complementarity (LGC) model under physiological flow.
3) Deliver and validate a clinical assay and predictor that outputs a ranked organotropism profile.

Aim 1: ELZA—map organ luminal endothelial lectins and GAG “zip codes”
- Scope: Lung, liver, bone marrow, brain, adrenal, lymph node, peritoneum, omentum.
- Samples: Human donor tissues (surgical discard, transplant-grade) and matched non-human primate/mouse for cross-species validation.
- Endothelial luminal capture:
  - Antibody-guided endothelial immunoaffinity enrichment (CD31/CD34/VE-cadherin) with cell-surface capture glycoproteomics to restrict to externally oriented N-glycosylated peptides.
  - Proximity biotinylation ex vivo via perfusion with membrane-impermeant NHS esters to label luminal-accessible proteins prior to endothelial isolation.
- Lectinome characterization:
  - Targeted proteomics for membrane-tethered or secreted endothelial lectins: selectins (E/P), organ-typed C-type lectins (e.g., liver sinusoidal lectins), galectins (luminally bound), scavenger/CLR-type receptors; confirmation by surface immuno-EM on microvessel fractions.
  - Spatial transcriptomics to support proteomic calls and filter inducible vs constitutive expression.
- GAG sulfation barcode:
  - Vessel-enriched heparan/chondroitin/dermatan sulfate disaccharide LC–MS to quantify domain-level NS/NAc and O-sulfation patterns.
  - Panel of sulfation-motif probe proteins (FGFs, chemokines, antithrombin variants) to infer mesoscale HS binding motifs on intact microvessels.
- Output: For each organ, an “endolectome vector” (lectin abundance, avidity state, multimerization) and a “GAG motif vector” (sulfation-domain features), standardized to a common units scale.

Aim 2: Parameterize LGC under physiological shear
- Tumor glycome acquisition (pan-cancer):
  - From primary tumor cells, CTCs, or organoid-derived cells: released N-/O-glycans by LC–MS, sialic acid linkages (α2,3/α2,6), fucosylation (Lewis antigens), LacNAc extension, terminal Gal/GalNAc features, ganglioside classes; quantify as a motif vector.
  - Complement with multiplex lectin-binding profiles on intact cells to capture multivalency/clustering.
- Interaction kinetics and avidity:
  - Create organ-mimetic surfaces: immobilize organ-specific lectin mixes and GAGs reflecting ELZA vectors at physiological densities; confirm functional orientation.
  - Under controlled flow (physiologic wall shear), measure rolling, tethering, firm adhesion, and detachment of tumor cells and glycan-decorated nanoparticles.
  - Derive per-organ effective on/off rates and adhesion work as functions of tumor motif abundance and clustering.
- LGC score:
  - Define LGC(organ|tumor) = f(lectin–glycan affinity matrix, motif abundances, multivalency, GAG-assisted co-recruitment, shear).
  - Calibrate LGC to observed adhesion probabilities and early extravasation in ex vivo microvessel-on-chip and precision-cut vessel slice assays.

Aim 3: Predictor and clinical assay; validation
- Predictor:
  - Train a Bayesian-multiphysics model mapping tumor motif vector × ELZA vectors → organ-specific LGCs → ranked metastasis risk.
  - Incorporate priors for organ blood flow and microvascular geometry only as normalization, not drivers.
- Clinical assay (device + panel):
  - A 12-plex microfluidic “ELGC-Chip” with parallel organ-mimetic channels displaying organ-specific lectin/GAG presentations at calibrated densities and flow.
  - Input: 1) CTCs from 10–20 mL blood, or 2) glycan-vesicles assembled from patient tumor membrane extracts.
  - Output: Real-time adhesion index per channel; software converts to organ risk ranks and confidence intervals.
- Validation:
  - Retrospective: Patients with known primary and first-site metastasis; blinded prediction from archived tumor glycome or banked CTCs.
  - Prospective: New diagnoses across major solid tumors; baseline ELGC-Chip result vs. first-site metastasis within 24 months.
  - Benchmarking: Compare against clinical variables and genomic signatures; primary endpoint = top-1 organ hit rate; secondary = time-to-event stratification.

Key design features and controls:
- Constitutive vs inducible filtering: Identify and down-weight inflammation-inducible lectins (e.g., cytokine-induced selectins) to isolate stable organ codes.
- Platelet/leukocyte bridging controls: Repeat flow assays with and without autologous plasma and depleted platelets to quantify trans-adhesion contributions separately.
- Tumor heterogeneity: Use single-cell lectin profiling to estimate subclone motif distributions; compute ensemble LGC with uncertainty bounds.

Deliverables:
- ELZA: Open atlas of human organ endothelial lectins and GAG motif profiles with density estimates.
- ELGC: A validated, generalizable scoring function and software that outputs organ-specific metastasis probabilities from any tumor glycome input.
- ELGC-Chip: A clinical-grade microfluidic assay providing a same-day organotropism report.

Milestones:
- Year 1: ELZA v1 for lung, liver, bone; flow assay prototypes; initial LGC parameterization.
- Year 2: ELZA expanded to brain, adrenal, peritoneum; ELGC-Chip engineering freeze; retrospective validation.
- Year 3: Multicenter prospective trial; analytical/clinical validation; regulatory pathway for laboratory-developed test.

Novelty and impact:
- Reframes metastasis prediction from tumor-sent signals to organ-inherent endothelial codes.
- Purely glycobiological readout with pan-cancer applicability.
- Predicts organ-specific destinations (ranked risks) rather than occurrence alone, enabling surveillance tailoring and pre-emptive interventions.

Go/no-go criteria:
- Go if LGC explains ≥50% variance in first-site destinations in retrospective cohorts and ELGC-Chip top-1 hit rate ≥60% across ≥4 cancer types.
- Pivot to include mobile lectins (platelet/immune) only if endothelial-only LGC underperforms after constitutive filtering.

Risk mitigation:
- If organ codes vary by age/comorbidity, stratify ELZA by demographic covariates and include adjustment in LGC.
- If specific tumor classes are glycan-silent for key motifs, add enzyme-masked glycome unmasking step ex vivo to reveal latent ligands for measurement only (no patient exposure).

Success criterion:
A validated, organ-ranked metastasis predictor driven by lectin–glycan complementarity that generalizes across solid tumors and informs organ-targeted surveillance and prophylaxis.

text:
Title: GlycoSeek—An acellular organ-glycocalyx microarray for pan-cancer prediction of organotropic metastasis from patient CTC behavior

Hypothesis/Question:
If organ microvascular and matrix glycocalyx patterns are the primary gatekeepers of intravascular arrest and extravasation, then presenting organ-specific glycan topologies under physiological shear will elicit preferential multivalent adhesion of circulating tumor cells (CTCs). The organ channel that maximizes adhesion kinetics reveals the patient’s imminent metastatic destination.

Atomic Strategy (single insight):
Encode organ identity using only its glycocalyx “sugar code”—not cells or proteins—then let patient CTCs reveal organotropism by their adhesion preference under flow.

Overview:
We will build a multiplexed microfluidic “glyco-organ” array in which each parallel channel displays a synthetic, organ-specific glycocalyx (liver, lung, bone, brain initially). Patient CTCs are flowed through all channels simultaneously at controlled shear. Rolling, arrest, and detachment kinetics are quantified to compute a Glyco-Organ Preference Index (GOPI) per organ. A trained model maps the GOPI vector to probabilities of first-site metastasis.

Why this is novel:
- Uses acellular, compositionally defined glycocalyx mimics as the sole organ determinant.
- Treats organotropism prediction as a direct behavioral choice assay by patient CTCs, not a correlative molecular signature.
- Encodes organ identity via multivalent glycan topology and density, including glycosaminoglycan (GAG) fine structure, enabling pan-cancer applicability.

Specific Aims:
1) Build organ-specific glycocalyx libraries
   - Define “glycan barcodes” per target organ: densities and cluster topology of sialylated N/O-glycans (e.g., sLeX/A, polyLacNAc), gangliosides, and GAGs (heparan sulfate with defined sulfation motifs, chondroitin variants, hyaluronan length).
   - Chemoenzymatically synthesize and site-specifically immobilize glycans into brush-like hydrogels with tunable stiffness (0.5–5 kPa) and nanoscale clustering (10–200 nm).

2) Engineer the GlycoSeek device
   - 8–16 parallel microchannels (1–2 cm), each coated with one organ’s glycan barcode; optional inclusion of immobilized, correctly glycosylated adhesion proteins only when required to maintain physiological presentation (kept constant across runs).
   - Flow control to recapitulate organ-specific microvascular shear (0.5–5 dyn/cm2).
   - Real-time brightfield/IRM imaging for rolling velocity and arrest; integrated impedance and shear-ramp modules to quantify detachment thresholds.

3) Derive the Glyco-Organ Preference Index (GOPI)
   - From each channel: fraction of cells that arrest ≥30 s, mean rolling velocity, on-rate (k_on) of arrest events, detachment shear at 50% release (τ50), and residence half-life (t1/2).
   - Normalize features by capture efficiency on a non-glycan control channel.
   - Compute GOPI per organ as a weighted composite; the patient-level vector is GOPIpatient = [GOPIliver, GOPIlung, GOPIbone, GOPIbrain, …].

4) Validate prediction of first-site metastasis
   - Calibration set: cell lines with known organotropic derivatives; CRISPR/enzymatic perturbations (e.g., sialidase, heparinase) confirm glycan-mediated causality.
   - Retrospective cohort (n≈120; breast, prostate, lung, colorectal, melanoma, pancreas, ovary, kidney, sarcoma): archival blood, known first-site outcomes.
   - Prospective cohort (n≈200): baseline and on-therapy draws; blinded prediction of first-site within 12–24 months.
   - Competing risks modeling (cause-specific and subdistribution hazards) with GOPI features; report AUC for first-site prediction, concordance, calibration, and net benefit.

Design and Methods (concise):
- Sample: 10–20 mL blood; label-free CTC enrichment by inertial focusing + negative selection to preserve glycocalyx.
- Assay: Run enriched CTCs through all channels in parallel at organ-matched shear for 20 min; shear ramp 0–20 dyn/cm2 to obtain τ50; total assay <2 hours.
- Readout: Automated tracking of rolling/arrest; impedance for cell-surface coverage; replicate channels for intra-patient heterogeneity.
- Mechanism mapping: On-chip glycan perturbation panels (local sialidase, heparinase, fucosidase; lectin or GAG blocking) to identify dominant adhesion modules per patient.
- Quality control: Lot-matched glycan brushes; density quantified by fluorophore-labeled reference lectins; stiffness by AFM.

Pan-cancer generalizability:
- Focus on conserved lectin–glycan modules used across cancers: selectin ligands (sLeX/A), galectin-binding polyLacNAc domains, Siglec ligands (α2,3/α2,6 sialylation), and HS sulfation patterns.
- Organ channels differ by relative densities, clustering, chain length, and sulfation “codes,” not by peptide cues, ensuring cancer-agnostic applicability.

Data Analysis:
- Feature engineering: per-cell kinetics aggregated by robust estimators; uncertainty captured by bootstrap.
- Model: Bayesian hierarchical classifier mapping GOPIpatient to organ risk probabilities; incorporates prior organ prevalence by cancer type but allows patient-specific deviations.
- Outputs: Ranked organ risk with credible intervals; “poly-organotropism” flag if multimodal.

Milestones:
- M1 (Month 6): Reproduce known tropisms in calibration lines; GOPI separation ≥0.3 between preferred vs non-preferred organs.
- M2 (Month 12): Retrospective AUC ≥0.78 for first-site prediction across pooled cancers.
- M3 (Month 24): Prospective AUC ≥0.80; decision-curve analysis shows net benefit vs. standard clinicopathologic models.

Controls and Validation:
- Negative controls: non-malignant epithelial cells; leukocytes; glycan-scrambled surfaces.
- Specificity: Loss of preference after enzymatic removal of key glycans on either channel or CTCs.
- Orthogonal readouts: Single-CTC “lectinome” profiling (benign, non-destructive fluorescent lectins post-assay) to correlate with GOPI features.

Risks and Mitigations:
- Phenotypic drift of CTCs: Minimize processing time; validate stability over 6 h.
- Non-glycan adhesion confounders: Keep peptide ligands absent or equalized; perturb with glycan-specific enzymes to confirm causality.
- Heterogeneity: Use replicate channels and mixture modeling; report multi-site risk when indicated.

Deliverable/Path to Translation:
- Bench-top instrument with disposable GlycoSeek cartridges.
- Software that returns per-organ risk probabilities and recommended imaging surveillance priorities.
- CLIA-ready LDT after prospective validation; manufacturing via roll-to-roll glycan brush patterning.

Success Criteria:
- Statistically significant improvement in predicting first-site metastasis over current standards.
- Demonstrated mechanistic specificity to glycan–lectin interactions.
- Reproducibility across cancer types and clinical sites.

Expected Impact:
- A fast, behavior-based, pan-cancer test to anticipate where metastasis will seed, enabling targeted surveillance and pre-emptive interventions.
- A mechanistic window into patient-specific glycan–lectin dependencies that could inform anti-metastatic strategies.

label: elements_bypass
text:
Title: GOT-Array: A pan-organ synthetic glycocalyx chip that elicits cancer cell “adhesiotypes” under flow to predict organ-specific metastasis

Integrated hypothesis-goal-question:
If organ-specific endothelial/parenchymal glycocalyces are the primary gatekeepers of metastatic lodging, then projecting each organ’s native glycan landscape onto a microfluidic array and measuring the binding kinetics of a patient’s circulating tumor cells (CTCs) under physiological flow will reveal an organ-resolved “adhesiotype” that predicts the next metastatic destination across cancers. Can we turn organotropism into an ex vivo, same-week readout by eliciting it directly against organ-mimetic glycocalyces?

Atomic strategy:
Project the human organ-resolved glycocalyx onto a chip and read out CTC multivalent glycan–lectin adhesion preferences under defined shear. The adhesiotype vector is the biomarker.

Innovation (what is fundamentally new):
- A pan-organ synthetic glycocalyx projection: organ-specific glycan identity, density, nanoscale spacing, and post-synthetic modifications (sialylation, fucosylation, sulfation) are recapitulated on inert surfaces, not cells.
- Direct functional elicitation of organotropism under physiological hemodynamic shear, rather than passive omics inference.
- A single quantitative output—the adhesiotype vector—maps to organ-specific metastatic risk through a calibrated probabilistic model.
- To our knowledge, no prior diagnostic projects multi-organ human glycocalyx states under flow to elicit and score patient CTC organotropism for pan-cancer prediction.

Specific aims:
1) Build organ-resolved glycocalyx modules
- Derive organ-specific glycan templates (liver, lung, bone, brain, adrenal, lymph node) from human spatial glycomics references and lectin-binding atlases.
- Fabricate polymer-brush “glycocalyx” monolayers presenting defined motifs with tunable: identity (e.g., α2,3/α2,6-sialylated LacNAc, Lewis antigens, HS/CS sulfation codes), density (0.1–10% mol), nanoscale spacing (5–50 nm via DNA-origami/PEG spacers), and tether stiffness.
- Chemoenzymatic editing stations (sialyl-/fucosyl-/sulfotransferases; sialidase/heparinase challenges) to dial organ-mimetic states and run mechanism-resolving perturbations.

2) Create the GOT-Array microfluidic assay
- Parallelized channels, each bearing one organ glycocalyx module; integrated pressure control to mimic microvascular wall shear (0.5–20 dyn/cm2).
- CTC preparation: immunomagnetic depletion of leukocytes, gentle enrichment of viable CTCs; optional co-flow of autologous platelets/plasma to capture bridging interactions.
- High-speed TIRF/oblique microscopy for single-cell adhesion under flow; automated tracking to extract on-rate, off-rate, rolling velocity, arrest fraction, and dwell-time distributions.

3) Learn the adhesiotype-to-organ mapping
- Define a per-organ adhesiotype feature set: {roll→arrest transition probability, dwell-time percentiles, bond cluster size, force-dependent off-rate, enzymatic sensitivity deltas}.
- Train a Bayesian competing-risks model to output, for each organ, P(first-site metastasis within 12 months | adhesiotype, cancer type, standard covariates).
- Generate interpretable “glycan dependency fingerprints” by comparing baseline vs enzyme/blocking shifts (e.g., P-/E-selectin, galectins, Siglecs, HS-binding inhibitors).

Study design:
- Phase 0 (mechanistic calibration): 12 well-characterized organotropic cell lines (e.g., lung-, bone-, brain-tropic sublines) to confirm expected preferences and shear dependence; blinded decoding of engineered glycan swaps.
- Phase 1 (feasibility, n=60): metastatic-risk enrichment across breast, lung, colorectal, melanoma, prostate (n≈12 each). Baseline GOT-Array within 72 h of blood draw; imaging follow-up q8–12 weeks for 12 months.
- Phase 2 (multicenter validation, n=300): stratified by primary site and stage; head-to-head against clinicopathologic nomograms and standard liquid biopsy.

Primary endpoints:
- Organ-specific time-to-first-metastasis prediction: cause-specific C-index and 12-month organ-AUC.
- Net reclassification improvement over standard of care for top-2 organ predictions.
Secondary endpoints:
- Mechanistic interpretability: fraction of prediction attributable to sialoglycan vs HS vs fucosylated determinants.
- Test–retest reproducibility (intraclass correlation) from duplicate runs and serial sampling (every 8 weeks).

Key experimental details:
- Glycocalyx fabrication
  - Organ modules prepared on carboxyl-PEG brushes; click chemistry to present defined glycan libraries; ligand density verified by fluorescent lectins and mass-tagged probes.
  - Nanoscale spatial patterning via DNA origami tiles or block-copolymer phase separation; AFM/SPR/QCM-D to quantify presentation and viscoelasticity.
- Flow assay
  - Shear ramp protocol (0.5→5→15 dyn/cm2) to probe catch–slip behavior; capture rolling and firm adhesion windows.
  - Competitive inhibition panels: soluble lactose, sLeX mimetics, heparin/HS oligos to map dependency; pre/post enzymatic edits to construct differential adhesiotypes.
- CTC handling
  - Low-stress magnetic depletion; size-based cleanup optional; viability dyes; parallel runs with/without platelets to assess cloaking effects.

Data and modeling:
- Feature engineering emphasizes physics-informed metrics (bond lifetime vs shear; multivalency index).
- Hierarchical partial pooling across cancer types to ensure pan-cancer applicability while allowing organ–tumor interactions.
- Calibration with decision curves to support clinical use (surveillance imaging prioritization, prophylactic site-directed therapies).

Validation of biological causality:
- If lung module predilection is abolished by sialidase or E-selectin blockade, lung-risk attribution is assigned to sialofucosylated selectin ligands.
- CRISPR or glycoediting of candidate CTC glycosyltransferases in reference lines shifts adhesiotypes as predicted (preclinical criterion).

Risk assessment and mitigations:
- Variability of human organ glycans: use population-averaged templates plus tunable enzyme “dials” and sensitivity deltas for robustness.
- CTC heterogeneity/low counts: aggregate across thousands of events from serial draws; Bayesian updating to refine individual risk.
- Non-glycan confounders (integrins/chemokines): standardized chemokine-free baseline; optional chemokine gradients as orthogonal module for sensitivity analyses without entering the clinical classifier.

Milestones and deliverables (24 months):
- M6: Library of validated organ glycocalyx modules with QC metrics; shear-calibrated assay.
- M12: Feasibility study complete; locked feature set; preliminary organ-specific AUCs.
- M18: External site reproducibility; finalized Bayesian model; clinical reporting format.
- M24: Multicenter validation readout; CLIA-ready SOPs; de-identified dataset and model card.

Clinical product concept:
- Form: a benchtop disposable microfluidic chip (GOT-Array) plus software that outputs an organ-ranked risk table and glycan-dependency explanation.
- Sample-to-answer: <48 hours from 10–20 mL peripheral blood.
- Output: Adhesiotype report with top-3 organ risks, confidence intervals, and mechanistic levers (e.g., “lung risk driven by sLeX–E-selectin; HS-insensitive”).

Expected impact:
- Converts organotropism from a months-long observation to a functional, same-week ex vivo readout.
- Pan-cancer utility with interpretable glycobiology, enabling organ-specific surveillance, trial stratification, and glycan-targeted intervention strategies.

text:
Title
GLYCAN-LOCK: Predicting organ-specific metastasis by matching single-cell CTC glycan motifs to an atlas of organ vascular glycocalyx/lectin signatures

Hypothesis and Research Goal
Hypothesis: The first committed step of organotropic metastasis is governed by a quantitative “glycan–lectin/glycocalyx complementarity” between circulating tumor cells (CTCs) and organ-specific vascular beds. A single scalar match score computed from CTC surface glycan motifs and organ endothelial glycocalyx/lectin profiles predicts the next metastatic destination from blood alone.
Goal: Develop and validate a pan-cancer blood-based predictor of organ-specific metastasis by measuring single-cell CTC glycomes and matching them to an Organ Vascular Glycome and Lectin Atlas (OVGLA).

Atomic Strategy
Reduce organotropism to a key–lock metric: a multivalent binding potential between (i) CTC-displayed glycan motifs and (ii) organ-specific endothelial lectins and glycocalyx chemotypes (selectins, siglecs, galectins, C-type lectins; heparan/chondroitin sulfate sulfation codes; sialylation/fucosylation states). Compute an organ-wise complementarity index under physiological shear to predict where CTCs will arrest and extravasate.

Specific Aims
Aim 1. Build OVGLA: a reference atlas of human organ vascular glycocalyx and lectin expression.
- Tissues: lung, liver, bone marrow, brain, adrenal, lymph node, peritoneum, skin.
- Inputs per organ: primary microvascular endothelial cells and decellularized microvessel fragments from donor tissues.
- Measurements:
  - Multiplex lectin-oligo sequencing (Lectin-Seq) to quantify accessible endothelial glycans.
  - Targeted glycosaminoglycan (GAG) disaccharide LC–MS to resolve heparan/chondroitin sulfate sulfation patterns.
  - Spatial proteomics for endothelial lectins (E/P/L-selectins, Gal-1/3/9, DC-SIGN family, Siglec repertoire), and mucin/adhesion scaffolds (PSGL-1 ligands, CD44 variants).
  - Shear-adjusted avidity parameters via surface plasmon resonance under flow for top motif–receptor pairs.
Deliverable: For each organ, an Organ Endothelial Interaction Vector (OEIV): concatenated motif weights for glycan accessibility, lectin densities/affinities, and GAG sulfation features.

Aim 2. Single-cell CTC glycome profiling from whole blood across cancers.
- Cohorts: 600 patients (discovery n=300; validation n=300) spanning breast, lung, colorectal, prostate, melanoma, pancreatic, renal, head & neck, and gynecologic cancers; stage II–IV; serial draws every 8–12 weeks.
- CTC isolation: antigen-agnostic enrichment (size/deformability microfluidics + CD45 depletion). Index single-cell capture.
- Measurements per CTC:
  - scLectin-Seq: 50–80 DNA-barcoded lectins resolving sialylation linkages (α2,3 vs α2,6), fucosylation (Lewis^x/a/y), branching (bisecting GlcNAc), LacNAc extension, O-GalNAc core types.
  - scGlyco-proteomics: nanoPOTS-FAIMS LC–MS/MS of intact glycopeptides for carrier proteins (mucins, integrins).
  - scGAG proximity labeling: nanocage-tethered enzymatic reporters to infer local heparan sulfate binding preferences.
  - Minimal transcript panel (20 genes) for epithelial/mesenchymal state to control for phenotype.
Deliverable: For each CTC, a CTC Glycan Motif Vector (CGMV) with calibrated intensities and multivalency parameters.

Aim 3. Compute organotropism from glycan complementarity and validate clinically.
- Model: Glycan–Lectin Complementarity Index (GLCI).
  - For organ o and CTC i: GLCI_i,o = Σ_k w_k,o × f(match(CGMV_i,k, OEIV_o,k), shear, multivalency), where k indexes motifs/receptors; f encodes on-rate under shear and off-rate stabilization by multivalent clustering.
  - Shear weights derived from organ-specific microvascular shear ranges; multivalency from lectin oligomerization and scaffold spacing.
- Output: Ranked organ propensity vector per patient; top-1 and top-2 predictions reported.
- Training/Validation:
  - Discovery: fit f and w via nested cross-validation using retrospective imaging/clinical metastasis destinations emerging within 6 months post-draw.
  - Prospective: blinded prediction in validation cohort; primary endpoint = accuracy of first-site metastasis within 12 months; secondary = time-to-metastasis discrimination, AUC for organ-specific hazards.
- Experimental orthogonal validation:
  - Competitive Organ Flowchip: parallel microchannels presenting immobilized OEIV-mimetic surfaces for all organs; quantify preferential CTC capture/rolling; compare to in vivo outcomes.
  - Blocking controls: motif-specific enzymatic desialylation/defucosylation on aliquots to test predicted loss of organ preference ex vivo.

Methods Overview
- OVGLA generation: standardized culture with organ-mimetic cues; confirm endothelial identity; validate glycan accessibility with enzyme controls (neuraminidase, fucosidase, heparinase).
- scLectin-Seq: 1) stain live CTCs with a panel of recombinant lectins bearing unique DNA barcodes; 2) UV-release and NGS quantification; 3) spike-in standards to normalize across runs.
- scGlycoproteomics: carrier-free prep; library search constrained by motif calls from Lectin-Seq to improve ID rates.
- Modeling: Bayesian hierarchical framework pooling across cancer types but allowing tumor-type random effects; integrate patient covariates (therapy, inflammation) as nuisance regressors; calibrate GLCI to absolute risk using time-dependent competing risks.

Pan-Cancer Applicability
- Glycan motifs are shared effectors across cancers despite genomic heterogeneity; model trained across indications with organ-level targets constant.
- Sub-analyses by cancer type ensure generalization; the predictor reports per-organ risk irrespective of tumor origin.

Innovation (Novelty)
- Converts organotropism into a single, quantitative glycan complementarity score measurable from blood.
- Integrates a first-of-its-kind Organ Vascular Glycome and Lectin Atlas with single-cell CTC glycomes.
- Uses competitive, multi-organ glycan-mimetic flow capture as a functional readout aligned with the computational score.
- Avoids tumor-tissue biopsies; leverages glycobiology rather than gene expression or mutation panels.

Milestones and Success Criteria
M1 (Year 1): OVGLA completed for 8 organs; batch-stable OEIVs; intra-organ CV <15%.
M2 (Year 2): scLectin-Seq panel locked; per-CTC technical CV <20%; recover ≥10 CTCs/sample in ≥60% of patients.
M3 (Year 3): Discovery model trained; top-1 organ prediction accuracy ≥55% (baseline clinical ≤30%); top-2 accuracy ≥75%.
M4 (Year 4): Prospective validation meets primary endpoint; cause-specific C-index gain ≥0.10 over clinicoradiologic models.
M5 (Year 5): CLIA-ready assay (GLYCAN-LOCK) with fixed 24-lectin minimal panel and software for GLCI reporting.

Risk and Mitigation
- Low CTC counts: aggregate across longitudinal draws; apply Bayesian borrowing; integrate ctDNA-derived glycan enzyme signatures as weak priors without violating glycobiology basis.
- Systemic inflammation confounding endothelial glycomes: incorporate plasma cytokine panel; adjust OEIVs with inflammation scalers learned from donors.
- Therapy-induced glycan remodeling: include therapy status and time-since-therapy as covariates; perform within-patient delta-GLCI analysis.

Deliverables
- OVGLA public resource (OEIVs, raw data, protocols).
- GLYCAN-LOCK assay: single-tube scLectin-Seq kit and cloud model producing per-organ GLCI with confidence intervals.
- Competitive Organ Flowchip as optional functional confirmatory test.
- Clinical decision report: ranked organ risks, recommended imaging windows per organ, and longitudinal trend.

Impact
A pan-cancer, blood-only, glycobiology-native predictor that transforms organotropism into a measurable complementarity problem, enabling earlier, organ-targeted surveillance and intervention without invasive biopsies.
