Title
MyoSOS-3x: A closed-loop mechano–calcium stress–responsive gene circuit that deploys membrane repair, scaffold reinforcement, and calcium homeostasis programs in dystrophin-deficient muscle

Central hypothesis and question
Hypothesis: A closed-loop genetic circuit that detects the pathological signature of dystrophin-deficient myofibers—sustained membrane stress with aberrant Ca2+ influx—can autonomously and reversibly upregulate endogenous repair, scaffold, and Ca2+-handling networks to prevent myofiber necrosis and restore function without re-expressing dystrophin.
Question: Can an adaptive, damage-gated circuit outperform constitutive single-gene therapies by matching therapeutic output to real-time injury load while minimizing off-target burden?

Atomic strategy
Exploit a pathognomonic state variable—coincident, sustained activation of mechano- and Ca2+-responsive transcriptional pathways—to drive an integrated triad of endogenous effectors via compact RNA-guided transcriptional modulation (CRISPRa/i), establishing a cell-intrinsic alarm-and-response loop that turns on only when and where damage occurs and turns off on recovery.

Specific aims
1) Engineer a mechano–calcium “AND-gate” promoter that activates only under sustained, supra-physiologic co-stimulation of TEAD (YAP/TAZ) and NFAT pathways, with tunable time-averaging to filter normal exercise transients.
2) Build a tri-modal effector panel that (a) accelerates membrane repair (ESCRT/annexin axis), (b) strengthens cytoskeleton–ECM coupling (integrin/talin/LARGE1 axis), and (c) normalizes Ca2+ handling (SERCA/PMCA upregulation with SOCE dampening), using endogenous-gene CRISPRa/i for compactness and scalability.
3) Demonstrate closed-loop efficacy and safety: reduced dye uptake/CK, preserved force, lowered necrosis/fibrosis, and minimal off-target activation across in vitro stretch/injury assays and dystrophic rodent/canine models, advancing to translational CMC readiness.

Circuit architecture
- Sensor (input layer): A synthetic composite promoter comprising:
  - 4–6x TEAD response elements (mechano-transduction via YAP/TAZ)
  - 4–6x NFAT response elements (calcineurin/Ca2+ pathway)
  - Minimal promoter with uORF-based thresholding
  - Kinetic filter (degron-tagged transactivator) to require persistence (>minutes) for activation and to self-extinguish on recovery
  - Optional NOT gate via NF-κB site knock-in with repressor to avoid chronic inflammation–driven misfiring
- Controller (processing layer):
  - AAV-expressed compact dCas effector (e.g., dCas12f fused to VPR for activation) under the Sensor promoter
  - Parallel small repressor (MS2-KRAB-MeCP2) constitutively low-level, recruited via aptamered guide RNAs to enable CRISPRi on selected targets
  - Guide RNA array (U6/Pol III cassettes) encoding:
    - Activation guides (CRISPRa): Anxa6, Chmp4b, Pdcd6 (ALG-2) for repair; Itga7, Tln2, Large1 for scaffold; Atp2a1 (SERCA1), Atp2b4 (PMCA4) for Ca2+ clearance
    - Repression guides (CRISPRi): Stim1 and Orai1 (dampen SOCE), Calpains (Capn1/2) if needed for proteolysis control
  - Built-in negative feedback: a Sensor-driven microRNA targeting the dCas12f transcript to cap maximal output and enforce adaptation
- Effectors (output layer): Endogenous loci modulation; no dystrophin/mini/micro-dystrophin or exon-skipping components

Delivery and manufacturability
- Vectorization: Dual-AAV strategy (AAV9 or AAVrh74) for skeletal and cardiac tropism
  - Vector A: Sensor promoter → dCas12f-VPR (+ small insulators, degron)
  - Vector B: U6 guide array with MS2 loops; EF1α-low → MS2-KRAB-MeCP2; muscle detargeting miRNA sites (miR-122/142-3p) to reduce liver/immune expression
- Payload economy: Endogenous-gene modulation avoids large ORFs; guides are easily reconfigurable for future tuning; dual-AAV fits within established CMC platforms
- Scalability: Standard suspension HEK293 production; existing AAV supply chains and release assays; modular guide arrays support rapid iteration without retooling capsids

Safety features
- Spatial restriction: Muscle-tropic capsid; miRNA detargeting for liver/hematopoietic cells
- Temporal restriction: Sensor-only activation under sustained mechano–Ca2+ stress; degron-based auto-off; no constitutive effector expression
- Dose capping: Negative feedback on dCas; ceiling on maximum promoter output via uORFs
- Genotoxicity minimization: No nucleases; transcriptional modulation only; off-target screens inform guide selection
- Immune risk management: Humanized effectors where possible; low basal expression reduces antigen burden

Efficacy readouts and success criteria
- In vitro (human DMD iPSC-myotubes):
  - Logic validation: AND-gate activation only with combined cyclic strain + Ca2+ ionophore stress; minimal activation under physiologic pacing
  - Repair kinetics: Reduced FM1-43/dextran influx, faster resealing time
  - Ca2+ homeostasis: Restored Ca2+ transient amplitude/decay; reduced SOCE
  - Mechanics: Improved sarcomere integrity under stretch; enhanced laminin adhesion
- In vivo (mdx and d2-mdx; then GRMD):
  - Function: Increased specific force, reduced eccentric contraction deficit
  - Histopathology: Fewer necrotic fibers, lowered Evans blue uptake, decreased fibrosis (Picrosirius Red), improved fiber size uniformity
  - Biomarkers: Lower serum CK/LDH; transcriptomic signature consistent with targeted upregulation/repression
  - Dynamics: Sensor activity spikes with exertion-induced injury and resolves at rest

Translation plan
- Indication: Ambulatory and non-ambulatory DMD; skeletal and cardiac involvement addressed via shared tropism and Ca2+ control
- Patient heterogeneity: Genotype-agnostic approach suitable across dystrophin mutations
- CMC/Regulatory: Leverage prior AAV9/rh74 precedents; modular guide arrays as well-defined constituents; non-integrating, non-nuclease mechanism simplifies risk profile
- Clinical entry strategy: Initial low-dose, regional limb-focused administration with systemic escalation contingent on safety; PD monitoring via circulating muscle-enriched miRNAs and imaging of a transient, detargeted reporter in first-in-human only (if allowed)

Risk analysis and mitigation
- Risk: Over-suppression of SOCE impairing adaptation
  - Mitigation: Weak CRISPRi guides; sensor gating ensures repression only during damage; reversal on recovery
- Risk: Over-stiffening from scaffold upregulation
  - Mitigation: TEAD/NFAT dependency links reinforcement to need; inclusion of degradable talin2 splice variant targets; removal if stiffness markers rise
- Risk: Immune responses to Cas effector
  - Mitigation: Minimal, intermittent expression; consider ortholog screening/humanization; steroid cover per standard gene therapy practice (regulated clinically)
- Risk: Cardiac-specific tuning required
  - Mitigation: Cardiac-optimized guide subset (e.g., ATP2A2 rather than ATP2A1); capsid selection; separate cardiac sensor variant if needed

Why this is novel
- Mechanism: A closed-loop, state-sensing gene circuit that computes a mechano–calcium signature to coordinate three endogenous repair axes has not been deployed in DMD.
- Modality: Endogenous network reprogramming via compact RNA-guided transcriptional control, rather than ORF replacement or dystrophin surrogates.
- Control theory: Built-in kinetic filtering and negative feedback yield adaptive, on-demand therapy matched to injury dynamics.

Milestones (Go/No-Go)
- M1: AND-gate specificity and tunability demonstrated in human DMD myotubes (Go if on/off ratio >20:1 and <5% basal leak)
- M2: Triad modulation achieves ≥50% reduction in membrane dye influx and ≥30% faster Ca2+ decay vs. controls in vitro
- M3: In mdx/d2-mdx, ≥25% improvement in specific force and ≥40% reduction in Evans blue–positive fibers at 12–16 weeks; no persistent off-target activation in liver/spleen
- M4: GRMD feasibility with functional gains and acceptable tox; CMC lock for dual-AAV

Scope boundaries and compliance
- No direct correction, restoration, or re-expression of dystrophin (no micro-dystrophin, exon skipping, or dystrophin editing).
- Gene therapy modality via AAV-delivered synthetic promoter and RNA-guided transcriptional regulators.
- Addresses membrane instability, Ca2+ dysregulation, and mechanical uncoupling; secondarily reduces inflammation/fibrosis via decreased necrosis load.

Expected outcome
MyoSOS-3x will convert damaging mechanical load into a targeted, self-limited genetic response that restores membrane integrity, re-establishes ECM anchoring, and normalizes Ca2+ fluxes, thereby reducing myofiber loss and improving function across DMD genotypes without engaging dystrophin.

Title
Mechanostability-Mimic Gene Therapy (M-MGT) for Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy

Rationale and central hypothesis
Dystrophin loss destabilizes the sarcolemma, distorts mechanotransduction, and shifts gene expression away from membrane repair, calcium homeostasis, and regeneration toward inflammation and fibrosis. We hypothesize that installing an artificial “stability signal” in myofibers—decoupled from actual membrane integrity—will drive a protective transcriptional setpoint that preemptively hardens muscle against damage without restoring dystrophin. In effect, muscle cells are “convinced” that their walls are strong, so they continuously express endogenous emergency-repair and homeostatic programs.

Atomic strategy
Replace missing mechanical cues with a single synthetic stability signal that persistently actuates a curated, multi-gene endogenous protection program in muscle.

Therapeutic design (gene therapy only)
- Component 1: Stability-Mimic Switch (SMS)
  - A compact, synthetic membrane-anchored receptor or scaffold that constitutively engages a muscle-safe mechanotransduction cascade (integrin/FAK→SRF; YAP/TAZ→TEAD) at a preset, non-oncogenic setpoint independent of external load or dystrophin.
  - Muscle-restricted expression; tunable activity via built-in degron or self-limiting feedback domain to maintain a narrow signaling window.

- Component 2: Protective Program Actuator (PPA)
  - A programmable transcriptional activator (compact CRISPRa or synthetic TF) that modestly upregulates a predefined panel of endogenous loci representing the “stable, protected myofiber” state. Categories include:
    - Membrane repair and resealing (annexin/ESCRT/MG53-like pathways).
    - Calcium homeostasis and excitability damping (SR Ca2+ uptake/ buffering; brakes on store-operated Ca2+ entry; calpain restraint).
    - Anti-inflammatory and anti-fibrotic tone (negative regulators of NF-κB; TGF-β antagonism).
    - Mitochondrial resilience and redox control (biogenesis and antioxidant programs).
    - Myofibrillar/ECM coupling enhancers that do not recreate dystrophin (select integrin/costamere stabilizers).
    - Regeneration competence (satellite cell support signals balanced to avoid exhaustion).
  - The PPA is transcriptionally gated downstream of the SMS; when the artificial stability cue is present, the PPA enforces the protective setpoint.

- Component 3: Safety and control
  - Myofiber-selective promoters; microRNA target cassettes to suppress expression in off-target tissues.
  - Activity ceiling via engineered negative feedback (e.g., SMS outputs induce a repressor above a set threshold).
  - Non-integrating vectors; an emergency shutdown transgene (clinically actionable kill-switch) encoded in a separate, co-delivered cassette.

Vectorization and delivery
- Dual or tri-vector AAV system optimized for skeletal and cardiac muscle, using clinically validated serotypes and payload-splitting strategies. Manufacturing and dose-sparing are supported by compact regulatory architecture and setpoint rather than maximal overexpression.

Disease processes addressed (system-level coverage)
- Membrane instability: constitutive readiness of resealing machinery; reinforcement of non-dystrophin adhesion nodes.
- Calcium dysregulation: restored uptake/buffering and reduced pathological influx, limiting calpainopathy.
- Inflammation: tonic induction of endogenous brakes on innate/adaptive activation.
- Fibrosis: counter-signaling to profibrotic pathways while preserving necessary ECM maintenance.
- Energetics: improved mitochondrial biogenesis/quality control to tolerate contraction-induced stress.
- Regeneration: preserved satellite cell pool function and coordinated differentiation upon injury.

Specific aims
- Aim 1: Define the stability-setpoint program.
  - Derive a consensus “mechanical-stability” gene signature from healthy load-bearing muscle vs. dystrophic muscle across species and ages. Select a minimal, safety-optimized target panel spanning the categories above; set effect-size ceilings for each.
- Aim 2: Build and validate the Stability-Mimic Switch (SMS).
  - Engineer and screen SMS variants to achieve steady, mid-level activation of SRF/TEAD-like outputs in myotubes without hyperproliferative signaling. Map dose–response and establish the safe operating window.
- Aim 3: Construct the Protective Program Actuator (PPA).
  - Program modest upregulation of the target panel using a compact activator. Validate multiplex specificity and absence of unintended pro-fibrotic or pro-oncogenic shifts in vitro.
- Aim 4: Integrate SMS→PPA (closed-loop setpoint control) and test efficacy.
  - In mdx and severe DMD models, assess sarcolemmal integrity, calcium handling, force, fatigue, fibrosis, necrosis, inflammation, and cardiac function. Benchmark against best-in-class non-dystrophin comparators.
- Aim 5: Safety, durability, and translational readiness.
  - Off-target transcriptomics/proteomics; vector biodistribution; immunogenicity profiling; long-term tumor surveillance; reversibility testing via the shutdown cassette. Establish release criteria for GMP lots and a first-in-human dosing rationale.

Milestones and go/no-go criteria
- M1: SMS achieves predefined reporter activation without increasing proliferation markers beyond baseline in primary human myotubes.
- M2: PPA raises each gene category within a narrow, pre-specified fold-change band; no enrichment of oncogenic/fibrotic signatures.
- M3: In mdx mice, ≥40% reduction in leak markers and ≥25% improvement in specific force with no fibrosis or arrhythmic liabilities.
- M4: Durable efficacy and safety at 6–9 months; scalable manufacturing metrics achieved.

Translation and clinical path
- Indication: ambulatory and early non-ambulatory DMD to protect residual muscle and myocardium, independent of mutation class.
- Route: systemic administration with cardiomuscular tropism.
- Pharmacodynamic biomarkers: serum CK reduction; transcriptional setpoint score in accessible tissue; imaging of fibrosis/inflammation; circulating cytokine/fibrosis panels.
- Safety monitoring: rhythm surveillance, proliferation/fibrosis imaging, vector shedding, immune responses; real-time deactivation option.

Anticipated risks and mitigations
- Excess mechanosignaling (hyperplasia/fibrosis): tight setpoint control, feedback ceilings, and predefined PD windows.
- Off-target transcriptional activation: multiplex design restricted to validated loci; genome-wide off-target screens; muscle-specific expression.
- Immunogenicity: humanized protein domains; de-targeting from APC-rich tissues; transient immune modulation only if required by safety review.
- Cardiac effects: separate cardiac-specific tuning and conservative setpoints validated in cardiomyocytes prior to systemic dosing.

Differentiation and novelty
- The therapy does not correct, restore, or re-express dystrophin. It installs a synthetic, dystrophin-independent stability signal that continuously enforces a protective, multi-locus endogenous program. This “mechanostability emulation” architecture—an artificial stability switch coupled to a multiplex actuator—constitutes a new gene therapy paradigm for DMD with a direct path to clinical translation via established AAV platforms and comprehensive safety gating.

Title
MiNoR-seq: a unified mitochondrial–nuclear targeted sequencing assay for simultaneous HSCT engraftment confirmation and multilineage clonal diversity tracking

Atomic strategy
Exploit naturally occurring, heritable mitochondrial heteroplasmy patterns as high-entropy clonal barcodes transmitted from donor HSCs into all progeny (including enucleate lineages), while concurrently genotyping a compact, ancestry-informative nuclear SNP panel for quantitative donor–recipient chimerism. Implement both within a single UMI-duplex targeted sequencing workflow applicable to minimally processed blood and magnetically enriched lineage fractions.

Specific aims
1) Build and analytically validate MiNoR-seq, a dual-panel assay that captures the full mitochondrial genome and a 400–600 site nuclear SNP panel in one library to output: a) % donor chimerism and b) lineage-resolved clonal diversity metrics.
2) Demonstrate comprehensive lineage coverage by applying MiNoR-seq to myeloid, lymphoid, erythroid (reticulocyte-enriched), and megakaryocytic (platelet) fractions, plus whole-blood back-up, at serial post-transplant timepoints through 1 year.
3) Establish clinical utility by correlating MiNoR-seq engraftment and diversity trajectories with standard STR chimerism and clinical outcomes, and by testing whether diversity contraction or donor-fraction decline anticipates graft failure or relapse.

Innovation and differentiation
- Not STR chimerism: thousands-fold higher information content via dense nuclear SNPs plus full mtDNA; directly outputs clonal diversity, not just mixture fraction.
- Not TCR/BCR repertoire: captures all hematopoietic lineages, including myeloid, erythroid, and megakaryocytic compartments; does not depend on antigen receptor loci.
- Not retroviral integration site analysis: requires no genetic modification; leverages endogenous mtDNA heteroplasmy as universal, lineage-transmissible barcodes.
- Single assay framework: one library prep yields both engraftment and clonal architecture across lineages and time.

Assay design
- Input and sampling
  - 8–12 mL peripheral blood (EDTA) per timepoint.
  - Fractions: CD15+ myeloid/granulocyte-enriched, CD3+ T/NK, CD19+ B, CD71+ reticulocytes (erythroid), CD41/CD61+ platelets (megakaryocytic), plus unfractionated leukocytes.
  - Baselines: donor and recipient pre-transplant buffy coat for nuclear and mtDNA references.
  - Longitudinal schedule: days +30, +60, +90, +180, +365 (±7 days), with optional early +14 in cord or haplo settings.

- Wet lab workflow (single library)
  - DNA extraction tailored to fraction (low-input protocol for platelets/reticulocytes).
  - UMI ligation (both ends) and duplex-aware amplification.
  - Target capture:
    - Mitochondrial genome: 46–64 tiled amplicons (150–220 bp), complete coverage including D-loop; primers avoid common NUMTs.
    - Nuclear SNP panel: 400–600 biallelic markers (MAF 0.3–0.5 across ancestries), including sex-chromosome sites; design supports EM-based donor/recipient genotype inference if pre-transplant samples are unavailable.
  - Sequencing: 2×150 bp on benchtop platform (e.g., MiSeq/NextSeq). Depth targets (per fraction): mtDNA ≥10,000× duplex-consensus; nuclear SNPs ≥500× duplex-consensus.
  - Turnaround: 48–72 hours sample-to-answer.

Computational pipeline
- Quality and error suppression
  - UMI collapsing and duplex consensus to suppress polymerase/oxidative artifacts; mtDNA low-VAF SNV and small deletion calling down to 0.1% VAF (validated LoD).
- Engraftment quantification
  - Bayesian mixture model on nuclear SNP panel using donor/recipient priors; outputs % donor chimerism and 95% CI per fraction and whole blood.
  - For enucleate lineages, mtDNA haplotype assignment against donor/recipient baselines to compute % donor (with cross-check from trace leukocyte carryover).
- Clonal barcoding and diversity
  - mtDNA clonotypes defined as co-occurring heteroplasmy haplotypes (SNVs + small deletions) after duplex correction.
  - Dirichlet process clustering across time and fractions to stabilize low-frequency clones.
  - Diversity metrics: Shannon entropy, Gini–Simpson index, Pielou evenness; clonal dominance index (top-1 and top-5 frequencies).
  - Cross-lineage clone-sharing matrix to infer multipotent vs lineage-biased clones; temporal transition analysis (hidden Markov model) for clonal emergence/extinction.

Validation plan
- Analytical validation (n=40 contrived and clinical mixes)
  - Linearity and LoD for chimerism: 0.5% across 0–100% using genotyped donor/recipient DNA.
  - Clonotype recall/precision: spike-in of cell lines with known mtDNA heteroplasmies; serial dilutions to 0.1% VAF.
  - Reproducibility: intra- and inter-run CV <10% for key metrics.
- Clinical pilot (n=60 HSCT recipients; mixed donor types)
  - Primary endpoints: agreement with STR chimerism (bias, Bland–Altman), proportion of timepoints with coherent multilineage donor assignment including platelets and reticulocytes.
  - Secondary endpoints: time to detect impending graft failure/relapse vs standard-of-care; association of early diversity indices (day +60/+90) with 1-year outcomes (event-free survival, GVHD incidence, infections).

Lineage coverage strategy
- Myeloid: CD15+ granulocyte fraction (nuclear + mtDNA).
- Lymphoid: CD3+ and CD19+ fractions (nuclear + mtDNA).
- Erythroid: CD71+ reticulocyte enrichment (mtDNA only; lineage assignment and clonal overlap to donor leukocyte clonotypes).
- Megakaryocytic: platelet-rich plasma (mtDNA only; donor assignment via mtDNA haplotype and clonotype overlap).
- Whole-blood back-up enables rapid initial engraftment calls when fractionation is not feasible.

Longitudinal tracking (1 year)
- Fixed schedule enables trajectory modeling of donor chimerism and diversity.
- Output includes alerts for:
  - Engraftment failure risk: donor % decrease >10% absolute with concordant diversity collapse.
  - Clonal skewing: rise of any single clonotype >30% within a lineage or across lineages.
  - Lineage discordance: delayed donor takeover in erythroid/megakaryocytic vs myeloid/lymphoid.

Clinical translation and feasibility
- Sample accessibility: standard peripheral blood; magnetic enrichment uses off-the-shelf clinical-grade reagents.
- Cost target: $300–500 per timepoint all-in (reduced further if whole-blood only).
- Turnaround: 2–3 days; fits inpatient and outpatient monitoring windows.
- Regulatory path: CLIA/CAP lab-developed test; no cell engineering; minimal ethical/regulatory burden; data are standard human genetic variants without therapeutic manipulation.

Risk mitigation
- Donor–recipient mtDNA haplotype similarity: rely on nuclear SNP-based chimerism for engraftment; use cross-lineage clonotype continuity to attribute enucleate fractions.
- Low heteroplasmy burden in young donors: increase mtDNA depth and leverage multi-site haplotype combinations; aggregate evidence across timepoints.
- Low reticulocyte counts: relax erythroid sampling at later timepoints; use early windows (+30–+90) where reticulocytes are most abundant; supplement with erythroid-enriched buffy coat when anemia/reticulocytosis present.
- Platelet leukocyte carryover: stringent leukoreduction and mtDNA copy-number normalization to minimize confounding.

Milestones and success criteria
- Month 0–6: finalize panel; achieve analytical LoD (chimerism 0.5%, clonotypes 0.1% VAF); reproducibility met.
- Month 6–18: enroll pilot; ≥95% lineage assignability for myeloid/lymphoid; ≥85% assignability for erythroid/megakaryocytic at ≥3 timepoints; agreement with STR within ±3% absolute in nucleated fractions.
- Month 18–24: demonstrate that MiNoR-seq detects ≥50% of engraftment failures or relapses ≥2 weeks earlier than standard monitoring, or that early diversity indices independently predict 1-year outcomes.

Expected outcomes and impact
- A single, clinically amenable assay that confirms engraftment and quantifies polyclonal reconstitution across all hematopoietic lineages, including enucleate compartments.
- Routine longitudinal surveillance that links donor fraction dynamics with clonal ecology, enabling earlier, lineage-aware clinical interventions.
- A platform extensible to gene-edited grafts and to post-therapy clonal safety monitoring without reliance on exogenous vector signatures.

text:
Title: SHaRP-Seq (Safe-Harbor RNA+DNA Barcode Profiling) for Unified Engraftment Confirmation and Polyclonal Hematopoietic Reconstitution Tracking after HSCT

Central hypothesis (question-as-hypothesis):
Can a single, minimal, safe-harbor genetic sentinel—comprising a clone-unique DNA barcode that is also transcribed as a short, noncoding polyadenylated RNA—enable quantitative, lineage-comprehensive, longitudinal measurement of donor engraftment and clonal diversity from routine blood samples up to 1 year post-transplant?

Atomic strategy (single perturbation):
Introduce into donor HSCs one site-specific, single-copy “barcode nano-transcript” cassette at a genomic safe harbor. The cassette’s barcode is readable:
- as DNA from any nucleated progeny (myeloid and lymphoid), and
- as a stabilized RNA carried into platelets and reticulocytes from megakaryocytes and erythroblasts, respectively.
One locus, two molecular readouts, all hematopoietic compartments, one assay.

Specific aims:
1) Build and qualify SHaRP, a CRISPR+AAV6-delivered, single-copy, clone-unique barcode nano-transcript at AAVS1 (or equivalent safe harbor) in human CD34+ HSPCs with clinical workflow compatibility.
2) Establish a single-tube, targeted sequencing assay that simultaneously quantifies:
   - engraftment (donor fraction) and
   - clonal diversity per lineage (myeloid, lymphoid, erythroid, megakaryocytic)
   using unified library prep across DNA (nucleated cells) and RNA (platelets/reticulocytes).
3) Longitudinally map clonal dynamics and inter-lineage fate coupling for 12 months, deriving actionable indices (effective engrafting clone number, evenness, dominance alerts).

Platform design (SHaRP genetic sentinel):
- Insertion site: AAVS1 (default), with validated off-target screening; single-copy HDR favored.
- Payload (≈600–900 bp):
  - Ubiquitous, minimal Pol II promoter driving a short, intron-containing, noncoding transcript.
  - 20–24 bp high-entropy clone barcode (CB) flanked by constant primer handles.
  - PolyA signal; no ORFs, no selection markers.
  - Cohort tag (CT): a fixed 12–16 bp sequence shared by all edited cells to quantify labeling fraction.
- Rationale:
  - DNA modality: CB amplified from genomic DNA in nucleated lineages.
  - RNA modality: the same CB present in a stable, polyadenylated transcript that is loaded into cytoplasm of megakaryocytes and erythroblasts; carried into platelets and retained in circulating reticulocytes, enabling readout from anucleate compartments.

Differentiation from existing methods:
- Not STR chimerism: uses engineered, single-locus barcodes instead of germline polymorphisms.
- Not TCR/BCR repertoire: lineage-agnostic clonal tags, independent of antigen receptor rearrangements.
- Not retroviral integration site analysis: no junction mapping; site-specific, standardized safe-harbor insertion with uniform amplicon interrogation.
- Novelty: dual-modality (DNA+RNA) readout from the same engineered locus specifically designed to capture anucleate outputs, enabling a single assay to cover all hematopoietic lineages.

Clinical workflow and assay:
- Ex vivo HSC engineering:
  - Donor or autologous CD34+ cells; CRISPR-Cas9 RNP electroporation + AAV6 donor template.
  - Release criteria: viability, CD34+ retention, VCN≈1 (ddPCR), on-target integration (amplicon NGS), off-target panel screen, absence of ORFs.
- Infusate fingerprint:
  - Deep-sequence CB distribution and CT abundance in an aliquot pre-infusion to establish clonal complexity and labeling fraction.
- Patient sampling (10–15 mL peripheral blood):
  - Timepoints: weeks 2, 4, 8, 12, 24, 36, 52.
  - Rapid fractionation (closed, bench-top, 90 minutes):
    - Granulocytes/monocytes (myeloid DNA).
    - T, B, NK (lymphoid DNA).
    - Platelets (RNA) and reticulocytes (CD71+ enrichment; RNA).
    - Optional plasma EV RNA for redundancy.
- Single-tube library prep per fraction:
  - UMI-tagged, anchored multiplex PCR (for DNA) and RT-UMI-PCR (for RNA) using the same universal primer pair flanking CB/CT.
  - Parallel 40–60 SNP mini-panel on genomic DNA to cross-check global donor chimerism in nucleated cells.
- Sequencing and TAT:
  - 1×150 or 2×150, 2–5 M reads/sample; 48–72 h turnaround in a CLIA-capable lab.

Quantification and analytics:
- Error correction: UMI collapsing; Hamming-distance clustering to denoise CBs.
- Engraftment:
  - Primary: presence and abundance of CT reads across nucleated fractions.
  - Cross-check: donor chimerism from SNP panel.
- Clonal diversity per lineage:
  - Richness (number of unique CBs), Shannon/Pielou evenness, Gini-Simpson, clone size distributions.
  - Cross-lineage fate coupling: Jaccard/overlap matrices and bipartite networks (clone ↔ lineage).
- Longitudinal dynamics (0–52 weeks):
  - Effective engrafting clone number (Ne) via capture–recapture using infusate CB priors and serial observations.
  - Dominance alerts: outlier growth trajectories (e.g., >30% single-clone share or accelerated growth slope) with configurable clinical triggers.
  - Resilience metrics: turnover rates in platelets/reticulocytes vs persistence in lymphoid compartments.

Validation plan (Phase I/feasibility):
- In vitro qualification:
  - PB-derived CD34+ editing efficiency (goal ≥50% labeled), single-copy confirmation, minimal transcript expression quantitation, no detectable peptide translation.
- Preclinical humanized model spiking:
  - Mixed labeled/unlabeled HSCs to calibrate capture–recapture estimators.
- Clinical pilot (autologous HSCT/gene therapy context first):
  - N=10–15 patients, serial sampling per schedule.
  - Endpoints: assay success rate (>95%), coefficient of variation on clone frequency estimates (<15% at ≥0.5% clone fraction), correlation of CT-based engraftment with clinical chimerism (r≥0.9), detection of all four compartments in ≥85% timepoints.

Safety and regulatory considerations:
- Minimal, noncoding insertion at a validated safe harbor; no therapeutic gene, no antibiotic markers.
- Single-copy HDR preferred; VCN and insertion site verified per lot.
- Off-target risk managed by high-fidelity Cas9, truncated gRNAs, targeted off-target panel pre-release.
- Run under gene-marking/observational IND framework, beginning in autologous settings; expand to allogeneic with donor consent and risk assessment.

Anticipated performance:
- Lineage coverage:
  - Myeloid/lymphoid: DNA detection limit ~0.05–0.1% clone fraction with 2–5 M reads.
  - Megakaryocytic/erythroid: RNA detection in platelets/reticulocytes with nested RT-UMI-PCR; expected sensitivity ~0.2–0.5% per draw (improves with replicate RTs).
- Cost per timepoint (all fractions): approximately $300–$500 reagents + $200–$300 sequencing at scale; 2–3 person-hours hands-on in a streamlined lab.
- Turnaround: 2–3 days from phlebotomy to report.

Risk assessment and mitigations:
- Suboptimal labeling fraction: CT enables back-estimation of total donor output; target ≥50% labeled; if lower, increase cell dose/optimize HDR with ssODN enhancer or transient NHEJ inhibitor.
- Low RNA yield in anucleate fractions: enrich reticulocytes (CD71+), use bead-based platelet capture; employ exonuclease-mediated rRNA depletion and nested RT-UMI-PCR; add optional EV RNA as redundancy.
- Barcode collision or synthesis bias: 20–24 bp CB with balanced base composition; pre-infusion sequencing to cull near-duplicates; library complexity >10× expected engrafting clone number.
- Clonal skew from insertional effects: safe-harbor targeting, single-copy, noncoding cassette; monitor growth trajectories with predefined stopping rules.

Milestones and timeline (12–18 months):
- Months 0–3: Cassette finalization, gRNA/AAV6 optimization, QC pipeline.
- Months 4–6: In vitro qualification; analytical LoD and precision established.
- Months 7–12: Pilot clinical enrollment; first 24-week interim readout; refine bioinformatics and clinical reporting.
- Months 13–18: Full 52-week longitudinal analysis; finalize dominance alert thresholds; prepare validation study.

Expected impact:
- A single standardized assay that confirms donor engraftment and quantifies polyclonal reconstitution across all hematopoietic lineages, including anucleate compartments, with routine blood sampling.
- Actionable, early detection of clonal dominance or lineage-restricted failures, enabling timely clinical intervention.
- A clinically tractable gene-marking platform that avoids the complexity of integration-site mapping and the lineage limitations of STR/TCR/BCR-based approaches.

Title
HaploSV-Clone: A single-assay, clinically translatable long-read haplotype barcoding platform using donor–recipient structural variants and mitochondrial variation to quantify engraftment and polyclonal hematopoietic reconstitution after HSCT

Overall Research Question and Hypothesis
Question-hypothesis: Can endogenous germline structural variant (SV) haplotypes distinguishing donor and recipient, coupled with high-resolution single-molecule readouts that also capture mitochondrial variants and epigenetic haplotypes, serve as a single integrated assay to (i) quantify lineage-specific engraftment and (ii) resolve clonal diversity and dynamics across all hematopoietic compartments for one year post-HSCT?

Atomic Strategy
Exploit natural, person-specific germline SV haplotypes as stable barcodes for donor vs recipient assignment, and simultaneously leverage endogenous, rapidly evolving mitochondrial variants and long-read methylation haplotypes as subclonal barcodes. Read all barcodes on the same long-read targeted sequencing libraries generated from sorted hematopoietic populations and scheduled marrow aspirates, enabling one assay to deliver quantitative chimerism and multi-lineage clonal architecture longitudinally.

Specific Aims
1) Engineer a personalized SV-barcode panel per donor–recipient pair and a unified long-read capture workflow that co-enriches nuclear SV loci and mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA), producing single-molecule haplotyped reads with base modification calls.
2) Demonstrate quantitative engraftment measurement across myeloid, lymphoid, erythroid, and megakaryocytic compartments using lineage-purified subsets and standard-of-care timepoints up to 365 days.
3) Reconstruct clonal structure and dynamics within donor-derived hematopoiesis by integrating mtDNA clonotypes and long-read methylation haplotypes, and track longitudinal shifts indicative of graft dominance, mixed chimerism, or oligoclonal expansions.

Novelty and Differentiation
- Not STR chimerism: uses long-read, haplotype-resolved germline SVs (50 bp–100 kb+) spanning breakpoints; immune to PCR stutter; allele-specific and molecule-phased.
- Not TCR/BCR repertoire: captures all hematopoietic lineages, not just lymphoid; clonal inference derives from endogenous mtDNA and methylation haplotypes rather than immune receptor recombination.
- Not retroviral integration mapping: requires no artificial marking; exploits natural genomic and epigenomic variation; immediately compatible with standard transplants.

Study Design

Cohort and Sampling
- n=60 HSCT recipients (matched sibling and matched unrelated donors), adult and pediatric arms.
- Timepoints: baseline (pre-HSCT genotyping), and post-HSCT days +14, +28, +60, +100, +180, +365.
- Specimens per timepoint:
  - Peripheral blood: whole blood for plasma cfDNA; sorted leukocyte fractions (CD15+ neutrophils, CD14+ monocytes, CD19+ B cells, CD3+ T cells, CD56+ NK cells); platelets.
  - Bone marrow aspirates (standard clinical timepoints: +30, +100, +180, +365): sorted erythroid precursors (CD71+GPA+), megakaryocytes (CD41a+/CD61+), and CD34+ progenitors when available.
- Parallel clinical comparators (for validation only): routine STR/dPCR chimerism; complete blood counts; clinical outcomes (engraftment, graft failure, relapse).

Assay Overview (Single Platform)
- Pretransplant personalization:
  - Low-pass long-read WGS (or short-read WGS with SV caller) on donor and recipient to identify 300–600 informative, uniquely mappable, high-VAF germline SVs where donor and recipient differ (insertions, deletions, inversions, mobile element insertions).
  - Design CRISPR/Cas9 excision or adaptive nanopore enrichment to target 30–120 kb windows flanking each breakpoint (on both haplotypes), balancing panel size and coverage (total on-target 20–40 Mb).
- Library and sequencing:
  - Single DNA extraction per specimen; unified long-read library prep that preserves base modifications.
  - Enrichment of SV windows plus unbiased co-capture of mtDNA (naturally enriched in long-read preps).
  - Oxford Nanopore (or PacBio HiFi) sequencing per timepoint; pooled lineages multiplexed with unique indexes.
- Readouts from the same dataset:
  - Donor–recipient assignment: molecule-spanning SV breakpoints and phased local SNP/indel haplotypes provide allele-specific counts per lineage (quantitative chimerism).
  - Clonal barcoding: mtDNA heteroplasmy variants (including private subclonal mutations) profiled per lineage; long-read methylation haplotypes across targeted windows (and mtDNA 5mC/5hmC when available) provide orthogonal subclonal fingerprints.
  - Optional analysis of on-target nuclear sSNVs accrued over time (when present) further refines clonotypes.

Computational Framework (HaploSV-Clone Analytics)
- Haplotype-aware alignment and SV-aware read assignment to donor vs recipient per molecule; Bayesian mixture modeling yields donor fraction and credible intervals per lineage and timepoint.
- mtDNA variant caller estimating heteroplasmy per lineage; Dirichlet-process clustering of mtDNA haplotypes across cell types/timepoints to define clonotypes; phylogenetic reconstruction infers clonal relationships and seeding across compartments.
- Long-read methylome extraction at CpG blocks within targeted windows; methylation haplotypes co-clustered with mtDNA clonotypes to resolve clones sharing nuclear epigenetic signatures.
- Diversity metrics: Shannon and Simpson diversity, clonal evenness, and Gini index per lineage; temporal dynamics via state-space models; detection thresholds for emergent dominant clones or graft attrition.
- Cross-compartment flux modeling: estimate contributions of identified donor clonotypes to myeloid, lymphoid, erythroid, and megakaryocytic outputs over time.

Endpoints and Analyses
Primary
- Accuracy and precision of lineage-specific donor chimerism versus clinical STR/dPCR across all timepoints (noninferiority margin ±3% absolute).
- Breadth of polyclonal resolution: number of stable donor-derived clonotypes detected per patient and lineage at day +100 and +365; within-patient Shannon diversity ≥ that observed in immune-repertoire methods for lymphoid and demonstrably measured for myeloid/erythroid/megakaryocytic.
Secondary
- Lead time to detect mixed chimerism or graft failure compared with clinical standard.
- Cross-lineage clonotype sharing and stability (evidence of multipotent HSC-derived clones contributing to multiple compartments).
- Association of clonotype dynamics with cytopenias, relapse, or graft-versus-host disease.

Clinical Translation Considerations
- Sample accessibility: uses routine peripheral blood; marrow aspirates at timepoints already standard in many HSCT protocols; no ex vivo manipulation beyond immunomagnetic sorting.
- Turnaround time: 48–72 hours from sample receipt to report (targeted enrichment + rapid long-read run + streamlined analytics).
- Cost: projected <$600 per comprehensive timepoint (all fractions pooled), leveraging barcoded multiplexing and targeted capture.
- Regulatory pathway: germline-SV chimerism and mtDNA heteroplasmy quantification as LDT under CLIA/CAP; no genetic modification, no viral marking; uses residual clinical specimens.
- Scalability: automated enrichment and cloud-based analytics; panel reusability across patients with rapid, per-pair informatics selection of informative SVs.

Coverage of All Hematopoietic Compartments
- Myeloid and lymphoid: purified leukocyte subsets from blood at all timepoints (nuclear SVs + mtDNA).
- Megakaryocytic: platelets (mtDNA clonotypes) across all timepoints; marrow megakaryocytes (nuclear SVs + mtDNA) at scheduled aspirates.
- Erythroid: marrow erythroid precursors (nuclear SVs + mtDNA) at scheduled aspirates; plasma cfDNA deconvolution using methylation signatures to estimate erythroid contribution between aspirates, anchored to donor/recipient SV haplotypes.

Power and Feasibility
- Informative SV yield: >200 loci per pair expected in >95% of unrelated or sibling pairs; simulation indicates <0.5% uncertainty in donor fraction at 200× on-target per lineage.
- Clonal detection: mtDNA clonotypes reliably detected at ≥1–2% frequency with 2,000× mtDNA coverage per fraction; combined with methylation haplotypes increases resolution of closely related clones.

Risk Assessment and Mitigations
- Low SV informativeness (e.g., closely related donor–recipient): augment with common indel/SNP haplotypes within long reads to maintain donor assignment; increase panel size via adaptive sampling.
- Limited erythroid nuclear access outside marrow timepoints: use cfDNA methylation deconvolution anchored to SV haplotypes as interim estimator.
- Low-abundance clones below detection: increase mtDNA depth and apply error-corrected consensus on long reads; aggregate across adjacent timepoints for sensitivity.

Milestones and Timeline
- Months 0–6: Assay engineering; informatics pipeline; analytical validation with contrived mixes and archived HSCT samples.
- Months 7–24: Prospective accrual; longitudinal sampling; interim analyses at months 12 and 18.
- Month 24: Final analysis; clinical utility modeling; readiness for CLIA validation.

Success Criteria
- Demonstrate single-assay, lineage-resolved donor chimerism with noninferior accuracy to STR/dPCR and added clonal-resolution value.
- Resolve ≥5 persistent donor-derived clonotypes per patient contributing to at least two distinct lineages by day +365.
- Detect emerging mixed chimerism or oligoclonal dominance ≥14 days earlier than standard testing in ≥30% of such events.

Outcome and Impact
HaploSV-Clone converts natural genomic and epigenomic variation into an endogenous, universal barcode system that simultaneously validates engraftment and quantifies clonal hematopoietic reconstitution across all lineages. It removes reliance on engineered marks, extends beyond lymphoid-restricted repertoire assays, and is immediately positioned for clinical translation with compelling turnaround, cost, and breadth.

text:
Title
MiNoBar-HSCT: A personalized mito+nuclear natural-barcode sequencing assay for simultaneous engraftment confirmation and multilineage clonal diversity tracking after HSCT

Unifying research question (hypothesis-as-question)
Can a single, clinically deployable sequencing assay that tracks pre-existing, naturally occurring somatic variants in nuclear DNA together with mitochondrial heteroplasmies provide quantitative, lineage-resolved, and longitudinal measurements of both donor engraftment and polyclonal hematopoietic reconstitution after HSCT?

Atomic strategy
Exploit each individual’s private, naturally acquired somatic “passenger” variants as immutable clonal barcodes. Pre-transplant, discover donor- and recipient-specific nuclear microhaplotypes and mitochondrial heteroplasmy patterns; post-transplant, repeatedly measure their frequencies in sorted blood lineages and acellular compartments using one error-corrected targeted assay. Donor-versus-recipient chimerism is read from owner-specific nuclear variants; clonal diversity is inferred from co-occurring nuclear microhaplotypes and mtDNA haplotype constellations shared across lineages and time.

Specific aims
1) Discover patient-specific natural barcodes: Identify hundreds to thousands of donor- and recipient-private nuclear microhaplotypes and mitochondrial heteroplasmies from a single pre-transplant blood draw.
2) Build a single, CLIA-amenable assay: Develop a duplex UMI–based capture panel that jointly targets personalized nuclear microhaplotypes and the full mitochondrial genome.
3) Achieve multilineage resolution: Apply the same assay to myeloid (neutrophils, monocytes), lymphoid (T, B, NK), megakaryocytic (platelets), and erythroid compartments (reticulocyte cDNA and standard-of-care marrow erythroid precursors).
4) Longitudinally quantify engraftment and clonal ecology: Model donor chimerism, clone number, evenness, and cross-lineage contribution at days +14, +30, +60, +100, +180, and +365.

Differentiation from existing methods
- Not STR chimerism: Uses private somatic nuclear microhaplotypes with molecule-level phasing and error-corrected counts; higher locus count and lower limit of detection.
- Not TCR/BCR repertoire: Independent of immune receptor rearrangements; covers all hematopoietic lineages including non-lymphoid.
- Not retroviral integration site analysis: No genetic modification or vector integration; relies solely on naturally occurring somatic variants.

Study design and methods
Cohort and sampling
- Participants: Allogeneic HSCT recipients and their donors.
- Timepoints: Pre-transplant baseline (donor and recipient), then post-transplant days +14, +30, +60, +100, +180, +365.
- Specimens per post-transplant timepoint (20 mL peripheral blood total):
  - Lineage-enriched fractions (magnetic bead isolation): neutrophils (CD66b+/CD15+), monocytes (CD14+), T cells (CD3+), B cells (CD19+), NK cells (CD56+).
  - Platelets (for megakaryocytic mtDNA).
  - Reticulocyte-enriched fraction (CD71+; RNA for cDNA).
  - Plasma cell-free DNA (cfDNA) to capture marrow-derived nucleated precursors and apoptotic contributions.
  - Standard-of-care marrow aspirate at clinically routine checkpoints (e.g., ~day +30 and +100) to profile erythroid precursors without adding procedures.

Pre-transplant barcode discovery
- Input: Donor apheresis or peripheral blood; recipient peripheral blood.
- Sequencing:
  - Nuclear: Targeted discovery over a 1.5–2.0 Mb panel of late-replicating, non-coding, selection-neutral regions with high passenger mutation density; duplex UMI sequencing at 1,000–2,000× unique coverage to call low-VAF private somatic SNVs/indels. Identify closely spaced variant clusters (≤150 bp) to construct microhaplotypes enabling molecule-level phasing.
  - Mitochondrial: Full mtDNA duplex sequencing at ≥10,000× unique coverage to define heteroplasmic variant constellations (haplotype “constellations” that serve as high-copy clonal anchors).
- Panel personalization: Select 1,200–2,000 nuclear loci per individual maximizing (i) pre-transplant VAF, (ii) neutrality, (iii) microhaplotype richness, plus full mtDNA. Merge donor and recipient loci into one capture design.

Clinical assay (single workflow for all post-transplant samples)
- Library prep: Duplex UMI hybrid-capture with unique dual indexes; identical probe set used for genomic DNA, cfDNA, and reticulocyte cDNA (amplicon-agnostic capture across targeted loci).
- Sequencing: 30–50 million read pairs per sample fraction; per-locus unique depth ~20,000× nuclear, ~50,000× mtDNA.
- Analytics:
  - Error correction: Duplex consensus generation to suppress artifacts to <10^-6.
  - Engraftment (primary readout): Maximum-likelihood chimerism using donor- vs recipient-private nuclear barcodes across fractions; report global and lineage-specific donor fraction with 95% CIs; LoD ≤0.01%.
  - Clonal inference: Joint Bayesian deconvolution harnessing (a) co-observed nuclear microhaplotypes on single molecules, (b) mtDNA constellation co-occurrence within the same fraction, and (c) longitudinal persistence. Nonparametric Dirichlet process mixture models estimate clone count and frequencies per lineage and timepoint.
  - Cross-lineage mapping: Match clones across fractions/time via shared mtDNA constellations and subset of nuclear haplotypes to quantify each clone’s multilineage contributions.
  - Diversity metrics: Shannon index, Simpson index, Hill numbers, Gini coefficient; lineage evenness and turnover (Jaccard/Bray-Curtis) across time.

Readouts and reporting (single integrated report)
- Engraftment confirmation: Overall and lineage-specific donor chimerism; comparison to prior timepoints; alert thresholds for declining donor fractions or recipient resurgence.
- Polyclonality: Clone number, dominance indices, and effective clone size per lineage; flags for oligoclonal drift or collapse.
- Cross-lineage architecture: Heatmap of clone contributions across myeloid, lymphoid, megakaryocytic, and erythroid compartments.
- Longitudinal dynamics: Trajectories of top clones and diversity indices through 1 year.

Coverage of all hematopoietic lineages
- Myeloid: Neutrophils, monocytes (gDNA).
- Lymphoid: T, B, NK cells (gDNA).
- Megakaryocytic: Platelets (mtDNA-rich; robust clonal anchors).
- Erythroid: Reticulocyte cDNA to read nuclear barcodes on expressed transcripts; calibration with standard-of-care marrow erythroid precursors (gDNA) at ~day +30/+100; supplemental erythroid-derived cfDNA signals in plasma.

Clinical translation and feasibility
- Sample accessibility: Peripheral blood at all timepoints; marrow only at routine clinical checkpoints (no added procedures).
- Turnaround time: 48–72 hours from sample receipt (batchable); discovery/panel build completed once pre-transplant (5–7 days).
- Cost targets: Discovery/panel build $800–$1,200 per donor–recipient pair; per timepoint $300–$500 (all fractions multiplexed).
- Regulatory pathway: LDT under CLIA/CAP; no genetic modification; analogous to personalized ctDNA MRD assays (patient-specific panels).
- Throughput: 24–48 patients/week on a mid-throughput sequencer; automated bead-based lineage enrichment.

Validation plan
- Benchmarks: Concordance and sensitivity vs STR chimerism for donor fraction; reproducibility across replicates/fractions; LoD studies using defined donor–recipient DNA mixes.
- Clinical correlations: Early oligoclonality or falling diversity with graft failure; recipient-clone resurgence with relapse/MRD; lineage-restricted clonal skewing with GVHD or infections.
- Success criteria: (i) Engraftment LoD ≤0.01% with CV <10%; (ii) ≥10 resolvable donor-derived clones by day +100 in at least three lineages; (iii) actionable alerts ≥30 days before clinical recognition of graft failure/relapse in >50% of events.

Risk analysis and mitigations
- Low private-variant yield in some individuals: Increase discovery panel size; prioritize microhaplotype-dense regions; rely more on mtDNA constellations where abundant.
- CHIP confounding: Annotate driver mutations; exclude from chimerism computation but include in diversity readouts with labels.
- Erythroid representation variability: Dual-source design (reticulocyte cDNA + routine marrow erythroid precursors) ensures coverage; cross-validate with plasma cfDNA contribution dynamics.
- Sorting/throughput constraints: Move to positive-selection magnetic kits and pooled library prep with demultiplexing; if needed, run an unsorted-whole-blood mode that still reports global engraftment and aggregate diversity.

Milestones
- Months 0–3: Panel discovery optimization; analytical LoD established.
- Months 4–9: Pilot (n=20 pairs); freeze assay and pipeline; CLIA validation.
- Months 10–18: Prospective clinical study (n=80) with 1-year follow-up; health-economic analysis; finalize implementation package.

Expected impact
MiNoBar-HSCT provides, within a single assay framework, high-sensitivity engraftment confirmation and comprehensive, lineage-resolved clonal ecology over the first post-transplant year, without genetic modification. By unifying nuclear microhaplotypes and mitochondrial constellations as natural barcodes, it extends beyond STRs, repertoire sequencing, and integration-site analyses to deliver clinically actionable, system-wide visibility into human hematopoietic reconstitution.

text:
Title
EndoTrack-HSCT: A single-assay, clinically translatable platform that uses donor-intrinsic nuclear and mitochondrial somatic variants as stable fingerprints to quantify engraftment and polyclonal reconstitution across all hematopoietic lineages for 1 year post-transplant

Atomic strategy
Exploit naturally occurring somatic mosaicism in donor hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs)—private nuclear single-nucleotide variants (nSNVs) and co-occurring mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) variants—as immutable, individual “fingerprints.” Pre-transplant single-cell mapping links each clone’s nSNVs to its mtDNA haplotype. After transplant, a personalized, targeted, error-corrected sequencing panel simultaneously (i) measures donor–recipient chimerism (engraftment) via informative germline SNPs and (ii) quantifies clonal diversity within the donor-derived fraction using nSNVs in nucleated lineages and linked mtDNA tags in anucleate lineages.

Hypothesis–goal
If donor HSPCs carry unique, stable combinations of endogenous nSNVs and mtDNA variants that are faithfully inherited by all progeny, then a unified, patient-specific targeted sequencing assay can (a) confirm and quantify donor engraftment in each lineage and (b) resolve the number, balance, stability, and lineage contributions of donor clones over time—discriminating robust polyclonal reconstitution from oligoclonal takeover and revealing failure modes attributable to transplant processes versus limitations of the donor HSC pool.

Specific aims
1) Build the donor clonal fingerprint map
- Perform pre-transplant single-cell profiling of donor CD34+ cells to jointly capture sparse nuclear variants and high-coverage mtDNA per cell.
- Infer clonal structure; select a minimal set of private, putatively neutral nSNVs per clone and their linked mtDNA variants.
- Add a compact germline SNP set that distinguishes donor from recipient for high-precision chimerism.

2) Construct a unified, personalized assay for all lineages
- Develop a multiplex, duplex-UMI error-corrected panel comprising:
  a) Donor–recipient-informative germline SNPs (engraftment readout).
  b) Clone-defining nSNVs (for nucleated cells).
  c) Clone-linked mtDNA variants (for platelets and reticulocytes).
- Optimize for low input, short turnaround, and compatibility with routine peripheral blood sampling and standard clinical cell enrichments.

3) Longitudinally track clonal dynamics across hematopoiesis
- At prespecified timepoints through 1 year post-HSCT (e.g., days ~+30, +60, +90, +180, +365), profile peripheral blood fractions enriched for:
  Myeloid (neutrophils, monocytes), lymphoid (T, B, NK), megakaryocytic (platelets), and erythroid (reticulocytes).
- Compute per-lineage donor chimerism and, within the donor fraction, clone frequencies, effective clone number, diversity indices, Gini coefficients, and cross-lineage clone-sharing metrics.

Study design and methods (high level)
- Donor mapping before conditioning: Use single-cell, low-coverage nuclear plus high-coverage mtDNA sequencing to associate each clone’s nSNVs with a unique mtDNA signature. Select 50–200 targets spanning ≥20–50 donor clones, prioritizing intergenic or synonymous sites to avoid reporting incidental pathogenic findings.
- Assay build: Synthesize a patient-specific amplicon/capture panel with duplex unique molecular identifiers for error suppression and rare-variant detection; include a standardized set of 200–400 common germline SNPs with high minor-allele frequency for chimerism quantification.
- Sampling scheme: 5–10 mL peripheral blood per timepoint. Use clinically routine immunomagnetic enrichments or low-parameter flow sorting to obtain major nucleated subsets; enrich reticulocytes; collect platelets. No bone marrow is required for longitudinal monitoring.
- Sequencing and analytics: Short-read, high-depth targeted sequencing with molecular consensus calling. Bioinformatic pipeline outputs:
  a) Engraftment per lineage from donor–recipient SNPs.
  b) Donor clonal composition per lineage from nSNVs (nucleated) and from linked mtDNA (platelets, reticulocytes).
  c) Temporal trajectories of each clone’s contribution to each lineage, with alerts for oligoclonal dominance, lineage restriction, or clone extinction/emergence.

Key outcomes and interpretation
- Engraftment success: High and concordant donor chimerism across lineages early post-HSCT; detection of mixed chimerism confined to specific compartments when present.
- Polyclonal diversity: Stable or increasing effective clone number with balanced cross-lineage contributions indicates healthy reconstitution; declining diversity, high Gini, or lineage-skewed dominance flags risk for graft failure, lineage-specific insufficiency, or donor-derived clonal hematopoiesis.
- Process vs. donor limitation: Early, global oligoclonality implicates transplant bottlenecks; persistent dominance of a pre-identified donor clone suggests intrinsic donor pool constraint.

Innovation relative to existing methods
- Not STR chimerism: Goes beyond donor/recipient fraction to resolve donor-internal clonal architecture.
- Not TCR/BCR repertoire: Captures all hematopoietic branches, not lymphoid only, and measures true HSC multipotency via cross-lineage clone sharing.
- Not retroviral integration site analysis: Requires no genetic modification; leverages naturally occurring donor mosaicism and linked nuclear–mitochondrial barcodes.
- Single framework: One assay yields both engraftment confirmation and quantitative clonal diversity across all compartments, including anucleate lineages via mtDNA.

Clinical translation and feasibility
- Sample accessibility: Peripheral blood only; uses routine clinical enrichment methods.
- Turnaround and cost: Personalized panel built once per donor–recipient pair; per-timepoint processing and reporting in ~5–7 days at costs comparable to current MRD panels.
- Regulatory path: Laboratory-developed test using targeted sequencing and computational reporting; minimal risk profile (non-interventional, no cell engineering).
- Reporting: Clear, lineage-specific chimerism, clone counts, diversity indices, and trend flags intended for transplant teams.

Risk assessment and mitigations
- Low donor mutation burden (e.g., very young donors): Increase pre-transplant single-cell depth to capture additional neutral variants; rely more on mtDNA multi-variant haplotypes; track fewer but still informative clones.
- mtDNA drift and heteroplasmy: Use multi-locus mtDNA haplotypes rather than single sites; anchor to pre-mapped nuclear–mtDNA linkages from the same clones.
- Erythroid coverage: Use reticulocyte-enriched fractions for mtDNA-based clonotyping; when reticulocytes are scarce, schedule erythroid sampling at recovery peaks or incorporate a limited bone marrow timepoint only if clinically indicated.
- Incidental findings: Restrict target selection to neutral regions; exclude known pathogenic loci during panel design.

Power, endpoints, and success criteria
- Analytical sensitivity: Detect clone-defining alleles at ≤0.1% variant allele frequency with duplex error correction; verify with synthetic mixes.
- Biological resolution: Resolve ≥20 donor clones across nucleated compartments in >80% of adult donors; concordant mtDNA-based assignment in platelets/reticulocytes for ≥70% of mapped clones.
- Clinical utility: Early identification of oligoclonal reconstitution or lineage-restricted engraftment predicts cytopenias or graft dysfunction; actionable reports delivered within clinically relevant windows.

Milestones and timeline
- Months −1 to 0 (pre-transplant): Donor single-cell mapping and personalized panel build.
- Post-transplant to 12 months: Serial blood collections and EndoTrack-HSCT profiling at predefined visits; interim analyses at day ~+100 and +180; final 1-year clonal reconstitution report.

Deliverables
- Validated EndoTrack-HSCT assay and computational pipeline.
- Prospective dataset linking engraftment and clonal diversity metrics to clinical outcomes.
- A pragmatic scoring framework for transplant teams that integrates engraftment confirmation and polyclonal health into a single, interpretable, longitudinal readout.

Title
DiBAR-HSCT: Division-Linked, Disappearing-Barcode Assay for Simultaneous Engraftment Quantification and Polyclonal Reconstitution Profiling After HSCT

Integrated hypothesis-goal
If donor CD34+ cells are transiently labeled ex vivo with uniquely barcoded, non-integrating DNA circuits that are mitotically inherited but do not self-replicate, then barcode copy number will decay at a lineage-specific rate proportional to cumulative divisions. Longitudinal measurement of barcode abundance and decay across myeloid, lymphoid, erythroid, and megakaryocytic compartments from peripheral blood will simultaneously (a) confirm donor engraftment and (b) quantify clonal diversity and dynamics for up to one year.

Atomic strategy (single insight)
Exploit controlled mitotic dilution of a transient, heritable genetic tag as a built-in “disappearing ink” timer to turn routine blood sampling into a quantitative lineage and clonal dynamics readout, without relying on endogenous polymorphisms, immune receptor repertoires, or integration-site mapping.

Platform concept and novelty
- What it is: A standardized, exogenous barcode cassette delivered to donor CD34+ cells that (i) is episomal/non-integrating and replication-incompetent, (ii) expresses a short, noncoding transcript carrying the same barcode sequence, and (iii) is designed for mitotic dilution with predictable binomial partitioning at cell division.
- How it’s novel:
  - Not STR chimerism: does not rely on donor/host polymorphisms; provides clone-level, not just bulk, engraftment estimates.
  - Not TCR/BCR repertoire: measures all hematopoietic lineages, not only adaptive lymphocytes; barcodes are exogenous and uniform across lineages.
  - Not retroviral integration-site analysis: does not infer clones from random genomic insertion sites; uses a standardized, non-integrating barcode whose quantitative decay encodes division history.
- Why it is clinically amenable: non-integrating DNA labeling of graft cells ex vivo under existing cell-processing workflows; readout via targeted amplicon sequencing/droplet digital PCR (ddPCR) from small-volume peripheral blood; 48–72 h turnaround; scalable and cost-contained.

Study design overview
- Population: Adults undergoing allogeneic HSCT; autologous HSCT arm optional for method generalization.
- Intervention (labeling step, ex vivo): Donor CD34+ cells are transiently labeled with a complex library of unique DNA barcodes using a non-integrating, GMP-compatible delivery modality. No genomic integration; limited-duration expression of a barcode transcript ensures detection in anucleate lineages.
- Clinical sampling: Peripheral blood at pre-specified timepoints (e.g., days 7, 14, 21, 28, then monthly to 12 months). Bone marrow aspirate optional at day ~28 for concordance testing.
- Lineage coverage per draw:
  - Myeloid: neutrophils, monocytes (gDNA barcode quantification).
  - Lymphoid: CD3+ T, CD19+ B, CD56+ NK (gDNA barcode quantification).
  - Erythroid: reticulocyte-enriched fraction and total RBC lysate (barcode RNA quantification).
  - Megakaryocytic: platelets (barcode RNA quantification).
  - Plasma: cell-free DNA/RNA as a surrogate for marrow progenitor turnover.
- Single-assay framework: Unified primer/probe set targets the barcode locus; two parallel inputs per sample (gDNA and total RNA) are prepared with identical capture chemistry and pooled for one sequencing/ddPCR run and one analysis pipeline.

Assay architecture
- Barcode design:
  - 20–24 nt random core with outer constant priming sites and error-correcting redundancy to support UMI-based molecule counting.
  - Non-integrating, nuclear-retained DNA scaffold that is mitotically partitioned but not replicated; expression unit produces a short, noncoding, polyadenylated transcript bearing the same barcode for detection in anucleate products.
- Controls and calibration:
  - Pre-infusion enumeration: quantify the per-cell barcode copy-number distribution in an aliquot of the labeled graft to calibrate absolute engraftment.
  - In-assay spike-ins: synthetic barcodes at fixed copy for run-to-run normalization.
  - Background panel: pre-transplant blood to define patient-specific false positive thresholds.

Primary endpoints
- Engraftment confirmation: Presence and expansion of donor barcodes in peripheral blood lineages above calibrated thresholds; time to 95% probability of successful donor contribution in myeloid fractions.
- Clonal diversity and stability: Longitudinal Hill numbers (q = 0, 1, 2), Gini-Simpson index, and evenness of barcode frequency distributions within and across lineages over 12 months.
- Lineage-coupled clonal kinetics: Inferred per-lineage effective division rates and contribution trajectories for each barcode-defined clone.

Modeling and analytics
- Generative model:
  - Division-linked dilution: barcode copy number per cell follows a binomial partitioning process with lineage-specific cell-cycle parameters; mature cells inherit the current barcode payload of their progenitors at commitment.
  - Expression link: barcode RNA abundance in anucleate lineages is proportional to contemporaneous DNA copy number in immediate precursors.
  - Sampling model: observed molecule counts arise from a negative binomial sampling process with technical parameters estimated from spike-ins and UMIs.
- Inference:
  - Bayesian hierarchical fitting jointly estimates (i) donor chimerism corrected for initial labeling fraction, (ii) clone-specific frequencies over time, (iii) lineage-specific effective division rates, and (iv) diversity metrics with credible intervals.
  - Cross-compartment coupling constrains shared ancestry, improving robustness when some compartments are transiently low-yield.
- Outputs (per visit and longitudinal):
  - Donor engraftment probability and adjusted fraction.
  - Clone count and diversity indices by lineage and globally.
  - Clone trajectories: emergence, expansion, contraction, or extinction.
  - Early-warning flags: oligoclonality, lineage skews, or dominance patterns.

Operational plan
- Sample requirements: ~10–15 mL whole blood per timepoint; magnetically enriched subsets using clinical-grade kits; no deep cell sorting required.
- Turnaround: 2–3 days from sample receipt to report.
- Cost discipline: Single-target library, short-read sequencing or ddPCR-compatible; multiplex up to dozens of patients per run.

Validation and benchmarking
- Analytical validation: Limit of detection for rare clones, linearity of dilution, reproducibility across runs and sites, stability of spike-ins.
- Biological validation:
  - Concordance with standard chimerism (as secondary comparator) for engraftment timing.
  - Agreement between neutrophil/monocyte compartments on early myeloid reconstitution.
  - Platelet and reticulocyte RNA signals tracking expected production dynamics.
- Stress tests: Mixed-donor simulations in vitro to verify model identifiability under varied initial barcode multiplicity and unequal transduction.

Safety and regulatory considerations
- Non-integrating, non-replicating DNA label minimizes insertional mutagenesis risk; transient expression of a noncoding reporter avoids protein overexpression.
- GMP-compatible ex vivo handling within existing HSCT cell-processing workflows; regulatory path aligns with minimal-risk, non-therapeutic cell marking under an IND.

Risk assessment and mitigations
- Uneven initial labeling of stem/progenitor subsets: calibrate with pre-infusion per-cell barcode measurements; model corrects for initial copy-number heterogeneity.
- Selective loss of labeled cells: monitor early post-infusion kinetics; sensitivity analyses exclude artifactual clonal inferences if global barcode burden declines unexpectedly.
- Low RNA yield in anucleate compartments: aggregate over multiple barcodes and apply UMI deduplication; supplement with plasma cfRNA.
- Assay contamination: dual-indexing, physical separation of pre- and post-PCR steps, barcode whitelist from infused product.

Milestones
- Phase 0: Barcode library QA, stability, and non-integration verification in human CD34+ cells ex vivo.
- Phase 1: Feasibility in 10 HSCT recipients with dense early sampling; refine kinetic priors and thresholds.
- Phase 2: Multicenter prospective study (n≥50) powered for correlation with clinical outcomes (engraftment timing, graft failure, lineage-specific recovery).
- Phase 3: Technical standardization package for clinical laboratories, including controls, software, and reporting templates.

Success criteria
- Engraftment detection equal or earlier than standard chimerism with higher lineage resolution.
- Stable, interpretable clonal diversity estimates with credible intervals ≤10% width after month 2 in major compartments.
- Demonstrated one-year longitudinal tracking with detection of clonal stability or shifts without invasive marrow sampling.

Deliverable
A clinically translatable, single-assay platform that uses disappearing, exogenous barcodes to confirm engraftment and quantify polyclonal hematopoietic reconstitution across all lineages over one year, independent of human polymorphisms, immune receptor rearrangements, or integration-site mapping.

text:
Title: mitoTRACE-HSCT: A single-assay, single-cell mitochondrial barcoding platform for simultaneous engraftment confirmation and polyclonal hematopoietic reconstitution mapping after HSCT

Central hypothesis-as-question
Can naturally occurring mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) haplotypes and somatic mtDNA mutations, read at single-cell resolution and linked to minimal immunophenotyping, function as universal, label-free barcodes that (i) confirm donor engraftment and (ii) quantify polyclonal reconstitution dynamics across myeloid, lymphoid, erythroid, and megakaryocytic compartments for up to 1 year post-transplant?

Atomic strategy
Treat the mitochondrial genome as a built-in, cell-intrinsic lineage and identity tag: donor-versus-recipient is encoded by divergent mtDNA haplotypes; clonal ancestry within donor-derived cells is encoded by private mtDNA variants accrued through stem/progenitor divisions. Reading this tag once per cell (or platelet) and coupling it to light-touch cell typing yields a single assay that simultaneously resolves chimerism and clonal diversity across all hematopoietic lineages.

Specific aims
1) Build mitoTRACE, a unified single-assay workflow that captures full-length single-cell mtDNA with unique molecular indexes and couples it to minimal cell typing (RNA and/or oligo-tagged surface proteins) to classify hematopoietic lineages, including platelets.
2) Validate mitoTRACE for clinical-grade engraftment assessment, establishing accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and turnaround time relative to current standards, while adding clonal-resolution outputs unavailable to existing methods.
3) Longitudinally map donor-derived clonal architecture and lineage outputs across compartments from day +14 to +365, quantifying diversity, dominance, and cross-lineage fate of individual donor clones.

Innovation and differentiation from existing methods
- Unlike STR chimerism (bulk, lineage-agnostic, no clonal structure), mitoTRACE resolves donor/recipient at single-cell resolution and simultaneously outputs clonal trees and diversity metrics.
- Unlike TCR/BCR repertoire sequencing (restricted to adaptive lymphocytes, confounded by antigen-driven expansion), mitoTRACE covers myeloid, lymphoid, erythroid precursors, and megakaryocytes/platelets using mtDNA present in organelles.
- Unlike retroviral integration site analysis (requires exogenous vectors, limited to gene-modified grafts), mitoTRACE is label-free and applicable to all HSCT types (allo, auto, haplo, cord).
- Single assay, dual readouts: engraftment status and polyclonal architecture within and across lineages from the same libraries.

Study design

Cohort and schedule
- Prospective, observational study of 60 HSCT recipients (matched related/unrelated, haploidentical, cord blood), with paired donor buccal swabs for germline mtDNA haplotypes.
- Timepoints: pre-transplant baseline; post-transplant days +14, +28, +60, +100, +180, +365.
- Specimens per timepoint:
  - Peripheral blood: PBMC, granulocyte-enriched fraction, and platelet-rich plasma.
  - Bone marrow aspirate: days +28, +100, +365 (standard-of-care windows) to sample erythroid precursors and megakaryocytes.
  - Opportunistic capture of circulating nucleated red cells (CD71+), if present early post-transplant.

Assay concept (single framework; no exogenous labels)
- Single-cell mtDNA capture: per cell/platelet, generate a high-coverage, UMI-indexed mtDNA library to call haplotypes and private variants; count mtDNA molecules per cell to support QC and heteroplasmy modeling.
- Minimal cell typing:
  - Nucleated cells: low-depth 3′ transcript capture to assign broad lineage state (e.g., HSPC/progenitor, myeloid, NK, T, B, erythroid precursor, megakaryocyte).
  - All cells/platelets: oligo-tagged antibody feature (ADT) panel for lineage-defining surface markers to ensure robust typing when RNA is sparse or absent (critical for platelets and late erythroid precursors).
- Output per cell/platelet: donor/recipient assignment probability, clonal ID (based on shared private mtDNA variants), lineage identity, and mtDNA copy/heteroplasmy QC metrics.

Computational analysis
- Donor–recipient assignment: haplotype clustering and likelihood models using donor and recipient baseline haplotypes; confidence scoring with explicit uncertainty.
- Clone inference: phylogenetic partitioning on shared somatic mtDNA variants; clone quality scored by variant co-occurrence and consistency across timepoints.
- Lineage mapping: integrated ADT+RNA to assign each cell/platelet to myeloid, T, B, NK, erythroid precursor, megakaryocyte/platelet; compute per-lineage donor fraction and clonal composition.
- Longitudinal dynamics: track clone frequencies across time and lineages; compute diversity (Shannon, Simpson, Gini), dominance thresholds, and cross-lineage fate bias for each clone.
- Reporting: single-page clinical summary per timepoint (engraftment by lineage; smallest detectable recipient fraction; emergent dominant clones; risk flags for graft failure or clonal skew).

Endpoints and performance targets
- Primary: Agreement of donor chimerism (%) with clinical STR chimerism in matched bulk and lineage-enriched fractions; target concordance R≥0.95 with detection of ≥1% minor fraction.
- Secondary:
  - Clonal diversity trajectories across lineages and time; establish normal ranges and detect early clonal dominance (>30% of any lineage) as a risk signal.
  - Time-to-engraftment detection: first timepoint with confident donor assignment ≥95% PPV in myeloid and platelet compartments.
  - Comprehensive lineage coverage: successful assignment in ≥90% of cells/platelets across all compartments per timepoint.
- Exploratory: Association of early clonal evenness with later cytopenias, GVHD, or relapse.

Clinical translation plan
- Sample accessibility: routine peripheral blood; marrow aspirates aligned with clinical care timepoints.
- Turnaround: 3–5 days from sample receipt to report; scalable throughput (10,000–50,000 cells/particles per run) enabling batched or rapid modes.
- Cost and infrastructure: targeted sequencing and short-read platforms widely available; per-timepoint consumable cost designed to be competitive with high-complexity NGS LDTs; bioinformatics pipeline containerized for CLIA implementation.
- Regulatory path: near-term as a CLIA laboratory-developed test for HSCT monitoring; standardized reporting; data retention and privacy conforming to clinical genomics norms.

Risk analysis and mitigations
- Donor and recipient share similar mtDNA haplotypes: pre-transplant baseline haplotypes used for supervised assignment; if ambiguity persists, a minimal, ancestry-agnostic nuclear SNP fingerprint (dozens of common biallelic SNPs) can be co-read without changing the core mitochondrial barcoding principle.
- Low mtDNA coverage or extreme heteroplasmy in specific subsets: enforce cell-level QC using mtDNA molecule counts and heteroplasmy variance models; rely on ADT-only lineage typing for identity and resample at next timepoint if necessary.
- Erythroid lineage accessibility: prioritize marrow erythroid precursors at clinical windows; opportunistic capture of circulating nucleated RBCs early post-transplant improves peripheral coverage.
- Confounding immune activation in lymphocytes: mtDNA-based clonotyping is activation-agnostic, reducing false clonal dominance signals common to receptor-based methods.

Milestones
- Months 0–6: Finalize assay design, antibody panel, and analysis pipeline; analytical validation on healthy donors and donor–recipient mixes.
- Months 6–18: Enroll and longitudinally profile HSCT cohort; interim analyses at day +100.
- Months 18–24: Lock clinical reporting, finalize performance metrics, and publish validation; prepare CLIA LDT documentation.

Deliverables
- A validated, single-assay platform and pipeline that returns: per-lineage engraftment confirmation; single-cell–resolved clonal architecture; longitudinal clonal dynamics through 1 year.
- Reference datasets and clinical reporting templates to enable multi-center adoption.

Impact
mitoTRACE converts every patient’s and donor’s mitochondrial genomes into universal, label-free barcodes readable in single cells and platelets. In one test, clinicians gain definitive engraftment confirmation and a quantitative view of polyclonal reconstitution across all hematopoietic lineages—precisely the missing link between chimerism assays and true, system-wide hematopoietic recovery.
