text:
Title: SYN-TRACE HSCT: A safe-harbor, self-writing developmental barcode for one-shot quantification of engraftment and polyclonal hematopoietic reconstitution

Question-as-Hypothesis:
If donor CD34+ hematopoietic stem/progenitor cells (HSPCs) are pre-inserted with a single, safe-harbor “self-writing” DNA cassette that (i) carries a high-diversity clonal barcode and (ii) undergoes deterministic, lineage-triggered edits along canonical hematopoietic bifurcations, then a single targeted NGS assay from patient samples will simultaneously (a) confirm engraftment and quantify chimerism and (b) resolve clonal diversity and lineage contributions across myeloid, lymphoid, erythroid, and megakaryocytic compartments longitudinally for 1 year post-transplant.

Atomic Strategy:
Pre-install a compact, orthogonal, and insulated genomic recorder—integrated once at a safe-harbor locus in donor HSPCs—that encodes both identity (cloneID) and fate (lineage-state bits). Endogenous, lineage-restricted regulatory cues transiently activate cassette-local, site-specific editing to flip predefined “bits” at each developmental branch. The cassette is then read by a single amplicon UMI-NGS assay from routine clinical samples.

Specific Aims:
1) Build a Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP)-amenable, single-locus synthetic recorder (SYN-TRACE) comprising a donor-level FamilyID, a high-entropy CloneID, and a five-bit hematopoietic lineage-state array.  
2) Validate deterministic lineage-state writing in vitro and in xenograft models, then in a pilot HSCT cohort, using one assay to quantify engraftment and polyclonality across all major lineages.  
3) Longitudinally track clonal dynamics up to 1 year and derive stability, evenness, and cross-lineage sharing metrics predictive of durable reconstitution.

Platform Architecture (SYN-TRACE cassette):
- Integration site: AAVS1 (or CCR5) safe harbor via CRISPR-Cas9 RNP + AAV6 donor; single-copy targeted insertion; insulators (cHS4) flanking the cassette.  
- FamilyID: 10–12 nt donor-product identifier (constant within a graft lot) used for unequivocal donor engraftment detection.  
- CloneID: 20–26 nt high-diversity random barcode (library complexity ~1–3×10^5) to resolve individual HSPC-derived clones.  
- Lineage-State Array (5 deterministic bits): a compact panel of orthogonal “edit tiles,” each uniquely addressable and locked once written:  
  - HSC→MPP branch gate (Bit0)  
  - MPP→CMP vs CLP gate (Bit1)  
  - CMP→GMP vs MEP gate (Bit2; myeloid vs erythro/meg)  
  - CLP→T vs B/NK gate (Bit3)  
  - MEP→Erythroid vs Megakaryocytic gate (Bit4)  
- Writing mechanism: cassette-local, orthogonal serine recombinase or CRISPR base-edit tiles activated by embedded, lineage-restricted regulatory logic.  
  - Option A (primary): human-codon–optimized, orthogonal serine recombinases (e.g., Bxb1, TP901, ΦC31 variants engineered for no genomic pseudosites) expressed from minimal, lineage-branch enhancers with miRNA logic gating to restrict off-lineage “leak.” Each recombinase inverts/excises a short tile, irreversibly setting a bit.  
  - Option B (fallback): cassette-local dCas12a-cytidine base editor expressed from an early progenitor-limited promoter with multiple gRNAs under lineage-restricted mini-promoters; edits occur only within synthetic protospacers absent from the human genome.  
- Safety scaffolds: polyA traps, microRNA target-site logic (e.g., miR-126, miR-451, miR-223, miR-150 panels) to confine expression to intended branches; degradation tags for rapid proteostasis; insulators to avoid enhancer interference; no antibiotic markers.

Manufacturing Workflow (Donor CD34+ HSPC product):
- Input: G-CSF–mobilized peripheral blood CD34+ cells (allogeneic or autologous).  
- Editing: Cas9 RNP electroporation targeting AAVS1; AAV6 donor delivers SYN-TRACE library; MOI and cell density tuned to favor single-copy HDR.  
- QC/Release: ddPCR for on-target copy number (≤1), off-target screening panel, droplet digital estimate of mark rate, viability, colony forming (CFU) potency, and sterility. No selection genes. Release in 36–48 h.  
- Infusion: standard HSCT workflow; no change to conditioning.

Clinical Sampling Plan:
- Peripheral blood: Days +14, +28, +56, +100, +180, +270, +365.  
- Fractions per time point (DNA-based):  
  - Unsorted WBC (for global engraftment and clone census)  
  - Immunomagnetically enriched: granulocytes (CD15+), monocytes (CD14+), T cells (CD3+), B cells (CD19+), NK cells (CD56+).  
- Bone marrow aspirate: Day +30 and Day +365 (standard-of-care windows) to profile nucleated erythroid (CD71+GPA+) and megakaryocytic (CD41+/CD42b+) progenitors.  
- Optional minimal marrow at Day +100 if clinically indicated.

Single-Assay Readout (one panel, one pipeline):
- Chemistry: UMI-tagged anchored multiplex PCR spanning the cassette (FamilyID + CloneID + 5-bit array) in a single 350–500 bp amplicon; dual-indexed library; 2×150 bp short-read.  
- Turnaround: 48–72 h from sample receipt; per-sample reagent cost targeted <$200 at scale.  
- Analytics:  
  - Engraftment/chimerism: copy-number–normalized fraction of cassette-positive genomes in bulk WBC (ddPCR cross-check) using FamilyID.  
  - Clonal diversity: Hill numbers (q=0,1,2), Gini-Simpson, Pielou evenness on CloneIDs; longitudinal mixed-effects models for clonal kinetics.  
  - Lineage mapping: deterministic bit patterns define branch identity; per-compartment clone sharing matrices (e.g., T/B/NK vs myeloid vs erythroid vs megakaryocytic).  
  - Stability metrics: time to oligoclonal plateau, emergence of dominant clones, cross-lineage persistence.

Validation Plan:
- In vitro differentiation: human CD34+ cells driven to myeloid, erythroid, and megakaryocytic lineages; thymopoiesis/lymphopoiesis on OP9-DLL4 co-culture; confirm bit-writing specificity and irreversibility.  
- In vivo feasibility: NSG mouse xenografts with engineered HSPCs; recover mature compartments and verify predicted bit states.  
- Pilot clinical study (Phase 0/feasibility): n=10 HSCT recipients; primary endpoints—assay success rate (>95%), safety (no graft impairment), and concordance with standard chimerism; secondary—poly-clonality metrics and lineage-bit fidelity.

Differentiation from existing methods:
- Not STR chimerism: measures only donor/host fractions; SYN-TRACE adds clone-resolved diversity and deterministic lineage states in the same assay.  
- Not TCR/BCR repertoire: limited to adaptive lymphocytes; SYN-TRACE covers myeloid, erythroid, and megakaryocytic compartments and relates shared clonal ancestry across all.  
- Not retroviral integration site analysis: no random genome scarring; single safe-harbor insertion with predefined high-entropy CloneID and fate bits; uniform capture with one amplicon.  
- Not lentiviral barcoding alone: adds built-in lineage-decision recording to make lineage identity intrinsic to the barcode, reducing dependence on extensive cell sorting.

Regulatory and Safety Considerations:
- Safe-harbor single-copy insertion; no therapeutic gene expression.  
- Cassette-local editing only; orthogonal recombinase sites or synthetic protospacers absent from the human genome; minimal, transient expression tightly gated by lineage cues.  
- Immunogenicity mitigation: low-level, short-duration expression; proteasomal degradation tags; no persistent nucleases; insulators to prevent positional effects.  
- Release testing aligned to current ex vivo HSPC gene-editing IND precedents.

Success Criteria and Milestones (12 months post–first infusion):
- M1–M3: Complete cassette library, in vitro specificity (bit error rate <1% off-target within cassette, none genome-wide by targeted panel).  
- M4–M6: Xenograft validation; correct bit signatures in ≥90% of recovered lineage cells.  
- M7–M12: Pilot HSCT:  
  - Engraftment call concordant with standard assays within ±5% at Days +28/+100/+365.  
  - Effective clone number (Hill q=1) ≥50 at Day +100 in uncomplicated grafts; stability of top-10 clone ranks across ≥2 consecutive timepoints.  
  - Lineage mapping coverage across all four compartments; erythroid/megakaryocytic resolved in marrow aspirates with predicted Bit2/Bit4 states.

Risk Mitigation:
- If any lineage-bit driver shows leakage, swap to alternative enhancer/miRNA logic or move that bit to base-edit tile (Option B).  
- If HDR marking <20%, increase AAV6 donor dose, employ short ssODN donor for minimal cassette with nested CloneID + bits, or apply transient HDR enhancers.  
- If immunogenicity signals arise, transition to split-recombinase with self-excising circuits post-bit writing.

Expected Impact:
A single, scalable, and regulatorily tractable assay that transforms HSCT monitoring from bulk chimerism snapshots to high-resolution, system-wide clonal cartography—linking engraftment quality, lineage balance, and clonal stability within one framework and within clinical turnaround times.

text:
Title: TRACE-H: Targeted, RNA-annotated, CRISPR-Embedded Heritable Barcodes for Simultaneous Engraftment Quantification and Polyclonal Reconstitution Profiling after HSCT

Atomic strategy (single insight):
Write a unique, single-copy, safe-harbor DNA barcode into each donor HSC ex vivo that also transcribes a short barcode RNA. After HSCT, quantify (a) engraftment by the fraction of edited molecules among bulk nucleated blood DNA, and (b) clonal diversity by counting unique barcodes across DNA from leukocytes and RNA from lineage-informative anucleate compartments (platelets, reticulocytes) without any cell sorting.

Why this is novel:
- Not STR chimerism: measures donor fraction via engineered-edit frequency, not native polymorphisms.
- Not TCR/BCR repertoire: lineage-agnostic, tracks all hematopoietic outputs, not only adaptive lymphocytes.
- Not retroviral integration site analysis: uses a fixed safe-harbor knock-in of a compact barcode (position-invariant), avoiding random multi-copy integrations and insertion-site mapping.

Specific aims:
1) Build and validate a clinical-grade safe-harbor barcode cassette and editing workflow for donor HSCs with high efficiency and minimal off-target risk.
2) Develop a single, low-cost, targeted sequencing assay that simultaneously outputs donor engraftment (edited fraction) and clonal ecology (barcode spectrum) from one blood draw.
3) Longitudinally map clonal dynamics across myeloid, lymphoid, erythroid, and megakaryocytic compartments for 12 months post-HSCT.

Platform design:
- Barcode locus: AAVS1 (or CCR5) safe harbor. Single-copy knock-in of a 160–220 bp DNA barcode composed of:
  - 18–24 variable positions encoded as an error-correcting code (Hamming distance ≥3) yielding >10^8 unique tags.
  - Flanking invariant primer/UMI handles for ultra-accurate amplicon sequencing.
  - Minimal Pol II promoter driving a 140–180 nt noncoding RNA containing the same barcode and a short synthetic 3′ UTR/polyA for ubiquitous, low-burden expression (transcribed in nucleated progeny; RNA cargo is packaged into platelets and persists in reticulocytes).
- Editing chemistry: Cas9 nuclease + AAV6 donor for precise HDR knock-in (GMP-compatible), or prime editing (PE5/PEmax mRNA + pegRNA library) to write barcodes without DSBs. Multiplicity of editing tuned (λ≈0.3–0.5) to favor one barcode per HSC.
- Ex vivo QC and calibration:
  - Deep amplicon sequencing of the manufactured graft to quantify: (i) barcode complexity, (ii) per-clone abundance, (iii) editing efficiency E (fraction barcoded among CD34+ cells).
  - Optional short-term colony assay (CFU-GM/BFU-E) with targeted genotyping to confirm single-barcode per colony.
- Release criteria: viability, CD34+ purity, preserved LTC-IC/NSG repopulation proxy, on-target specificity, no gross karyotypic change.

Clinical sampling and lineage coverage without sorting:
- At each timepoint: a single 10–15 mL peripheral blood draw partitioned into:
  - Buffy coat gDNA (nucleated leukocytes; myeloid + lymphoid).
  - Platelet-rich plasma for platelet RNA (megakaryocytic output).
  - Reticulocyte-enriched fraction by density/filtration (no immunosorting) for RNA (early erythroid output).
- Optional standard-of-care marrow aspirates (e.g., days +30 and +365) for confirmatory progenitor-level profiling (no surface marker sorting; bulk mononuclear prep only).

Single-assay readout:
- Dual-template targeted sequencing from the same locus:
  - DNA-UMI amplicon: quantifies total edited vs unedited molecules (engraftment metric) and enumerates unique DNA barcodes (clonal diversity in nucleated lineages).
  - RNA-UMI amplicon: from platelet and reticulocyte RNA to detect the same barcodes as lineage-informative transcripts, capturing megakaryocytic and erythroid outputs.
- Library construction: two-step PCR with UMIs and unique dual indices; 2 × 150 bp on benchtop sequencer; 1–3 million reads per sample set.
- Turnaround time: 48–72 hours; projected cost <$250 per timepoint (all three compartments).

Primary endpoints and metrics:
- Engraftment success:
  - Donor chimerism estimate = (fraction of edited DNA molecules in buffy coat) / E, where E is editing efficiency measured in the infused graft; capped at 100%.
  - Compartmental engraftment confirmation via presence/abundance of barcode RNA in platelets/reticulocytes.
- Clonal diversity and stability:
  - Counts of unique barcodes, rarefaction-corrected richness, Shannon index, Gini coefficient.
  - Clonal evenness and dominance thresholds (e.g., any clone >20% sustained).
  - Cross-compartment clone sharing matrices (DNA vs platelet-RNA vs retic-RNA) to quantify multilineage output.
- Dynamics:
  - Longitudinal trajectories of top clones and turnover half-lives.
  - Early-to-late contribution mapping to identify durable HSC-derived vs short-term progenitor waves.

Study schema (12 months):
- Timepoints: baseline graft (day 0, product), peripheral blood on days +14, +28, +56, +84, +112, +168, +224, +280, +336, +365; optional marrow at +30 and +365 (standard-of-care aligned).
- Cohort: 20–30 HSCT recipients (allogeneic and autologous exploratory strata), with matched graft QC.

Bioinformatic pipeline:
- Error suppression: UMI consensus, duplex-simulation filtering, and barcode whitelist from the infused product.
- Clone calling: exact-match to whitelist; Levenshtein distance rescue within error-correcting bounds.
- Diversity estimation: bias-corrected estimators (Chao1/ACE) with bootstrapped CIs; longitudinal state-space modeling for clone kinetics.
- Safety surveillance: outlier detection for expanding single clones; alert if growth rate exceeds pre-specified slope or dominance threshold.

Validation plan:
- Analytical validation: limit of detection for engraftment (≥0.5% donor fraction), barcode calling precision/recall, inter-run CV.
- Biological validation: concordance with standard clinical chimerism (STR/indel) for engraftment magnitude, yet added resolution for clonality; correlation of platelet/retic RNA barcodes with platelet counts/reticulocyte indices.
- Stress tests: simulated low-input, inflammatory leukocytosis, transfusion interference controls.

Regulatory and safety considerations:
- Fixed safe-harbor knock-in minimizes insertional mutagenesis risk compared to random integration; single-copy design reduces genotoxic burden.
- GMP manufacturing with release tests; traceability of barcode dictionary restricted to protocol; noncoding barcode transcript lacks ORF and uses humanized minimal elements to avoid immunogenicity.
- Investigational-device exemption path for the assay; protocol aligned with existing ex vivo HSC editing frameworks.

Expected outcomes and impact:
- A clinically practical, single-locus assay that confirms engraftment and quantifies reconstitution ecology across all hematopoietic compartments without cell sorting.
- Month-scale, low-cost longitudinal monitoring enabling early detection of graft failure, oligoclonal dominance, or lineage-restricted deficits.
- A generalizable platform for future trials evaluating conditioning intensity, graft engineering, or gene-editing interventions using robust clonal endpoints.

Title: CONCERTO — A single-assay, blood-only platform to quantify engraftment and polyclonal reconstitution by temporal multi-lineage clonal fingerprints

Central hypothesis and atomic strategy
- Hypothesis: Each donor-derived hematopoietic stem/progenitor cell (HSPC) clone has a characteristic, time-lagged, multi-lineage output profile that is identifiable from peripheral blood alone. Stable, naturally occurring somatic mitochondrial variants and ultramutable nuclear repeats act as inherited “clone tags” that propagate to all mature progeny; by repeatedly sampling these genetic fingerprints across all blood lineages and modeling their coordinated dynamics, we can simultaneously confirm engraftment and infer clonal diversity without bone marrow biopsies.
- Atomic strategy: Use private mitochondrial heteroplasmies (plus a compact panel of hypermutable nuclear microsatellites) as endogenous barcodes measured across fractionated blood lineages at serial time points, then invert the mixture using a mechanistic, lifespan-constrained blind source separation model to reconstruct clone number, size, lineage bias, and turnover.

Innovation (what is fundamentally new)
- Endogenous multi-lineage barcoding: Leverages naturally occurring somatic mitochondrial variants and nuclear repeat drift as universal, non-engineered clonal tags across myeloid, lymphoid, erythroid (via reticulocytes), and megakaryocytic (via platelets) compartments.
- Temporal deconvolution with physiological priors: Identifies clones by their coordinated, time-lagged abundance trajectories across lineages, constrained by known maturation and lifespan priors, enabling robust inference even when any single lineage is sparse.
- Single integrated assay: A unified sequencing workflow simultaneously reports donor–recipient chimerism (engraftment) and clonal ecology metrics, replacing separate STR chimerism tests and lineage-restricted repertoire methods.
- Clinically amenable: Peripheral blood only; magnetically enriched lineage fractions; targeted, UMI-enabled sequencing; results designed for CLIA/LDT deployment with <1-week turnaround and per-sample costs aligned with current chimerism plus NGS assays.

Overview of the CONCERTO platform
1) Patient sampling and lineage coverage
- Matrix: 10–20 mL peripheral blood at predefined timepoints (e.g., weekly to day 60, biweekly to day 100, monthly to 12 months).
- Fractions: Neutrophils, monocytes, eos/basophils, NK cells, CD4 T cells, CD8 T cells, B cells, platelets (megakaryocytic output), and CD71+ reticulocytes (erythroid output). Fractionation via closed-system immunomagnetic enrichment compatible with clinical labs.
- Rationale: Platelets carry abundant mtDNA; reticulocytes preserve mitochondria and transcripts transiently, enabling erythroid representation without marrow access.

2) Single-library targeted sequencing
- Panel A (Engraftment backbone): ~300 ancestry-informative nuclear SNPs enabling high-confidence donor vs recipient genotyping across fractions (primary engraftment call anchored in short-lived granulocytes).
- Panel B (Clonal tags): Full mitochondrial genome with UMI-based, duplex error suppression to detect low-frequency heteroplasmies across fractions; compact set of nuclear ultramutable microsatellites increases tagging density and stability.
- Output: For each timepoint × fraction, precise estimates of donor chimerism and a vector of clonal-tag allele fractions.

3) Temporal multi-lineage deconvolution (“Orchestra” model)
- Model class: Nonnegative matrix factorization with physiological regularization.
- Priors: Lineage-specific production lags and survival (e.g., neutrophils ~days, platelets ~1–2 weeks, reticulocytes ~days, lymphocytes ~weeks–months) constrain feasible clone-output trajectories.
- Inference: Jointly estimates (i) number of active clones, (ii) clone-specific tag haplotypes, (iii) per-clone contribution to each lineage over time, and (iv) turnover metrics (expansion/contraction rates).
- Outputs: EngraftmentScore (donor fraction in short-lived myeloid), ClonalRichness (estimated clone count), ClonalEvenness (Shannon/Simpson), LineageBias Index, CloneTurnover Half-life, and Early Warning Flags (loss of diversity, dominant clone emergence).

Specific aims
Aim 1: Engineering and analytical validation of CONCERTO
- Build and lock the dual-panel assay (engraftment SNPs + clonal tags) with UMI-enabled chemistry and standardized lineage enrichment.
- Establish analytic sensitivity/specificity for heteroplasmy detection and microsatellite drift across cell fractions; demonstrate cross-fraction concordance of private tags for known mixtures.
- Deliver locked bioinformatics: basecalling → error suppression → tag calling → chimerism estimation → Orchestra deconvolution with uncertainty quantification.

Aim 2: Physiologically grounded temporal deconvolution
- Calibrate lineage priors using published maturation and lifespan ranges and refine on a 30-donor healthy reference cohort sampled longitudinally.
- Benchmark clone inference on orthogonal truth sets (e.g., colony assays or sorted progenitor mtDNA profiles in leftover clinical marrow from a subset, when available) to quantify accuracy of clone count and contributions.

Aim 3: Prospective HSCT study for 12-month longitudinal performance
- Cohort: Allogeneic HSCT recipients (n≈80) with standard-of-care monitoring.
- Schedule: Pre-HSCT baseline (recipient), day +14, +21, +28, then monthly to month 12.
- Endpoints:
  - Primary: Concordance of EngraftmentScore with clinical engraftment; time-to-engraftment detection versus standard STR chimerism.
  - Secondary: Clonal ecology metrics predicting graft failure, poor graft function, relapse, or GVHD; association of early diversity loss or extreme lineage bias with adverse outcomes.
  - Exploratory: Stability of clone tags across lineages and time; detection of transient donor–recipient mosaicism in mixed chimerism.

Study design and analysis plan
- Sampling: Blood-only workflow; immediate fractionation; single-library preparation per timepoint.
- Quality controls:
  - Technical: Synthetic spike-ins for error calibration; replicate fractions at sentinel timepoints.
  - Biological: Cross-lineage co-occurrence of the same mtDNA tag validates clonality; nuclear repeat concordance as secondary evidence.
- Statistics:
  - Pre-specified thresholds for engraftment positivity from granulocyte SNPs with Bayesian credible intervals.
  - Diversity measures (richness, Shannon) tracked over time; mixed-effects models to associate trajectories with clinical outcomes.
  - Simulation studies to define minimal sampling density to resolve K clones given observed noise, enabling adaptive sampling if clinic schedules vary.

Milestones and deliverables
- Month 0–6: Assay build; limit-of-detection and precision claims; locked analysis pipeline.
- Month 6–18: Healthy reference and pilot HSCT feasibility; finalize priors and reporting metrics.
- Month 18–36: Full HSCT accrual; interim analyses at 6 and 12 months; clinical decision-support report prototype with EngraftmentScore and Clonal Ecology Dashboard.

Risk mitigation
- Low reticulocyte counts: Increase blood volume modestly at sparse timepoints and/or pool adjacent timepoints for erythroid estimates; model imputes erythroid output using cross-lineage couplings with uncertainty flags.
- MtDNA drift within clones: Dual-tagging with nuclear repeats stabilizes clonal identity; Orchestra model treats slow drift as a latent process.
- Mixed chimerism and recipient persistence: Engraftment SNPs resolve donor/recipient; clone calling restricted to donor-haplotype background for reconstitution metrics.

Clinical translation and regulatory path
- Sample accessibility: Peripheral blood only; closed-system enrichment; no marrow aspiration required.
- Turnaround and cost: Single-library, targeted NGS with automated reporting; designed for 3–5 business days and cost comparable to combined chimerism + targeted NGS assays.
- Regulatory feasibility: Developed as a CLIA laboratory-developed test with analytical validation; clear separation of clinical decision thresholds (engraftment) from exploratory research metrics (diversity) during initial deployment.

Expected impact
- A unified, minimally invasive, and mechanistically grounded assay that confirms engraftment earlier than current standards while revealing the hidden clonal ecology of hematopoietic reconstitution across all major lineages. By listening to the “orchestra” of peripheral outputs over time and reading each section’s inherited genetic motifs, CONCERTO reconstructs the number and behavior of the musicians—providing actionable, patient-specific insight throughout the first post-transplant year.

Title
State-Contingent Allelic Imbalance for Penetrance Prediction (SCAIP): a clinically translatable assay and model that integrates genotype with stimulus-resolved cellular state

Central hypothesis and research goal
Incomplete penetrance arises when risk variants are only functional in specific, inducible cellular states. Measuring how an individual’s risk alleles manifest as state-contingent allelic imbalance (SCAI) under standardized stimuli will predict who develops disease among carriers better than genotype alone. Goal: build and validate a blood-based SCAIP score that combines (a) genotype at risk SNPs and (b) stimulus-resolved allele-specific expression from accessible immune cell types to forecast future disease onset and flares.

Atomic strategy (single conceptual insight)
Penetrance is the probability that a risk allele becomes regulatory-active in the right cellular state. Quantify this directly by measuring delta-allelic imbalance (stimulated vs. baseline) at risk loci in relevant blood cell subsets; aggregate these locus×state readouts into an interpretable penetrance score.

Specific aims
1) Assay development: Create a low-cost, targeted, multiplexed RNA-based allele-specific expression (ASE) panel to measure SCAI across 200–400 fine-mapped disease-risk loci in magnetically enriched blood cell types (CD14+ monocytes, CD4+ T cells, B cells).
2) Reference atlas and feature engineering: Build a normative map of SCAI responses to three standardized ex vivo stimuli that span key immune axes: LPS (innate/TLR4), IFN-α (antiviral), and dexamethasone (glucocorticoid). Derive individual-level features: per-locus delta-ASE, stimulus selectivity, and switch-like imbalance.
3) Predictive modeling and validation: Train a sparse, interpretable hierarchical model that outputs a SCAIP score predicting incident disease (primary) and near-term flare (secondary) in prospective cohorts, benchmarking vs. and complementing polygenic risk scores (PRS).

Study design overview
- Participants: N=800 discovery (healthy carriers of risk alleles and early/at-risk individuals), N=600 external validation (disease-relevant cohorts). Blood draws at enrollment, with 12–24 month clinical follow-up for incident diagnosis or flare endpoints.
- Sample type: 12–20 mL peripheral blood. Practical in clinic settings.
- Cell processing: PBMC isolation; magnetic bead enrichment for CD14+, CD4+, CD19+ (15–30 minutes per subset).
- Stimulation: 4-hour exposure to LPS (100 ng/mL), IFN-α (1,000 U/mL), dexamethasone (100 nM), plus matched unstimulated controls, in duplicate.
- Nucleic acids: DNA (for genotyping) and RNA from each condition×cell type.

Integrated measurement (simultaneous genotype-state capture)
- Genotype: Low-cost array or low-pass WGS with imputation to call the risk SNP panel.
- State-contingent function: Targeted UMI-tagged amplicon cDNA sequencing across panel transcripts overlapping risk SNPs and sentinel exonic proxies. ASE inherently binds genotype to transcriptomic state in the same molecules; delta-ASE quantifies state-specific allelic activity.

Assay details (moderate complexity, costed)
- Target panel: 200–400 loci prioritized by high fine-mapping probability, blood eQTL colocalization, and stimulus-responsive TF motif overlap. Each locus covered by 2–3 amplicons (exonic or 3′ UTR SNPs in LD with causal noncoding variants).
- Library: One-step multiplex RT-PCR with UMIs, followed by pooled indexing; 0.5–1.0 million reads per sample suffices (cost target <$120 per patient including genotyping).
- QC: RNA integrity, UMI deduplication, allele-specific bias correction using synthetic equimolar spike-ins.

Primary features (interpretable)
- Locus-level:
  - Delta-ASEl,s = log2(Ref/Alt)stimulus − log2(Ref/Alt)baseline per locus l, stimulus s.
  - State selectivity Sl = argmaxs |Delta-ASEl,s|.
  - Thresholded “switch” indicator Il,s = 1 if |Delta-ASEl,s| > θ and FDR<0.05.
- Individual-level:
  - SCAI burden Bs = Σl wl,s·Il,s (weighted by prior causal probability).
  - SCAI magnitude Ms = Σl wl,s·|Delta-ASEl,s|.
  - Network coherence Cs = correlation of Il,s with stimulus-specific TF target sets (predefined).
- Composite SCAIP score: linear combination of Bs, Ms, Cs across stimuli and cell types with learned nonnegative weights; optionally combined with PRS as an additive term for transparency.

Modeling strategy (simple and interpretable)
- Sparse Bayesian logistic regression (horseshoe prior) predicting endpoint from SCAIP features (+/- PRS).
- Hierarchical shrinkage across stimuli/cell types to favor few, strong, biologically coherent signals.
- Output: Probability of disease onset within time horizon, with feature attribution (which locus×state drove risk).

Validation plan
- Technical: Reproducibility across replicates; stability across freeze–thaw; batch-bridging controls; cross-site ring trial.
- Biological:
  - Test–retest (two draws, 4–8 weeks apart) for within-person stability.
  - Pharmacologic perturbation: ex vivo glucocorticoid should dampen dex-induced SCAI features, validating mechanism.
- Clinical:
  - Discovery: 5-fold cross-validation; calibration and decision curves vs. PRS alone.
  - External: Pre-registered validation in independent site; endpoints adjudicated blinded to SCAIP.
  - Subgroup analyses: age, sex, ancestry; demonstrate portability after ancestry-aware normalization of ASE baselines.

Disease contexts and endpoints
- Autoimmune/inflammatory exemplar (primary): incident inflammatory bowel disease or systemic lupus erythematosus in high-risk relatives or antibody-positive individuals.
- Secondary: flare prediction in established disease (e.g., relapse within 6 months).

Success criteria
- AUC improvement ≥0.10 over PRS; net reclassification improvement ≥15% at clinically relevant thresholds.
- Calibration slope 0.9–1.1 and Brier score improvement vs. PRS.
- Per-feature interpretability: top 10 contributing locus×state pairs map to known pathway biology.

Clinical translatability
- Workflow: Standard phlebotomy → PBMC isolation and magnetic selection → 4-hour plate stimulation → RT-PCR panel → benchtop sequencer.
- Turnaround: 24–36 hours; batched processing feasible.
- Cost target: <$200/sample all-in at scale.
- Output: One-page report with SCAIP probability, traffic-light risk tier, and top contributing locus×state features for clinician interpretation.

Risk management and contingencies
- Limited heterozygosity at some loci: large multi-locus panel ensures each individual contributes >40 informative loci on average; model weights adapt to available loci per person.
- Cell-type confounding: light-touch enrichment (3 subsets) balances resolution and complexity; deconvolution checks with reference markers.
- Overfitting: strict prespecification, external validation, and locked model before clinical testing.

Milestones and timeline (24 months)
- M0–6: Panel design, assay optimization, spike-ins, analytical validation.
- M6–12: Reference atlas (N≈250), feature selection lock.
- M12–20: Discovery cohort accrual and modeling.
- M20–24: External validation and clinical reporting prototype.

Deliverables
- Validated SCAIP assay kit (primer pool, controls, analysis pipeline).
- Locked, interpretable model and reporting software.
- Public reference atlas of stimulus-resolved ASE for common risk loci.
- Prospective evidence for clinical utility beyond PRS.

Title
Serum-Activated Allelic Response (SAAR) test for predicting penetrance of disease-risk SNPs

Central hypothesis-question
Do circulating factors in an individual’s blood currently possess the capacity to activate that individual’s risk alleles in disease-relevant cells, and does the magnitude and direction of this genotype-conditioned activation predict who will manifest disease within a defined horizon?

Atomic strategy
Use a universal, integrated reporter-cell assay that measures, in one perturbation, the allele-specific transcriptional activation of a targeted set of risk regulatory elements when exposed to a patient’s serum/plasma. The minimal sufficient statistic for penetrance is the genotype-conditioned differential response of risk versus protective alleles to that patient’s circulating milieu.

Overview of the system
- Input: 2–4 mL peripheral blood (for plasma/serum and low-plex cytokines) and a low-cost SNP genotype (array or imputed WGS, existing data acceptable).
- Engineered cells: A standardized, banked “sentinel” human cell line for the disease class (e.g., hepatocyte-like cells for metabolic disease; microvascular endothelial or fibroblast-like cells for inflammatory disease), each harboring an Allelic Reporter Panel (ARP).
- ARP design: 150–300 short enhancer/promoter elements (≈200 bp) centered on high-confidence disease-risk SNPs. Each locus is present as matched reference and alternate allele variants, each linked to 3 unique molecular barcodes and integrated at a safe-harbor landing pad (single-copy per cell), enabling direct measurement of allele-specific transcription upon stimulation.
- Perturbation: Expose reporter cells to patient serum (10% v/v; optional 30% for dose-response) for 6 hours (primary) and 24 hours (secondary).
- Readout (integrated genotype–state capture):
  1) Targeted RNA-seq to quantify barcode expression (allele-specific enhancer activity) and a 200-gene sentinel transcript panel capturing core cellular-state modules (inflammation, stress, metabolism).
  2) Optional low-plex targeted epigenomic add-on in the same wells (CUT&Tag-lite for H3K27ac at 30–50 sentinel enhancers) for cohorts where chromatin context is required.
  3) 30-plex cytokine/chemokine immunoassay on the patient serum for interpretable environmental features.
- Output: A Penetrance Activation Score (PAS) derived from allele-specific activation features aligned to the patient’s genotype, plus interpretable pathway and cytokine drivers.

Mechanistic rationale
Many risk SNPs act by altering TF binding at regulatory elements; cytokines, hormones, lipids, and metabolites modulate TF activity and chromatin state. If a patient’s circulating milieu contains sufficient activators, risk alleles will show disproportionate enhancer output compared with reference alleles in disease-relevant cells, initiating downstream disease programs. Measuring this ex vivo genotype-conditioned response operationalizes penetrance.

Assay details (kept moderate in complexity)
- Sentinel cell lines (one primary per disease class; optional second for robustness) derived from a well-characterized iPSC background with stable growth and minimal batch effects.
- ARP construction: piggyBac or recombinase-mediated landing pad to insert a compact library (≤1,200 cassettes including both alleles and barcodes). Library complexity verified once and banked as master cell stocks.
- Plate format: 96-well; each patient uses 2–4 wells (two serum doses × one timepoint; optional second timepoint batched). Include pooled healthy serum and pooled disease-positive serum as calibrators per plate.
- Sequencing: Single targeted capture library per plate that jointly enriches barcode UTRs and the 200-gene sentinel panel; 5–8 million reads per well suffice.
- Turnaround: 48–72 hours from blood draw to score.

Feature engineering and model
- Per-locus Allelic Activation Differential (AAD): log2(RNA-barcodeALT/RNA-barcodeREF) under patient serum, normalized to pooled healthy control in the same plate and adjusted by library-specific barcode effects.
- Genotype conditioning: For each patient, only aggregate AADs for risk alleles they carry (heterozygotes weighted by expected allelic dosage; homozygotes by full weight). Loci not carried contribute zero.
- Pathway state: Scores from the 200-gene sentinel panel (e.g., NF-κB, JAK/STAT, lipid metabolism, ER stress) captured as standardized module activities.
- Environment features: Cytokine/chemokine z-scores and limited clinical chemistries (e.g., CRP if available).
- Model: Elastic-net logistic regression (primary) with monotonic constraints on biologically directional features; calibrated to 2–5 year incident disease (or flare) as endpoint. A parsimonious gradient-boosted tree serves as sensitivity analysis.
- Output: Penetrance Activation Score (PAS, 0–1), 95% CI via bootstrapping; interpretable report listing top contributing loci, pathways, and cytokines.

Study design
- Discovery cohort: N≈300 at-risk individuals without clinical disease at baseline; enrich for carriers of targeted SNPs. Collect serum and genotype, run SAAR, longitudinal follow-up for incident disease over 24–60 months.
- Independent validation: N≈200, pre-registered thresholds for PAS. Secondary validation in a case-control set to test discriminative ability at diagnosis.
- Endpoints: Incident disease meeting consensus criteria or documented flare (disease-specific). Secondary: time-to-event.
- Comparators: PRS alone; clinical risk scores; serum cytokines alone. Primary metric: AUC improvement and Net Reclassification Index versus PRS; decision-curve analysis for clinical utility.

Clinical translation plan
- Sample logistics: Standard phlebotomy; serum/plasma prepared in routine labs; 2 mL minimum volume.
- Cost targets: Reagents and sequencing <$250 per test at scale; total <$500 with overheads.
- Reporting: Binary high/low PAS threshold pre-specified for intended-use context, with interpretable drivers and suggested re-testing interval (e.g., 6–12 months).
- Regulatory path: LDT in a CLIA setting using a locked reporter-cell bank; move toward IVD with frozen assay kits (cryopreserved cells, capture reagents, calibrators).

Quality control and normalization
- Internal controls: Synthetic RNA spike-ins for library normalization; per-plate positive/negative serum calibrators; replicate wells for 5% of samples.
- Batch correction: Plate-wise mixed-effects modeling using calibrators; acceptance criteria on control AAD distributions.
- Robustness checks: Heat-inactivation sub-assay on a subset to distinguish complement-dependent effects; dose concordance (10% vs 30% serum) as QC.

Risk assessment and mitigations
- Variability in serum composition: Mitigated via within-plate calibrators and dose-response; repeat sampling in a subset to characterize intra-individual variability.
- Cell-context mismatch: Disease-specific sentinel cell selection informed by eQTL/caQTL tissue relevance; optional second sentinel cell increases coverage with minimal complexity.
- Reporter context effects: Safe-harbor integration and multiple barcodes per allele reduce positional artifacts; validate a subset of loci at endogenous sites in a pilot.

Milestones and success criteria
- M1 (6 months): Complete ARP design/build; demonstrate reproducible allele-specific activation for ≥60% of loci with at least one canonical stimulus; establish assay CV <15%.
- M2 (12 months): Pilot with 60 participants; establish feature stability and preliminary PAS discrimination (AUC ≥0.70 vs PRS ≤0.62 for short-horizon events).
- M3 (24–36 months): Prospective validation achieving pre-specified AUC improvement ≥0.08 over PRS, significant net reclassification at clinically relevant thresholds, and robust interpretability with ≤15 features in the locked model.

Intended impact
SAAR reframes risk prediction from static genotype to genotype-conditioned environmental activation. By functionally testing whether the current body chemistry can turn genetic predisposition into disease programs, SAAR aims to resolve incomplete penetrance and deliver an interpretable, clinically practical prediction of near-term disease manifestation.

text:
Title: Dynamic Allele-Specific Response Profiling (DARP) to Map Exposure-Conditional Disease Penetrance

Abstract
Incomplete penetrance of disease-risk SNPs reflects context-dependent regulatory effects that are silent at baseline but emerge under specific environmental states. We propose DARP, a clinically translatable blood-based system that quantifies how individual risk alleles “wake up” under controlled, short-term perturbations. By measuring allele-specific shifts in RNA and chromatin from the same samples before and after standardized immune, stress, and metabolic challenges, we derive interpretable Triggerability Scores per locus and construct individual Conditional Penetrance Profiles that predict not just who is at risk, but under which conditions disease programs activate.

Central question and hypothesis
Question-hypothesis: Which standardized exposures switch risk loci from silent to active states in human blood cells, and do within-person, allele-specific regulatory responses to these exposures predict exposure-conditional disease risk more accurately than static polygenic scores?

Atomic strategy
Quantify the change in allelic imbalance at disease-linked regulatory and transcript loci in peripheral blood cells after brief, standardized perturbations. The within-locus, within-person shift in allele-specific expression (ASE) and allele-specific chromatin accessibility (ASCA) captures causal gene-by-environment (G×E) activation and resolves penetrance dynamically.

Specific aims
1) Build a targeted allele-specific multi-omic panel in PBMCs that simultaneously reads genotype and cellular state.
- Perturbation set (6 axes): type I interferon (IFN-α), NF-κB (LPS), glucocorticoid receptor (low-dose dexamethasone), insulin/glucose (OGTT-mimic in vitro), lipid stress (palmitate/albumin), and mitochondrial stress (oligomycin A, low dose).
- Assay: paired targeted-ATAC capture and targeted-amplicon RNA-seq focused on ~1,000 sentinel regulatory elements and ~300 risk-linked genes (common autoimmune, inflammatory, cardiometabolic, neuro-immune loci).
- Sample: 10–20 mL whole blood → PBMCs; 0 h (baseline) and 4 h post-perturbation.
- Integrated readout: allele-specific signals intrinsically couple genotype (ref/alt reads) with cell state (stimulus-induced molecular response) in the same experiment.

2) Derive Triggerability Scores and construct individual Conditional Penetrance Profiles (CPPs) that are low-cost and interpretable.
- Feature engineering:
  - Locus-level Triggerability Score (TS): change in allelic imbalance after perturbation relative to baseline, with uncertainty.
  - Pathway-trigger index: aggregate TS across loci mapping to curated disease pathways.
- Modeling: generalized linear mixed models per locus (fixed: genotype dosage, stimulus; interaction: G×E; random: subject), with empirical Bayes shrinkage; no deep nets needed.
- Output: a per-person conditional risk matrix (stimulus × pathway) with traffic-light interpretation (green = quiescent, amber = inducible, red = highly triggerable).
- Cost target: <$250 per subject per panel at scale (multiplexed sequencing, capture-based panels).

3) Validate exposure-conditional predictions in controlled micro-challenges and short-term prospective follow-up.
- In-clinic micro-challenges (standardized, low risk):
  - Seasonal influenza vaccination (type I IFN axis).
  - 2-hour oral glucose tolerance test (metabolic axis).
  - Single low-dose dexamethasone tablet (stress axis).
- Endpoints:
  - Acute molecular concordance: DARP TS vs. serum cytokines, phospho-signaling, and targeted proteomics.
  - Clinical concordance: in at-risk carriers, prediction of flare proxies (e.g., transient CRP, autoantibody titers, glucose excursions) and 12-month incident/subclinical phenotypes captured by EHR and wearables.
- Comparison: DARP-CPP vs. conventional PRS and baseline eQTL/epigenetic markers.

Study design and methods
- Cohort: n=300 adults enriched for heterozygosity at sentinel loci (identified by low-pass WGS or genotyping array with imputation and phasing). Include both disease-free carriers and early/mild cases for calibration.
- Laboratory workflow (per subject):
  1) PBMC isolation and aliquoting into 7 wells (1 control + 6 perturbations).
  2) 4-hour incubation; harvest RNA and nuclei from identical aliquots.
  3) Library prep:
     - Targeted-amplicon RNA-seq (UMI-labeled) over exonic SNPs and splice sites of ~300 genes.
     - ATAC-seq followed by hybrid-capture to ~1,000 risk enhancers/promoters harboring functional SNPs.
  4) Sequencing: shallow-to-moderate depth (e.g., 1–2 M reads per RNA amplicon library; 10–20 M per captured ATAC library), pooled across subjects with barcodes.
- Data processing and QC:
  - Allele-aware mapping, duplicate removal via UMIs, cell-type deconvolution from RNA profiles with flow cytometry anchors (CD3, CD14, CD19, CD56) for interpretability.
  - ASE/ASCA calling with beta-binomial models; harmonization across stimuli.
- Modeling and reporting:
  - TS computed per locus per stimulus with false discovery control.
  - CPP generated as a simple matrix and summarized into 3–5 exposure rules per person (e.g., “Under viral-like inflammation, loci A/B trigger strongly; consider pre-emptive vaccination and early antiviral response plans”).
  - Minimal explanatory set: the smallest subset of loci whose TS explains >80% of a person’s CPP signal to enhance clinical interpretability.

Clinical translation plan
- Sample type: venous blood; total lab time <48–72 hours; report-ready within 1 week.
- Report: exposure-conditional risk matrix, top explanatory loci, pathway summaries, and action cues (preventive strategies, monitoring triggers).
- Use cases:
  - Pre-disease carriers: identify high-risk conditions and personalize prevention.
  - Established disease: identify flare triggers for relapse prevention.
  - Drug response: map GR- or IFN-responsiveness at risk loci to guide therapy selection.

What makes this beyond PRS
- PRS is static; DARP is conditional. It reveals whether risk alleles are functionally competent only in specific states, quantified as stimulus-induced allelic shifts.
- Integration is intrinsic: genotype and cellular state are read from the same molecules in the same sample via ASE/ASCA.
- Interpretability: exposure-by-pathway matrix with minimal feature sets, not opaque global scores.

Power, feasibility, and complexity management
- Power: within-person contrasts and allele-specific reads increase sensitivity to small effect sizes with modest N.
- Complexity: targeted panels, brief perturbations, and GLMM-based statistics keep costs and compute moderate.
- Discovery-to-clinic bridge: run a one-time high-resolution single-cell multiome in a 30-subject subset to refine the targeted capture panel, then lock the clinical panel.

Risks and mitigations
- Limited heterozygosity at some loci: expand panel to include trans-acting readouts and haplotype blocks; prioritize common variants.
- Cell-type specificity: incorporate deconvolution and optional magnetic enrichment of major lineages in a subset to calibrate models.
- Non-responders to a stimulus: verify dose/time; add orthogonal ligand within same axis (e.g., R848 for NF-κB) if needed.
- Safety: low-dose, short-duration perturbations; medical oversight for micro-challenges.

Milestones
- Months 0–6: finalize target list; build capture panels; benchmarking on cell lines and 20 healthy donors.
- Months 6–18: enroll n=150; complete assay and model lock; interim validation with influenza vaccination and OGTT.
- Months 18–30: enroll to n=300; prospective micro-challenges; 12-month follow-up; head-to-head PRS comparison.
- Months 30–36: clinical reporting prototype; health-system pilot.

Deliverables
- A validated, low-cost DARP assay kit (targeted RNA and ATAC capture panels).
- Open-source pipelines for ASE/ASCA calling and CPP construction.
- A clinician-facing conditional risk report with exposure rules.

Expected outcomes and impact
- A trigger-resolved penetrance map that converts static genetic risk into actionable, exposure-conditional guidance.
- Improved prediction of when and under what conditions disease programs activate, enabling targeted prevention and early intervention in routine clinical settings.

Title
GxS-Gate: A clinically translatable, SNP-by-state buffering index to resolve incomplete penetrance from a single blood draw

Atomic strategy
Penetrance is not fixed by genotype alone; it is gated by inducible cellular programs that can counteract or amplify risk-allele effects. Quantify, per individual, how strongly short-term, standardized immune stimuli pull cis-regulated transcripts back toward healthy setpoints despite risk genotypes. This “buffering capacity” is measured as allele-specific and pathway-level transcriptional responses from the same blood sample and used to reweight genetic risk for predicting who develops disease.

Hypothesis
Among carriers of disease-risk SNPs, individuals who remain unaffected exhibit stronger, stimulus-evoked cis-by-state buffering at risk-linked genes and pathways; a compact, interpretable buffering index built from these responses will outperform polygenic risk scores (PRS) alone in distinguishing affected from unaffected carriers and will point to druggable protective mechanisms.

Specific aims
1) Engineer a SNP-aware, state-responsive blood assay that jointly measures genotype-linked and cellular-state signals with moderate complexity.
2) Derive the GxS-Gate score: a per-person penetrance index integrating risk genotype with allele-specific and pathway response metrics under controlled stimuli.
3) Validate predictive performance and clinical interpretability in a carrier-enriched, case/unaffected cohort; map low-buffering mechanisms to actionable interventions.

Study design overview
- Population: Adults carrying established risk variants for an immune-mediated disease (e.g., HLA- and non-HLA loci in type 1 diabetes, IBD, or MS). Three groups: affected carriers (cases), age/sex-matched unaffected carriers (protected), and non-carrier controls (ancillary).
- Sample: One routine phlebotomy (6–10 mL). Whole blood is partitioned into four preloaded tubes: null, IFN-α, LPS, and TNF (TruCulture-style), incubated 0, 90, and 360 minutes at 37°C.
- Primary readout: SNP-aware targeted RNA-seq (800–1,200 genes) designed around GWAS/eQTL neighborhoods, capturing exons harboring informative transcribed SNPs to enable allele-specific expression (ASE) while quantifying pathway responses with UMIs for absolute counts.
- Genotype anchor: A 300–600 variant amplicon panel from the same draw (buffy coat DNA) covering sentinel risk SNPs and exonic tags used for ASE phasing; used to (a) confirm carrier status and (b) weight locus importance.
- Optional subset (mechanistic depth only): low-input ATAC-seq on pooled stimulated PBMCs for enhancer “readiness” at key loci (not required for clinical deployment).

Assay details (moderate complexity, clinical fit)
- Wet lab
  - Pre-filled stimulation tubes; 30–60 min hands-on per batch.
  - RNA extraction at each timepoint; targeted capture library with probe sets for: (i) cis-genes near risk loci with exonic SNPs, (ii) sentinel pathway reporters (IFN, TNF/NF-κB, IL-6/STAT3, oxidative stress/NRF2, autophagy, ER stress), (iii) cell composition markers.
  - UMI-based counting; 1–2 million reads per tube sufficient.
  - Amplicon genotyping in parallel; turnaround <48 hours.
- Bioinformatics (kept simple)
  - Demultiplex UMIs; estimate gene counts and ASE per target.
  - Deconvolve major blood cell fractions from the targeted panel.
  - Quality controls: stimulation efficacy signatures; replicate concordance.

Core metrics and modeling
- Locus-level Allelic Response Ratio (ARR): For a gene g with an informative transcribed SNP, ARRg,s = log2[(Alt/Ref)stim / (Alt/Ref)baseline] under stimulus s. Positive ARR counter to the known disease-risk eQTL direction indicates buffering.
- Pathway Response Slope (PRSlope): Stimulus-induced log-fold change for pathway reporter sets, adjusted for cell composition and batch.
- Gated Effect (GE) per locus: GEg = sign(eQTLrisk) × (−ARRg,any) aggregated across stimuli; >0 implies buffering against risk direction.
- Buffering Capacity Index (BCI): Weighted sum of GE across loci, with weights from locus effect sizes and tissue relevance; scaled 0–1.
- GxS-Gate score: Logistic model with three terms—(i) PRS, (ii) BCI, and (iii) key PRSlope terms capturing trans-buffers—with elastic net for stability. No deep learning; coefficients reported for interpretability.
- Output: Individual report with overall GxS-Gate (0–1 risk of progression), top buffered and unbuffered loci, and pathway knobs (e.g., “type I IFN low-buffered”).

Validation plan
- Discovery (n≈400 carriers; 200 cases, 200 unaffected ≥60 years or long follow-up without disease): Train elastic net; internal cross-validation; primary endpoint AUC improvement over PRS alone; secondary endpoints NRI, calibration, and decision-curve analysis.
- External test (n≈200 carriers from independent site): Locked-model evaluation.
- Longitudinal pilot (subset n≈100 autoantibody-positive, disease-free): Baseline GxS-Gate vs. 2–3 year conversion; time-to-event modeling.
- Mechanistic checks: In vitro augmentation (e.g., IFN-β priming, NRF2 activator, autophagy inducer) in PBMCs from low-BCI vs. high-BCI carriers to test reversibility of low-buffer signatures and sharpen causal interpretation.

Clinical translation
- Sample type: Standard venipuncture; room-temperature stimulation tubes compatible with outpatient clinics.
- Cost target: ~$150–$250 per patient all-in at scale (four tubes × targeted RNA-seq + amplicon genotyping).
- Turnaround: 48–72 hours; amenable to centralized lab workflow.
- Interpretability: Report highlights which protective programs are weak and nominate drug classes that upregulate them (e.g., JAK agonism of IFN signaling, NRF2 activators, autophagy enhancers), enabling preemptive trials in high-risk, low-BCI carriers.

Innovation beyond PRS
- Moves from static genotype to inducible genotype-by-state measurement in primary human cells.
- Uses ASE dynamics as a built-in, within-person instrument to read cis-regulatory buffering without needing large cohorts.
- Produces a mechanistically grounded, pathway-resolved penetrance index that is both predictive and prescriptive.

Milestones and deliverables (24 months)
- M6: Validated targeted panel and stimulation SOP; analytical pipeline v1.
- M12: Discovery cohort complete; interim AUC gain over PRS ≥0.10.
- M18: External validation; finalized GxS-Gate; locked coefficients and clinical report template.
- M24: Longitudinal pilot readout; shortlist of protective pathways with matched drug candidates for a prevention trial.

Risks and mitigations
- Limited ASE at some loci: Prioritize targets with informative exonic SNPs; use gene-level response and pathway buffering when ASE unavailable.
- Cell composition shifts confound signals: Include deconvolution markers; adjust models; optionally sort a small subset for sensitivity analysis.
- Disease non-immune contexts: Swap stimuli to disease-relevant cues (e.g., metabolic, hormonal) and re-target the panel to the appropriate tissue proxies.

Success criteria
- Statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement over PRS in distinguishing affected vs. unaffected carriers.
- Transparent, pathway-anchored outputs that nominate actionable protective mechanisms.
- A scalable assay and model suitable for prospective prevention trials in genetically at-risk populations.

Title: Allele-Specific Risk-Circuit Engagement (ARCE) to Resolve Penetrance and Reveal Natural Protection

Core hypothesis-goal (merged):
Disease emerges in genetic carriers when a small set of risk-variant enhancers in relevant blood-immune cells become engaged in state-specific contexts; resilient carriers avoid disease because protective trans-acting programs keep these risk circuits disengaged, even under common inflammatory stimuli. Measuring “which risk alleles are in use” (not just which are present) will both distinguish affected from resilient carriers and expose protective mechanisms that can be therapeutically mimicked.

Atomic strategy:
Quantify allele-specific enhancer engagement at fine-mapped risk loci—at baseline and after a brief, standardized ex vivo stimulus—then aggregate per-individual engagement into an interpretable Regulome Penetrance Score while mining anti-engagement programs as candidate protective levers.

Study design overview:
- Population:
  - Disease areas with accessible blood correlates (e.g., type 1 diabetes, IBD, CAD). 
  - Three groups per disease: (1) affected carriers, (2) resilient carriers (age ≥50 or disease-free past typical onset window despite carrying the same lead risk alleles/PRS), (3) non-carrier controls for reference.
  - N≈400 discovery (balanced across groups), N≈300 prospective validation.
- Sample and workflow:
  - 2 × 10 mL peripheral blood per participant → PBMC isolation.
  - Two conditions per donor: unstimulated and a 2-hour disease-relevant cytokine mix (e.g., IFN-γ + TNF-α ± IL-1β; disease-specific alternatives allowed for a second small panel without increasing complexity per subject).
  - Turnaround target: 48 hours from blood draw to preliminary scores.

Integrated assay platform (clinically practical):
- Capture-ATAC for risk loci (ARCE-Capture):
  - A hybridization capture panel (1,000–5,000 peaks) covering fine-mapped disease enhancers and their LD proxies.
  - Low-input ATAC-seq performed per condition; capture enriches for targeted open-chromatin fragments to boost depth at risk loci with 15–25M reads/library.
  - Built-in allele-specificity: reads spanning heterozygous SNPs provide allele-of-origin counts, directly integrating genotype and cellular state in one measurement.
- Targeted RNA panel (200–500 genes):
  - Modules downstream of risk circuits (inflammation, resolution, oxidative stress, lipid handling, regulatory TF targets).
  - Quantified via multiplexed targeted RNA (e.g., ligation-based or probe-based) from the same PBMC aliquots and conditions.
- Optional low-complexity cell-state control:
  - Either sort three major PBMC classes (T, B, monocytes) or apply robust deconvolution using ATAC/RNA markers embedded in panels; choose one to maintain moderate complexity.

Primary readouts and scores (interpretable):
- Per-locus Allelic Engagement Score (AES):
  - AES = log2(risk-allele ATAC reads / non-risk-allele ATAC reads), adjusted for total peak accessibility, mappability, and batch.
  - Defined at heterozygous loci; for homozygous risk/non-risk, use peak-level accessibility as a secondary proxy with lower weight.
- Stimulus Engagement Delta (SED):
  - Within-individual change in AES after stimulation; captures conditional penetrance windows.
- Regulome Penetrance Score (RPS):
  - A sparse, calibrated sum of locus-level AES/SED weighted by their association with case status in discovery.
  - Output includes the top contributing loci to preserve interpretability.
- Protective Program Index (PPI):
  - Module scores from the RNA panel that anti-correlate with AES/SED and with case status (e.g., NRF2-like oxidative stress buffering, cholesterol efflux, IL-10/TGF-β resolution, unfolded protein response tuning).
  - Each PPI reports its leading genes and putative upstream regulators (TF motifs enriched in disengaged risk enhancers).

Modeling and complexity control:
- Statistics: penalized logistic regression (group lasso) on AES/SED and RNA module scores; cell-type proportions as covariates when not sorted.
- Calibration: Platt scaling to yield absolute risk of near-term conversion for at-risk cohorts.
- Output: a one-page clinician-facing report listing RPS (0–100), top engaged risk circuits, and top protective modules with plain-language labels.
- Compute footprint: fits on a standard workstation; no deep models required.

Discovery of natural protection and therapeutic levers:
- Contrast resilient vs affected carriers matched by PRS and demographics to identify:
  - Loci with systematically lower AES/SED in resilient carriers (cis targets for engagement suppression).
  - RNA modules with higher PPI in resilient carriers (candidate trans protectors).
- Mechanistic inference:
  - Motif enrichment within disengaged risk enhancers to flag protective TFs.
  - Integrate lipid/metabolic module readouts to implicate targetable pathways (e.g., LXR/PPAR, glutathione metabolism).
- Functional validation (ex vivo):
  - Short-term perturbations (approved small molecules or cytokines) in PBMCs from affected carriers to attempt “resilience mimicry,” measuring reversal of AES/SED and PPI shifts.
  - CRISPRi/CRISPRa in donor-derived cells for top TFs/regulators (research-phase, not clinical) to confirm causality on engagement.

Prospective validation:
- Enroll at-risk carriers (e.g., first-degree relatives or high-PRS individuals) without disease at baseline.
- Test whether baseline RPS and PPI predict 2–3 year conversion independent of PRS, age, and clinical labs.
- Define actionable thresholds:
  - High RPS + low PPI → high vigilance and prevention trials.
  - Low RPS or high PPI → reassurance and reduced screening intensity.

Clinical translation plan:
- Feasibility: blood-based, two-condition assay; uses commodity sequencers and targeted panels.
- Cost target: <$300/sample at scale (one ATAC-capture + one targeted RNA per condition).
- Reporting: interpretable, locus- and module-level outputs; no black-box requirements.
- Integration: complements PRS; can guide enrollment and endpoint selection in prevention trials.

Milestones and success criteria:
- Year 1:
  - Build ARCE-Capture panel; pilot N=60 for technical reproducibility.
  - AES/SED technical CV <15%; inter-lab concordance established.
- Year 2:
  - Case–resilient discovery (N=400). Lock RPS/PPI model.
  - AUC ≥0.80 distinguishing affected vs resilient carriers matched on PRS.
  - Identify ≥3 reproducible protective modules and ≥5 disengaged sentinel loci.
- Year 3:
  - Prospective cohort (N=300). PPV/NPV improvement over PRS by ≥20% relative.
  - Ex vivo resilience mimicry: ≥30% median reduction in RPS after pathway-targeted perturbation in affected-carrier PBMCs.

Risk management:
- Limited heterozygosity at some loci:
  - Include LD proxies and peak-level proxies; hierarchical weights penalize weaker evidence.
- Cell-type confounding:
  - Prefer 3-way sorting in discovery; fixed deconvolution model in validation to keep clinical flow simple.
- Stimulus mis-specification:
  - Use one primary and one secondary stimulus per disease with fixed recipes; predefine success by SED informativeness.

What is novel beyond PRS:
- Direct, allele-specific measurement of state-conditional enhancer usage turns static genetic risk into a functional penetrance readout (RPS) and exposes endogenous protective programs (PPI) that can be mimicked, enabling a path from prediction to prevention.

Title
BRISC: Burst Regulation Instability in Single Cells as a clinically translatable predictor of penetrant disease risk

Unified hypothesis–goal–question
Among individuals carrying the same disease-risk SNPs, those who will manifest disease exhibit cell-state–specific instability in transcriptional bursting (abnormal burst frequency and/or size) in accessible blood immune cells. Can an individual-level “burst instability” profile, jointly conditioned on genotype and cell state, predict penetrant risk beyond polygenic risk scores?

Atomic strategy
Treat “burst control” as the phenotype. Instead of mean expression, estimate per-individual deviations in transcriptional burst parameters in defined blood cell states, and link these deviations to cis risk variants. Aggregate these deviations into an interpretable, cell-state–resolved risk score.

Study overview
- Population: Adults carrying known risk SNPs for a chosen disease class (e.g., autoimmune, neurodegenerative, cardiometabolic), including:
  - Penetrant carriers (cases) and resilient carriers (age- and ancestry-matched, no disease by follow-up).
  - Prospective cohort of new carriers for longitudinal validation.
- Sample: Peripheral blood, single time point at baseline; optional second draw (3–6 months) for stability checks.

Assay design (moderate-complexity, integrated genotype–state)
- Genotype: Low-pass whole-genome sequencing or dense SNP array with phasing (per individual).
- Single-cell transcriptome: 10x droplet scRNA-seq on PBMCs (target 20–30k cells/sample, UMIs), with a targeted enrichment add-on for:
  - Exonic SNPs in cis to risk loci to enable allele-aware UMI assignment.
  - A panel of 300–500 sentinel genes linked to risk loci (discovery-phase derived; see below).
- Optional discovery subset (n≈100 individuals): 10x Multiome (ATAC+RNA) to refine cell states and TF programs. Deployment phase uses scRNA targeted panel only.

Key quantitative phenotypes
- Burst frequency (kon proxy) and burst size (s proxy) per gene–cell state–individual inferred from UMI count distributions using a Poisson–beta (negative binomial) hierarchical model with empirical-Bayes shrinkage.
- Allele-specific bursting (ASB): For heterozygous exonic SNPs, allele-aware UMIs estimate cis effects on burst parameters.
- Variance/eXpression residuals: Fano-factor residuals and zero-inflation residuals after conditioning on mean and cell state.

Core metrics
- Burst Instability Index (BII): For each gene g in cell state c and individual i,
  BII(g,c,i) = standardized deviation of inferred kon and/or s from a reference distribution at matched mean and state, with shrinkage across individuals.
- Module BII: Aggregate BIIs over genes linked to the same cis-locus or regulon within a cell state.
- Individual-level BRISC score: Weighted sum of Module BIIs for modules mapped to that individual’s risk variants, with weights learned in training and constrained for sparsity and interpretability.

Cis linkage map (kept simple and interpretable)
- Link risk SNPs to sentinel genes using one or more of:
  - Fine-mapped cis-eQTL target genes in blood cell types.
  - Chromatin-to-gene links from the discovery Multiome subset (peak–gene co-variation within state).
- Lock the final sentinel panel and links before validation to prevent leakage.

Modeling pipeline (moderate computational burden)
1) Cell-state harmonization
   - Map PBMCs to canonical states (e.g., naive/memory T, monocyte subsets, B, NK, plasmablasts) using a compact reference and batch-correct with a lightweight latent model (e.g., scVI with small latent dimension).
2) Burst parameter inference
   - Fit a two-parameter NB per gene–state with individual-level random effects to estimate kon and s (and dispersion ϕ).
   - Compute BII as residual instability beyond mean-level effects and technical covariates (depth, ambient RNA).
3) Allelic integration
   - Assign allele-specific UMIs at informative SNPs to estimate ASB-kon and ASB-s in cis to risk variants.
4) Feature construction
   - Per individual: Module BIIs within each cell state for risk-linked modules; ASB features where available.
5) Predictor
   - Sparse logistic regression or monotone gradient-boosted trees with:
     - Inputs: Module BIIs, ASB features, cell-composition covariates, and PRS (as a baseline feature).
     - Outputs: Probability of disease manifestation among carriers; Shapley-style attributions by module and cell state.

Discovery → deployment path
- Discovery phase (n≈400 carriers: 200 penetrant, 200 resilient):
  - Whole-transcriptome scRNA-seq (+Multiome subset) to select sentinel genes/modules with the highest stable BII separation and robust ASB evidence.
- Deployment phase:
  - Targeted scRNA panel (300–500 genes + SNP enrichment) on 20–30k PBMCs/sample.
  - End-to-end cost goal: <$300/sample at scale; turnaround <7 days.

Validation plan
- Internal cross-validated performance within discovery cohort.
- Independent external cohort (n≈300–500 carriers) for locked model validation.
- Prospective longitudinal test (n≈500 carriers, 2–3 years):
  - Primary endpoint: incident disease or clinically relevant progression.
  - Metrics: AUROC, AUPRC, calibration slope, net reclassification improvement over PRS and clinical covariates.
- Stress-test robustness:
  - Repeat sampling in a 50-person subset after mild intercurrent events (e.g., vaccination) to quantify BII stability.
  - Sensitivity analyses excluding individuals with acute inflammation (CRP high).

Clinical translation and interpretability
- Report elements:
  - BRISC score (0–1) with calibrated risk strata.
  - Top 5 unstable modules and their dominant cell states (e.g., “IFN-response module in classical monocytes”).
  - Allelic evidence: loci with strongest ASB-burst effects supporting mechanistic plausibility.
- Actionability:
  - Enrollment enrichment for prevention trials.
  - Monitoring: individuals with high BRISC undergo repeat low-cost targeted assay annually.

Feasibility and complexity management
- One tube of blood; one droplet-based single-cell assay per draw; individual-level genotyping once.
- Computation: per-sample burst inference using moment-based initialization + small hierarchical fits; total runtime scaled linearly with genes and states.
- No reliance on complex time-lapse measurements; bursting inferred from cross-sectional UMI statistics with rigorous controls.

Confounders and mitigations
- Cell composition shifts: include composition covariates; compute BIIs within states; use compositional balance adjustments.
- Technical noise/dropout: UMI modeling, ambient-RNA correction, ERCC or internal controls; replicate libraries for a subset.
- Phasing/allelic assignment errors: require minimum allele-UMI counts; propagate uncertainty; ASB used as supporting evidence, not sole criterion.
- Batch effects: randomized processing; include batch as a random effect; anchored reference mapping.

Statistical power (order-of-magnitude targets)
- With 20–30k cells/sample and 300–500 genes across ~8–12 states, expect >100–300 observations per gene–state–individual.
- Discovery n≈400 yields >90% power to detect medium effect-size differences in BII modules (standardized Δ≥0.35) at FDR 5%, assuming modest inter-individual variance after shrinkage.

Milestones
- M1 (Months 0–6): Cohort assembly, assay standardization, pilot n=60 for BII reproducibility.
- M2 (Months 6–18): Discovery cohort complete; sentinel panel freeze; initial BRISC model.
- M3 (Months 18–30): External validation; refine clinical report.
- M4 (Months 30–48): Prospective longitudinal readout; health-economic analysis.

Deliverables
- Open (pre-registered) statistical analysis plan for BII/ASB inference.
- Locked sentinel gene panel and SNP enrichment design.
- BRISC software (burst inference + scoring), with per-module explanations.
- Validated, clinically translatable single-cell targeted assay workflow for penetrant risk prediction in carriers.

text:
Title
Dynamic Allelic Resilience Assay (DARA): predicting incomplete penetrance from stress-recovery kinetics in blood cells with integrated allele-specific readouts

Central hypothesis-question
If an individual’s regulatory feedback capacity is intact, their blood immune cells return to baseline quickly after a standardized, reversible stress. In carriers of disease-risk SNPs who will develop disease, the same stress exposes latent fragility: recovery is slower and allele-specific regulatory imbalances are amplified. Can brief ex vivo stress and short-timescale recovery measurements, integrated with allele-specific transcript signals from the same assay, predict which risk carriers will manifest disease?

Atomic strategy
Estimate each person’s “return-to-homeostasis” time constant from a small panel of sentinel pathways while simultaneously reading allele-specific expression at informative SNPs within those sentinel genes. Combine these into a single, interpretable Resilience Index that conditions recovery kinetics on cis-genetic dosage measured in the same molecules.

Study population and sample
- Sample type: fresh whole blood (10–20 mL), collected in standard tubes.
- Cell types: magnetically isolated CD14+ monocytes and CD4+ T cells (two major, robust PBMC subsets with distinct homeostatic programs).
- Target use-cases: any disease area with known risk variants and incomplete penetrance (e.g., autoimmune, neurodegenerative with peripheral immune signatures, cardiometabolic).

Standardized perturbation and timing
- Perturbation: 20 minutes heat-shock at 42°C followed by recovery at 37°C (proteostasis and general stress response with strong, reversible dynamics in blood cells).
- Timepoints: T0 (baseline), T1 (60 minutes into recovery), T2 (240 minutes into recovery).
- Rationale: three points are sufficient to estimate a single-exponential return-to-baseline constant while limiting complexity and cost.

Integrated measurement (simultaneous genotype and state)
- Assay: targeted UMI-based RNA sequencing using smMIP/AmpliSeq-style panels (200–300 genes).
  - Panel composition:
    1) Sentinel modules: heat-shock/proteostasis, unfolded protein response, oxidative stress, NF-κB/inflammation, glucocorticoid feedback, mitochondrial biogenesis, and cytoskeletal homeostasis (∼10–20 genes per module).
    2) Cell-state controls: housekeeping and activation markers.
    3) Allele-informative exonic/3′UTR SNPs: probes spanning common transcribed SNPs in sentinel genes, enriched for loci in LD with known risk variants.
- Output per gene per timepoint per cell type:
  - Total UMI counts → expression level.
  - Reference/alternate UMI counts at heterozygous positions → allele-specific expression (ASE).
- This yields cellular state and cis-genotype signals from the same molecules without a separate genotyping experiment. Optional: a low-cost SNP array can be added to expand genotype coverage, but the core classifier relies on in-panel ASE.

Primary features
- Kinetic recovery constants:
  - For each module m and cell type c, fit y(t) = y∞ + (y0 − y∞)e−t/τm,c from T0–T2 module scores; extract τm,c (time constant) and overshoot metrics.
- Dynamic ASE:
  - For each heterozygous SNP g in gene i: compute ASE(t) = log2(Alt/Ref) across T0–T2; extract ΔASE = ASE(T2) − ASE(T0) and slope sASE.
  - Interpretation: stress-unmasked cis-imbalance indicating fragile regulation at specific loci.
- Coupled features:
  - Gene-level coupling κi = correlation between expression recovery and ASE shift; flags loci where cis effects specifically dysregulate recovery.

Modeling framework (moderate complexity, interpretable)
- Resilience Index (R):
  - R = Σw(m,c)·τm,c + Σv(i)·|sASEi| + Σu(i)·|κi|,
  - with non-negative weights learned via L1-regularized logistic regression to predict disease status among risk-allele carriers.
- Two-stage training:
  1) Module discovery and weight shrinkage on a development set (N≈300–500).
  2) Locked model evaluated in a held-out set and external cohort.
- Outputs:
  - Individual probability of disease manifestation within a prespecified horizon.
  - Ranked contributions: top modules and loci driving risk (clinically interpretable).
- Complexity control:
  - Small gene panel, three timepoints, two cell types, closed-form τ estimation, sparse linear classifier.

Experimental workflow
1) Blood draw → PBMC isolation (Ficoll) → magnetic bead enrichment of CD14+ and CD4+ cells.
2) Perturbation (42°C, 20 min) → recovery at 37°C; harvest at T0, T1, T2.
3) RNA capture with targeted UMI panels in 96-well format; pooled library per patient, sequenced to ~2–3M reads per timepoint per cell type.
4) Bioinformatics (same-day):
   - UMI deduplication, expression quantification.
   - ASE calling on targeted SNPs with beta-binomial shrinkage for low counts.
   - Module scoring, τ estimation, ASE slopes, coupling κ.
   - Compute R and calibrated disease probability.
5) Turnaround: 48–72 hours from blood draw to report.

Validation plan
- Phase 1 (cross-sectional case-control within carriers):
  - Recruit carriers of the same risk variant(s) split into affected vs. unaffected (age/sex-matched).
  - Primary endpoint: AUC of DARA vs. PRS-only and vs. static transcriptomics; secondary: net reclassification improvement.
  - Mechanistic checks: affected > unaffected for τ in proteostasis/GR modules; increased |sASE| at sentinel genes proximal to risk loci.
- Phase 2 (prospective cohort of variant carriers):
  - Baseline DARA; follow for 2–5 years.
  - Endpoint: time-to-onset; Cox model with R as predictor, adjusted for age/sex/PRS.
  - Decision thresholds set by desired sensitivity/specificity; decision-curve analysis for clinical utility.

Clinical translatability
- Sample: routine venipuncture; no living cell reinfusion; biosafety level 2.
- Cost target: <$250 per patient (two cell types × three timepoints targeted RNA-seq).
- Scalability: 96/384-well automated library prep; single-instrument benchtop sequencers.
- Interpretability: report lists slowed-recovery modules and stress-unmasked ASE loci, with plain-language explanations.

Why this goes beyond PRS
- PRS estimates inherited load; DARA measures functional buffering capacity and cis-regulatory fragility unmasked by stress.
- The integrated allele-specific dynamic readout ties genotype to real-time regulatory failure in the same assay, not by static association.

Key risks and mitigations
- Low heterozygosity at targeted SNPs: design redundant probes per module; rely on τ features when ASE not available.
- Inter-individual variability in baseline activation: use within-sample normalization to T0; include housekeeping anchors.
- Stress dose miscalibration: run a short pilot to standardize heat-shock intensity maximizing dynamic range without cytotoxicity; monitor viability and immediate-early markers.
- Disease specificity: while the stress is generic, module-level signatures and ASE coupling provide disease-relevant stratification; optional addition of a second orthogonal stress (e.g., dexamethasone pulse) in later phases if needed.

Milestones and deliverables
- Month 0–6: finalize sentinel gene panel with allele-informative sites; assay optimization; SOPs.
- Month 6–18: Phase 1 study in two diseases; locked classifier; technical/clinical validation report.
- Month 18–36: Prospective cohort interim analysis; health-economic model; CLIA-ready protocol.

Success criterion
A locked, low-cost assay that, among carriers of known risk variants, improves prediction of disease manifestation over PRS by ≥0.10 AUC and provides actionable, interpretable module/locus-level insights grounded in dynamic recovery and allele-specific regulation.
