text:
Title
KAPS (Keloid-Activated Pericellular Softening): a single-application, topical, ECM-tethered polymer brush that forms only in keloid tissue to mechanically insulate adipocytes and prevent their myofibroblast-like transition

Atomic hypothesis
If we convert the pathologically stiff, LOX-crosslinked keloid ECM immediately surrounding adipocytes into a locally soft, non-adhesive interface, we will block integrin/YAP–TAZ/TGF-β tension signaling that drives adipocyte dedifferentiation to myofibroblast-like cells, while leaving normal skin adipocytes unaffected because the polymer interface will not form at sufficient density in non-keloid ECM.

Therapeutic concept (single insight implemented)
Exploit the high density of LOX-generated collagen aldehydes (allysine) and elevated matrix stiffness unique to keloids to template in situ formation of a nanometric, tethered polymer brush (“mechanical cushion”) on pericellular collagen. The brush only arises when anchoring sites exceed a threshold density—achievable in keloids but not in normal skin—thereby specifically lowering the effective modulus and integrin clustering at adipocyte–ECM contacts within lesions.

Formulation design (topical, single administration, sustained effect)
- Active material: AO-Brush macromer, a high–grafting-density-capable, aminooxy-terminated bottlebrush polymer (PEG-based backbone with short, zwitterionic side chains).
- Selective anchoring chemistry: rapid, catalyst-free oxime ligation of aminooxy end groups to LOX-derived allysine on collagen/elastin. High allysine density in keloid ECM yields high tethering density; normal skin provides insufficient sites, preventing brush formation.
- Function-on-threshold: above a grafting density set by keloid crosslink abundance, chains enter the polymer-brush regime, creating a soft, non-fouling, entropic repulsion layer (tens of nanometers) that reduces focal adhesion maturation and force transmission.
- Delivery: a single-use, dissolvable microneedle patch or spreadable film-forming gel that localizes the AO-Brush macromer to superficial/mid-dermal keloid ECM; no systemic exposure.
- Durability: oxime bonds provide months-scale residence; slow hydrolysis ensures eventual resorption. The brush maintains effect without repeated dosing.
- Inertness: no receptor agonists/antagonists; preserves lipid metabolism and regenerative signaling of adipocytes outside keloids.

Mechanism of action
- Physical: lowers local effective stiffness and ligand accessibility at the adipocyte surface; disrupts integrin clustering and catch-bond maturation under high tension.
- Biochemical consequence: reduces mechanical activation of latent TGF-β (via αv integrins), suppresses YAP/TAZ nuclear localization, and prevents induction of ACTA2, COL1A1, and other myofibroblast programs in adipocyte-derived cells.
- Functional preservation: maintains PPARγ-driven adipocyte identity, insulin responsiveness, and adipokine secretion in normal skin, where no brush forms.

Selectivity and safety
- Microenvironment selectivity: requires pathologic allysine site density to achieve brush regime; inert coil state elsewhere is cleared without appreciable ECM coating.
- Spatial specificity: topical, ECM-tethered localization limits diffusion; absence of pharmacologic pathway blockers minimizes off-target metabolic effects.
- Immunocompatibility: PEG/zwitterionic brushes reduce protein adsorption and immune activation.

Research plan

Aim 1: Validate keloid-selective anchoring and brush formation
- Human tissue slices (keloid versus matched normal skin): apply fluorescent AO-Brush; quantify covalent tethering (carbonyl-reactive dye competition), brush formation (FRAP mobility, nanoscale force mapping by AFM).
- Threshold behavior: correlate local allysine density with grafting density and brush signatures; define the minimal site density required for brush regime.

Aim 2: Demonstrate prevention of adipocyte dedifferentiation in keloid-like mechanics
- 3D co-cultures of human dermal adipocytes on tunable-collagen matrices that model keloid versus normal stiffness and crosslinking: treat with AO-Brush.
- Readouts: TGF-β activation reporters; YAP/TAZ nuclear:cytoplasmic ratio; α-SMA fiber formation; collagen I deposition; adipocyte identity markers (PPARγ, adiponectin), insulin-stimulated glucose uptake and lipolysis assays.
- Single-dose durability: repeat measures over weeks to establish sustained mechanoprotection.

Aim 3: Ex vivo and in vivo proof-of-concept
- Ex vivo human keloid organ culture: single topical application; track adipocyte lineage fate (lipid droplet retention; loss/gain of myofibroblast markers), pericellular stiffness mapping, and TGF-β bioactivity.
- In vivo xenograft model of human keloid: single application via microneedle patch; endpoints include dWAT preservation, reduced myofibroblast burden, and mechanical relaxation at the adipocyte interface without altering normal dermis.

Milestones and success criteria
- Keloid-selective tethering >10× versus normal skin and confirmed brush formation only in keloid ECM.
- ≥70% reduction in adipocyte-to-myofibroblast transition markers under profibrotic cues, with unchanged adipocyte metabolic function in normal-skin conditions.
- Single application retains effect for ≥8 weeks in organ culture/xenograft with no adverse local inflammation.

Risk assessment and mitigations
- Variability in allysine accessibility: incorporate short, flexible linkers to improve reach; adjust aminooxy valency to maintain thresholding without off-target anchoring.
- Excess softening at lesion margins: dose-ranging studies to tune grafting density; use competitive quenchers to cap overshoot if needed.
- Clearance in low-allysine regions: intended; confirms microenvironmental safety.

Translational considerations
- Materials: PEG and zwitterionic monomers with established biocompatibility; oxime ligation widely used in biomaterials.
- Manufacturing: solvent-free macromer synthesis and sterile microneedle/gel processing.
- Regulatory path: device–drug borderline leaning toward device-like biomaterial with local action, facilitating early safety evaluation.

Expected outcome
A first-in-class, microenvironment-gated, purely physical therapeutic that prevents adipocyte dedifferentiation and myofibroblast-like transition inside keloid lesions after a single topical administration, while preserving the metabolic and regenerative roles of normal skin adipocytes elsewhere.

label: elements_bypass
text:
Title
LOX-triggered, compliance-restoring in situ hydrogel to block adipocyte-to–myofibroblast transition selectively within keloid microenvironments

Central Hypothesis
Spontaneous keloid regression occurs when local adipocyte niches transiently normalize ECM crosslinking and stiffness, preventing adipocyte dedifferentiation. A topical material that self-assembles only in the LOX-high, stiff, acidic niche of keloid tissue to create a soft, compliant interpenetrating network will reproduce this protective state and durably block adipocyte-to–myofibroblast transition while sparing normal skin.

Atomic Strategy (single conceptual insight)
Exploit the keloid-specific mechano-enzymatic signature—elevated lysyl oxidase (LOX)–driven collagen crosslinking and high stiffness—to trigger in situ formation of a soft hydrogel that diverts LOX activity away from native ECM and mechanically “re-niches” adipocytes, thereby preserving adipocyte identity without direct pathway inhibition.

Specific Aims
1) Identify protective microenvironments in spontaneously regressing keloids and define their mechano-enzymatic phenotype (LOX activity, crosslink density, modulus, pH/lactate).
2) Engineer a LOX-activated dual-precursor topical that polymerizes only in keloid tissue to form a compliant, long-lived hydrogel (0.5–2 kPa) interpenetrating the upper dermis/dWAT.
3) Demonstrate selective blockade of adipocyte dedifferentiation and myofibroblast-like transition in human keloid organoids and in a keloid xenograft model after single administration.

Therapeutic Design
- Trigger logic (keloid selectivity):
  - Primary trigger: extracellular LOX abundance and activity.
  - Secondary gating: microacidic pH (≈6.5–6.8) characteristic of keloid tissue to unmask reactive groups.
- Precursors (topical, two-component, admixed on-tissue):
  - Precursor A: PEG8–graft–poly(ε-lysine) (PEG8-PLL), 40–80 kDa; LOX substrate segments provide ε-amine sites that LOX oxidatively deaminates to allysine (aldehydes).
  - Precursor B: aminooxy–hyaluronan (AO-HA), 200–500 kDa; aminooxy groups are pH-masked with acid-labile protecting groups that deprotect at pH ≤6.8.
- Assembly mechanism:
  - In LOX-high niches, lysine residues on Precursor A are converted to aldehydes; deprotected aminooxy groups on Precursor B undergo oxime ligation with the newly formed aldehydes, rapidly forming an interpenetrating network (IPN).
  - Self-limiting, spatially confined gelation occurs only where LOX activity and low pH co-localize; negligible assembly in normal skin (low LOX, neutral pH).
- Functional phenotype:
  - Target storage modulus: 0.5–2 kPa (below YAP/TAZ activation threshold), tuned by A:B ratio.
  - The IPN intercalates between collagen bundles, reduces effective fiber alignment/tension, and acts as a “mechanical sink,” disrupting mechanotransduction cues that drive adipocyte dedifferentiation.
  - By serving as a preferential LOX substrate field and sterically shielding collagen, the gel diverts crosslinking away from native ECM, attenuating further stiffening without systemic enzyme inhibition.
- Persistence and clearance:
  - Oxime bonds provide multiweek stability; hyaluronan enables endogenous hyaluronidase-mediated clearance over 6–10 weeks.
  - Degradation products (PEG, HA, short peptides) are biocompatible.

Formulation and Single-Administration Topical Delivery
- Format: dissolvable, two-compartment microneedle patch (MN) delivering lyophilized Precursors A and B into the papillary/upper reticular dermis over keloid and margins.
- Single 30–60 min wear: upon insertion, interstitial fluid rehydrates depots; precursors diffuse millimeters; LOX/pH triggers in situ IPN formation. Patch is removed; gel persists 6–10 weeks, covering the high-risk window for adipocyte fate switching.
- No chronic reapplication; re-dose only if stiffness or LOX activity re-emerges after natural degradation.

Selectivity and Preservation of Normal Adipocyte Function
- Spatial: activation requires co-occurrence of high LOX and acidic pH—rare in normal skin—minimizing gelation outside keloid.
- Mechanistic: no direct modulation of PPARγ/TGF-β/Wnt; preserves metabolic/regenerative programs of adipocytes.
- Mechanical: restored niche compliance supports adipocyte lipid handling and insulin responsiveness.

Research Plan

Aim 1: Natural experiment mapping in spontaneous regression
- Cohort: banked/regressing vs persistent human keloids; fresh biopsies where available.
- Measurements:
  - LOX/LOXL2 activity mapping (activity probes), collagen crosslink ratios (HP/LP, pyridinoline), AFM nanoindentation (modulus), SHG fiber alignment, micro-pH/lactate by fluorescent sensors.
  - Adipocyte lineage fate markers: PPARγ, adiponectin, PLIN1; myofibroblast markers: α-SMA, COL1A1; YAP/TAZ localization.
- Outcome: define thresholds for LOX activity and modulus that correlate with preserved adipocyte identity; parameterize gel design targets.

Aim 2: Material engineering and validation
- Synthesis/characterization:
  - Precursor A (PEG8-PLL): degree of substitution, LOX kinetics (kcat/Km vs collagen telopeptides), aldehyde yield per kDa.
  - Precursor B (AO-HA): deprotection pKa and half-time; oxime formation kinetics at pH 6.6–7.4.
  - Rheology: in situ gelation profiles under graded LOX/pH; final G’ tuning to 0.5–2 kPa.
  - Selectivity: negligible gelation at physiologic pH 7.4 with low LOX.
- Ex vivo human tissue penetration: fluorescently labeled A/B in keloid vs normal skin explants; depth and confinement.

Aim 3: Functional efficacy (ex vivo and in vivo)
- Human keloid organoids with dWAT/dermal adipocyte co-culture:
  - Conditions: untreated, vehicle, A-only, B-only, A+B under LOX-high/pH 6.6 vs LOX-low/pH 7.4.
  - Readouts (days 3–28): adipocyte morphology (lipid droplet size), lineage tracing, α-SMA+ cells derived from adipocytes, YAP/TAZ nuclear fraction, ECM stiffness, collagen alignment.
  - Metabolic assays: insulin-stimulated glucose uptake, lipolysis/lipogenesis, adiponectin/leptin secretion.
- Xenograft model (human keloid implants in immunodeficient mice):
  - Single MN administration over graft; longitudinal ultrasound elastography and microdialysis (lactate).
  - Endpoints (week 6–10): graft thickness, modulus (AFM), crosslink density, α-SMA area fraction, adipocyte marker retention, off-target effects in adjacent normal skin.

Readouts, Milestones, and Go/No-Go Criteria
- M1: LOX/modulus thresholds from Aim 1 define a design window (e.g., LOX activity ≥X a.u.; modulus ≥5 kPa) and correlate with adipocyte preservation in regressing sites.
- M2: In situ gelation only under LOX≥X and pH≤6.8; final G’ 0.5–2 kPa; diffusion-limited spread ≤3 mm from keloid border.
- M3: ≥60% reduction in adipocyte-to–α-SMA transition vs vehicle in organoids; adipocyte metabolic function within 90–110% of baseline.
- M4: In vivo: ≥30% reduction in graft modulus and thickness; ≥50% decrease in collagen fiber alignment index; no gel in adjacent normal skin; no impairment of wound re-epithelialization.

Risk and Mitigation
- Insufficient selectivity if LOX elevates in normal wounds: tighten pH gate; add lactate-responsive boronate crosslinks that strengthen only when lactate >10 mM.
- Excess softness destabilizing dermis: cap minimum G’ at 0.5 kPa and limit gel volume via MN dosing maps.
- Incomplete persistence: increase AO density or introduce secondary reversible hydrophobic associations to extend half-life without increasing modulus.
- Immunogenicity: use endotoxin-free synthetic blocks; monitor mast cell activation; pivot to zwitterionic backbones if needed.

Regulatory and Manufacturability
- Components (PEG, HA, poly(ε-lysine)) with established safety; solvent-free lyophilized MN fabrication; room-temperature stable cassettes.

Expected Outcomes and Impact
- Proof that reproducing the regressing-keloid mechano-enzymatic state—rather than pathway blockade—prevents adipocyte dedifferentiation and myofibroblast emergence.
- A first-in-class, single-application, microenvironment-activated topical that selectively “softens” keloids from within, preserves normal adipocyte metabolic/regenerative function, and reduces recurrence risk without systemic exposure.

Definition of Success
Within 24 months, demonstrate selective in situ gelation in human keloid tissue, sustained modulus normalization for ≥6 weeks after one administration, and ≥50% reduction of adipocyte-derived myofibroblasts with preserved adipocyte metabolism and no measurable impact on adjacent normal skin.

label: elements_bypass
text:
Title: AdipoLock-Switch: A stiffness-gated, adipocyte-restricted genetic switch that locks dermal adipocytes against myofibroblast transition in keloid-prone wounds via a single topical microneedle dose

Central hypothesis
- During early keloid initiation, dermal adipocytes at the wound edge experience pathological matrix stiffness that elevates YAP/TAZ activity and transiently decommissions PPARγ super-enhancers, creating an “unlocked” plastic state that permits myofibroblast-like transition. An adipocyte-intrinsic gene switch that turns on only under high YAP/TAZ (i.e., high stiffness) and reinforces PPARγ enhancer occupancy will relock adipocyte identity in situ, preventing keloid formation without perturbing normal adipocyte metabolism elsewhere.

Atomic strategy
- Encode a mechano-AND-adipocyte gene circuit on a non-integrating minicircle that expresses a short-lived “PPARγ coactivator microprotein clamp” only when (1) local stiffness drives TEAD/YAP transcriptional activity and (2) the cell is an adipocyte, thereby locking identity precisely where the keloid microenvironment emerges.

Specific aims
1) Map the adipocyte “unlocking window” at keloid-prone wound edges and calibrate a TEAD-threshold sensor that reports pathological stiffness before collagenous nodules are established.
2) Engineer and validate AdipoLock-Switch: a dual-input promoter that requires TEAD activity AND adipocyte identity to express a tunable, nucleus-targeted microprotein that stabilizes PPARγ-driven chromatin programs while remaining metabolically neutral.
3) Achieve single-dose, weeks-long protection via a topical, enzyme-anchoring microneedle patch that localizes the minicircle cargo to the dermal white adipose tissue (dWAT) at wound margins.

Mechanistic rationale
- Pathological stiffness activates YAP/TAZ and MRTF-A, which antagonize PPARγ transcriptional residency at adipocyte identity enhancers. Preventing this displacement specifically when stiffness is high should keep adipocytes locked, blocking the adipocyte-to-myofibroblast trajectory that seeds keloid overgrowth.
- Restricting the effector to adipocytes avoids interfering with fibroblast contractility needed for normal closure and preserves adipocyte metabolic functions.

Therapeutic design

A. Sensing and logic
- Mechanical input (Sensor 1): A compact synthetic promoter with multimerized TEAD-binding elements (8xTEAD) placed upstream of a minimal promoter provides graded activation proportional to YAP/TAZ nuclear activity. The promoter is tuned ex vivo to activate only at elastic moduli characteristic of keloid-precursor stroma.
- Cell-identity input (Sensor 2): An adipocyte-restricted gate using a minimal ADIPOQ/PPARG2 enhancer cassette plus intronic enhancer elements ensures transcription only in mature dWAT adipocytes.
- AND gate implementation: Split transcription factor strategy. TEAD-driven half expresses Gal4-VP16; adipocyte enhancer drives a Gal4-responsive minimal promoter (UASx5) controlling the effector OR, alternatively, a two-promoter intersection where the effector open reading frame (ORF) is split and reconstituted by split inteins, each half under one sensor.

B. Effector (“PPARγ coactivator microprotein clamp”)
- A 9–12 kDa, nucleus-localized, PEST-tagged microprotein containing tandem LXXLL motifs from MED1/PGC1α (2–3 repeats) fused to a weak activation domain. Function: increase PPARγ residency at adipocyte identity super-enhancers without supraphysiologic lipogenesis.
- Built-in metabolic neutrality: (i) weak activation domain to avoid hyperlipogenesis; (ii) PEST degron for rapid turnover when Sensor 1 falls below threshold (i.e., when stiffness normalizes); (iii) 3’ UTR miRNA target sites (miR-21/143/145 logic) to minimize expression in fibroblasts/smooth muscle–like cells even if cargo leaks.

C. Topical single-dose delivery
- Format: Dissolvable hyaluronic acid microneedle patch that deposits (i) adipocyte-tropic lipid–minicircle nanocomplexes into upper dWAT and (ii) a TG2-reactive anchoring hydrogel precursor.
- Nanocomplex: Cholesterol- and oleic-acid–decorated, CD36-targeting lipid nanoparticles complexed with CpG-depleted minicircle DNA (≤3 kb). This biases uptake to adipocytes, which highly express CD36 and fatty-acid transport machinery.
- On-tissue anchoring: A gelatin–hyaluronan hydrogel bearing TG2-reactive glutamine/lysine motifs rapidly crosslinks in the keloid-prone wound bed where transglutaminase-2 is elevated, creating a local depot that retains nanoparticles at the edge-zone. This leverages a keloid-specific enzymatic microenvironment to extend exposure from a single application.
- Dosing kinetics: Minicircle expression window 4–8 weeks to span the high-risk remodeling phase; hydrogel degradation timed to normal remodeling completion.

Selectivity features
- Environmental: Activation requires pathological stiffness (TEAD-high), absent in normal wounds/skin.
- Cellular: Adipocyte enhancer restriction plus CD36-targeted uptake.
- Temporal: Effector degrades quickly when stiffness normalizes, minimizing long-term perturbation.
- Spatial: TG2-anchored depot localizes to keloid-prone edges; topical microneedles confine delivery to the wound site.

Preservation of adipocyte metabolic and regenerative functions
- Effector is a partial coactivator clamp tuned to restore baseline adipocyte identity programs (PLIN1, ADIPOQ, CEBPA) without driving pathological lipid accumulation; insulin-stimulated glucose uptake and lipolysis rhythms are assayed to confirm neutrality.
- No global inhibition of contractility or respiration; fibroblast function is unaltered because the circuit is silent in non-adipocytes.

Research plan

Aim 1: Identify the unlocking window and calibrate Sensor 1
- Model: Ex vivo human skin wound healing system seeded with lineage-traced human dWAT adipocytes; orthogonal validation in a mechanical-loading human skin xenograft model.
- Readouts: Time-resolved scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq of dWAT cells across days 1–28 post-injury to map PPARγ enhancer decommissioning, YAP/TAZ target induction, and ACTA2 trajectory. Parallel AFM stiffness mapping.
- Calibration: Transfect TEAD-luc reporters into adipocytes embedded in tunable polyacrylamide gels to set the TEAD element copy number and minimal promoter for a stiffness activation threshold matching pre-keloid moduli.

Aim 2: Build and validate AdipoLock-Switch
- Construct: Minicircles encoding the AND gate and microprotein variants (1x vs 3x LXXLL; different PEST strengths).
- In vitro screens: Human adipocytes on soft vs stiff matrices ± TGF-β. Endpoints: PPARγ ChIP-seq occupancy, enhancer H3K27ac, adipocyte markers (ADIPOQ, PLIN1), myofibroblast markers (ACTA2, TAGLN, COL1A1), and mitochondrial respiration/lipolysis to ensure metabolic neutrality.
- Specificity: Co-culture with dermal fibroblasts and keratinocytes; include miRNA-target–safety elements; off-target expression assessed by reporter fusions and single-cell transcriptomics.

Aim 3: Single-dose topical delivery and efficacy
- Patch engineering: Optimize microneedle length for upper dWAT deposition; TG2-anchoring kinetics; nanoparticle size/ligand density for CD36-mediated uptake.
- In vivo efficacy: Apply a single patch at day 3 post-injury (predicted unlocking onset). Outcomes at weeks 2–8: (i) keloid thickness/volume (ultrasound), (ii) collagen architecture (SHG imaging), (iii) dWAT integrity (PLIN1 area, adipocyte size distribution), (iv) myofibroblast burden (αSMA+ cells), (v) stiffness normalization (AFM), and (vi) circuit activity (reporter).
- Safety: Local and systemic cytokines; glucose/insulin tolerance surrogates; lipid panels; wound tensile strength.

Milestones and success criteria
- Sensor calibration achieves >10-fold dynamic range between keloid-like vs normal stiffness.
- Effector restores PPARγ occupancy and blocks ACTA2 induction in ≥80% of adipocytes on stiff matrices, with ≤10% change in basal lipogenesis or insulin responsiveness.
- Single-dose patch reduces keloid-like lesion burden ≥50% and preserves dWAT morphology vs control, without impairing re-epithelialization or tensile strength.

Risk mitigation
- If TEAD thresholding is leaky, add a third post-transcriptional gate using a mechanically induced miRNA sensor (e.g., miR-21 high in fibrotic zones) via toehold switches.
- If metabolic neutrality is compromised, swap effector to a minimal KLF15 microprotein or SUMOylation-biased PPARγ clamp that favors identity over lipogenesis.
- If CD36 targeting is insufficient, incorporate adipocyte-binding peptide ligands (e.g., prohibitin-targeting) on the nanoparticle corona.

Translational path
- The components (hyaluronic microneedles, minicircle DNA, lipid nanoparticles) have precedents for topical use; the novelty lies in the mechano-AND-adipocyte logic and microprotein clamp.
- First-in-human use case: prophylactic application at high-risk surgical wound edges (e.g., keloid-prone patients) as a single-use patch during dressing change.

Expected impact
- Converts keloid management from reactive scar reduction to proactive identity locking of adipocytes exactly when and where they become permissive to fibrotic transition, while preserving normal adipocyte metabolic and regenerative functions elsewhere.

Project title
Mechano-AND “Clutch Lock” for Keloids: a single-dose, topical, tri-input–gated mechanocovalent stapling of adipocyte talin to permanently block myofibroblast-like transition

Atomic strategy
Convert the three defining keloid cues—hypoxia, inflammatory protease activity, and pathological tensile strain/stiffness—into a one-time, adipocyte-specific mechanocovalent “clutch lock” of talin at integrin–actin junctions, making adipocytes mechanically deaf to keloid forces while preserving their metabolic and regenerative functions.

Hypothesis-and-goal (merged)
If a topical therapeutic installs a permanent, tension-thresholded staple in adipocyte talin only when hypoxia, inflammation, and high mechanical strain co-occur, then adipocytes within keloids will resist dedifferentiation into myofibroblast-like cells without affecting normal skin adipocytes that never present the full triad.

Therapeutic concept
- Core mechanism: Irreversible, intramolecular “stapling” of talin rod domains to prevent pathologic unfolding and focal-adhesion maturation. This reduces YAP/TAZ and MRTF-driven contractile reprogramming while leaving basal adipocyte signaling sufficient for lipolysis, endocrine secretion, and progenitor renewal.
- Format: A single-application topical hydrogel/patch delivering Tri-AND mechanochemical prodrug nanoparticles (Tri-AND MPNs) that home to dermal adipocytes and execute an AND gate before exposing a talin-stapling chemistry.
- Selective targeting: Adipocyte-preferring surface ligands to bias uptake to dermal adipocytes residing in keloid tissue.

Tri-AND selectivity gate (pathology-as-key design)
- Hypoxia gate: A hypoxia-reduced molecular mask must be removed by low-O2 enzymatic reduction before any reactivity is possible.
- Inflammation gate: A protease-cleavable tether (tuned to keloid-associated protease spectrum) must be cut to free the pro-stapler.
- Mechanics gate: A membrane-/cytoskeleton-tension–activated mechanophore must be strained beyond a threshold achievable only within stiff, stretched keloid matrices; this fracture unmasks the final reactive handle. All three gates must be satisfied to reveal the active stapler.
- Optional protein-guided precision: A catalysis-dead, talin-binding protein adaptor that undergoes conformational opening only after the three inputs, positioning the stapler near talin without activity in normal tissue. This satisfies tri-input protein logic without gene delivery.

Permanence and memory
- One-time event: Once activated, the stapler forms covalent intramolecular links within talin, lowering force transduction gain for the lifespan of the protein and through renewal cycles via reduced positive-feedback signaling that otherwise reinforces myofibroblast identity. Repeated unfolding is prevented, creating a durable “mechanical memory” of the protected state.
- Network inertia: By chronically blunting high-gain mechanotransduction, adipocyte identity circuits (PPARγ-centered) maintain dominance without continuous pharmacologic drive.

Why normal adipocytes are preserved
- Contextual selectivity: Normal skin lacks concurrent deep hypoxia, high inflammatory proteases, and supraphysiologic tension; the stapler remains masked.
- Functional sparing: Adipocytes rely weakly on large, mature focal adhesions for core metabolism; partial talin locking reduces pathological reinforcement but retains sufficient adhesion for viability and tissue homeostasis.
- Spatial bias: Topical residence and adipocyte-targeting ligands limit exposure to off-target cells.

Topical delivery design
- Shear-thinning hydrogel/adhesive patch that deposits Tri-AND MPNs across the keloid surface and upper dermis, then self-quenches. No systemic exposure required.
- Single administration: Formulation tuned for local residency long enough to encounter tri-cue windows typical of keloid tissue, then clear inertly.

Validation plan (high-level)
- Mechanistic confirmation: In human adipocyte–ECM constructs with tunable stiffness, hypoxia, and cytokines, show tri-input dependence for talin stapling, reduced talin unfolding events under force, and suppressed YAP/TAZ nuclear localization.
- Selectivity: Demonstrate no activation under any single or dual cue, and no activation in normal skin explants.
- Function preservation: Verify maintained adipocyte lipid handling, adipokine secretion, mitochondrial respiration, and capacity to re-enter adipogenesis after injury signals.
- Phenotypic efficacy: In human keloid explants and relevant scar models, show durable reduction of adipocyte-to-myofibroblast transition markers (e.g., ACTA2, COL1A1 upregulation suppression), reduced traction forces, and improved tissue biomechanics after single dosing.
- Safety: Local histology, barrier integrity, nociception, pigmentation, and immune profiling to exclude adverse remodeling.

Risk points and mitigations
- Insufficient tri-input exclusivity: Increase orthogonality by adding a lactate-threshold cofactor or ROS-scavenging decoy that raises activation bar without altering the atomic mechanism.
- Over-suppression of adhesion: Engineer self-limiting staple density via competitive nonreactive binders to cap maximal talin modification.
- Heterogeneity in keloid microenvironments: Formulate MPNs with staggered activation thresholds to capture spatial gradients while retaining AND logic.

Readouts for success
- Strict AND gating fidelity in vitro and ex vivo.
- Single-dose, months-long suppression of adipocyte dedifferentiation within keloid tissue with preserved adipocyte metabolic function in adjacent normal skin.
- No impairment of wound repair in non-keloid skin.

Deliverable
A first-in-class, single-application, topical “mechanical memory” therapy that immobilizes the adipocyte mechanotransduction clutch only where keloid pathologic cues co-exist, durably preventing myofibroblast-like transition while sparing normal tissue function.

Title
PeriShield-LOX: A LOX-gated, perilesional “signal-sponge” mesh that armors skin adipocyte precursors and blocks myofibroblast-like transition at keloid margins after a single topical administration

Central hypothesis
Keloid margins are enriched for lysyl oxidase (LOX) activity, stiffness, protease activity, acidity, lactate, and oxidative stress. Harnessing this pathological signature to in situ assemble a long-lived, ECM-anchored sequestration mesh around perilesional adipocyte precursors will (i) catalytically capture keloid-derived profibrotic signals and extracellular vesicles (EVs), (ii) dampen mechanotransduction to YAP/TAZ, and (iii) provide microdosed, locally gated PPARγ support—thereby preventing adipocyte dedifferentiation/myofibroblast-like transition (AMT) while preserving normal adipocyte metabolic and regenerative functions.

Atomic strategy
Exploit elevated LOX activity and stiffness at the keloid perimeter to covalently anchor and crosslink a multifunctional polymer “armor” selectively in the diseased microenvironment; the armor converts resident perilesional preadipocytes into sentinel cleanup crews that sequester and neutralize keloid-emitted drivers of AMT and reinforce adipocyte identity.

Specific aims
1) Build a LOX-activated, ECM-anchoring topical mesh that forms only at keloid margins and persists for months.
2) Encode selective capture/neutralization of keloid-derived TGF-β family ligands and EVs within the mesh without perturbing homeostatic signaling in normal skin.
3) Deliver a mechano/enzymatically uncaged microdose of PPARγ agonism to perilesional adipocyte precursors to resist AMT, with no systemic metabolic impact.
4) Demonstrate, in human-relevant models, sustained blockade of AMT and prevention of keloid radial expansion while preserving adipocyte regenerative function.

Therapeutic design and formulation
- Topical format: a single-use dissolving microneedle patch (≤600 μm) that deposits two-component precursors circumferentially around the keloid (perimeter ring application).
- Component A: HA-PeriArmor polymer
  - Backbone: hyaluronic acid (50–150 kDa) bearing (i) catechol (DOPA) for wet adhesion and frictional damping, (ii) aminooxy groups for oxime ligation to allysine, and (iii) latent heparan-sulfate mimetic brushes (sulfated styrene/allyl glycosides) for multivalent growth-factor binding.
  - Targeting/anchoring: collagen-binding peptide (CBP) and elastin-binding peptide to concentrate at dense, stiff ECM.
  - Logic-gated capture: masked aptamer mix (anti-TGF-β1/3 LAP complexes; anti-CTGF; anti-CD63/CD81 EV markers) shielded by ROS- and acidity-labile boronate and hydrazone caps so unmasking occurs only in keloid-like ROS/pH.
- Component B: Mechano-PPARγ nanodepots
  - Core: lipidoid nanoparticles displaying a PDGFRα-homing peptide to bias uptake by dermal adipocyte precursors.
  - Cargo: ultra-low-dose PPARγ agonist (e.g., rosiglitazone analog) caged via an MMP2/9-cleavable linker and tethered to the nanoparticle with a stiffness-burst mechanophore shell (shear above ~1–2 kPa triggers permeability), ensuring release only in stiff, protease-rich margins.
- Activation and persistence
  - LOX gating: endogenous LOX generates allysine on perilesional collagen/elastin; HA-PeriArmor aminooxy groups form stable oxime bonds, and catechols undergo secondary LOX/metal-assisted crosslinking, producing a pericellular mesh with months-long half-life.
  - Mechanical damping: the catechol-HA network reduces local effective modulus sensed by adipocyte precursors, lowering YAP/TAZ nuclear entry without softening distant normal skin.

Selectivity features
- Multi-input AND gate: requires co-occurrence of LOX (anchoring), elevated MMPs (PPARγ uncaging), acidity/ROS (aptamer unmasking), and high stiffness (nanodepot mechanophore opening). Normal skin lacks this signature; the system remains inert.
- Spatial confinement: perilesional ECM binding and short diffusion lengths limit spread; no integration into central keloid to avoid fueling core fibroplasia.

Proposed mechanism of action
- Signal sequestration: heparan-mimetic brushes and unmasked aptamers capture TGF-β1/3, CTGF, PDGF, and profibrotic EVs, depleting AMT drivers that leak into normal skin.
- Mechanotransduction buffering: the adherent catechol network reduces strain transfer to preadipocytes, limiting RhoA/ROCK and YAP/TAZ activation that otherwise promotes AMT.
- Identity reinforcement: nanodepots release microdosed PPARγ agonist only at the perimeter, sustaining adipogenic transcriptional programs (PPARγ, C/EBPα, adiponectin) without systemic exposure.

Experimental plan
Aim 1: Chemistry and gating
- Synthesize HA-PeriArmor (degree of substitution: catechol ~10%, aminooxy ~5%, HS-mimetic ~2%).
- Validate LOX-dependent oxime anchoring on collagen/elastin films; quantify kinetics and bond stability.
- Rheology on keloid-mimetic gels (15–50 kPa) vs normal-dermis gels (1–4 kPa) to confirm stiffness-dependent deposition and damping.

Aim 2: Capture efficacy and selectivity
- In vitro flow chamber with conditioned media from human keloid fibroblasts: measure depletion of TGF-β1/3, CTGF, and EV counts (NTA), with/without ROS/pH gating.
- Off-target assessment in normal skin media for retained homeostatic levels of EGF/FGF.

Aim 3: Anti-AMT function in human cells
- Human dermal adipocyte precursor cultures exposed to keloid-conditioned media ± PeriShield-LOX.
  - Readouts: αSMA, COL1A1, TAGLN, YAP nuclear ratio; adipogenic markers PPARγ, ADIPOQ, PLIN1; lipid droplet content; OCR/ECAR for metabolic function.
- 3D human skin equivalents with perilesional adipocyte layer and keloid fibroblast plug; live imaging of AMT at the boundary.

Aim 4: In vivo proof of concept and durability
- Human keloid xenograft on NSG mice with autologous human dermal adipocyte precursors implanted perilesionally; perimeter microneedle application once.
  - Endpoints at weeks 1–16: AMT indices (αSMA+ adipocyte-lineage cells), adipocyte function (insulin-stimulated glucose uptake ex vivo), perimeter expansion rate (ultrasound/optical coherence), local cytokine/EV gradients, mesh persistence (fluor-tagged HA-PeriArmor).
- Safety: systemic drug levels (LC-MS), glucose/insulin tolerance, local wound healing scores, histology for inflammation.

Success criteria
- ≥60% reduction in AMT of perilesional adipocyte precursors vs vehicle at 8 weeks.
- No impairment of adipocyte metabolic function (≤10% change in OCR/insulin response vs baseline).
- ≥50% reduction in keloid radial expansion rate vs control.
- Mesh retention at perimeter for ≥8 weeks with no foreign body granulomas.

Risk analysis and mitigations
- Risk: Excess sequestration of growth factors affecting normal repair.
  - Mitigation: Tune HS-mimetic density; include reversible low-affinity motifs; cap total binding capacity to pathologic-range concentrations.
- Risk: Systemic PPARγ exposure.
  - Mitigation: Microdose payload; strong ECM anchoring; rapid systemic clearance profile; confirm sub-ng/mL plasma levels.
- Risk: Heterogeneous LOX levels in patients.
  - Mitigation: Dual anchoring via catechol metal-chelation and oxime ligation; optional co-formulation with low-dose LOX-mimetic nanozyme restricted by pH/ROS gating if needed.

Manufacturability and single-dose durability
- All components are chemically defined and compatible with GMP polymer conjugation.
- Single administration yields covalently anchored mesh with slow hydrolytic erosion (oxime stability) designed for 8–16 weeks; repeat dosing feasible if needed.

Regulatory and translational notes
- Topical device–drug combination with localized exposure.
- Components selected with precedent in dermal biomaterials (HA, catechol chemistries, peptides); aptamers and lipidoid depots remain localized.

Novelty
- First use of endogenous LOX/stiffness at keloid margins to gate in situ assembly of an ECM-anchored, dual-function perimeter mesh that both sequesters profibrotic cytokines/EVs and delivers locally gated PPARγ support to prevent AMT of skin adipocyte precursors after a single topical dose.

Projected timeline (18 months)
- Months 0–6: Synthesis, gating validation, rheology, capture assays.
- Months 6–12: Cell/3D model AMT blockade and metabolic preservation.
- Months 12–18: Xenograft efficacy, durability, safety; candidate selection for IND-enabling studies.

Anticipated impact
A perimeter-first, pathology-gated, single-application topical therapy that protects healthy skin adipocytes from keloid-driven reprogramming, halts scar spread, and preserves normal skin metabolic/regenerative function without perturbing unaffected tissue.

Title
KAPTURE: Keloid-Activated Pro-resolving Topical depot to Unset adipocyte REprogramming

Central Hypothesis
A brief, localized pulse of a natural resolution cue that re-engages adipocyte lipid identity (PPARγ/SPM axis) is the physiological “stop signal” that terminates the transient, fibroblast-like plasticity of dermal adipocytes during normal wound resolution. Delivering this stop signal only within the keloid microenvironment—defined by concurrent hypoxia and LOX-driven matrix crosslinking—will block adipocyte dedifferentiation and adipocyte-to–myofibroblast–like transition without perturbing metabolic or regenerative functions of adipocytes in normal skin.

Atomic Strategy
Reinstate the resolution checkpoint of adipocyte plasticity by delivering a short burst of a specialized pro-resolving mediator (SPM) signal (maresin-1 analog) that drives PPARγ-dependent redifferentiation and YAP/TAZ deactivation—but gate its release with an AND-logic keyed to two keloid hallmarks (hypoxia and elevated lysyl-oxidase activity) so the effect remains confined to pathological tissue.

Therapeutic Concept
- Agent: NIm-MaR1, a hypoxia-reducible, nitroimidazole-caged maresin-1 analog (SPM) that is inert in normoxia and releases active MaR1 in hypoxic cells (adipocyte lineage and macrophages) via intracellular nitroreduction.
- Depot: LOX-anchoring, catechol-modified chitosan-lipid nanodepot (100–150 nm) that undergoes LOX-mediated catechol oxidation/Schiff-base coupling to collagen in highly crosslinked keloid ECM, forming an in situ, soft, interpenetrating depot to sustain release for 4–6 weeks after a single topical application.
- Topical vehicle: Folliculotropic cream with volatile co-solvent to enhance follicular uptake and interstitial spreading over keloid surface; no microneedles or systemic permeation enhancers.

Selectivity Logic (AND-gated)
- Gate 1—Tissue stiffness/crosslinking: High LOX activity in keloids oxidizes catechol groups on the nanodepot shell, covalently anchoring the depot within the scar ECM; in normal skin (low LOX), particles do not immobilize and are cleared.
- Gate 2—Hypoxia: NIm-MaR1 remains caged in normoxic tissue; in hypoxic keloid parenchyma, intracellular nitroreductases decage the SPM, producing a brief, local MaR1 pulse that resets adipocyte identity and dampens profibrotic signaling.

Mechanistic Outcomes in Keloid Tissue
- Adipocyte lineage: PPARγ target reactivation, restoration of lipid droplet program (PLIN1, G0S2), suppression of ATGL-driven lipolytic dedifferentiation, nuclear export of YAP/TAZ, blockade of α-SMA induction.
- Microenvironment: Pro-resolving macrophage skewing, reduced latent TGF-β activation, normalization of ECM synthesis dynamics without impairing normal dWAT regenerative cycling.
- Persistence: Anchored depot yields low-level, intermittent MaR1 replenishment (weeks), reinforcing a stable, differentiated adipocyte state after a single administration.

Formulation Blueprint
- Core: Phosphatidylcholine-rich lipid matrix solubilizing NIm-MaR1.
- Shell: Catechol-modified chitosan (degree of substitution ~15–20%) for LOX-mediated anchoring; optional short EDA-fibronectin–binding peptide motif to increase residency on keloid ECM without affecting normal dermis.
- Particle size: 100–150 nm; zeta potential +10 to +20 mV in formulation, neutralized upon skin contact.
- Vehicle: Water-in-silicone cream with fast-evaporating silicone to concentrate particles at the scar surface; pH 6.5–6.8.

Research Plan

Aim 1. Define the physiological “stop signal” in human keloid and normal skin models.
- Ex vivo human keloid explants and matched normal dermis with lineage-traced adipocyte progenitors.
- Test: 2-hour MaR1 pulse vs vehicle under controlled oxygen and stiffness conditions.
- Endpoints: scRNA-seq of adipocyte lineage states; YAP/TAZ localization; α-SMA, COL1A1; PLIN1, G0S2, PPARG targets; mitochondrial respiration and lipolysis/lipogenesis responsiveness.

Go/No-Go: MaR1 pulse reduces adipocyte-to–myofibroblast–like transition ≥50% in keloid conditions without altering basal metabolic/regenerative metrics in normal dermis.

Aim 2. Engineer and validate the dual-gated, single-dose depot.
- Chemistry: Synthesize NIm-MaR1 via carbonate linkage; quantify hypoxia-dependent release kinetics and oxygen threshold; assemble catechol-chitosan–lipid nanodepots.
- Keloid selectivity: In vitro LOX-rich vs LOX-low gel phantoms; human keloid vs normal dermis ECM slices—measure anchoring, diffusion, and washout.
- Safety/metabolism: Cytocompatibility in human keratinocytes, fibroblasts, adipocytes; ensure minimal MaR1 leak in normoxia.

Milestones: AND-gating yields ≥20-fold higher active MaR1 AUC in keloid-mimetic conditions vs normal; depot half-life in ECM >21 days.

Aim 3. Single-application efficacy and durability in vivo.
- Models: Human keloid xenograft on NSG mice and porcine scar model with keloid-like features.
- Dosing: One topical administration; follow 8–12 weeks.
- Readouts: Spatial proteomics and scRNA-seq for adipocyte lineage stabilization; biomechanical mapping (AFM) of tissue softening; collagen architecture; keloid volume and recurrence indices; systemic exposure (LC-MS/MS).

Success Criteria
- ≥60% reduction in adipocyte-to–myofibroblast–like transition markers within treated keloid with no change in adjacent normal skin adipocyte metabolic/regenerative functions.
- Depot persistence and localized activation confirmed for ≥4 weeks after one dose.
- No epidermal barrier disruption, irritation, or systemic SPM exposure above physiologic background.

Risk Mitigation
- If hypoxia gating is insufficiently selective, increase caging density or switch to dual-lock decaging (nitroaryl + ROS-boronate).
- If LOX anchoring is weak, raise catechol substitution or add short EDA-fibronectin–binding motif; if too persistent, include hydrolysable spacers to time-limit depot.
- If MaR1 potency is inadequate, pivot to an alternative endogenous stop signal with the same gate: 15d-PGJ2 analog or adiponectin-mimetic peptide (ADP355) prodrug.

Novelty
- Targets the physiological resolution checkpoint rather than blocking a single profibrotic pathway.
- Dual microenvironmental logic (LOX anchoring + hypoxia decaging) confines action to keloid tissue.
- Topical, single-dose, sustained pro-resolving depot designed to reset adipocyte identity without impairing normal adipocyte metabolism or regenerative cycling.

Translational Path
- Utilize GRAS excipients and scalable nanoprecipitation.
- Dermatologic safety panel and human repeat-insult patch testing.
- Early-phase trial: single-application study on mature keloids, with spatial biomarkers of adipocyte redifferentiation and scar remodeling as primary endpoints.

text:
Title
Traction-Gated Adipocyte Reversion (TGAR) cream: a single-dose, mechano-selective topical that reverts partially transformed adipocytes in keloids while sparing normal skin

Atomic Strategy
Exploit the uniquely high cell–matrix traction forces present in stiff, inflamed keloid ECM to mechanically unlock a pro-adipogenic cue only at those sites. The cue remains inert in normal, soft dermis, preserving native adipocyte metabolism and regeneration.

Hypothesis and Goal
Hypothesis: Partially transformed adipocytes in keloids reside in a reversible state maintained by high matrix stiffness and persistent inflammatory signaling. If a pro-adipogenic signal is delivered only when integrin-transmitted traction exceeds a calibrated threshold characteristic of keloid tissue, these cells can be driven back to a stable adipocyte identity without affecting normal adipocytes. Goal: Develop a single-application topical cream whose cargo is released exclusively under pathological traction, restoring adipocyte fate and blocking myofibroblast-like transition.

Therapeutic Design

1) Mechano-selective nanosystem (MechanoLock NPs)
- Core: Mesoporous silica nanoparticle (MSN; 80–120 nm) loaded with a PPARγ-biased partial agonist (pro-adipogenic with minimal adipocyte hypertrophy signature).
- Gate: Force-calibrated molecular tethers (mechanosensitive caps) spanning the MSN pores. Two interchangeable options will be developed and down-selected:
  a) DNA hairpin tension gates engineered to unfold at 15–20 pN.
  b) Polymer mechanophores (e.g., spiropyran or cyclobutane motifs) that scission under comparable pico–nanoNewton forces transduced through the gate.
- Force transduction: The gates are connected to an integrin-binding ligand array (multivalent cyclic RGD for αvβ3/α5β1) and a collagen/fibronectin-binding peptide (CBP, EDA-FN–affine) to couple NPs to tension-bearing adhesions within keloid ECM. When cells pull against a stiff matrix, traction loads the gate and opens the pore; on soft matrices, tension stays below threshold and the gate remains closed.

2) Pathology targeting and retention
- Dual anchoring: RGD/CBP decorations concentrate NPs in keloid ECM enriched in EDA-fibronectin and crosslinked collagen. In normal skin, weaker binding and lower traction limit accumulation and release.
- Inflammation-aided residence: Catechol-modified NP coronas form reversible covalent interactions with oxidized ECM residues, extending local retention only where oxidative stress is elevated.

3) Payload and mechanism of action
- Primary payload: A PPARγ partial agonist (biased toward adipogenic lineage commitment with limited lipogenic program) to re-establish adipocyte gene networks (PPARG2, CEBPA, FABP4) and antagonize TGF-β/Smad3, Wnt/β-catenin, and YAP/TAZ outputs that drive myofibroblast features (ACTA2, COL1A1).
- Optional micro-dose co-payload (only if needed after Aim 2): a low-potency ROCK inhibitor microload to transiently lower actomyosin tone specifically where release occurs; remains below systemic-relevant levels due to mechanogating and depot confinement.

4) Topical formulation and single-dose durability
- Vehicle: An ultradeformable liposomal cream (transfersome-like) with skin-compatible penetration enhancers (e.g., propylene glycol/oleic acid) to ferry MechanoLock NPs across stratum corneum via follicular and intercellular routes.
- In situ depot: Upon reaching the dermis, NPs anchor within keloid ECM via CBP/catechol chemistry. Release is event-driven (cell traction) rather than time-driven, producing weeks-long pulsatile delivery tied to ongoing mechano-inflammatory activity. A single application targets the full “closing-door” window by metering release as cells cycle through high-tension states during remodeling.

Selectivity Rationale
- Mechanical AND-gate: Requires (i) stiff ECM to transmit traction and (ii) active cell pulling to surpass the force threshold. Normal adipocytes in compliant dermis do not open the gate; payload stays sequestered and is cleared intact.
- Pathology-local retention: Binding to EDA-FN/collagen crosslinks concentrates the depot within keloids, further lowering off-target exposure.
- Payload choice: A biased PPARγ agonist reinforces adipocyte identity without broadly activating lipid storage programs, helping preserve normal adipocyte metabolic/regenerative functions even if trace exposure occurs.

Experimental Plan

Aim 1. Define the reversible window of adipocyte-to-myofibroblast-like transition (AMT)
- Model: Human dermal adipocyte progenitors and mature adipocytes cultured on tunable stiffness (1, 10, 40 kPa) with keloid-conditioned media or keloid ECM slices.
- Readouts: Fate markers (PPARG2, CEBPA, FABP4; ACTA2, TAGLN, COL1A1), chromatin accessibility at adipogenic super-enhancers (ATAC-seq), traction force microscopy (TFM), and reversibility assays after transient exposure to stiffness/inflammation.
- Output: Force and time thresholds defining when AMT is still reversible.

Aim 2. Engineer and calibrate MechanoLock NPs
- Fabrication: Load MSNs with candidate PPARγ partial agonists. Install RGD/CBP ligands and mechanogates with defined rupture forces (10, 15, 20, 25 pN series).
- Bench testing: Single-molecule force spectroscopy to validate gate rupture forces. In vitro TFM-coupled release assays on substrates of varying stiffness with adipocytes/AMT cells to map traction–release transfer functions.
- Down-select: Choose gate design/threshold that maximizes release on 20–50 kPa (keloid-like) and minimizes release on ≤5 kPa (normal dermis-like).

Aim 3. Demonstrate selective, traction-gated release in human keloid explants
- Ex vivo human keloid vs patient-matched normal dermis slices; topical cream application on the epidermal side.
- Endpoints: NP penetration and retention (multiphoton imaging), local payload liberation (FRET-based cargo release reporters), and off-target release quantification. Confirm that release correlates with local α-SMA+ stress fiber density and YAP nuclear localization.

Aim 4. Therapeutic reversal and functional outcomes
- Treatment: Single-dose TGAR cream to keloid explants and to human keloid xenografts in immunodeficient mice.
- Primary outcomes: Reversion of AMT (↑PPARG2/CEBPA/FABP4; ↓ACTA2/COL1A1), reduced YAP/Smad3 target expression, restoration of dermal white adipose islands, decreased tissue stiffness by AFM, and normalized collagen architecture (SHG imaging).
- Durability: Weekly assessments up to 8 weeks to confirm sustained effect from a single administration tied to ongoing traction events.
- Safety: Local cytokine profiling, metabolic panels in adjacent normal skin, and systemic exposure (LC–MS/MS) to ensure minimal spillover.

Aim 5. Preservation of normal adipocyte function
- Normal skin organoids and porcine dermis treated with TGAR cream.
- Endpoints: Basal lipolysis, insulin-stimulated glucose uptake, adipocyte progenitor colony formation, and wound re-epithelialization; expect no significant changes vs vehicle due to lack of gate opening.

Risk and Mitigation
- Risk: Insufficient dermal penetration. Mitigation: Optimize ultradeformable vesicles and follicular targeting; confirm by intravital imaging.
- Risk: Gate opens at unintended forces. Mitigation: Iterate gate thresholds and ligand densities; incorporate mixed-population gates requiring cooperative loading to open.
- Risk: Payload choice drives hypertrophy. Mitigation: Screen biased PPARγ partial agonists for pro-adipogenic, low-lipogenic transcriptomic signatures before in vivo use.

Novelty
- First use of integrin-transduced traction as an on-site actuator to release a fate-reversion cue in fibrosis.
- Selectivity arises from a physical property (cell-ECM force on stiff matrices), not just biochemical markers, meeting the requirement for microenvironment-driven specificity.

Go/No-Go Milestones
- M1: Gate calibration achieves ≥10× release on 40 kPa vs 1 kPa substrates.
- M2: Ex vivo keloid slices show ≥70% of release events co-localized with α-SMA+ stress fibers and near-zero release in matched normal dermis.
- M3: Single-dose in xenograft reduces α-SMA area by ≥50% and restores adipocyte markers to ≥60% of normal by week 6 without metabolic perturbation in adjacent skin.
- No-Go: Off-target release >10% of total in normal dermis or evidence of impaired normal adipocyte function.

Expected Impact
A single-application, mechano-gated topical that re-opens the “door” of adipocyte fate only where keloid mechanics and inflammation keep it ajar, thereby reversing AMT, softening scars, and preserving the metabolic and regenerative roles of normal skin adipocytes.

text:
Title
Topo-LOCK: A microenvironment-gated epigenetic lock that traps keloid-adjacent adipocytes in a terminally mature state to halt adipocyte-to–myofibroblast transition

Objective
Create a topical, single-dose therapy that permanently prevents adipocytes within keloid tissue from dedifferentiating into myofibroblast-like cells, without impairing the metabolic or regenerative functions of adipocytes in normal skin.

Atomic Strategy
Exploit the keloid microenvironment (hypoxia, high stiffness/YAP activity, and TGF-β tone) as an AND-gate to transiently express a locus-specific epigenetic writer in adipocytes only within keloids, installing durable repressive chromatin at myofibroblast fate–determinant enhancers. Once these enhancers are locked, adipocytes remain terminally mature and cannot fuel scar expansion.

Mechanism of Action
- Sensing: A synthetic promoter requiring concurrent HIF-1 (hypoxia) and TEAD (stiffness/YAP) response elements, plus SMAD-responsive elements (TGF-β), drives expression only where all three cues are present at keloid levels.
- Cell-type restriction: The sensor is embedded within an adipocyte-restricted enhancer context (e.g., FABP4/ADIPOQ elements) so that even in keloids, only adipocytes can express the payload.
- Effector: A programmable epigenetic silencer (dCas9 fused to KRAB–DNMT3A) guided to super-enhancers and promoters that switch adipocytes toward a myofibroblast state under stress (e.g., ACTA2, TAGLN, COL1A1, CTGF, MRTFA, WWTR1/TAZ regulatory hubs). Brief expression installs DNA methylation/heterochromatin that persists after the payload is gone.
- Outcome: Adipocytes in keloids are “locked” in a terminally mature state (PPARG-driven program preserved), occupying space but unable to activate myofibroblast genes despite ongoing mechanical and hypoxic stress. Normal skin lacks the AND-gated cues; adipocytes there are untouched.

Therapeutic Design (Topical, Single Administration)
- Formulation: Dissolving microneedle patch that deposits a shear-thinning hydrogel depot within the keloid upper dermis.
- Vehicle: Hypoxia-activated, MMP-cleavable lipid nanocapsules carrying circular RNA encoding the gated dCas9–KRAB–DNMT3A and a pooled set of guide RNAs. The nanocapsule surface displays peptides that bind keloid-enriched ECM (e.g., EDA-fibronectin/tenascin-C) to concentrate payload in scar tissue.
- Dosing and durability: A single patch creates a local depot that releases over ~1–2 weeks; circRNA expression windows of days are sufficient for stable DNA methylation. The installed epigenetic state is expected to persist for months in post-mitotic adipocytes, sustaining effect without chronic dosing.

Selectivity and Preservation of Normal Adipocyte Function
- Spatial selectivity: Physical targeting to stiff, protease-rich keloid ECM plus hypoxia/MMP activation of the carrier limits exposure to normal skin.
- Transcriptional selectivity: AND-gated microenvironmental promoter ensures payload expression only under keloid-like hypoxia+YAP+TGF-β, while adipocyte enhancers restrict expression to adipocytes, not fibroblasts or keratinocytes.
- Functional sparing: The effector edits only myofibroblast-transition hubs; adipocyte metabolic genes (PPARG, CEBPA, ADIPOQ, PLIN1) are not targeted, preserving lipid handling and endocrine function in normal skin.

Planned Studies

Aim 1: Validate the keloid-gated sensor and adipocyte restriction
- Build reporter constructs with the HIF/TEAD/SMAD AND-gated promoter within adipocyte enhancers.
- Test activation thresholds in primary human adipocytes exposed to controlled oxygen tension, substrate stiffness, and TGF-β. Confirm off-state in normoxic, soft, low-TGF-β conditions and in non-adipocyte skin cells.

Aim 2: Define a minimal guide set that installs a durable lock
- Use ATAC-seq and H3K27ac ChIP-seq in adipocytes subjected to keloid-mimetic stress to map inducible myofibroblast super-enhancers.
- Nominate a minimal gRNA panel (3–6 sites) that, when targeted by dCas9–KRAB–DNMT3A, prevents induction of ACTA2/TAGLN/COL1A1/CTGF and mechanotransduction nodes (e.g., MRTFA, WWTR1) without depressing adipocyte identity markers.
- Assess durability after washout (weeks) by bisulfite sequencing and re-challenge with stress cues.

Aim 3: Demonstrate topical delivery, selectivity, and disease modification
- Ex vivo: Human keloid skin slices treated with the patch; measure spatial expression of the payload, methylation at target loci, adipocyte identity retention, and suppression of myofibroblast markers.
- In vivo: Keloid xenograft or humanized skin models; single administration of patch vs. control. Endpoints: reduction in αSMA+ cells derived from perilipin+ lineage, collagen organization, scar thickness/stiffness, and maintenance of adipocyte lipid content/endocrine readouts in adjacent normal skin.

Readouts and Success Criteria
- Molecular lock: ≥70% increase in DNA methylation and reduced accessibility at targeted enhancers in perilipin+ cells that persists ≥12 weeks post-dose.
- Fate protection: ≤10% conversion of adipocytes to αSMA+ cells under keloid stress (vs. ≥40% in controls), with preserved PPARG/ADIPOQ expression.
- Tissue effect: ≥30% reduction in keloid stiffness/thickness and collagen I/III ratio normalization without lipoatrophy in adjacent normal skin.
- Safety: No payload activation in normal skin; minimal systemic exposure; no cytokine spikes or impaired wound closure in standardized injury assays outside keloid sites.

Risk Mitigation
- Off-target editing: Use high-specificity gRNAs; incorporate self-limiting degrons in the effector; restrict expression window via circRNA half-life. Include miRNA target sites enriched in fibroblasts/keratinocytes to silence any ectopic expression.
- Over-suppression of adipocyte function: Exclude adipocyte metabolic loci from gRNA panel; benchmark insulin responsiveness and adipokine secretion in treated normal adipocytes.
- Heterogeneity of keloid cues: Tune promoter thresholds and include modular response elements to cover a physiologic band of hypoxia/stiffness/TGF-β seen across patients.

Why This Is Novel
- Converts defining keloid features (hypoxia, stiffness/YAP activation, TGF-β tone) into a spatially confined epigenetic intervention.
- Uses a one-time, topical, microenvironment-gated epigenome editor to install durable, locus-specific repressive marks at fate-switch enhancers, “locking in” adipocyte maturity rather than merely inhibiting signaling.
- Integrates environmental logic and cell-type restriction to preserve normal adipocyte metabolism and skin regeneration while starving the keloid of new myofibroblast-like cells.

text:
Title
Topical, microenvironment‑gated epigenetic “write‑protection” of dermal adipocytes to prevent myofibroblast transition in keloid scars

Central hypothesis
A one‑time, locally delivered epigenetic editor that installs heritable repression at the adipocyte‑to‑myofibroblast decision node—only when exposed to the hypoxic, stiff, TGF‑β–rich milieu of keloids—will permanently block dedifferentiation of dermal adipocytes without impairing their metabolic or regenerative functions in normal skin.

Atomic strategy
Exploit a keloid‑specific logic gate (hypoxia × stiffness × TGF‑β) to transiently activate a CRISPRoff‑class repressor in dermal adipocytes that heritably silences the myofibroblast entry switch (MRTFA and the ACTA2 super‑enhancer). Once these loci are silenced, pro‑fibrotic cues cannot induce α‑SMA/myofibroblast programs; endogenous PPARγ‑driven adipocyte identity and metabolism persist. The editor turns on only in keloids; the epigenetic memory persists after it turns off.

Therapeutic design

1) Keloid‑selective transcriptional logic
- Triple‑input AND promoter driving the editor, assembled from:
  - Hypoxia response elements (HRE) for HIF‑1α stabilization.
  - TEAD/MRTF‑SRF elements reporting high matrix stiffness/mechanotransduction.
  - SMAD‑binding elements reporting TGF‑β activity.
- Optional adipocyte restriction layer: an adipocyte‑active enhancer (PPARG/ADIPOQ) controlling guide RNA expression, so only adipocytes can execute the edit.

2) Epigenetic payload (“LOCK”)
- A split, hypoxia‑complemented CRISPRoff module (dCas9–KRAB–DNMT3A/3L halves) that reconstitutes only under the AND‑gate promoter.
- Guide set targets:
  - MRTFA promoter: heritable repression of the myocardin‑related coactivator required for α‑SMA induction.
  - ACTA2 super‑enhancer: silencing the α‑SMA node to block myofibroblast cytoskeletal commitment.
- Rationale: disabling this convergence node prevents transition regardless of upstream ligands (TGF‑β, mechanical stress, IL‑6), while sparing PPARG/CEBPA metabolic circuits.
- Self‑limiting expression: oxygen‑labile degrons and protease sites ensure rapid editor decay as hypoxia/stiffness/TGF‑β resolve.

3) Topical microdevice for single‑dose delivery
- Dissolvable microneedle patch (≤500 μm) with a mechano‑adhesive, collagen‑binding base that preferentially anchors in stiff, cross‑linked keloid ECM.
- Hypoxia/acid‑triggered linkers release lipid‑nanoparticles (LNPs) carrying:
  - mRNA for split‑CRISPRoff halves under the AND‑gate promoter.
  - sgRNA cassette under adipocyte‑enhanced control.
- Physical selectivity: patch adheres and releases preferentially on stiff, hypoxic, acidic keloid surfaces; normal skin (softer, normoxic, neutral pH) shows minimal release and little/no transcriptional activation.

Why this preserves normal adipocyte function
- Activity occurs only where all three inputs co‑exist (keloid core/periphery).
- Repressed targets (MRTFA/ACTA2 enhancer) are dispensable for basal lipid storage, lipolysis, glucose uptake, and adipokine secretion in mature adipocytes, whereas PPARγ/insulin signaling remain intact.
- In normoxic, soft, TGF‑β‑low skin, the editor is not expressed; no epigenetic change occurs.

Experimental plan

Aim 1: Build and validate the keloid‑logic promoter.
- Engineer HRE×TEAD/SRF×SMAD AND‑gate reporters and quantify activation across oxygen tension, substrate stiffness, and TGF‑β1 gradients in primary human dermal adipocytes and keloid stromal co‑cultures.
- Success criterion: ≥50‑fold induction only under hypoxia (<2% O2), high stiffness (>20 kPa), and TGF‑β1 (>5 ng/mL); <2‑fold in any single or double condition.

Aim 2: Define the minimal “LOCK” edit set.
- Compare sgRNA sets to MRTFA vs ACTA2 super‑enhancer vs combined.
- Challenge with TGF‑β1, cyclic stretch, and substrate stiffening; readouts: ACTA2/TAGLN induction, α‑SMA stress fibers, collagen I secretion, traction force.
- Persistence: track silencing and resistance to myofibroblast conversion over ≥20 cell doublings after editor extinction.
- Metabolic preservation: insulin‑stimulated glucose uptake, lipolysis, mitochondrial respiration, adipokine secretion (adiponectin/leptin), and de novo adipogenesis from preadipocytes adjacent to edited adipocytes.

Aim 3: Topical device selectivity and single‑dose durability.
- Ex vivo human keloid and matched normal skin explants: quantify patch adherence, LNP penetration, and expression selectivity (reporter under AND‑gate).
- Single‑dose edit durability: measure methylation/heterochromatin marks and resistance to myofibroblast conversion for ≥12 weeks in explants.

Aim 4: Efficacy in vivo and safety.
- Human keloid xenografts with intradermal adipocyte lineage labeling.
- Endpoints: reduction in α‑SMA+ adipocyte‑derived cells, collagen organization, stiffness (AFM), scar volume, and recurrence after injury re‑challenge.
- Safety: off‑target editing (GUIDE‑seq in adipocytes), biodistribution, local inflammation, systemic cytokines, wound‑healing competence outside the treated field.

Readouts and milestones
- Gate fidelity: high dynamic range, negligible leak in normal skin.
- Edit success: sustained repression at MRTFA/ACTA2 loci with preserved PPARG program.
- Function: unchanged adipocyte metabolic assays vs untreated controls.
- Outcome: ≥60% reduction in adipocyte‑derived myofibroblasts and ≥40% decrease in scar stiffness/volume with a single application.

Risk analysis and mitigations
- Gate leakiness: add microRNA “safety lock” (miR‑dense non‑adipocyte targets) to degrade editor transcripts outside adipocytes.
- Over‑silencing effects: prioritize ACTA2 enhancer‑only edit if MRTFA repression alters metabolism; prespecify go/no‑go thresholds for adipocyte function assays.
- Delivery depth mismatch: tune needle length and LNP size to target dermal white adipose layer while sparing epidermis.
- Immunogenicity: use deimmunized Cas variants and transient mRNA expression; include proteasomal degrons for rapid clearance.

Expected impact
A first‑in‑class, single‑dose topical therapy that installs a keloid‑restricted, heritable “write‑protection” on dermal adipocytes, preventing their myofibroblast transition while preserving normal adipocyte metabolism and skin regeneration elsewhere. This leverages hypoxia, stiffness, and TGF‑β as selectors rather than targets, converting a pathological microenvironment into a one‑time opportunity to permanently stabilize cell identity and halt keloid progression.
