text:
Title
Tensional Homeostasis Microstents (THM): a bioresorbable, subdermal lattice to preserve dermal ECM and fibrous septa integrity during weight loss without impairing lipolysis

Central hypothesis and research goal
Hypothesis: Loss of tissue tensional homeostasis during adipocyte deflation is the trigger for catabolic dermal remodeling (MMP/elastase upregulation) and buckling of subcutaneous fibrous septa. If we maintain a physiological tensile set-point across the dermis–septa–superficial fascia unit during active fat loss, fibroblasts sustain collagen/elastin assembly and septa remain load-bearing, preventing laxity and contour collapse while lipolysis proceeds unaltered.
Goal: Develop and clinically translate a few-session, minimally invasive, drug-free, bioresorbable implant that reestablishes and holds this tensile set-point for the duration of weight loss, then safely disappears.

Atomic strategy
Preserve tensional homeostasis of the skin–fat composite by delivering a sustained, distributed, low-level tensile preload within the subdermal fibrous network. Mechanotransduction at this set-point suppresses protease-driven ECM degradation and stabilizes septa architecture despite declining fat volume.

Platform description
- Device: THM microstents—injectable, shape-memory, bioresorbable microfilaments (diameter 150–300 μm; length 10–25 mm) with anisotropic microbarbs that engage dermis-facing septa and superficial fascia.
- Material: Medical-grade shape-memory copolymer (PLLA-PCL) tuned to recover at 30–34°C; radioscatter and ultrasound-visible via embedded Mg or BaSO4 microparticles; surface microtexture to distribute shear and minimize focal stress.
- Biomechanics: Each microstent recovers into a gentle arcuate/zigzag profile imparting 0.5–2.0 kPa local tensile preload over 2–4 cm2. Lattice placement (1.5–2.0 cm spacing) yields a mesoscale prestressed network that:
  - Maintains dermal and septal strain within a physiological window that downregulates MMP1/3/9 and elastase, sustains YAP/TAZ nuclear localization, and promotes organized collagen I/III and elastin fiber deposition.
  - Functions as micro-splints that resist septal buckling as adipocytes shrink, preserving vertical tethering and surface contour.
- Deployment: Single percutaneous session per body zone using a 16–18G cannula under ultrasound guidance to the superficial adipose compartment; lattice mapped along Langer’s lines and septal trajectories. Optional touch-up at 8–12 weeks.
- Bioresorption: Mass loss 6–9 months; complete resorption by 12–15 months, matching typical weight-loss timelines.

Selectivity for lipolysis preservation
- No pharmacologic modulation of adipocytes. Mechanical preload targets the ECM–septa network, not triglyceride metabolism.
- Bench/in vivo confirmation: unchanged catecholamine-stimulated glycerol/FFA release, HSL/ATGL expression, and weight-loss trajectories vs untreated controls.

Specific aims
Aim 1: Engineer and validate THM microstent mechanics and degradation
- Define force–displacement profiles delivering 0.5–2.0 kPa tissue-level preload for ≥16 weeks.
- Characterize recovery kinetics, pull-out forces in ex vivo human adipose/dermis, and fatigue under cyclic strain.
- Verify ultrasound and low-dose CT visibility; optimize cannula deployment ergonomics.

Aim 2: Demonstrate prevention of ECM catabolism and septal collapse during weight loss in a large-animal model
- Model: Diet-induced 12–15% weight loss in swine; bilateral flank and abdomen sites randomized to THM vs sham.
- Primary outcomes (12 and 24 weeks):
  - Dermal biomechanics: cutometry (R2, R7), shear-wave elastography.
  - Imaging: 3D ultrasound/MRI for septal angle/buckling metrics, dermal thickness, and surface topography (optical profilometry).
  - Histology/molecular: collagen I/III ratio (PSR), elastin fiber orientation (multiphoton), MMP1/3/9 and TIMP1 IHC, YAP/TAZ nuclear translocation, LOX expression; second-harmonic generation for fiber alignment.
- Secondary: Unchanged lipolysis markers (glycerol/FFA), adipocyte size distribution, inflammation (CD68/CD206), nerve/vessel integrity.

Aim 3: First-in-human feasibility in planned weight-loss participants
- Design: Prospective, randomized, contralateral split-body study in 30 adults targeting ≥10% body-weight reduction over 4 months (diet/GLP-1/bariatric pathways permitted but recorded).
- Intervention: Single THM session to one side of abdomen/flank/arm; contralateral control (no treatment or standard RF tightening sub-study).
- Endpoints (16 and 32 weeks):
  - Co-primary: Blinded global aesthetic improvement score (GAIS) and change in skin elasticity (R2).
  - Key secondary: Surface laxity index, dermal thickness and stiffness, patient-reported outcomes (BODY-Q), preservation of contour curvature (3D scan).
  - Safety: AEs, pain, bruising, dysesthesia, palpable nodules, ultrasound assessment of placement and resorption.

Mechanistic rationale and readouts
- Tensional set-point sustains fibroblast anabolic programs: expect decreased MMP transcripts/proteins, increased procollagen C-peptide, organized elastin deposition, and maintained YAP/TAZ nuclear fraction in THM zones vs controls.
- Septa stabilization: reduced septal tortuosity and buckling angle changes on MRI/US; preserved superficial fascial plane geometry correlating with improved macroscopic contour.

Treatment paradigm
- Few-session course: 1 session per zone; optional 1 touch-up. No energy devices or drugs required.
- Compatible with ongoing lifestyle, pharmacologic (e.g., GLP-1) or surgical weight loss.

Safety and risk mitigation
- Placement layer: superficial adipose above Scarpa’s fascia using ultrasound to avoid vessels/nerves.
- Material: established resorbables; EtO sterilization; barbs engineered to limit peak contact pressure below capillary closing pressure.
- Explantability: retrieval within first 2 weeks via micro-incision if needed.
- Monitoring: serial ultrasound for position and resorption; prophylactic compression for 48 h.

Manufacturability and regulatory path
- Scalable microextrusion and laser microtexturing; in-line QA for filament diameter, barb geometry, and SMP transition temperature.
- Anticipated pathway: Class II De Novo as absorbable subdermal support device; precedents include absorbable barbed sutures and soft-tissue support meshes.
- Shelf life: ≥2 years in nitrogen-purged barrier pouches.

Novelty and IP positions
- Method of preserving tensional homeostasis during active weight loss to prevent ECM catabolism and septal collapse.
- Injectable, ultrasound-guided deployment of resorbable shape-memory microstents forming a predefined lattice that delivers a calibrated tissue-level tensile preload for months.
- Design claims on anisotropic microbarb geometry, SMP composition/transition window, radiovisibility, and lattice mapping algorithms tied to septal architecture.
- Outcome-linked dosing (kPa–cm2 preload per area) as a treatment parameter.

Development milestones and success criteria
- M1 (6 months): Prototype meeting mechanical/degradation specs; ex vivo human tissue anchoring >0.3 N pull-out; ultrasound visibility confirmed.
- M2 (12 months): Swine study: ≥25% improvement vs control in R2 elasticity; ≥30% reduction in MMP1/3/9; significant reduction in septal buckling angle change; no impairment of lipolysis markers.
- M3 (24 months): First-in-human: ≥1-point GAIS improvement, ≥20% increase in R2, improved surface laxity index with noninferior safety to sham/RF.
- Go/No-Go: If lipolysis trajectory deviates or neuropraxia >5%, redesign barb density and preload targets.

Exploratory extensions (optional, post-proof)
- Bioactive surface nanopeptides that bias integrin α2β1 engagement without altering adipocyte metabolism.
- Personalized lattice planning using pre-procedural shear-wave elastography to target low-stiffness corridors.

Impact
If successful, THM establishes a first-in-class, few-session, purely mechanobiologic therapy that allows fat to decrease while preserving skin elasticity and body contour by holding the native dermal–septa scaffold at its physiological tensile set-point throughout weight loss, then vanishing once remodeling is complete.

label: elements_bypass
text:
Title: Pre-lipolysis Mechano-Priming of the Dermis–Subcutis Unit to Prevent Post–Weight-Loss Laxity

Core hypothesis–question (inseparable):
Can short-course, controlled cyclic stretching of the dermis–subcutis unit, delivered before intentional fat reduction, pre-align and strengthen dermal ECM and fibrous septa sufficiently to preserve skin elasticity and contour during subsequent weight loss without impairing lipolysis?

Atomic strategy:
Use closed-loop, low-frequency, low-strain cyclic suction–shear to “train” the dermal collagen–elastin network and subcutaneous fibrous septa into a stably pretensioned, anisotropic architecture prior to fat loss, leveraging endogenous mechanotransduction (integrin–FAK–YAP/TAZ, Piezo1/2) to upregulate alignment, elastogenesis, and lysyl oxidase–mediated crosslinking while suppressing MMP predominance.

Mechanistic rationale (concise):
- Repeated sub-failure cyclic strain (5–15% at 0.1–1 Hz) drives fibroblast reorientation, stress fiber assembly, and nuclear YAP/TAZ, biasing synthesis and aligned deposition of collagen I/III and tropoelastin with increased LOX activity and mature crosslinks.
- Multi-axial tissue excursions transmitted into the hypodermis thicken and align fibrous septa, increasing septal tensile capacity and maintaining lobular partitioning as adipocyte volume contracts.
- Gentle pre-tensioning increases resting anisotropic modulus and recoil; by pre-adapting the scaffold, the later loss of internal fat turgor produces less contour collapse.
- Device parameters restrict temperature rise and acoustic/mechanical indices to avoid adipocyte injury, preserving catecholamine-driven lipolysis during weight loss.

Platform and treatment concept:
- Noninvasive device: handheld applicator with programmable negative-pressure oscillation (max −25 to −45 kPa), lateral shear rollers, and optional low-intensity acoustic radiation force pulses (non-thermal) to achieve distributed, multi-axial cyclic strain across dermis and superficial/subcutaneous septa.
- Closed-loop control via real-time shear-wave elastography and surface optical strain mapping to titrate strain amplitude/frequency and ensure session-to-session reproducibility and safety.
- Protocol: 3 sessions over 10–14 days before initiating weight-loss intervention, each 30–45 minutes per anatomic zone; optional single booster at week 6 if weight loss exceeds 10% body mass.
- Safety constraints: skin surface temperature ≤38°C; mechanical index and duty cycle limited to avoid cavitation/thermal effects; no exogenous metabolic agents.
- Optional minimally invasive adjunct (for subset mechanistic arm only, not required for effect): a single-use microneedle patch (600–900 µm) applied immediately post-session delivering microdosed copper peptide (GHK-Cu) and ascorbate localized to reticular dermis to transiently support LOX-dependent crosslink maturation without reaching adipocyte lobules.

Specific aims:
Aim 1. Define the mechanotransductive dose–response that maximizes dermal alignment and septal strengthening without adipocyte impairment.
- Model: human skin–fat explants from abdominoplasty; biomechanical rig delivering defined cyclic suction–shear.
- Readouts: SHG microscopy for collagen fiber alignment index; elastin fiber density/orientation (immunostaining); LOX activity; pyridinoline/desmosine crosslinks; MMP1/3/9 and TIMP1/2; fibroblast YAP/TAZ localization; adipocyte lipolysis competence (isoproterenol-stimulated glycerol release, pHSL Ser563).
- Success criteria: ≥25% increase in dermal anisotropy index; ≥15% increase in septal thickness or collagen bundle coherency; MMP:TIMP ratio shift toward inhibition; no reduction in stimulated lipolysis vs control.

Aim 2. Engineer and validate a closed-loop preconditioning protocol guided by elastography.
- Build device control that adapts strain amplitude/frequency per zone to reach a target increase in in vivo shear modulus (ΔSWS) and anisotropy during each session while maintaining comfort and safety.
- Human feasibility (n=20, abdomen/flanks): determine inter-session repeatability, dose ceiling, and durability of ECM gains at 2 and 6 weeks pre–weight loss.
- Success criteria: reproducible within-subject ΔSWS ≥15% maintained at least 4 weeks; no adverse events beyond Grade 1 erythema/ecchymosis.

Aim 3. Prospective, randomized pilot to test preservation of skin elasticity and contour during weight loss.
- Population: adults planning ≥10% intentional weight loss via diet or bariatric pathway; stratify by age and baseline BMI.
- Arms: A) Mechano-priming (3 sessions pre–weight loss) vs B) Sham (light contact, no suction/shear). Optional C) Mechano-priming + single GHK-Cu/ascorbate microneedle patch (mechanistic signal only).
- Endpoints at 12 and 24 weeks after weight-loss onset:
  - Primary: change in cutometric elasticity (R2) and retraction (R7); blinded dermatologic laxity scores; 3D surface topography sagging index.
  - Secondary: ultrasound shear-wave elastography (dermal modulus, anisotropy); MRI or high-frequency ultrasound of septal architecture (thickness, continuity); patient-reported outcome (skin comfort, body image); rate of post-weight-loss contouring consults.
  - Mechanistic: dermal microdialysate MMP/TIMP balance; circulating collagen turnover biomarkers (PRO-C3, C3M); optional mini-biopsies for fiber orientation and LOX activity.
  - Lipolysis non-inferiority: total weight loss, regional fat thickness change, fasting glycerol/NEFA, adipocyte size distribution (subset biopsies) equivalent across arms.
- Success criteria: ≥20% attenuation in laxity progression vs sham at equivalent fat loss; maintained or improved recoil; no decrement in fat loss metrics.

Selectivity and non-impairment of lipolysis:
- Mechanical parameters and thermal limits preclude adipocyte apoptosis or necrosis.
- Outcomes explicitly test catecholamine-stimulated lipolysis and regional fat reduction parity.
- Any adjunct delivery confined to reticular dermis to avoid adipocyte exposure.

Clinical translatability:
- Device class II predicate space (negative-pressure massage, shear-wave elastography) with added closed-loop control; no drugs required for core effect.
- Few-session regimen aligns with preoperative or program onboarding visits.
- Manufacturing: off-the-shelf pumps, sensors, and elastography modules; disposable interface cups; microneedle patches (if used) built from existing GMP processes.

Risk management:
- Exclude patients with connective tissue disorders, anticoagulation, severe varicosities.
- Monitor for bruising, petechiae, pain; stop rules on elastography overshoot or discomfort.
- Data Safety Monitoring for bariatric patients.

IP and novelty:
- Claims on method of preserving skin elasticity during planned fat reduction by pre-lipolysis cyclic suction–shear tuned via real-time elastography to achieve specified dermal anisotropy and modulus thresholds.
- Claims on closed-loop control algorithms that adapt strain frequency and amplitude to maximize ECM alignment while constraining adipocyte mechanical exposure.
- Optional claims on timed dermal-localized LOX cofactor delivery immediately post-mechano-priming.

Milestones and go/no-go:
- M1 (6 months): Ex vivo dose–response map and safety window established; targets for Δanisotropy and ΔSWS set.
- M2 (12 months): Human feasibility shows durable preconditioning (ΔSWS ≥15%, maintained 4 weeks).
- M3 (24 months): Randomized pilot meets primary endpoint (≥20% laxity attenuation) with non-inferior fat loss.

Potential outcomes and impact:
- If validated, mechano-priming becomes a short, noninvasive preparatory step preceding diet or bariatric interventions, selectively reinforcing dermal ECM and septa to prevent contour collapse while allowing unimpeded fat loss.

text:
Title: Preconditioning the Dermis–Subcutis Interface with Injectable Magneto-Mechanoexpanders to Preserve Skin Elasticity and Septal Integrity During Subsequent Weight Loss

Core Question-Hypothesis:
Can a short, pre–weight loss regimen of controlled, low-amplitude cyclic stretching focused at the dermis–subcutis interface activate fibroblasts and adipose stromal/progenitor cells to build an elastin-rich, pre-tensioned, and crosslinked septal matrix that resists collapse as fat volume decreases—without impairing later lipolysis?

Atomic Strategy (single conceptual perturbation):
Before weight loss begins, deliver gentle, repeated microstrain specifically across the dermal–hypodermal junction and fibrous septa to prime resident fibroblasts and adipose stromal cells via mechanotransduction (integrins/YAP–TAZ/Piezo1–TRPV4), inducing aligned collagen I/III and elastin assembly (ELN, FBLN5) with physiological crosslinking (LOX/LOXL1, TG2). This creates a pre-tensioned, reinforced scaffold that maintains contour when adipocyte volume subsequently declines.

Platform Overview: Injectable Magneto-Mechanoexpander (MME) Microgels
- Composition: Shear-thinning, in situ–gelling microgel slurry (alginate–gelatin/oxidized dextran) embedding superparamagnetic iron oxide nanoparticle (SPION) chainlets. Optional surface-presented fibronectin-mimetic RGD/PR_b peptides to bias α5β1 integrin engagement and limit profibrotic TGF-β dominance. Optional trace Cu2+ chelated within GRAS peptide (e.g., GHK) to cofactor LOX activity; drug-free version prioritized for first-in-human.
- Placement: Fan-pattern microcannula injections into the superficial hypodermis to lace along retinacula cutis and septa (5–8 mm depth), forming a sparse, resorbable mechanoactive lattice beneath the dermis.
- Actuation: External, wearable magnet driver generates alternating field gradients that elongate SPION chainlets and transiently expand microgels, imparting 1–3% tissue strain at 0.1–1 Hz to septa and the dermis–subcutis interface.
- Dosing paradigm: Two to three 30–45 min sessions over 14 days; final session 3–5 days before initiating caloric restriction or anti-obesity pharmacotherapy. No actuation during active weight loss.
- Resorption: Enzymatic hydrolysis and ion exchange yield full clearance in 4–6 weeks; SPIONs at microdose retained in tissue macrophages then cleared hepatically within accepted exposure limits.

Mechanism of Action and Selectivity
- Mechanical cue: Low-amplitude cyclic strain preferentially activates fibroblast and adipose stromal cell mechanosensors (α5β1 integrins, Piezo1/TRPV4) and YAP/TAZ nuclear translocation under dynamic—not static—loading, favoring elastogenesis and matrix alignment over scar-like fibrosis.
- ECM program: Upregulation of ELN, FBLN5, EMILIN-1, COL1A1/COL3A1; physiological crosslinking via LOX/LOXL1 and TG2; increased microfibril organization (fibrillin-1, MAGP-1) and elastic fiber insertion into papillary/reticular dermis.
- Septal reinforcement: Thickened, aligned fibrous septa with improved load sharing between dermis and superficial fascia, reducing septal buckling as adipocyte volume decreases.
- Lipolysis neutrality: No thermal or cytolytic energy; no anti-lipolytic biomolecules. Preconditioning concludes before weight-loss onset; preserves β-adrenergic lipolysis (HSL/ATGL) and perilipin signaling. Post-priming tissue stiffness increase is modest (target +10–20%) to avoid hampering adipocyte shrinkage.

Specific Aims
1) Define safe and effective microstrain dosing that maximizes elastogenesis while avoiding fibrosis.
2) Demonstrate preserved dermal elasticity and septal integrity after induced fat loss without impairing lipolysis.
3) Establish a minimally invasive, few-session clinical workflow suitable for combination with lifestyle or pharmacologic weight-loss programs.

Preclinical Plan
- Human skin–fat explants:
  - Protocol: Inject MME lattice; actuate 0.5%/1%/3% strain at 0.2/0.5/1 Hz, 30 min/session, 3 sessions/14 days. Controls: sham injection, static gel, non-magnetic gel.
  - Readouts: YAP/TAZ nuclear localization; qPCR/proteomics for ELN, FBLN5, EMILIN-1, COL1A1/3A1, LOX/LOXL1, TGM2; second harmonic generation and multiphoton imaging of collagen alignment; immunostaining of elastic fibers; biaxial tensile testing and shear-wave elastography ex vivo; septal thickness by micro-CT.
  - Lipolysis assay: Isoproterenol-stimulated glycerol/NEFA release; HSL/ATGL phosphorylation; perilipin dynamics; compare to sham to confirm neutrality.
  - Fibrosis safety: TGF-β1, ACTA2 (αSMA) thresholds; hydroxyproline content; histopathology for keloidal features.
- Large-animal model (porcine flank):
  - Protocol: MME injection + actuation as above; then 6-week calorie deficit or GLP-1 analogue to induce 10–15% fat reduction.
  - Imaging and biomechanics: Serial ultrasound elastography (dermis and septa), MRI Dixon (fat volume), 3D surface scanning for laxity/ptosis, blinded dermatopathology scoring.
  - Biodistribution/tox: SPION PK (liver/spleen), iron indices, local macrophage response, resorption timeline.

First-in-Human Feasibility (n=30; BMI 27–40 kg/m2)
- Design: Randomized, split-body (e.g., abdominal hemifields). Two MME sessions (Day 0, Day 10), optional third at Day 14. Begin standardized weight-loss program Day 17.
- Endpoints (12 and 24 weeks):
  - Primary: Change in regional skin laxity index and contour retention by 3D stereophotogrammetry; dermal and septal shear modulus by ultrasound elastography.
  - Secondary: Patient/physician-reported outcome (skin firmness), blinded photo grading, MRI Dixon fat change equivalence between sides (non-inferiority margin <3%), safety (AEs, iron labs, histamine/pruritus, nodularity).
  - Mechanistic biopsies (subset): Elastic fiber density, collagen alignment, LOX/LOXL1 activity, YAP/TAZ localization.
- Stopping rules: Any signal of impaired lipolysis (reduced fat loss on treated side), sustained nodularity, or fibrotic signature > preset thresholds.

Clinical Workflow and Feasibility
- Setting: Outpatient, local anesthesia; 3–5 entry sites per field with microcannula fanning. Wearable magnet patch actuates hands-free; real-time strain proxy via optional skin-mounted accelerometer.
- Sessions: 2–3 total over 2 weeks; no maintenance during weight loss.
- Manufacturing: Aseptic, prefilled syringes; SPIONs are clinically established materials; scalable microgel production (emulsion or microfluidic); terminal sterilization or sterile filtration of components.

Risk Mitigation
- Over-stiffening/fibrosis: Use dynamic, not static, loading; cap strain at ≤3%; α5β1-biased ligands to limit αv integrin/TGF-β–driven scarring; monitor αSMA.
- Interference with fat loss: Cessation of actuation before weight loss; confirm β-adrenergic responsiveness preclinically; strict nonthermal regimen.
- Particle safety: Low SPION dose within known exposure; track clearance; option for fully biodegradable magnetic composites if needed.

Regulatory Pathway
- Initial product as device-led combination: Primary mode of action mechanical. De Novo or 510(k) if predicate for magnetically actuated injectable exists; otherwise IDE for early feasibility. Drug-free version first to simplify; Cu-peptide arm as follow-on.

Intellectual Property (novelty)
- Claims: Injectable magnetically actuated microgels specifically configured to deliver sub-5% cyclic strain to dermis–subcutis interface/septa; timing of preconditioning relative to weight-loss onset; α5β1-biased surface ligands to steer elastogenesis; parametric windows (frequency, duty cycle, session count) that preserve lipolysis while increasing dermal/septal modulus; use for preventing post–weight loss laxity.

Milestones (18–24 months)
- M1 (6 months): Parameter map in explants; select clinical window (1–2% strain, 0.5 Hz, 2–3 sessions).
- M2 (12 months): Porcine study shows ≥20% increase in elastic fiber density and ≤10% decline in contour retention vs baseline after 10–15% fat loss; no lipolysis impairment.
- M3 (18–24 months): First-in-human split-body trial demonstrates ≥25% reduction in laxity progression on treated side with equivalent fat loss; safety acceptable.

Success Criterion
A few-session, pre–weight loss, mechano-priming intervention that measurably increases dermal elastic fiber content and septal robustness, maintains skin contour as fat volume declines, and does not reduce the magnitude or rate of lipolysis.

text:
Title
Lipolysis-Gated Adipocyte-to-ECM Producer Reprogramming (LiGER-ECM) to Preserve Dermal Elasticity and Subcutaneous Septa During Fat Loss

Problem and Unmet Need
Caloric deficits and pharmacologic weight loss reduce adipocyte volume but secondarily weaken dermal collagen/elastin networks and collapse subcutaneous fibrous septa, producing laxity and contour loss. Existing approaches (energy devices, fillers, threads) treat symptoms, require multiple sessions, and do not synchronize with the biology of fat loss.

Central Hypothesis
Shrinking adipocytes undergoing active lipolysis can be transiently reprogrammed in situ into non-contractile, ECM-secreting “adipo-fibroblasts” that reinforce dermal collagen/elastin and subcutaneous septa exactly when and where structural support is threatened—without impairing lipolysis.

Atomic Strategy (single conceptual insight)
Exploit the adipocyte’s own lipolysis signal as the gate that triggers a short, self-limited ECM-production program. In other words: convert the catabolic lipolysis cue (high cAMP/PKA, lipid-droplet depletion) into a temporally coupled, local “matrix replacement mode” that deposits correctly composed collagen/elastin around dermis–subcutis interfaces and along fibrous septa while fat volume decreases.

Therapeutic Modality
- Payload: A compact, non-integrating gene-regulation cassette that (a) upregulates a balanced ECM set (e.g., COL1A1/COL3A1 ratioing, ELN assembly support, fibronectin as scaffold, controlled LOX/LOXL1 crosslinking) and (b) suppresses myofibroblast contractile differentiation markers to avoid stiffness (e.g., limiting ACTA2/CTGF axis). Implemented via transient transcriptional modulators (e.g., CRISPRa/i or RNA-based regulators) configured for pulse expression.
- Gating logic: AND gate requiring adipocyte identity + active lipolysis (adipocyte-restricted promoter/enhancer plus lipolysis-responsive elements tied to cAMP/PKA/CREB activity and/or lipid-droplet shrinkage sensors). The circuit turns on only during lipolysis bursts, then auto-attenuates.
- Delivery: Adipose- and dermis-homing LNPs carrying synthetic mRNA(s) for the transient regulators and the logic circuit components. Regional subdermal/intradermal administration to target treatment zones, with 1–2 sessions spaced over the anticipated weight-loss window. LNP is chosen for non-integration, manufacturability, and regulatory familiarity.

Mechanism of Action (MoA)
- Spatial selectivity: Adipocyte-specific expression confines activity to subcutaneous fat pads adjacent to the dermis and fibrous septa.
- Temporal coupling: Only during high lipolytic flux do shrinking adipocytes execute the ECM program, depositing collagen I/III, elastin-supporting components, and organizing fibrils along septal planes and at the dermal–fat interface.
- Phenotypic boundary: The program induces an ECM-secreting, non-contractile state (no sustained myofibroblast features), preserving pliability and recoil rather than scar-like stiffness.
- System outcome: As fat mass declines, septa are reinforced and dermal matrix is renewed, maintaining contour and elasticity without inhibiting fat loss.

Specific Aims
1) Build and validate the LiGER-ECM circuit
- Engineer and screen minimal lipolysis-gated regulatory designs that activate a balanced ECM gene set while suppressing contractility programs, with strict on/off kinetics and no effect on lipolysis rate.
- Quantify matrix composition, fiber alignment, and elastin assembly in primary human adipocyte and adipose organoid systems under lipolytic stimulation.

2) Develop a regionally targeted, few-session LNP delivery
- Formulate adipose/dermis-homing LNPs optimized for subdermal spread and uptake by mature adipocytes and periseptal cells, with transient expression windows calibrated to weight-loss dynamics.
- Establish dose–response for on-target ECM deposition versus inflammation and confirm minimal hepatic exposure.

3) Demonstrate preservation of dermal elasticity and septal integrity during weight loss
- In diet/pharmacologic weight-loss models, test whether LiGER-ECM maintains: (i) dermal thickness/elastic recoil, (ii) collagen I/III ratio and fiber crimp by SHG imaging, (iii) elastin content and functional recoil, and (iv) septal continuity and tethering on MRI/ultrasound elastography—while confirming unchanged fat-loss kinetics.

Selectivity and Safety Features
- Dual gating (adipocyte identity AND lipolysis activity) to avoid off-target ECM deposition.
- Auto-attenuation via built-in feedback: expression decays as lipolysis subsides; microRNA- and degron-based safeguards reduce duration and prevent persistent phenotype.
- Non-integrating, transient expression to minimize genotoxicity; avoidance of broad TGF-β activation to reduce fibrosis risk.
- Immunogenicity minimization through humanized regulators and repeat-dosing mitigation strategies appropriate for LNPs.

Clinical Use Case and Regimen
- Candidate indications: skin laxity prevention during intentional weight loss (e.g., GLP-1–assisted programs) in abdomen, arms, thighs, submental areas.
- Regimen: 1–2 regional LNP administrations bracketing the main weight-loss phase; no device downtime; compatible with lifestyle interventions. Primary outcomes: blinded laxity scales, shear-wave elastography, patient-reported contour satisfaction; secondary: histologic biomarkers in optional micro-biopsies.

Translatability and Manufacturing
- LNPs with GMP-ready lipids and scalable microfluidic production; synthetic, sequence-defined RNAs.
- Established regulatory precedents for transient mRNA LNPs; clear pharmacology (local, non-integrating, time-limited).
- Regional administration aligns with ambulatory dermatology/plastic surgery workflows.

Risk Mitigation
- Fibrosis/stiffness: predefine ECM expression ratios and cap crosslinking enzyme activity; monitor viscoelastic spectra; halt criteria if stiffness exceeds threshold.
- Interference with lipolysis: design screens include glycerol/FFA flux; circuit revisions if any attenuation detected.
- Off-target deposition: biodistribution mapping; refine targeting ligands and dosing volumes.
- Immune responses: adaptive scheduling, minimal necessary exposure, and adjuvant-sparing formulations.

Milestones and Go/No-Go
- M1: Lipolysis-gated activation with >20-fold on/off and zero impact on glycerol release in vitro.
- M2: Balanced ECM deposition with target collagen I/III ratio and elastin assembly comparable to youthful dermis benchmarks in organoids.
- M3: In vivo preservation of septal continuity and dermal elasticity with non-inferior fat-loss rate versus controls; safety margins established.

Innovation and IP Position
- First use of endogenous lipolysis as a therapeutic gate to drive transient, local ECM replacement from shrinking adipocytes.
- Dual objective (dermis plus fibrous septa) via a single, temporally coupled reprogramming pulse.
- Balanced ECM program that avoids myofibroblast conversion, enabling elasticity preservation rather than fibrosis.
- Claims on lipolysis-activated gene circuits for ECM modulation in adipocytes; adipose/dermis-homing LNP delivery for synchronized structural reinforcement during weight loss.

Expected Impact
LiGER-ECM converts catabolism into repair in real time, maintaining skin elasticity and subcutaneous architectural integrity as fat decreases—reducing the need for multiple aesthetic procedures and offering a few-session, disease-modifying intervention with clear clinical translatability.

Title
PRE-LOAD: A pre-emptive, anisotropic, resorbable micro‑lattice to preserve dermal ECM and subcutaneous fibrous septa during weight loss

Central hypothesis (merged with research question)
If the skin–fat unit is pre-loaded with an oriented, stress-bearing, mechano-instructive scaffold that spans dermis to superficial fascia, fibroblasts will deposit aligned collagen along native tension vectors, maintaining dermal elastic function and preventing septal buckling as adipocyte volume decreases—without impairing lipolysis. Can such a few-session, resorbable, clinically translatable scaffold outperform post hoc immune-modulatory strategies in preventing contour laxity?

Atomic strategy
Program the mechanical field in advance. Inject an in situ–forming, anisotropically aligned micro‑lattice that temporarily bears tensile load and templates collagen along natural stress lines (Langer’s lines and septal vectors); as fat volume decreases, load transfers to the maturing collagen framework while the scaffold hydrolyzes away.

Specific aims
1) Engineering: Create an injectable, shear‑alignable micro‑lattice that bridges the deep dermis–subcutis interface and resists early protease bursts while degrading on a 6–9 month clock.
2) Mechanism and selectivity: Demonstrate that the scaffold maintains fibroblast mechanotransduction and aligned collagen/elastin architecture while leaving adipocyte lipolysis kinetics unchanged.
3) Efficacy vs. post hoc control: In large-animal weight‑loss models, test whether pre‑loading preserves elasticity and septal integrity better than interventions started after weight loss.

Scaffold design and formulation
- Composition: Hyaluronan–PEG Michael-addition hydrogel (HA‑SH + 4‑arm PEG‑VS). Rationale: clinically familiar backbones, low immunogenicity, tunable modulus/viscoelasticity, hyaluronidase reversibility for safety.
- Architecture: Point‑of‑care extrusion of 50–150 μm microstrands through a multiport fan‑tip cannula; injection shear aligns strands along the cannula path. Two depth planes: deep reticular dermis and superficial subcutis; the microstrands interpenetrate to form a continuous anisotropic lattice that couples dermis and fibrous septa.
- Mechanics: Initial storage modulus 2–4 kPa (dermal range) with high strain‑stiffening to carry tensile loads without bulk stiffening the tissue. Viscoelastic relaxation tuned (t1/2 ≈ 30–60 s) to permit physiologic motion while maintaining alignment.
- Degradation: Dual-pathway linkers—(i) hydrolytically cleavable ester spacers (target t50 ≈ 6–9 months) for time‑based resorption, (ii) a minority of MMP‑sensitive linkers shielded within dense microstrand cores to limit early proteolysis yet permit late cellular remodeling. No bioactive drug payloads (mechanics-only instruction).
- Immunoquiet features: Endotoxin‑screened excipients; zwitterionic surfactant trace to limit protein fouling; porosity >30% to preserve perfusion and lymphatic flow.
- Reversibility: On‑label hyaluronidase enables emergency partial removal.

Preclinical plan

Aim 1: Engineering and mapping
- Bench characterization: Rheology (G′, nonlinearity), creep/relaxation, fiber alignment index (confocal + structure tensor), permeability, enzymatic/hydrolytic degradation kinetics at 37°C, mechanical fatigue over 10^6 cycles.
- Tissue conformability: Ex vivo human abdominoplasty skin–fat slabs; ultrasound-guided delivery to validate dermis–subcutis spanning and lattice continuity; SHG microscopy to quantify alignment transfer to native collagen.
- Injection mapping protocol: Align cannula passes with Langer’s lines (surface) and ultrasound-defined septal vectors (depth). “Skip‑lattice” pattern (1 cm pitch) to minimize material while achieving percolation.

Aim 2: Mechanism and selectivity
- Small animal model: Diet‑induced obese rats placed on caloric restriction or GLP‑1 agonist; unilateral flank treated pre‑loss vs contralateral control.
- Mechanotransduction: Immunostaining for YAP/TAZ nuclear localization, pFAK; fibroblast orientation vs lattice (~θ error). ECM metrics: collagen I/III ratio, elastin content (tropoelastin, LOX), fiber coherency by SHG.
- Protease milieu: In vivo MMP activity imaging and zymography; scaffold integrity vs native ECM degradation over time.
- Lipolysis non‑interference: Microdialysis for glycerol/NEFA flux during isoproterenol/insulin clamps; ex vivo adipose lobule lipolysis assays ± scaffold proximity; RNA-seq for adipocyte β‑AR, HSL/ATGL expression. Acceptance: ≤10% deviation from control lipolysis kinetics.

Aim 3: Large‑animal efficacy and head‑to‑head
- Model: Obese minipigs (n≥6) undergoing 15–20% weight loss over 16–20 weeks.
- Arms: (A) Pre‑load scaffold at week −2; (B) Vehicle control; (C) Post hoc immune‑modulation (e.g., anti‑inflammatory topical/biologic started at week 6; no direct mechanical support).
- Endpoints:
  - Primary: Regional elastography (shear‑wave) of dermis and superficial fat; cutometer skin retraction (R2/R5); 3D optical contour change (ptosis index).
  - Septal integrity: HF‑ultrasound + micro‑CT with contrast to quantify septal angle, connectivity, buckling strain.
  - Histology: Collagen orientation coherency, elastin preservation, adipocyte size distribution, macrophage infiltration (CD68), fibrosis score.
  - Safety: Nodule rate, vascular compromise (Doppler), lymphatic flow (ICG lymphography), systemic chemistries.
- Success criteria (vs control): ≥25% preservation of elastic modulus, ≥30% higher collagen alignment coherency, ≥30% reduction in septal buckling index; non‑inferior lipolysis metrics; no increase in adverse events.

Clinical translation plan
- Indication: Prevention of skin laxity during intentional weight loss (including pharmacologic weight‑loss programs).
- Procedure: Two-session regimen—baseline (week −2 to 0) full‑field lattice injection under ultrasound guidance; optional touch‑up at week 8 for high‑velocity weight loss trajectories. Outpatient; 18–22G fan‑tip cannula; local anesthesia.
- First‑in‑human pilot (n=30): Adults on GLP‑1 therapy targeting ≥10% weight loss. Randomized split‑body design (treated vs internal control). Primary at 6 months: elastography, blinded aesthetic panel contour grading. Secondary: patient‑reported outcomes (BODY‑Q), ultrasound septal metrics, safety. Follow‑up to 12 months for scaffold clearance.

Manufacturability and regulatory path
- Materials: Pharmaceutical‑grade HA‑SH and PEG‑VS, sterile dual‑syringe kit with static mixer and multiport cannula; room‑temperature gelation (pH 7.4) within 3–5 minutes.
- CMC: GMP synthesis, endotoxin control, residuals <10 ppm, lot‑release on gel time, modulus, viscosity.
- Regulatory: Likely Class III combination (resorbable implantable filler); pathway analogous to HA fillers but with added performance testing. Bench/animal data above support IDE; human reversibility via hyaluronidase strengthens safety case.

Risk analysis and mitigations
- Nodule/overfill: Low‑density “skip‑lattice”; reversible with hyaluronidase; ultrasound mapping to avoid boluses.
- Vascular/lymphatic compromise: Large‑pore, low‑volume passes; Doppler guidance in high‑risk areas.
- Interference with fat loss: Validated in Aim 2; restrict placement to septal/dermal planes, not intralobular.
- Over‑stiffening/scar: Target G′ ≤4 kPa and high porosity; no pro‑fibrotic payloads; monitor myofibroblast markers.

Novelty and IP strategy
- Core claims: (i) Pre‑emptive, anisotropic, injectable micro‑lattice that spans dermis and subcutaneous septa to prevent septal buckling during adipocyte volume loss; (ii) Shear‑aligned, pre‑strained lattice deposited along mapped Langer’s and septal vectors; (iii) Dual‑pathway degradation (hydrolytic clock + shielded protease‑cleavable minority) to resist early MMP surges while enabling late remodeling; (iv) Use of hyaluronidase reversibility as a safety feature in a pre‑emptive contour‑preservation indication.
- Freedom to operate: Distinct from isotropic fillers and from energy‑based skin tightening; distinct from post hoc anti‑inflammatory or antifibrotic drugs.

Milestones and go/no‑go
- M1 (Month 6): Achieve aligned micro‑lattice with coherency ≥0.6 and G′ 2–4 kPa; degradation t50 6–9 months. Go if met.
- M2 (Month 12): Rodent model shows preserved elastography (+≥20%) and non‑inferior lipolysis (≤10% delta). Go if met.
- M3 (Month 20): Minipig efficacy meets success criteria; clean safety. Proceed to IDE.
- Kill criteria: Any persistent lipolysis impairment >10%, lymphatic obstruction, or pro‑fibrotic response (α‑SMA↑, collagen crosslinking↑) vs control.

Expected outcome and impact
A few‑session, mechanics‑only, reversible intervention that preserves skin elasticity and contour by templating ECM before fat loss begins—selectively shielding dermal networks and fibrous septa without touching lipolysis—establishing a new, pre‑emptive standard beyond post hoc immune control.

text:
Title
Mechanopriming the skin before weight loss: acoustically driven fibroblast epigenetic entrainment to preserve dermal ECM and subcutaneous fibrous septa during fat reduction

Integrated Hypothesis-Question
Can a short, pre-diet course of spatially targeted, cyclic micromechanical stimulation “train” dermal and septal fibroblasts to establish a durable, pro-elastocollagen remodeling memory—via YAP/TAZ-dependent chromatin bookmarking—so that, as adipocytes shrink during subsequent caloric lipolysis, the dermal collagen/elastin network and subcutaneous fibrous septa maintain tensile architecture and do not collapse?

Atomic Strategy
Impart a precisely dosed mechanical waveform to fibroblasts in the reticular dermis and fibrous septa using biodegradable, acoustically responsive hyaluronan microgels as local force amplifiers plus low‑intensity focused ultrasound (LIFU). This transient “mechanopriming” induces mechanotransduction programs (YAP/TAZ→MRTF‑A/TEAD; FBLN5/ELN/LOX up; TIMP1/3 up; MMP1/3/9 restrained) and establishes epigenetic bookmarks (H3K27ac/H3K4me3 at ECM enhancers) that persist for weeks, selectively reinforcing ECM without inhibiting adipocyte lipolysis.

Specific Aims
1) Establish a mechanical dose and waveform that induces durable pro-ECM memory in human dermal and septal fibroblasts with minimal fibrosis risk.
2) Engineer and validate injectable, biodegradable, acoustically responsive HA microgels that localize to reticular dermis and fibrous septa and amplify safe LIFU fields.
3) Demonstrate, in large-animal and pilot human studies, that pre-diet mechanopriming preserves dermal elasticity and septal integrity during controlled weight loss while leaving lipolysis intact.

Platform Components
- Microgel amplifier (MG-A): sterile, injectable hyaluronan-tyramine/gelatin-methacrylate porous microgels (40–120 μm), enzymatically degradable (t1/2 ~6–10 weeks), compressibility > tissue to enhance local strain under LIFU; lightly loaded with trace SPIO for ultrasound/MRI visualization; no bioactive drugs.
- Energy delivery: LIFU at 1–3 MHz, spatial-peak temporal-average intensity 30–120 mW/cm2, 10–20% duty, envelope 0.5–1.5 Hz, 8–12 min per field, 2–3 fields per zone; guided by ultrasound to confine to dermis/septa.
- Imaging feedback: shear-wave elastography and ARFI to map local strain; microgel localization by power Doppler/hyperechoic speckle; optional MRI for septal tracking.
- Treatment schedule: two to three sessions on days −28, −14, and optional −7 relative to diet start; no further treatments during weight loss.

Mechanism of Action
- Local cyclic microstrain (0.5–3%) at fibroblast length scale aligns and densifies pericellular matrix; integrin/FAK activation drives nuclear YAP/TAZ and MRTF‑A.
- Transcriptional upregulation: COL1A1/3A1, ELN, FBLN5, LOX/LOXL1, FBN1, LTBP4, TIMP1/3; restrained MMP1/3/9; organized microfibril assembly and elastin crosslinking.
- Epigenetic memory: increased accessibility and H3K27ac at ECM super-enhancers; sustained TEAD occupancy; reduced miR‑29 and miR‑146a; memory half-life targeted at 6–12 weeks.
- Septal reinforcement: amplified strain within fibrous septa biases fibro-adipogenic progenitors toward matrix-supportive fibroblasts without myofibroblast persistence; collagen bundles maintain anisotropy and buckle resistance as adipocytes shrink.
- Selectivity: parameters avoid cavitation and thermal rise; fields and microgels are spatially restricted to dermis/septa, sparing adipocyte parenchyma; no agents that alter lipid metabolism are used.

Preclinical Plan
In vitro/ex vivo (Months 0–9)
- Human primary reticular-dermal fibroblasts and septal fibroblasts in 3D collagen-elastin hydrogels under cyclic strain (0.5–3%, 1 Hz, 10 min/day ×3 days).
- Readouts (days 1–42): RNA-seq (ECM genes), ATAC-seq and CUT&RUN (H3K27ac, TEAD1/4), YAP/TAZ nuclear fraction, elastin fiber imaging (EM, two-photon), collagen alignment (SHG), MMP/TIMP activity, α‑SMA resolution kinetics.
- Human abdominoplasty skin-fat explants with MG-A distribution; LIFU dosing matrix; microstrain mapping by digital volume correlation.

Large animal (porcine, Months 6–18)
- N=12 minipigs; flank zones randomized: Control, LIFU-only, MG-A only, MG-A+LIFU.
- Mechanopriming at −28/−14 days; then 12-week caloric reduction (10–15% weight loss).
- Endpoints: dermal thickness and elastic modulus (cutometer, elastography), SHG/EM fiber architecture, septal integrity (MRI/MRE), adipocyte size distribution (histomorphometry), serum glycerol/NEFA (systemic lipolysis), local lipolysis imaging (Dixon MRI). Safety: CK, inflammatory markers; off-target effects.

Translational pilot (IDE/EFS, Months 18–30)
- Open-label, N=20, BMI 27–35; abdomen/flanks.
- Two mechanopriming sessions at −28/−14 days; 12-week standardized diet and activity.
- Primary: change in skin retraction ratio and elastic modulus vs matched untreated area; septal continuity score by MRI; blinded photo-derived contour metrics.
- Secondary: patient-reported laxity; biopsy subset for ECM gene expression and H3K27ac persistence.
- Safety: pain, edema, nodules, fibrosis; metabolic labs; no differences in weight-loss kinetics between treated and control zones.

Dose and Field Engineering
- Target pericellular strain: 1–2% peak; pulse train: 1 Hz, 600 cycles/session; 2–3 sessions.
- Microgel volume fraction: dermis 0.5–1.0% v/v; septa 0.2–0.5% v/v via fanning cannula technique along septal tracts.
- Real-time titration: if shear-wave velocity increase >20% during session, reduce intensity by 25%; aim for 10–15% acute stiffening that resolves to 5–8% at 24 h.

Selectivity: Preserving Lipolysis While Reinforcing ECM
- Spatial selectivity: ultrasound focus limited to 2–4 mm below epidermis for dermis and linear passes along septa; avoid homogeneous insonation of adipocyte lobules.
- Biologic selectivity: no adipocyte cytotoxicity; confirm via glycerol release assays and perilipin staining; systemic lipolysis (glycerol/NEFA) and regional adipocyte size reduction equivalent between treated/untreated zones.
- Parametric guardrails: I-SPTA ≤120 mW/cm2; MI ≤0.5; absolute temp rise <0.5°C.

Manufacturability and Regulatory Path
- MG-A: HA-tyramine/GelMA microgels via microfluidic droplet polymerization; ISO 10993 biocompatibility; terminal sterilization with low-dose e-beam; SPIO concentration <0.05% w/w.
- Device: LIFU platform with imaging guidance; existing LIPUS safety pedigree.
- Combination product: drug-device; pursue 505(b)(2)/de novo pathway leveraging HA and LIPUS precedents; initial EFS under IDE with cGMP microgel production.

Novelty and IP Position
- Use of biodegradable, acoustically responsive HA microgels as sub-epidermal “mechanical amplifiers” to epigenetically entrain fibroblasts prior to weight loss.
- Defined preconditioning waveform and dosing algorithm guided by elastography to induce durable ECM-specific chromatin bookmarking without fibrosis.
- Targeted deposition into subcutaneous fibrous septa to prevent septal collapse during adipocyte volume loss.
- Methods claims on timing (−28/−14 day window), spatial targeting, biomarker panel (YAP/TAZ nuclear persistence + H3K27ac at ELN/FBLN5/LOX enhancers), and imaging-based dose control.

Risk Analysis and Mitigations
- Fibrosis risk: limit sessions; monitor α‑SMA resolution within 7–10 days; cease if persistent; use lower duty cycles.
- Nodule formation: optimize microgel size distribution (D50 ~70 μm), porosity, and degradation rate; ultrasound guidance to avoid bolus clumping.
- Insufficient elastogenesis: adjust envelope frequency and session spacing; enrich septal targeting where elastin fiber anchorage dominates.
- Off-target adipocyte effects: maintain low MI; restrict exposure volume; real-time thermometry.

Milestones and Go/No-Go
- M1 (Month 6): in vitro memory signature ≥8 weeks (sustained H3K27ac and ECM gene upregulation after stimulus removal).
- M2 (Month 12): porcine model shows ≥20% improvement in elastic modulus and ≥30% reduction in septal discontinuities vs control with no change in adipocyte size reduction.
- M3 (Month 24): human pilot achieves ≥1 grade improvement in validated skin laxity scale vs contralateral control with noninferior weight loss kinetics.

Clinical Use Concept
- Two brief pre-diet visits for image-guided MG-A placement and LIFU mechanopriming; patient then completes standard weight-loss program with no maintenance treatments.
- Indications: anticipated rapid or moderate weight loss (diet, GLP‑1 therapy taper, postpartum, post-bariatric), areas prone to laxity (abdomen, flanks, upper arms, thighs).

Success Criteria
Demonstrate that preconditioning alone—without ongoing therapy—maintains dermal elasticity and septal architecture during fat mass reduction, preserving contour while leaving lipolysis efficiency unchanged.

text:
Title
Deep Fractional Photochemical Crosslinking (DF‑PCXL) to Pre‑Strengthen Dermal ECM and Subcutaneous Fibrous Septa Prior to Weight Loss

Unified Hypothesis/Research Question
If we pre‑strengthen the skin’s load‑bearing scaffolds (dermal collagen/elastin network and subcutaneous fibrous septa) with depth‑targeted, spatially fractionated, visible‑light photochemical crosslinking while the tissue is gently pre‑strained, then subsequent adipose volume reduction will proceed without septal collapse or dermal laxity, preserving skin elasticity and contour without impairing lipolysis.

Atomic Strategy
Create a patterned, depth‑specific, light‑activated crosslinking “backbone” within the dermis and upper subcutaneous septa before weight loss, using riboflavin- or rose bengal–mediated visible‑light photochemistry delivered through light‑guiding microneedles under controlled mechanical pre‑strain. This increases tensile strength and fatigue resistance of the ECM where loads concentrate, without altering adipocyte metabolism.

Specific Aims
1) Engineer a clinically translatable DF‑PCXL platform that deposits chromophore and light at two discrete depths (upper/mid‑dermis and upper subcutis) while applying mild tissue pre‑strain.
2) Quantify how DF‑PCXL alters multiscale mechanics (tension, shear, creep/fatigue) and microarchitecture (collagen/elastin alignment, septal integrity).
3) Test whether DF‑PCXL, given 2–6 weeks prior to diet‑induced fat loss, prevents dermal thinning and septal buckling without impeding lipolysis.
4) Define dose, fractionation, and safety margins to maintain physiologic compliance and avoid over‑stiffening or fibrosis.

Mechanistic Rationale
- Visible‑light photosensitizers (riboflavin 450–470 nm; or rose bengal 520–545 nm) generate singlet oxygen–mediated covalent crosslinks (e.g., dityrosine and lysine‑derived) between collagen/elastin amino acid residues.
- Spatial fractionation (micro‑islands of reinforced ECM amid normal tissue) preserves overall compliance while raising yield strength and reducing creep.
- Pre‑strain during illumination aligns fibers; crosslinking under load “locks in” anisotropic reinforcement along physiologic tension lines and septal axes.
- Adipocytes are spared: illumination and chromophores at chosen fluences do not impact triglyceride hydrolysis pathways; treatment is extra‑cellular and structural, not metabolic.
- Reinforced septa distribute stress as fat lobules shrink, preventing microtears and node‑to‑node collapse that telegraph as surface laxity.

Platform Modality (Few‑Session Intervention)
- Device: Reusable handpiece with interchangeable, sterile, light‑guiding microneedle arrays (lengths 1.5–6.0 mm; two‑tiered). Each needle is a side‑emitting polymer waveguide fed by high‑power blue/green LEDs; integrated thermistors for closed‑loop thermal control (<41°C).
- Delivery: Hydrogel‑based, low‑diffusivity chromophore formulation (riboflavin‑5’‑phosphate or rose bengal 0.05–0.2%) loaded into the microneedle bores for intradermal/subdermal deposition at insertion; optional hyaluronidase‑free to limit spread.
- Mechanics: Vacuum‑assisted cup (−15 to −25 kPa) applies gentle, uniform pre‑strain and stabilizes tissue thickness; optional dynamic shear pulses to align septa.
- Dosing: 1–2 sessions, 14–28 days pre‑weight‑loss; 10–20% fractional coverage per session in a honeycomb pattern; fluence 3–15 J/cm² per depth, duty‑cycled to avoid heating.
- Procedure time: 20–45 minutes for abdomen/flanks; topical anesthetic only.

Selectivity and Preservation of Lipolysis
- Crosslinking targets ECM proteins; adipocyte membranes and enzymes (ATGL, HSL) are not directly modulated.
- No pharmacologic anti‑lipolytic agents used; diet/GLP‑1s/bariatric or exercise‑induced fat loss proceeds unaltered.
- Patterned reinforcement prevents load‑induced MMP surges that typically follow rapid lobule shrinkage, indirectly reducing ECM degradation while sparing adipocyte biology.

Preclinical Plan
Models
- Ex vivo: Human abdominoplasty skin‑fat slabs (10–25 mm thickness) for depth‑resolved optics and mechanics.
- In vivo: Mini‑pig flank/abdomen; murine diet‑induced obesity with caloric restriction–driven weight loss.

Endpoints and Assays
- Optics/Dosimetry: Monte Carlo modeling and optical coherence tomography to validate light distribution at target depths; dye concentration mapping by MALDI imaging.
- Crosslinking Biochemistry: Dityrosine fluorescence; LC‑MS crosslink quantification; LOX‑independent vs LOX‑assisted crosslink signatures; ROS by EPR spin trapping to set safe windows.
- Mechanics: Uniaxial/biaxial tensile tests, shear rheology, cyclic creep/fatigue; cutometer and shear‑wave elastography in vivo; burst strength of isolated septa.
- Architecture: Second‑harmonic generation (collagen alignment), multiphoton elastin autofluorescence; micro‑CT with iodine contrast for septal lattice integrity; ultrasound to quantify septal thickness/continuity.
- Function Under Weight Loss: 3D surface scanning (ptosis, contour index), blinded photo‑scoring; histology for septal buckling/microtears; adipocyte size distribution; serum glycerol/FFA; ex vivo glycerol release from treated vs control fat pads.
- Safety: CPD/6‑4PP DNA adducts (confirm absent with visible light); TUNEL (adipocytes/fibroblasts); thermal maps; nociceptor immunostaining; mast cell activation; delayed hypersensitivity; range‑of‑motion/compliance testing to avoid over‑stiffening.
- Selectivity: qPCR/ELISA for MMP‑1/2/9, TIMP‑1/2; lipolysis gene panel; scRNA‑seq of fibroblasts/adipocytes to ensure no pro‑fibrotic drift.

Dosing Matrix and Fractionation
- Variables: chromophore (riboflavin vs rose bengal), concentration, light wavelength/fluence, duty cycle, fraction size/spacing, pre‑strain magnitude.
- Optimization goal: Raise septal yield strength ≥30% and dermal modulus at low strain by 10–20% while maintaining tangent modulus at high strain within 10% of baseline and preserving skin recoil (R2 on cutometry ≥ baseline).

First‑in‑Human Feasibility (n=20; open‑label, split‑area)
- Population: Adults planning ≥10% weight loss over 12–24 weeks (dietary ± GLP‑1), BMI 28–38, abdomen/flanks.
- Intervention: DF‑PCXL at week −4 and −1 pre‑program; contralateral control.
- Primary Outcomes (week 24): Change in ptosis angle, contour uniformity, and laxity grade; noninferiority of lipolysis (ultrasound‑measured fat thickness reduction equivalent between sides).
- Secondary: Patient‑reported appearance/fit scores; elasticity (R0, R2); safety (AEs, dysesthesia, dyspigmentation).
- Imaging: Shear‑wave elastography and 3D surface topography; MRI Dixon (subset) to visualize septal architecture.

Manufacturability and Regulatory Path
- Device: Class II LED light source with sterile, disposable polymeric optical microneedle array; leverages existing materials (PMMA/PC waveguides, cyclic olefin polymers); vacuum cup from predicate RF/laser devices.
- Drug Component: Low‑dose riboflavin‑5’‑phosphate or rose bengal topical/intradermal solution; combination product with a well‑characterized photosensitizer; local exposure minimizes systemic risk.
- Quality: In‑process dosimetry, needle emission uniformity, chromophore lot photostability; shelf‑stable kits.
- Feasibility: Few‑session regimen aligns with elective aesthetic/adjunctive metabolic care.

Novelty and IP Rationale
- Depth‑specific, fractionated ECM crosslinking in skin/subcutis using light‑guiding microneedles under defined pre‑strain.
- Dual‑depth illumination targeting both dermis and subcutaneous septa in one pass.
- Low‑diffusivity chromophore depot that confines crosslinking to predefined islets, preserving global compliance.
- Protocolized pre‑conditioning timing relative to weight‑loss onset.

Key Risks and Mitigations
- Over‑stiffening/fibrosis: Use fractional pattern, capped fluence, and pre‑specified mechanical endpoints; abort criteria via real‑time elastography.
- Nerve or vascular injury: Ultrasound‑guided depth mapping; needle length matched to regional maps; side‑emission profile avoids hot spots.
- Pigmentation changes: Visible light and low thermal load reduce risk; include Fitzpatrick IV–VI cohorts with cautious dosing.
- Insufficient septal reach in very thick pannus: Longer arrays (6–8 mm) or staged passes; focus on upper septal network that governs surface contour.

Milestones and Success Criteria (18–24 months)
- M1: Demonstrate confined crosslink islets with ≥2× dityrosine signal and <1°C peak temperature rise ex vivo.
- M2: Achieve targeted mechanical gains (Aim 2) with preserved high‑strain compliance in pig model.
- M3: In vivo weight‑loss study shows ≥30% reduction in laxity/ptosis metrics on treated side with equal fat‑thickness loss vs control.
- M4: Complete GLP safety and submit IDE for first‑in‑human trial.

Expected Impact
A pre‑emptive, few‑session, structure‑preserving adjunct that allows patients to lose fat volume while maintaining dermal elasticity and septal integrity, reducing post‑weight‑loss skin laxity without altering lipolysis or requiring extensive post hoc correction.

Title
Pre-weight-loss mechanopreconditioning with resorbable subdermal micro-tensioners to preserve dermal ECM and subcutaneous fibrous septa during fat reduction

Core hypothesis (inseparable from research goal)
If we reset cutaneous tensional homeostasis before caloric or pharmacologic fat loss by delivering gentle, sustained subdermal tensile loading, dermal fibroblasts and septal fibro-adipogenic cells will reorganize and strengthen collagen-elastin scaffolds and fibrous septa without impairing adipocyte lipolysis. This preconditioning will maintain skin elasticity and contour as fat volume decreases.

Atomic strategy
A single perturbation: impose a controlled, low-amplitude, long-duration tensile pre-stress across the dermis–superficial fat interface using temporary, bioresorbable “micro-tensioner” lattices placed pre-weight loss. The pre-stress drives mechano-transcriptional programs (integrin–YAP/TAZ–LOX/ELN axis), increasing fiber alignment, crosslinking, and septal thickness, thereby preventing ECM degradation and septal collapse when adipocyte volume shrinks.

Therapeutic platform (clinically translatable, few-session)
Modality: MECHAPREP micro-tensioners
- Form factor: 20 × 20 mm ultra-thin, perforated lattices (thickness 250–400 µm) of medical-grade PCL or PLGA-PCL copolymer struts joined by hygroscopic PEG-based hydrogel nodes.
- Mechanism of action: after percutaneous placement into the superficial adipose (just below the dermis), hydrogel nodes absorb interstitial fluid and expand 25–40% over 5–7 days, exerting a constant, sub-physiologic outward traction (target 0.5–1.5 kPa surface-equivalent stress; ~5–10% local tissue strain) maintained for 6–10 weeks, then gradually decline as the device resorbs by 16–20 weeks.
- Anchoring: micro-fenestrated, non-cutting dermal/septal “micro-crowns” that distribute load over a broad area to avoid focal ischemia and lymphatic compression.
- Safety features: high-void lattice to preserve perfusion; radiolucent and ultrasound-visible markers; buffered polymer (carbonate microfillers) to limit local acidosis during resorption.
- Procedure: one session under local anesthesia via 14–16G blunt cannula; ultrasound-guided planar deployment of tiles along Langer’s lines with 10–20 mm spacing to create a quasi-isotropic tensile field. No removal required.

Mechanistic rationale (selective preservation without blocking lipolysis)
- Dermis: sustained tensile load increases integrin clustering (α2β1/α5β1/αv), nuclear YAP/TAZ localization, and synthesis/organization of COL1A1/COL3A1, elastin (ELN), fibrillin-1, fibulin-5, and decorin; upregulates lysyl oxidase (LOX/LOXL2) for crosslinking; reduces MMP1/3 expression; aligns fibers along stress lines, improving shear modulus and recoil.
- Fibrous septa: load-bearing cues thicken and align collagenous septa that suspend fat lobules, preventing their bowing and collapse during adipocyte shrinkage; preserves the superficial fascial system continuity.
- Adipocytes: mechanical field magnitude and distribution are chosen to avoid compression; lipolysis signaling (β-adrenergic–HSL/ATGL) and perfusion are preserved.

Indications and timing
- Candidates: individuals planning large or rapid fat loss (GLP-1 therapy initiation, bariatric surgery, or aggressive caloric deficit), and patients undergoing regional lipolysis (e.g., cryolipolysis, ultrasound).
- Timeline: implantation at T−6 to −8 weeks; begin weight-loss program at T0; device maintains pre-stress through the rapid-loss window (T0 to T+12 weeks); resorbs by T+16–20 weeks after ECM reinforcement is established.

Specific aims
Aim 1. Define the mechanobiologic dose that maximizes ECM reinforcement while preserving lipolysis.
- Models: (a) human abdominoplasty dermis–superficial fat explants mounted in biaxial stretch bioreactors; (b) 3D human skin–fat organoids.
- Dosing matrix: stress 0.3–2.0 kPa; strain 3–15%; duration 1–10 weeks.
- Readouts: SHG/TPEF for collagen/elastin organization; immuno (COL1/3, ELN, FBN1, FBLN5, LOX/LOXL2, MMP1/3); YAP/TAZ nuclear:cytoplasmic ratio; mechanical testing (tangent modulus, hysteresis, residual strain); septal thickness/alignment by polarized microscopy.
- Lipolysis selectivity: isoproterenol-stimulated glycerol/NEFA release, pHSLSer660, ATGL levels, oxygenation (pimonidazole) under load vs. control.

Aim 2. Engineer and validate MECHAPREP micro-tensioners to deliver the target mechanodose in vivo.
- Design targets: near-constant traction despite tissue creep (osmotic hydrogel with slow swelling kinetics, pre-curved struts for spring-like force compensation).
- Bench: force–displacement in gel surrogates; fatigue and creep over 12 weeks; degradation (mass loss, pH, byproducts).
- Biocompatibility: ISO 10993 panel (cytotox, irritation, sensitization, systemic toxicity, genotox), extractables/leachables; particulate shedding.
- Imaging: ultrasound visibility and placement fidelity.

Aim 3. Demonstrate preservation of skin elasticity and contour during induced weight loss in a large-animal model and in a first-in-human pilot.
- Large-animal study (porcine; n≈8): bilateral abdominal fields randomized to MECHAPREP vs. sham; GLP-1 or caloric restriction to induce 15–20% body-weight loss over 8–10 weeks.
  - In-life metrics: 3D surface scanning (sag index, curvature retention), ultrasound shear-wave elastography (kPa), OCT elastography of dermis, high-frequency ultrasound for septal continuity, perfusion (laser speckle).
  - Endpoint histology: SHG collagen alignment index, elastin fiber length/branching, septal thickness, MMP/LOX balance; tensile testing of dermis and dermis–fat composite.
  - Lipolysis: ex vivo catecholamine-stimulated glycerol release and pHSL from adipose biopsies.
- Human early feasibility (single-arm, n=20): abdomen/arms prepped at T−6 weeks, begin GLP-1 at T0.
  - Primary endpoint (T+12 weeks): change in skin shear modulus vs. baseline; 3D photogrammetry sag index.
  - Secondary: Cutometer recoil (R2/R7), dermatologist-rated laxity scales, patient-reported contour satisfaction, adverse events.
  - Exploratory biomarkers: serum PRO-C3/C6 neo-epitopes; suction blister proteomics for ECM remodeling signatures.

Clinical workflow (few sessions)
- Visit 1: assessment and ultrasound mapping; deploy tiles (30–60 minutes per region).
- Remote monitoring: optional adhesive wearable that logs regional strain via ultrasound-guided calibration at week 2.
- Visit 2 (week 6–8): confirm placement/strain; initiate or continue weight loss if not already started.
- No removal required.

Selectivity safeguards
- Stress window capped at 1.5 kPa; high-void lattice to avoid vascular/lymphatic compression.
- Placement in superficial fat with ultrasound clearance from perforators.
- Exclusion: severe thin dermis (<1.2 mm), uncontrolled coagulopathy, active dermatologic disease.

Risk analysis and mitigation
- Inflammation: buffered polymers; slow-degrading PCL blend; preclinical histopathology thresholds.
- Nerve entrapment: non-cutting anchors; deployment depth guides.
- Infection: single-dose peri-procedural antibiotics; resorbable device eliminates removal breach.

Manufacturability and regulatory path
- Materials and processes aligned with existing resorbable implant manufacturing (injection-molded PCL lattices; photopolymerized PEG hydrogel nodes; gamma or EtO sterilization).
- Regulatory: De Novo 510(k)-like pathway for Class II temporary subdermal soft-tissue support with intended use: “temporary cutaneous mechanopreconditioning prior to planned weight loss to reduce skin laxity.”
- Preclinical: ISO 10993, mechanical characterization, degradation profiles, animal safety, and proof-of-effect.

Intellectual property (novelty)
- Method: preconditioning skin with resorbable micro-tensioners prior to planned systemic or regional fat loss to preserve elasticity and contour.
- Device: osmotic-node lattice that maintains near-constant low-level traction despite tissue creep; dermal-septa distributing micro-crowns; buffered bioresorbable composition.
- Dosing: definition of mechanobiologic dose window (stress/strain/time) for selective ECM reinforcement without impairing lipolysis.
- Biomarker-guided titration: ultrasound elastography and SHG-derived alignment indices to individualize tile density and placement.

Quantitative success criteria (go/no-go)
- Aim 1: ≥30% increase in SHG collagen alignment index and ≥20% increase in dermal tangent modulus vs. unloaded controls; no reduction in catecholamine-stimulated glycerol release (non-inferiority margin −10%).
- Aim 2: device maintains 0.5–1.5 kPa traction ±20% over 8 weeks in bench gels; ISO 10993 pass.
- Aim 3 animal: ≥25% reduction in sag index and ≥20% increase in shear modulus vs. sham at equal fat loss; septal thickness +20% with intact perfusion markers.
- Human pilot: median improvement in laxity grade by ≥1 point and ≥15% increase in shear modulus at T+12 weeks; SAE rate <5%.

Development timeline (18–24 months to first-in-human)
- Months 0–6: in vitro dose mapping; device design freeze; bench tests; ISO 10993 initiation.
- Months 6–12: large-animal efficacy/safety; manufacturing scale-up.
- Months 12–18: regulatory submission; first-in-human pilot enrollment.
- Months 18–24: readout and pivotal trial design.

Anticipated impact
By resetting the mechanical “set point” of the dermis–fat unit before volume loss, this single-intervention, resorbable device preserves the skin’s scaffold and the subcutaneous support network while allowing unimpeded lipolysis, enabling durable contour maintenance with minimal visits and clear translational feasibility.

text:
Project title: PRETENSE—Pre-Tension Encoding of Dermal and Septal ECM to Preserve Skin Contour During Subsequent Fat Loss

Integrated hypothesis-goal (question cannot be distinguished):
If we encode a new, shorter resting length and higher buckling resistance into the dermal collagen–elastin network and subcutaneous fibrous septa via controlled cyclic mechanostimulation coupled to transient pro-elastogenic cofactor delivery, will the skin maintain elasticity and contour when adipose volume later decreases without impairing lipolysis?

Atomic strategy:
Encode residual pre-tension and elastin-rich, oriented reinforcement in dermis and fibrous septa before weight loss by synchronizing low-frequency cyclic strain and mild heat with microdosed copper/ascorbate to bias LOX-mediated crosslinking and elastic fiber assembly, thereby increasing tensile set, anisotropic modulus, and septal critical load—without targeting adipocytes or beta-adrenergic pathways.

Platform and intervention:
- Device: Handheld applicator delivering patterned cyclic negative pressure and lateral shear with closed-loop thermal control.
  - Parameters (tunable by anatomy): 15–25 kPa vacuum; 0.2–0.7 Hz; 5–12% tissue strain; 2–4 mm shear amplitude; 41–42°C at dermis for 12–16 minutes per field (two fields/session).
  - Vectoring: Shear oriented along Langer’s lines for dermis and radially across superficial adipose to load fibrous septa in tension and torsion.
- Patch: Dissolvable microneedle array (300–500 μm) worn under the applicator, releasing within 10 minutes:
  - Copper peptide (GHK-Cu, 0.5–1 mg/site) as LOX cofactor source.
  - Ascorbate (5–10 mg/site) for prolyl/lysyl hydroxylase activity and tropoelastin maturation.
  - Excipient: Hyaluronan matrix (50–150 kDa) to increase interstitial residence and mechanotransductive hydration.
- Treatment schedule: 2–3 sessions over 4–6 weeks completed before initiating caloric deficit or pharmacologic weight-loss therapy.

Mechanism of action (systems view):
- Dermis:
  - Cyclic strain + mild heat → integrin/FAK → YAP/TAZ nuclear localization → upregulation of COL1A1/3A1, ELN, FBLN5, FBN1, LOX; suppression of MMP1/9 via mechanosensitive signaling and thermal shock proteins.
  - Copper/ascorbate bias endogenous LOX-mediated crosslinking toward mature, elastic fiber–anchored architecture rather than scar-like random fibrosis.
  - Repetitive oriented loading aligns collagen crimp and elastic fibers along Langer’s lines, reducing post-loss laxity by shortening functional resting length (tensile set).
- Subcutaneous fibrous septa:
  - Alternating suction–shear loads perilobular septa, stimulating fibroblast matrix synthesis and increasing septal thickness/anisotropic stiffness; torsional cycles raise Euler buckling threshold during later adipose deflation.
  - Hydrated HA excipient enhances fluid–solid coupling, amplifying mechanotransduction at septal–dermal junctions.
- Selectivity:
  - No direct anti-lipolytic signaling; parameters avoid adipocyte cavitation or cytolysis (no HIFU, no cryo).
  - Thermal ceiling of 42°C preserves adipocyte viability and endocrine function; intervention ends weeks before caloric/GLP-1–driven lipolysis begins.

Key outcomes and biomarkers:
- Mechanical/structural
  - Shear-wave elastography: dermal modulus and anisotropy index; septal echogenic thickness.
  - Cutometer: immediate distension (Ue), viscoelastic recovery (Uv), net elasticity (R2).
  - Second-harmonic/OCT elastography (subset biopsies/ex vivo): collagen orientation index, elastic fiber density.
  - 3D surface photogrammetry: ptosis/sag metrics under standardized pose.
- Molecular (biopsy subset)
  - mRNA/protein: ELN, FBLN5, FBN1, LOX, COL1A1/3A1, TIMP1/3, MMP1/9; YAP/TAZ nuclear:cytosolic ratio.
  - Desmosine/isodesmosine content as elastin crosslink readout.
- Clinical
  - Maintenance of contour and skin pinch recoil after 10–15% body-weight loss at 12 and 24 weeks vs sham.
  - Patient- and evaluator-rated laxity scales (validated).

Preclinical plan:
- Ex vivo human skin–fat explants: map strain/temperature fields; quantify ELN/LOX induction vs parameter space; SHG alignment changes after 3 sessions.
- Porcine model (n=12): treat flank fields; complete 3 sessions; induce 10% weight loss via diet; outcomes at baseline, post-preconditioning, and post–weight loss.
- Safety: histology for adipocyte integrity, neurovascular structures; copper/ascorbate PK in plasma; thermal dosimetry margins.

First-in-human feasibility (N=30, randomized, single-blind):
- Population: BMI 27–38, trunk or thigh target zones; planned weight-loss program starting Day 28.
- Arms: PRETENSE x3 vs device-only (no patch) vs sham suction/heat.
- Endpoints at Weeks 0, 4, 12, 24:
  - Primary: Change in Cutometer R2 and dermal anisotropic modulus from baseline to Week 12 despite ≥10% weight loss.
  - Secondary: Septal thickness by high-frequency US; 3D ptosis metric; blinded GAIS; safety.

Clinical translatability:
- Safety: Non-ablative thermal range; microneedle doses within cosmetic topical exposure; copper/ascorbate GRAS-adjacent profiles; no systemic metabolism effect.
- Manufacturability: Off-the-shelf components (vacuum, shear stage, Peltier heater, NTC sensors); single-use microneedle patches in sterile pouches; ISO 13485-ready.
- Regulatory: Device as Class II (510(k) pathway leveraging massage/vacuum/RF precedents) with drug–device combination as 505(b)(2) topical microdose; or de-risk by first filing as device + cosmetic patch, then pursue combination labeling for preconditioning indication.

Risk and mitigation:
- Excess stiffening/fibrosis: limit session count; maintain 41–42°C; use oriented loading to promote elasticity; monitor MMP/TIMP balance.
- Hyperpigmentation: melanocyte-safe temperature; contact cooling between passes.
- Off-target adipocyte effects: monitor serum adipokines; ultrasound adipocyte morphology; conservative suction in low-SAT areas.

Success criteria (go/no-go):
- ≥20% increase in dermal anisotropic modulus and ≥15% increase in R2 at Week 4 vs baseline without adverse events.
- After ≥10% weight loss, ≤5% decline from post-preconditioning mechanical gains and ≥25% reduction in ptosis vs controls.

Novelty and IP claims (exemplars):
- Method to precondition skin prior to weight loss by encoding residual pre-tension and elevating fibrous septa buckling resistance using synchronized cyclic suction–shear and controlled hyperthermia.
- Combination with dissolvable microneedle delivery of LOX cofactors (copper/ascorbate) timed to mechanical loading to bias elastic fiber assembly.
- Parameterization linking target “delta-rest-length shift” and septal critical load to ultrasound elastography feedback control.
- Use of anisotropy-guided vectoring along Langer’s lines to set directional tensile set before adipose reduction.

Development milestones:
- M1 (3 months): parameter safety map; explant molecular validation; patch stability/assay.
- M2 (6 months): porcine efficacy with elastography/histology endpoints; refine applicator ergonomics.
- M3 (12 months): IRB-approved FIH, endpoint readouts at Week 12; pre-submission to FDA with device master file.
- M4 (18 months): pivotal design lock, manufacturing scale-up, multi-site RCT planning.

Deliverable:
A few-session, selective, mechanobiology-first preconditioning therapy that preserves skin elasticity and contour during subsequent fat loss by installing a new mechanical set and reinforcing subcutaneous fibrous architecture without impeding lipolysis.
