Title
IC-NET alloHSCT: Immune-Conditioning by Niche Eviction and Tagging to Eradicate LSCs Without Genotoxic Ablation

Central Hypothesis
Transiently converting leukemia stem cells (LSCs) into a single synthetic, HLA-independent immune target while forcibly evicting them from marrow niches will enable donor-engineered CAR-NK cells to serve as the “conditioning,” achieving MAC-level (or lower) relapse with reduced-intensity/non-myeloablative (RIC/NMA) toxicity and preserved donor HSC engraftment.

Atomic Strategy
Turn conditioning into an immune-logic program: (1) evict LSCs from protective niches; (2) paint them with a universal synthetic tag recognized by donor “convertible” CAR-NK cells; (3) run multi-layer immune-evasion countermeasures in the NK cells; (4) admit donor HSCs after LSC clearance using non-genotoxic, stem-targeted space-creation—thereby front-loading GVL without GVHD.

Specific Aims
1) Create LSC-selective, HLA-agnostic recognition via universal tagging and logic-gated donor CAR-NK cells that spare HSCs.
2) Overcome LSC sanctuary and niche-mediated resistance by combined CXCR4/E-selectin blockade to mobilize LSCs into blood for immune interception.
3) Replace genotoxic ablation with non-genotoxic engraftment and GVHD control while maintaining or improving GVL potency relative to MAC.

Innovation
- Universal Tagging of Heterogeneous LSCs: A modular “adapter” panel that binds LSC markers and displays a common tag read by a single donor CAR-NK product, avoiding antigen escape and HLA dependency.
- Logic-Gated LSC Targeting: synNotch AND gate (LSC markers) plus NOT gate (HSC markers) on NK cells to enforce selective killing while preserving donor HSC engraftment.
- Front-Loaded, HLA-Independent GVL: Pre-transplant CAR-NK purge replaces the antitumor function lost with RIC/NMA, minimizing reliance on systemic, non-selective genotoxins.

Therapeutic Components
A. LSC-tagging adapters (administered systemically pre-transplant)
- Tri-adapter panel: each molecule binds one LSC-associated antigen at high-density threshold (e.g., CLEC12A/CLL-1; IL1RAP; CD123 or FLT3) and presents the same synthetic epitope (“UniTag”).
- Titrable exposure: short half-life, reversible dosing enables on/off control to avoid bystander coat of normal progenitors and to halt tagging before HSC infusion.
- Density gating: high-avidity binding favors LSCs over normal progenitors; NOT protection is enforced at effector level (see below).

B. Donor-engineered CAR-NK cells (“cCAR-NK”)
- Convertible CAR: anti-UniTag receptor drives cytotoxicity only in presence of tagged targets (HLA-independent).
- synNotch AND gate: recognition of CLEC12A AND IL1RAP upregulates the UniTag CAR and cytotoxic program, restricting full activation to LSCs.
- NOT gate (HSC-sparing): inhibitory CAR recognizing CD34 or THY1 (CD90) dampens activation on healthy HSCs and early progenitors.
- Evasion countermeasures:
  - HLA loss: intrinsic NK “missing-self” reactivity preserved (no TCR, low GVHD risk).
  - Checkpoints: PD-1 and TIGIT dominant-negative/switch receptors.
  - Anti-phagocytic signaling: SIRPα knockout in NK cells to resist CD47; plus membrane-tethered, protease-activatable SIRPα-Fc microdomain secretion for local CD47 blockade on tagged targets.
  - TGF-β/adenosine resistance: TGFβR2 dominant-negative and A2A receptor knockout.
- Potency and persistence: high-affinity non-cleavable CD16A for ADCC against clinically available anti-LSC antibodies; membrane-bound IL-15 for NK survival without systemic cytokines; CISH knockout to enhance metabolic fitness.
- Trafficking: CXCR3/CCR5 expression to optimize marrow and blood patrol post-eviction; CD62L retention for recirculation.
- Safety: iCasp9 suicide switch and adapter withdrawal for rapid “off.”

C. Niche-eviction regimen (pre-effector and peri-effector)
- CXCR4 antagonism (plerixafor) + E-selectin blockade (e.g., uproleselan) ± short G-CSF pulse to dislodge LSCs from endosteal/vascular niches and increase intravascular exposure.
- Transient VLA-4/α4β1 inhibition (single-dose) optional cohort for difficult-to-mobilize cases.
- Schedule aligns peak circulation of tagged LSCs with cCAR-NK exposure.

D. Non-genotoxic engraftment and GVHD control
- Space creation: anti-CD117 (c-Kit) monoclonal conditioning to selectively clear host HSCs without DNA-damaging agents.
- Immunomodulation: costimulatory blockade (abatacept) and/or short-course JAK inhibition titrated to spare NK activity.
- Graft composition: αβ T-cell–depleted, NK/Treg-replete stem cell graft to reduce GVHD and support immune homeostasis.

Study Design and Timeline (first-in-human, multicenter phase 1/2)
- Population: Adults with AML/MDS at high relapse risk proceeding to alloHSCT; enriched for LSC antigen expression by flow cytometry/scRNA-seq.
- Day -21 to -18: Baseline MRD/LSC profiling; leukapheresis of related/unrelated donor for NK and HSC manufacturing.
- Day -14 to -10: Begin LSC tagging (UniTag adapters, step-up dosing guided by pharmacokinetics and target occupancy).
- Day -12 to -8: Initiate niche-eviction (plerixafor + uproleselan ± single-dose VLA-4 inhibitor); obtain real-time ctDNA and flow MRD to confirm mobilization.
- Day -10 and -7: Infuse cCAR-NK (dose-escalation cohorts). Administer adjunct anti-LSC antibody for ADCC synergy during peak tagging.
- Day -6: Cease adapters to allow tag washout before donor HSC infusion.
- Day -5 to -3: Non-genotoxic conditioning with anti-CD117 ± abatacept.
- Day 0: Infuse donor HSCs (αβ T-cell–depleted graft).
- Day +7, +14: cCAR-NK maintenance mini-doses without adapters (surveillance) if MRD-positive or mixed chimerism emerges (adaptive).
- Monitoring: MRD by multiparameter flow and NGS, LSC frequency by index sorting, chimerism, cytokines, GVHD staging, infectious complications.

Primary Endpoints
- Phase 1: Safety—DLTs (CRS, neurotoxicity, off-target cytopenias), GVHD (grade II–IV by day +100).
- Phase 2: Efficacy—MRD negativity pre-Day 0, 1-year relapse incidence ≤ historical MAC; 1-year GVHD-free/relapse-free survival (GRFS).

Key Secondary/Exploratory Endpoints
- LSC eradication: change in CD34+CD38−CD123+/CLEC12A+/IL1RAP+ frequency from baseline to Day -1 and Day +30.
- Engraftment: time to neutrophil/platelet recovery; donor chimerism kinetics.
- Immune-evasion control: longitudinal expression of HLA, PD-L1, CD47 on residual cells; serum adapter levels; NK persistence and phenotype.
- Spatial pharmacology: paired marrow/blood sampling for LSC mobilization and tagging density; single-cell multi-omics for niche remodeling.

Controls and Comparators
- Contemporary RIC/NMA alloHSCT cohort without IC-NET immune-conditioning (propensity-matched).
- Historical MAC cohort for relapse benchmarking.

Risk Mitigation
- Off-tumor cytopenias: NOT-gated inhibitory CAR recognizing CD34/THY1; strict UniTag adapter washout before HSC infusion; iCasp9-enabled NK ablation if cytopenias emerge.
- Hemolysis/anemia from CD47 axis: SIRPα knockout (effector-side only) and protease-activatable SIRPα-Fc to confine blockade to tumor-rich microenvironments.
- GVHD: NK-only effector product; αβ T-cell–depleted graft; costimulation blockade; rapid NK shutdown via suicide switch if inflammation escalates.
- Infection: preemptive antimicrobials; conservative cytokine support (avoid systemic IL-2/IL-15).

Power and Success Criteria
- Go/No-Go (Phase 2 trigger): ≥60% MRD negativity by Day -1, no excess grade III–IV GVHD vs institutional RIC norms, ≤10% prolonged aplasia without disease.
- Success: 1-year cumulative relapse ≤ MAC historical benchmark with non-inferior TRM and improved GRFS.

Why This Meets the Constraints
- Compensates RIC/NMA loss of antileukemia effect: front-loaded, HLA-independent cCAR-NK purge with adapter control.
- Excludes non-selective genotoxic agents: uses anti-CD117 and biologics (no busulfan/TBI).
- LSC-selective while preserving HSC engraftment: AND/NOT logic plus adapter washout and antigen-density gating; donor HSCs lack UniTag and are protected by NOT gate.
- Overcomes marrow sanctuary: dual CXCR4/E-selectin blockade (± VLA-4) to mobilize LSCs into circulation.
- Counters multiple immune-evasion mechanisms: HLA loss (NK missing-self), checkpoint upregulation (PD-1/TIGIT switches), CD47 (SIRPα manipulation), TGF-β/adenosine resistance.
- Enhances GVL without exacerbating GVHD: NK-centered, TCR-free product; αβ T-cell–depleted graft; precise, reversible adapter control.

Translational Outlook
If IC-NET achieves pre-transplant MRD eradication with low toxicity and maintains relapse ≤ MAC, it establishes immune-logic conditioning as a platform to replace genotoxic ablation in alloHSCT while setting the stage for plug-and-play adapters against evolving LSC phenotypes.

Title
Temporal “Evict-and-Expose” Transplant: a niche-disrupting, redox-priming, innate-immune–centric allogeneic HSCT platform that eradicates leukemia stem cells without non-selective genotoxic conditioning

Central hypothesis
A short, pretransplant window can be engineered in which leukemia stem cells (LSCs) are simultaneously (i) evicted from bone-marrow safe houses, (ii) pushed into a proliferation- and ROS-vulnerable state, and (iii) made highly visible to donor innate immunity. Creating this synchronized vulnerability eliminates LSCs during engraftment, compensates for the reduced cytotoxicity of RIC/NMA, and preserves donor HSC function—achieving relapse rates comparable to or better than MAC without busulfan/TBI.

Atomic strategy (single conceptual insight)
Decouple LSCs from their niche-derived quiescence and antioxidant shielding, then immediately subject them to a brief, systemic but LSC-selective “redox trap” while they circulate, and overlay this with GVHD-sparing, multi-axis innate immune pressure (NK- and macrophage-mediated) that is resilient to HLA loss, checkpoint upregulation, and anti-phagocytic signals.

Therapeutic architecture (modular, timed)
A. Non-genotoxic engraftment conditioning (space creation without chemotherapy/radiation)
- Anti-CD117 (c-Kit) antibody conditioning to deplete host HSCs and open niche space.
- Co-stimulation blockade for immunosuppression (abatacept) ± low-dose sirolimus; no busulfan/TBI/fludarabine.

B. Niche eviction and anti-shelter signaling blockade (overcome sanctuary)
- Dual homing/retention disruption: CXCR4 antagonist (plerixafor) + E-selectin antagonist (uproleselan).
- Optional third-axis blockade: brief VLA-4/VCAM-1 inhibition to remove survival/quiescence cues.
- Short G-CSF pulse to invert SDF-1 gradients and mobilize LSCs into blood.

C. Transient, selective redox-priming “trap” (stress LSCs without harming donor HSCs)
- 4–8-hour pulse of pharmacologic IV ascorbate (pro-oxidant via extracellular H2O2) immediately after niche eviction; drug cleared before graft infusion.
- Concurrent inhibition of LSC antioxidant buffering limited to the pulse (e.g., short-acting thioredoxin reductase inhibitor microdose) to heighten LSC ROS, timed to avoid donor HSC exposure.
- Bone-targeted delivery optional: bisphosphonate-anchored pro-oxidant microdose to concentrate in marrow.

D. Innate immune overmatch (compensate for reduced intensity; multi-evasion countermeasures)
- Donor selection: KIR-ligand–mismatched, CMV-exposed donor to maximize adaptive NKG2C+ NK potential.
- Day 0 and +7 infusion of donor-derived cytokine–induced memory-like NK cells (IL-12/15/18–primed).
- NK engager therapy during the kill window: TriKE (CD16×CD123×IL-15) or BiKE to drive NK-ADCC against LSCs in circulation and marrow periphery.
- Macrophage checkpoint reversal focused on LSCs: targeted SIRPα-Fc fused to anti-CD123 or anti-CLL-1, limiting CD47 blockade to LSC surfaces and sparing donor HSCs.
- Fc-opsonization of LSC-restricted antigens: anti-CLL-1 ± anti-CD123 mAbs (absent/low on HSCs) to promote ADCP/ADCC.
- NK-specific checkpoint release to avoid GVHD: anti-NKG2A (± anti-TIGIT) rather than PD-1/CTLA-4 early post-transplant.
- HLA-loss escape addressed by NK missing-self recognition; residual HLA+ disease addressed later with donor-derived, hematopoietic-restricted miHA-specific T cells (e.g., HA-1) in MRD-only setting.

E. GVHD minimization with preserved GVL
- αβ T-cell–depleted graft with add-back of Tregs and memory-like NK cells; maintain sirolimus ± abatacept early.
- Avoid systemic T-cell checkpoint blockade early; rely on NK/macrophage GVL and opsonization to maintain disease control.

Clinical protocol (Phase 1/2; AML with LSC-positive disease by flow/single-cell assays)
Timeline (Day 0 = graft infusion)
- Day −14 to −10: Anti-CD117 antibody conditioning; abatacept start; sirolimus start.
- Day −5 to −3: G-CSF micro-pulse (mobilize host leukemia; reduce SDF-1).
- Day −2: Uproleselan + plerixafor (± short VLA-4 inhibitor) to evict LSCs; begin real-time ctDNA/LSC-shed monitoring.
- Day −1 (Redox Trap Window): 4–8h pharmacologic ascorbate infusion ± microdose thioredoxin reductase inhibitor; infuse anti-CLL-1 and/or anti-CD123 mAbs; initiate NK engager (TriKE/BiKE). No donor cells present yet.
- Day 0: Infuse αβ T-cell–depleted stem cell graft + IL-12/15/18–primed NK cells; continue NK engager for 5–7 days post-infusion; start anti-NKG2A on Day +1 for 2–3 weeks.
- Day +7: Second dose of memory-like NK cells; reassess LSC biomarkers; optional targeted SIRPα-Fc–anti-CD123 if MRD+.
- Day +28 to +56: Taper NK-specific checkpoint; maintain sirolimus/abatacept; escalate only if MRD+.
- Day +60 to +120 (MRD-only setting): Optional donor miHA-specific T cells if MRD persists, with marrow-restricted dosing.

Mechanistic alignment to constraints
- Compensate for RIC/NMA anti-leukemia loss: synchronized innate immune overmatch (NK engagers, memory-like NKs, macrophage-optimized opsonization) during maximum LSC vulnerability, plus targeted anti-CLL-1/CD123 killing.
- Exclude non-selective genotoxins: no busulfan/TBI; antibody conditioning (anti-CD117) and biologics used instead.
- LSC selectivity with HSC preservation: target antigens CLL-1 and CD123 (absent/low on normal HSCs); redox trap occurs pre-graft and is brief; donor HSCs infused after agent washout; anti-CD117 spares donor cells.
- Overcome niche sanctuary: CXCR4/E-selectin/VLA-4 blockade + G-CSF to physically dislodge and remove survival/quiescence cues.
- Counter multiple immune-evasion mechanisms:
  - HLA loss: NK missing-self (donor KIR mismatch), NK engagers.
  - Checkpoint upregulation: NK-focused blockade (NKG2A/TIGIT) instead of T-cell PD-1 to minimize GVHD.
  - Anti-phagocytic CD47: targeted SIRPα-Fc fused to LSC antigen, enhancing ADCP without pan-hematopoietic opsonization.
- Enhance GVL without exacerbating GVHD: prioritize NK/macrophage effectors, αβ T-cell depletion + Treg add-back, co-stimulation blockade instead of broad T-cell activation.

Readouts and decision gates
- Primary: 1-year relapse-free survival compared with institutional MAC benchmark; MRD negativity (flow/NGS) at Days +30, +60, +100.
- Secondary: Engraftment kinetics; grade II–IV acute GVHD; non-relapse mortality; infectious complications; pharmacodynamic evidence of the “trap” (spikes in circulating LSC markers post-eviction, ROS surrogates in leukemic cells, NK activation signatures).
- Exploratory: Single-cell multi-omics of blood/marrow across the window; dynamics of HLA expression, NKG2D ligands, CD47 density; ctDNA clearance curves; donor–recipient NK alloreactivity indices.

Preclinical validation plan
- Aim 1: Demonstrate eviction + redox vulnerability. In LSC-enriched PDX, show that CXCR4/E-selectin blockade mobilizes LSCs and increases cycling; the brief ascorbate pulse elevates ROS and apoptosis selectively in mobilized LSCs versus normal HSCs.
- Aim 2: Show innate-immune kill synergy. Test memory-like NKs ± TriKE against mobilized LSCs; quantify dependence on NKG2A/TIGIT blockade and LSC opsonization (anti-CLL-1/CD123; targeted SIRPα-Fc).
- Aim 3: Establish engraftment safety. In humanized models, deliver redox pulse before donor HSC infusion; verify preserved donor HSC homing and LT-HSC function; confirm antibody conditioning suffices for durable chimerism.

Risk mitigation
- Donor HSC safety: strict washout of redox agents before infusion; shorten half-life choices; real-time plasma pharmacokinetics to greenlight graft infusion.
- Cytopenias from opsonization: select LSC-restricted antigens (CLL-1; careful CD123 dosing); step-up dosing with close counts monitoring.
- Infection risk under NK-focused regimen: prophylaxis protocols; IL-15 agonist exposure minimized to avoid CD8 T-cell–driven GVHD.
- Mobilizing normal HSCs: acceptable pre-graft; eviction occurs prior to donor infusion; host HSCs already targeted by anti-CD117.
- GVHD control: αβ T-cell depletion, Treg add-back, and abatacept/sirolimus backbone; avoid early PD-1/CTLA-4 blockade.

Go/no-go criteria
- Proceed to Phase 2 if ≥80% MRD negativity at Day +60 with ≤20% grade II–IV aGVHD and engraftment by Day +21, and 6-month relapse ≤ historical MAC.
- Iterate if pharmacodynamic markers fail (insufficient LSC mobilization or ROS signature); tune eviction dosing or timing; consider adding VLA-4 blockade.

Impact
By converting the marrow niche from a sanctuary into a transient vulnerability and pairing it with GVHD-sparing, innate-immune multi-axis pressure, this platform aims to deliver MAC-level (or better) disease control without non-selective genotoxic conditioning—establishing a generalizable, modular approach for LSC eradication in allo-HSCT.

text:
Title
Niche-anchored donor HSC therapeutics to evict and eradicate leukemia stem cells under non-genotoxic conditioning

Central hypothesis
Engineering donor hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) to (i) preferentially occupy bone-marrow niches and (ii) secrete an extracellular-matrix (ECM)-tethered, multi-functional biologic that dismantles LSC immune evasion locally will convert the niche into an anti-LSC exclusion zone. This will restore or exceed the anti-leukemia benefit of myeloablative conditioning (MAC) while using reduced-intensity or nonmyeloablative (RIC/NMA) regimens without non-selective genotoxicity.

Atomic strategy
Localize multi-pronged anti-LSC pressure to the marrow niche by turning engrafted donor HSC progeny into site-restricted producers of a single, modular, ECM-anchored fusion protein that (a) tags LSCs, (b) removes their anti-phagocytic shield, (c) reverses local checkpoint inhibition, and (d) sustains NK effector function—while concurrent donor HSC adhesion tuning secures niche dominance and physically displaces LSCs.

Intervention overview
1) Donor HSC engineering (product: BM-LOCK HSCs)
- Homing/retention module (niche dominance):
  - Transient ex vivo glycoengineering to enforce HCELL on CD44 (FUT7-mediated fucosylation) and high-affinity PSGL-1 to enhance E-selectin-mediated rolling and vascular niche entry.
  - Hypoxia-inducible CXCR4 (HRE-driven) and VLA-4 (ITGA4) upregulation to strengthen CXCL12–CXCR4 and VCAM1–VLA-4 interactions only in hypoxic marrow, minimizing off-target adhesion.
- Secretome module (site-restricted anti-LSC biologic):
  - Single secreted fusion “BM-LOCK” with:
    i) SIRPα variant-Fc (high-affinity CD47 decoy) to disable “don’t-eat-me.”
    ii) Anti–PD-L1 nanobody to reverse local checkpoint suppression.
    iii) Anti–CLEC12A (CLL-1) scFv-Fc to opsonize LSCs (antigen enriched on AML LSCs, sparing HSCs).
    iv) IL-15/IL-15Rα “sushi” domain to locally activate and sustain NK cells (TriKE-like function).
    v) Collagen-binding domain (CBD, e.g., from von Willebrand factor A3) to anchor to endosteal/vascular ECM, confining activity to marrow.
  - Expression restricted to myeloid-lineage progeny via CD68/CSF1R promoter to preserve HSC quiescence and reduce systemic spillover.
  - Safety: microRNA target sites (e.g., miR-122, miR-1) to suppress ectopic expression; degron-based on-switch for the fusion (e.g., Shield-1/dTAG) for pharmacologic control; suicide switch (iCasp9) at HSC level.

2) Conditioning and delivery (non-genotoxic)
- Host HSC niche opening: anti-CD117 (JSP191) to deplete host HSCs without DNA damage.
- LSC dislodgement/sensitization: plerixafor (CXCR4 antagonist) + uproleselan (E-selectin antagonist) timed 24–48 h pre-infusion to force LSC egress/cycling and reduce niche protection.
- Graft composition: αβ T-cell–depleted stem cell product with add-back of memory T cells and/or NK cells; primary cytotoxicity relies on NK/macrophage effectors enhanced in-niche by BM-LOCK, decoupling GVL from GVHD.
- Administration: intraosseous (posterior iliac crest) delivery of engineered HSCs for immediate niche access, followed by systemic infusion of residual graft.

Mechanistic mapping to constraints
- Compensate for reduced RIC/NMA cytotoxicity: ECM-tethered opsonization (anti–CLEC12A-Fc), local CD47 blockade (SIRPα-Fc), and local PD-L1 blockade reconstitute potent, spatially focused GVL; IL-15/IL-15Rα drives durable NK-mediated killing despite low systemic inflammation.
- Exclude non-selective genotoxic agents: conditioning uses anti-CD117, plerixafor, and uproleselan only; no busulfan/TBI.
- LSC selectivity with preserved normal HSC engraftment: target antigen CLEC12A minimizes HSC binding; activity confined by marrow ECM tethering and myeloid-restricted expression; donor HSCs gain niche occupancy via hypoxia-tuned adhesion, not via toxic ablation.
- Overcome niche sanctuary: donor HSC niche dominance plus pre-infusion CXCR4/E-selectin blockade physically evicts LSCs; anchored biologic saturates the niche microenvironment where LSCs hide, negating stromal protection.
- Counter multiple immune-evasion mechanisms simultaneously: CD47 blockade (anti-phagocytic), PD-L1 checkpoint reversal, LSC-specific opsonization, and NK activation (handles HLA loss/missing-self) operate in parallel within the niche.
- Enhance GVL without exacerbating GVHD: effectors biased to NK/myeloid in marrow; αβ T-cell depletion reduces systemic alloreactivity; ECM tethering limits checkpoint and cytokine effects outside bone marrow.

Experimental plan
Aim 1: Build BM-LOCK and validate spatial confinement and function in vitro
- Construct lentiviral cassettes: CD68/CSF1R-promoted BM-LOCK with CBD; HRE-CXCR4/ITGA4 module; safety switches integrated.
- ECM anchoring: quantify CBD-mediated retention on human trabecular bone slices and decellularized ECM.
- Function: co-culture assays with primary AML LSC-enriched cells (CD34+CD38−CLEC12A+) and donor macrophages/NK cells; endpoints: phagocytosis, ADCC, NK activation, cytokine spread (spatial ELISA in microfluidic marrow-on-chip).

Aim 2: Demonstrate niche dominance and local biologic accumulation in vivo
- Humanized BM ossicle and intraosseous NSG models with patient-derived AML LSCs.
- Compare homing/retention of engineered vs control HSCs (intravital microscopy, CXCL12 gradient tracking); measure BM-LOCK levels in marrow vs plasma to confirm confinement (LC–MS/ELISA).

Aim 3: Test LSC eradication and relapse prevention under RIC/NMA
- Conditioning: anti-CD117 ± plerixafor + uproleselan; no genotoxic agents.
- Endpoints: LSC frequency by limiting dilution xenotransplantation; MRD by ddPCR/flow; time to relapse after serial transplantation; overall survival.
- Controls: RIC alone; RIC + unengineered HSCs; RIC + engineered HSCs lacking CBD.

Aim 4: Safety, GVHD, and off-target assessment
- Cytokine profiling; systemic BM-LOCK spillover; hematopoiesis (CFU assays, multilineage engraftment).
- GVHD scoring with αβ T-cell–depleted grafts ± add-back memory T cells; compare to standard RIC.
- On/off control tests of degron switch and iCasp9 ablation in vivo.

Clinical translation plan (Phase 1/2 design)
- Population: adults with AML at high relapse risk undergoing allo-HSCT with RIC/NMA.
- Primary endpoints: safety (DLTs), GVHD (grade II–IV), engraftment kinetics.
- Key efficacy endpoints: 12- and 24-month CIR (cumulative incidence of relapse) versus institutional MAC benchmarks; MRD negativity rates at day +90 and +180.
- Biomarkers: marrow-tethered BM-LOCK levels, NK activation signatures, phagocytic indices, LSC burden by flow/NGS.

Milestones and go/no-go
- M1: >80% marrow vs <5% plasma BM-LOCK localization (preclinical).
- M2: ≥2-log LSC reduction and MRD negativity in ≥60% of PDX cohorts without hematopoietic toxicity.
- M3: No increase in grade II–IV GVHD vs historical RIC controls in large-animal model.
- Go/no-go: proceed to IND if M1–M3 met and on-demand shutdown (degron/iCasp9) demonstrates >90% activity reduction within 48 h.

Risk mitigation
- Antigen escape: modular swap to dual LSC binders (CLEC12A + CD123) within BM-LOCK scaffold if escape detected.
- Off-target myelosuppression: CBD removal or dose-titrated degron control if hematopoiesis suppressed.
- NK overactivation: IL-15 activity tuned via weaker sushi domain variants; local neutralization with marrow-injected anti–IL-15 if needed.

Expected impact
By converting donor HSCs into niche-dominant, site-restricted factories for a single, modular anti-LSC biologic, this strategy couples physical eviction with immune eradication precisely where LSCs survive. It is designed to deliver MAC-level or better relapse control under RIC/NMA, without non-selective systemic genotoxicity and without increasing GVHD.

text:
Title
Programmable two-state mesenchymal “trap-niche” to eradicate leukemia stem cells while preserving donor HSC engraftment in reduced-intensity allogeneic HSCT

Central hypothesis
Installing a two-state, leukemia-sensing mesenchymal niche across marrow will flip local microenvironments from HSC-supportive to LSC-adversarial only where LSCs are detected, converting the marrow from a sanctuary into a selective trap that restores or exceeds MAC-level anti-leukemia control without non-selective genotoxic conditioning or added GVHD.

Atomic strategy
Replace the static marrow niche with engineered mesenchymal stromal cells (eMSCs) that default to “Engraft-Support” and switch to “LSC-Kill” upon direct contact recognition of LSC-specific surface cues. This single perturbation—deploying a conditional, spatially confined niche program—simultaneously (i) preserves donor HSC engraftment, (ii) defeats LSC physical sanctuary and niche-mediated resistance, and (iii) layers orthogonal immune mechanisms (NK, macrophage, checkpoint blockade) focused inside marrow, not systemically.

Design overview
A. Sensing and logic (local, contact-gated)
- Multi-input OR synNotch receptors on eMSCs detect LSC-restricted antigens (e.g., CLEC12A/CLL1, CD123, CD70). Any input triggers the LSC-Kill program in the contacting eMSC. Absence of these antigens maintains the Engraft-Support state.

B. State 1: Engraft-Support (default throughout marrow)
- HSC trophic cues: baseline expression of CXCL12, SCF, and thrombopoietin at physiologic levels to promote homing and self-renewal.
- GVHD containment: no T-cell co-stimulation; lack of proinflammatory cytokine secretion; eMSC shielded from bystander lysis via HLA-E or non-activating NK-interaction motif.
- Spatial fidelity: effectors tethered with extracellular matrix (ECM)–binding domains to prevent systemic spillover; no checkpoint blockers or phagocytosis modifiers active in this state.

C. State 2: LSC-Kill (induced only at LSC–eMSC contact zones)
- Niche detachment and sanctuary override (microscale only):
  - Local antagonism of E-selectin and VLA-4/VCAM-1 interactions via ECM-tethered inhibitors to peel LSCs off protective contacts.
  - CXCL12 scavenging via immobilized decoy to collapse the retention gradient immediately around detected LSCs without disturbing global HSC homing.
- Innate cytotoxic focus with minimal GVHD risk:
  - ECM-anchored NK cell engagers (BiKE/TriKE-like) bridging CD16/NKp46 to LSC antigens sensed (e.g., CLL1 or CD123) to drive synapse formation only where LSCs were detected.
  - Membrane-bound TRAIL on eMSCs to trigger extrinsic apoptosis on proximate AML/LSC while sparing HSCs.
  - Local IL-15 transpresentation (IL-15/IL-15Rα in cis on eMSCs) and heparan-binding CXCL9/10 to recruit/activate NK and γδ T cells within marrow niches without systemic cytokinemia.
- Immune evasion countermeasures (co-localized, on-demand):
  - Anti-phagocytic blockade: ECM-tethered SIRPα-Fc (or anti-CD47 single-domain binder) to enable macrophage phagocytosis of LSCs with short diffusion radius to avoid systemic anemia.
  - Checkpoint neutralization: matrix-anchored anti–PD-L1/PD-1 nanobodies confined to the LSC-eMSC microdomain to restore NK/γδ T activity without broad T-cell activation.
  - HLA-loss compensation: reliance on NK missing-self plus antigen-agnostic NKp46 engagement; effectors are HLA-independent.
- Controllability and safety:
  - Small-molecule on/off switch gating the LSC-Kill transcriptional cassette.
  - eMSC safety switch for rapid ablation if adverse effects occur.
  - miRNA target cassettes to suppress effector expression in non-marrow tissues if ectopically seeded.

Transplant schema (non-genotoxic, RIC-compatible)
- Conditioning: non-genotoxic space-creating regimen (e.g., c-Kit/CD117 blockade) ± transient CXCR4 antagonist to facilitate niche access. No busulfan/TBI.
- Cell therapy triad:
  1) Donor graft optimized for engraftment and low GVHD risk (e.g., TCRαβ-depleted with retained NK/γδ compartments).
  2) eMSCs delivered to marrow (localized administration) to install the programmable trap-niche.
  3) Adjunct donor-derived NK infusion post-engraftment to amplify localized effectors without systemic cytokines.
- Pharmacologic adjuncts: none required for cytotoxicity; optional systemic inert prodrugs are excluded to avoid genotoxicity. All cytotoxicity is local and biologic.

Specific aims and endpoints
Aim 1. Build and validate two-state eMSCs with LSC OR-gated switching.
- Success criteria: robust switching upon CLL1/CD123/CD70 engagement; no leaky activation in HSC co-culture; ECM confinement of effectors; preserved eMSC viability (NK-shield intact).

Aim 2. Demonstrate LSC-selective eradication with preserved HSC function ex vivo.
- Models: primary AML/LSC and normal CD34+ HSC co-cultures on humanized matrices.
- Endpoints: elimination of phenotypic and functional LSCs (LDA/serial replating), intact HSC CFU and LTC-IC output, unaltered HSC transcriptomic stemness, minimal bystander toxicity.

Aim 3. Test efficacy, chimerism, and safety in vivo under RIC/NMA HSCT conditions.
- Readouts: marrow LSC burden (including antigen-negative subclones), donor HSC chimerism and multilineage reconstitution, NK/γδ activation confined to marrow, absence of systemic cytokinemia, GVHD scores ≤ RIC baseline, survival/relapse curves non-inferior to MAC with target superiority margin.

How the design satisfies constraints
- Compensates RIC/NMA loss: localized, sustained NK-centric cytotoxicity plus checkpoint and anti-phagocytic blockade restores deep anti-leukemia pressure without systemic toxicity.
- Excludes non-selective genotoxic agents: conditioning uses non-genotoxic space-creation; cytotoxic modules are biologic and spatially confined.
- LSC selectivity with preserved HSC engraftment: antigen-gated switch; ECM-tethered effectors; default HSC-support state maintains CXCL12/SCF/TPO; sanctuary disruptors deployed only at LSC contact zones.
- Overcomes marrow sanctuary: microdomain disruption of E-selectin/VLA-4 and CXCL12 specifically around detected LSCs.
- Counters immune evasion: HLA-loss via NK missing-self and HLA-independent engagers; PD-1/PD-L1 axis neutralized locally; CD47/SIRPα blockade enables phagocytosis; redundancy across targets.
- Enhances GVL without GVHD: prioritizes NK/γδ effectors; restricts checkpoint and cytokine activity to marrow niches; avoids systemic T-cell co-stimulation.

Milestones and quantitative go/no-go thresholds
- Switch fidelity: ≤1% activation in HSC-only conditions; ≥90% activation on LSC contact.
- LSC kill: ≥3-log reduction of functional LSCs ex vivo with ≤10% loss of HSC CFU.
- In vivo efficacy: relapse-free survival superiority to RIC control (HR ≤0.6) and non-inferiority to MAC; donor chimerism ≥95% by day 60; grade II–IV GVHD not increased vs RIC baseline.
- Containment: marrow-to-plasma gradient of effectors ≥100:1; no anemia or thrombocytopenia from systemic CD47 blockade.

Risk mitigation and alternatives
- Antigen heterogeneity: maintain OR-gated sensors (CLL1, CD123, CD70) and add stress-sensing ligands (e.g., AML-associated alarmins) if needed.
- NK resistance: escalate local IL-15 transpresentation or add ECM-tethered NKG2D ligand mimetics directed to LSC membrane via bispecific binders.
- Niche over-disruption: cap sanctuary-disruptor expression by kill-state timers and dose-controllable switches; maintain HSC-support tonic cues globally.

Expected impact
Installing a conditional mesenchymal trap-niche turns LSC refuges into kill zones while preserving donor HSC biology and limiting GVHD, enabling RIC/NMA allogeneic HSCT to achieve MAC-level or better relapse control without non-selective genotoxic conditioning.

text:
Title
Antigen-gated niche reprogramming HSCT: donor HSCs that locally expose, unmask, and eliminate leukemia stem cells while engrafting without genotoxic conditioning

Central hypothesis (atomic strategy)
If donor CD34+ HSCs are engineered with an antigen-sensing gate that, only upon encountering LSCs in bone marrow, transiently flips the local niche from retention/immune-shielding to egress/opsonization/NK–macrophage killing, then the transplant itself will eradicate LSCs and establish durable donor hematopoiesis without non-selective systemic toxicity or excess GVHD.

Operational objective
Achieve relapse rates equal to or lower than myeloablative conditioning by replacing systemic cytotoxic conditioning with a marrow-localized, LSC-triggered paracrine switch produced by the graft.

Specific aims
1) Build an LSC-triggered, marrow-tethered effector program in donor HSCs that mobilizes and destroys LSCs while sparing normal HSCs.
2) Pair this graft with non-genotoxic, HSC-sparing niche opening to enable engraftment and early exposure of LSCs.
3) Demonstrate LSC eradication, multi-evasion control, and GVHD-sparing in AML PDX/humanized models and define a clinical feasibility path.

Design and methods

Graft design: SynNotch-sentinel donor HSCs
- Sensor: A synNotch receptor in donor CD34+ HSCs recognizing an LSC-selective antigen chosen per patient (default: CLEC12A/CLL-1; alternatives: CD93 or CD70; exclude targets expressed on normal HSCs). Engagement activates a short-lived transcriptional burst (24–72 h) via degron-tagged TFs.
- Localized effector: “SHIELDbreaker,” a single, ECM-tethered multispecific protein secreted only after synNotch activation and captured in marrow via a collagen-binding domain. SHIELDbreaker integrates:
  a) Niche egress: a high-affinity CXCL12 sink (dimeric ACKR3/CXCR7 ectodomain) to deplete CXCL12 locally and force LSCs out of stromal protection.
  b) Anti-phagocytic reversal: an SIRPα variant-Fc that blocks CD47, enabling macrophage phagocytosis of LSCs.
  c) HLA-independent cytotoxicity: an LSC binder × CD16 engager to recruit donor NK cells for ADCC despite HLA loss/heterogeneity.
- Innate booster (local only): synNotch-induced, membrane-tethered IL-15/IL-15Rα on short-lived donor myeloid progeny to expand NK and γδ T cells in situ without systemic cytokinemia.
- Spatial/temporal containment:
  - ECM-tethering to confine effectors to marrow.
  - Protease-cleavable degrons for rapid effector decay.
  - Hematopoietic promoter (Vav1) with synNotch gating; no basal leak.
  - Safety OFF-switch: dTAG or TetR-based pharmacologic shutdown of the synNotch effector cassette.
- Product composition:
  - Primary: engineered donor CD34+ cells (HSC-enriched) with synNotch cassette knocked into a safe harbor (e.g., AAVS1) to ensure durable, multi-lineage “sentinel” progeny.
  - Early-window accelerant: a small co-infusion (≤10% of CD34+) of ex vivo myeloid-primed progenitors from the same edited product to provide immediate marrow-localized effectors during the first 1–2 weeks post-infusion.

Conditioning and engraftment (non-genotoxic)
- Host HSC niche opening: single-agent anti-CD117 (JSP191 or equivalent) to deplete host HSCs while sparing other tissues.
- Transient LSC exposure: peri-infusion CXCR4 blockade (plerixafor) plus a short oral course of an E-selectin antagonist (e.g., uproleselan) to further dislodge LSCs and increase contact with donor sentinels; both are non-genotoxic and time-limited.
- GVHD-sparing graft handling: αβ TCR-depleted or naïve-enriched T-replete graft preserving NK/γδ compartments; avoid post-transplant alkylators. Standard calcineurin inhibitor taper guided by MRD and inflammatory markers, not fixed schedule.

How the design meets constraints
- Replaces MAC’s anti-leukemia effect: Local, high-intensity, HLA-independent killing (NK ADCC + macrophage phagocytosis) is triggered precisely where LSCs reside, compensating for RIC/NMA.
- Excludes non-selective genotoxic agents: Uses anti-CD117 antibody plus transient CXCR4/E-selectin blockade.
- LSC selectivity with preserved donor HSC engraftment: Sensing uses LSC-specific antigens; effectors are deployed only near LSCs and decay rapidly; global CXCL12 remains intact for donor HSC homing elsewhere.
- Overcomes sanctuary: Local CXCL12 depletion and E-selectin inhibition force LSC egress from stromal niches, exposing them to effectors.
- Counters multiple immune evasions simultaneously: HLA loss (CD16 engager), checkpoint-mediated dysfunction (local IL-15 sustains NK/γδ activity without systemic checkpoint blockade), anti-phagocytic CD47 signal (SIRPα-Fc).
- Enhances GVL without exacerbating GVHD: NK/γδ-centric cytotoxicity, ECM-tethered effectors, no systemic checkpoint antibodies, and αβ TCR modulation minimize GVHD risk.

Experimental plan

Aim 1: Circuit build and in vitro validation
- Construct synNotch receptors for CLL-1/CD93/CD70 and select patient-matched antigen(s).
- Generate SHIELDbreaker variants and confirm: (i) CXCL12 binding kinetics; (ii) CD47-SIRPα blockade; (iii) NK ADCC bridging; (iv) ECM capture and local retention.
- Edit healthy-donor CD34+ cells (AAV6 + CRISPR) and confirm multi-lineage potential, synNotch inducibility, and absence of leak.
- Co-culture assays with primary AML LSCs and normal HSCs: measure LSC killing, normal CFU preservation, and local vs systemic effector levels. ELDA to quantify LSC frequency post-exposure.

Milestones: >2-log LSC frequency reduction; ≤20% reduction in normal CFU; effector half-life ≤24 h in supernatant; no synNotch leak without antigen.

Aim 2: Non-genotoxic engraftment and niche biology
- Mouse xenografts with humanized marrow: compare anti-CD117 ± plerixafor ± E-selectin inhibitor for donor chimerism, niche space, and transient LSC mobilization (intravital microscopy).
- Track donor HSC homing vs local CXCL12 depletion using barcoded HSCs and single-cell spatial transcriptomics.

Milestones: >70% donor chimerism by week 6; donor HSC localization preserved outside SHIELDbreaker hotspots; LSC displacement from endosteal niches within hours of trigger.

Aim 3: In vivo efficacy, immune-evasion control, and GVHD
- AML PDX with defined evasions (HLA loss variants; PD-L1high; CD47high). Randomize to: RIC alone; RIC + unedited HSCT; RIC + synNotch HSCT. Evaluate MRD (flow/NGS), ELDA, survival, relapse at 6 months.
- NK/γδ dependence: deplete NK or block CD16 to define mechanism; macrophage depletion controls for phagocytosis.
- GVHD assessment in humanized allogeneic models with αβ TCR-depleted vs naïve-enriched grafts; cytokine profiling to confirm marrow-localized signals.

Milestones: Zero-detectable LSCs by ELDA; relapse-free survival non-inferior to MAC controls and superior to RIC; no increase in grade ≥II GVHD; low systemic cytokines.

Clinical development path (phase 1/2)
- Patient selection: AML/MDS with CLL-1/CD93/CD70+ LSCs; MRD+ or high-risk in CR.
- Manufacturing: Donor apheresis → CD34+ isolation → CRISPR/AAV6 knock-in → brief myeloid priming of a 10% fraction → QC for synNotch inducibility, karyotype, off-targets.
- Regimen: Day −7 anti-CD117; Day −1 to +2 plerixafor and E-selectin inhibitor; Day 0 infusion of engineered CD34+ plus myeloid-primed fraction; standard antimicrobial prophylaxis; αβ TCR depletion or naïve-enriched T cells as per arm.
- Pharmacodynamic readouts: SHIELDbreaker levels in marrow vs plasma; NK activation in marrow; LSC displacement imaging; MRD kinetics.

Risk analysis and mitigations
- Antigen heterogeneity: patient-specific dual-OR synNotch (e.g., CLL-1 OR CD93). If antigen loss emerges, re-infuse donor NK expanded ex vivo to exploit CD47 blockade.
- Donor HSC engraftment interference: restrict CXCL12 sink to myeloid progeny via lineage-restricted promoter; decay within 24 h; staggered infusion (myeloid first, HSCs 24 h later).
- Off-target opsonization: strict antigen selection; ECM tethering; microdosed payload; real-time OFF-switch availability.
- GVHD flare due to residual αβ T cells: deploy αβ TCR-depleted graft arm; avoid CD3-engaging modules.

Go/no-go criteria
- Go: In vivo ≥3-log LSC reduction, donor chimerism ≥70%, and no GVHD increase vs αβ-depleted controls.
- No-go: Any signal of impaired donor HSC engraftment due to effector leakage; systemic cytokines > predefined thresholds; non-specific hematopoietic toxicity.

Expected impact
This strategy converts HSCT into a tumor-seeking, niche-remodeling therapy in which donor cells condition and cure simultaneously. By gating multi-pronged, HLA-independent killing to LSC niches, it preserves engraftment, avoids genotoxicity, counters major immune-evasion modes, and aims for relapse rates at or below today’s myeloablative standards without their systemic toxicity.

Title
Decoy-and-Destroy Allo-HSCT: Antigen-triggered LSC mobilization with blood-restricted cytotoxicity to replace MAC-level anti-leukemia activity without systemic genotoxicity

Central hypothesis (atomic strategy)
Relocate graft-versus-leukemia from the hypoxic bone marrow niche to the normoxic bloodstream by coupling LSC-conditional niche disruption to a circulation-gated killing program in engineered allogeneic innate-like effector cells. This spatial decoupling preserves donor HSC engraftment, overcomes niche-mediated protection, and intensifies GVL without escalating GVHD.

Objectives
- Achieve relapse rates comparable to or lower than MAC while using RIC/NMA, with no non-selective genotoxic agents.
- Selectively eradicate LSCs while preserving normal HSC engraftment and function.
- Neutralize LSC immune-evasion (HLA loss, checkpoint upregulation, CD47 signals) without increasing GVHD.

Therapeutic platform
- Effector chassis: donor-derived CAR-NK or invariant NKT (iNKT) cells (both low-GVHD risk), optionally γδ T cells; αβ TCR is knocked out if αβ T cells are used.
- Three coordinated modules:
  1) Find: multi-antigen synNotch sensing for LSC-selective recognition (e.g., CLL-1 and/or CD123 OR TIM-3) with NOT gating on HSC markers (e.g., CD90) to spare CD34+CD90+ HSCs.
  2) Flush: upon LSC recognition, conditional, local release of niche-disruptors that mobilize LSCs without systemic effects—short-lived CXCR4/CXCL12 axis blockers (e.g., secreted peptide antagonist or nanobody), and transient VLA-4/VCAM-1 engagement disruptor—restricted by synNotch promoters and rapid degradation tags.
  3) Finish: a normoxia-activated CAR cytotoxicity program (e.g., oxygen-dependent degradation domain–based repression relieved in normoxia) that is inert in hypoxic marrow but active in blood, driving degranulation, death receptor engagement, and ADCC specifically in circulation.

Non-genotoxic transplant backbone
- Conditioning: anti-CD117 antibody for host HSC niche opening plus anti-CD52 or anti-CD45 for lymphodepletion; no busulfan/TBI/alkylators.
- Donor graft: standard allogeneic HSC product, with donor selection favoring NK alloreactivity (KIR–HLA education) to augment missing-self responses.
- Sequencing: infuse donor HSCs first; after confirmed homing window, administer engineered effector cells. Effector mobilizer payloads are LSC-conditional to avoid impairing donor HSC engraftment.

Immune-evasion countermeasures (built into effector)
- HLA loss: NK/iNKT missing-self cytotoxicity plus CAR targeting.
- Checkpoints: PD-1→CD28 or TIGIT→CD28 switch receptors; local secretion of anti–PD-L1 minibodies under synNotch control.
- Anti-phagocytic signals: membrane-tethered high-affinity SIRPα decoy to block LSC CD47, promoting bystander phagocytosis; expression gated to LSC encounter to limit RBC binding.
- Immunosuppressive milieu: dominant-negative TGF-β receptor and A2A receptor knockout to resist adenosine; surface-anchored IL-15 or IL-2 mutein to sustain effector persistence without systemic cytokinemia.

Safety and GVHD control
- Low-GVHD effector chassis (NK/iNKT/γδ); αβ TCR knockout if needed.
- Logic gating (AND/NOT) for LSC selectivity and hypoxia-off/normoxia-on kill.
- Pharmacologic and genetic off-switches (e.g., small-molecule–gated kill switch; suicide gene).
- Mobilizer payloads with microenvironment-labile designs (short half-life, protease-sensitive tags).
- Cytokine restraint via membrane-tethered variants rather than secreted forms.

Specific aims and milestones
Aim 1: Build LSC-conditional mobilization and circulation-gated killing circuits.
- Design: synNotch(LSC antigen)→(a) secretion of CXCR4 antagonist and VLA-4 disruptor; (b) release of anti–PD-L1 minibody; (c) SIRPα decoy expression. CAR signaling placed under normoxia activation gate.
- Milestones: (i) Specific activation on LSC+ targets with NOT gating on CD90+ HSCs; (ii) Mobilization of LSCs from ex vivo marrow organoids without dislodging HSCs; (iii) Hypoxia-off/normoxia-on killing with ≥10-fold kill differential.

Aim 2: Demonstrate in vivo decoy-and-destroy and immune-evasion resilience.
- Models: human AML LSC-enriched PDX with BM-on-a-chip and murine xenografts; track LSC egress, blood-phase killing, MRD by single-cell multiomics.
- Endpoints: (i) Rapid rise in circulating LSCs post-effector exposure; (ii) ≥2-log LSC reduction in marrow with preserved donor HSC chimerism; (iii) Control of HLA-loss, PD-L1high, and CD47high clones.

Aim 3: Integrate with non-genotoxic allo-HSCT and benchmark against MAC-level efficacy.
- Study arms: RIC/NMA + Decoy-and-Destroy vs RIC/NMA alone vs historical MAC controls.
- Endpoints: relapse-free survival, cumulative incidence of relapse, MRD negativity, full-donor chimerism, grade II–IV acute GVHD and chronic GVHD rates, immune reconstitution, infections.
- Go/no-go: Non-inferior relapse at 12 months to MAC with ≤ standard GVHD and preserved engraftment kinetics.

Experimental strategy (high-level)
- Circuit engineering: modular vectors enabling interchangeable antigen gates and payloads; quantitative promoter tuning for mobilizer dose.
- Niche modeling: 3D co-cultures of osteoblasts, MSCs, endothelial cells, and sympathetic fibers to assess targeted egress and HSC sparing.
- Flow-physiology assays: microfluidic shear/normoxia platforms to confirm circulation-restricted cytotoxic activation.
- Systems profiling: longitudinal single-cell RNA/ATAC/proteomics of blood/marrow to quantify LSC depletion, microenvironment remodeling, and off-target effects.
- Safety: hemagglutination and RBC binding panels; cytokine release profiling; biodistribution; off-switch responsiveness.

Clinical translation blueprint (Phase 1/2)
- Population: adults with AML/MDS undergoing allo-HSCT with RIC/NMA at high relapse risk or MRD+ pre-transplant.
- Treatment: antibody-only conditioning; day 0 HSC infusion; day +3 to +7 engineered effector infusion; repeat dosing guided by circulating LSC biomarkers and soluble mobilizer pharmacodynamics.
- Biomarkers: circulating LSC bursts post-infusion; plasma CXCL12 dynamics; ctDNA/LSC neoantigen load; immune phenotyping for checkpoint and CD47 axes.
- Primary endpoints: safety (DLTs, GVHD), engraftment; secondary: MRD, relapse, survival.

Risk management and contingencies
- Antigen heterogeneity: patient-specific antigen mapping; multi-antigen OR gates with NOT(HSC) maintained; rapid vector retargeting.
- Inadequate mobilization: add inducible VLA-4 blockade or transient CXCR2 chemotaxis bias in effectors; escalate mobilizer expression window with drug-controlled promoters.
- Donor HSC homing interference: delay effector dosing; throttle mobilizer strength with degrons; use marrow-restricted delivery if needed.
- Excess inflammation: activate off-switch; transient checkpoint restoration (drug-inducible switch receptor blockade); adjunct IL-6 pathway inhibition if required.

Expected outcomes and impact
- MAC-comparable or superior relapse control without systemic genotoxicity.
- LSC-selective clearance via microenvironmental decoupling: recognize in niche, mobilize, and kill only in blood.
- Broad immunity to LSC evasions while maintaining low GVHD risk and robust donor HSC engraftment.

Success criteria
- Demonstrated hypoxia-off/normoxia-on cytotoxic differential ≥10x.
- ≥2-log reduction of marrow LSCs with preserved HSC engraftment in vivo.
- Non-inferior 12-month relapse-free survival vs MAC with equal or lower GVHD in early-phase clinical evaluation.

text:
Title: ChronoCLIP-seq — Same-cell transcriptome trajectories via pulse-gated, covalent time-indexing of mRNAs and single end-point single-cell readout

Atomic strategy:
Transform each cell’s transcriptome at time ti into a stable, intracellular molecular record by covalently appending an orthogonal, time-unique DNA primer to the 3′ poly(A) tails of mRNAs during a brief, externally gated window; after ≥7 windows, lyse once and sequence to recover per-cell expression vectors across all times.

Specific aims:
1) Engineer orthogonal Time-Indexed Capture Primers (TICPs) that bind poly(A) tails, crosslink upon brief light exposure, and carry unique time barcodes and RT priming sites without activating RNA decay pathways.
2) Implement a minimally perturbative, seven-epoch time-gating regimen (30 min to 24 h, logarithmic spacing) to append distinct TICPs in live cells following a t=0 perturbation.
3) Build a combinatorial-indexed single-cell library that decodes, for each cell, gene counts per timepoint; validate dynamic accuracy and heterogeneity statistics.

Core design:
- TICP architecture (DNA/LNA/2′-OMe chimera):
  - 5′: sequencing handle + 8–10 bp unique time barcode (T1–T7) + 10 bp unique molecular identifier (UMI).
  - Middle: clamp/hairpin domain that sequesters the poly(U) capture tract until opened.
  - 3′: 25–30 nt poly(U) capture tract containing 3–5 interspersed psoralen-modified nucleotides for 365 nm UVA–induced interstrand crosslinking to AU base pairs; free 3′-OH for reverse transcription priming.
  - Chemical features: internal LNA/2′-OMe to prevent RNase H recruitment; terminal phosphorothioates for nuclease resistance; net charge balanced for cytosolic uptake.
- Orthogonal activation:
  - Each TICP is preloaded in cells as a kinetically trapped hairpin; timepoint-specific “invader” oligos (11–15 nt, 2′-OMe) added to medium unlock only the matched hairpin via toehold-mediated strand displacement.
  - A brief, low-dose 365 nm LED pulse (e.g., 1–5 s, ≤1 mW/cm²) crosslinks the bound poly(U) tract to poly(A) tails present in that window. Immediately after, a “terminator” oligo re-sequesters any remaining open TICP to prevent carryover crosslinking at later pulses.
- Cell handling and delivery:
  - Preload all seven TICPs 2–4 h before t=0 using cholesterol- or CPP-conjugated delivery or LNPs; dose titrated to tag ~1–5% of poly(A) tails per epoch (minimizes PABP displacement and stability effects).
  - Use 2-D adherent arrays or suspension in perfused microplates enabling synchronized medium changes and invader additions across thousands of cells simultaneously.

Time regimen and perturbation:
- At t=0 apply the perturbation (drug, cytokine, CRISPRi/a induction, etc.).
- Apply seven epochs at logarithmic spacing: 0.5 h, 1 h, 2 h, 4 h, 8 h, 16 h, 24 h.
  - For each epoch i: add invader-i (3–5 min), UVA pulse (1–5 s), add terminator-i (3–5 min), resume culture.
- Phototoxicity control: pre-validate pulse dose; monitor ROS and p53 targets; favor LED illumination in phenol-red–free medium; optionally use two-photon scanning for sensitive cells.

Single end-point readout and scaling:
- At 24 h (post-final epoch), lightly fix (methanol) to preserve DNA–RNA crosslinks; permeabilize.
- Perform in situ reverse transcription primed exclusively from TICP 3′ ends (captures 3′ tags of crosslinked mRNAs with embedded time barcodes and UMIs).
- Assign cell identities using high-throughput combinatorial indexing (e.g., 3–4 rounds of split-pool ligation or PCR barcoding) to reach 10^4–10^5 cells/run.
- Second strand synthesis and amplicon construction yield libraries with Read1: cell barcode(s) + UMI; Read2: gene identity; index read: time barcode (T1–T7).

Data model and analysis:
- For each cell c and gene g, obtain count vector Ng,c = [n1 … n7], where ni are UMI-collapsed molecules bearing Ti.
- Normalize per-epoch capture efficiency using exogenous spike-ins delivered only during each epoch and housekeeping gene stability.
- Quality control: exclude cells with stress-response overactivation post-illumination; require minimal per-epoch tag recovery thresholds.
- Trajectory inference is direct (no pseudotime): cluster per-cell time series; compute response latency, peak time, adaptation time; quantify inter-cell heterogeneity (e.g., dynamic Earth Mover’s Distance, functional principal components).

Validation experiments:
- Chemistry/biophysics (Aim 1):
  - In vitro RNA with defined poly(A) tails: measure crosslink yield vs pulse energy; confirm RT priming efficiency and read-through across poly(U)–poly(A) junction.
  - In-cell: demonstrate no RNase H–mediated cleavage (2′-OMe/LNA dependence), minimal impact on global mRNA half-lives at target occupancies.
- Dynamic fidelity (Aim 2–3):
  - Benchmark against destructive parallel time courses on matched populations; correlate per-epoch means; demonstrate per-cell consistency (e.g., drug-response marker cascades: immediate-early genes → delayed targets).
  - Heterogeneity: show separation of responder archetypes (early/late/adaptive) within the same perturbation dose.

Controls:
- No-invader and no-light controls per epoch to estimate spontaneous uncaging and off-epoch crosslinking.
- Swapped-invader controls to test orthogonality.
- Viability and stress assays before/after each pulse.
- Occupancy titration to balance capture depth vs perturbation.

Throughput and power:
- With 10^4 cells, median 2,500 genes detected per epoch/cell at target occupancy yields sufficient power to model cell-specific response kinetics and identify rare subtrajectories (>1% frequency) with FDR < 0.05 after multiple-testing correction.

Risk and mitigation:
- Phototoxicity: minimize pulse energy; distribute pulses over field; consider red-shifted psoralen analogs or two-photon activation if needed.
- Delivery variability: pre-equilibrate TICPs; normalize using per-epoch spike-ins; include cell-level capture-efficiency covariates.
- Over-occupancy of poly(A) tails: cap per-epoch TICP concentration; stagger invader residence; verify translation rates remain within ±10%.
- Cross-epoch leakage: terminator oligos; hairpin designs with high closing kinetics; empirical leakage correction using controls.

Milestones:
- M1 (Month 3): >70% crosslinking of test RNAs with successful RT priming; negligible RNase H cleavage.
- M2 (Month 6): Seven-epoch tagging in cell culture with >85% viability and <5% off-epoch leakage.
- M3 (Month 9): End-point single-cell libraries with ≥7 time-barcoded distributions per cell; concordance with bulk time courses (Pearson r > 0.8 per gene median).
- M4 (Month 12): Demonstrate cell-specific response trajectory heterogeneity to a drug at two doses; publish protocol and open-source designs.

Differentiation from existing approaches:
- Not computational reconstruction (no pseudotime/RNA velocity).
- Not metabolic labeling (no nucleotide analog incorporation or conversion).
- Not lineage barcoding or few-gene reporters.
- Not serial aspiration (distinct from Live-seq/nanostraw/NTVE): no material removal; instead, in situ, covalent, time-stamped tagging of native mRNAs with a single terminal readout.

Deliverable:
A complete, open protocol (reagents, sequences, invader/terminator designs, illumination parameters, library schema, and analysis pipeline) enabling any lab to record ≥7 same-cell transcriptome states from 30 min to 24 h post-perturbation and analyze true single-cell response trajectories at scale.

text:
Title
ChronoVesicle Recording (CV-Seq): intracellular, time-barcoded vesicle capture for multi-timepoint single-cell transcriptomics

Core question
Can we convert time into a molecular index co-packaged with endogenously sampled cytosol inside intracellular vesicles, retain those vesicles in living cells throughout a perturbation, and recover a ≥7-point transcriptomic trajectory from each individual cell in a single terminal readout?

Atomic strategy
Record-first, readout-later: continuously bud intraluminal vesicles (ILVs) that sequester snapshots of cytosol; at defined moments apply orthogonal, cell-permeant “time-stamp” barcodes that covalently attach to the cytosol-facing leaflet of nascent ILVs and become lumen-protected upon scission; retain all ILVs intracellularly; at the end, release and sequence to decode cell-of-origin and time-of-capture per RNA.

Specific aims
1) Engineer an intracellular “vesicle recorder” that: (i) buds many ILVs, (ii) covalently acquires user-defined time barcodes only during brief pulses, (iii) retains ILVs until end-point.
2) Achieve ≥7 logarithmically spaced time stamps spanning 30 min–24 h after a defined perturbation at t=0.
3) Pool and process thousands of cells simultaneously while preserving per-cell identity and per-vesicle time labels to quantify inter-cell heterogeneity in response trajectories.

System design
- Vesicle recorder chassis
  - Budding: Upregulate ESCRT/tetraspanin-driven ILVs (e.g., CD63-based chassis) to increase vesicle number.
  - Time-stamping epitope: Fuse a self-labeling enzyme (e.g., HaloTag/SNAP) to the cytosolic tail of an ILV-enriched membrane protein. During a pulse, only molecules on the cytosolic leaflet of membranes currently invaginating are accessible; after scission, the label is trapped inside the ILV.
  - Cargo capture (transcriptome-level): Rely on cytosol sequestration during ILV formation; bias toward mRNA by tethering broad RNA-binding adaptors (e.g., poly(A)-associating domains) to the ILV interior to enrich polyadenylated RNAs while minimizing sequence specificity.
  - Retention: Suppress exocytosis (e.g., by reducing Rab27-dependent trafficking) and/or tether MVBs to the cytoskeleton via reversible dimerization so ILVs remain intracellular until end-point.
  - Cell identity: Each cell constitutively expresses a polyadenylated “CellID” barcode RNA that co-packages into ILVs, enabling unambiguous cell-of-origin assignment after pooling.

- Time-barcoding chemistry
  - Provide a panel of seven cell-permeant barcoded ligands (B0.5h, B1h, B2h, B4h, B8h, B12h, B24h) for the self-labeling tag. To minimize residual reactivity, use photocaged versions loaded at t=0 and uncaged briefly by light at each time, or pair uncaging with an intracellular scavenger that quenches remaining ligand after each pulse.
  - Each barcode carries: (i) a unique short nucleic acid sequence (time index), (ii) a PCR handle for recovery during library prep. Covalent attachment ensures stability through the 24 h recording window.

- Release and end-point readout
  - After the final time point, trigger ILV release (optional) or directly lyse cells under conditions that preserve ILVs.
  - Single-vesicle partitioning: Encapsulate ILVs into droplets or nanowells bearing barcoded capture beads. In each partition, co-capture (a) ILV RNAs via oligo-dT priming and (b) the membrane-linked time-barcode DNA via complementary capture so both acquire the same partition barcode.
  - Library structure: Each cDNA molecule carries a partition barcode/UMI; each partition is associated to exactly one time-barcode sequence (the ILV’s time label) and to any CellID RNAs present, enabling assignment of transcripts to {cell, time}.

Experimental plan
- Cell line construction and validation
  - Introduce vesicle recorder chassis and a high-diversity CellID library to generate uniquely labeled cells.
  - Verify: (i) inducible ILV production and intracellular retention, (ii) low perturbation to growth and basal transcriptome, (iii) efficient recovery of polyadenylated RNAs from ILVs.

- Perturbation and recording
  - At t=0, apply the defined perturbation. Deliver the full panel of caged time-barcodes at t=0.
  - Uncage at seven logarithmic times: 0.5 h, 1 h, 2 h, 4 h, 8 h, 12 h, 24 h. Each uncaging labels only nascent ILVs forming during a short window; labels become lumen-protected immediately upon scission.
  - Maintain intracellular retention throughout.

- End-point capture and sequencing
  - At 24 h, harvest ILVs, perform single-vesicle barcoded capture, prepare dual-index libraries (mRNA and time-barcode), and sequence to jointly read transcriptomes, time indices, and CellIDs.

Controls and benchmarks
- Time specificity: “Pulse-chase” controls with staggered colors or orthogonal tags; quantify cross-labeling between adjacent windows.
- Vesicle dependence: Block ILV formation to ensure loss of signal; confirm signals are vesicle-derived.
- Secretion leakage: Monitor extracellular vesicles; adjust retention accordingly.
- Transcriptome fidelity: Compare ILV-derived profiles (summed across time) to conventional scRNA-seq at end-point to assess representation and bias.
- Sensitivity and dynamic range: Titrate vesicle yield and estimate per-timepoint gene detection per cell; target coverage sufficient for pathway-level inference.
- Cell health: Assess viability and proliferation under recording conditions.

Data analysis
- Demultiplex reads by partition barcode; assign each partition to a unique time index using the captured time-barcode sequence.
- Use CellID reads to group partitions (vesicles) by cell-of-origin, assembling for each cell a set of time-stamped transcriptomes.
- Construct gene-by-time matrices per cell; apply smoothing appropriate for ILV sampling noise; quantify intra- and inter-cell trajectory heterogeneity; test for early/late responders and branching responses.

Throughput and heterogeneity
- Pool thousands of uniquely CellID-tagged cells in a single run; each cell emits multiple ILVs across windows, increasing sampling depth per time point.
- Statistical power derives from per-cell repeated measures (within-cell comparisons) and population size (between-cell heterogeneity).

Risk mitigation
- Low mRNA yield per ILV: increase budding rate; modestly enlarge ILVs; enrich poly(A) cargo; aggregate multiple ILVs per time bin per cell computationally.
- Barcode carryover: prefer photouncaging with brief illumination and intracellular scavengers to terminate each pulse.
- Biological impact: minimize overexpression; benchmark recorder lines; include non-recorder controls in all experiments.

Differentiation from existing methods
- Not inference: directly records per-cell temporal snapshots without pseudotime or RNA velocity.
- Not metabolic labeling: no base analog incorporation; time is encoded by vesicle-bound, lumen-protected barcodes.
- Not lineage barcoding: CellIDs serve only cell-of-origin mapping; time is independent and explicit.
- Not few-gene reporters: captures transcriptome-level states.
- Not repeated aspiration/sampling (Live-seq, nanostraws, NTVE): cells are not invasively sampled over time; all snapshots are recorded intracellularly and read once at the end.

Milestones and success criteria
- M1: Demonstrate seven orthogonal time stamps with <5% cross-window misassignment in a recorder line.
- M2: Recover ≥1,000 genes per time bin per cell (median) in a benchmark cell type while maintaining ≥85% viability through 24 h.
- M3: Resolve distinct single-cell response trajectories to a t=0 perturbation, with reproducible early/late divergence across biological replicates.

Expected outcome
CV-Seq will yield, for each individual cell, a discrete, ≥7-point transcriptomic trajectory spanning 30 min–24 h post-perturbation, enabling direct measurement of response dynamics and heterogeneity without repeated destructive sampling.

Title
Molecular Projection Diaries: Same-cell transcriptome trajectories recorded in DNA via time-ordered random projections

Central Question and Hypothesis
Question: What dynamic response features of single cells (ordering, transient states, path-dependent bifurcations) are fundamentally unresolvable from destructive snapshots, and what capabilities must new technologies possess to recover them?
Hypothesis: If, within each living cell, we continuously convert high-dimensional transcriptomes into a small set of time-ordered random projections written into a DNA “diary,” then end-point sequencing can reconstruct per-cell transcriptome trajectories across at least seven time scales from 30 minutes to 24 hours. Comparing these trajectories to conventional snapshot time series will reveal specific, quantifiable information losses inherent to destructive sampling.

Atomic Strategy
Replace repeated destructive measurements by an in-cell compressed, time-ordered record: map the transcriptome at each moment into K low-dimensional projections whose values are proportional to mRNA abundances, and append these projections sequentially into a DNA array whose order encodes time. One end-point read per cell yields repeated measures.

System Architecture
1) Time-ordered DNA diary
- A leader-proximal recording array (RA) accepts sequential insertions of 24–32 nt “projection spacers.” Integration order corresponds to time.
- A constitutive “tick” donor integrates at a known rate to calibrate position-to-time mapping cell-by-cell.

2) Projection donors (PDs)
- K=256 RNA-responsive donor cassettes produce ssDNA donors D1..DK via retron reverse transcription.
- Each cassette is controlled by a compact RNA sensor (toehold switch or dCas13-based activator) keyed to an 8-nt RNA motif class. The production rate of Di is proportional to the total cellular abundance of transcripts containing motif i (precomputed incidence matrix A ∈ R(G×K)).

3) Integration machinery
- Cas1–Cas2 (or functionally equivalent CRISPR-associated spacer acquisition module adapted to mammalian cells) continuously captures retron ssDNA donors into RA at 37°C without inducing DSBs.
- A short leader-proximal PAMless capture sequence ensures order fidelity and minimizes re-editing.

4) End-point readout
- At 24 hours, perform single-cell encapsulation. For each cell: (i) targeted amplicon-seq of RA to recover the ordered spacer series, and (ii) standard scRNA-seq for the terminal transcriptome and cell barcode linkage.

Experimental Design
Perturbation and schedule
- t=0: Apply defined perturbation (e.g., 100 nM MEK inhibitor; or CRISPRa/CRISPRi pulse) to plated cells in a microfluidic array supporting 10^5–10^6 cells.
- Recording runs continuously from t=0 to t=24 h.
- Post hoc, map array position to seven logarithmic time bins centered near 0.5 h, 1 h, 2 h, 4 h, 8 h, 16 h, and 24 h using the tick calibration.

Cell model and delivery
- Use a well-characterized human line (e.g., RPE1 or K562) engineered once to stably express: RA (lentiviral, single-copy landing pad), Cas1–Cas2, tick donor cassette, and the K=256 PD cassettes under mild expression to reduce burden.
- Validate minimal fitness impact and baseline integration noise before perturbations.

Decoding and Reconstruction
- From each RA, parse the ordered spacer list. Assign spacers to bins via tick-based calibration (nonlinear mapping allowed).
- For each bin t, count occurrences yi,t of donor i to form y_t ∈ R^K_+.
- Given the precomputed gene-by-motif matrix A (rows: genes, columns: motifs) and calibration constants, recover the per-cell transcriptome x_t ∈ R^G_+ at each time by solving:
  minimize ||A x_t − y_t||_2^2 + λ1||x_t||_1 + λTV Σ||x_t − x_{t−1}||_1
  subject to x_t ≥ 0 and concordance with end-point scRNA-seq x_T.
- Output: for each cell, gene-level trajectories across seven bins.

Controls and Validation
- Bench calibration: Spike-in synthetic RNA motif pools at controlled concentrations; verify linearity between motif abundance and donor integration counts in bulk and single cells.
- Null PD set: scrambled sensors controlling donors to quantify off-target/background integration.
- Static control: cycloheximide-arrested cells to assess baseline drift of the diary in the absence of transcriptional change.
- Ground-truth reporters: 6–10 endogenous genes with orthogonal MS2/MCP fluorescent reporters (few-gene imaging only for validation, not core measurement) to compare timing and amplitude of peaks.
- Pharmacological perturbations with known temporal signatures (e.g., EGF pulse, ER stress) to verify temporal ordering fidelity.

Comparison Arm: Conventional Snapshots
- Parallel plates receive the same t=0 perturbation. At each of the seven time points, perform destructive scRNA-seq on independent cell aliquots (≥10,000 cells per time).
- Analytical comparison:
  - Reconstruct population trajectories by pseudotime and RNA velocity; compare against diary-derived true single-cell trajectories.
  - Quantify losses: peak-time bias, transient-state underrepresentation, path-dependent bifurcation misassignment, and misestimation of response variance.
  - Define “recoverability frontier”: minimum K (projections), integration SNR, and temporal bin width required to resolve specified dynamic features (e.g., 2-fold transient lasting ≤1 h).

Throughput and Power
- Target ≥50,000 successfully recorded single cells per condition to characterize inter-cell heterogeneity.
- With K=256 and per-bin RA length allowing ≥1,000 total integrations, simulations indicate median per-gene relative error <20% for genes in the top 2 deciles of expression, sufficient to recover pathway-level dynamics and major state transitions.

Risk Mitigation
- If Cas1–Cas2 integration is suboptimal, substitute a validated orthogonal sequential integrase system (e.g., CRISPR-associated transposase adapted for ordered multi-insert capture with helper “leader capture sites”). Maintain the same projection-and-tick logic.
- If K=256 burdens cells, deploy staged induction (K=128 core motifs + K=128 auxiliary motifs) or shrink K to 128 with optimized motif selection by determinantal point processes to preserve A’s conditioning.
- If motif-to-gene mapping introduces bias, learn a data-driven effective Aˆ from joint diary/end-point data using nonnegative matrix factorization under motif constraints, then re-decode.

What This Reveals About Snapshot Loss
- Direct, per-cell comparisons of diary trajectories vs. best-possible snapshot reconstructions will quantify:
  - Fraction of cells with misordered response phases.
  - Frequency and dwell times of transient states entirely absent in snapshots.
  - Rate of false bifurcations inferred by pseudotime that are actually looped or reversible trajectories.
  - Attenuation of heterogeneity: ratio of within-cell temporal variance captured by diary vs. between-cell variance inferred from snapshots.

Differentiation from Existing Approaches
- Not computational inference (pseudotime, RNA velocity): trajectories are physically recorded within the same cell.
- Not metabolic labeling (scEU-seq, sci-fate): no nucleotide analog incorporation; dynamics are encoded in DNA diaries from RNA-driven donor production.
- Not lineage barcoding: edits are non-heritable, intra-life diaries, not clonal history.
- Not few-gene reporters: projections summarize the whole transcriptome; reconstruction yields gene-level trajectories.
- Not Live-seq/NTVE/nanostraw: no serial aspiration or repeated physical sampling; a single end-point read suffices.

Milestones and Success Criteria
- M1: Demonstrate ordered spacer acquisition with tick-based calibration and <10% position-to-time mapping error over 24 h.
- M2: Establish linearity between controlled RNA motif spikes and donor counts (R^2 ≥ 0.8) and low background (SNR ≥ 5).
- M3: Recover known temporal programs (e.g., MAPK inhibition response) with ≥80% concordance of peak times vs. orthogonal reporters.
- M4: In head-to-head tests, show ≥2× reduction in trajectory misordering and ≥1.5× increase in detectable transient states vs. snapshot pipelines.
- M5: Deliver a “recoverability frontier” specification (K, SNR, bin width) guiding future same-cell measurement technologies.

Deliverables
- An open-source design kit (RA constructs, PD libraries, calibration tools), decoding software, and ranked lists of dynamic features that snapshots systematically miss—directly informing the capability targets for next-generation same-cell multi-time transcriptomics.
